Dutiye atthavikappe atthaṃ na kāmentīti [M 0.0067] anatthakāmātiādi asamatthasamāsopi yojito. “Asūriyapassāni mukhānī”tiādīsu viya hi yena samāso, na tassāyaṃ paṭisedhako a-kāroti. Yasmiṃ kismiñci nibbhaye yogakkhema-saddo niruḷho dukkhayogato khemattā.

199. 'Disagreeable' means not approached, not entered. 'Harm' means calamity or suffering. 'Unbeneficial' means its cause. In the second alternative interpretation, the phrase 'not desiring benefit' is applied to 'desiring harm,' etc., as an irregular compound. For just as in phrases like 'faces not seeing the sun,' the negative particle 'a-' does not negate the word with which it is compounded. In any state of fearlessness, the term 'security from the yoke' is established, meaning security from the yoke of suffering.

Saṅgatiādīsu saṅkhāravasena yaṃ labbhati, taṃ gahetabbaṃ. Na hi saṅkhārānaṃ ṭhānanisajjādayo bhojanādikiccesu vā sahakaraṇaṃ vijjatīti pacchimadvayaṃ tadatthavasena labbhatīti na sakkā vattunti. Yaṃ labbhatīti vā yaṃ atthajātaṃ labbhatīti attho. Tena yathā labbhati saṅgatiādīsu attho, tathā yojetabbo. Puggalassa hi saṅgati gantvā saṅkhārehi saṃyogo [V 0.0067] hoti, āgatehi ca tehi, puggalassa ca attano ṭhānādīsu saṅkhārehi sahabhāvo hoti, sabbakiriyāsu ca missībhāvoti. Anatthabhāvo upaddavabhāvo.

In cases like 'association,' whatever is obtained by way of formations should be understood. For formations have no cooperative role in actions like standing, sitting, etc., or in activities such as eating; hence, it cannot be said that the latter two are obtained based on their meaning. Or, 'whatever is obtained' means 'whatever kind of meaning is obtained.' Therefore, the meaning in cases like 'association' should be construed as it is obtained. For a person’s association is the connection with formations by going to them, and with those that have come; and for a person there is coexistence with formations in one's own standing, etc., and a mingling in all activities. 'The state of harm' means the state of calamity.

Aniṭṭhānaṃ āpāthagamanamattaṃ taṃgahaṇamattañca appiyasampayogo, na pana pathaviphassādayo viya appiyasampayogo nāma eko dhammo atthīti āha “so atthato eko dhammo nāma natthī”ti. Aniṭṭhāni kaṇṭakādīni amittā ca usuādīhi vijjhanādidukkhaṃ uppādenti.

Association with the disagreeable is merely the coming into range of the undesirable and the mere grasping of it; but, unlike the earth element, contact, etc., there is no single phenomenon called 'association with the disagreeable.' Therefore, it is said, 'In reality, there is no such single phenomenon.' Undesirable things, like thorns, and enemies, cause suffering such as being pierced with arrows, etc.

Idhāti imasmiṃ loke dukkhaṃ hotīti vā idha imasmiṃ dukkhasaccaniddese dukkho vuttoti vā yojetabbaṃ.

The word 'here' should be construed either as 'suffering exists in this world' or as 'here, in this exposition of the truth of suffering, suffering is spoken of.'

Piyavippayoganiddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of Separation from the Beloved

200. Minantīti nāḷiyādīsu dhaññaṃ viya anto pakkhipanti, na bahi karontīti attho. Amā-saddo sahabhāvadīpako. Ñāyanti vā ajjhattikāicceva. Ñātibyasanādiko hutvā upaṭṭhātīti byasanapaccupaṭṭhāno. Sokuppādaneneva sarīraṃ sosenti, kisaṃ karonti, akisampi nirojatākaraṇena milāpenti, tato ca kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ uppajjatīti taduppādakatā vuttā.

200. 'They measure' means they place inside, like grain in a bamboo tube or other measure, not putting it outside; this is the meaning. The word 'amā' indicates coexistence. Or, 'they are known' refers only to what is internal. It manifests as calamity because it arises as the loss of relatives, etc. By producing sorrow, they cause the body to dry up and become thin; even if not thin, they cause it to wither by producing ill-health, and from that bodily suffering arises—thus its causality is stated.

Sokasarasamappitāti etena cetasikadukkhaṃ dasseti, vitujjantīti etena kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ.

By 'struck by the dart of sorrow,' mental suffering is shown; by 'they are pierced,' bodily suffering is shown.

Icchāniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of What is Wished For

201. Yasmiṃ [M 0.0068] kāle jātiyā na āgantabbaṃ, taṃ kālaṃ gahetvā āha “parinibbutesu ca vijjamānaṃ jātiyā anāgamana”nti. Yampīti yenapīti attho vutto. Yadāpi pana yaṃ-saddo “iccha”nti etaṃ apekkhati, tadāpi alābhavisiṭṭhā icchā vuttā hoti. Yadā “na labhatī”ti etaṃ apekkhati, tadā icchāvisiṭṭho alābho vutto hoti. So panatthato añño dhammo natthi, tathāpi alabbhaneyyaicchāva vuttā hoti. Apāpuṇitabbesu pavattattā eva “appattipaccupaṭṭhānā”ti vuttā. Yattha hi sā icchā pavattā, taṃ vatthuṃ apāpuṇantī hutvā gayhatīti.

201. Taking the time when birth should not come about, he said: ‘the non-coming of birth existing even for those who have attained final Nibbāna.’ ‘Yampi’ is said to mean ‘yenapi.’ However, when the word ‘yaṃ’ refers to ‘desire’ (icchā), then desire distinguished by non-attainment is stated. When it refers to ‘does not obtain’ (na labhati), then non-attainment distinguished by desire is stated. But in meaning, there is no other phenomenon; even so, it is simply called ‘desire for the unattainable.’ Because it operates towards what is not to be obtained, it is called ‘having non-attainment as its manifestation.’ For wherever that desire arises, that object is grasped as being unattained.

Chinnabhinnagaṇenāti nillajjena dhuttagaṇena, kappaṭikagaṇena vā.

‘By a broken and shattered group’ (chinnabhinnagaṇena) means by a shameless, rogue group, or by a group of rag-wearers.

Vighātamayanti [V 0.0068] cittavighātamayaṃ domanassaṃ cittavighātato eva uppannaṃ ubbandhanajarātisārādikāyikaṃ dukkhañca. Icchitālābhanti alabbhaneyyaicchameva vadati.

‘They cause vexation’ (vighātamayanti) refers to mental distress, sorrow born from mental agitation, and also bodily suffering such as choking, fever, and dysentery, which arises from mental agitation itself. ‘Non-attainment of what is desired’ (icchitālābhaṃ) speaks merely of a desire for the unattainable.

Upādānakkhandhaniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of the Aggregates of Clinging

202. Vitthiṇṇassa dukkhassa ettakanti dassanaṃ dukkhassa saṅkhepo, taṃ kātuṃ na sakkā vitthārassa anantattā. Dukkhavitthāragataṃ pana desanāvitthāraṃ pahāya yattha sabbo dukkhavitthāro samodhānaṃ gacchati, tattha desanāya vavatthānaṃ saṅkhepo, taṃ kātuṃ sakkā tādisassa vatthuno sabbhāvā.

202. To demonstrate that extensive suffering is ‘only this much’ is a condensation of suffering, but that cannot be done because the expanse of suffering is endless. However, abandoning a detailed exposition that concerns the expanse of suffering, a condensation, which is a delimitation of the teaching at the point where the entire expanse of suffering converges, can be done, because of the existence of such a subject matter.

Desaṃ jānanto maggakkhāyikapuriso desako. Bhagavāpi dukkhassa desako. “Dukkhantadesakenā”ti vā pāṭho, dukkhantakkhāyikoti attho.

One who knows the region, a man who points out the path, is a teacher. The Blessed One is also a teacher of suffering. Alternatively, the reading may be ‘by the one who points out the end of suffering’ (dukkhantadesakena), meaning the proclaimer of the end of suffering.

Pāvakādayo yathā indhanādīni bādhenti, evaṃ bādhayamānā. Māraṇantikadukkhābhighātenāti iminā atipākaṭena jātijarādukkhavighātajasokādayo dasseti. Tatoti paridevato uddhaṃ. Kaṇṭha sosādi sandhi bandhacchedanādi janaka dhātukkhobha samāyogato kāyassa ābādhanadukkhaṃ dukkhaṃ. Yesu kesucīti tissassa vā phussassa vā upādānakkhandhesu sabbampi cakkhurogādidukkhaṃ sabbasattagataṃ evaṃpakāramevāti saṅkhipitvā dassentoti attho.

Just as fires, etc., afflict fuel, etc., so too do they afflict. By ‘the assault of suffering that ends in death’ (māraṇantikadukkhābhighātena), which is extremely obvious, he indicates the grief, etc., arising from the destruction of the suffering of birth and aging. From that—that is, from lamentation onwards. The suffering of bodily affliction is the suffering arising from the combination of elemental disturbance that generates drying of the throat, severing of the joints, etc. ‘In whatever things’ (yesu kesuci) means that all suffering, from eye-disease onwards, which pertains to all beings, whether in Tissa’s or Phussa’s aggregates of clinging, is only of this kind. Thus, summarizing, this is the meaning he shows.

Dukkhasaccaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Truth of Suffering is completed.

2. Samudayasaccaniddesavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Exposition of the Truth of Origin

203. Uttarapadalopaṃ [M 0.0069] katvā “punabbhavakaraṇaṃ punobbhavo”tiāha. “Manosamphasso”ti ettha mano viya ca purimapadassa okārantatā daṭṭhabbā. Atha vā sīlaṭṭhena ika-saddena gamiyatthattā kiriyāvācakassa saddassa adassanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ yathā “apūpabhakkhanasīlo āpūpiko”ti. “Taddhitā”iti bahuvacananiddesā vicittattā vā taddhitānaṃ abhidhānalakkhaṇattā [V 0.0069] vā “punabbhavaṃ detī”tiādīsu atthesu ponobbhavikasaddasiddhi daṭṭhabbā. Tattha kammasahajātā punabbhavaṃ deti, kammasahāyabhūtā tadasahajātā punabbhavāya saṃvattati, duvidhāpi punappunaṃ bhave nibbatteti. Tenevāha “punabbhavassa dāyikāpī”tiādi. Ponobbhavikāyevāti nāmaṃ labhatīti punabbhavaṃ dāyikāpi adāyikāpi punabbhavaṃ deticceva ponobbhavikāti samānavipākāti nāmaṃ labhati samānasabhāvattā tadānubhāvattā ca. Evaṃ itaresu daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tattha upadhimhi yathānibbatte attabhāve vipaccanakammaṃ etissāti upadhivepakkā. Nandanaṭṭhena nandī, rañjanaṭṭhena rāgo. Yo ca nandirāgo, yā ca taṇhā, ubhayametaṃ ekatthaṃ, byañjanameva nānanti taṇhā “nandirāgena saddhiṃ atthato ekattaṃ gatā”ti vuttā. Rāgasambandhena “uppannassā”ti vuttaṃ. Rūpārūpabhavarāgo visuṃ vakkhatīti kāmabhave eva bhavapatthanāuppatti vuttāti veditabbā.

203. Having elided the latter word, it is said: ‘The making of renewed existence is renewed existence.’ Here, in ‘Manosamphasso,’ the ending of the first word in ‘o’ should be seen as being like ‘mano.’ Alternatively, because the meaning is understood by the suffix ‘ika’ in the sense of habit, the absence of a word denoting action should be noted, as in ‘one whose habit is eating cakes is a cake-eater.’ Regarding ‘Taddhitā,’ because of the plural indication, or because of the diversity of taddhita suffixes, or because they have the characteristic of naming, the formation of the word ‘ponobbhavika’ should be seen in meanings such as ‘it gives renewed existence.’ Therein, being co-nascent with kamma, it gives renewed existence; being an ally of kamma but not co-nascent with it, it leads to renewed existence. Both produce existence again and again. Therefore he said: ‘also a giver of renewed existence,’ and so on. It is called ‘ponobbhavikā’ itself. Because it gives renewed existence—whether it is a giver or not a giver—it is called ‘ponobbhavikā,’ and it obtains the name ‘having a common result’ on account of its common nature and its influence. Thus it should be seen in the other cases. Therein, ‘upadhivepakkā’ means that for which kamma ripens in the individual existence that has arisen in the substratum. ‘Nandī’ is delight in the sense of enjoying; ‘rāgo’ is passion in the sense of delighting. Both this delight-and-passion and craving have one meaning; only the expression is different. Thus, craving is said to be ‘united in meaning with delight-and-passion.’ In connection with passion, ‘of the arisen’ is said. Because the passion for form and formless existence will be spoken of separately, it should be understood that the arising of the longing for existence is stated here only in the context of the sensual realm.

Tasmiṃ tasmiṃ piyarūpe paṭhamuppattivasena “uppajjatī”ti vuttā, punappunaṃ pavattivasena “nivisatī”ti, pariyuṭṭhānānusayavasena vā uppattinivesā yojetabbā. Sampattiyanti manussasobhagge devatte ca. Attano cakkhunti savatthukaṃ cakkhumāha, sapasādaṃ vā maṃsapiṇḍaṃ. Vippasannapañcapasādanti parisuddhanīlapītalohitakaṇhaodātavaṇṇapasādaṃ. Rajatapanāḷikaṃ viya chiddaṃ abbhantare odātattā. Pāmaṅgasuttaṃ viya lambakaṇṇabaddhaṃ. Tuṅgā uccā dīghā nāsikā tuṅganāsikā, evaṃ laddhavohāraṃ attano ghānaṃ. “Laddhavohārā”ti vā pāṭho. Tasmiṃ sati tuṅgā nāsikā yesaṃ, te tuṅganāsikā. Evaṃ laddhavohārā sattā attano ghānanti yojanā kātabbā. Jivhaṃ…pe… maññanti vaṇṇā saṇṭhānato kiccato ca. Manaṃ…pe… uḷāraṃ maññanti atītādiatthavicinanasamatthaṃ. Attanā paṭiladdhānīti ajjhattañca sarīragandhādīni [M 0.0070] bahiddhā ca vilepanagandhādīni. Uppajjamānā uppajjatīti yadā uppajjamānā hoti, tadā ettha uppajjatīti sāmaññena gahitā uppādakiriyā lakkhaṇabhāvena vuttā, visayavisiṭṭhā lakkhitabbabhāvena. Na hi sāmaññavisesehi nānattavohāro na hotīti. Uppajjamānāti vā anicchito uppādo hetubhāvena vutto. Uppajjatīti nicchito phalabhāvena “yadi uppajjamānā hoti, ettha uppajjatī”ti. So hi tena upayojito viya hoti.

In whatever is pleasing, it is said ‘it arises’ by way of initial arising, and ‘it settles’ by way of repeated occurrence; or the arising and settling should be connected by way of obsession and latent tendency. ‘In attainment’ refers to human beauty and the divine state. ‘One's own eye’ means the eye with its physical basis, or the lump of flesh with its sensitivity. ‘Perfectly clear sensitivity’ refers to the purified sensitivity of blue, yellow, red, black, and white colors. Like a silver tube, it is hollow and white within. Like a pāmaṅga thread, it is hanging, attached to the ear. A ‘high nose’ is a high, elevated, long nose; thus is the conventional term for one's own nose. Alternatively, the reading may be ‘laddhavohārā’ (those who have obtained conventional usage). In that case, ‘tuṅganāsikā’ refers to those who have a high nose. Thus, it should be construed that beings who have obtained this conventional usage refer to their own noses. The tongue... they perceive in terms of color, shape, and function. The mind... they perceive as sublime due to its ability to analyze the meaning of past things, etc. ‘Obtained by oneself’ refers to both internal things like bodily scents and external things like perfumes. ‘Arising, it arises’: when it is in the process of arising, then ‘here it arises’—the action of arising, taken generally, is stated as the characteristic, while that which is distinguished by the object is stated as what is to be characterized. For there is indeed a conventional distinction between the general and the specific. Alternatively, ‘arising’ is the undetermined arising stated as the cause, while ‘it arises’ is the determined arising stated as the effect, as in: ‘if it is arising, here it arises.’ For it is as if employed by that.

Samudayasaccaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the exposition of the truth of arising is concluded.

3. Nirodhasaccaniddesavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Exposition of the Truth of Cessation

204. Anūhateti [V 0.0070] anuddhate, appahīneti attho.

204. ‘Not uprooted’ means uneliminated, the meaning being not abandoned.

Sīho vedhake paṭipajjati, na usumhi, suvāno leḍḍumhi paṭipajjati, na pahārake. Khayagamanavasena virajjati, appavattigamanavasena nirujjhati. Anapekkhatāya cajanavasena hānivasena ca cajīyati, puna yathā na pavattati, tathā dūrakhipanavasena paṭinissajjīyati, bandhanabhūtāya mocanavasena muccati, asaṃkilesavasena na allīyati. Āyūhanaṃ samudayo, tappaṭipakkhavasena anāyūhanaṃ.

A lion attends to the hunter, not to the arrow; a dog attends to a clod, not to the thrower. It fades away through the aspect of dissolution, ceases through the aspect of non-arising. Through detachment, by way of abandonment and decrease, it is relinquished; and it is discarded by way of distant-rejection, so that it does not recur again. It is freed through the aspect of release from what binds; and it does not adhere through the aspect of non-defilement. Accumulation is origination; non-accumulation is its opposing aspect.

Apaññattinti apaññāpanaṃ, “tittaalābu atthī”ti vohārābhāvaṃ vā. Tittaalābuvalliyā appavattiṃ icchanto puriso viya maggo daṭṭhabbo, tassa tassā appavattininnacittassa mūlacchedanaṃ viya maggassa nibbānārammaṇassa taṇhāpahānaṃ. Tadāppavatti viya taṇhāya appavattibhūtaṃ nibbānaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Dutiyūpamāya dakkhiṇadvāraṃ viya nibbānaṃ, coraghātakā viya maggo daṭṭhabbo, purimā vā upamā maggena niruddhāya piyarūpasātarūpesu niruddhāti vattabbatādassanatthaṃ vuttā, pacchimā nibbānaṃ āgamma niruddhāyapi.

'Non-designation' means non-designating, or the absence of the conventional expression, 'there is a bitter gourd.' The path should be regarded like a person who wishes for the non-growth of a bitter gourd vine; just as that person, whose mind is inclined toward its non-growth, cuts its root, so the path, having Nibbāna as its object, is the abandoning of craving. Nibbāna should be regarded as the non-arising of craving, like the non-growth of that vine. In the second simile, Nibbāna is like the southern gate, and the path should be regarded like the executioners of thieves. The former simile was stated to show that craving, being ceased by the path, is ceased in regard to pleasant and delightful forms; the latter shows that it is also ceased by arriving at Nibbāna.

Nirodhasaccaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the exposition of the truth of cessation is concluded.

4. Maggasaccaniddesavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Exposition of the Truth of the Path

205. Aññamaggapaṭikkhepanatthanti [M 0.0071] titthiyehi kappitassa maggassa dukkhanirodhagāminipaṭipadābhāvaṃ paṭikkhepetunti attho, aññassa vā maggabhāvapaṭikkhepo aññamaggapaṭikkhepo. Puggalassa ariyabhāvakarattā ariyaṃ karotīti ariyo, ariyaphalapaṭilābhakarattā ariyaṃ labhāpeti janetīti ariyo. Attano kiccavasena phalavasena ca ariyanāmalābho eva vuttoti daṭṭhabbo. Aṭṭha aṅgāni assāti aññapadatthasamāsaṃ akatvā “aṭṭhaṅgāni assa santīti aṭṭhaṅgiko”ti padasiddhi daṭṭhabbā.

205. 'For the purpose of rejecting other paths' means to reject the path devised by sectarians on account of its not being the practice leading to the cessation of suffering; this is the meaning. Or, the rejection of another's state of being a path is the rejection of other paths. Because it makes a person noble, it is called noble (ariya); because it causes the attainment of noble fruits, it is called noble (ariya). It should be understood that the name 'noble' is thus obtained on account of its function and its fruit. The derivation of the word should be understood as follows: without forming a compound implying another word's meaning, the word `aṭṭhaṅgiko` is formed from the phrase 'possessing eight factors'.

Caturaṅgasamannāgatā [V 0.0071] vācā janaṃ saṅgaṇhātīti tabbipakkhaviratisabhāvā sammāvācā bhedakaramicchāvācāpahānena jane sampayutte ca pariggaṇhanakiccavatī hotīti “pariggahalakkhaṇā”ti vuttā. Yathā cīvarakammādiko kammanto ekaṃ kātabbaṃ samuṭṭhāpeti nipphādeti, taṃtaṃkiriyānipphādako vā cetanāsaṅkhāto kammanto hatthapādacalanādikaṃ kiriyaṃ samuṭṭhāpeti, evaṃ sāvajjakattabbakiriyāsamuṭṭhāpakamicchākammantappahānena sammākammanto niravajjasamuṭṭhāpanakiccavā hoti, sampayuttadhamme ca samuṭṭhāpento eva pavattatīti “samuṭṭhāpanalakkhaṇo”ti vutto. Kāyavācānaṃ khandhasantānassa ca saṃkilesabhūtamicchāājīvappahānena sammāājīvo “vodāpanalakkhaṇo”ti vutto.

Speech endowed with four factors gathers people together; thus, right speech, which has the nature of abstaining from its opposite, by abandoning divisive wrong speech has the function of embracing people and associated states; hence, it is said to be 'characterized by inclusion.' Just as a task like robe-making establishes and accomplishes what is to be done, or just as intention, known as 'action,' being the producer of various activities, establishes actions like moving the hands and feet, so too, right action, by abandoning wrong action that produces blameworthy activities, has the function of establishing what is blameless, and it proceeds by establishing associated states—hence it is called 'characterized by production.' Right livelihood, by abandoning wrong livelihood that is a defilement of body, speech, and the continuum of aggregates, is called 'characterized by purification.'

Attano paccanīkakilesā diṭṭhekaṭṭhā avijjādayo. Passatīti pakāsetīti attho. Teneva hi aṅgena tattha paccavekkhaṇā pavattatīti. Tathevāti attano paccanīkakilesehi saddhinti attho.

One's own opposing defilements, headed by ignorance, have wrong view as their single foundation. 'Passati' means 'illuminates'; this is the meaning. Indeed, it is by that very factor that reflection proceeds. 'Tatheva' means 'together with one's own opposing defilements.'

Kiccatoti pubbabhāgehi dukkhādiñāṇehi kattabbakiccassa idha nipphattito, imasseva vā ñāṇassa dukkhādippakāsanakiccato. Tīṇi nāmāni labhati kāmasaṅkappādippahānakiccanipphattito. Sikkhāpadavibhaṅge (vibha. 703 ādayo) “viraticetanā sabbe sampayuttadhammā ca sikkhāpadānī”ti vuttāti tattha padhānānaṃ viraticetanānaṃ vasena “viratiyopi honti cetanāyopī”ti āha. Musāvādādīhi viramaṇakāle vā viratiyo subhāsitādivācābhāsanādikāle ca cetanāyo yojetabbā, maggakkhaṇe viratiyova [M 0.0072] cetanānaṃ amaggaṅgattā ekassa ñāṇassa dukkhādiñāṇatā viya ekāya viratiyā musāvādādiviratibhāvo viya ca ekāya cetanāya sammāvācādikiccattayasādhanasabhāvābhāvā sammāvācādibhāvāsiddhito, taṃsiddhiyañca aṅgattayattāsiddhito ca.

'From the function' refers to the accomplishment here of the duty to be done by the knowledge of suffering etc. in the preliminary stage, or from the function of this very knowledge in revealing suffering etc. It obtains three names due to the accomplishment of the duty of abandoning sensual thoughts etc. In the analysis of the training rules (Vibhaṅga 703 onwards), it is said, 'Abstentions, intentions, and all associated states are the training rules.' There, on account of the predominance of abstentions and intentions, it is stated, 'They are both abstentions and intentions.' Abstentions should be applied at the time of refraining from false speech etc., and intentions at the time of speaking well-spoken words etc. At the moment of the path, there are only abstentions, as intentions are not path factors. Just as a single knowledge has the nature of being the knowledge of suffering etc., and a single abstention has the nature of being the abstention from false speech etc., so too, because a single intention lacks the nature of accomplishing the threefold function of right speech etc., the state of being right speech etc. is not established; and because that is not established, the threefold nature of the factors is not established.

Pubbabhāgepi maggakkhaṇepi sammāsamādhi evāti yadipi samādhiupakārakānaṃ abhiniropanānumajjanasampiyāyanabrūhanasantasukhānaṃ vitakkādīnaṃ vasena catūhi jhānehi sammāsamādhi vibhatto, tathāpi vāyāmo viya anuppannākusalānuppādanādicatuvāyāmakiccaṃ, sati viya ca asubhāsukhāniccānattesu kāyādīsu subhādisaññāpahānacatusatikiccaṃ, eko samādhi catukkajjhānasamādhikiccaṃ na sādhetīti pubbabhāgepi paṭhamajjhānasamādhicitte jhānasamādhi [V 0.0072] paṭhamajjhānasamādhi eva maggakkhaṇepi, tathā pubbabhāgepi catutthajjhānasamādhicitte jhānasamādhi catutthajjhānasamādhi eva maggakkhaṇepīti attho.

Even in the preliminary stage and at the moment of the path, right concentration is just so. That is, although right concentration is distinguished through the four jhānas by means of thought etc.—which are auxiliary to concentration, such as fixing, stroking, delighting, nourishing, and peaceful happiness—still, just as effort has the fourfold task of preventing the arising of unarisen unwholesome states etc., and mindfulness has the fourfold task of abandoning perceptions of beauty etc. in the body etc., which are foul, unpleasant, impermanent, and not-self, a single concentration does not accomplish the task of the fourfold jhāna concentration. Thus, in the preliminary stage, in the mind of first jhāna concentration, the jhāna concentration is simply first jhāna concentration, and likewise at the moment of the path. Similarly, in the preliminary stage, in the mind of fourth jhāna concentration, the jhāna concentration is simply fourth jhāna concentration, and likewise at the moment of the path. This is the meaning.

Vacībhedassa upakārako vitakko sāvajjānavajjavacībhedanivattanapavattanakarāya sammāvācāyapi upakārako evāti “svāya”ntiādimāha. Vacībhedaniyāmikā vācā kāyikakiriyāniyāmakassa sammākammantassa upakārikā. Idaṃ vīriyanti catusammappadhānavīriyaṃ. Gatiyoti nipphattiyo, kiccādisabhāve vā. Samanvesitvāti upadhāretvā.

The thought (vitakka) that aids in verbal expression is also beneficial for right speech, which causes the turning away from and turning toward blameworthy and blameless verbal expression; thus, it is said, 'this very one,' and so forth. Speech that determines verbal expression is helpful to right action, which determines bodily action. 'This is the effort' refers to the effort of the four right exertions. 'Gatiyo' means accomplishments, or the nature of function and so on. 'Samanvesitvā' means having ascertained.

Purimāni dve saccāni uggaṇhitvāti sambandho. Iṭṭhaṃ kantanti nirodhamaggesu ninnabhāvaṃ dasseti, na abhinandanaṃ, tanninnabhāvoyeva ca tattha kammakaraṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

'Having learned the first two truths' is the connection. 'Desirable, pleasing'—this shows inclination toward cessation and the path, not rejoicing; and that very inclination should be seen there as the performance of the action.

Kiccatoti pariññādito. Ārammaṇapaṭivedhoti sacchikiriyāpaṭivedhamāha. Sabbampi paṭivedhañāṇaṃ lokuttaranti kasmā vuttaṃ, nanu uggahādipaṭivedho ca paṭivedhova, na ca so lokuttaroti? Na, kevalena paṭivedha-saddena uggahādipaṭivedhānaṃ avacanīyattā, paṭivedhanimittattā vā uggahādivasena pavattaṃ dukkhādīsu pubbabhāge ñāṇaṃ “paṭivedho”ti vuttaṃ, na paṭivedhattā, paṭivedhabhūtameva pana ñāṇaṃ sandhāyāha “sabbampi paṭivedhañāṇaṃ lokuttara”nti. Uggahaparipucchāñāṇānipi savanañāṇe eva avarodhaṃ gacchantīti “savanadhāraṇasammasanañāṇaṃ lokiya”nti tividhameva ñāṇamāha. Uggahādīhi saccapariggaṇhanaṃ pariggaho.

'From the function' means by way of full understanding, etc. 'Realization of the object' refers to the realization that is direct experience. Why is it said that all knowledge of realization is supramundane? Is not the realization through initial grasping, etc., also a realization, and yet not supramundane? No, because the term 'realization' alone does not refer to the realization through initial grasping etc., or because the knowledge arising in the preliminary stage regarding suffering etc., which occurs by way of initial grasping etc., is called 'realization' due to being a cause for realization, not because it is realization itself. However, the actual knowledge that is realization is indeed meant when it is said, 'All knowledge of realization is supramundane.' The knowledges of initial grasping and questioning also fall under the knowledge of listening, so it is said, 'The knowledges of listening, retention, and examination are mundane.' Thus, only these three types of knowledge are mentioned. The grasping of the truths by means of initial grasping, etc., is 'grasping'.

Payogoti [M 0.0073] kiriyā, vāyāmo vā. Tassa mahantatarassa icchitabbataṃ dukkarataratañca upamāhi dasseti “bhavaggagahaṇattha”ntiādinā.

'Payogo' means action, or effort. Its greater desirability and greater difficulty are shown by similes such as 'for the sake of grasping the peak of existence,' etc.

Padaghātanti ettha gatamaggo “pada”nti vuccati. Yena cupāyena kāraṇena kāmavitakko uppajjati, so tassa gatamaggoti tassa ghāto padaghāto. Ussukkāpetvāti uddhaṃ uddhaṃ santivisesayuttaṃ katvā, vaḍḍhetvāti attho.

'Padaghātaṃ': here, the trodden path is called 'pada.' The means or cause by which sensual thought arises is its trodden path, and the striking down of that is 'padaghāta.' 'Ussukkāpetvā' means having made it higher and higher, endowed with special peace; 'having increased it' is the meaning.

Pāḷiyaṃ vibhattesūti katarapāḷiyaṃ? Dhammasaṅgahe tāva aṭṭha kasiṇāni dasa asubhā cattāro brahmavihārā cattāri āruppāni vibhattāni, āgamesu dasa anussatiyo āhāre paṭikūlasaññā [V 0.0073] catudhātuvavatthānanti imāni cāti tattha tattha vibhattaṃ. Imesu tīsūti kāmādīsu tīsu ṭhānesu.

'In the Pāḷi where they are classified'—in which Pāḷi? First, in the Dhammasaṅgaha, eight kasiṇas, ten foulness meditations, four divine abodes, and four formless attainments are classified. In the Āgamas, the ten recollections, the perception of repulsiveness in food, and the analysis of the four elements are also classified here and there. 'Among these three' (`imesu tīsu`) refers to the three spheres, beginning with the sensual sphere.

Micchāvācāsaṅkhātāyāti etena ekāya cetanāya pahātabbaekattaṃ dasseti. Idha ariyasāvako sakalyāṇaputhujjanako sekkho. Kāyadvāravītikkamāti ājīvahetukato pāṇātipātādito visuṃ visuṃ viramaṇaṃ yojetabbaṃ.

"Designated as wrong speech" indicates that the entirety of wrong speech is to be abandoned by a single intention. Here, the noble disciple, the virtuous ordinary person, and the trainee are meant. "Transgression through the body-door" refers to abstaining separately from transgressions such as killing, etc., committed for the sake of livelihood.

Ayaṃ panassāti maggabhāvena catubbidhampi ekattena gahetvā assa maggassa ayaṃ jhānavasena sabbasadisasabbāsadisaekaccasadisatā viseso. Pādakajjhānaniyāmena hotīti idha pādakajjhānaniyāmaṃ dhuraṃ katvā āha, aṭṭhasāliniyaṃ pana vipassanāniyāmaṃ tattha sabbavādāvirodhato, idha pana sammasitajjhānapuggalajjhāsayavādanivattanato pādakajjhānaniyāmaṃ. Vipassanāniyāmo pana sādhāraṇattā idhāpi na paṭikkhittoti daṭṭhabbo. Aññe cācariyavādā vakkhamānā vibhajitabbāti yathāvuttameva tāva pādakajjhānaniyāmaṃ vibhajanto āha “pādakajjhānaniyāmena tāvā”ti.

"This of his" means, taking even the fourfold path as one by way of the path, this path has distinctions based on jhāna, such as being similar to all, dissimilar to all, or similar to some. "It is by the principle of the base jhāna": here, the principle of the base jhāna is taken as the main point. In the Aṭṭhasālinī, however, the principle is insight, since there is no contradiction with any doctrine; here, however, the principle is the base jhāna, because it refutes the doctrines concerning the inclinations of individuals who have attained jhāna through reflection. But the principle of insight, being common, should be seen as not rejected here either. Other teachers' doctrines, to be discussed later, should be analyzed. Thus, analyzing the principle of the base jhāna as stated above, it is said, "By the principle of the base jhāna, first..."

Āruppe catukkapañcaka…pe… vuttaṃ aṭṭhasāliniyanti adhippāyo. Nanu tattha “āruppe tikacatukkajjhānaṃ uppajjatī”ti vuttaṃ, na “catukkapañcakajjhāna”nti? Saccaṃ, yesu pana saṃsayo atthi, tesaṃ uppattidassanena, tenatthato catukkapañcakajjhānaṃ uppajjatīti vuttameva hotīti evamāhāti veditabbaṃ. Samudāyañca apekkhitvā “tañca lokuttaraṃ, na lokiya”nti āha. Catutthajjhānameva hi lokiyaṃ tattha uppajjati, na catukkaṃ pañcakañcāti. Ettha [M 0.0074] kathanti pādakajjhānassa abhāvā kathaṃ daṭṭhabbanti attho. Taṃjhānikāva tassa tattha tayo maggā uppajjanti tajjhānikaṃ paṭhamaphalādiṃ pādakaṃ katvā uparimaggabhāvanāyāti adhippāyo, tikacatukkajjhānikaṃ pana maggaṃ bhāvetvā tatthuppannassa arūpajjhānaṃ tajjhānikaṃ phalañca pādakaṃ katvā uparimaggabhāvanāya aññajhānikāpi uppajjantīti jhānaṅgādiniyāmikā pubbābhisaṅkhārasamāpatti pādakaṃ, na sammasitabbāti phalassapi pādakatā daṭṭhabbā.

"In the immaterial realms, the fourfold and fivefold..." and so on is the meaning, as stated in the Aṭṭhasālinī. But is it not said there that “the threefold and fourfold jhāna arises in the immaterial realm,” not the “fourfold and fivefold jhāna”? True, but for those in whom there is doubt, by showing the arising, it is thereby in meaning said that the fourfold and fivefold jhāna arises—this is how it should be understood. And considering the aggregate, it is said, “That is supramundane, not mundane.” For there, only the fourth jhāna arises mundanely, not the fourfold or the fivefold. "Here, how?" means: since the base jhāna is absent, how should it be understood? The meaning is that for one of that jhāna, the three paths arise there, having made the first fruition and so on pertaining to that jhāna the base for the development of the higher paths. But for one who has arisen there after developing a path pertaining to the threefold and fourfold jhāna, having made the immaterial jhāna and the fruition pertaining to that jhāna the base for the development of a higher path, paths pertaining to other jhānas also arise. The attainment based on prior volitional formations, determined by the jhāna factors and so on, is the base, not the object of contemplation; thus, the nature of fruition as a base should also be seen.

Dukkhañāṇādīnaṃ rūpādichaḷārammaṇattā nekkhammasaṅkappādīnaṃ kasiṇāditaṃtaṃkusalārammaṇārammaṇattā [V 0.0074] sammāvācādīnaṃ aṅgānaṃ taṃtaṃviramitabbādiārammaṇattā “yathānurūpa”nti āha. Tadanurūpoti avippaṭisārakarasīlaṃ vāyāmassa visesapaccayoti sīlānurūpatā vāyāmassa vuttā sampayuttassapi, sampayuttasseva ca vacanato “sīlabhūmiyaṃ patiṭṭhitassā”ti avatvā “patiṭṭhamānassā”ti vuttaṃ. Cetaso asammosoti “ekārakkho”ti ettha vuttena satārakkhena cetaso rakkhitatā. Tenāha “iti…pe… suvihitacittārakkhassā”ti.

Because the knowledge of suffering and so on has the six objects beginning with form as its object, because the thoughts of renunciation and so on have the respective wholesome objects such as the kasiṇas as their object, and because the factors beginning with right speech have their respective objects to be abstained from and so on as their object, it is said, "according to what is appropriate." "Appropriate to that" means that virtue which causes no regret is a special condition for effort; thus the appropriateness of virtue for effort is stated, even for that which is associated. And precisely because it is associated, instead of saying "for one established in the foundation of virtue," it is said "for one who is being established." "Non-confusion of mind" means the protection of the mind by the guard of mindfulness, which is called 'the one guard' here. Therefore, it is said, "thus... to one whose mind is well-guarded."

Āsavakkhayañāṇassa vijjābhāvo vuttoti āsavakkhayasaṅkhāte magge tīhi khandhehi saṅgahite paññākkhandho vijjā, sīlassa catunnañca jhānānaṃ caraṇabhāvo vuttoti itare dve khandhā caraṇaṃ. Yanti etena nibbānaṃ gacchantīti yānaṃ, vipassanāva yānaṃ vipassanāyānaṃ. Sīlaṃ samādhissa visesapaccayo, samādhi vipassanāyāti samathassa upakārattā sīlakkhandho ca samathayānena saṅgahito. Vipassanāyānena kāmesu ādīnavaṃ vibhāvento samathayānena nirāmisaṃ jhānasukhaṃ apariccajanto antadvayakummaggaṃ vivajjeti. Paññā viya mohassa, sīlasamādhayo ca dosalobhānaṃ ujuvipaccanīkā adosālobhehi sādhetabbattā. Sīlasamādhipaññāyogato ādimajjhapariyosānakalyāṇaṃ. Sīlādīni hi sāsanassa ādimajjhapariyosānanti. Yasmiṃ ṭhito maggaṭṭho phalaṭṭho ca ariyo hoti, taṃ maggaphalasaṅkhātaṃ khandhattayasaṅgahitaṃ sāsanaṃ ariyabhūmi.

Because the knowledge of the destruction of the taints is said to be knowledge, in the path designated as the destruction of the taints, which is comprised of three aggregates, the aggregate of wisdom is knowledge. Because virtue and the four jhānas are said to be conduct, the other two aggregates are conduct. 'One goes by this, one proceeds to Nibbāna,' thus it is a vehicle; insight itself is the vehicle, the vehicle of insight. Virtue is a special condition for concentration, and concentration for insight; thus, because of its supportiveness to serenity, the aggregate of virtue is also included in the vehicle of serenity. By the vehicle of insight, one discerns the danger in sensual pleasures, and by the vehicle of serenity, one does not abandon the unworldly bliss of jhāna, thus avoiding the wrong path of the two extremes. Just as wisdom is the direct opposite of delusion, so too are virtue and concentration the direct opposites of hatred and greed, because they are to be accomplished by non-hatred and non-greed. From the union of virtue, concentration, and wisdom, it is good in the beginning, middle, and end. For virtue and so on are the beginning, middle, and end of the teaching. Established in which, one on the path and one in the fruit becomes a noble one; that teaching, comprised of the three aggregates designated as path and fruit, is the noble ground.

Maggasaccaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Truth of the Path is concluded.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Suttanta Division is concluded.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Abhidhamma Division

206-214. Ariyasacca-saddo [M 0.0075] samudaye vattamāno pariññeyyabhāvarahite ekantapahātabbe taṇhāsaṅkhāte samudaye pavattati, na pahātabbapariññeyyesu avasesakilesāvasesākusalesu appahātabbesu ca sāsavakusalamūlāvasesasāsavakusalesūti sappadeso tattha samudayo hoti, kevalaṃ saccasadde nippadesoti āha “nippadesato samudayaṃ dassetu”nti. Dukkhanirodhā pana ariyasaccadesanāyaṃ dhammato nippadesā eva. Na hi tato añño dhammo atthi, yo saccadesanāyaṃ [V 0.0075] dukkhaṃ nirodhoti ca vattabbo siyā, maggopi aṭṭhaṅgikapañcaṅgikavāresu apubbo natthi, tasmā samudayameva “nippadesato dassetu”nti vadati tassa sabbattha tīsupi vāresu apubbassa dassitattā. Apubbasamudayadassanatthāyapi hi saccadesanāyaṃ “tattha katamo dukkhasamudayo? Taṇhā”ti vacanaṃ kevalāya taṇhāya sacca-saddassa pavattidassanatthanti. Desanāvasena pana taṃ taṃ samudayaṃ ṭhapetvā dukkhaṃ tassa tassa pahānavasena nirodho aṭṭhaṅgikapañcaṅgikasabbalokuttarakusalavasena maggo ca ariyasaccadesanāyaṃ na vuttoti dukkhādīni ca tattha sappadesāni dassitāni hontīti tāni ca nippadesāni dassetuṃ saccadesanā vuttāti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Paccayasaṅkhātanti kammakilesavasena jātiādidukkhassa mūlabhūtanti attho.

206-214. When the term "noble truth" refers to the origin, it applies to craving alone, which is designated as the origin, to be utterly abandoned and devoid of the characteristic of being fully comprehended. It does not apply to the remaining defilements and unwholesome states, which are to be abandoned and fully comprehended, nor to what should not be abandoned, such as the remaining wholesome roots with taints or wholesome states with taints. Thus, the origin is specifically indicated in that context; in the term "truth" alone, it is without specific indication. Hence, it is said, "to show the origin without specific indication." However, in the teaching of the noble truths, the cessation of suffering is by its nature indeed without specific indication, for there is no other phenomenon that could be called the cessation of suffering in the teaching of the truths. The path, too, in its eightfold and fivefold versions, is not unprecedented. Therefore, only of the origin is it said "to show without specific indication," because it is shown as unprecedented in all three instances. Indeed, in the teaching of the truths, the statement, "What is the origin of suffering? Craving," is for the purpose of showing that the term "truth" applies to craving alone. However, it is fitting to say that the teaching of the truths is stated in order to show these others without specific indication as well, for in the teaching of the noble truths, suffering, cessation (as the abandoning of each respective cause), and the path (in its eightfold, fivefold, and all supramundane wholesome aspects) are not fully stated apart from each respective origin, and thus suffering and the others are shown there with specific indication. The term "designated as condition" means that it is the root of suffering such as birth, in terms of kamma and defilements.

Nirodhasaccaṃ…pe… pañcahākārehi niddiṭṭhanti ariyasaccadesanato saccadesanāya visesaṃ dasseti. Tattha “tiṇṇannañca kusalamūlānaṃ avasesānañca sāsavakusalānaṃ pahāna”nti idaṃ tesaṃ paccayānaṃ avijjātaṇhāupādānānaṃ pahānavasena, avijjādīsu vā pahīnesu tesaṃ appavattivasena vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Na hi kusalā pahātabbāti. Pahānanti ca maggakiccavasena tadadhigamanīyaṃ nirodhaṃ dasseti, nirodhasseva vā taṇhādīnaṃ appavattibhāvo pahānanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

"The truth of cessation... is explained in five ways" shows the distinction of the teaching of the truths from the teaching of the noble truths. Herein, "the abandoning of the three wholesome roots and the remaining wholesome states with taints" should be understood as stated through the abandoning of their conditions—ignorance, craving, and clinging—or, because when ignorance and the rest are abandoned, these do not occur. For wholesome states are not to be abandoned. "Abandoning" indicates the cessation to be attained thereby, through the function of the path; or, the non-occurrence of craving and the like, which is cessation itself, should be seen as "abandoning."

Yadipi “pubbeva kho panassa kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ ājīvo suparisuddho hoti, evamassāyaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchatī”ti (ma. ni. 3.431) lokuttaramaggakkhaṇe aṭṭhaṅgikamaggapāripūriyā upanissayadassanatthaṃ idaṃ [M 0.0076] vuttaṃ, tathāpi “pubbeva kho panā”ti vacanaṃ kāyakammādisuddhiyā dūratarupanissayataṃ, cakkhādīsu asārajjantassa asaṃyuttassa asammūḷhassa ādīnavānupassino viharato tāyeva vuṭṭhānagāminiyā vipassanāya āyatiṃ pañcupādānakkhandhesu apacayaṃ gacchantesu sabbasaṅkhāresu vivaṭṭanavasena, ponobbhavikataṇhāya pahīyamānāya kilesadūrībhāvena, kāyikacetasikadarathasantāpapariḷāhesu pahīyamānesu passaddhakāyacittavasena kāyikacetasikasukhe paṭisaṃvediyamāne “yā tathābhūtassa diṭṭhi, sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhī”tiādinā (ma. ni. 3.431) vuttānaṃ vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanākkhaṇe pavattānaṃ pañcannaṃ sammādiṭṭhādīnaṃ aṅgānaṃ āsannatarupanissayatañca dassetīti āsannatarupanissayavasena pañcaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ sukhaṃ bujjhantānaṃ puggalānaṃ ajjhāsayavasena [V 0.0076] pañcaṅgikamaggadesanāya pavattataṃ dīpeti. Tenāha “pubbeva kho…pe… suparisuddho hotīti vacanato”tiādi. Evamidaṃ vacanatoti nissakkavacanaṃ desanupāyassa ñāpakanidassanaṃ hoti, vacanatoti vā attano vacanānurūpaṃ pañcaṅgikopi maggo paṭipadā evāti bhagavatā desitoti attho. Katthāti? Devapure, tasmā taṃ desitanayaṃ dassetuṃ pañcaṅgikavāropi niddiṭṭho dhammasaṅgāhakehi. Atha vā “pubbeva kho panassā”ti vacaneneva ajjhāsayavisesakāraṇanidassakena puggalajjhāsayavasena pañcaṅgiko maggopi paṭipadā evāti desito hotīti āha “pubbeva kho pana…pe… vacanato pana…pe… desito”ti, tasmā taṃ suttante desitanayaṃ dassetuṃ pañcaṅgikavāropi niddiṭṭho bhagavatā devapureti attho.

Even though it is said, “Moreover, his bodily action, verbal action, and livelihood were already well purified beforehand, and thus this Noble Eightfold Path reaches fulfillment in development” (MN 3.431) to show the supporting condition for the fulfillment of the eightfold path at the moment of the supramundane path, nevertheless, the statement “moreover, beforehand” indicates that the purification of bodily action and so on is a more distant supporting condition. For one who dwells uninfatuated, unattached, and unconfused in regard to the eye and so on, seeing the dangers, through that very insight leading to emergence—as the future five aggregates subject to clinging proceed toward diminishment—by way of turning away from all conditioned things, with the abandoning of craving leading to renewed existence, through the distancing of defilements, with the abandoning of bodily and mental distress, affliction, and fever, by way of a tranquil body and mind, experiencing bodily and mental happiness—then, “the view of one who has become thus is his right view,” and so on (MN 3.431). This shows the nearer supporting condition for the five factors of right view and so on, which arise at the moment of insight leading to emergence. Thus, it reveals that the teaching of the fivefold path is presented in accordance with the inclination of individuals who easily awaken through this nearer supporting condition. Therefore, it is said, “By the statement ‘moreover, beforehand… was well purified’…” and so on. Thus, this statement is a conclusive statement, an illustrative indication of the teaching method. Or, by the word 'statement' (vacanato), the meaning is that the fivefold path is also indeed the practice taught by the Blessed One in accordance with his own words. Where? In Devapura. Therefore, to demonstrate that taught method, the section on the fivefold path was also specified by the compilers of the Dhamma. Or, by the phrase “moreover, beforehand” itself, which indicates the cause of the special inclination, it is shown that the fivefold path is indeed taught as the practice in accordance with the inclinations of individuals. Hence, it is said, “Moreover, beforehand… by the statement… it is taught.” Therefore, to demonstrate that method taught in the Sutta, the section on the fivefold path was also specified by the Blessed One in Devapura—this is the meaning.

Jhānehi desanāpaveso, bhāvanāpaveso vā jhānābhiniveso. Ekekasmiṃ koṭṭhāse catunnaṃ catunnaṃ nayasahassānaṃ dassanaṃ gaṇanāsukhatthanti veditabbaṃ. Yathā pana pāḷi ṭhitā, tathā ekekissā paṭipadāya suññatādīsu ca pañca pañca koṭṭhāse yojetvā pāḷigamanaṃ katanti viññāyati. Tattha aṭṭhaṅgikavāre dutiyajjhānādīsu tasmiṃ samaye sattaṅgiko maggo hotīti yojanā kātabbā, sabbasaṅgāhikavāre ca yathā vijjamānadhammavasenāti.

Entry into the teaching by means of the jhānas, or entry into development by means of the jhānas, is immersion in jhāna. It should be understood that in each section, the presentation of four thousand methods each is for the sake of ease in enumeration. However, as the Pāli stands, it is understood that for each practice, the Pāli text proceeds by applying five sections each to emptiness and so on. Therein, in the section on the eightfold path, regarding the second jhāna and so on, the application should be made that at that time the path is sevenfold. And in the all-inclusive section, it is according to the existing phenomena.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Abhidhamma division is concluded.

3. Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā

3. Exposition on the Questioner

215. Evaṃ [M 0.0077] purimesupi dvīsūti kasmā vuttaṃ, nanu suttantabhājanīye dukkhanirodhagāminipaṭipadāniddese lokiyalokuttaramissako maggo vutto. Tassa hi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (vibha. aṭṭha. 205) “catūsu saccesu uggahādivasena pubbabhāgañāṇuppattiṃ sandhāya idaṃ ‘dukkhe ñāṇa’ntiādi vuttaṃ, paṭivedhakkhaṇe pana ekameva ñāṇaṃ hotī”ti sammādiṭṭhiyā, tathā sammāsaṅkappādīnañca lokiyalokuttaramissakatā dassitā “apicesā sammādiṭṭhi nāma pubbabhāge nānākkhaṇā nānārammaṇā hoti, maggakkhaṇe ekakkhaṇā ekārammaṇā”tiādinā cāti? Saccametaṃ, evaṃ pana āgamanavasena tatthāpi catusaccakammaṭṭhānadassanādimukhena ariyova [V 0.0077] aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo dassito. Evañca katvā “paṭivedhakkhaṇe pana ekameva ñāṇaṃ hotī”ti maggañāṇassa ekasseva dukkhañāṇāditā, “maggakkhaṇe pana…pe… ekova kusalasaṅkappo uppajjati, ayaṃ sammāsaṅkappo nāmā”tiādinā maggasaṅkappādīnaṃ sammāsaṅkappāditā ca niddhāritā, pāḷiyañca aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ uddisitvā tameva niddisituṃ “dukkhe ñāṇa”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tena suttantabhājanīyepi dvinnaṃ lokiyatā, dvinnaṃ lokuttaratā vuttā “evaṃ purimesupi dvīsūti etenāti.

215. Why is it said, 'Thus, in the previous two as well'? Is it not the case that in the Suttanta division, in the exposition of the path leading to the cessation of suffering, a path mixed with the mundane and supramundane is stated? For in its commentary (Vibhaṅga Aṭṭhakathā 205), it is said, 'With regard to the four truths, referring to the arising of knowledge in the preliminary stage by way of grasping, etc., this is called “knowledge of suffering,” etc., but at the moment of penetration, there is only one knowledge.' Similarly, the state of right view, and right intention, etc., being mixed with the mundane and supramundane is shown: 'Moreover, this right view, in the preliminary stage, has diverse moments and diverse objects, but at the path moment, it is single in moment and single in object,' and so on. This is true. However, according to the tradition, there too, the noble eightfold path is shown through the means of demonstrating the meditation subject of the four truths, and so on. And having done so, the state of the single path knowledge as the knowledge of suffering, etc., is determined by the statement, 'At the moment of penetration, however, there is only one knowledge.' And the state of the path-intentions and so on as right intention and so on is determined by the statement, 'At the path moment… only one wholesome intention arises—this is called right intention,' and so on. And in the Pāli, after stating the eightfold path in brief, 'knowledge of suffering,' and so on is stated to explain that very path in detail. Therefore, by this statement, 'thus, in the previous two as well,' it is said that in the Suttanta division also, the mundaneness of two and the supramundaneness of two are stated.

Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition on the Questioner is concluded.

Saccavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of the Truths is concluded.

5. Indriyavibhaṅgo

5. The Analysis of the Faculties

1. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Abhidhamma Division

219. Cakkhudvāre [M 0.0078][V 0.0078] indaṭṭhaṃ kāretīti cakkhudvārabhāve taṃdvārikehi attano indabhāvaṃ paramissarabhāvaṃ kārayatīti attho. Tañhi te rūpaggahaṇe attānaṃ anuvatteti, te ca taṃ anuvattantīti. Esa nayo itaresupi. Yena taṃsamaṅgīpuggalo taṃsampayuttadhammā vā aññātāvino honti, so aññātāvibhāvo pariniṭṭhitakiccajānanaṃ.

219. 'It exercises its faculty-function in the eye-door' means that, in its state as the eye-door, it causes its own lordly nature, its supreme authority, to be exercised by those phenomena associated with that door. For it makes them conform to itself in the grasping of forms, and they conform to it. This is the method for the others as well. That by which a person endowed with it, or the phenomena associated with it, becomes a knower of what was not known, that state of being a knower of what was not known is the knowing whose task is completed.

Katthaci dveti “dvinnaṃ kho, bhikkhave, indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu aññaṃ byākaroti…pe… ariyāya ca paññāya ariyāya ca vimuttiyā. Yā hissa, bhikkhave, ariyā paññā, tadassa paññindriyaṃ. Yā hissa ariyā vimutti, tadassa samādhindriya”ntiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 5.516) dve, “tiṇṇaṃ kho, bhikkhave, indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā piṇḍolabhāradvājena bhikkhunā aññā byākatā…pe… satindriyassa samādhindriyassa paññindriyassā”ti (saṃ. ni. 5.519), “tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni tīṇi? Anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ aññindriyaṃ aññātāvindriya”nti (saṃ. ni. 5.493), “tīṇimāni…pe… itthindriyaṃ purisindriyaṃ jīvitindriya”nti (saṃ. ni. 5.492) ca evamādīsu tīṇi, “pañcimāni, brāhmaṇa, indriyāni nānāvisayāni…pe… cakkhundriyaṃ…pe… kāyindriya”nti (saṃ. ni. 5.512), “pañci…pe… sukhindriyaṃ…pe… upekkhindriya”nti (saṃ. ni. 5.501 ādayo), “pañci…pe… saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriya”nti (saṃ. ni. 5.486 ādayo) ca evamādīsu pañca. Tattha suttante dukādivacanaṃ nissaraṇupāyādibhāvato dukādīnaṃ. Sabbāni pana [V 0.0079] indriyāni abhiññeyyāni, abhiññeyyadhammadesanā ca abhidhammoti idha sabbāni ekato vuttāni.

In some places, two are mentioned, as in: “Monks, it is through having developed and cultivated two faculties that a monk who is an arahant declares final knowledge… through noble wisdom and noble liberation. For him, monks, that noble wisdom is the faculty of wisdom. That noble liberation is the faculty of concentration,” and so on (SN 5.516). In other places, three are mentioned, as in: “Monks, it is through having developed and cultivated three faculties that the monk Piṇḍolabhāradvāja declared final knowledge… the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom” (SN 5.519); and “Monks, there are these three faculties. Which three? The faculty of ‘I shall come to know the unknown,’ the faculty of final knowledge, and the faculty of one who has final knowledge” (SN 5.493); and “Monks, there are these three… the female faculty, the male faculty, and the life faculty” (SN 5.492). In other places, five are mentioned, as in: “Brahmin, there are these five faculties with different domains… the eye faculty… the body faculty” (SN 5.512); and “There are five… the faculty of pleasure… the faculty of equanimity” (SN 5.501); and “There are five… the faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom” (SN 5.486). Therein, in the Suttas, the mention of pairs, triads, and so on is because these pairs, etc., are the means of escape, and so on. However, all faculties are to be directly known, and the teaching of phenomena to be directly known is the Abhidhamma; therefore, here all are stated together.

Khīṇāsavassa bhāvabhūto hutvā uppattito “khīṇāsavasseva uppajjanato”ti vuttaṃ.

It is said, 'because it arises only in one whose taints are destroyed,' for it arises having become the very state of one whose taints are destroyed.

Liṅgeti gameti ñāpetīti liṅgaṃ, liṅgīyati vā etenāti liṅgaṃ, kiṃ liṅgeti, kiñca vā liṅgīyatīti? Indaṃ indo vā, indassa liṅgaṃ indaliṅgaṃ, indaliṅgassa attho taṃsabhāvo indaliṅgaṭṭho, indaliṅgameva vā [M 0.0079] indriya-saddassa attho indaliṅgaṭṭho. Sajjitaṃ uppāditanti siṭṭhaṃ, indena siṭṭhaṃ indasiṭṭhaṃ. Juṭṭhaṃ sevitaṃ. Kammasaṅkhātassa indassa liṅgāni, tena ca siṭṭhānīti kammajāneva yojetabbāni, na aññāni. Te ca dve atthā kamme eva yojetabbā, itare ca bhagavati evāti “yathāyoga”nti āha. Tenāti bhagavato kammassa ca indattā. Etthāti etesu indriyesu. Ulliṅgenti pakāsenti phalasampattivipattīhi kāraṇasampattivipattiavabodhato. “So taṃ nimittaṃ āsevatī”tiādīsu (a. ni. 9.35) gocarakaraṇampi āsevanāti vuttāti āha “kānici gocarāsevanāyā”ti. Tattha sabbesaṃ gocarīkātabbattepi “kānicī”ti vacanaṃ avipassitabbānaṃ bahulīmanasikaraṇena anāsevanīyattā. Paccavekkhaṇāmattameva hi tesu hotīti. “Tassa taṃ maggaṃ āsevato”tiādīsu (a. ni. 4.170) bhāvanā “āsevanā”ti vuttāti bhāvetabbāni saddhādīni sandhāyāha “kānici bhāvanāsevanāyā”ti. Ādhipaccaṃ indriyapaccayabhāvo, asati ca indriyapaccayabhāve itthipurisindriyānaṃ attano paccayavasena pavattamānehi taṃsahitasantāne aññākārena anuppajjamānehi liṅgādīhi anuvattanīyabhāvo, imasmiñcatthe indanti paramissariyaṃ karonticceva indriyāni. Cakkhādīsu dassitena nayena aññesañca tadanuvattīsu ādhipaccaṃ yathārahaṃ yojetabbaṃ.

It signifies, indicates, and makes known, thus it is a characteristic (liṅgaṃ). Or, it is characterized by this, thus it is a characteristic (liṅgaṃ). What does it signify? And what is characterized by it? Inda is the lord, or Inda; the characteristic of Inda is the mark of Inda (indaliṅgaṃ). The meaning of the mark of Inda is its own nature, which is the meaning of 'indaliṅga' (indaliṅgaṭṭho). Or, the meaning of the term 'indriya' is the mark of Inda itself, which is the meaning of 'indaliṅga' (indaliṅgaṭṭho). Created, produced, is 'siṭṭha'. Created by Inda is 'indasiṭṭha'. 'Juṭṭhaṃ' means frequented, practiced. The characteristics of Inda designated as kamma, and those created by it—only those born of kamma should be connected, not others. And those two meanings should be connected to kamma itself, while others are to be connected to the Blessed One as is appropriate—hence it is said: 'as is appropriate' (yathāyogaṃ). By that—due to the Blessed One being Inda, and kamma being Inda. Here—in these faculties (indriyesu). They indicate, they make clear, through the success and failure of the result, by understanding the success and failure of the cause. In passages like, 'he cultivates that sign (nimittaṃ),' even the making of an object-field (gocara) is called 'cultivation' (āsevanā); hence it is said, 'some for the cultivation of the object-field' (gocarāsevanāya). There, although all should be made into an object-field, the term 'some' (kānicī) is used because of the unsuitability for cultivation through frequent attention to those things which should not be contemplated with insight. For in them, there is only mere reviewing (paccavekkhaṇā). In passages like, 'as he cultivates that path (maggaṃ),' development (bhāvanā) is called 'cultivation' (āsevanā); hence, referring to what should be developed—faith (saddhā) and so on—it is said, 'some for the cultivation of development' (bhāvanāsevanāya). Dominance (ādhipaccaṃ) is the state of being a faculty-condition (indriyapaccayabhāvo). And when the faculty-condition is absent, for the male and female faculties, which proceed by way of their own conditions, there is the state of being conformed to by characteristics and so on, which do not arise in another form in the continuity associated with them. In this sense, 'they exercise lordship' (indanti), that is, they exercise supreme sovereignty, thus they are faculties (indriyāni). In the case of the eye faculty and so on, as shown, and in the case of others that follow them, dominance should be applied as is appropriate.

Heṭṭhāti aṭṭhasāliniyaṃ. Amoho eva, na visuṃ cattāro dhammā, tasmā amohassa paññindriyapade vibhāvitāni lakkhaṇādīni tesañca veditabbānīti adhippāyo. Sesāni aṭṭhasāliniyaṃ lakkhaṇādīhi sarūpeneva āgatāni. Nanu ca sukhindriyadukkhindriyānaṃ tattha lakkhaṇādīni na vuttānīti? Kiñcāpi na vuttāni, somanassadomanassindriyānaṃ pana vuttalakkhaṇādivasena viññeyyato etesampi vuttāneva honti. Kathaṃ? Iṭṭhaphoṭṭhabbānubhavanalakkhaṇaṃ sukhindriyaṃ, iṭṭhākārasambhogarasaṃ, kāyikassādapaccupaṭṭhānaṃ, kāyindriyapadaṭṭhānaṃ[V 0.0080]. Aniṭṭhaphoṭṭhabbānubhavanalakkhaṇaṃ dukkhindriyaṃ, aniṭṭhākārasambhogarasaṃ, kāyikābādhapaccupaṭṭhānaṃ, kāyindriyapadaṭṭhānanti. Ettha ca iṭṭhāniṭṭhākārānameva ārammaṇānaṃ sambhogarasatā veditabbā, na viparītepi iṭṭhākārena aniṭṭhākārena ca sambhogarasatāti.

'Below' means in the Aṭṭhasālinī. It is non-delusion alone, not four separate dhammas. Therefore, the intention is that the characteristics and so forth of non-delusion, explained in the section on the wisdom faculty, should be understood for these as well. The remaining ones are presented in the Aṭṭhasālinī with their characteristics and so forth in their own form. But were not the characteristics and so forth of the faculties of pleasure and pain mentioned there? Although they were not mentioned, they are nevertheless considered mentioned because they can be known by way of the mentioned characteristics and so forth of the faculties of gladness and sadness. How so? The faculty of pleasure has the characteristic of experiencing a desirable tangible object, the function of experiencing its agreeable aspect, the manifestation as bodily delight, and the body faculty as its proximate cause. The faculty of pain has the characteristic of experiencing an undesirable tangible object, the function of experiencing its disagreeable aspect, the manifestation as bodily affliction, and the body faculty as its proximate cause. And here, it should be understood that the function of experiencing pertains only to objects that have an agreeable or disagreeable aspect respectively, and not the reverse; that is, the function of experiencing is not of an agreeable aspect in relation to a disagreeable one, nor of a disagreeable aspect in relation to an agreeable one.

Sattānaṃ [M 0.0080] ariyabhūmipaṭilābho bhagavato desanāya sādhāraṇaṃ padhānañca payojananti āha “ajjhattadhammaṃ pariññāyā”tiādi. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ itthipurisindriyānantaraṃ jīvitindriyadesanakkamo vutto, so indriyayamakadesanāya sameti. Idha pana indriyavibhaṅge manindriyānantaraṃ jīvitindriyaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ purimapacchimānaṃ ajjhattikabāhirānaṃ anupālakattena tesaṃ majjhe vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Yañca kiñci vedayitaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ. Yāva ca duvidhattabhāvānupālakassa jīvitindriyassa pavatti, tāva dukkhabhūtānaṃ etesaṃ vedayitānaṃ anivattīti ñāpanatthaṃ. Tena ca cakkhādīnaṃ dukkhānubandhatāya pariññeyyataṃ ñāpeti. Tato anantaraṃ bhāvetabbattāti bhāvanāmaggasampayuttaṃ aññindriyaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Dassanānantarā hi bhāvanāti.

The attainment of the noble plane by beings is the common and principal purpose of the Blessed One's teaching; thus he said, 'for the full understanding of internal dhammas,' etc. In the commentary, the order of teaching the life faculty is stated to be after the female and male faculties, and this accords with the teaching of the Indriyayamaka. Here, however, in the Indriyavibhaṅga, the life faculty is mentioned after the mind faculty. This should be understood as being stated in the middle because it is the sustainer of the preceding and following, the internal and external. Whatever is felt, all that is suffering. And for the purpose of making it known that for as long as the life faculty—the sustainer of the twofold state—continues, there is no cessation of these feelings which have become suffering. And thereby it makes known that the eye faculty and so on are to be fully understood due to their connection with suffering. Immediately after that, it was said with reference to the faculty of final knowledge associated with the path of development, because it is to be developed. For development comes immediately after seeing.

Satipi purejātādipaccayabhāve indriyapaccayabhāvena sādhetabbameva kiccaṃ “kicca”nti āha tassa anaññasādhāraṇattā indriyakathāya ca pavattattā. Pubbaṅgamabhāvena manindriyassa vasavattāpanaṃ hoti, nāññesaṃ. Taṃsampayuttānipi hi indriyāni sādhetabbabhūtāneva attano attano indriyakiccaṃ sādhenti cetasikattāti. “Sabbattha ca indriyapaccayabhāvena sādhetabba”nti ayaṃ adhikāro anuvattatīti daṭṭhabbo. Anuppādane anupatthambhe ca tappaccayānaṃ tappavattane nimittabhāvo anuvidhānaṃ. Chādetvā pharitvā uppajjamānā sukhadukkhavedanā sahajāte abhibhavitvā sayameva pākaṭā hoti, sahajātā ca tabbasena sukhadukkhabhāvappattā viyāti āha “yathāsakaṃ oḷārikākārānupāpana”nti. Asantassa apaṇītassapi akusalatabbipākādisampayuttassa majjhattākārānupāpanaṃ yojetabbaṃ, samānajātiyaṃ vā sukhadukkhehi santapaṇītākārānupāpanañca. Pasannapaggahitaupaṭṭhitasamāhitadassanākārānupāpanaṃ yathākkamaṃ saddhādīnaṃ. Ādi-saddena uddhambhāgiyasaṃyojanāni gahitāni, maggasampayuttasseva ca indriyassa kiccaṃ dassitaṃ, teneva phalasampayuttassa taṃtaṃsaṃyojanānaṃyeva paṭippassaddhipahānakiccatā dassitā hotīti. Sabbakatakiccaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ aññassa kātabbassa abhāvā amatābhimukhameva tabbhāvapaccayo ca hoti, na itarāni viya kiccantarapasutañca. Tenāha “amatābhimukhabhāvapaccayatā cā”ti.

Even though there is the state of being a pre-arisen condition, etc., he said 'function' for the function that is to be accomplished precisely by the faculty-condition, because it is not shared by others and because the discourse on faculties is proceeding. The mind faculty's gaining of control occurs through its state of being a forerunner, not so for the others. For even the faculties associated with it, being mental factors, accomplish their respective faculty-functions as things to be accomplished. It should be seen that this heading, 'and everywhere it is to be accomplished by way of the faculty-condition,' is carried forward. In non-production and non-support, conformity is the state of being a sign for their conditions in their occurrence. Pleasant and painful feeling, arising while covering and pervading, becomes manifest by itself, having overpowered the co-arisen states; and the co-arisen states, by dependence on it, seem to attain a state of pleasure or pain. Thus it is said, 'the bringing about of their respective gross aspects.' For what is not tranquil or sublime, associated with unwholesome states, their results, etc., the bringing about of a neutral aspect should be applied; or, in the same class with pleasure and pain, the bringing about of a tranquil and sublime aspect. The bringing about of the aspects of seeing with confidence, energy, establishment, and concentration, respectively for faith and so on. By the word 'etc.,' the higher fetters are included, and the function of the faculty associated with the path only is shown; thereby, for the one associated with fruition, the function of calming and abandoning those very fetters is shown to be accomplished. The faculty of one who has finally known (aññātāvindriya), having accomplished all that was to be done, is directed towards the deathless because there is nothing further to be done, and it is a condition for that state, not being engaged in other functions like the others. Therefore, it is said, 'and the state of being a condition for being directed towards the deathless.'

220. Evaṃ [M 0.0081][V 0.0081] santepīti satipi sabbasaṅgāhakatte vīriyindriyapadādīhi saṅgahetabbāni kusalākusalavīriyādīni, cakkhundriyapadādīhi saṅgahetabbāni kālapuggalapaccayādibhedena bhinnāni cakkhādīni saṅgaṇhanticceva sabbasaṅgāhakāni, na yassā bhūmiyā yāni na vijjanti, tesaṃ saṅgāhakattāti attho. Tena ca avisesitattā sabbesaṃ sabbabhūmikattagahaṇappasaṅge taṃnivattanena sabbasaṅgāhakavacanaṃ avijjamānassa saṅgāhakattadīpakaṃ na hotīti dasseti.

220. 'Even so' means: even when there is the all-inclusive nature, the terms 'energy faculty,' etc., are all-inclusive precisely because they include wholesome and unwholesome energy, etc., and the terms 'eye faculty,' etc., are all-inclusive because they include the eye, etc., which are differentiated by distinctions of time, person, condition, and so on. The meaning is that this is not an inclusion of those things which do not exist in a particular plane. And thereby he shows that, since it is not specified, to prevent the possible assumption that all faculties exist in all planes, the statement 'all-inclusive' does not indicate the inclusion of what is non-existent.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Abhidhamma Division is concluded.

2. Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Question Section

223. Idha anābhaṭṭhanti ekantānārammaṇattena bhāsitaṃ. “Rūpamissakattā anārammaṇesu rūpadhammesu saṅgahita”nti kasmā vuttaṃ, nanu missakattā eva jīvitindriyaṃ anārammaṇesu asaṅgahitaṃ. Na hi aṭṭhindriyā anārammaṇāti vuttāti? Saccametaṃ, jīvitindriyaekadesassa pana anārammaṇesu rūpadhammesu saṅgahitataṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ, arūpakoṭṭhāsena parittārammaṇāditā atthīti siyāpakkhe saṅgahitanti adhippāyo. Arūpakoṭṭhāsena pana parittārammaṇāditā, rūpakoṭṭhāsena ca navattabbatā atthīti missakassa samudāyasseva vasena siyāpakkhe saṅgahitaṃ, na ekadesavasenāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Na hi anārammaṇaṃ parittārammaṇādibhāvena navattabbaṃ na hotīti. “Rūpañca nibbānañca anārammaṇā, sattindriyā anārammaṇā”tiādivacanañca avijjamānārammaṇānārammaṇesu navattabbesu anārammaṇattā navattabbataṃ dasseti, na sārammaṇasseva navattabbataṃ, navattabbassa vā sārammaṇataṃ. Na hi navattabba-saddo sārammaṇe niruḷho. Yadipi siyā, “tisso ca vedanā rūpañca nibbānañca ime dhammā navattabbā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā”tiādi na vucceyya, athāpi parittārammaṇādisambandho navattabba-saddo sārammaṇesveva vattati, “dvāyatanā siyā parittārammaṇā”tiādiṃ avatvā “manāyatanaṃ siyā parittārammaṇaṃ…pe… appamāṇārammaṇa”ntipi, “dhammāyatanaṃ siyā parittārammaṇaṃ…pe… appamāṇārammaṇa”ntipi, “siyā anārammaṇa”ntipi vattabbaṃ siyā. Na hi pañhapucchake sāvasesā desanā atthīti[M 0.0082]. “Aṭṭhindriyā siyā ajjhattārammaṇā”ti ettha ca jīvitindriyassa [V 0.0082] ākiñcaññāyatanakāle arūpassa rūpassa ca anārammaṇattā navattabbatā veditabbā.

223. Here, 'anābhaṭṭha' is spoken of as being exclusively without an object. Why is it said, 'Because of being mixed with form, it is included among form phenomena that are without an object'? Is it not precisely because of being mixed that the life faculty is not included among phenomena that are without an object? For it is not said that the eight faculties are without an object, is it? This is true. However, this is said with reference to the inclusion of a portion of the life faculty among form phenomena that are without an object. The intention is that it is included in the 'may be' aspect because, through its immaterial portion, it has limited objects, etc. However, through its immaterial portion, it has limited objects, etc., and through its form portion, there is the state of being unstatable (`navattabba`). Thus, it should be understood that it is included in the 'may be' aspect by way of the mixed aggregate as a whole, not by way of a part. For it is not that what is without an object ceases to be unstatable by virtue of being classifiable as having limited objects, etc. And the statements such as 'Form and Nibbāna are without an object, the seven faculties are without an object,' show that for objectless and unstatable phenomena, their unstatability is due to their being objectless; it does not show that what has an object is unstatable, nor that what is unstatable has an object. For the term 'unstatable' is not established as referring to what has an object. Even if it were so, one would not say, 'The three feelings, form, and Nibbāna—these phenomena are unstatable, associated with pleasant feeling,' etc. Moreover, if the term 'unstatable' in relation to limited objects, etc., were to apply only to things with an object, then instead of saying, 'The two bases may have limited objects,' etc., one should also have said, 'The mind base may have a limited object... or an immeasurable object,' and 'The phenomena base may have a limited object... or an immeasurable object,' and 'it may be without an object.' For when answering a question, the teaching is not left incomplete. And in the statement, 'The eight faculties may have an internal object,' it should be understood that the life faculty is unstatable (`navattabba`) at the time of the base of nothingness because both its immaterial and material components are without an object.

Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition on the Questioner is completed.

Indriyavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of the Faculties is completed.

6. Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅgo

6. The Analysis of Dependent Origination

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Suttanta Exposition

Uddesavāravaṇṇanā

Exposition of the Summary Section

225. “‘Kiṃvādī [M 0.0083][V 0.0083] bhante sammāsambuddho’ti? ‘Vibhajjavādī mahārājā’”ti (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.tatiyasaṅgītikathā) moggaliputtatissattherena vuttattā sammāsambuddhasāvakā vibhajjavādino. Te hi venayikādibhāvaṃ vibhajja vadanti, cīvarādīnaṃ sevitabbāsevitabbabhāvaṃ vā sassatucchedavāde vā vibhajja vadanti “sassato attā ca loko cā”tiādīnaṃ ṭhapanīyānaṃ ṭhapanato rāgādikkhayassa sassatassa rāgādikāyaduccaritādiucchedassa ca vacanato, na pana ekaṃsabyākaraṇīyādayo tayo pañhe apanetvā vibhajjabyākaraṇīyameva vadantīti. Vibhajjavādīnaṃ maṇḍalaṃ samūho vibhajjavādimaṇḍalaṃ, vibhajjavādino vā bhagavato parisā vibhajjavādimaṇḍalantipi vadanti. Ācariyehi vuttaaviparītatthadīpanena te anabbhācikkhantena. “Avijjā puññāneñjābhisaṅkhārānaṃ hetupaccayo hotī”tiādiṃ vadanto kathāvatthumhi paṭikkhitte puggalavādādike ca vadanto sakasamayaṃ vokkamati nāma, tathā avokkamantena. Parasamayaṃ dosāropanabyāpāravirahena anāyūhantena. “Idampi yuttaṃ gahetabba”nti parasamayaṃ asampiṇḍentenāti keci vadanti.

225. Because it was stated by the Elder Moggaliputtatissa, '“Venerable sir, what is the doctrine of the Perfectly Enlightened One?” “He is an analyst, great king”' (Pārā. Aṭṭh. 1, Account of the Third Council), the disciples of the Perfectly Enlightened One are analysts (`vibhajjavādino`). For they speak analytically, distinguishing matters pertaining to the Vinaya and so on, or the permissibility and impermissibility of using robes and so on, or regarding eternalist and annihilationist views by setting aside what should be set aside, such as 'the self and the world are eternal,' and by affirming the permanence of the destruction of lust and so on, and the annihilation of bodily misconduct and so on, which arise from lust. However, it is not that they speak only by way of analytical answers, having dismissed the other three types of questions beginning with those to be answered categorically. The circle or assembly of the analysts is the 'circle of analysts' (`vibhajjavādimaṇḍala`), or some say the assembly of the Blessed One is the 'circle of analysts.' (This commentary is written) by one who expounds the unerring meaning stated by the teachers, without misrepresenting them. One who, while speaking of such things as, 'Ignorance is a condition for meritorious, demeritorious, and imperturbable formations,' also speaks of the personalist view and other views rejected in the Kathāvatthu, is said to deviate from his own doctrine; (this is written) by one who does not so deviate. By one who does not attack another's doctrine, being free from the effort of imputing faults. Some say (this means): by one who does not amalgamate another's doctrine, thinking, 'This too is reasonable and should be accepted.'

“Tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati anañña”ntiādiṃ (ma. ni. 1.396) vadanto suttaṃ paṭibāhati nāma, tathā appaṭibāhantena. “Tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā [V 0.0084] bhagavatā, te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā”ti (ma. ni. 1.234; pāci. 418, 429), “supinante kato vītikkamo āpattikaro hotī”ti ca evamādiṃ vadanto vinayaṃ paṭilometi nāma, tabbipariyāyena taṃ anulomentena. Paṭilomento hi kammantaraṃ bhindanto dhammatañca vilometi. Suttante vutte cattāro mahāpadese, aṭṭhakathāyañca vutte suttasuttānulomaācariyavādaattanomatimahāpadese olokentena. Taṃolokanena hi sutte [M 0.0084] vinaye ca santiṭṭhati nātidhāvati. Dhammanti paṭiccasamuppādapāḷiṃ. Atthanti tadatthaṃ. Hetuhetuphalāni idha nādhippetāni. “Dukkhādīsu aññāṇaṃ avijjā”ti vuttamatthaṃ parivattitvā puna “pubbante aññāṇa”ntiādīhi aparehipi pariyāyehi niddisantena. “Saṅkhārā iminā pariyāyena bhavoti vuccanti, taṇhā iminā pariyāyena upādāna”ntiādinā niddisantenāti vadanti.

One who says, 'I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One in this way: it is this very same consciousness that runs on and transmigrates, not another' (M.N. 1.396), is said to repudiate the Sutta; (this is written) by one who does not so repudiate. One who says, 'I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One in this way: those things said by the Blessed One to be obstructions are not able to obstruct one who engages in them' (M.N. 1.234; Pācittiya 418, 429), and, 'A transgression committed in a dream incurs an offense,' and so on, is said to contradict the Vinaya; (this is written) by one who, conversely, conforms to it. For one who contradicts (the Vinaya) disrupts the formal acts (of the Sangha) and violates the very nature of the Dhamma. (This is written) by one who examines the four great references stated in the Suttas, and the great references stated in the commentaries, namely, the Sutta, conformity to the Sutta, the teachers' tradition, and one's own opinion. For by that examination, one stands firm in the Suttas and the Vinaya and does not overstep them. 'Dhamma' refers to the Pāli text of Dependent Origination. 'Meaning' refers to its meaning. Cause, the cause of a cause, and results are not intended here. (This is written) by one who, having restated the meaning given as 'Ignorance is unknowing regarding suffering, etc.,' then indicates it by other alternative phrases such as 'unknowing regarding the past,' and so on. They say (this is written) by one who indicates thus: 'In this sense, formations are called 'becoming'; in this sense, craving is called 'clinging,'' and so on.

Sattoti sattasuññatāti vadanti, sattasuññesu vā saṅkhāresu sattavohāro. Paccayākārameva cāti paccayākāro eva ca, ma-kāro padasandhikaro.

They say 'a being' (`satto`) means the emptiness of a being (`sattasuññatā`), or it is the conventional designation 'being' used for formations that are empty of a being. The phrase `Paccayākārameva cāti` is `paccayākāro eva ca` (and merely the mode of conditions); the letter 'm' is for euphonic conjunction.

Tasmāti vuttanayena atthavaṇṇanāya kātabbattā dukkarattā ca.

Therefore, because the explanation of the meaning must be done according to the method stated, and also because of its difficulty.

Patiṭṭhaṃ nādhigacchāmīti yattha ṭhitassa vaṇṇanā sukarā hoti, taṃ nayaṃ attanoyeva ñāṇabalena nādhigacchāmīti attho. Nissayaṃ pana ācikkhanto āha “sāsanaṃ panida”ntiādi. Idha sāsananti pāḷidhammamāha, paṭiccasamuppādameva vā. So hi anulomapaṭilomādinānādesanānayamaṇḍito abbocchinno ajjāpi pavattatīti nissayo hoti. Tadaṭṭhakathāsaṅkhāto ca pubbācariyamaggoti.

'I do not find a footing' means: 'I do not find, by the power of my own knowledge, that method based on which the explanation would be easy.' But when pointing out the support, he says, 'But this teaching,' and so on. Here, 'teaching' refers to the Pāli Dhamma, or to Dependent Origination itself. For it, adorned with various methods of teaching such as the forward and reverse orders, continues unbroken even today, and thus it is a support. And so too is the path of the ancient teachers, known as its commentary.

“Taṃ suṇātha samāhitā”ti ādarajanane kiṃ payojananti taṃ dassento āha “vuttañheta”ntiādi. Aṭṭhiṃ katvāti atthaṃ katvā, yathā vā na nassati, evaṃ aṭṭhigataṃ viya karonto aṭṭhiṃ katvā. Pubbakālato aparakāle bhavaṃ pubbāpariyaṃ. Paṭhamārambhādito pabhuti khaṇe khaṇe ñāṇavisesaṃ kilesakkhayavisesañca labhatīti attho.

To show the purpose in generating respect by saying, 'Listen to that with focused attention,' he said, 'For it has been stated,' and so on. 'Having made it the essence' (`aṭṭhiṃ katvā`) means having made it the meaning (`atthaṃ katvā`), or making it as if it has gone to the bone (`aṭṭhigataṃ`) so that it does not perish. 'Sequence' (`pubbāpariyaṃ`) is that which exists in a later time arising from an earlier time. The meaning is that from the very first moment of striving onward, at every moment, one obtains special knowledge and a special destruction of defilements.

Kammavipākakilesavaṭṭānaṃ mūlakāraṇattā ādito vuttattā ca avijjā paṭiccasamuppādassa mūlaṃ. Tattha valliyā mūle diṭṭhe tato pabhuti valliyā haraṇaṃ viya paṭiccasamuppādassa [V 0.0085] mūle diṭṭhe tato pabhuti paṭiccasamuppādadesanāti upamāsaṃsandanā na kātabbā. Na hi bhagavato “idameva diṭṭhaṃ, itaraṃ adiṭṭha”nti vibhajanīyaṃ atthi sabbassa diṭṭhattā. Mūlato pabhuti pana valliyā haraṇaṃ viya mūlato pabhuti paṭiccasamuppādadesanā katāti idamettha sāmaññamadhippetaṃ, bodhaneyyajjhāsayavasena vā bodhetabbabhāvena mūlādidassanasāmaññañca yojetabbaṃ.

Ignorance is the root of dependent origination because it is the root cause of the cycles of kamma, results, and defilements, and because it is stated at the beginning. Here, the comparison with the simile—'just as when the root of a creeper is seen, the creeper is taken from that point onward, so too when the root of dependent origination is seen, the teaching of dependent origination is given from that point onward'—should not be made. For the Blessed One has nothing that can be divided as 'this is seen, the other is unseen,' since everything has been seen by him. However, 'just as the creeper is taken from the root onward, so too the teaching of dependent origination is given from the root onward'—this is the general point intended here. Or, the general principle of showing the root and so on should be applied according to the disposition of those to be enlightened or according to their capacity to be enlightened.

Tassāti [M 0.0085] –

Regarding that:

“Sa kho so, bhikkhave, kumāro vuddhimanvāya indriyānaṃ paripākamanvāya pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito…pe… rajanīyehi, so cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā piyarūpe rūpe sārajjati, apiyarūpe rūpe byāpajjati, anupaṭṭhitakāyasatī ca viharati parittacetaso. So tañca cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Yatthassa te uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti, so evaṃ anurodhavirodhaṃ samāpanno yaṃ kiñci vedanaṃ vedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, so taṃ vedanaṃ abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhatī”ti (ma. ni. 1.408) –

"Monks, that young boy, as he grows and his faculties mature, is endowed with the five cords of sensual pleasure... with things that are enticing.
