The commentary on the exposition of the term ‘volitional formations’ is concluded.

Viññāṇapadaniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of the Term ‘Consciousness’

227. Yathāvuttasaṅkhārapaccayā [V 0.0101] uppajjamānaṃ taṃkammanibbattameva viññāṇaṃ bhavituṃ arahatīti “bāttiṃsa lokiyavipākaviññāṇāni saṅgahitāni hontī”ti āha. Dhātukathāyaṃ (dhātu. 466) pana vippayuttenasaṅgahitāsaṅgahitapadaniddese –

227. Since the consciousness arising dependent on formations as stated is fit to be only consciousness produced by that kamma, it is said: “Thirty-two mundane resultant consciousnesses are included.” However, in the Dhātukathā (Dhātu. 466), in the exposition of the terms ‘included’ and ‘not included’ by way of the dissociated—

“Saṅkhārapaccayā [M 0.0102] viññāṇena ye dhammā…pe… saḷāyatanapaccayā phassena, phassapaccayā vedanāya ye dhammā vippayuttā, te dhammā katihi khandhehi…pe… saṅgahitā? Te dhammā asaṅkhataṃ khandhato ṭhapetvā ekena khandhena ekādasahāyatanehi ekādasahi dhātūhi saṅgahitā. Katihi asaṅgahitā? Catūhi khandhehi ekenāyatanena sattahi dhātūhi asaṅgahitā”ti –

Those phenomena that are dissociated from consciousness conditioned by formations... from contact conditioned by the six sense bases, and from feeling conditioned by contact—by how many aggregates... are they included? Those phenomena, excluding the unconditioned from the aggregates, are included by one aggregate, eleven sense bases, and eleven elements. By how many are they not included? They are not included by four aggregates, one sense base, and seven elements.

Vacanato sabbaviññāṇaphassavedanāpariggaho kato. Yadi hi ettha viññāṇaphassavedanā sappadesā siyuṃ, “vipākā dhammā”ti imassa viya vissajjanaṃ siyā, tasmā tattha abhidhammabhājanīyavasena saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇādayo gahitāti veditabbā. Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā ca abhidhammabhājanīye catubhūmakakusalasaṅkhāro akusalasaṅkhāro ca vuttoti so eva dhātukathāyaṃ gahitoti daṭṭhabbo. Bhavo pana dhātukathāyaṃ kammupapattibhavavisesadassanatthaṃ na abhidhammabhājanīyavasena gahito. Evañca katvā tattha “upādānapaccayā bhavo”ti anuddharitvā “kammabhavo”tiādināva nayena bhavo uddhaṭo. Vipākañhetanti viññāṇassa vipākattā saṅkhārapaccayattaṃ sādheti, tassa pana sādhanatthaṃ “upacitakammābhāve vipākābhāvato”ti vuttanti taṃ vivaranto “vipākañcā”tiādimāha.

By the statement, the comprehension of all consciousness, contact, and feeling is made. If here consciousness, contact, and feeling were partial, there would be an answer like 'resultant phenomena'; therefore it should be understood that there, by way of the Abhidhamma classification, consciousness and so forth conditioned by formations are taken. And formations conditioned by ignorance are stated in the Abhidhamma classification as the wholesome formation and unwholesome formation of the four planes, so it should be seen that this is taken in the Dhātukathā. However, becoming is not taken in the Dhātukathā by way of the Abhidhamma classification, for the purpose of showing the distinction between kamma-becoming and rebirth-becoming. And having done so, there, 'becoming conditioned by clinging' is not extracted, and becoming is brought out only by the method of 'kamma-becoming,' etc. 'For it is a resultant'—because consciousness is a resultant, this establishes its being conditioned by formations. But for the purpose of establishing that, it is said, 'because of the absence of a resultant in the absence of accumulated kamma,' and explaining this, he says 'and a resultant,' etc.

Yebhuyyena lobhasampayuttajavanāvasāneti javanena tadārammaṇaniyame somanassasahagatānantaraṃ somanassasahagatatadārammaṇassa vuttattā somanassasahagatāneva sandhāya vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Yasmā pana tihetukajavanāvasāne ca kadāci ahetukaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ hoti, tasmā “yebhuyyenā”ti āha. Sakiṃ vāti “dirattatirattā”dīsu viya veditabbaṃ. Dvikkhattumeva pana uppajjantīti vadanti. “Dirattatiratta”nti ettha pana vā-saddassa abhāvā vacanasiliṭṭhatāmattena dirattaggahaṇaṃ katanti yujjati, “nirantaratirattadassanatthaṃ vā”ti. Idha pana vā-saddo vikappanattho vuttoti sakiṃ [V 0.0102] eva ca kadāci pavattiṃ sandhāya “sakiṃ vā”ti vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Teneva hi sakiṃ tadārammaṇappavattiyā vicāretabbataṃ dassento “cittappavattigaṇanāyaṃ panā”tiādimāha. Tattha cittappavattigaṇanāyanti vipākakathāyaṃ balavarūpādike ārammaṇe vuttaṃ cittappavattigaṇanaṃ sandhāyāha. Tattha hi dveva tadārammaṇuppattivārā āgatā. Javanavisayānubhavanañhi tadārammaṇaṃ [M 0.0103] āsannabhede tasmiṃ visaye ekacittakkhaṇāvasiṭṭhāyuke na uppajjeyyāti adhippāyo. Anurūpāya paṭisandhiyāti akusalavipākassa apāyapaṭisandhi, kāmāvacarādikusalavipākānaṃ kāmarūpārūpasugatipaṭisandhiyo yathākammaṃ anurūpā.

‘For the most part, at the end of javana associated with greed’—since in the rule of registering consciousness after javana, it is stated that after a joy-accompanied javana, a joy-accompanied registering consciousness arises, it should be understood that this is said with reference only to joy-accompanied javanas. But because sometimes at the end of a three-rooted javana, a rootless registering consciousness arises, therefore he says 'for the most part.' ‘Once or’—this should be understood as in ‘for two or three nights,’ etc. But some say it arises only twice. Regarding ‘two or three nights,’ here, due to the absence of the word ‘or,’ the taking of ‘two nights’ is done merely for the elegance of speech, or ‘for the purpose of showing an uninterrupted three nights.’ Here, however, the word ‘or’ is used in the sense of an alternative, thus it should be seen that ‘once or’ is said with reference to its occasional occurrence. For this very reason, showing that the occurrence of the registering consciousness once should be considered, he says ‘but in the counting of thought-processes,’ etc. There, ‘in the counting of thought-processes’—he says this with reference to the counting of thought-processes stated in the section on resultants regarding strong, excellent, etc., objects. For there, only two occasions of the arising of a registering consciousness are mentioned. For the registering consciousness is the experiencing of the object of the javana; in the case of a very clear object, if the lifespan of that object had only one thought-moment remaining, it would not arise—this is the intention. ‘By a suitable rebirth-linking’—for an unwholesome resultant, the rebirth-linking in the planes of misery is suitable; for wholesome resultants of the sense-sphere, etc., the rebirth-linkings in the happy destinations of the sense-sphere, fine-material sphere, and immaterial sphere are suitable according to the kamma.

Paṭisandhikathā mahāvisayāti katvā pavattimeva tāva dassento “pavattiyaṃ panā”tiādimāha. Ahetukadvayādīnaṃ dvāraniyamāniyamāvacanaṃ bhavaṅgabhūtānaṃ sayameva dvārattā cutipaṭisandhibhūtānañca bhavaṅgasaṅkhātena aññena ca dvārena anuppattito niyataṃ aniyataṃ vā dvāraṃ etesanti vattuṃ asakkuṇeyyattā. Ekassa sattassa pavattarūpāvacaravipāko pathavīkasiṇādīsu yasmiṃ ārammaṇe pavatto, tato aññasmiṃ tassa pavatti natthīti rūpāvacarānaṃ niyatārammaṇatā vuttā. Tatrassāti pavattiyaṃ bāttiṃsavidhassa.

Having considered the topic of rebirth-linking as vast, for now showing just the process of existence, he says, 'But in the process of existence,' etc. The reason it is not stated whether the doors for the two rootless kinds, etc., are fixed or unfixed is that it is impossible to state this: for those that have become the life-continuum are themselves doors, and those that have become death and rebirth-linking do not arise through another door designated as the life-continuum. For a single being, the resultant fine-material sphere consciousness that has arisen in relation to one object such as the earth kasiṇa does not arise for that being in relation to another object; thus, the fine-material sphere consciousnesses are said to have fixed objects. 'Therein' means in the process of existence, of the thirty-two kinds.

Indriyappavattiānubhāvato eva cakkhusotadvārabhedena, tassa ca viññāṇavīthibhedāyattattā vīthibhedena ca bhavitabbaṃ, tasmiñca sati “āvajjanānantaraṃ dassanaṃ savanaṃ vā tadanantaraṃ sampaṭicchana”ntiādinā cittaniyamena bhavitabbaṃ. Tathā ca sati sampaṭicchanasantīraṇānampi bhāvo siddho hoti, na indriyappavattiānubhāvena dassanasavanamattasseva, nāpi indriyānaṃ eva dassanasavanakiccatāti imamatthaṃ dassento āha “dvāravīthibhede cittaniyamato cā”ti. Paṭhamakusalena ce tadārammaṇassa uppatti hoti, taṃ paṭhamakusalānantaraṃ uppajjamānaṃ janakaṃ anubandhati nāma, dutiyakusalādianantaraṃ uppajjamānaṃ janakasadisaṃ anubandhati nāma, akusalānantaraṃ uppajjamānañca kāmāvacaratāya janakasadisanti.

Precisely by the power of the occurrence of the faculties, there must be a distinction of eye and ear doors; and since this depends on the distinction of the cognitive process, there must also be a distinction of the process. And when that exists, it must be by the fixed order of consciousness, as follows: 'After adverting, seeing or hearing; then receiving,' and so on. Thus, when that exists, the occurrence of receiving and investigating is also established—not merely seeing or hearing by the power of the occurrence of the faculties, nor is it that the faculties alone perform the function of seeing or hearing. To show this meaning, he says: 'By the distinction of the door and process, and by the fixed order of consciousness.' If the arising of a registering consciousness occurs after the first wholesome javana, that which arises immediately after the first wholesome is called 'following the producer.' That which arises immediately after the second wholesome, and so on, is called 'following what is similar to the producer.' And that which arises immediately after an unwholesome javana is called 'similar to the producer' on account of being of the sense-sphere.

Ekādasa tadārammaṇacittāni…pe… tadārammaṇaṃ na gaṇhantīti tadārammaṇabhāvatāya “tadārammaṇa”nti laddhanāmāni tadārammaṇabhāvaṃ na gaṇhanti, tadārammaṇabhāvena nappavattantīti attho. Atha vā nāmagottaṃ ārabbha javane javite tadārammaṇaṃ tassa javanassa ārammaṇaṃ na gaṇhanti, nālambantīti attho. Rūpārūpadhammeti rūpārūpāvacare dhamme. Idaṃ pana vatvā “abhiññāñāṇaṃ [V 0.0103] ārabbhā”ti visesanaṃ parittādiārammaṇatāya kāmāvacarasadisesu ceva tadārammaṇānuppattidassanatthaṃ. Micchattaniyatā dhammā maggo viya bhāvanāya siddhā mahābalā cāti tattha javanena pavattamānena sānubandhanena na bhavitabbanti tesu tadārammaṇaṃ paṭikkhittaṃ. Lokuttaradhamme [M 0.0104] ārabbhāti eteneva siddhe “sammattaniyatadhammesū”ti visuṃ uddharaṇaṃ sammattamicchattaniyatadhammānaṃ aññamaññapaṭipakkhāti balavabhāvena tadārammaṇassa avatthubhāvadassanatthaṃ.

The eleven registering consciousnesses... [do not take that object]. This means that although they have received the name 'registering consciousness' due to their nature of being such, in this case they do not take up the state of being a registering consciousness, meaning they do not function as a registering consciousness. Alternatively, when impulsion has occurred with respect to mentality-materiality, the registering consciousness does not take the object of that impulsion, meaning it does not take it as its object. 'Material and immaterial phenomena' refers to phenomena pertaining to the fine-material and immaterial spheres. Having stated this, the specification 'with respect to higher knowledge' is given to show that the object is limited, etc., and to demonstrate the non-arising of registering consciousness in the sense-sphere and similar states. Wrongly fixed phenomena, like the path, are powerful due to being perfected through development, and thus, when impulsion occurs with continuity, a registering consciousness should not arise after them; thus, a registering consciousness is rejected in those cases. Although this is established by the phrase 'with respect to supramundane phenomena,' the separate mention of 'in rightly fixed phenomena' is made to show that rightly and wrongly fixed phenomena are mutually opposed and, due to their powerful nature, are not a basis for a registering consciousness.

Evaṃ pavattiyaṃ viññāṇappavattiṃ dassetvā paṭisandhiyaṃ dassetuṃ “yaṃ pana vutta”ntiādimāha. Kena katthāti kena cittena kasmiṃ bhave. Ekūnavīsati paṭisandhiyo tena tena cittena pavattamānā paṭisandhikkhaṇe rūpārūpadhammāti tena tena cittena sā sā tattha tattha paṭisandhi hotīti vuttā. Tassāti cittassa.

Having thus shown the process of consciousness in the course of existence, to show it in rebirth-linking, he says, 'Now, what was said,' and so on. 'By what, where?' means 'By which consciousness, in which existence?' The nineteen rebirth-linkings, occurring by means of this or that consciousness at the moment of rebirth-linking, are material and immaterial phenomena—thus, it was said that by means of this or that consciousness, this or that rebirth-linking occurs in this or that place. 'Of that' means 'of the consciousness.'

Āgantvāti āgataṃ viya hutvā. Gopakasīvalīti rañño hitārakkhe gopakakule jāto sīvalināmako. Kammādianussaraṇabyāpārarahitattā “sammūḷhakālakiriyā”ti vuttā. Abyāpāreneva hi tattha kammādiupaṭṭhānaṃ hotīti. “Pisiyamānāya makkhikāya paṭhamaṃ kāyadvārāvajjanaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ nāvaṭṭeti attanā cintiyamānassa kassaci atthitāyā”ti keci kāraṇaṃ vadanti, tadetaṃ akāraṇaṃ bhavaṅgavisayato aññassa cintiyamānassa abhāvā aññacittappavattakāle ca bhavaṅgāvaṭṭanasseva asambhavato. Idaṃ panettha kāraṇaṃ siyā – “tānissa tamhi samaye olambanti ajjholambanti abhippalambantī”ti (ma. ni. 3.248) vacanato tīsu javanavāresu appavattesveva kammādiupaṭṭhānena bhavitabbaṃ. Anekajavanavārappavattiyā hi ajjholambanaṃ abhippalambanañca hotīti. Tasmā kāyadvārāvajjanaṃ anāvaṭṭetvā manodvārāvajjanameva kammādiālambaṇaṃ paṭhamaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ āvaṭṭeti, tato phoṭṭhabbassa balavattā dutiyavāre kāyaviññāṇavīthi paccuppanne phoṭṭhabbe pavattati, tato purimajavanavāragahitesveva kammādīsu kamena manodvārajavanaṃ javitvā mūlabhavaṅgasaṅkhātaṃ āgantukabhavaṅgasaṅkhātaṃ vā tadārammaṇaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ otarati, tadārammaṇābhāve vā bhavaṅgameva. Etasmiṃ ṭhāne kālaṃ karotīti tadārammaṇānantarena cuticittena, tadārammaṇābhāve vā bhavaṅgasaṅkhāteneva cuticittena cavatīti attho. Bhavaṅgameva hi cuticittaṃ hutvā pavattatīti cuticittaṃ idha “bhavaṅga”nti vuttanti. Manodvāravisayo lahukoti lahukapaccupaṭṭhānaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “arūpadhammānaṃ…pe… lahuko”ti. Arūpadhammassa [V 0.0104] hi manodvārassa visayo lahukapaccupaṭṭhānoti. Balavati ca rūpadhammassa kāyadvārassa [M 0.0105] visaye appavattitvā manodvāravisaye kammādimhi paṭhamaṃ cittappavattidassanena arūpadhammānaṃ visayassa lahukatā dīpitāti. Rūpānaṃ visayābhāvepi vā “arūpadhammāna”nti vacanaṃ yesaṃ visayo atthi, taṃdassanatthamevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tena lahukammādīsu cittappavattito lahugahaṇīyatā visayassa lahukatā.

“Having come” means “as if one has come.” “Gopakasīvalī” means Sīvali, born in the Gopaka clan, who was in the service of the king's welfare and protection. Because he was free from the activity of recollecting kamma, etc., it is said, “he died bewildered.” For indeed, at that time, the presentation of kamma, etc., occurs without any activity. Some say the reason is: “When a fly is being crushed, the first adverting at the body-door does not interrupt the life-continuum for one who is thinking of something else, because of the existence of something he is thinking of.” But this is not a reason, because from the perspective of the life-continuum, there is no other thought present, and at the time of the arising of another thought, the interruption of the life-continuum is impossible. Here, however, this might be the reason: “At that time, they hang on, cling to, and are attached to it” (MN 3.248). Thus, even when three courses of impulsion have not occurred, the presentation of kamma, etc., must still occur. For in the occurrence of many courses of impulsion, there is clinging and attachment. Therefore, without interrupting the adverting at the body-door, only the adverting at the mind-door first interrupts the life-continuum with kamma, etc., as its object. Then, due to the strength of the tangible, the body-consciousness process arises in the second course with the present tangible as its object. After that, having taken the kamma, etc., in the previous courses of impulsion, the mind-door impulsion gradually runs its course with kamma, etc., as its object, and then descends into the registration-bhavaṅga called the root-bhavaṅga or the guest-bhavaṅga. If there is no registration, it descends into the life-continuum itself. At this point, “he dies” means that he passes away with the death-consciousness immediately following the registration, or if there is no registration, with the death-consciousness reckoned as the life-continuum itself. For it is the life-continuum itself that arises, having become the death-consciousness. Here, the death-consciousness is called “life-continuum.” The mind-door object is light—this is said with reference to its easy presentation: “For immaterial phenomena… it is light.” For the object of the mind-door, an immaterial phenomenon, has an easy presentation. And because consciousness does not arise with respect to the strong object of the body-door, a material phenomenon, but is first seen to arise with respect to the mind-door object, kamma, etc., the lightness of the object of immaterial phenomena is thereby demonstrated. Or, even though immaterial phenomena have no object, the phrase “of immaterial phenomena” should be understood as being for the purpose of showing those that do have an object. Therefore, from the arising of consciousness with respect to light kamma, etc., the lightness of the object is its being easily graspable.

Kammādīnaṃ bhūmicittupādādivasena vitthārato ananto pabhedoti “saṅkhepato”ti āha.

The detailed classification of kamma and so on is endless, due to the variety arising by way of plane, consciousness, arising, etc.; therefore, it is spoken of “briefly.”

Avijjātaṇhādikilesesu anupacchinnesveva kammādino upaṭṭhānaṃ, tañcārabbha cittasantānassa bhavantaraninnapoṇapabbhāratā hotīti āha “anupacchinnakilesabalavināmita”nti. Santāne hi vināmite tadekadesabhūtaṃ paṭisandhicittañca vināmitameva hoti, na ca ekadesavināmitabhāvena vinā santānavināmitatā atthīti. Sabbattha pana “duggatipaṭisandhininnāya cutiyā purimajavanāni akusalāni, itarāya ca kusalānī”ti nicchinanti. “Nimittassādagadhitaṃ vā, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ tiṭṭhamānaṃ tiṭṭhati anubyañjanassādagadhitaṃ vā. Tasmiṃ ce samaye kālaṃ karoti, ṭhānametaṃ vijjati, yaṃ dvinnaṃ gatīnaṃ aññataraṃ gatiṃ upapajjeyya nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā”ti (saṃ. ni. 4.235) vuttaṃ. Tasmā āsannaṃ akusalaṃ duggatiyaṃ, kusalañca sugatiyaṃ paṭisandhiyā upanissayo hotīti.

When the defilements such as ignorance and craving are not yet severed, the presentation of kamma, etc., occurs. And, due to this, the stream of consciousness becomes inclined toward a new existence, burdened with the weight of becoming. Thus, it is said: “swayed by the unbroken force of defilements.” For when the stream is swayed, the rebirth-linking consciousness, being part of that stream, is also swayed. Indeed, without a part being swayed, there is no swaying of the stream. Moreover, it is determined: “For one destined for an unfortunate rebirth, the impulsion moments before death are unwholesome; for others, they are wholesome.” “It is said, monks, that consciousness persists when it clings to the delight in signs or the delight in details. If at that time one dies, it is possible that one may be reborn in one of two destinations—either in hell or in the animal realm” (Saṃyutta Nikāya 4.235). Therefore, an unwholesome state near death is a supporting condition for rebirth in an unfortunate realm, and a wholesome state is a supporting condition for rebirth in a fortunate realm.

Rāgādihetubhūtaṃ hīnamārammaṇanti akusalavipākassa ārammaṇaṃ bhavituṃ yuttaṃ aniṭṭhārammaṇaṃ āha. Tampi hi saṅkappavasena rāgassapi hetu hotīti. Akusalavipākajanakakammasahajātānaṃ vā taṃsadisāsannacutijavanacetanāsahajātānañca rāgādīnaṃ hetubhāvo eva hīnatā. Tañhi pacchānutāpajanakakammānamārammaṇaṃ kammavasena aniṭṭhaṃ akusalavipākassa ārammaṇaṃ bhaveyya, aññathā ca iṭṭhārammaṇe pavattassa akusalakammassa vipāko kammanimittārammaṇo na bhaveyya. Na hi akusalavipāko iṭṭhārammaṇo bhavitumarahatīti. Pañcadvāre ca āpāthamāgacchantaṃ paccuppannaṃ kammanimittaṃ āsannakatakammārammaṇasantatiyaṃ uppannaṃ taṃsadisañca daṭṭhabbaṃ, aññathā tadeva paṭisandhiārammaṇūpaṭṭhāpakaṃ tadeva ca paṭisandhijanakaṃ bhaveyya, na ca paṭisandhiyā upacārabhūtāni viya “etasmiṃ tayā [M 0.0106] pavattitabba”nti paṭisandhiyā ārammaṇaṃ anupādentāni viya [V 0.0105] ca pavattāni cutiāsannāni javanāni paṭisandhijanakāni bhaveyyuṃ. “Katattā upacitattā”ti (dha. sa. 431) hi vuttaṃ. Tadā ca taṃsamānavīthiyaṃ viya pavattamānāni kathaṃ katūpacitāni siyuṃ, na ca assāditāni tadā, na ca lokiyāni lokuttarāni viya samānavīthiphalāni honti.

He says that an inferior object, which is a cause of lust, etc., is an undesirable object suitable to be the object of unwholesome result. For even that can become a cause of lust through the force of thought. The inferiority lies in its being a cause for lust, etc., co-nascent with kamma that generates unwholesome results, or co-nascent with the volitions of impulsion moments similar to those proximate to death. For that, being the object for kamma that generates subsequent regret, would become an undesirable object for unwholesome result through the force of kamma. Otherwise, the result of unwholesome kamma that arose with a desirable object would not take a kamma-sign as its object. Indeed, an unwholesome result is not fit to have a desirable object. And in the five sense-doors, a present kamma-sign that comes into range should be understood as arising in a continuity of objects of recently performed kamma and as similar to them. Otherwise, that very same thing would be both the presenter of the object for rebirth-linking and the producer of rebirth-linking. And the impulsion moments proximate to death, proceeding as if they were access moments to rebirth-linking and as if they were not producing an object for rebirth-linking, saying as it were, 'You must proceed in this,' would not be producers of rebirth-linking. For it is said, “Because it has been done and accumulated” (Dhammasaṅgaṇī 431). And at that time, proceeding as if in the same cognitive process, how could they be 'done and accumulated'? They are not relished then, nor do mundane kammas have their results in the same cognitive process, like supramundane kammas do.

“Pubbe vāssa taṃ kataṃ hoti pāpakammaṃ dukkhavedanīyaṃ, pacchā vāssa taṃ kataṃ hoti pāpakammaṃ dukkhavedanīyaṃ, maraṇakāle vāssa hoti micchādiṭṭhi samattā samādinnā, tena so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjatī”ti (ma. ni. 3.303) –

“Either he has done an evil kamma in the past that leads to painful feeling, or he has done an evil kamma later that leads to painful feeling, or at the time of death he adopts and completes wrong view. Therefore, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, the lower realms, hell” (MN 3.303).

Ādinā sutte maraṇakāle samattāya samādinnāya micchādiṭṭhiyā sammādiṭṭhiyā ca sahajātacetanāya paṭisandhidānaṃ vuttaṃ, na ca dubbalehi pañcadvārikajavanehi micchādiṭṭhi sammādiṭṭhi vā samattā hoti samādinnā. Vakkhati ca –

In the aforementioned sutta, it is said that rebirth-linking is given by volition co-arising with wrong view or right view that has been completed and undertaken at the time of death. But wrong view or right view is not completed nor undertaken by weak five-door impulsion moments. And it will be said—

“Sabbampi hetaṃ kusalākusaladhammapaṭivijānanādicavanapariyosānaṃ kiccaṃ manodvārikacitteneva hoti, na pañcadvārikenāti sabbassapetassa kiccassa karaṇe sahajavanakāni vīthicittāni paṭikkhittānī”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 766).

“All this function, from the discernment of wholesome and unwholesome states up to its culmination in death, is performed by mind-door consciousness, not by five-door consciousness. Therefore, in performing all this function, process-consciousnesses with their co-arisen impulsion moments are rejected” (Vibh. Aṭṭha. 766).

Tattha hi “na kiñci dhammaṃ paṭivijānātīti ‘manopubbaṅgamā dhammā’ti (dha. pa. 1-2) evaṃ vuttaṃ ekampi kusalaṃ vā akusalaṃ vā na paṭivijānātī”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 766) ca vuttaṃ. Yesaṃ paṭivibhāvanappavattiyā sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā anveti, tesaṃ sā pavatti pañcadvāre paṭikkhittā, kusalākusalakammasamādānañca tādisamevāti. Tadārammaṇānantaraṃ pana cavanaṃ, tadanantarā ca upapatti manodvārikā eva hoti, na sahajavanakavīthicitte pariyāpannāti iminā adhippāyena idha pañcadvārikatadārammaṇānantaraṃ cuti, tadanantaraṃ paṭisandhi ca vuttāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tattha avasesapañcacittakkhaṇāyuke rūpādimhi uppannaṃ paṭisandhiṃ sandhāyeva “paccuppannārammaṇaṃ upapatticittaṃ paccuppannārammaṇassa bhavaṅgassa anantarapaccayena paccayo”ti, avasesekacittakkhaṇāyuke ca uppannaṃ sandhāya “paccuppannārammaṇaṃ [M 0.0107] upapatticittaṃ atītārammaṇassa [V 0.0106] bhavaṅgassa anantarapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 2.19.28) vuttanti veditabbaṃ.

Here, it is said: “He does not cognize any phenomenon,” and also, “He does not cognize even a single wholesome or unwholesome state” (Vibh-a 766), as stated in ‘Phenomena are preceded by mind’ (Dhp. 1-2). For those whom pleasure or pain follows from the process of discernment, that process is excluded from the five sense-doors, and the undertaking of wholesome or unwholesome kamma is likewise. However, the passing away that immediately follows the registering consciousness, and the subsequent rebirth, occur only through the mind-door and are not included in a cognitive process containing impulsion moments. With this meaning in mind, it should be understood that here, the passing away following the five-door registering consciousness and the subsequent rebirth-linking are spoken of. In this context, with reference to a rebirth-linking that has arisen in relation to a visible form, etc., that has five mind-moments of life remaining, it is said: “The rebirth-linking consciousness with a present object is a condition for the life-continuum with a present object by way of contiguity condition” (Paṭṭh. 2.19.28). And with reference to a rebirth-linking that has arisen when there is only one mind-moment of life remaining, it is said: “The rebirth-linking consciousness with a present object is a condition for the life-continuum with a past object by way of contiguity condition” (Paṭṭh. 2.19.28).

Suddhāya vāti mahaggatakammanimittārammaṇāya javanavīthiyā tadārammaṇarahitāyāti attho. Sā pana javanavīthi mahaggatavipākassa upacāro viya daṭṭhabbā. Keci pana taṃ vīthiṃ mahaggatāvasānaṃ vadanti. Atītārammaṇā ekādasavidhā, navattabbārammaṇā sattavidhā.

Or, for the pure impulsion process that has a sublime kamma-sign as its object, the meaning is that it is devoid of registering consciousness. That impulsion process should be regarded as being like the preliminary stage of the sublime resultant consciousness. Some, however, call that process the culmination of the sublime. There are eleven kinds with a past object, and seven kinds with an unspecifiable object.

Etenānusārena āruppacutiyāpi anantarā paṭisandhi veditabbāti idaṃ kasmā vuttaṃ, nanu “pathavīkasiṇajjhānādivasena paṭiladdhamahaggatasugatiyaṃ ṭhitassā”ti evamādike eva naye ayampi paṭisandhi avaruddhāti? Na, tattha rūpāvacaracutianantarāya eva paṭisandhiyā vuttattā. Tattha hi “pathavīkasiṇādikaṃ vā nimittaṃ mahaggatacittaṃ vā manodvāre āpāthamāgacchati. Cakkhusotānaṃ vā”tiādikena rūpāvacaracutiyā eva anantarā paṭisandhi vuttāti viññāyati. Athāpi yathāsambhavayojanāya ayampi paṭisandhi tattheva avaruddhā, arūpāvacaracutianantarā pana rūpāvacarapaṭisandhi natthi, arūpāvacare ca uparūparicutiyā heṭṭhimā heṭṭhimā paṭisandhīti catutthāruppacutiyā navattabbārammaṇā paṭisandhi natthi. Tena tato tattheva atītārammaṇā kāmāvacare ca atītapaccuppannārammaṇā paṭisandhi itarāhi ca yathāsambhavaṃ atītanavattabbārammaṇā āruppapaṭisandhi, atītapaccuppannārammaṇā ca kāmāvacarapaṭisandhi yojetabbāti imassa visesassa dassanatthaṃ visuṃ uddharaṇaṃ kataṃ.

‘Following this reasoning, it should be understood that rebirth-linking also occurs immediately after decease from the formless sphere.’ Why is this said? Is it not that this rebirth-linking is also included in such a method as, ‘for one established in a sublime happy destination attained by means of the earth-kasiṇa jhāna, etc.’? No, because there it is stated that rebirth-linking occurs only immediately after decease from the fine-material sphere. For there it is understood that rebirth-linking occurs only immediately after decease from the fine-material sphere, as it is said that ‘either the earth-kasiṇa or another sign, or a sublime consciousness, comes into the range of the mind-door, or of the eye or ear, etc.’ Yet, by applying it as is possible, this rebirth-linking is also included there. However, after decease from the formless sphere, there is no rebirth-linking in the fine-material sphere. And in the formless sphere, with decease from a higher and higher attainment, there is rebirth-linking in a lower and lower one; thus, after decease from the fourth formless attainment, there is no rebirth-linking with an unspecifiable object. Therefore, from there, rebirth-linking occurs in that same sphere with a past object, or in the sensual sphere with a past or present object. And for the other formless attainments, as is possible, formless rebirth-linking occurs with a past or unspecifiable object, and sensual-sphere rebirth-linking with a past or present object. To show this distinction, a separate exposition has been made.

Evaṃ ārammaṇavasena ekavidhāya kāmāvacarasugaticutiyā duvidhā duggatipaṭisandhi, duggaticutiyā duvidhā sugatipaṭisandhi, kāmāvacarasugaticutiyā dviekadvippakārānaṃ kāmarūpāruppānaṃ vasena pañcavidhā sugatipaṭisandhi, rūpāvacaracutiyā ca tatheva pañcavidhā, duvidhāya āruppacutiyā paccekaṃ dvinnaṃ dvinnaṃ kāmāruppānaṃ vasena aṭṭhavidhā ca paṭisandhi dassitā, duggaticutiyā pana ekavidhāya duggatipaṭisandhi duvidhā na dassitā, taṃ dassetuṃ “duggatiyaṃ ṭhitassa panā”tiādimāha. Yathāvuttā pana –

Thus, by way of the object, it has been shown that: from the one kind of decease from a sensual-sphere happy destination, there is a twofold rebirth-linking in a woeful destination; from decease from a woeful destination, a twofold rebirth-linking in a happy destination; from decease from a sensual-sphere happy destination, a fivefold rebirth-linking in a happy destination, by way of the two, one, and two kinds pertaining to the sensual, fine-material, and formless spheres respectively; and from decease from the fine-material sphere, it is similarly fivefold. And from the two kinds of decease from the formless sphere, an eightfold rebirth-linking has been shown, by way of two kinds each pertaining to the sensual and formless spheres. However, from decease from a woeful destination, a twofold rebirth-linking in a woeful destination has not been shown. To show this, he says: ‘But for one established in a woeful destination…,’ etc. But as has been stated:

Dvidvipañcappakārā ca, pañcāṭṭhaduvidhāpi ca;

Catuvīsati sabbāpi, tā honti paṭisandhiyo.

Of two, two, and five kinds,

And also of five, eight, and two kinds;

All these rebirth-linkings

Amount to twenty-four in total.

“Kāmāvacarassa [M 0.0108][V 0.0107] kusalassa kammassa katattā”tiādinā (dha. sa. 431, 455, 498) nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayabhāvo dassitappakāroti upanissayapaccayabhāvameva dassento “vuttañheta”ntiādimāha.

By the passage beginning, ‘On account of wholesome sensual-sphere kamma having been done…’ (Dhs §§431, 455, 498), the mode is shown whereby kamma is a condition at different moments. Thus, showing only its nature as a decisive-support condition, he says, ‘For this has been said…,’ etc.

Ādinā sahātiādinā vimissaviññāṇena saha. Omato dve vā tayo vā dasakā uppajjantīti gabbhaseyyakānaṃ vasena vuttaṃ. Aññattha hi aneke kalāpā saha uppajjanti. Brahmattabhāvepi hi anekagāvutappamāṇe aneke kalāpā sahuppajjantīti tiṃsato adhikāneva rūpāni honti gandharasāhārānaṃ paṭikkhittattā cakkhusotavatthusattakajīvitachakkabhāvepi tesaṃ bahuttā. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana tatthapi cakkhusotavatthudasakānaṃ jīvitanavakassa ca uppatti vuttā, pāḷiyaṃ pana “rūpadhātuyā upapattikkhaṇe ṭhapetvā asaññasattānaṃ devānaṃ pañcāyatanāni pātubhavanti, pañca dhātuyo pātubhavantī”ti vuttaṃ, tathā “rūpadhātuyā cha āyatanāni nava dhātuyo”ti sabbasaṅgahavasena tattha vijjamānāyatanadhātuyo dassetuṃ vuttaṃ. Kathāvatthumhi ca ghānāyatanādīnaṃ viya gandhāyatanādīnañca tattha bhāvo paṭikkhitto “atthi tattha ghānāyatananti? Āmantā, atthi tattha gandhāyatananti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe”tiādinā (kathā. 519), na ca aphoṭṭhabbāyatanānaṃ pathavīdhātuādīnaṃ viya agandharasāyatanānaṃ gandharasānaṃ tattha bhāvo sakkā vattuṃ phusituṃ asakkuṇeyyatāvinimuttassa pathavīādisabhāvassa viya gandharasabhāvavinimuttassa gandharasasabhāvassa abhāvā.

‘With the initial’ means: with consciousness mixed with the initial. ‘At a minimum, two or three decads arise’: this is said with reference to womb-born beings. Elsewhere, indeed, many material groups arise together. Even in the Brahmā-state, in an area spanning many leagues, many material groups arise together. Thus, there are more than thirty material phenomena; for although odor, taste, and nutriment are excluded, there is an abundance of them, such as the eye-septad, ear-septad, heart-base-septad, and life-hexad. In the commentary, however, it is stated that even there the eye-decad, ear-decad, heart-base-decad, and life-nonad arise. But in the Pāli Canon it is said: ‘At the moment of rebirth in the fine-material realm, except for the non-percipient devas, five bases and five elements appear.’ Similarly, it is said: ‘In the fine-material realm, there are six bases and nine elements’—this is stated to show, in a comprehensive way, the bases and elements existing there. And in the Kathāvatthu, the existence there of the odor base, etc., just like the nose base, etc., is rejected in the passage beginning: ‘Is there a nose base there? Yes. Is there an odor base there? It should not be said thus…’ (Kv 519). Nor can it be said that odor and taste exist there (without being bases), just as the earth element, etc., exist (without being the tangible base), because just as there is no nature of earth, etc., separate from its tangibility, so there is no nature of odor and taste separate from their own intrinsic nature.

Yadi ca ghānasamphassādīnaṃ kāraṇabhāvo natthīti āyatanānīti tena vucceyyuṃ, dhātu-saddo pana nissattanijjīvavācakoti gandhadhāturasadhātūti avacane natthi kāraṇaṃ, dhammabhāvo ca tesaṃ ekantena icchitabbo sabhāvadhāraṇādilakkhaṇato aññassa abhāvā, dhammānañca āyatanabhāvo ekantato yamake (yama. 1. āyatanayamaka.13) vutto “dhammo āyatananti? Āmantā”ti. Tasmā tesaṃ gandharasāyatanabhāvābhāvepi koci āyatanasabhāvo vattabbo. Yadi ca phoṭṭhabbabhāvato añño pathavīdhātuādibhāvo viya gandharasabhāvato añño tesaṃ koci sabhāvo siyā, tesaṃ dhammāyatane saṅgaho. Gandharasabhāve pana āyatanabhāve ca sati gandho ca so āyatanañca gandhāyatanaṃ, raso [M 0.0109] ca so āyatanañca rasāyatananti idamāpannamevāti gandharasāyatanabhāvo ca na sakkā nivāretuṃ, “tayo āhārā”ti (vibha. 993) ca vacanato [V 0.0108] kabaḷīkārāhārassa tattha abhāvo viññāyati. Tasmā yathā pāḷiyā avirodho hoti, tathā rūpagaṇanā kātabbā. Evañhi dhammatā na vilomitā hotīti.

And if it is because nose-contact and so on have no causal function there that they are not called ‘bases,’ then, since the word ‘element’ (dhātu) signifies what is non-sentient and non-living, there would be no reason for not saying ‘odor-element’ and ‘taste-element.’ Moreover, their nature as dhammas must certainly be accepted, as they have no other characteristic than that of bearing their own nature, etc. And that dhammas have the nature of a base is definitively stated in the Yamaka: ‘Is a dhamma a base? Yes’ (Yam I. Āyatanayamaka §13). Therefore, even if they lack the nature of being the odor-base and taste-base, some nature as a base must be ascribed to them. If they had some other nature apart from their nature as odor and taste—just as the earth element, etc., have a nature apart from being tangible—they would be included in the dhamma-base. But when there is both the nature of odor and taste and the nature of a base, then it follows that ‘it is odor and it is a base, thus odor-base; it is taste and it is a base, thus taste-base,’ and so their nature as the odor-base and taste-base cannot be denied. Moreover, from the statement ‘three nutriments’ (Vibh §993), it is understood that physical nutriment is absent there. Therefore, the enumeration of material phenomena should be done in a way that does not contradict the Pāli Canon. For in this way, the natural order is not violated.

Jātiuṇṇāyāti gabbhaṃ phāletvā gahitauṇṇāyātipi vadanti. Sambhavabhedoti atthitābhedo. Nijjhāmataṇhikā kira niccaṃ dukkhāturatāya kāmaṃ sevitvā gabbhaṃ na gaṇhanti.

'Of wool from a live animal' means 'of wool taken by splitting the womb'; so they say. 'Difference of origin' means difference of existence. It is said that those with burnt-out craving, being constantly afflicted by suffering, indulge in sensual pleasures and thus do not conceive.

Rūpībrahmesu tāva opapātikayonikesūti opapātikayonikehi rūpībrahme niddhāreti. “Saṃsedajopapātīsu avakaṃsato tiṃsā”ti etaṃ vivaranto āha “avakaṃsato panā”tiādi, taṃ panetaṃ pāḷiyā na sameti. Na hi pāḷiyaṃ kāmāvacarānaṃ saṃsedajopapātikānaṃ aghānakānaṃ upapatti vuttā. Dhammahadayavibhaṅge (vibha. 1007) hi –

'Among the corporeal Brahmās, those of spontaneous birth': he thus specifies the corporeal Brahmās by their being of spontaneous birth. Explaining the statement, 'Among the moisture-born and the spontaneously born, there are at a minimum thirty,' he says, 'but at a minimum...,' etc. This, however, does not agree with the Pāli Canon. For in the Canon, the arising in the sensual sphere of moisture-born and spontaneously born beings who are without a nose-organ is not mentioned. For in the Dhammahadayavibhaṅga (Vibh §1007) it is said:

“Kāmadhātuyā upapattikkhaṇe kassaci ekādasāyatanāni pātubhavanti, kassaci dasāyatanāni, kassaci aparāni dasāyatanāni, kassaci navāyatanāni, kassaci sattāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti –

"At the moment of arising in the sensual realm, for some, eleven bases appear; for some, ten bases; for some, another ten bases; for some, nine bases; for some, seven bases appear."

Vuttaṃ, na vuttaṃ “aṭṭhāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti. Tathā “dasāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti tikkhattuṃ vattabbaṃ siyā, aghānakaupapattiyā vijjamānāya tikkhattuñca “navāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti, na ca taṃ vuttaṃ. Evaṃ dhātupātubhāvādipañhesu yamakepi ghānajivhākāyānaṃ sahacāritā vuttāti.

This is said, but it is not said, 'eight bases appear.' Similarly, if the arising of beings without a nose existed, then 'ten bases appear' would have to be said a third time, and 'nine bases appear' a third time, but this is not said. Thus, in the questions on the appearance of elements, etc., even in the Yamaka, the concomitance of the nose, tongue, and body is stated.

Cutipaṭisandhīnaṃ khandhādīhi aññamaññaṃ samānatā abhedo, asamānatā bhedo. Nayamukhamattaṃ dassetvā vuttaṃ avuttañca sabbaṃ saṅgaṇhitvā āha “ayaṃ tāva arūpabhūmīsuyeva nayo”ti. Rūpārūpāvacarānaṃ upacārassa balavatāya tato cavitvā duggatiyaṃ upapatti natthīti “ekaccasugaticutiyā”ti āha. Ekaccaduggatipaṭisandhīti ettha ekaccaggahaṇassa payojanaṃ maggitabbaṃ. Ayaṃ panetthādhippāyo siyā – nānattakāyanānattasaññīsu vuttā ekacce vinipātikā tihetukādipaṭisandhikā, tesaṃ taṃ paṭisandhiṃ vinipātabhāvena duggatipaṭisandhīti gahetvā sabbasugaticutiyāva sā [M 0.0110] paṭisandhi hoti, na ekaccasugaticutiyā evāti taṃnivattanatthaṃ ekaccaduggatiggahaṇaṃ kataṃ. Apāyapaṭisandhi eva hi ekaccasugaticutiyā hoti, na [V 0.0109] sabbasugaticutiyā. Atha vā duggatipaṭisandhi duvidhā ekaccasugaticutiyā anantarā duggaticutiyā cāti. Tattha pacchimaṃ vajjetvā purimaṃ eva gaṇhituṃ āha “ekaccaduggatipaṭisandhī”ti. Ahetukacutiyā sahetukapaṭisandhīti duhetukā tihetukā ca yojetabbā. Maṇḍūkadevaputtādīnaṃ viya hi ahetukacutiyā tihetukapaṭisandhipi hotīti.

The similarity of decease and rebirth-linking in regard to the aggregates, etc., is non-difference; their dissimilarity is difference. Having shown just the entry point to the method and gathered together all that was said and unsaid, he says: 'This, for now, is the method only for the formless planes.' Because of the strength of the access concentration of those in the fine-material and formless spheres, there is no arising in a woeful destination after passing away from there; hence he says, 'from decease from some happy destinations.' In the phrase 'rebirth-linking in some woeful destinations,' the purpose of including the word 'some' should be investigated. The intention here might be this: some beings in a state of downfall, mentioned among those 'with diverse bodies and diverse perceptions,' have a triple-rooted rebirth-linking, etc. Taking that rebirth-linking of theirs as a woeful rebirth-linking because it is a state of downfall, that rebirth-linking follows decease from any happy destination, not just from some. To exclude that case, the term 'some woeful destination' is used. For rebirth-linking in the planes of misery follows only decease from some happy destinations, not from all happy destinations. Alternatively, rebirth-linking in a woeful destination is of two kinds: that immediately following decease from some happy destinations, and that immediately following decease from a woeful destination. Here, excluding the latter and taking only the former, he says, 'rebirth-linking in some woeful destinations.' In the phrase 'from a rootless decease, a rooted rebirth-linking,' both double-rooted and triple-rooted should be connected. For, as in the case of Maṇḍūka the devaputta, there can be a triple-rooted rebirth-linking even after a rootless decease.

Tassa tassa viparītato ca yathāyogaṃ yojetabbanti “ekaccasugaticutiyā ekaccaduggatipaṭisandhī”tiādīsu bhedavisesesu “ekaccaduggaticutiyā ekaccasugatipaṭisandhī”tiādinā yaṃ yaṃ yujjati, taṃ taṃ yojetabbanti attho. Yujjamānamattāpekkhanavasena napuṃsakaniddeso kato, yojetabbanti vā bhāvattho daṭṭhabbo. Amahaggatabahiddhārammaṇāya mahaggataajjhattārammaṇātiādīsu pana viparītayojanā na kātabbā. Na hi mahaggataajjhattārammaṇāya cutiyā arūpabhūmīsu amahaggatabahiddhārammaṇā paṭisandhi atthi. Catukkhandhāya arūpacutiyā pañcakkhandhā kāmāvacarapaṭisandhīti etassa vipariyāyo sayameva yojito. Atītārammaṇacutiyā paccuppannārammaṇā paṭisandhīti etassa ca vipariyāyo natthi evāti. Bhedaviseso eva ca evaṃ vitthārena dassito, abhedaviseso pana ekekasmiṃ bhede tattha tattheva cutipaṭisandhiyojanāvasena yojetabbo “pañcakkhandhāya kāmāvacarāya pañcakkhandhā kāmāvacarā…pe… avitakkaavicārāya avitakkaavicārā”ti, catukkhandhāya pana catukkhandhā sayameva yojitā. Eteneva nayena sakkā ñātunti pañcakkhandhādīsu abhedaviseso na dassitoti. Tato hetuṃ vināti tattha hetuṃ vinā.

And in each case, the opposite should be applied as appropriate. In distinctions such as 'from decease from a happy destination, rebirth in a woeful destination,' the meaning is that whatever is fitting should be applied, such as 'from decease from a woeful destination, rebirth in a happy destination,' and so on. The neuter gender is used with a view to what is merely fitting, or 'yojetabbaṃ' should be understood as a verbal noun. However, in cases like 'from a non-exalted, external object to an exalted, internal object,' the opposite application should not be made. For there is no rebirth with a non-exalted, external object in the formless realms after decease with an exalted, internal object. The reverse of 'from a four-aggregate decease in the formless realm to a five-aggregate rebirth in the sensual sphere' is already applied by itself. And there is no reverse for 'from a past-object decease to a present-object rebirth.' Thus, the distinctions have been shown in detail. As for the non-distinctions, in each case, the connection between decease and rebirth should be applied accordingly, such as 'from a five-aggregate in the sensual sphere to a five-aggregate in the sensual sphere… up to… from non-initial application and non-sustained application to non-initial application and non-sustained application.' For the four-aggregate, the four-aggregates are already applied by themselves. By this very method, it can be understood, and thus the non-distinctions in the five-aggregate and other cases are not shown. Then, 'without a cause' means 'without a cause' in that context.

Aṅgapaccaṅgasandhīnaṃ bandhanāni aṅgapaccaṅgasandhibandhanāni, tesaṃ chedakānaṃ. Niruddhesu cakkhādīsūti atimandabhāvūpagamanaṃ sandhāya vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Pañcadvārikaviññāṇānantarampi hi pubbe cuti dassitā. Yamake ca (yama. 1.āyatanayamaka.120) –

The bonds of the joints of limbs and minor limbs are the bonds of the joints of limbs and minor limbs; for those who cut them. When it is said 'when the eye and so on cease,' it should be understood as referring to the attainment of an extremely weak state. For even immediately after five-door consciousness, decease was shown previously. And in the Yamaka (Yam. 1. Āyatanayamaka.120) –

“Yassa [M 0.0111] cakkhāyatanaṃ nirujjhati, tassa manāyatanaṃ nirujjhatīti? Āmantā. Yassa vā pana manāyatanaṃ nirujjhati, tassa cakkhāyatanaṃ nirujjhatīti? Sacittakānaṃ acakkhukānaṃ cavantānaṃ tesaṃ manāyatanaṃ nirujjhati, no ca tesaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ nirujjhati. Sacakkhukānaṃ cavantānaṃ tesaṃ manāyatanañca nirujjhati, cakkhāyatanañca nirujjhatī”ti –

"When one's eye-base is ceasing, is one's mind-base ceasing? Yes. Or, when one's mind-base is ceasing, is one's eye-base ceasing? For those with consciousness but without eyes who are passing away, their mind-base is ceasing, but their eye-base is not ceasing. For those with eyes who are passing away, their mind-base is ceasing, and their eye-base is also ceasing."

Ādinā [V 0.0110] cakkhāyatanādīnaṃ cuticittena saha nirodho vuttoti. Laddho avaseso avijjādiko viññāṇassa paccayo etenāti laddhāvasesapaccayo, saṅkhāro. Avijjāpaṭicchāditādīnave tasmiṃ kammādivisaye paṭisandhiviññāṇassa ārammaṇabhāvena uppattiṭṭhānabhūte taṇhāya appahīnattā eva purimuppannāya ca santatiyā pariṇatattā paṭisandhiṭṭhānābhimukhaṃ viññāṇaṃ ninnapoṇapabbhāraṃ hutvā pavattatīti āha “taṇhā nāmetī”ti. Sahajātasaṅkhārāti cutiāsannajavanaviññāṇasahajātacetanā, sabbepi vā phassādayo. Tasmiṃ paṭisandhiṭṭhāne kammādivisaye viññāṇaṃ khipanti, khipantā viya tasmiṃ visaye paṭisandhivasena viññāṇapatiṭṭhānassa hetubhāvena pavattantīti attho.

By this, the cessation of the eye-base and so forth is said to occur together with the death-consciousness. The remainder, consisting of ignorance and the like, is obtained as a condition for consciousness by this; thus, it is called the 'condition of obtained remainder,' which is formations. Because craving has not been abandoned, and because the previously arisen continuity has matured, consciousness, due to the faults concealed by ignorance and so on, in that sphere of kamma and the like, which is the place of arising for rebirth-linking consciousness by way of object, flows toward the place of rebirth-linking, becoming inclined and sloping. Thus, it is said, 'Craving inclines it.' The co-nascent formations are the volition co-arisen with the death-proximate javana-consciousness, or all the associated mental factors like contact and so on. In that place of rebirth-linking, in the sphere of kamma and the like, they cast consciousness, or rather, as if casting, they function as the cause for the establishment of consciousness in that sphere by way of rebirth-linking—this is the meaning.

Tanti taṃ viññāṇaṃ, cutipaṭisandhitadāsannaviññāṇānaṃ santativasena viññāṇanti upanītekattaṃ. Taṇhāya nāmiyamānaṃ…pe… pavattatīti namanakhipanapurimanissayajahanāparanissayassādananissayarahitapavattanāni santativasena tassevekassa viññāṇassa honti, na aññassāti dasseti. Santativasenāti ca vadanto “tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati anañña”nti (ma. ni. 1.396) idañca micchāgāhaṃ paṭikkhipati. Sati hi nānattanaye santativasena ekattanayo hotīti. Orimatīrarukkhavinibaddharajju viya purimabhavattabhāvavinibandhaṃ kammādiārammaṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ, puriso viya viññāṇaṃ, tassa mātikātikkamanicchā viya taṇhā, atikkamanapayogo viya khipanakasaṅkhārā. Yathā ca so puriso paratīre patiṭṭhahamāno paratīrarukkhavinibaddhaṃ kiñci assādayamāno anassādayamāno vā kevalaṃ pathaviyaṃ sabalapayogeheva patiṭṭhāti, evamidampi bhavantarattabhāvavinibaddhaṃ hadayavatthunissayaṃ pañcavokārabhave assādayamānaṃ catuvokārabhave anassādayamānaṃ vā kevalaṃ ārammaṇasampayuttakammeheva pavattati. Tattha assādayamānanti pāpuṇantaṃ, paṭilabhamānanti attho.

That consciousness, by way of continuity of death-consciousness, rebirth-linking consciousness, and consciousness proximate to them, is brought to a unity as 'consciousness'. When it is said 'drawn by craving… it proceeds,' it shows that inclining, throwing, abandoning the former support, relishing the latter support, and proceeding without support all occur by way of continuity for that very same consciousness, not for another. And by speaking of continuity, the text rejects the wrong view: “This same consciousness wanders and transmigrates, not another” (Majjhima Nikāya 1.396). For when there is a mode of diversity, there is a mode of unity by way of continuity. Like a rope tied to a tree on this shore, one should see the object of kamma, etc., as bound to the state of existence in the previous life. Consciousness is like the man, his desire to cross the boundary is like craving, and the effort to cross is like the propelling formations. And just as that man, establishing himself on the far shore, whether relishing or not relishing something bound to a tree on the far shore, stands firmly on the ground solely by his own forceful effort, so too this consciousness, bound to the state of existence in the next life and supported by the heart-base, whether relishing in the five-constituent existence or not relishing in the four-constituent existence, proceeds solely by the kamma associated with the object. Here, 'relishing' means reaching, obtaining—that is the meaning.

Bhavantarādipaṭisandhānatoti [M 0.0112] bhavantarassa ādisambandhanato, bhavantarādayo vā bhavayonigativiññāṇaṭṭhitisattāvāsantarā, tesaṃ paṭisandhānatoti attho. Kammanti paṭisandhijanakaṃ kammaṃ. Saṅkhārāti cutiāsannajavanaviññāṇasahagatā khipanakasaṅkhārā.

Because of linking to another existence and so on (bhavantarādipaṭisandhānato) means because it connects to the beginning of another existence; or, 'another existence and so on' refers to the various realms, wombs, destinations, consciousness-stations, and abodes of beings, and the meaning is 'because of linking to them'. Kamma means the kamma that generates rebirth-linking. Saṅkhārā refers to the propelling formations accompanied by the death-proximate javana-consciousness.

Saddādihetukāti ettha paṭighoso saddahetuko, padīpo padīpantarādihetuko, muddā lañchanahetukā, chāyā ādāsādigatamukhādihetukā. Aññatra agantvā hontīti saddādipaccayadesaṃ [V 0.0111] agantvā saddādihetukā honti tato pubbe abhāvā, evamidampi paṭisandhiviññāṇaṃ na hetudesaṃ gantvā taṃhetukaṃ hoti tato pubbe abhāvā, tasmā na idaṃ hetudesato purimabhavato āgataṃ paṭighosādayo viya saddādidesato, nāpi tattha hetunā vinā uppannaṃ saddādīhi vinā paṭighosādayo viyāti attho. Atha vā aññatra agantvā hontīti pubbe paccayadese sannihitā hutvā tato aññatra gantvā tappaccayā na honti uppattito pubbe abhāvā, nāpi saddādipaccayā na honti, evamidampīti vuttanayena yojetabbaṃ. Esa nayoti bījaṅkurādīsu sabbahetuhetusamuppannesu yathāsambhavaṃ yojanā kātabbāti dasseti. Idhāpi hi hetuhetusamuppannaviññāṇānaṃ ekantamekatte sati na manussagatiko devagatibhūto siyā, ekantanānatte na kammavato phalaṃ siyā. Tato “rattassa bījaṃ, rattassa phala”ntiādikassa viya “bhūtapubbāhaṃ, bhante, rohitasso nāma isī”tiādikassa (saṃ. ni. 1.107) vohārassa lopo siyā, tasmā ettha santānabandhe sati hetuhetusamuppannesu na ekantameva ekatā vā nānatā vā upagantabbā. Ettha ca ekantaekatāpaṭisedhena “sayaṃkataṃ sukhaṃ dukkha”nti imaṃ diṭṭhiṃ nivāreti, ekantanānatāpaṭisedhena “paraṃkataṃ sukhaṃ dukkha”nti, hetuhetusamuppannabhāvavacanena “adhiccasamuppanna”nti. Etthāti ekasantāne.

When it is said 'caused by sound and so on,' here an echo is caused by sound, a lamp by another lamp and so on, an imprint by a seal, a shadow by a face in a mirror and so on. The meaning is that 'they arise without having gone elsewhere' means they arise caused by sound and so on without having gone to the location of the sound and other conditions, because they were absent before that. Similarly, this rebirth-linking consciousness does not go to the location of its cause and become caused by it, because it was absent before that. Therefore, this consciousness does not come from the location of its cause, from the previous existence, just as echoes and the like do not come from the location of their respective sounds; nor does it arise there without a cause, just as echoes and the like do not arise without their respective sounds. Alternatively, 'they arise without having gone elsewhere' means: they are not first present in the location of the condition and then, having gone elsewhere from there, become caused by it, because they are absent before their arising; nor are they not caused by sound and other conditions. This should be applied in the same way to the present case. 'This is the method' shows that in the case of seeds, sprouts, and so on—all things that arise from causes and conditions—the application should be made as is appropriate. Here too, if there were absolute identity for consciousnesses arising from causes and conditions, one who was a human being could not become a deva; and if there were absolute difference, the result of kamma would not accrue to the doer. Then, the conventional usage in statements like 'the seed of a red plant, the fruit of a red plant' and 'Venerable sir, I was formerly the seer named Rohitassa' (Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.107) would be lost. Therefore, in this context of the binding continuity, regarding things that arise from causes and conditions, neither absolute identity nor absolute difference should be accepted. Here, by rejecting absolute identity, the view 'pleasure and pain are self-made' is refuted; by rejecting absolute difference, the view 'pleasure and pain are made by another' is refuted; and by stating that things arise from causes and conditions, the view that 'they arise by chance' is refuted. 'Here' means in a single continuum.

Catumadhuraalattakarasādibhāvanā ambamātuluṅgādibījānaṃ abhisaṅkhāro. Ettha bījaṃ viya kammavā satto, abhisaṅkhāro viya kammaṃ, bījassa aṅkurādippabandho viya sattassa paṭisandhiviññāṇādippabandho, tatthuppannassa madhurassa rattakesarassa vā phalassa vā tasseva bījassa, tato eva ca abhisaṅkhārato bhāvo viya kammakārakasseva sattassa, taṃkammato eva [M 0.0113] ca phalassa bhāvo veditabbo. Bālasarīre kataṃ vijjāpariyāpuṇanaṃ sippasikkhanaṃ osadhappayogo ca na vuḍḍhasarīraṃ gacchanti. Atha ca taṃnimittaṃ vijjāpāṭavaṃ sippajānanaṃ anāmayatā ca vuḍḍhasarīre hoti, na ca taṃ aññassa hoti taṃsantatipariyāpanne eva vuḍḍhasarīre uppajjanato, na ca yathāpayuttena vijjāpariyāpuṇanādinā vinā aññato hoti tadabhāve abhāvato. Evamidhāpi santāne yaṃ phalaṃ, etaṃ nāññassa, na ca aññatoti yojetabbaṃ. Na aññatoti etena ca saṅkhārābhāve phalābhāvameva dasseti, nāññapaccayanivāraṇaṃ karoti.

The application of the four sweet substances, red lac dye, and so on, is the preparation of seeds like mango and citron. Here, the being who possesses kamma is like the seed, the kamma is like the preparation, the sequence of sprouts and so forth of the seed is like the sequence of rebirth-linking consciousness and so forth of the being. The arising of the sweet, red-filamented fruit there is from that very seed and from that very preparation; just so, the arising of the result should be understood as belonging to the very being who is the doer of the kamma and as coming from that very kamma. The learning of scriptures, the mastering of crafts, and the application of medicine done in a young body do not transfer to an old body. And yet, as a result of that, proficiency in learning, skill in crafts, and freedom from disease arise in the old body. These do not belong to another, for they arise in the old body that is included in that very continuum. Nor do they arise from another source without the applied effort of learning scriptures and so forth, for in the absence of the cause, there is an absence of the effect. Similarly here, whatever fruit arises in the continuum, it is not of another, nor is it from another; thus it should be understood. And by 'not from another,' it shows only the absence of the fruit in the absence of the formations; it does not preclude other conditions.

Yampi vuttaṃ, tattha vadāmāti vacanaseso. Tattha vā upabhuñjake asati siddhā bhuñjakasammutīti sambandho. Phalatīti sammuti phalatisammuti.

Regarding what was said, the remainder of the sentence is 'we will speak on that'. Or, the connection is this: even when there is no enjoyer, the convention of an 'enjoyer' is established. `Phalatisammuti` is the convention 'it fruits'.

Evaṃ [V 0.0112] santepīti asaṅkantipātubhāve, tattha ca yathāvuttadosapariharaṇe sati siddheti attho. Pavattito pubbeti kammāyūhanakkhaṇato pubbe. Pacchā cāti vipaccanapavattito pacchā ca. Avipakkavipākā katattā ce paccayā, vipakkavipākānampi katattaṃ samānanti tesampi phalāvahatā siyāti āsaṅkānivattanatthaṃ āha “na ca niccaṃ phalāvahā”ti. Na vijjamānattā vā avijjamānattā vāti etena vijjamānattaṃ avijjamānattañca nissāya vuttadoseva pariharati.

'Even so' means: when there is non-transmigration and arising, and when the aforementioned faults have been avoided, it is established. 'Prior to its proceeding' means before the moment of accumulating kamma. 'And later' refers to after the proceeding of the ripening. To dispel the doubt that, since causes are made while their results are unripened, and since the fact of having been made is the same for those whose results have ripened, these latter too might bear fruit, it is said, 'But they do not always bear fruit.' By the phrase 'Not by its existing, nor by its not existing,' he avoids the very faults that were stated with reference to existence and non-existence.

Tassā pāṭibhogakiriyāya, bhaṇḍakīṇanakiriyāya, iṇagahaṇādikiriyāya vā karaṇamattaṃ taṃkiriyākaraṇamattaṃ. Tadeva tadatthaniyyātane paṭibhaṇḍadāne iṇadāne ca paccayo hoti, aphalitaniyyātanādiphalanti attho.

The mere doing of that action is the mere doing of the act of guaranteeing, the act of buying goods, or the act of taking a loan. That very act becomes a condition for delivering for that purpose, for giving back the goods, and for repaying the debt. The meaning is that the result is the fruitful delivering and so on.

Avisesenāti “tihetuko tihetukassā”tiādikaṃ bhedaṃ akatvāva sāmaññato, piṇḍavasenāti attho. Sabbattha upanissayapaccayo balavakammassa vasena yojetabbo. “Dubbalañhi upanissayapaccayo na hotī”ti vakkhamānamevetaṃ paṭṭhānavaṇṇanāyanti. Avisesenāti sabbapuññābhisaṅkhāraṃ saha saṅgaṇhāti. Dvādasākusalacetanābhedoti ettha uddhaccasahagatā kasmā gahitāti vicāretabbametaṃ. Ekassa viññāṇassa tatheva paccayo paṭisandhiyaṃ, no pavatteti ekasseva paccayabhāvaniyamo paṭisandhiyaṃ, no pavatte. Pavatte hi sattannampi paccayoti adhippāyo. “Tathā kāmāvacaradevalokepi aniṭṭhā rūpādayo natthī”ti [M 0.0114] vuttaṃ, devānaṃ pana pubbanimittapātubhāvakāle milātamālādīnaṃ aniṭṭhatā kathaṃ na siyā.

'Without distinction' means generally, without making distinctions such as 'a three-rooted kamma for a three-rooted result'; the meaning is 'in a collective way'. Everywhere, the decisive-support condition should be connected by way of strong kamma. For it will be said in the commentary to the Paṭṭhāna: 'For a weak thing is not a decisive-support condition'. 'Without distinction' includes all meritorious formations together. Regarding the twelve types of unwholesome volition, it should be investigated here why the one accompanied by restlessness is included. For one consciousness, the condition is just so at rebirth-linking, not in the course of existence. Thus, the rule that it is a condition for only one applies at rebirth-linking, not in the course of existence. The intention is that in the course of existence, it is a condition for all seven. It is said, 'Similarly, in the deva-worlds of the sense sphere, there are no undesirable forms, etc.' But how could there not be undesirability for devas at the time when the preliminary signs of their passing appear, such as faded garlands?

Sveva dvīsu bhavesūti ettha ekūnatiṃsacetanābhedampi cittasaṅkhāraṃ cittasaṅkhārabhāvena ekattaṃ upanetvā “svevā”ti vuttaṃ. Tadekadeso pana kāmāvacaracittasaṅkhārova terasannaṃ navannañca paccayo daṭṭhabbo. Ekadesapaccayabhāvena hi samudāyo vuttoti.

Herein, regarding 'in the two existences only,' the mental formation, which is the twenty-nine kinds of volition, having been brought to oneness by way of being a mental formation, is referred to as 'that very one.' However, a portion of it, namely the sense-sphere mental formation alone, should be seen as the condition for the thirteen and the nine. For the aggregate is spoken of by way of being a partial condition.

Yattha ca vitthārappakāsanaṃ kataṃ, tato bhavato paṭṭhāya mukhamattappakāsanaṃ kātukāmo āha “ādito paṭṭhāyā”ti. Tena “dvīsu bhavesū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatiyajjhānabhūmivasenāti etena ekattakāyaekattasaññīsāmaññena catutthajjhānabhūmi ca asaññāruppavajjā gahitāti veditabbā. Yathāsambhavanti ekavīsatiyā kāmāvacararūpāvacarakusalavipākesu cuddasannaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte ca, sattannaṃ pavatte eva. Ayaṃ yathāsambhavo.

And where a detailed explanation has been given, from that existence onwards, wishing to give only a summary explanation, he said, 'Starting from the beginning.' Therefore, 'In two existences,' etc., was said. By 'by way of the third jhāna plane,' it should be understood that the fourth jhāna plane is also included—excluding the non-percipient and immaterial planes—due to the commonality of having a unified body and unified perception. 'As is possible' means: among the twenty-one sense-sphere and form-sphere wholesome resultants, fourteen operate in rebirth-linking and in the course of existence, and seven operate only in the course of existence. This is the meaning of 'as is possible'.

Catunnaṃ [V 0.0113] viññāṇānanti bhavādayo apekkhitvā vuttaṃ, catūsu antogadhānaṃ pana tiṇṇaṃ viññāṇānaṃ tīsu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu ca paccayabhāvo yojetabbo, aviññāṇake sattāvāse saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇe avijjamānepi tassa saṅkhārahetukattaṃ dassetuṃ “apicā”tiādimāha. Etasmiñca mukhamattappakāsane puññābhisaṅkhārādīnaṃ duggatiādīsu pavattiyaṃ kusalavipākādiviññāṇānaṃ paccayabhāvo bhavesu vuttanayeneva viññāyatīti na vuttoti veditabbo.

'Of the four consciousnesses' is said with reference to existence and so on. However, the conditionality of the three consciousnesses included within the four should be connected with the three stations of consciousness. Although consciousness conditioned by formations does not exist in the non-conscious abode of beings, to show that it has formations as its cause, he said, 'Moreover,' etc. And in this summary explanation, it should be understood that the conditionality of meritorious formations, etc., for wholesome resultant consciousness, etc., in the course of existence in bad destinations, etc., is not stated because it is understood by the same method explained in the section on existences.

Viññāṇapadaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the exposition of the term 'consciousness' is concluded.

Nāmarūpapadaniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of the Term 'Name-and-Form'

228. Suttantābhidhammesu nāmarūpadesanāviseso desanābhedo. Tayo khandhāti etaṃ yadipi pāḷiyaṃ natthi, atthato pana vuttameva hotīti katvā vuttanti veditabbaṃ.

228. The difference in the teaching of name-and-form in the Suttanta and Abhidhamma is a particularity of the teaching. Although the statement 'three aggregates' is not found in the Pāli text, it should be understood that it is stated because it is, in terms of meaning, indeed stated.

Aṇḍajānañca abhāvakānanti yojetabbaṃ. Santatisīsānīti kalāpasantānamūlāni. Yadipi vikārarūpāni paṭisandhikkhaṇe na santi, lakkhaṇaparicchedarūpāni [M 0.0115] pana santīti tāni aparinipphannāni paramatthato vivajjento āha “rūparūpato”ti.

And 'of the egg-born' should be connected with 'of those without.' 'Heads of continuity' means the roots of the continuity of groups. Although altered material phenomena are not present at the moment of rebirth-linking, characteristic and defining material phenomena are present. Therefore, rejecting these as not being ultimately accomplished, he says, 'from essential material form.'

Kāmabhave pana yasmā sesaopapātikānanti ettha kiñcāpi kāmabhave “opapātikā”ti vuttā na santi, yena sesaggahaṇaṃ sātthakaṃ bhaveyya, aṇḍajagabbhaseyyakehi pana opapātikasaṃsedajā sesā hontīti sesaggahaṇaṃ katanti veditabbaṃ. Atha vā brahmakāyikādikehi opapātikehi vuttehi sese sandhāya “sesaopapātikāna”nti āha. Te pana arūpinopi santīti “kāmabhave”ti vuttaṃ, aparipuṇṇāyatanānaṃ pana nāmarūpaṃ yathāsambhavaṃ rūpamissakaviññāṇaniddese vuttanayena sakkā dhammagaṇanāto viññātunti na vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

However, in the sense-sphere existence, regarding the phrase 'of the remaining spontaneously born beings': although in the sense-sphere existence there are no beings called 'spontaneously born' in such a way that the inclusion of 'remaining' would be meaningful, it should be understood that the inclusion of 'remaining' is made because the spontaneously born and moisture-born are what remain after the egg-born and womb-born. Alternatively, he says 'of the remaining spontaneously born beings' with reference to the remainder after the spontaneously born, such as the Brahmakāyika devas, have been mentioned. But since those also exist as formless beings, 'in the sense-sphere existence' is stated. However, it should be seen that the name-and-form of those with incomplete sense bases is not stated, because it can be known from the enumeration of phenomena, as is possible, by the method explained in the exposition of consciousness mixed with form.

Avakaṃsato dve aṭṭhakāneva utucittasamuṭṭhānāni hontīti sasaddakālaṃ sandhāya “ukkaṃsato dvinnaṃ navakāna”nti vuttaṃ. Pubbeti khandhavibhaṅgeti vadanti. Tattha hi “ekekacittakkhaṇe [V 0.0114] tikkhattuṃ uppajjamāna”nti vuttaṃ. Idheva vā vuttaṃ santatidvayādikaṃ sattakapariyosānaṃ sandhāyāha “pubbe vuttaṃ kammasamuṭṭhānaṃ sattatividha”nti, taṃ panuppajjamānaṃ ekekacittakkhaṇe tikkhattuṃ uppajjatīti iminādhippāyena vuttaṃ “ekekacittakkhaṇe tikkhattuṃ uppajjamāna”nti. Catuddisā vavatthāpitāti aññamaññasaṃsaṭṭhasīsā mūlena catūsu disāsu vavatthāpitā aññamaññaṃ āliṅgetvā ṭhitā bhinnavāhanikā viya.

At minimum, only two octads originate from temperature and consciousness. Referring to a time when there is sound, it is said, 'at maximum, two nonads.' 'Previously'—they say this refers to the Analysis of Aggregates. For there it is said, 'arising three times in each mind-moment.' Or, referring to what is stated here—the two continuities, etc., ending with the heptad—he says, 'the previously stated sevenfold kamma-originated.' But that, arising, arises three times in each mind-moment; with this intention it is said, 'arising three times in each mind-moment.' 'Established in the four directions' means: with heads intermingled, established by their roots in the four directions, they stand embracing one another, like separate caravans.

Pañcavokārabhave ca pavattiyanti rūpājanakakammajaṃ pañcaviññāṇappavattikālaṃ sahajātaviññāṇapaccayañca sandhāyāha. Tadā hi tato nāmameva hotīti, kammaviññāṇapaccayā pana sadāpi ubhayaṃ hotīti sakkā vattuṃ, pacchājātaviññāṇapaccayā ca rūpaṃ upatthaddhaṃ hotīti. Asaññesūtiādi kammaviññāṇapaccayaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, pañcavokārabhave ca pavattiyanti bhavaṅgādijanakakammato aññena rūpuppattikālaṃ nirodhasamāpattikālaṃ bhavaṅgādiuppattikālato aññakālañca sandhāya vuttanti yuttaṃ. Bhavaṅgādiuppattikāle hi taṃjanakeneva kammunā uppajjamānaṃ rūpaṃ, so ca vipāko kammaviññāṇapaccayo hotīti sakkā vattuṃ. Sahajātaviññāṇapaccayānapekkhampi hi pavattiyaṃ kammena pavattamānaṃ rūpaṃ nāmañca na kammaviññāṇānapekkhaṃ hotīti. Sabbatthāti paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte ca. Sahajātaviññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ, kammaviññāṇapaccayā ca nāmarūpañca yathāsambhavaṃ yojetabbaṃ. Nāmañca [M 0.0116] rūpañca nāmarūpañca nāmarūpanti ettha nāmarūpa-saddo attano ekadesena nāma-saddena nāma-saddassa sarūpo, rūpa-saddena ca rūpa-saddassa, tasmā “sarūpānaṃ ekaseso”ti nāmarūpa-saddassa ṭhānaṃ itaresañca nāmarūpa-saddānaṃ adassanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

'And in the five-constituent existence, in the course of life'—he says this referring to the time of the occurrence of the five sense-consciousnesses born of kamma that does not generate form, and with reference to co-nascent consciousness as a condition. For at that time, only name arises from that. But it can be said that both always arise conditioned by kamma-consciousness, and material form is supported by post-nascent consciousness as a condition. 'In the non-percipient beings,' etc., is said with reference to kamma-consciousness as a condition. And 'in the five-constituent existence, in the course of life' is appropriately said with reference to the time of the arising of form from kamma other than that which generates the life-continuum, etc., to the time of the attainment of cessation, and to a time other than the time of the arising of the life-continuum, etc. For at the time of the arising of the life-continuum, etc., the material form that arises is produced by that very kamma which generates it, and it can be said that that resultant is conditioned by kamma-consciousness. For in the course of life, even material form proceeding from kamma without dependence on co-nascent consciousness as a condition, and name, are not independent of kamma-consciousness. 'Everywhere' means at rebirth-linking and in the course of life. Name-and-form conditioned by co-nascent consciousness, and name-and-form conditioned by kamma-consciousness, should be connected as is possible. Herein, in 'name, form, and name-and-form are nāmarūpa,' the word 'nāmarūpa', by its own component part, is identical in form with the word 'nāma' through the word 'nāma', and with the word 'rūpa' through the word 'rūpa'. Therefore, the presence of the word 'nāmarūpa' and the absence of the other words should be seen as an 'ellipsis of identical forms'.

Vipākato aññaṃ avipākaṃ. Yato dvidhā mataṃ, tato yuttameva idanti yojetabbaṃ. Kusalādicittakkhaṇeti ādi-saddena akusalakiriyacittakkhaṇe viya vipākacittakkhaṇepi vipākājanakakammasamuṭṭhānaṃ saṅgahitanti veditabbaṃ. Vipākacittakkhaṇe pana abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇapaccayā pubbe vuttanayena ubhayañca upalabbhatīti tādisavipākacittakkhaṇavajjanatthaṃ “kusalādicittakkhaṇe”ti vuttaṃ.

Other than resultant is non-resultant. Since it is considered twofold, it is proper that this should be connected thus. In 'at the moment of wholesome consciousness, etc.,' by the word 'etc.' it should be understood that what is originated by kamma that does not generate a resultant is included, as at the moment of unwholesome and functional consciousness, and also at the moment of resultant consciousness. However, at the moment of resultant consciousness, conditioned by formational consciousness, both are found, according to the method previously stated. Therefore, for the purpose of excluding such moments of resultant consciousness, the phrase 'at the moment of wholesome consciousness, etc.' is stated.

Suttantikapariyāyenāti paṭṭhāne rūpānaṃ upanissayapaccayassa avuttattā vuttaṃ, suttante pana “yasmiṃ sati yaṃ hoti, asati ca na hoti, so tassa upanissayo nidānaṃ hetu pabhavo”ti [V 0.0115] katvā “viññāṇūpanisaṃ nāmarūpa”nti rūpassa ca viññāṇūpanissayatā vuttā. Vanapatthapariyāye ca vanasaṇḍagāmanigamanagarajanapadapuggalūpanissayo iriyāpathavihāro, tato ca cīvarādīnaṃ jīvitaparikkhārānaṃ kasirena ca appakasirena ca samudāgamanaṃ vuttaṃ, na ca vanasaṇḍādayo ārammaṇūpanissayādibhāvaṃ iriyāpathānaṃ cīvarādisamudāgamanassa ca bhajanti, tasmā vinā abhāvo eva ca suttantapariyāyato upanissayabhāvo daṭṭhabbo. Nāmassa abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇaṃ kammārammaṇapaṭisandhiādikāle ārammaṇapaccayova hotīti vattabbameva natthīti rūpasseva suttantikapariyāyato ekadhā paccayabhāvo vutto. Sasaṃsayassa hi rūpassa taṃpaccayo hotīti vutte nāmassa hotīti vattabbameva natthīti.

'By the Suttanta method' is said because in the Paṭṭhāna the decisive support condition for material phenomena is not stated. In the Suttas, however, having said, 'When this exists, that is; when this is absent, that is not. That is its decisive support, source, cause, origin,' the status of consciousness as a decisive support for material form is also stated by 'name-and-form has consciousness as its decisive support.' And in the Vanapattha Sutta method, the decisive support of forests, groves, villages, towns, cities, districts, and individuals for one's posture and way of living is stated, and from that, the acquisition of robes and other life-requisites with or without difficulty is stated. But forests, groves, and so on do not partake of the state of being an object-decisive-support, etc., for one's posture or for the acquisition of robes. Therefore, the state of being a decisive support according to the Suttanta method should be seen as simply that without which the effect is not. For name, formational consciousness is only an object condition at the time of kamma, object, rebirth-linking, etc., so there is nothing to be said. Thus, for material form alone, the state of being a condition is stated in one way according to the Suttanta method. For when it is said that it is a condition for material form, about which there is some doubt, there is nothing to be said about it being so for name.

Pavattassa pākaṭattā apākaṭaṃ paṭisandhiṃ gahetvā pucchati “kathaṃ paneta”ntiādinā. Suttato nāmaṃ, yuttito rūpaṃ viññāṇapaccayā hotīti jānitabbaṃ. Yuttito sādhetvā suttena taṃ daḷhaṃ karonto “kammasamuṭṭhānassapi hī”tiādimāha. Cittasamuṭṭhānassevāti cittasamuṭṭhānassa viya. Yasmā nāmarūpameva pavattamānaṃ dissati, tasmā tadeva vadantena anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ. Suññatāpakāsanañhi dhammacakkappavattananti adhippāyo. Nāmarūpamattatāvacaneneva vā pavattiyā dukkhasaccamattatā vuttā, dukkhasaccappakāsanena ca tassa samudayo, tassa ca [M 0.0117] nirodho, nirodhagāmī ca maggo pakāsito eva hoti. Ahetukassa dukkhassa hetunirodhā, anirujjhanakassa ca abhāvā, nirodhassa ca upāyena vinā anadhigantabbattāti catusaccappakāsanaṃ dhammacakkappavattanaṃ yojetabbaṃ.

Because what is occurring is manifest, taking up the unmanifest rebirth-linking, he asks, 'But how is this?' and so on. Name is to be known from the Sutta; that form is conditioned by consciousness is to be known from reasoning. Having established it by reasoning and strengthening it with the Sutta, he says, 'For even that which has arisen from kamma,' and so on. 'Like that which has arisen from mind' means 'like that which has arisen from mind.' Because only name-and-form is seen occurring, therefore, by stating just that, the unsurpassed Wheel of Dhamma was set in motion. For the declaration of emptiness is indeed the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma—this is the intended meaning. Or, by the mere statement of the bare fact of name-and-form, the bare fact of the truth of suffering in the course of existence is stated. And by the declaration of the truth of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path leading to its cessation are indeed declared. Because suffering is not without a cause and its cause ceases, and because there is nothing that does not cease, and because cessation is unattainable without a means—thus, the declaration of the Four Noble Truths should be connected with the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma.

Nāmarūpapadaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Section on Name-and-Form is concluded.

Saḷāyatanapadaniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of the Section on the Six Sense Bases

229. Niyamatoti ca idaṃ catunnaṃ bhūtānaṃ, channaṃ vatthūnaṃ, jīvitassa ca yathāsambhavaṃ sahajātanissayapurejātaindriyādinā ekantena saḷāyatanassa pavattamānassa paccayabhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Rūpāyatanādīnaṃ pana sahajātanissayānupālanabhāvo natthīti aggahaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Ārammaṇārammaṇapurejātādibhāvo [V 0.0116] ca tesaṃ na santatipariyāpannānameva, na ca cakkhādīnaṃ viya ekappakārenevāti aniyamato paccayabhāvo. Niyamato…pe… jīvitindriyanti evanti ettha evaṃ-saddena vā rūpāyatanādīnampi saṅgaho veditabbo. Chaṭṭhāyatanañca saḷāyatanañca saḷāyatananti ettha yadipi chaṭṭhāyatanasaḷāyatana-saddānaṃ saddato sarūpatā natthi, atthato pana saḷāyatanekadesova chaṭṭhāyatananti ekadesasarūpatā atthīti ekadesasarūpekaseso katoti veditabbo. Atthatopi hi sarūpānaṃ ekadesasarūpekasesaṃ icchanti “vaṅko ca kuṭilo ca kuṭilā”ti, tasmā atthato ekadesasarūpānañca ekasesena bhavitabbanti.

229. And this term 'necessarily' is stated with reference to the fact that the four great elements, the six physical bases, and the life faculty are conditions for the occurring six sense bases, exclusively and as is possible, by way of co-nascence, support, pre-nascence, faculty, and so on. However, it should be understood that the form-base and other such bases are not included because they do not have the nature of co-nascent support and maintenance. And their nature as object, object-pre-nascence, etc., does not pertain only to those included in one's own continuity, nor is it of a single kind like that of the eye, etc.; thus, their conditionality is not fixed. In the phrase 'Necessarily... up to... life faculty thus,' by this word 'thus,' the inclusion of the form-base and so on should also be understood. As for 'the sixth sense base and the six sense bases are the six sense bases,' although the words 'sixth sense base' and 'six sense bases' are not identical in form, in meaning the sixth sense base is merely a part of the six sense bases. Thus, there is a partial identity of form, and it should be understood that a single-residue formation based on partial identity of form has been made. For they accept a single-residue formation based on partial identity of form even for things that are identical in meaning, as in 'crooked and bent are bent.' Therefore, for things with partial identity of form in meaning, there must also be a single-residue formation.

Atha vā chaṭṭhāyatanañca manāyatanañca chaṭṭhāyatananti vā, manāyatananti vā, chaṭṭhāyatanañca chaṭṭhāyatanañca chaṭṭhāyatananti vā, manāyatanañca manāyatanañca manāyatananti vā ekasesaṃ katvā cakkhādīhi saha “saḷāyatana”nti vuttanti tameva ekasesaṃ nāmamattapaccayassa, nāmarūpapaccayassa ca manāyatanassa vasena kataṃ atthato dassento āha “chaṭṭhāyatanañca saḷāyatanañca saḷāyatananti evaṃ katekasesassā”ti. Yathāvuttopi hi ekaseso atthato chaṭṭhāyatanañca saḷāyatanañcāti evaṃ kato nāma hotīti. Sabbattha ca ekasese kate ekavacananiddeso [M 0.0118] katekasesānaṃ saḷāyatanādisaddavacanīyatāsāmaññavasena katoti daṭṭhabbo. Abyākatavāre vakkhatīti kiñcāpi akusalavāre kusalavāre ca “nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatana”nti vuttaṃ, suttantabhājanīye pana vipākachaṭṭhāyatanameva gahitanti adhippāyena abyākatavārameva sādhakabhāvena udāhaṭanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Paccayanaye pana “chaṭṭhā hoti taṃ avakaṃsato”tiādinā avipākassapi paccayo uddhaṭo, so niravasesaṃ vattukāmatāya uddhaṭoti veditabbo. Idha saṅgahitanti idha ekasesanayena saṅgahitaṃ, tattha abyākatavāre lokiyavipākabhājanīye vibhattanti veditabbanti adhippāyo.
