An unevenly cut bundle leaks water unevenly; similarly, to show that the body leaks unevenly through the pores of the hair and other openings—above, below, and across—the term 'unevenly cut' is used.

Atikaṭukaaccuṇhādiko visabhāgāhāro uṇhakāle pavattamānānaṃ dhātūnaṃ visabhāgattā.

Incompatible food, such as that which is excessively pungent or excessively hot, is so called because of its incompatibility with the elements active during the hot season.

Ekattārammaṇabaleneva vāti vikkhambhitanīvaraṇena susamāhitacittena upaṭṭhitassa nānārammaṇavipphandanavirahena ekasabhāvassa ārammaṇassa vasena. Tañhi ekattārammaṇaṃ upaṭṭhahamānameva attani abhiratiṃ, sātisayaṃ pharaṇapītiṃ, iṭṭhākārānubhavanañca somanassaṃ uppādeti. Na hi abhiratisomanassehi vinā anatikkantapītisukhassa ekattupaṭṭhānaṃ atthīti.

Or by the power of a single object—that is, by means of an object of a single nature for one whose mind is well-concentrated with hindrances suppressed, and who is free from the agitation of diverse objects. For that single object, when present, generates delight in oneself, excellent pervasive joy, and gladness in experiencing desirable aspects. For without delight and gladness, there is no establishing of oneness for one who has not surpassed joy and happiness.

Avisesato [V 0.0152] pana sādhāraṇavasenāti paṭikūladhātuvaṇṇavisesaṃ akatvā samathavipassanāsādhāraṇavasenāti attho. Tividhenāti anulomādinā vakkhamānena. Cha māseti addhamāse ūnepi māsaparicchedena paricchijjamāne sajjhāye cha māsā paricchedakā hontīti katvā vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Paricchijjamānassa māsantaragamananivāraṇañhi chamāsaggahaṇaṃ, na sakalachamāse parivattadassanatthaṃ. Ācariyāti aṭṭhakathācariyā.

Generally, in a shared manner—meaning without making a distinction in the color of the repulsive element, but in a manner common to serenity and insight. Threefold—by way of the forthcoming method beginning with the forward order. Six months—it should be understood that this is said because, when defining by a limit of months, even if it is less than half a month short, six months are taken as the limit for the recitation. For the taking of six months is to prevent the passing of another month for what is being defined, not for the purpose of seeing a complete six-month cycle. Teachers—the commentary teachers.

Lakkhaṇanti dhātupaṭikūlalakkhaṇaṃ. Janaṃ na arahantīti ajaññā, jane pavesetuṃ ayuttā jigucchanīyāti vuttaṃ hoti.

Characteristic—the characteristic of the repulsiveness of the elements. 'Not worthy of people' (ajaññā) means unsuitable to be introduced among people, disgusting; this is what is said.

Paṭipāṭiyā aṭṭhīnīti paṭipāṭiyā aṭṭhīni koṭiyā ṭhitāni. Na ettha koci attā nāma atthi, aṭṭhīni eva aṭṭhipuñjamatto evāyaṃ saṅghāṭoti dasseti[M 0.0154]. Anekasandhiyamitoti anekehi sandhīhi yamito sambaddho so aṭṭhipuñjoti dasseti. Na kehicīti yamentaṃ attānaṃ paṭisedheti. Codito jarāya maraṇābhimukhagamanena codito.

The bones are in order—the bones are placed in order at the end. Here there is no self whatsoever; it shows that this framework is just bones, merely a heap of bones. Bound by many joints—it shows that this heap of bones is restrained and connected by many joints. Not by anyone—it denies a self that restrains it. Urged on—urged on by decay, by the going towards death.

Mahābhūtaṃ upādārūpena paricchinnaṃ “nīlaṃ pītaṃ sugandhaṃ duggandha”ntiādinā. Upādārūpaṃ mahābhūtena tannissitassa tassa tato bahi abhāvā. Chāyātapānaṃ ātapapaccayachāyuppādakabhāvo aññamaññaparicchedakatā. Rūpakkhandhassa pariggahitattā tadantogadhānaṃ cakkhādiāyatanadvārānaṃ vasena taṃtaṃdvārikā arūpino khandhā pākaṭā honti, āyatanāni ca dvārāni ca āyatanadvārānīti vā attho. Tena rūpāyatanādīnañca vasenāti vuttaṃ hoti.

The great elements are defined by derived form, such as 'blue, yellow, fragrant, foul-smelling,' and so on. Derived form is defined by the great elements, because, being dependent on them, it does not exist outside of them. The mutual defining of shade and sunlight is the fact that sunlight is the condition for the arising of shade. Because the form aggregate is comprehended, the formless aggregates, which have their respective doors, become manifest by means of the sense-base doors, such as the eye, which are included within it. Or, the meaning is that sense bases and doors are 'sense-base doors.' Therefore, it is said to be by means of the form sense-base and so on.

Sappaccayāti sappaccayabhāvā, paccayāyattaṃ hutvā nibbattanti vuttaṃ hoti. Samāno vā sadiso yutto paccayo sappaccayo, tasmā sappaccayā.

'With conditions' means because of the state of having conditions; it is said that they arise having become dependent on conditions. Or, a similar, corresponding, suitable condition is a 'good condition' (sappaccayo); therefore, they are 'with conditions' (sappaccayā).

Ettakoti yathāvuttena ākārena paguṇo koṭṭhāso. Uggahova uggahasandhi. Vaṇṇādimukhena hi upaṭṭhānaṃ ettha sandhīyati sambajjhatīti “sandhī”ti vuccati.

'This much' is the portion that is proficient in the manner described. Learning itself is the 'learning-connection.' For because the appearance by way of color and so on is joined and connected here, it is called a 'connection' (sandhi).

Upaṭṭhātīti vaṇṇādivasena upaṭṭhātīti attho. Pañcaṅgasamannāgateti nātidūranāccāsannagamanāgamanasampannanti ekaṅgaṃ, divā abbokiṇṇaṃ rattiṃ appasaddaṃ appanigghosanti ekaṃ, appaḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassanti [V 0.0153] ekaṃ, tasmiṃ kho pana senāsane viharantassa appakasirena uppajjati cīvara…pe… parikkhāroti ekaṃ, tasmiṃ pana senāsane therā bhikkhū viharanti bahussutāti ekaṃ (a. ni. 10.11). Pañcaṅgasamannāgatenāti appābādhāsāṭheyyasaddhāpaññāvīriyehi padhāniyaṅgehi samannāgatena.

'It appears' means it appears by way of color and so on. 'Endowed with five factors' means: not too far and not too near, suitable for coming and going—this is one factor; by day, uncrowded, by night, quiet and with little noise—this is one factor; with few gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things—this is one factor; for one dwelling in such a lodging, robes… and other requisites arise with little difficulty—this is one factor; in that lodging, elder monks dwell who are very learned—this is one factor (AN 10.11). 'Endowed with five factors' means endowed with the factors of striving: few illnesses, honesty, faith, wisdom, and energy.

Uṭṭhānakadāyanti tehi khettehi uṭṭhānakaṃ, tehi dātabbadhaññanti attho. Ettha ca aṭṭhakumbhadāyakakhettaṃ viya mukhadhovanakiccaṃ, soḷasakumbhadāyakaṃ viya khādanabhuñjanakiccaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ lahukagarukabhāvato. Tato pana yaṃ dukkhaṃ nibbattati, taṃ aññañca dvattiṃsākāramanasikārena ca nivattatīti āha “ettheva kammaṃ kātabba”nti. Ettāvatāti ekadivasaṃ tiṃsa vāre manasikāraṭṭhapanena.

'Yielding produce' means the produce from those fields, that is, the grain to be given from them. And here, the task of washing the face should be seen as like a field yielding eight pots, and the task of eating and consuming as like a field yielding sixteen pots, due to their respective lightness and heaviness. Furthermore, the suffering that arises from that, and other suffering, is averted by the contemplation of the thirty-two parts; thus he said, 'Here the work must be done.' 'By this much' means by establishing the contemplation thirty times in a single day.

Sahassuddhāraṃ [M 0.0155] sādhetvāti sahassavaḍḍhitaṃ iṇaṃ yojetvā. Uddharitabboti uddhāroti hi vaḍḍhi vuccatīti. Suddhacittenāti vikkhepādikilesavirahitacittena. Kesādīsu tace rajjantā succhavicammaṃ tacoti gahetvā “suvaṇṇādivaṇṇo me taco”tiādinā rajjanti.

'Having settled a thousandfold interest' means having settled a debt increased a thousandfold. For interest is called 'extraction' (uddhāro) because it is to be extracted. 'With a pure mind' means with a mind free from defilements such as distraction. Among hair and so on, those who delight in the skin, taking the fine-complexioned hide as 'skin,' delight in it, saying, 'My skin is the color of gold,' and so on.

Tesu dve ekamaggaṃ paṭipajjamānā nāma na hontīti yathā tathā vā palāyantīti attho. Tattha rāgādivatthubhāvena dvattiṃsākārānaṃ corasadisatā anatthāvahatā daṭṭhabbā.

The meaning is that those two are not ones who travel the same path, but flee this way and that. Therein, the resemblance of the thirty-two parts to thieves should be seen in their bringing of harm by being a basis for lust and so on.

Kammameva visesādhigamassa ṭhānanti kammaṭṭhānaṃ bhāvanā vuccati. Tenāha “manasikarontassa appanaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti. Kammassa vā bhāvanāya ṭhānaṃ ārammaṇaṃ appanārammaṇabhāvūpagamanena appanaṃ pāpuṇātīti vuttaṃ.

Meditation is called a 'basis of work' (kammaṭṭhāna) because work itself is the basis for the attainment of distinction. Therefore, he said, 'For one who gives attention, it reaches absorption.' Or, it is said that the basis of the work of meditation is the object, and it reaches absorption by arriving at the state of being an absorption-object.

Mānajātikoti etena laṅghanasamatthatāyogena upasamarahitataṃ dasseti. Cittampi hi tathā nānārammaṇesu vaḍḍhitaṃ upasamarahitanti dassetabbanti.

'Of a proud breed'—by this, through its possession of the ability to leap, it shows its lack of tranquility. For it should be shown that the mind, too, when it has grown amidst various objects, is likewise lacking in tranquility.

Hatthe gahitapañhavatthu pākatikamevāti visuddhimagge vuttataṃ sandhāyāha. Tattha hi vuttaṃ –

He says, 'The subject matter of the question taken in hand is just natural,' with reference to what was said in the Visuddhimagga. For there it is said:

“Mālakatthero kira dīghabhāṇakaabhayattheraṃ hatthe gahetvā ‘āvuso abhaya, imaṃ tāva [V 0.0154] pañhaṃ uggaṇhāhī’ti vatvā āha ‘mālakatthero dvattiṃsakoṭṭhāsesu dvattiṃsapaṭhamajjhānalābhī, sace rattiṃ ekaṃ, divā ekaṃ samāpajjati, atirekaḍḍhamāsena puna sampajjati. Sace pana devasikaṃ ekameva samāpajjati, atirekamāsena puna sampajjatī’”ti.

It is said that the Elder Mālaka, taking the Elder Abhaya the Dīghabhāṇaka by the hand, said, 'Friend Abhaya, first learn this question.' Then he said, 'The Elder Mālaka is an obtainer of the thirty-two first jhānas in the thirty-two parts. If he attains it once at night and once during the day, it is accomplished again in over half a month. But if he attains it just once daily, it is accomplished again in over a month.'

Idaṃ pana ekaṃ manasikarontassa ekaṃ pāṭiyekkaṃ manasikarontassa dvattiṃsāti etassa sādhanatthaṃ nidassanavasena ānītanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

This, however, should be seen as brought as an illustration for the purpose of proving this: 'For one who contemplates one part, it is one; for one who contemplates each part individually, it is thirty-two.'

Anupādinnakapakkhe ṭhitānīti etena cetiyapabbatavāsī mahātissatthero viya, saṅgharakkhitattherupaṭṭhākasāmaṇero viya ca anupādinnakapakkhe ṭhapetvā gahetuṃ sakkontassa dasavidhāsubhavasena jīvamānakasarīrepi upaṭṭhite upacārappatti dassitā hotīti veditabbā. “Atthissa kāye”ti pana sattavasena kesādīsu gayhamānesu yathā “imasmiṃ [M 0.0156] kāye”ti satta-ggahaṇarahite ahaṃkāravatthumhi viddhastāhaṃkāre sadā sannihite pākaṭe ca attano kāye upaṭṭhānaṃ hoti, na tathā tatthāti appanaṃ appattā ādīnavānupassanāva tattha hotīti adhippāyenāha “asubhānupassanāsaṅkhātā pana vipassanābhāvanā hotīti veditabbā”ti.

By 'those standing on the side of the non-appropriated'—by this it should be known that for one who is able, like the great elder Mahātissa who lived at Cetiyapabbata or the novice attendant of the elder Saṅgharakkhita, to take it after placing it on the side of the non-appropriated, the attainment of access concentration is shown by way of the tenfold foulness even when it appears in a living body. But as for 'in his body,' when hair, etc., are grasped by way of a 'being,' mindfulness is not established in the same way as it is in one's own body—which is always present and manifest, the basis for 'I-making' where the grasping of a 'being' is absent and 'I-making' is destroyed. Thus, because absorption is not attained, there is only the contemplation of danger. With this intention, he says, 'It should be known that there is only the development of insight, designated as the contemplation of the foul.'

357. Ādimhi sevanā āsevanā, vaḍḍhanaṃ bhāvanā, punappunaṃ karaṇaṃ bahulīkammanti ayametesaṃ viseso.

357. 'Repeated practice' (āsevanā) is pursuing in the beginning; 'cultivation' (bhāvanā) is development; 'making much of' (bahulīkammaṃ) is doing again and again—this is the distinction among these.

362. Vatthupariññāyāti abhijjhādomanassānaṃ vatthubhūtassa kāyassa parijānanena. Appitāti gamitā, sā ca vināsitatāti āha “vināsitā”ti. Appavattiyaṃ ṭhapitātipi appitāti ayamattho niruttisiddhiyā vuttoti daṭṭhabbo. Vigatantā katāti idāni kātabbo anto etesaṃ natthīti vigatantā, evaṃbhūtā katāti attho. Kammameva visesādhigamassa ṭhānaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ, kamme vā ṭhānaṃ bhāvanārambho kammaṭṭhānaṃ, tañca anupassanāti āha “anupassanāya kammaṭṭhāna”nti, anupassanāya vuttanti adhippāyo.

362. 'By full understanding of the basis' means by fully understanding the body which has become the basis for covetousness and displeasure. 'Applied' means sent forth; and that means destroyed, thus he said 'destroyed.' It should be seen that this meaning, 'placed in non-occurrence,' is also said for 'applied' through etymological derivation. 'Made to have their end gone' means their end to be made now does not exist, thus 'their end gone'; the meaning is 'made to be such.' Work itself is the basis for the attainment of distinction, hence 'meditation subject' (kammaṭṭhāna); or, the basis in the work is the start of cultivation, hence 'meditation subject.' And that is contemplation; thus he said 'the meditation subject of contemplation,' the intention being 'said by way of contemplation'.

Kāyānupassanāniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the exposition of the contemplation of the body is finished.

Vedanānupassanāniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Contemplation of Feeling

363. Sampajānassa [V 0.0155] vediyanaṃ sampajānavediyanaṃ. Vatthunti sukhādīnaṃ ārammaṇamāha, tena vatthu ārammaṇaṃ etissāti vatthuārammaṇāti samāso daṭṭhabbo. Vohāramattaṃ hotīti etena “sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī”ti idaṃ vohāramattena vuttanti dasseti.

363. The experiencing of one who is clearly comprehending is 'experiencing with clear comprehension'. By 'basis', it refers to the object of pleasure and so on; thereby, the compound 'basis-as-object' should be understood as 'that which has the basis as its object'. By 'it is a mere convention', it shows that the statement 'I feel a pleasant feeling' is spoken merely by way of convention.

Vīriyasamādhiṃ yojetvāti adhivāsanavīriyassa adhimattatāya tassa samatāya ubhayaṃ saha yojetvā. Saha paṭisambhidāhīti lokuttarapaṭisambhidāhi saha. Lokiyānampi vā sati uppattikāle tattha samatthataṃ sandhāya “saha paṭisambhidāhī”ti vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Samasīsīti vārasamasīsī hutvā paccavekkhaṇavārassa anantaravāre parinibbāyīti [M 0.0157] attho. Saṅkhepamanasikāravasena mahāsatipaṭṭhāne, vitthāramanasikāravasena rāhulovādadhātuvibhaṅgādīsu.

'Having yoked energy and concentration' means having yoked both together through the excellence of the energy of endurance and its balance. 'Together with the analytical knowledges' means together with the supramundane analytical knowledges. Or, it should be understood that 'together with the analytical knowledges' is said with reference to the competence of even the mundane ones therein at the time of their arising. 'With heads level' means having become one whose turn has a level head, he attains final Nibbāna in the turn immediately following the turn of reviewing; this is the meaning. By way of concise attention in the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna, and by way of detailed attention in the Rāhulovāda, Dhātuvibhaṅga, and so on.

Phassapañcamakeyevāti eva-saddena vuttesu tīsupi mukhesu pariggahassa samānataṃ dasseti. Nāmarūpavavatthānassa adhippetattā niravasesarūpapariggahassa dassanatthaṃ “vatthu nāma karajakāyo”ti āha, na cakkhādīni chavatthūnīti. Karajakāyassa pana vatthubhāvasādhanatthaṃ “idañca pana me viññāṇaṃ ettha sitaṃ, ettha paṭibaddha”nti (dī. ni. 1.235; ma. ni. 2.252) suttaṃ ābhataṃ.

By 'only in the pentad with contact', the word 'only' shows the similarity of the comprehension in all three methods mentioned. Because the determination of name-and-form is intended, in order to show the comprehension of form without remainder, it is said, 'the basis is the physical body', not the six bases such as the eye. Furthermore, to establish the status of the physical body as the basis, the sutta 'and this consciousness of mine is dependent on this, is bound to this' is cited.

Phassaviññāṇānaṃ pākaṭatā kesañci hotīti yesaṃ na hoti, te sandhāyāha “phassavasena vā hi…pe… na pākaṭaṃ hotī”ti. Tesaṃ pana aññesañca sabbesaṃ veneyyānaṃ vedanā pākaṭāti āha “vedanāvasena pana pākaṭaṃ hotī”ti. Satadhotasappi nāma satavāraṃ vilāpetvā vilāpetvā udake pakkhipitvā uddharitvā gahitasappi.

The manifestation of contact and consciousness occurs for some; referring to those for whom it does not occur, it is said, 'for by way of contact... it is not manifest'. But for them and for all other disciples, feeling is manifest; thus it is said, 'but by way of feeling, it is manifest'. 'Ghee washed a hundred times' is ghee that has been obtained by repeatedly melting it, putting it in water, and taking it out a hundred times.

Vinivattetvāti catukkhandhasamudāyato visuṃ uddharitvā. Mahāsatipaṭṭhānasuttādīsu katthaci paṭhamaṃ rūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ vatvā pacchā arūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ vedanāvasena vinivattetvā dassitaṃ. Katthaci arūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ eva vedanāvasena arūparāsito, ñātapariññāya pariññātato vā rūpārūparāsito vā vinivattetvā dassitaṃ. Tatthāpi yesu paṭhamaṃ ñātapariññā vuttā, tesu tadantogadhaṃ[V 0.0156]. Yesu na vuttā, tesu ca vedanāya ārammaṇamattaṃ saṃkhittaṃ pāḷianāruḷhaṃ rūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ sandhāya rūpakammaṭṭhānassa paṭhamaṃ kathitatā vuttāti veditabbā.

'Having separated' means having extracted it separately from the aggregate of the four aggregates. In the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta and others, sometimes the form meditation subject is stated first, and afterwards the formless meditation subject is shown, having been separated by way of feeling. Sometimes, the formless meditation subject itself is shown, having been separated by way of feeling from the formless mass, or from what is fully understood by the full understanding of the known, or from the form-and-formless mass. Therein, in those cases where the full understanding of the known is stated first, it is included in that. And in those cases where it is not stated, it should be understood that the form meditation subject is said to be stated first with reference to the form meditation subject which is concise, not found in the Pāli canon, and is merely an object for feeling.

“Manoviññeyyānaṃ dhammānaṃ iṭṭhānaṃ kantāna”ntiādinā (ma. ni. 3.306) nayena vuttaṃ chagehassitasomanassaṃ pañcakāmaguṇesu assādānupassino eva hotīti āha “pañcakāmaguṇāmisanissitā cha gehassitasomanassavedanā”ti.

The six kinds of household joy spoken of in the manner of 'of mind-cognizable dhammas that are wished for, desired' and so on, occur only for one who contemplates gratification in the five strands of sensual pleasure; thus, it is said, 'the six feelings of household joy are dependent on the bait of the five strands of sensual pleasure'.

Vedanānupassanāniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the exposition on the contemplation of feeling is concluded.

Cittānupassanāniddesavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Exposition on the Contemplation of Mind

365. Kilesasampayuttānaṃ [M 0.0158] dhammānaṃ kehici kilesehi vippayogepi sati yehi sampayuttā, tehi saṃkilesabhāvena sadisehi saṃkiliṭṭhattā itarehipi na visuddhatā hotīti āha “na pacchimapadaṃ bhajantī”ti. Duvidhanti visuṃ vacanaṃ sarāgasadosehi visiṭṭhaggahaṇatthaṃ. Avipassanupagattā “idha okāsova natthī”ti vuttaṃ.

365. Even when there is disassociation from some defilements for dhammas associated with defilements, because they are defiled by those with which they are associated—which are similar in their nature of defiling—there is no purity from the others either. Thus, it is said, 'they do not partake of the latter term'. The separate statement 'twofold' is for the purpose of grasping the distinction between 'with lust' and 'with hate'. Because it is not conducive to insight, it is said, 'here there is no opportunity at all'.

Cittānupassanāniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the exposition on the contemplation of mind is concluded.

Dhammānupassanāniddeso

Exposition on the Contemplation of Dhammas

Ka. nīvaraṇapabbavaṇṇanā

A. Explanation of the Section on the Hindrances

367. Kaṇhasukkānaṃ yuganaddhatā natthīti pajānanakāle abhāvā “abhiṇhasamudācāravasenā”ti āha.

367. Because at the time of knowing there is an absence of the yoking together of the dark and the bright, it is said, 'by way of frequent practice'.

Subhampīti [V 0.0157] kāmacchandopi. So hi attano gahaṇākārena “subha”nti vuccati, tenākārena pavattamānakassa aññassa kāmacchandassa nimittattā “nimitta”nti cāti. Ākaṅkhitassa hitasukhassa anupāyabhūto manasikāro anupāyamanasikāro. Tatthāti nipphādetabbe ārammaṇabhūte ca duvidhepi subhanimitte.

'Even the attractive' also means sensual desire. For it is called 'attractive' by its own mode of grasping, and because it is a sign for another sensual desire that proceeds in that mode, it is also called 'a sign'. Attention that is not a means to the wished-for welfare and happiness is inappropriate attention. 'There' refers to both types of attractive signs: that which is to be produced and that which is an object.

Asubhampīti asubhajjhānampi. Taṃ pana dasasu asubhesu kesādīsu ca pavattaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kesādīsu hi saññā asubhasaññāti girimānandasutte vuttāti. Ettha catubbidhassapi ayonisomanasikārassa yonisomanasikārassa ca dassanaṃ niravasesadassanatthaṃ katanti veditabbaṃ. Tesu pana asubhe subhanti asubhanti ca manasikāro idhādhippeto, tadanukulattā vā itarepīti.

'Even the unattractive' also means the meditation on the unattractive. That, however, should be seen as occurring in the ten kinds of unattractiveness and in the parts beginning with the hair of the head. For the perception regarding hair and so on is the perception of the unattractive, as stated in the Girimānanda Sutta. Here, it should be understood that the showing of both the fourfold unwise attention and wise attention is done for the purpose of showing without remainder. But among these, attention to the unattractive as attractive and as unattractive is what is intended here, or others also, because they are in accordance with that.

Bhojane mattaññuno thinamiddhābhibhavābhāvā otāraṃ alabhamāno kāmarāgo pahīyatīti vadanti. Bhojananissitaṃ pana āhārepaṭikūlasaññaṃ, tabbipariṇāmassa tadādhārassa tassa ca upanissayabhūtassa asubhatādidassanaṃ, kāyassa ca āhāraṭṭhitikatādidassanaṃ so [M 0.0159] uppādetīti tassa kāmacchando pahīyateva, abhidhammapariyāyena sabbopi lobho kāmacchandanīvaraṇanti āha “arahattamaggenā”ti.

They say that for one who knows moderation in eating, because there is no overcoming by sloth and torpor, sensual lust, finding no opportunity, is abandoned. Moreover, he generates the perception of repulsiveness in nutriment, which is based on food; the seeing of the foulness of its transformation, its container, and that which is its support; and the seeing that the body is sustained by food. Thus, for him, sensual desire is indeed abandoned. According to the Abhidhamma method, all greed is the hindrance of sensual desire; thus, it is said, '[it is abandoned] by the path of arahantship'.

Odissakānodissakadisāpharaṇānanti attagaruatippiyasahāyamajjhattavasena odissakatā, sīmābhede kate anodissakatā, ekadisāpharaṇavasena disāpharaṇatā mettāya uggahaṇe veditabbā. Vihāraracchāgāmādivasena vā odissakadisāpharaṇaṃ, vihārādiuddesarahitaṃ puratthimādidisāvasena anodissakadisāpharaṇanti evaṃ vā dvidhā uggahaṃ sandhāya “odissakānodissakadisāpharaṇāna”nti vuttaṃ. Uggaho ca yāva upacārā daṭṭhabbo, uggahitāya āsevanā bhāvanā. Tattha “sabbe sattā pāṇā bhūtā puggalā attabhāvapariyāpannā”ti etesaṃ vasena pañcavidhā, ekekasmiṃ “averā hontu, abyāpajjā, anīghā, sukhī attānaṃ pariharantū”ti catudhā pavattito vīsatividhā vā anodhisopharaṇā mettā, “sabbā itthiyo purisā ariyā anariyā devā manussā vinipātikā”ti sattodhikaraṇavasena pavattā sattavidhā, aṭṭhavīsatividhā vā odhisopharaṇā mettā, dasahi disāhi disodhikaraṇavasena pavattā dasavidhā ca disāpharaṇā mettā, ekekāya vā disāya sattādiitthiādiaverādiyogena asītādhikacatusatappabhedā anodhisoodhisopharaṇā veditabbā.

'Specific, non-specific, and directional pervasions': In the learning of loving-kindness, specificity should be understood by way of a respected person, a very dear friend, and a neutral person; non-specificity is when the boundary is broken; directional pervasion is by way of pervading one direction. Alternatively, 'specific, non-specific, and directional pervasions' is said with reference to the twofold learning: specific directional pervasion by way of a monastery, road, village, etc., and non-specific directional pervasion by way of the directions such as east, etc., without specifying a monastery, etc. The learning should be seen as up to access concentration; for what has been learned, there is cultivation and development. Therein, the unspecified pervasion of loving-kindness is fivefold by way of 'all beings, all living things, all creatures, all individuals, all who are included in a personality'; as it proceeds in four ways for each one—'may they be free from enmity, free from ill will, free from trouble, and may they live happily'—it becomes twentyfold. The specified pervasion of loving-kindness is sevenfold, proceeding by way of the seven subjects: 'all women, men, noble ones, non-noble ones, devas, humans, and those in states of deprivation'; or it is twenty-eightfold. And the directional pervasion of loving-kindness is tenfold, proceeding by way of the ten directions as subjects. Or, for each direction, by applying freedom from enmity, etc., to beings, etc., women, etc., the unspecified and specified pervasions should be understood as having four hundred and eighty divisions.

Kāyavināmanāti [V 0.0158] kāyassa vividhena ākārena nāmanā.

'Bending of the body' means the bending of the body in various ways.

Atibhojane nimittaggāhoti atibhojane thinamiddhassa nimittaggāho, “ettake bhutte thinamiddhassa kāraṇaṃ hoti, ettake na hotī”ti thinamiddhassa kāraṇākāraṇaggāhoti attho. Dhutaṅgānaṃ vīriyanissitattā āha “dhutaṅganissitasappāyakathāyapī”ti.

'Grasping the sign in overeating' means grasping the sign of sloth and torpor in overeating; the meaning is grasping the cause and non-cause of sloth and torpor, thinking, 'When this much is eaten, it is a cause for sloth and torpor; when this much is eaten, it is not'. Because the ascetic practices are dependent on energy, it is said, 'even in talk on what is suitable, based on the ascetic practices'.

Kukkuccampi katākatānusocanavasena pavattamānaṃ uddhaccena samānalakkhaṇaṃ avūpasamasabhāvamevāti cetaso avūpasamo “uddhaccakukkuccamevā”ti vutto.

Worry, arising through regretting what was done and what was not done, has the same characteristic as restlessness, being inherently unpacified. Therefore, the mind's unpacified state is called "restlessness and worry."

Bahussutassa ganthato ca atthato ca atthādīni vicinantassa cetaso vikkhepo na hoti yathāvidhipaṭipattiyā yathānurūpapatikārappavattiyā katākatānusocanañcāti “bāhusaccenapi uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahīyatī”ti āha. Vuḍḍhasevitā ca vuḍḍhasīlitaṃ āvahatīti cetovūpasamakarattā uddhaccakukkuccappahānakāritā [M 0.0160] vuttā. Vuḍḍhataṃ pana anapekkhitvā vinayadharā kukkuccavinodakā kalyāṇamittā vuttāti daṭṭhabbā.

For one who is learned, examining the meaning and the text, discerning the things implied by the meaning, there is no mental distraction. And by means of practice in accordance with the Dhamma, by means of acting in accordance with the appropriate remedy, and by means of abandoning remorse regarding what was done or not done, it is said, 'restlessness and worry are abandoned even through much learning.' And associating with elders brings the practice of elders; thus, because it makes for the calming of the mind, it is said to cause the abandonment of restlessness and worry. But, irrespective of seniority, those versed in the Vinaya are said to be good friends who dispel worry—this should be understood.

Tiṭṭhati etthāti ṭhānīyā, vicikicchāya ṭhānīyā vicikicchāṭhānīyā. Ṭhātabbāti vā ṭhānīyā, vicikicchā ṭhānīyā etesūti vicikicchāṭhānīyā.

"Here it stands," thus it is a 'standing place' (ṭhānīyā); the 'standing place' for doubt (vicikicchā) is 'a standing place for doubt' (vicikicchāṭhānīyā). Or, 'it should be stood upon,' thus it is a 'standing place' (ṭhānīyā); doubt has a 'standing place' in these, thus, 'a standing place for doubt' (vicikicchāṭhānīyā).

Kāmaṃ bahussutatāparipucchakatāhi aṭṭhavatthukāpi vicikicchā pahīyati, tathāpi ratanattayavicikicchāmūlikā sesavicikicchāti katvā āha “tīṇi ratanāni ārabbhā”ti. Vinaye pakataññutā “sikkhāya kaṅkhatī”ti (dha. sa. 1008; vibha. 915) vuttāya vicikicchāya pahānaṃ karotīti āha “vinaye ciṇṇavasībhāvassapī”ti. Okappaniyasaddhāsaṅkhātaadhimokkhabahulassāti anupavisanasaddhāsaṅkhātaadhimokkhena adhimuccanabahulassa. Adhimuccanañca adhimokkhuppādanamevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Saddhāya vā ninnatā adhimutti.

Though even the eight-fold doubt is abandoned through much learning and questioning, still, considering that other doubt is rooted in doubt about the Three Jewels, it is said, 'with regard to the Three Jewels.' Proficiency in the Discipline causes the abandonment of the doubt expressed as, 'he is uncertain about the training' (Dhs. 1008; Vibh. 915), hence it is said, 'even for one accomplished in the Discipline.' The phrase 'one who is abundant in resolve reckoned as conviction-faith' means one who is often resolved through resolve reckoned as penetrating faith. And resolving should be understood as the arising of resolve itself. Or, resolve is an inclination to faith.

Nīvaraṇapabbavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the section on the hindrances is concluded.

Kha. bojjhaṅgapabbavaṇṇanā

Kha. Explanation of the Section on the Factors of Enlightenment

Khandhādipāḷiyā [V 0.0159] attho khandhādīnaṃ atthoti katvā āha “khandha…pe… vipassanānaṃ atthasannissitaparipucchābahulatā”ti. Tena pāḷimuttakapucchā na tathā paññāsaṃvattanikā, yathā atthapaṭipucchāti dasseti.

The meaning of the Pāli text beginning with 'aggregates' is taken as the meaning of 'aggregates' and so forth, and thus it is said: 'abundance in questioning dependent on the meaning of the aggregates... insight.' This shows that questioning merely detached from the Pāli text is not as conducive to the development of wisdom as questioning about the meaning.

Mandattā aggijālādīsu āpodhātuādīnaṃ viya vīriyādīnaṃ sakicce asamatthatā vuttā.

Due to sluggishness, the inability of energy and so forth to perform their own function is stated, just as the water element and so forth are unable to function in a blazing fire and so forth.

Pattaṃ nīharantova taṃ sutvāti ettha pañcābhiññattā dibbasotena assosīti vadanti.

Having heard it just as he was carrying out the bowl—here, they say he heard it with the divine ear, due to having attained the five higher knowledges.

Pasādasinehābhāvenāti pasādasaṅkhātassa sinehassa abhāvena. Gadrabhapiṭṭhe lūkharajo lūkhataro hutvā dissatīti atilūkhatāya taṃsadise.

Due to the absence of the affection of clarity—namely, the absence of the affection designated as clarity. It is similar to that due to extreme coarseness, just as coarse dust on a donkey's back appears even coarser.

Saṃvejanapasādanehi tejanaṃ tosanañca sampahaṃsanāti.

By arousing a sense of urgency and inspiring clarity, it is inspiring, gladdening, and delighting.

Bojjhaṅgapabbavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Section on the Factors of Enlightenment is concluded.

Samathavipassanāsuddhavipassanāvasena [M 0.0161] paṭhamassa itaresañca kathitattāti attho. Maggasampayuttā sati kāyānupassanā nāmāti āgamanavasena vuttaṃ. Evaṃ tāva desanā puggale tiṭṭhatīti kāyānupassīādīnaṃ āgamanavasena visesetvā vuttā satipaṭṭhānadesanā puggale tiṭṭhatīti attho. Na hi sakkā ekassa anekasamaṅgitā vattuṃ ekakkhaṇe anekasatisambhavāvabodhapasaṅgā, puggalaṃ pana āmasitvā sakiccaparicchinne dhamme vuccamāne kiccabhedena ekissāpi satiyā anekanāmatā hotīti dassento “kāye panā”tiādimāha. Yathā hi puggalakiccaṃ dhammā evāti dhammabhedena kāyānupassīādipuggalabhedova hoti, na evaṃ dhammassa dhammo kiccanti na dhammabhedena tassa bhedo, tasmā ekāva sati catuvipallāsappahānabhūtā magge samiddhā anatthantarena tappahānakiccabhedena cattāri nāmāni labhatīti ayamettha adhippāyo.

The meaning is that the first method and the others are explained by way of serenity-and-insight and pure insight. Mindfulness associated with the path is called 'contemplation of the body' in terms of its textual occurrence. Thus, 'the teaching abides in the individual' means that the teaching of the foundations of mindfulness, having been specified by way of the textual occurrence of 'contemplator of the body' and so forth, abides in the individual. For it is not possible to speak of one mindfulness having many simultaneous characteristics, as that would lead to the absurd conclusion that multiple mindfulnesses arise in a single moment. But when referring to a person and speaking of phenomena defined by their specific function, a single mindfulness can have multiple names due to functional differences. Showing this, he says, 'and in the body,' etc. Just as the functions of an individual are indeed phenomena, so too the difference in individuals, such as the contemplator of the body and so on, is due to the difference in phenomena. But it is not the case that one phenomenon performs the function of another phenomenon, and thus a difference in phenomena does not lead to a difference in the phenomenon itself. Therefore, a single mindfulness, being the means of abandoning the four distortions and fully developed on the path, obtains four names according to the differences in its function of abandoning those distortions, without any other meaning. This is the intended meaning here.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Suttanta division is concluded.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Abhidhamma Division

374. Abhidhammabhājanīye [V 0.0160] “kathañca bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye…pe… dandhābhiññaṃ kāye kāyānupassī, yā tasmiṃ samaye satī”tiādinā āgamanavasena visesitāni satipaṭṭhānāni puggale ṭhapetvā desetvā puna “tattha katamaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ? Idha bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye…pe… dandhābhiññaṃ…pe… yā tasmiṃ samaye satī”tiādinā puggalaṃ anāmasitvā āgamavisesanañca akatvā catukiccasādhakekasativasena suddhikasatipaṭṭhānanayo vuttoti ayamettha nayadvaye viseso.

374. In the Abhidhamma division, by the text beginning, 'And how does a monk dwell contemplating the body in the body? Here, a monk at such a time... slow understanding... contemplating the body in the body, whatever mindfulness there is at that time,' the foundations of mindfulness are specified by way of textual occurrence, having first been established and taught in relation to a person. Then again, by the text beginning, 'Herein, what is the foundation of mindfulness? Here, a monk at such a time... slow understanding... whatever mindfulness there is at that time,' without referring to the person and without making a textual specification, the method of the pure foundation of mindfulness is taught as a single mindfulness accomplishing four tasks. This is the difference between the two methods here.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Abhidhamma division is concluded.

Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Exposition of the Foundations of Mindfulness is concluded.

8. Sammappadhānavibhaṅgo

8. The Exposition of the Right Efforts

1. Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Suttanta Division

390. Kāraṇappadhānāti [M 0.0162][V 0.0161] “anuppannapāpakānuppādādiatthā”ti gahitā tatheva te hontīti taṃ atthaṃ sādhentiyevāti etassa atthassa dīpako sammā-saddoti yathādhippetatthassa anuppannapāpakānuppādādino kāraṇabhūtā, padhānakāraṇabhūtāti attho. Sammāsaddassa upāyayonisoatthadīpakataṃ sandhāya “upāyappadhānā yonisopadhānā”ti vuttaṃ. Paṭipannakoti bhāvanamanuyutto. Bhusaṃ yogo payogo, payogova parakkamo payogaparakkamo. Etānīti “vāyamatī”tiādīni “āsevamāno vāyamatī”tiādinā yojetabbāni.

390. 'Predominant by way of cause' means: because they are taken as having the meaning of 'the non-arising of unarisen unwholesome states and so forth,' and because they exist just so, they accomplish that very meaning. The word 'sammā' is indicative of this meaning, signifying that they are the cause, the primary cause, of the intended meaning, namely, the non-arising of unarisen unwholesome states and so forth. With reference to the word 'sammā' indicating the meaning of skillful means and wise attention, it is said, 'predominant by way of skillful means, predominant by way of wise attention.' 'Paṭipannako' means one engaged in cultivation. 'Bhusaṃ yogo<x_bin_42>o' means intense application is exertion; 'payogova parakkamo' means exertion itself is vigor; 'payogaparakkamo' means exertion and vigor. These—'strives' and so on—should be connected with 'strives while cultivating' and so on.

Anuppannāti avattabbataṃ āpannānanti bhūmiladdhārammaṇādhiggahitāvikkhambhitāsamugghātituppannānaṃ.

'Unarisen' refers to those qualities that have attained the state of not being spoken of as arisen—namely, those that, though arisen, have not gained a foothold in the mind-ground, have not seized an object, have not been suppressed, and have not been uprooted.

391. Dhammacchandoti taṇhādiṭṭhivīriyacchandā viya na añño dhammo, atha kho chandaniyasabhāvo evāti dassento āha “sabhāvacchando”ti. Tattha “yo kāmesu kāmacchando”tiādīsu (dha. sa. 1103) taṇhā chandoti vuttāti veditabbo, “sabbeva nu kho, mārisa, samaṇabrāhmaṇā ekantavādā ekantasīlā ekantachandā ekantaajjhosānā”ti (dī. ni. 2.366) ettha diṭṭhi, pamādaniddese “nikkhittachandatā nikkhittadhuratā”ti vīriyanti vaṇṇeti.

391. 'Desire for the Dhamma' is not a different kind of phenomenon from desires such as craving, view, and effort; rather, showing that it is indeed the very nature of desiring, he said, 'desire by nature.' There, it should be understood that in passages such as 'whatever desire for sensual pleasures' (Dhs. 1103), craving is called 'chanda'; here, in 'all ascetics and brahmins... are of one desire...' (DN 2.366), it refers to view; and in the explanation of negligence, in 'having given up desire, having given up the yoke,' he explains it as effort.

394. Vāyamati [V 0.0162] vīriyaṃ ārabhatīti padadvayassapi niddeso vīriyaniddesoyevāti adhippāyenāha “vīriyaniddese”ti.

394. With the intention that the explanation of both terms, 'strives' and 'arouses energy,' is indeed an explanation of energy, he says, 'in the explanation of energy.'

406. Sabbapubbabhāgeti sabbamaggānaṃ pubbabhāge. Purimasminti “anuppannā me kusalā dhammā anuppajjamānā anatthāya saṃvatteyyu”nti etthāpi “samathavipassanāva gahetabbā”ti vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ, taṃ pana maggānuppannatāya bhāvato anuppajjamāne ca tasmiṃ vaṭṭānatthasaṃvattanato na yuttanti paṭikkhipati.

406. 'Sabbapubbabhāge' means in the preliminary part of all the paths. As for 'Purimasmiṃ' (in the former), even here, regarding 'Unarisen wholesome qualities for me, if they do not arise, would lead to harm,' it is said in the commentary, 'Only serenity and insight should be taken.' However, he refutes that, saying it is not fitting because, due to the path not having arisen, and if that path does not arise, it would lead to harm in the round of existence.

Mahantaṃ [M 0.0163] gāravaṃ hoti, tasmā “saṅghagāravena yathāruci vindituṃ na sakkā”ti saṅghena saha na nikkhami. Atimandāni noti nanu atimandānīti attho. Santasamāpattito aññaṃ santhambhanakāraṇaṃ balavaṃ natthīti “tato parihīnā santhambhituṃ na sakkontī”ti āha. Na hi mahārajjumhi chinne suttatantū sandhāretuṃ sakkontīti. Samathe vatthuṃ dassetvā tena samānagatikā vipassanā cāti iminā adhippāyenāha “evaṃ uppannā samathavipassanā…pe… saṃvattantī”ti.

There is great respect; therefore, he did not leave with the Saṅgha, thinking, 'It is not possible to obtain things as one pleases due to respect for the Saṅgha.' 'Atimandāni no' means, 'are they not extremely sluggish?' There is no stronger cause for steadiness than the attainment of peace; therefore, he said, 'Those deficient in that are not able to steady themselves.' For indeed, when a large rope is cut, threads of yarn are not able to hold it together. Having shown the basis in serenity, and with the intention that insight also has the same course as that, he said, 'Thus arisen, serenity and insight... lead to...'

Tattha anuppannānanti ettha tattha duvidhāya sammappadhānakathāya, tattha vā pāḷiyaṃ “anuppannāna”nti etassa ayaṃ vinicchayoti adhippāyo. Eteyevāti anamatagge saṃsāre uppannāyeva.

Herein, regarding 'of the unarisen' (anuppannānaṃ), the intention is: this is the determination of it in the twofold discourse on right effort, or, in the Pāli text, this is the determination of 'anuppannānaṃ.' 'Eteyeva' means those that have already arisen in beginningless saṃsāra.

Cuddasa mahāvattāni khandhake vuttāni āgantukaāvāsikagamikaanumodana bhattagga piṇḍacārika āraññika senāsana jantāgharavaccakuṭi ācariyaupajjhāyasaddhivihārikaantevāsikavattāni cuddasa. Tato aññāni pana kadāci tajjanīyakammakatādikāle pārivāsikādikāle ca caritabbāni dvāsīti khuddakavattānīti kathitāni daṭṭhabbāni. Na hi tāni sabbāsu avatthāsu caritabbāni, tasmā mahāvatte agaṇitāni. Tattha “pārivāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ paññāpessāmī”ti ārabhitvā “na upasampādetabbaṃ…pe… na chamāyaṃ caṅkamante caṅkame caṅkamitabba”nti (cūḷava. 76) vuttāni pakatatte caritabbavattāvasānāni chasaṭṭhi, tato paraṃ “na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā pārivāsikavuḍḍhatarena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahena, mānattārahena, mānattacārikena, abbhānārahena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vatthabba”ntiādīni (cūḷava. 82) pakatatte caritabbehi anaññattā visuṃ visuṃ [V 0.0163] agaṇetvā pārivāsikavuḍḍhatarādīsu puggalantaresu caritabbattā tesaṃ vasena sampiṇḍetvā ekekaṃ katvā gaṇetabbāni pañcāti ekasattati vattāni, ukkhepanīyakammakatavattesu vattapaññāpanavasena vuttaṃ “na pakatattassa bhikkhuno abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… nahāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ sāditabba”nti (cūḷava. 75) idaṃ abhivādanādīnaṃ assādiyanaṃ ekaṃ, “na pakatatto bhikkhu sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsetabbo”tiādīni (cūḷava. 51) ca dasāti evaṃ dvāsīti honti. Etesveva kānici tajjanīyakammakatādivattāni, kānici pārivāsikādivattānīti aggahitaggahaṇena dvāsītivattanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Fourteen major duties are mentioned in the Khandhaka: duties for incoming monks, duties for resident monks, duties for departing monks, duties concerning thanksgiving, duties concerning the refectory, duties concerning alms-rounds, duties concerning forest dwellings, duties concerning lodgings, duties concerning the steam-bath room, duties concerning the restroom, duties toward teachers, duties toward preceptors, duties toward co-residents, and duties toward pupils—these are the fourteen. Beyond these, however, eighty-two minor duties are said to be observed occasionally, such as during the time when a tajjaniyakamma has been enacted, or during the period of parivāsa, and so on. These should be understood as stated. For indeed, they are not to be observed in all circumstances, which is why they are not counted among the major duties. Here, beginning with the statement, 'I will prescribe the duties for monks on probation,' up to 'One should not be ordained... nor should one walk on a walking path while pacing on the ground' (Cūḷavagga 76), sixty-six duties are stated, concluding with those to be observed in relation to a monk in good standing. After that, from the passage, 'Monks, a monk on probation should not stay under the same roof with a senior monk on probation, one deserving to be sent back to the origin, one deserving the mānatta penalty, one undergoing mānatta, or one deserving rehabilitation' (Cūḷavagga 82), and so on—these are not separately counted because they are not different from the duties applicable to a monk in good standing. Instead, since they apply to different individuals, such as senior monks on probation and others, they should be grouped together by person and counted as five, making a total of seventy-one duties. In the case of duties for those undergoing ukkhepaniyakamma, it is stated, by way of prescribing duties, 'A monk in good standing should not accept a greeting, standing up... nor should his back be massaged while bathing' (Cūḷavagga 75). This non-acceptance of greeting and so on counts as one. Further, 'A monk in good standing should not be harassed for a moral failing' (Cūḷavagga 51), and so on—these make ten. Thus, the total comes to eighty-two. Among these, some are duties for those undergoing tajjaniyakamma and similar penalties, while others are duties for those on parivāsa and so forth. By the method of including and excluding, the eighty-two duties should be understood.

Idha [M 0.0164] vipākānubhavanavasena tadārammaṇaṃ, avipakkavipākassa sabbathā avigatattā bhavitvā vigatamattavasena kammañca “bhutvā vigatuppanna”nti vuttaṃ, na aṭṭhasāliniyaṃ (dha. sa. aṭṭha. 1) viya rajjanādivasena anubhutvāpagataṃ javanaṃ, uppajjitvā niruddhatāvasena bhūtāpagatasaṅkhātaṃ sesasaṅkhatañca “bhūtāpagatuppanna”nti, tasmā idha okāsakatuppannaṃ vipākameva vadati, na tattha viya kammampīti. Anusayitakilesāti appahīnā maggena pahātabbā adhippetā. Tenāha “atītā vā…pe… na vattabbā”ti. Tesañhi ambataruṇopamāya vattamānāditā na vattabbāti.

Here, tadārammaṇa occurs by way of experiencing a result. And since the unripened result has not entirely passed away, kamma is said to be 'experienced, passed away, and arisen' in the sense of merely having come to be and passed away. This is not like in the Aṭṭhasālinī, where javana is 'passed away after experiencing' by way of lust and so on. That which is designated 'past and gone' in the sense of having arisen and ceased, and the remaining conditioned phenomena, are termed 'past, gone, and arisen.' Therefore, here it speaks only of the result that arises when the opportunity is made, not of kamma as in that other text. By 'latent defilements' are meant those that are unabandoned and are to be abandoned by the path. Thus it is said, 'whether past... or... cannot be stated.' For of these, their state as present and so on cannot be stated, by the simile of the young mango.

Āhatakhīrarukkho viya nimittaggāhavasena adhigataṃ ārammaṇaṃ, anāhatakhīrarukkho viya avikkhambhitatāya antogadhakilesaṃ ārammaṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ, nimittaggāhakāvikkhambhitakilesā vā puggalā āhatānāhatakhīrarukkhasadisā. Purimanayenevāti avikkhambhituppanne viya “imasmiṃ nāma ṭhāne nuppajjissantīti na vattabbā asamugghāṭitattā”ti yojetvā vitthāretabbaṃ.

An object apprehended by grasping at a sign should be seen as like a struck milk-tree, while an object with unsuppressed defilements latent within should be seen as like an unstruck milk-tree. Or, individuals who grasp at signs, and those with unsuppressed defilements, are like struck and unstruck milk-trees, respectively. By 'as in the previous method' it is meant that, just as with defilements that have arisen but are unsuppressed, one should connect and elaborate by saying, 'It cannot be said that they will not arise in this particular place, because they have not been eradicated.'

Pāḷiyanti paṭisambhidāpāḷiyaṃ (paṭi. ma. 3.21). Maggena pahīnakilesānameva tidhā navattabbataṃ apākaṭaṃ pākaṭaṃ kātuṃ ajātaphalarukkho ābhato, atītādīnaṃ appahīnatādassanatthampi “jātaphalarukkhena dīpetabba”nti āha. Tattha yathā acchinne rukkhe nibbattirahāni phalāni chinne anuppajjamānāni na kadāci sasabhāvāni ahesuṃ honti bhavissanti cāti atītādibhāvena na vattabbāni, evaṃ maggena pahīnakilesā ca daṭṭhabbā. Yathā ca chede asati phalāni uppajjissanti, sati ca nuppajjissantīti chedassa sātthakatā, evaṃ maggabhāvanāya ca sātthakatā yojetabbā.

By 'in the Pāli text' is meant in the Pāli of the Paṭisambhidāmagga (Paṭis. Ma. 3.21). To make evident what was not apparent—namely, that defilements abandoned by the path cannot be spoken of in three ways—a tree that has not yet borne fruit is adduced. And to show the unabandoned nature of past and so forth, he said, 'It should be illustrated by a fruit-bearing tree.' There, just as fruits that are apt to arise in an uncut tree do not arise when it is cut, and thus it cannot be said that they ever existed, exist, or will exist with their own nature, in terms of being past and so forth, so too should defilements abandoned by the path be seen. And just as when there is no cutting, fruits will arise, but when there is cutting, they will not arise, thus the cutting is meaningful; so too should the meaningfulness of path cultivation be applied.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Suttanta Section is concluded.

3. Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā

3. Exposition of the Section on Questions

427. Pañhapucchake [V 0.0164] yaṃ vuttaṃ “vīriyajeṭṭhikāya pana aññassa vīriyassa abhāvā na vattabbāni maggādhipatīnīti vā na maggādhipatīnīti vā”ti, ettha “maggādhipatīnī”ti [M 0.0165] na vattabbatāya eva aññassa vīriyassa abhāvo kāraṇanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Chandassa pana cittassa vā namaggabhūtassa adhipatino tadā abhāvā “na maggādhipatīnī”ti na vattabbānīti vuttaṃ. Chandacittānaṃ viya namaggabhūtassa aññassa vīriyādhipatino abhāvāti vā adhippāyo. Sammappadhānānaṃ tadā maggasaṅkhātaadhipatibhāvato vā “na maggādhipatīnī”ti navattabbatā vuttāti veditabbā.

427. Regarding what was said in the Section on Questions: 'When energy is pre-eminent, because there is no other energy, it cannot be said whether they are 'masters of the path' or 'not masters of the path'.' Here, it should be understood that the absence of any other energy is the reason why it cannot be said that they are 'masters of the path'. However, because at that time there is no desire or mind that is not part of the path to be a dominant factor, it is said that it cannot be said that they are 'not masters of the path'. Or the meaning is that, just as with desire and mind, there is no other energy as a dominant factor that is not part of the path. Alternatively, it should be understood that because the right efforts at that time have the nature of a path and the state of a dominant factor, it is said that it cannot be said that they are 'not masters of the path'.

Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Section on Questions is concluded.

Sammappadhānavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Analysis of Right Efforts is concluded.

9. Iddhipādavibhaṅgo

9. Analysis of the Bases of Power

1. Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

1. Exposition of the Suttanta Section

431. Iddhi-saddassa [M 0.0166][V 0.0165] paṭhamo kattuattho, dutiyo karaṇattho vutto, pāda-saddassa eko karaṇamevattho vutto. Pajjitabbāva iddhi vuttā, na ca ijjhantī pajjitabbā ca iddhi pajjanakaraṇena pādena samānādhikaraṇā hotīti “paṭhamenatthena iddhi eva pādo iddhipādo”ti na sakkā vattuṃ, tathā iddhikiriyākaraṇena sādhetabbā ca vuddhisaṅkhātā iddhi pajjanakiriyākaraṇena pajjitabbāti dvinnaṃ karaṇānaṃ na asamānādhikaraṇatā sambhavatīti “dutiyenatthena iddhiyā pādo iddhipādo”ti ca na sakkā vattuṃ, tasmā paṭhamenatthena iddhiyā pādo iddhipādo, dutiyenatthena iddhi eva pādo iddhipādoti evaṃ yojanā yujjati.

431. Of the word 'iddhi,' the first meaning is that of the agent, and the second is said to be that of the instrument. Of the word 'pāda,' only the meaning of instrument is stated. Iddhi is said to be that which is to be attained; and the succeeding iddhi which is to be attained is not co-referential with pāda, which is the instrument of attainment. Therefore, it cannot be said that 'by the first meaning, iddhi itself is pāda, thus iddhipāda.' Similarly, since the iddhi designated as growth, which is to be accomplished by the instrument of the act of psychic power, is to be attained by the instrument of the act of attaining, the two instruments cannot be non-co-referential. Thus, it also cannot be said that 'by the second meaning, the pāda of iddhi is iddhipāda.' Therefore, the following interpretation is suitable: by the first meaning, the pāda of iddhi is iddhipāda; by the second meaning, iddhi itself is pāda, thus iddhipāda.

“Chandaṃ ce…pe… ayaṃ vuccati chandasamādhī”ti imāya pāḷiyā chandādhipati samādhi chandasamādhīti adhipati-saddalopaṃ katvā samāso vuttoti viññāyati, adhipati-saddatthadassanavasena pana “chandahetuko chandādhiko vā samādhi chandasamādhī”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Padhānabhūtāti vīriyabhūtāti keci vadanti. Saṅkhatasaṅkhārādinivattanatthañhi padhānaggahaṇanti. Atha vā taṃ taṃ visesaṃ saṅkharotīti saṅkhāro, sabbaṃ vīriyaṃ. Tattha catukiccasādhakato aññassa nivattanatthaṃ padhānaggahaṇanti padhānabhūtā seṭṭhabhūtāti attho. Catubbidhassa pana vīriyassa adhippetattā bahuvacananiddeso kato. Adhiṭṭhānaṭṭhenāti duvidhatthāyapi iddhiyā adhiṭṭhānatthena. Pādabhūtanti iminā visuṃ samāsayojanāvasena pana yo pubbe iddhipādattho pāda-saddassa upāyatthataṃ gahetvā yathāyutto vutto, so vakkhamānānaṃ paṭilābhapubbabhāgānaṃ kattukaraṇiddhibhāvaṃ, uttaracūḷabhājanīye vā vuttehi [V 0.0166] chandādīhi iddhipādehi sādhetabbāya iddhiyā kattiddhibhāvaṃ, chandādīnañca karaṇiddhibhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttoti veditabbo.

By the Pāli text, 'If desire... this is called desire-concentration,' it is understood that the compound 'desire-concentration' is stated by eliding the word 'dominant factor,' meaning 'concentration with desire as its dominant factor.' However, by way of showing the meaning of the word 'dominant factor,' it should be known that in the commentary it is said, 'Concentration that has desire as its cause or has desire as its chief is desire-concentration.' Some say that 'being a striving' means 'being energy.' For the inclusion of 'striving' is for the purpose of excluding constructed formations and so on. Or, 'formation' is that which forms this or that distinction; it is all energy. Therein, the inclusion of 'striving' is for the purpose of excluding what is other than the accomplisher of the four functions; the meaning is 'being a striving' is 'being excellent.' However, because the fourfold energy is intended, the plural designation is made. 'By the meaning of determination' means by the meaning of determination for psychic power of two kinds. By 'being a basis': however, by way of a separate compound construction, the meaning of 'basis of psychic power' which was previously stated as appropriate by taking the word 'basis' in the sense of 'means,' should be understood as stated with reference to the state of being the agent-psychic-power and instrument-psychic-power for the preliminary parts of the attainment to be described; or, with reference to the state of being the agent-psychic-power for the psychic power to be accomplished by the bases of psychic power beginning with desire, as stated in the subsequent Cūḷabhājanīya; and with reference to the state of being the instrument-psychic-power for desire and so on.

Vīriyiddhipādaniddese “vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgata”nti dvikkhattuṃ vīriyaṃ āgataṃ. Tattha purimaṃ samādhivisesanaṃ “vīriyādhipati samādhi vīriyasamādhī”ti, dutiyaṃ samannāgamaṅgadassanaṃ. Dveyeva hi sabbattha samannāgamaṅgāni samādhi padhānasaṅkhāro ca, chandādayo samādhivisesanāni, padhānasaṅkhāro [M 0.0167] pana padhānavacaneneva visesito, na chandādīhīti na idha vīriyādhipatitā padhānasaṅkhārassa vuttā hoti. Vīriyañca samādhiṃ visesetvā ṭhitameva samannāgamaṅgavasena padhānasaṅkhāravacanena vuttanti nāpi dvīhi vīriyehi samannāgamo vutto hotīti. Yasmā pana chandādīhi visiṭṭho samādhi, tathā visiṭṭheneva ca tena sampayutto padhānasaṅkhāro sesadhammā ca, tasmā samādhivisesanānaṃ vasena cattāro iddhipādā vuttā. Visesanabhāvo ca chandādīnaṃ taṃtaṃavassayanavasena hotīti “chandasamādhi…pe… iddhipāda”nti ettha nissayatthepi pāda-sadde upāyatthena chandādīnaṃ iddhipādatā vuttā hoti. Teneva uttaracūḷabhājanīye “cattāro iddhipādā chandiddhipādo”tiādinā chandādīnameva iddhipādatā vuttā. Pañhapucchake ca “cattāro iddhipādā idha bhikkhu chandasamādhī”tiādināva (vibha. 462) uddesaṃ katvāpi puna chandādīnaṃyeva kusalādibhāvo vibhattoti. Upāyiddhipādadassanatthameva hi nissayiddhipādadassanaṃ kataṃ, aññathā catubbidhatā na hotīti ayamettha pāḷivasena atthavinicchayo veditabbo.

In the exposition of the basis of psychic power through energy, in the phrase ‘possessed of energy-concentration and striving-formations,’ the word ‘energy’ occurs twice. Therein, the first is a qualifier of concentration: ‘concentration with energy as its dominant factor is energy-concentration.’ The second indicates the factor of endowment. For in every case there are just two factors of endowment: concentration and the striving-formation. Desire and the others are qualifiers of concentration, while the striving-formation is qualified only by the word ‘striving,’ not by desire and the others. Thus the dominance of energy is not stated here for the striving-formation. And energy, having qualified concentration, is stated by the word ‘striving-formation’ by way of a factor of endowment, and so it is not said that one is endowed with two kinds of energy. But since concentration is distinguished by desire and the others, and the striving-formation and the other states associated with it are similarly distinguished, therefore the four bases for psychic power are stated by way of the qualifiers of concentration. And since the qualifying role of desire and the others is due to their respective dependence, in the passage ‘desire-concentration … basis for psychic power,’ even though the word ‘basis’ (pāda) is in the sense of support, the status of desire and the others as bases for psychic power is stated in the sense of means. For this very reason, in the subsequent Cūḷabhājanīya it is said: ‘The four bases for psychic power are the desire-basis for psychic power,’ etc., where only desire and the others are called bases for psychic power. And in the Section of Questions, after stating the formula, ‘The four bases for psychic power: here, a bhikkhu has desire-concentration,’ etc. (Vibhaṅga 462), it further analyzes only the wholesome and other qualities of desire and the others. For the demonstration of the basis of psychic power as support is made for the very purpose of showing the basis of psychic power as means; otherwise, the fourfold division would not obtain. This is how the meaning should be determined here in accordance with the Pāli.

433. Rathadhureti rathassa purato. Hīnajātiko caṇḍālo upaṭṭhānādiguṇayogepi senāpatiṭṭhānādīni na labhatīti āha “jātiṃ sodhetvā…pe… jātiṃ avassayatī”ti. Amantanīyoti hitāhitamantane na araho.

433. By 'at the chariot's pole' (rathadhureti) is meant 'in front of the chariot' (rathassa purato). It is said, 'Having purified birth... one relies on birth,' because even a low-born outcaste, though possessing qualities like service and so forth, does not attain positions such as army commander and the like. By 'not to be consulted' (amantanīyo) is meant 'not worthy of being consulted on matters of benefit or harm'.

Raṭṭhapālatthero chande sati kathaṃ nānujānissantīti sattapi bhattāni abhuñjitvā mātāpitaro anujānāpetvā pabbajitvā chandameva avassāya lokuttaradhammaṃ nibbattesīti āha “raṭṭhapālatthero viyā”ti.

It is said, 'like Raṭṭhapāla the Elder,' because when Raṭṭhapāla the Elder had desire, how could they not consent? Without eating even seven meals, he persuaded his parents to permit him and went forth, and relying solely on desire, he realized the supramundane Dhamma.

Mogharājatthero vīmaṃsaṃ avassayīti tassa bhagavā “suññato lokaṃ avekkhassū”ti (su. ni. 1125) suññatākathaṃ [V 0.0167] kathesi, paññānissitamānaniggahatthañca dvikkhattuṃ pucchito pañhaṃ na kathesi. Tattha punappunaṃ chanduppādanaṃ tosanaṃ viya hotīti chandassa upaṭṭhānasadisatā vuttā, thāmabhāvato vīriyassa sūrattasadisatā, “chadvārādhipati rājā”ti (dha. pa. aṭṭha. 2.181 erakapattanāgarājavatthu) vacanato pubbaṅgamattā cittassa visiṭṭhajātisadisatā.

Because Mogharāja the Elder relied on investigation, the Blessed One spoke to him a discourse on emptiness, saying, 'Look upon the world as empty' (Sn. 1125), and when questioned twice, he did not answer the question, for the sake of subduing pride based on wisdom. Therein, because the repeated arising of desire is like satisfying, the similarity of desire to attendance is stated; from its state of firmness, the similarity of energy to heroism; and from the mind being foremost, as it is said, 'The king is the lord of the six doors' (DhA. 2.181, the story of the Nāga-king Erakapatta), its similarity to a distinguished lineage.

Abhedatoti [M 0.0168] chandādike tayo tayo dhamme sampiṇḍetvā, iddhiiddhipāde amissetvā vā kathananti attho. Tattha chandavīriyādayo visesena ijjhanti etāyāti iddhīti vuccanti, ijjhatīti iddhīti avisesena samādhipadhānasaṅkhārāpīti.

By 'without distinction,' the meaning is the explanation that combines the three qualities beginning with desire, or that speaks without mixing psychic power and the bases of psychic power. Therein, desire, energy, and so on are called 'psychic power' because one especially succeeds by means of them. 'Because it succeeds, it is psychic power'—this applies without distinction also to concentration and striving-formations.

Chandiddhipādasamādhiddhipādādayo visiṭṭhā, pādo sabbiddhīnaṃ sādhāraṇattā avisiṭṭho, tasmā visiṭṭhesveva pavesaṃ avatvā avisiṭṭhe ca pavesaṃ vattuṃ yuttanti dassetuṃ sabbattha “pāde patiṭṭhātipi vattuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti āha. Tatthevāti chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhāraiddhipādesu, catūsu chandādikesvevāti attho. “Chandavato ko samādhi na ijjhissatī”ti samādhibhāvanāmukhena bhāvitā samādhibhāvitā.

The bases of psychic power—the desire-basis, the concentration-basis, and so forth—are distinguished. The 'base' is common to all psychic powers and thus undistinguished. Therefore, to show that it is proper not to speak of entry into the distinguished ones alone, but also to speak of entry into the undistinguished, he said that everywhere 'it is also fitting to say, “one is established in the base.”' 'Therein' means in the bases of psychic power comprising desire, concentration, and striving-formations; the meaning is, in the four beginning with desire. 'For one with desire, what concentration will not succeed?' That which is developed by way of developing concentration is 'concentration-developed'.

Ettha panāti bhedakathāyaṃ abhedakathanato abhinavaṃ natthīti attho. Ye hi tayo dhammā abhedakathāyaṃ iddhiiddhipādotveva vuttā, te eva bhedakathāyaṃ iddhīpi honti iddhipādāpi, sesā iddhipādā evāti evaṃ abhinavābhāvaṃ dassento “chando samādhī”tiādimāha. Ime hi tayo…pe… na vinā, tasmā sesā sampayuttakā cattāro khandhā tesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ ijjhanena iddhi nāma bhaveyyuṃ, na attano sabhāvenāti te iddhipādā eva honti, na iddhīti evamidaṃ purimassa kāraṇabhāvena vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Atha vā tiṇṇaṃ iddhitā iddhipādatā ca vuttā, sesānañca iddhipādatāva, taṃ sabbaṃ sādhetuṃ “ime hi tayo…pe… na vinā”ti āha. Tena yasmā ijjhanti, tasmā iddhi. Ijjhamānā ca yasmā sampayuttakehi saheva ijjhanti, na vinā, tasmā sampayuttakā iddhipādā, tadantogadhattā pana te tayo dhammā iddhipādāpi hontīti dasseti. Sampayuttakānampi pana khandhānaṃ iddhibhāvapariyāyo atthīti dassetuṃ “sampayuttakā panā”tiādimāha. Catūsu khandhesu ekadesassa iddhitā, catunnampi “iddhiyā pādo iddhipādo”ti iminā atthena iddhipādatā, punapi catunnaṃ khandhānaṃ “iddhi eva pādo iddhipādo”ti iminā atthena iddhipādatā ca dassitā, na aññassāti katvā āha “na aññassa [V 0.0168] kassaci adhivacana”nti. Iminā “iddhi nāma anipphannā”ti idaṃ vādaṃ paṭisedheti.

'Here, however' means that in the explanation with distinction, there is nothing new compared to the explanation without distinction. Indeed, those three states which in the explanation without distinction were called both psychic power and basis of psychic power, in the explanation with distinction are both psychic power and bases of psychic power, while the rest are only bases of psychic power. Thus, showing this absence of novelty, he said, 'desire, concentration,' and so forth. For these three... are not without. Therefore, the remaining four associated aggregates, through the success of those three, might be called 'psychic power,' but not by their own nature; thus they are only bases of psychic power, not psychic power. This should be understood as stated as the reason for the preceding. Alternatively, for the three, both the state of being psychic power and the state of being a basis of psychic power are stated, while for the rest, only the state of being a basis of psychic power is mentioned. To establish all this, it is said, 'For these three... are not without.' By this it is shown that because they succeed, they are psychic power. And because, while succeeding, they succeed only together with their associated states, not without them, the associated states are bases of psychic power; and because those three states are included within them, they are also bases of psychic power. Further, to show that there is also a way for the associated aggregates to be psychic power, it is said, 'but the associated...' and so forth. For the four aggregates, the state of being psychic power for one part is shown; for all four, the state of being a basis of psychic power by this meaning: 'the basis for psychic power is a basis of psychic power'; and again for the four aggregates, the state of being a basis of psychic power by this meaning: 'psychic power itself is the basis, a basis of psychic power,' and not for any other. Thus, it is said, 'it is not a designation for anything else.' By this, he refutes the view that 'psychic power is unproduced'.

Paṭilābhapubbabhāgānaṃ paṭilābhasseva ca iddhiiddhipādatāvacanaṃ apubbanti katvā pucchati “kenaṭṭhena iddhi, kenaṭṭhena pādo”ti. Paṭilābho pubbabhāgo [M 0.0169] cāti vacanaseso. Upāyo ca upāyabhāveneva attano phalassa patiṭṭhā hotīti āha “patiṭṭhānaṭṭheneva pādo”ti. Chandoyeva…pe… vīmaṃsāva vīmaṃsiddhipādoti kathitaṃ, tasmā na cattāro khandhā iddhiyā samānakālikā nānākkhaṇikā vā iddhipādā, jeṭṭhakabhūtā pana chandādayo eva sabbattha iddhipādāti ayameva tesaṃ aṭṭhakathācariyānaṃ adhippāyo. Suttantabhājanīye hi abhidhammabhājanīye ca samādhivisesanavasena dassitānaṃ upāyabhūtānaṃ iddhipādānaṃ pākaṭakaraṇatthaṃ uttaracūḷabhājanīyaṃ vuttanti. Kecīti uttaravihāravāsitherā kira.

Taking the statement that the preliminary part of acquisition and acquisition itself are psychic power and the bases of psychic power as unprecedented, he asks: 'In what sense is it psychic power? In what sense is it a base?' The remainder of the statement is: 'Acquisition and the preliminary part.' The means, by its very nature as a means, serves as the foundation for its own fruit, hence it is said: 'It is a base precisely in the sense of being a foundation.' Desire alone... and so forth... investigation—this is called the base of psychic power of investigation. Therefore, the four aggregates are not bases of psychic power, whether simultaneous with psychic power or occurring at different moments. Rather, desire and the others, being the foremost, are everywhere the bases of psychic power. This indeed is the intention of the commentary teachers. For in the Suttanta division and the Abhidhamma division, the subsequent minor division is stated for the purpose of making evident the bases of psychic power, which are means shown by way of distinguishing concentration. Some—this refers to the elders residing at Uttaravihāra, it is said.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Suttanta Division is concluded.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Abhidhamma Division

444. Abhidhammabhājanīye “iddhipādoti tathābhūtassa phasso…pe… paggāho avikkhepo”ti (vibha. 447) iddhiiddhipādatthadassanatthaṃ paggāhāvikkhepā vuttā, cittapaññā ca saṅkhipitvāti. Cattāri nayasahassāni vibhattānīti idaṃ sādhipativārānaṃ paripuṇṇānaṃ abhāvā vicāretabbaṃ. Na hi adhipatīnaṃ adhipatayo vijjanti, ekekasmiṃ pana iddhipādaniddese ekeko adhipativāro labbhatīti soḷasa soḷasa nayasatāni labbhanti.

444. In the Abhidhamma Division, it is said: 'The basis of psychic power is contact of one who is thus... exertion... non-distraction' (Vibha. 447). Exertion and non-distraction are stated to show the meaning of psychic power and the bases of psychic power, and mind and wisdom are summarized. The statement 'four thousand methods have been analyzed' should be considered in light of the absence of complete sections on dominance. For there are no dominant conditions of dominant conditions, but in each explanation of a basis of psychic power, one section on dominance is obtained; thus, sixteen hundred methods are obtained.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Abhidhamma Division is concluded.

3. Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Section of Questions

Nanu [V 0.0169] ca cattāropi adhipatayo ekakkhaṇe labbhanti, aññamaññassa pana adhipatayo na bhavanti “cattāro iddhipādā na maggādhipatino”ti vuttattā. Rājaputtopamāpi hi etamatthaṃ dīpetīti? Na, ekakkhaṇe dutiyassa adhipatino abhāvato eva, “na maggādhipatino”ti vuttattā rājaputtopamā adhipatiṃ na karontīti imamevatthaṃ dīpeti, na adhipatīnaṃ sahabhāvaṃ. Taṃ kathaṃ jānitabbanti? Paṭikkhittattā. Adhipatipaccayaniddese [M 0.0170] hi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (paṭṭhā. aṭṭha. 1.3) vuttā “kasmā pana yathā hetupaccayaniddese ‘hetū hetusampayuttakāna’nti vuttaṃ, evamidha ‘adhipatī adhipatisampayuttakāna’nti avatvā ‘chandādhipati chandasampayuttakāna’ntiādinā nayena desanā katāti? Ekakkhaṇe abhāvato”ti. Sati ca catunnaṃ adhipatīnaṃ sahabhāve “ariyamaggasamaṅgissa vīmaṃsādhipateyyaṃ maggaṃ bhāventassā”ti visesanaṃ na kattabbaṃ siyā avīmaṃsādhipatikassa maggassa abhāvā. Chandādīnaṃ aññamaññādhipatikaraṇabhāve ca “vīmaṃsaṃ ṭhapetvā taṃsampayutto”tiādinā chandādīnaṃ vīmaṃsādhipatikattavacanaṃ na vattabbaṃ siyā. Tathā “cattāro ariyamaggā siyā maggādhipatino, siyā na vattabbā maggādhipatino”ti (dha. sa. 1429) evamādīhipi adhipatīnaṃ sahabhāvo paṭikkhitto evāti.

Is it not that all four dominant factors are obtained in a single moment, but they do not become dominant factors for each other, since it is said, 'The four bases of psychic power are not dominant factors of the path'? Does the simile of the prince also illustrate this point? No, because in a single moment a second dominant factor is absent, and since it is said, 'They are not dominant factors of the path,' the simile of the prince illustrates this very point that they do not create a dominant factor, not that the dominant factors coexist. How is this to be understood? Because it is rejected. For in the explanation of the dominance condition in the commentary (Paṭṭhāna Aṭṭhakathā 1.3), it is said: 'Why, just as in the explanation of the root condition it is said, "Roots are for those associated with roots," is the teaching here not given by saying, "Dominant factors are for those associated with dominant factors," but rather in the manner of "Desire-dominance is for those associated with desire," and so on? Because they do not exist in a single moment.' And if the four dominant factors were to coexist, the qualification, 'for one endowed with the noble path, developing the path with investigation as the dominant factor,' would not need to be made, since there would be no path without the dominance of investigation. And if desire and so on were to create mutual dominance, the statement regarding desire and so on being dominated by investigation, such as 'excluding investigation, what is associated with it,' would not need to be made. Likewise, in statements such as, 'The four noble paths might be dominant factors of the path, or it might not be said that they are dominant factors of the path' (Dhammasaṅgaṇī 1429), the coexistence of dominant factors is indeed rejected.

Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Section of Questions is concluded.

Iddhipādavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of the Bases of Psychic Power is concluded.

10. Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅgo

10. Analysis of the Enlightenment Factors

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Suttanta Division

Paṭhamanayavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the First Method

466. Patiṭṭhānāyūhanā [M 0.0171][V 0.0170] oghataraṇasuttavaṇṇanāyaṃ (saṃ. ni. aṭṭha. 1.1.1) –

466. In the commentary on the Oghataraṇa Sutta (Crossing the Flood) (Saṃ. Ni. Aṭṭha. 1.1.1), regarding establishment and exertion:

“Kilesavasena patiṭṭhānaṃ, abhisaṅkhāravasena āyūhanā. Tathā taṇhādiṭṭhīhi patiṭṭhānaṃ, avasesakilesābhisaṅkhārehi āyūhanā. Taṇhāvasena patiṭṭhānaṃ, diṭṭhivasena āyūhanā. Sassatadiṭṭhiyā patiṭṭhānaṃ, ucchedadiṭṭhiyā āyūhanā. Līnavasena patiṭṭhānaṃ, uddhaccavasena āyūhanā. Kāmasukhānuyogavasena patiṭṭhānaṃ, attakilamathānuyogavasena āyūhanā. Sabbākusalābhisaṅkhāravasena patiṭṭhānaṃ, sabbalokiyakusalābhisaṅkhāravasena āyūhanā”ti –

"Establishment is by way of defilements, exertion is by way of volitional formations. Likewise, establishment is through craving and views, exertion is through the remaining defilements and volitional formations. Establishment is by way of craving, exertion is by way of views. Establishment is through the eternalist view, exertion is through the annihilationist view. Establishment is by way of sloth, exertion is by way of restlessness. Establishment is by way of indulgence in sensual pleasure, exertion is by way of self-mortification. Establishment is by way of all unwholesome volitional formations, exertion is by way of all worldly wholesome volitional formations."

Vuttesu pakāresu idha avuttānaṃ vasena veditabbā.

Among the types mentioned, those not stated here should be understood by way of them.

Sammappavatte dhamme paṭisañcikkhati, upapattito ikkhati, tadākāro hutvā pavattatīti paṭisaṅkhānalakkhaṇo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo. Evañca katvā “paṭisaṅkhā santiṭṭhanā gahaṇe majjhattatā”ti upekkhākiccādhimattatāya saṅkhārupekkhā vuttā. Anukkamanikkhepe payojanaṃ purimassa purimassa pacchimapacchimakāraṇabhāvo.

One reflects on the Dhamma as it proceeds rightly, observes it from its arising, and proceeds having become of that nature—this is the characteristic of the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is reflection. And so, having done this, 'reflection, persistence, neutrality in grasping' is called equanimity towards formations due to the predominance of the function of equanimity. The purpose of the sequential arrangement is that each preceding factor is the cause for each succeeding one.

467. Balavatī [V 0.0171] eva sati satisambojjhaṅgoti katvā balavabhāvadīpanatthaṃ paññā gahitā, na yassa kassaci sampadhāraṇasati, kusaluppattikāraṇassa pana saraṇaṃ satīti dassento “vattaṃ vā”tiādimāha. Vattasīse ṭhatvāti “aho vata me dhammaṃ suṇeyyuṃ, sutvā ca dhammaṃ pasīdeyyuṃ, pasannā ca me pasannākāraṃ kareyyu”nti evaṃcitto ahutvā “svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo…pe… viññūhi, aho vata me dhammaṃ suṇeyyuṃ, sutvā ca dhammaṃ ājāneyyuṃ, ājānitvā ca pana tathatthāya paṭipajjeyyu”nti dhammasudhammataṃ paṭicca kāruññaṃ anuddayaṃ anukampaṃ upādāya mahākassapattherena viya bhāsitanti attho. Vimuttāyatanasīseti “na heva kho [M 0.0172] satthā, apica kho yathāsutaṃ yathāpariyattaṃ dhammaṃ vitthārena paresaṃ desessāmī”ti evaṃ vimuttikāraṇapadhānabhāve ṭhatvā. Cirakatavattādivasena taṃsamuṭṭhāpako arūpakoṭṭhāso vutto, bhāvatthattā eva vā katabhāsita-saddā kiriyābhūtassa arūpakoṭṭhāsassa vācakāti katvā āha “kāyaviññattiṃ…pe… koṭṭhāsa”nti.

467. Strong mindfulness itself is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness. To show its strength, wisdom is taken, not just any mindfulness of consideration. However, showing that mindfulness is the support for the cause of the arising of the wholesome, it is said, 'the custom or...' Standing at the forefront of the custom means not having a mind that thinks, 'Oh, may they listen to the Dhamma from me, and having listened, may they gain faith in the Dhamma. Having gained faith, may they act in accordance with that faith,' but rather, based on the excellent nature of the Dhamma, taking up compassion, sympathy, and kindness, like the great elder Mahākassapa, it is spoken thus: 'Well-proclaimed is the Dhamma by the Blessed One... by the wise. Oh, may they listen to the Dhamma from me, and having listened, may they understand the Dhamma. Having understood, may they practice accordingly for that purpose.' Standing at the forefront of the sphere of liberation means standing in the state of being primary for the cause of liberation, thinking, 'It is not I who am the Teacher, but rather, I will teach others the Dhamma in detail as I have heard and learned it.' The formless part that originates it by way of long-performed custom, etc., is stated. Or, because they have the meaning of an action, words like 'done' and 'spoken' are designators of the formless part which is an action; having taken it thus, it is said, 'bodily intimation... the part.'

Bojjhaṅgasamuṭṭhāpakatā purimānaṃ channaṃ attano attano anantarikassa, paresaṃ sabbesaṃ vā taṃtaṃpariyāyena samuṭṭhāpanavasena yojetabbā. Kāmalokavaṭṭāmisāti taṇhā tadārammaṇā khandhāti vadanti, pañcakāmaguṇiko ca rāgo tadārammaṇañca kāmāmisaṃ, “sassato attā ca loko cā”tiādinā lokaggahaṇavasena pavatto sassatucchedasahagato rāgo tadārammaṇañca lokāmisaṃ, lokadhammā vā, vaṭṭassādavasena uppanno saṃsārajanako rāgo tadārammaṇañca vaṭṭāmisaṃ. Maggassa pubbabhāgattā pubbabhāgā.

The state of being a cause for the arising of the enlightenment factors should be connected for each of the preceding six with its own immediate successor, or for all the others, by way of causing their arising in their respective turns. As for 'sensual, worldly, and round-of-existence bait,' they say it is craving and the aggregates that are its objects. And lust connected with the five strands of sensual pleasure, and what has them as its object, is sensual bait. Lust accompanied by eternalist and annihilationist views, proceeding by way of grasping the world as 'the self and the world are eternal,' etc., and what has that as its object, is worldly bait, or worldly conditions. Lust arisen by way of delight in the round, generating saṃsāra, and what has that as its object, is the bait of the round. Because they are the preliminary part of the path, they are preliminary parts.

Paṭhamanayavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the First Method is concluded.

Dutiyanayavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Second Method

468-469. Abhiññeyyā dhammā nāma “sabbe sattā āhāraṭṭhitikā, dve dhātuyo, tisso dhātuyo, cattāri ariyasaccāni, pañca vimuttāyatanāni, cha anuttariyāni, satta niddasavatthūni, aṭṭhābhibhāyatanāni, navānupubbavihārā, dasa nijjaravatthūnī”ti evaṃpabhedā dhammā[V 0.0172], “sabbaṃ, bhikkhave, abhiññeyya”nti (saṃ. ni. 4.46) dassitā khandhādayo ca. Vānanti vinandhanaṃ bhavādīnaṃ, gamanaṃ vā piyarūpasātarūpesu.

468–469. The phenomena to be directly known are: “All beings are sustained by food, the two elements, the three elements, the Four Noble Truths, the five bases for liberation, the six unsurpassed things, the seven subjects of designation, the eight bases for mastery, the nine successive abodes, the ten grounds for wearing away”—phenomena thus classified, and the aggregates and so on, as shown in “All, bhikkhus, is to be directly known” (Saṃyutta Nikāya 4.46). Vāna means either the binding of existence and so on, or the going after what is pleasing and agreeable.
