Caṅkamaṃ adhiṭṭhahantassa uppannavīriyaṃ vipassanāsahagatanti veditabbaṃ. Ettakenāti “lokiyalokuttaramissakā kathitā”ti ettāvatā. Lokiyanti vadanto na kilamatīti kāyaviññattisamuṭṭhāpakassa lokiyattā acodanīyoti attho. Alabbha…pe… paṭikkhittāti rūpāvacare alabbhamānakaṃ pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ upādāya labbhamānāpi avitakkaavicārā pīti paṭikkhittā, “pītisambojjhaṅgo”ti na vuttoti attho. Kāmāvacare [M 0.0173] vā alabbhamānakaṃ avitakkaavicāraṃ pītiṃ upādāya labbhamānakāva pītibojjhaṅgabhūtā paṭikkhittā, avitakkaavicāro pītisambojjhaṅgo na vuttoti attho.

For one who undertakes walking meditation, the energy that has arisen should be understood as accompanied by insight. By this much: this means, “The mundane and supramundane have been discussed as mixed.” Regarding the phrase, “When speaking of the mundane, one does not become fatigued,” the meaning is that one is not to be blamed, because the originator of bodily intimation is mundane. “Unobtainable… rejected”: with reference to the joy-enlightenment factor being unobtainable in the form realm, even the joy that is obtainable without initial and sustained application is rejected, meaning it is not called the “joy-enlightenment factor.” Or, with reference to joy without initial and sustained application being unobtainable in the sensual realm, even the obtainable joys that constitute the joy-enlightenment factor are rejected, meaning joy without initial and sustained application is not called the “joy-enlightenment factor.”

Ajjhattavimokkhanti ajjhattadhamme abhinivisitvā tato vuṭṭhitamaggo “ajjhattavimokkho”ti idha vuttoti adhippāyo. Na vāretabboti vipassanāpādakesu kasiṇādijhānesu satiādīnaṃ nibbedhabhāgiyattā na paṭikkhipitabboti attho. Anuddharantā pana vipassanā viya bodhiyā maggassa āsannakāraṇaṃ jhānaṃ na hoti, na ca tathā ekantikaṃ kāraṇaṃ, na ca vipassanākiccassa viya jhānakiccassa niṭṭhānaṃ maggoti katvā na uddharanti. Tattha kasiṇajjhānaggahaṇena tadāyattāni āruppānipi gahitānīti daṭṭhabbāni. Asubhajjhānānaṃ avacanaṃ avitakkāvicārassa adhippetattā.

“Internal liberation”: the intention here is that the path that has arisen after entering into internal phenomena is called “internal liberation.” “It should not be prevented”: the meaning is that it should not be rejected, because in the kasiṇa jhānas and so on, which are the basis for insight, mindfulness and other factors are conducive to penetration. However, they do not bring it up because jhāna is not the proximate cause of the path to enlightenment in the same way as insight, nor is it an exclusive cause in the same way, and the culmination of the function of jhāna is not the path, as is the culmination of the function of insight. Here, by the mention of kasiṇa jhāna, the formless attainments dependent on it should be understood as also being included. The foulness meditations are not mentioned because that which is without initial and sustained application is intended.

Dutiyanayavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the second method is concluded.

Tatiyanayavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Third Method

470-471. Tadaṅgasamucchedanissaraṇavivekanissitataṃ vatvā paṭippassaddhivivekanissitattassa avacanaṃ “satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvetī”tiādinā (saṃ. ni. 5.182; vibha. 471) idha bhāvetabbānaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ vuttattā. Bhāvitabojjhaṅgassa hi sacchikātabbā phalabojjhaṅgā [V 0.0173] abhidhammabhājanīye vuttāti. Vossagga-saddo pariccāgattho pakkhandanattho cāti vossaggassa duvidhatā vuttā. Yathāvuttenāti tadaṅgasamucchedappakārena tanninnabhāvārammaṇakaraṇappakārena ca. Pariṇāmentaṃ vipassanākkhaṇe, pariṇataṃ maggakkhaṇe.

470–471. Having stated the dependence on abandonment by substitution, abandonment by eradication, escape, and seclusion, the non-mention of dependence on tranquility-seclusion is because the enlightenment factors to be developed here are mentioned with “one develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness,” etc. (Saṃyutta Nikāya 5.182; Vibhaṅga 471). For one who has developed the enlightenment factors, the fruition enlightenment factors to be realized are described in the Abhidhamma section. The word vossagga has two meanings, that of relinquishment and that of leaping forward; thus, the twofold nature of vossagga is stated. “As stated” refers to the manner of abandonment by substitution and by eradication, and to the manner of making it an object with an inclination towards that. “Transforming” is at the moment of insight; “transformed” is at the moment of the path.

Tatiyanayavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the third method is concluded.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Suttanta division is concluded.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Abhidhamma Division

472. Upekkhanavasenāti [M 0.0174] sabhāvaniddesataṃ dasseti, hāpanavaḍḍhanesu byāpāraṃ akatvā upapattito ikkhanavasenāti attho. Lokiyaupekkhanāya adhikā upekkhanā ajjhupekkhanāti ayamattho idha lokuttarā eva adhippetāti yuttoti.

472. “By way of equanimity” shows that it is a description of its inherent nature; the meaning is that it operates by way of seeing from its arising, without engaging in diminishing or increasing. The meaning of ajjhupekkhanā is an equanimity superior to mundane equanimity; it is fitting that here the supramundane alone is intended.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Abhidhamma division is concluded.

Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Analysis of the Enlightenment Factors is concluded.

11. Maggaṅgavibhaṅgo

11. Analysis of the Path Factors

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Abhidhamma Division

490. Abhidhamme [M 0.0175][V 0.0174] lokuttaracittabhājanīyepi “tasmiṃ kho pana samaye cattāro khandhā honti…pe… aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo hotī”ti (dha. sa. 337) vuttattā idhāpi abhidhammabhājanīye abhidhammānurūpaṃ desanaṃ karonto “aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo”ti ariyopapadataṃ na karoti.

490. In the Abhidhamma, even in the section on supramundane consciousness, it is said: “At that time, there are four aggregates… the eightfold path exists” (Dhammasaṅgaṇī 337). Therefore, here too, in the Abhidhamma section, while teaching in accordance with the Abhidhamma, he does not use the term “eightfold path” with the attribute “noble.”

493. Tasmiṃ samayeti lokiyakālena etesaṃ atirekakiccaṃ dasseti. Viratiuppādanena micchāvācādīni puggalaṃ pajahāpentīti sammādiṭṭhādīni pañca “kārāpakaṅgānī”ti vuttāni. Sammāvācādikiriyā hi virati, tañca etāni kārāpentīti. Virativasenāti viramaṇakiriyāvasena, na kārāpakabhāvena kattubhāvena cāti attho. Imaṃ…pe… kiccātirekataṃ dassetunti lokuttarakkhaṇepi imāneva pañca sammāvācādittayassa ekakkhaṇe kārāpakānīti dassetunti attho. Micchādiṭṭhādikā dasa, tappaccayā akusalā ca dasāti vīsati akusalapakkhiyā, sammādiṭṭhādikā dasa, tappaccayā ca kusalā dasāti vīsati kusalapakkhiyā ca mahācattārīsakasutte (ma. ni. 3.136) vuttāti tassa etaṃ nāmaṃ.

493. “At that time”: this shows their additional function by way of worldly time. Because they cause a person to abandon wrong speech and so on by producing abstinence, the five factors beginning with right view are called “causative factors.” For the action of right speech and so on is abstinence, and these factors cause it. “By way of abstinence”: the meaning is by way of the action of refraining, not by way of being a causative factor or an agent. “This… shows the additional function”: the meaning is that it shows that even at the supramundane moment, these same five factors are the cause for the triad of right speech and so on in a single moment. Wrong view and the other nine, making ten, and the ten unwholesome states conditioned by them—these twenty belong to the unwholesome side. Right view and the other nine, making ten, and the ten wholesome states conditioned by them—these twenty belong to the wholesome side. This is stated in the Mahācattārīsaka Sutta (Majjhima Nikāya 3.136); hence, this name.

Puññabhāgiyāti puññakoṭṭhāse bhavā, puññābhisaṅkhārekadesabhūtāti attho. Khandhopadhiṃ vipaccati, tattha vā vipaccatīti upadhivepakkā.

“Partaking of merit” means existing in the category of merit; the meaning is being a component of meritorious formations. “Ripening with a substrate” means it ripens with the aggregates as its substrate, or it ripens therein.

Pañcaṅgikamaggaṃ uddisitvā tattha ekekaṃ pucchitvā tassa tasseva samayavavatthānaṃ katvā vissajjanaṃ [V 0.0175] “pāṭiyekkaṃ pucchitvā pāṭiyekkaṃ vissajjana”nti vuttaṃ. Saha pana pucchitvā pañcannampi samayavavatthānaṃ katvā vissajjane “tattha katamā sammādiṭṭhiyā paññā”tiādiko paṭiniddeso ekato vissajjanapaṭiniddesattā na pāṭiyekkaṃ pucchāvissajjanaṃ nāma hotīti. Tattha pañcaṅgikavāre eva pāṭiyekkaṃ pucchāvissajjanaṃ sammādiṭṭhādīsu kārāpakaṅgesu ekekamukhāya bhāvanāya magguppattiṃ sandhāya katanti veditabbaṃ. Vācādīni hi pubbasuddhiyā sijjhanti, na maggassa upacārenāti.

Having set forth the five-factored path, to question each factor individually and then, having determined the specific occasion for each, to answer—this is called “questioning individually and answering individually.” But when questioning them together and, after determining the occasion for all five, answering, the detailed explanation beginning, “Therein, what is the wisdom in right view?” is not called individual questioning and answering, because it is a detailed explanation that answers collectively. Here, in the section on the five-factored path, it should be understood that the individual questioning and answering is done with reference to the arising of the path in the causative factors, beginning with right view, through development with each one as the main approach. For speech and the other factors are accomplished through prior purification, not through proximity to the path.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Abhidhamma division is concluded.

Maggaṅgavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Analysis of the Path Factors is concluded.

12. Jhānavibhaṅgo

12. Analysis of Jhāna

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Section on Discourses

Mātikāvaṇṇanā

Exposition of the Mātikā

508. Jhānassa [M 0.0176][V 0.0176] pubbabhāgakaraṇīyasampadā pātimokkhasaṃvarādi. Asubhānussatiyo lokuttarajjhānāni ca ito bahiddhā natthīti sabbappakāra-ggahaṇaṃ karoti, suññā parappavādā samaṇebhīti (ma. ni. 1.139; a. ni. 4.241) vacanena samaṇabhāvakarapubbabhāgakaraṇīyasampadāsampannassapi abhāvaṃ dasseti. Sikkhāpadesu nāmakāyādivasena vuttesu vacanānatikkamavasena sikkhitabbesu, avītikkamanaviraticetanāsaṅkhātesu vā sikkhākoṭṭhāsesu paripūraṇavasena sikkhitabbesu sā sā bhikkhusikkhādikā sikkhāpadekadesabhūtā sikkhitabbāti āha “sikkhāpadesūti idamassa sikkhitabbadhammaparidīpana”nti.

508. The accomplishment of the preliminary duties for jhāna is the restraint of the Pātimokkha and so on. Because the recollections of the unattractive and the supramundane jhānas are not found outside of this teaching, an inclusion of all types is made. By the statement, “Empty are the doctrines of others of ascetics” (MN 1.139; AN 4.241), it shows the absence even of one accomplished in the preliminary duties that make one an ascetic. Regarding the training rules—which are stated in terms of name-group and so on, and which are to be trained in by not transgressing the words, or which are to be trained in by fulfilling the sections of training defined as the volition of abstaining from transgression—those various trainings, such as the bhikkhu's training, being a part of the training rules, should be trained in. Thus it is said: “‘In the training rules’—this is the elucidation of the Dhamma to be trained in.”

Santosādivasena itarītarasantosaṃ, tassa ca vaṇṇavāditaṃ, aladdhā ca aparitassanaṃ, laddhā ca agadhitaparibhoganti ete guṇe dasseti. Jhānabhāvanāya kārakoti paridīpanaṃ kārakabhāvaparidīpanaṃ. Araññantiādinā senāsanassa pabhedaṃ, appasaddantiādinā nirādīnavataṃ, paṭisallānasāruppanti ānisaṃsaṃ dīpetīti āha “senāsanappabhede…pe… paridīpana”nti.

He shows these qualities: contentment with whatever is obtained, speaking in praise of that, not being anxious when not obtaining, and consuming what is obtained without greed. The elucidation 'as one who cultivates jhāna' is an elucidation of the state of being a doer. By 'forest' and so on, he indicates the variety of lodgings; by 'with little noise' and so on, the state of being without drawbacks; and by 'suitable for seclusion,' the benefits. Thus he said: 'In the classification of lodgings...up to...the elucidation.'

Mātikāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The exposition of the Mātikā is concluded.

Niddesavaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Niddesa

509. Kammatthehi [V 0.0177] diṭṭhi-saddādīhi sāsanaṃ vuttanti “diṭṭhattā diṭṭhī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Sabhāvaṭṭhenāti aviparītaṭṭhena. Sikkhiyamāno kāyādīni vineti, na aññathāti āha “sikkhitabbaṭṭhena vinayo”ti, vinayo vā sikkhitabbāni [M 0.0177] sikkhāpadāni, khandhattayaṃ sikkhitabbanti vinayo viyāti vinayoti dasseti. Satthu anusāsanadānabhūtaṃ sikkhattayanti āha “anusiṭṭhidānavasenā”ti.

509. The teaching is spoken of by way of its functions, such as view, faith, and so on, hence it is said, 'a view because of being seen,' and so on. By way of intrinsic nature—that is, by way of its unerring nature. One who trains disciplines the body and so forth, not otherwise; thus it is said: 'Discipline by way of what should be trained.' Or, discipline refers to the training rules which are to be trained in; since the threefold aggregate is to be trained in, it is like a means of discipline, thus it is shown to be 'discipline'. The threefold training, which is the act of giving the Teacher's instruction, is said 'by way of giving instruction.'

Sammādiṭṭhipaccayattāti sammādiṭṭhiyā paccayattā. Tisso hi sikkhā sikkhantassa sammādiṭṭhi paripūratīti. “Tasmātiha tvaṃ bhikkhu ādimeva visodhehi kusalesu dhammesu, ko cādi kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ? Sīlañca suvisuddhaṃ diṭṭhi ca ujukā”ti (saṃ. ni. 5.369) vacanato sammādiṭṭhipubbaṅgamaṃ sikkhattayaṃ. Etasmiñca atthadvaye phalakāraṇopacārehi sikkhattayaṃ “diṭṭhī”ti vuttaṃ, kusaladhammehi vā attano ekadesabhūtehīti adhippāyo. Bhagavato vinayanakiriyattā vinayo sikkhattayaṃ, taṃ pana vinayanaṃ dhammeneva avisamasabhāvena, desanādhammena vā pavattaṃ, na daṇḍādināti “dhammavinayo”ti vuttaṃ.

'Because of right view' means due to being a condition for right view. For one training in the three trainings, right view becomes fulfilled. By the statement 'Therefore, monk, purify at the very beginning the wholesome qualities. And what is the beginning of wholesome qualities? Virtue that is well-purified and view that is straight' (SN 5.369), the threefold training is preceded by right view. In these two meanings, the threefold training is called 'view' by way of metaphorical usage regarding effect and cause, or because it is part of one's own wholesome qualities—this is the intention. Due to the Blessed One's act of disciplining, the threefold training is 'discipline.' That disciplining, however, proceeds by means of the Dhamma—through its even nature or through the teaching of the Dhamma—not by means of a stick and the like. Hence, it is called 'Dhamma-Vinaya.'

Anavajjadhammatthanti paramānavajjanibbānatthaṃ, akuppacetovimuttiatthaṃ vā. Dhammesu abhiññeyyādīsu abhijānanādikāraṇaṃ sikkhattayanti taṃ “dhammavinayo”ti vuttaṃ. “Imissā imasmi”nti punappunaṃ vuccamānaṃ niyamakaraṇaṃ hoti, eva-saddalopo vā katoti adhippāyenāha “niyamo kato”ti.

'For the purpose of the blameless Dhamma' means for the purpose of the supreme blameless Nibbāna, or for the purpose of the unshakable liberation of mind. The threefold training is called 'Dhamma-Vinaya' because it is the cause of direct knowledge and so on, in the phenomena to be directly known and other such phenomena. The repeated statement 'of this, in this' constitutes the making of a rule; or, intending that the word 'eva' has been elided, he said, 'a rule has been made.'

510. Bhikkhukoti anaññatthena ka-kārena padaṃ vaḍḍhitanti “bhikkhanadhammatāyā”ti atthamāha. Bhikkhakoti pana pāṭhe bhikkhatīti bhikkhakoti attho. Jallikaṃ rajamissaṃ malaṃ, amissaṃ malameva. Bhinnapaṭadharoti nibbacanaṃ bhinnapaṭadhare bhikkhu-saddassa niruḷhattā vuttaṃ.

510. 'Bhikkhuko'—the word is expanded by the suffix 'ka' to denote its specific nature; thus, he gives the meaning 'because of the nature of begging.' But in the reading 'bhikkhaka,' the meaning is 'one who begs.' 'Jallikaṃ' refers to dirt mixed with dust; 'amissaṃ' means unmixed dirt. The explanation 'wearer of torn robes' is stated because the word 'bhikkhu' is established in the meaning of one who wears torn robes.

Yassa bhāvetabbo pahātabbo ca odhi avasiṭṭho atthi, so odhiso, arahā pana tadabhāvā odhirahitoti “anodhiso kilesānaṃ pahānā bhikkhū”ti vutto. Odhi-saddo vā ekadese [V 0.0178] niruḷhoti sabbamaggā sabbakilesā ca arahatā bhāvitā pahīnā ca “odhī”ti na vuccanti. Pahānāti idañca nibbacanaṃ bhedanapariyāyavasena vuttanti veditabbaṃ.

One who still has a remnant (odhi) to develop and abandon is called 'odhiso' (one with remnants), whereas an arahant, due to the absence of that, is 'odhirahito' (one without remnants). Thus, it is said, 'a bhikkhu is one without remnants (anodhiso) by the abandonment of defilements.' Or, the word 'odhi' is established only in a partial sense; for an arahant, all paths and all defilements have been developed and abandoned, so they are not called 'odhī.' 'Pahānā'—this explanation should be understood as being stated in terms of the mode of breaking apart.

Sekkhotiādinā [M 0.0178] bhikkhu-saddena vuccamānaṃ atthaṃ guṇavasena dasseti, heṭṭhā pana “samaññāya paṭiññāyā”ti paññāyanavasena, “bhikkhatī”tiādinā nibbacanavasena dassito.

By 'trainee' and so on, he shows the meaning expressed by the word 'bhikkhu' by way of qualities. But previously, it was shown by way of designation ('by common designation, by acknowledgment'), and by way of derivation ('he begs,' and so on).

Sekkho bhikkhūti satta sekkhā kathitā, bhinnattā pāpakānaṃ…pe… bhikkhūti khīṇāsavova kathitoti idaṃ dvayaṃ “sekkhoti puthujjanakalyāṇakena saddhiṃ satta ariyā, bhinnattāti iminā pana cattāro phalaṭṭhā”ti iminā dvayena na sameti, tadidaṃ nippariyāyadassanaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. “Sesaṭṭhānesu puthujjanakalyāṇakādayo kathitā”ti vuttaṃ, nanu paṭiññāya bhikkhusīlopi vuttoti? Vutto, na pana idhādhippeto sabbappakārajjhānanibbattakassa adhippetattā.

'A bhikkhu who is a trainee'—here the seven trainees are spoken of. 'A bhikkhu because of having broken evil things...'—here only the one whose cankers are destroyed is spoken of. This pair of definitions does not align with the other pair of explanations, namely: that 'trainee' refers to the seven noble ones along with the virtuous worldling, and that 'bhinnattā' refers to the four established in the fruit. This should be understood as the direct meaning being stated. It is said, 'In the remaining instances, virtuous worldlings and others are spoken of.' But was not the one virtuous as a bhikkhu by acknowledgment also spoken of? He was, but that is not the intention here, because the producer of all kinds of jhāna is intended.

Bhagavato vacanaṃ upasampadākammakaraṇassa kāraṇattā ṭhānaṃ, tadanurūpaṃ ṭhānārahaṃ, anūnañattianussāvanaṃ uppaṭipāṭiyā ca avuttanti attho.

The Blessed One's word is the basis for performing the act of ordination, being the cause; what is in accordance with that is worthy of the basis. The meaning is that 'a motion and announcement without deficiency' means that it is not recited with omissions or out of order.

511. Nippariyāyato sīlaṃ samādānaviratiavītikkamanaviratibhāvatoti adhippāyo. Anabhijjhādīni sandhāya cetasikasīlassa pariyāyasīlatā vuttā. Nagaravaḍḍhakī vatthuvijjācariyoti vadanti. Catubbidho āhāro asitādīni, bhakkhitabbabhuñjitabbalehitabbacubitabbāni vā.

511. The intention is that, in a direct sense, virtue is the state of being abstention by undertaking and abstention from transgression. Referring to non-covetousness and so on, the figurative nature of mental virtue is stated. They say that a 'nagaravaḍḍhakī' is a master of architecture. The fourfold nutriment is what is eaten and so on, or what is to be chewed, eaten, licked, and sucked.

Pātimokkhasaṃvarena upeto pihitindriyo hoti tiṇṇaṃ sucaritānaṃ indriyasaṃvarāhārattā, pātimokkhasaṃvaro vā indriyasaṃvarassa upanissayo hoti. Iti pātimokkhasaṃvarena pihitindriyo “pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto”ti vutto. Iminā adhippāyena “saṃvuto”ti etassa pihitindriyoti atthamāha. Pātimokkhena ca saṃvarena cāti idaṃ pātimokkhato aññaṃ sīlaṃ kāyikaavītikkamādiggahaṇena gahitanti iminā adhippāyena vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Dutiyo panattho dvinnampi ekatthataṃ sandhāya vutto.

Endowed with restraint by the Pātimokkha, one has guarded sense faculties, because restraint of the senses is the nutriment for the three good conducts. Or, restraint by the Pātimokkha is the supporting condition for restraint of the senses. Thus, one with guarded sense faculties through restraint by the Pātimokkha is called 'restrained by the Pātimokkha restraint.' With this intention, he states the meaning of 'saṃvuto' (restrained) as 'pihitindriyo' (one with guarded sense faculties). And 'by the Pātimokkha and by restraint'—this should be understood as being stated with the intention that virtue other than the Pātimokkha is included by the mention of bodily non-transgression and so on. The second meaning, however, is stated with reference to the single meaning of both.

513. Sabbampi [V 0.0179] dussīlyanti iminā abhijjhādayo ca gahitāti sandhāyāha “manasāpi ācarati eva, tasmā taṃ dassetu”nti. Tatthāti kāyikavītikkamādivasena vuttesu anācāresu. Garubhaṇḍavissajjanamāpajjatīti thullaccayaṃ āpajjatīti attho.

513. 'All misconduct' implies that covetousness and so on are also included; intending this, he said, 'One also acts with the mind; therefore, that should be shown.' 'Here' refers to the misconducts mentioned with reference to bodily transgression and so forth. 'Incurring the disposal of a serious item' means incurring a thullaccaya—that is the meaning.

Aropimoti [M 0.0179] saṅghikabhūmiyaṃ uṭṭhito vutto. Phātikammanti garubhaṇḍantarabhūtaṃ kammaṃ. Daṇḍakammanti yathāvuttaṃ hatthakammamāha. Sināyanti etenāti sinānaṃ, cuṇṇādi.

'Aropimo' is said of one who has stood up on land belonging to the Saṅgha. 'Phātikamma' means an action included among serious items. 'Daṇḍakamma' refers to the manual act as stated. 'Sināna' means that by which one bathes, such as powder and so on.

Saccālīkena piyavādī “cāṭū”ti vuccati, cāṭuṃ attānaṃ icchatīti cāṭukāmo, tassa bhāvo cāṭukamyatā. Muggasūpassa appavisanaṭṭhānaṃ nāma natthi sabbāhārehi aviruddhattāti adhippāyo. Paribhaṭati dhāreti, poseti vāti paribhaṭo, atha vā parivārabhūto bhaṭo sevako paribhaṭo.

One who speaks pleasing words with a mixture of truth and falsehood is called a 'flatterer' (cāṭu); one who desires to be a flatterer is a 'cāṭukāmo'; and the state of that is 'cāṭukamyatā' (desire to flatter). The intention is that there is no place unsuitable for mung bean soup, as it is not incompatible with any food. One who attends to, maintains, or nourishes is 'paribhaṭo'; or alternatively, a servant who is part of the retinue is 'paribhaṭo.'

Bhaṇḍāgārikakammaṃ gihīnaṃ kariyamānaṃ vuttaṃ. Piṇḍatthaṃ paṭipiṇḍadānaṃ, piṇḍaṃ datvā paṭipiṇḍaggahaṇaṃ vā piṇḍapaṭipiṇḍaṃ. Saṅghabhogacetiyabhogānaṃ ayoniso vicāraṇaṃ saṅghuppādacetiyuppādapaṭṭhapanaṃ, attano santake viya paṭipajjananti keci.

The work of a storekeeper being done by householders is spoken of. Giving a return-alms for the sake of an alms, or giving an alms and then taking a return-alms, is 'piṇḍapaṭipiṇḍa' (alms in exchange for alms). Some say that unwise management of the Saṅgha's property or the property of a shrine, establishing detriment for the Saṅgha or detriment for a shrine, and treating them as if they were one's own, is 'saṅghuppādacetiyuppādapaṭṭhapana.'

514. Gāvo caranti etthāti gocaro, gocaro viyāti gocaro, abhiṇhaṃ caritabbaṭṭhānaṃ. Gāvo vā cakkhādīni indriyāni, tehi caritabbaṭṭhānaṃ gocaro. Ayutto gocaro agocaroti tadañño yutto “gocaro”ti vutto.

514. 'Cows wander here,' thus it is 'gocaro' (pasture); like a pasture, it is a pasture—a place to be frequented. Or, the 'cows' are the faculties, such as the eye; the place where they should wander is 'gocaro'. An unsuitable pasture is 'agocaro' (not a pasture); what is other than that, the suitable one, is called 'gocaro' (a pasture).

Vā-saddo vidhunanatthopi hotīti katvā āha “viniddhutakibbisāni vā”ti.

Thinking that the word 'vā' also has the meaning of shaking off, he said, 'or having shaken off defilements.'

515. Avarā pacchimā mattā etesanti oramattakāni. Saṃyamakaraṇīyānīti kāyavācāsaṃyamamattena kattabbapaṭikammāni, vikkhipitabbāni vā. “Puna na evaṃ karomī”ti cittena saṃvaramattena, indriyasaṃvareneva vā karaṇīyāni saṃvarakaraṇīyāni. Divivihārajanapadavāsī divivihāravāsī. Manassa adhiṭṭhānameva adhiṭṭhānāvikammaṃ. Desanā idha “vuṭṭhānāvikamma”nti adhippetā. Tattha “cittuppādakaraṇīyāni manasikārapaṭibaddhānī”ti vacanato pātimokkhasaṃvaravisuddhatthaṃ [V 0.0180] anatikkamanīyāni anāpattigamanīyāni vajjāni vuttānīti ācariyassa adhippāyo. Catubbidhassāti attānuvādaparānuvādadaṇḍaduggatibhayassa.

515. The later measures are inferior; therefore, they are minor. Actions to be done by way of restraint are remedial actions to be done with mere restraint of body and speech, or those that should be abandoned. Actions to be done by way of self-restraint are those to be done with the thought, 'I will not do this again,' with mere restraint of mind, or with restraint of the senses. One who dwells in a village by day is a day-dweller. The determination of the mind itself is non-transgression of resolve. Here, 'teaching' is meant as 'non-transgression of emergence.' In that context, the teacher's intention is that the statement 'actions to be done relating to the arising of the mind, connected with attention,' refers to faults that are not to be transgressed and do not lead to an offense, stated for the purpose of purity of restraint by the Pātimokkha. The fourfold fear is fear of self-accusation, fear of others' accusation, fear of punishment, and fear of a bad destination.

516. “Idha bhikkhū”ti bhikkhu eva adhippetoti sandhāya “sesasikkhā pana atthuddhāravasena sikkhā-saddassa atthadassanatthaṃ vuttā”ti āha. Bhikkhuggahaṇaṃ [M 0.0180] pana aggaparisāmukhena sabbajjhānanibbattakānaṃ catunnampi parisānaṃ dassanatthaṃ kataṃ. Guṇato vā bhikkhu adhippetoti sabbāpi sikkhā idhādhippetāti daṭṭhabbā. Sabbena sikkhāsamādānenāti ettha yena samādānena sabbāpi sikkhā samādinnā honti, taṃ ekampi sabbasamādānakiccakarattā sabbasamādānaṃ nāma hoti, anekesu pana vattabbameva natthi. Sabbena sikkhitabbākārenāti avītikkamadesanāvuṭṭhānavattacaraṇādiākārena. Vītikkamanavasena sesassapi nissesatākaraṇaṃ sandhāya “bhinnassapī”tiādimāha.

516. Referring to 'Here, a bhikkhu,' it is said that a bhikkhu is intended, and 'the remaining trainings, however, are stated for the purpose of showing the meaning of the word "training" by way of extracting its meaning.' The inclusion of 'bhikkhu,' however, is done for the purpose of showing all four assemblies, which bring forth all jhānas, by means of the foremost assembly. Or, a bhikkhu is intended by way of virtue; thus, all the trainings should be seen as intended here. Regarding 'by undertaking all trainings,' here, whatever single undertaking by which all trainings are undertaken is called 'all undertakings' because it performs the function of all undertakings; in the case of multiple undertakings, there is nothing more to be said. Regarding 'in every manner to be trained,' it means in the manner of non-transgression, teaching, emergence, the practice of proper conduct, and so on. Referring to the complete vitiation of the rest by way of transgression, it is said: 'even of the broken,' and so on.

519. Āvaraṇīyehi cittaparisodhanabhāvanā jāgariyānuyogoti katvā āha “bhāvana”nti. Suppapariggāhakanti “suppapariggāhakaṃ nāma idaṃ ito pubbe ito parañca natthi, ayametassa paccayo”tiādinā pariggāhakaṃ.

519. Because the practice of wakefulness is the cultivation of purifying the mind from obstacles, it is said, 'cultivation.' As for 'well-comprehended,' it is that which is comprehended by statements such as, 'This is well-comprehended; there is nothing before this or after this; this is its condition,' and so on.

520-521. Yuttoti ārambhamāno. Sātaccaṃ nepakkañca pavattayamāno jāgariyānuyogaṃ anuyutto hotīti sambandhaṃ dasseti.

520-521. 'Yoked' means undertaking. This shows the connection that by maintaining persistence and wisdom, one is devoted to the practice of wakefulness.

522. Lokiyāyapi…pe… āhāti idaṃ vipassanābhāvanāya satipaṭṭhānādayo ekasmiṃ ārammaṇe saha nappavattanti, pavattamānānipi indriyabalāni bojjhaṅgesveva antogadhāni honti. Pītisambojjhaṅgaggahaṇena hi tadupanissayabhūtaṃ saddhindriyaṃ saddhābalañca gahitameva hoti “saddhūpanisaṃ pāmojja”nti (saṃ. ni. 2.23) vuttattā. Maggaṅgāni pañceva vipassanākkhaṇe pavattantīti imamatthaṃ sandhāya vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

522. He says, 'Even in the mundane...'—here, the foundations of mindfulness and so on, in insight meditation, do not arise simultaneously on a single object; and even when they arise, the faculties and powers are included within the enlightenment factors. For by the inclusion of the enlightenment factor of joy, the faculty of faith and the power of faith, which are its supporting conditions, are already included, as it is said: 'Joy has faith as its decisive support' (Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.23). It should be understood that this statement—that only five path factors arise in the moment of insight—is made with this meaning in mind.

523. Samantato, sammā, samaṃ vā sātthakādipajānanaṃ sampajānaṃ, tadeva sampajaññaṃ. Tenāti satisampayuttattā eva uddese avuttāpi sati niddese “sato”ti iminā vuttāti adhippāyo.

523. Clear comprehension is the knowing—all-round, rightly, or equally—of what is beneficial and so forth; that itself is sampajañña. By that, the intention is that because it is associated with mindfulness, even though mindfulness is not stated in the summary, it is stated in the detailed explanation by the word 'mindful' (sato).

Sātthakānaṃ [V 0.0181] abhikkamādīnaṃ sampajānanaṃ sātthakasampajaññaṃ. Evaṃ sappāyasampajaññaṃ. Abhikkamādīsu pana bhikkhācāragocare aññatthāpi ca pavattesu avijahite kammaṭṭhānasaṅkhāte gocare sampajaññaṃ gocarasampajaññaṃ. Abhikkamādīsu asammuyhanameva sampajaññaṃ asammohasampajaññaṃ.

Clear comprehension of what is purposeful in going forward and so on is purposeful clear comprehension. Similarly, there is suitable clear comprehension. Furthermore, in going forward and so on, in the domain of the alms round, and also in other occurrences, clear comprehension within the domain known as the meditation subject, which is not abandoned, is clear comprehension of the domain. Clear comprehension that is simply non-confusion in going forward and so on is clear comprehension of non-delusion.

Dve [M 0.0181] kathāti vacanakaraṇākaraṇakathā na kathitapubbā. Vacanaṃ karomi eva, tasmā subbacattā paṭivacanaṃ demīti attho.

'The two talks' refers to the talk about doing and not doing what is said, which was not spoken of before. The meaning is: 'I will indeed do what is said; therefore, because I am amenable, I give a reply.'

Kammaṭṭhānasīsenevāti kammaṭṭhānaggeneva, kammaṭṭhānaṃ padhānaṃ katvā evāti attho. Tena “pattampi acetana”ntiādinā vakkhamānaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ, yathāparihariyamānaṃ vā avijahitvāti dasseti. “Tasmā”ti etassa “dhammakathā kathetabbāyevāti vadantī”ti etena sambandho. Bhayeti paracakkādibhaye.

'With the meditation subject as the head' means with the meditation subject as chief, that is, having made the meditation subject primary. This shows that the meditation subject—which will be explained by the phrase 'even the bowl is inanimate,' and so on—should not be abandoned, or should not be abandoned while it is being handled. The word 'therefore' is connected with the phrase 'they say that a Dhamma talk should indeed be spoken.' 'In fear' refers to fear of a foreign army and so forth.

Avasesaṭṭhāneti yāguaggahitaṭṭhāne. Ṭhānacaṅkamanamevāti adhiṭṭhātabbiriyāpathavasena vuttaṃ, na bhojanādikāle avassaṃ kattabbanisajjāyapi paṭikkhepavasena.

'In the remaining place' means in the place where rice-gruel is taken. 'Only standing or walking' is stated by way of the postures to be resolved upon; it is not by way of prohibiting even the sitting that must necessarily be done at meal times and so on.

Thero dārucīriyo –

The elder Dārucīriya—

“Tasmātiha te, bāhiya, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ. Diṭṭhe diṭṭhamattaṃ bhavissati, sute mute viññāte. Yato kho te, bāhiya, diṭṭhe diṭṭhamattaṃ bhavissati, sute mute viññāte viññātamattaṃ bhavissati, tato tvaṃ, bāhiya, na tena, yato tvaṃ, bāhiya, na tena. Tato tvaṃ, bāhiya, na tattha, yato tvaṃ, bāhiya, na tattha. Tato tvaṃ, bāhiya, nevidha na huraṃ na ubhayamantarena. Esevanto dukkhassā”ti (udā. 10) –

Therefore, Bāhiya, you should train yourself thus: In the seen, there will be only the seen; in the heard, only the heard; in the sensed, only the sensed; in the cognized, only the cognized. When, Bāhiya, for you in the seen there is only the seen, in the heard only the heard, in the sensed only the sensed, in the cognized only the cognized, then, Bāhiya, you will not be 'by that.' Since you are not 'by that,' Bāhiya, you will not be 'in that.' Since you are not 'in that,' Bāhiya, you will be neither here nor beyond nor in between the two. This itself is the end of suffering.

Ettakena arahattaṃ sacchākāsi.

With just that, he realized arahantship.

Khāṇuādipariharaṇatthaṃ, patiṭṭhitapādapariharaṇatthaṃ vā passena haraṇaṃ vītiharaṇanti vadanti. Yāva [V 0.0182] patiṭṭhitapādo, tāva āharaṇaṃ atiharaṇaṃ, tato paraṃ haraṇaṃ vītiharaṇanti ayaṃ vā etesaṃ viseso. Avīcinti nirantaraṃ.

They say that carrying by the side, for the purpose of avoiding stumps and so forth, or for avoiding established plants, is 'carrying past' (vītiharaṇaṃ). Or this is the distinction between them: as long as the foot is planted, bringing is 'carrying too far' (atiharaṇaṃ), and carrying beyond that is 'carrying past' (vītiharaṇaṃ). 'Avīci' means continuously.

Paṭhamajavanepi…pe… na hotīti idaṃ pañcaviññāṇavīthiyaṃ itthipurisoti rajjanādīnaṃ abhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tattha hi āvajjanavoṭṭhabbanānaṃ ayoniso āvajjanavoṭṭhabbanavasena iṭṭhe itthirūpādimhi lobho, aniṭṭhe ca paṭigho uppajjati. Manodvāre pana itthipurisoti rajjanādi hoti, tassa [M 0.0182] pañcadvārajavanaṃ mūlaṃ, yathāvuttaṃ vā sabbaṃ bhavaṅgādi. Evaṃ manodvārajavanassa mūlavasena mūlapariññā vuttā. Āgantukatāvakālikatā pana pañcadvārajavanasseva apubbatittaratāvasena. Maṇisappo sīhaḷadīpe vijjamānā ekā sappajātīti vadanti. Calananti kampanaṃ.

'In the first impulsion...' and so on, '...it does not occur'—this is said with reference to the absence of lust and so forth regarding 'male' or 'female' in the five-sense-door cognitive process. For in that case, due to unwise adverting and determining, greed arises toward a desirable object such as a woman’s form, and aversion arises toward an undesirable one. In the mind-door process, however, lust and so forth regarding 'male' or 'female' do occur. Its root is the five-door impulsion, or all states as stated, beginning with the life-continuum. Thus, the full understanding of the root is stated by way of the root of the mind-door impulsion. The adventitious and temporary nature, however, pertains specifically to the five-door impulsion, by way of its being unprecedented and swift. They say that the 'jewel-snake' is a species of snake found on the island of Sri Lanka. 'Movement' means trembling.

Atiharatīti yāva mukhā āharati. Vītiharatīti tato yāva kucchi, tāva harati, kucchigataṃ vā passato harati. Allattañca anupāletīti vāyuādīhi ativisosanaṃ yathā na hoti, tathā pāleti. Ābhujatīti pariyesanajjhoharaṇajiṇṇājiṇṇatādiṃ āvajjeti, vijānātīti attho. Taṃtaṃvijānananipphādakoyeva hi payogo “sammāpayogo”ti vuttoti. Atha vā “sammāpaṭipattimāgamma abbhantare attā nāma koci bhujanako natthī”tiādinā vijānanaṃ ābhujanaṃ.

'He carries it too far' means he brings it as far as the mouth. 'He carries it past' means from there he carries it as far as the stomach, or he carries it while observing that it has reached the stomach. 'And he maintains its moisture' means he protects it so that it does not become excessively dry from wind and so on. 'He reflects' means he adverts to the searching, swallowing, state of being digested or undigested, and so on; the meaning is that he discerns. For it is the application that accomplishes the discernment of each particular thing that is called 'right application.' Alternatively, 'reflecting' is the discernment, by way of 'having undertaken the right practice, there is no inner self called an "eater,"' and so on.

Aṭṭhāneti manussāmanussapariggahite ayutte ṭhāne khettadevāyatanādike. Tumbato veḷunāḷiādiudakabhājanato. Tanti chaḍḍitaṃ udakaṃ.

'In an inappropriate place' means in an unsuitable place occupied by humans and non-humans, such as fields, shrines of deities, and so on. 'From a gourd' means from a water vessel such as a gourd, a bamboo tube, and so on. 'That' refers to the discarded water.

Gateti gamaneti pubbe abhikkamapaṭikkamaggahaṇena gamanepi purato pacchato ca kāyassa atiharaṇaṃ vuttanti idha gamanameva gahitanti veditabbaṃ, vakkhamāno vā etesaṃ viseso.

'Going' (gati) means the act of going (gamana). It should be understood that although previously, with the inclusion of 'going forward' and 'going back,' the carrying of the body too far forward and backward in the act of going was mentioned, here only the act of going itself is taken. Or, the distinction between these will be explained.

Ettakenāti kammaṭṭhānaṃ avissajjetvā catunnaṃ iriyāpathānaṃ pavattanavacanamattena gocarasampajaññaṃ na pākaṭaṃ hotīti attho. Evaṃ pana sutte kammaṭṭhānaṃ avibhūtaṃ hotīti caṅkamanaṭṭhānanisajjāsu eva pavatte pariggaṇhantassa sutte pavattā apākaṭā hontīti attho.

'By this much' means that clear comprehension of the resort is not made evident merely by the statement of practicing the four postures without relinquishing the meditation subject—this is the meaning. Furthermore, because the meditation subject is not manifest while sleeping, for one who comprehends the practice only while walking, standing, or sitting, the practices occurring in sleep remain unmanifest—this is the meaning.

Kāyādikiriyāmayattā [V 0.0183] āvajjanakiriyāsamuṭṭhitattā ca javanaṃ, sabbampi vā chadvārappavattaṃ kiriyāmayapavattaṃ nāma, dutiyajjhānaṃ vacīsaṅkhāravirahā “tuṇhībhāvo”ti vuccati.

Impulsion is so called because it consists of the activity of the body and so forth, and because it arises from the act of adverting; or, all that occurs at the six doors is called a process consisting of activity. The second jhāna, due to the absence of verbal formations, is called 'silence.'

526. Upāsanaṭṭhānanti issāsānaṃ viya upāsanassa sikkhāyogakaraṇassa kammaṭṭhānaupāsanassa ṭhānanti attho. Tameva hi atthaṃ dassetuṃ “yogapatha”nti āhāti. Sīsaṃ dhovatīti icchādāsabyā bhujissataṃ ñāpayati, micchāpaṭipannehi vā pakkhittaṃ ayasarajaṃ dhovati.

526. 'A place for practice' means a place for the practice of the meditation subject, which is the application of training, like the practice of archers—this is the meaning. To show this very meaning, he says 'path of application.' 'He washes his head' means he makes known his freedom from the servitude of desire, or he washes off the dust of disrepute cast by those of wrong practice.

529. Vinayapariyāyena [M 0.0183] adinnādānapārājike āgataṃ. Suttantapariyāyena āraññakasikkhāpade “pañcadhanusatikaṃ pacchima”nti āgataṃ āraññikaṃ bhikkhuṃ sandhāya. Na hi so vinayapariyāyike araññe vasanato “āraññako pantasenāsano”ti sutte vuttoti.

529. According to the Vinaya method, it is found in the Pārājika rule on taking what is not given. According to the Suttanta method, it is found in the training rule for forest-dwellers with the phrase 'five hundred bow-lengths at the furthest,' referring to a forest-dwelling bhikkhu. For it is not because of dwelling in a forest as defined by the Vinaya method that one is called 'a forest-dweller with a secluded lodging' in the Sutta.

530. “Nitumba”ntipi “nadīkuñja”ntipi yaṃ vadanti, taṃ kandaranti apabbatapadesepi vidugganadīnivattanapadesaṃ kandaranti dasseti.

530. What they call a 'thicket' or a 'river-grove,' that is a ravine. He shows that even in a region without mountains, a place where a river turns in difficult terrain is called a ravine.

531. Bhājetvā dassitanti etena bhājetabbataṃ ante niddesassa kāraṇaṃ dasseti.

531. 'Having analyzed, he shows'—by this, he indicates the reason for the analysis at the end of the exposition.

533. Rahassa kiriyā rahassaṃ, taṃ arahati tassa yogganti rāhasseyyakaṃ. Vicittā hi taddhitāti. Rahasi vā sādhu rahassaṃ, tassa yoggaṃ rāhasseyyakaṃ.

533. A secret action is a secret; that which is worthy of it, suitable for it, is 'rāhasseyyaka.' For secondary derivatives are varied. Or, what is good in secret is a secret; suitable for that is 'rāhasseyyaka.'

536. Paṇihitoti suṭṭhu ṭhapito.

536. 'Well-directed' means well-established.

537. Pariggahitaniyyānanti pariggahitaniyyānasabhāvaṃ, kāyādīsu suṭṭhu pavattiyā niyyānasabhāvayuttanti attho. Kāyādipariggahaṇaṃ ñāṇaṃ vā pariggaho, taṃ-sampayuttatāya pariggahitaṃ niyyānabhūtaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ katvāti attho.

537. 'Comprehended means of escape' means having the nature of a comprehended means of escape; that is, it is endowed with the nature of a means of escape through its proper occurrence in regard to the body and so on. The comprehension of the body and so on is knowledge, or the act of comprehending. The meaning is: having made the establishment, which has become a means of escape, comprehended through its association with that.

542-543. Vikārappattiyāti cittassa vikārāpattibhāvenāti attho. Sabbasaṅgāhikavasenāti sattasaṅkhāragatasabbakodhasaṅgāhikavasena. Sabbasaṅgahaṇañca samucchedappahānassapi adhippetattā katanti veditabbaṃ.

542-543. 'Due to its susceptibility to alteration' means due to the mind's becoming susceptible to alteration. 'By way of complete inclusion' means by way of including all anger related to what is designated as 'beings.' And it should be understood that this complete inclusion is done because the abandonment by eradication is also intended.

546. Idaṃ [V 0.0184] sandhāyāti “dve dhammā”ti sandhāya. Ekavacanena “thinamiddha”nti uddisitvāpi niddese “santā”ti vacanabhedo, bahuvacanaṃ katanti attho. Nirodhasantatāyāti vacanaṃ aṅgasantatāya, sabhāvasantatāya vā santatānivāraṇatthaṃ.

546. 'Referring to this' means referring to 'two phenomena.' Although 'sloth and torpor' is specified with a singular term, in the exposition the number is changed to the plural 'santā,' meaning it is made plural. The word is used to preclude discontinuity, either as a continuity of components or as a continuity of nature.

550. Thinamiddhavikāravirahā tappaṭipakkhasaññā ālokasaññā nāma hoti. Teneva vuttaṃ “ayaṃ saññā ālokā hotī”ti.

550. Due to the absence of the influence of sloth and torpor, the perception that is their counterpart is called the perception of light. For that reason it is said, 'This perception is light.'

553. “Vantattā muttattā”tiādīni, “ālokā hotī”tiādīni ca “cattattātiādīnī”ti vuttāni. Ādi-saddena vā dvinnampi niddesapadāni [M 0.0184] saṅgahetvā tattha yāni yesaṃ vevacanāni, tāneva sandhāya “aññamaññavevacanānī”ti vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Paṭimuñcatoti etena sārambhaṃ abhibhavaṃ dasseti. Nirāvaraṇā hutvā ābhujati sampajānātīti nirāvaraṇābhogā, taṃsabhāvattā vivaṭā.

553. The phrases beginning with 'due to being disgorged, due to being released' and those beginning with 'it is light' are said to be like the phrases beginning with 'due to being abandoned.' Alternatively, it should be understood that by the word 'etc.,' the terms of exposition for both are included, and referring to whichever of them are synonyms for the others, they are called 'mutual synonyms.' By 'he releases,' the overcoming of agitation is shown. 'Unhindered application' means: having become unhindered, one applies the mind and clearly comprehends; because it has this nature, it is 'open.'

556. “Vikālo nu kho, na nu kho”ti anicchayatāya katavatthujjhācāramūlako vippaṭisāro vatthujjhācāro kāraṇavohārena vuttoti daṭṭhabbo.

556. It should be understood that the remorse rooted in improper conduct regarding an object, which arises from the uncertainty, 'Is it the wrong time, or is it not?' is called 'improper conduct regarding an object' by way of causal designation.

562. Kilissantīti kilesentīti atthaṃ vadanti, sadarathabhāvena sayameva vā kilissanti. Na hi te uppajjamānā kilesarahitā uppajjantīti.

562. They say that 'they are defiled' means 'they defile'; or, they themselves are defiled by being afflicted. For when they arise, they do not arise without defilements.

564. Idheva ca vibhaṅge “upeto hotī”tiādi tattha tattha vuttameva.

564. And right here in the Vibhaṅga, the phrase 'he is endowed' and so on is stated in various places.

588. Niddesavasenāti “tattha katamā upekkhā? Yā upekkhā”tiādiniddesavasena. “Imāya upekkhāya upeto hotī”tiādi paṭiniddesavasenāti vadanti. “Tattha katamā…pe… imāya upekkhāya upeto hotī”ti etena puggalo niddiṭṭho hoti, “samupeto”tiādinā paṭiniddiṭṭho. Yāva vā “samannāgato”ti padaṃ, tāva niddiṭṭho, “tena vuccati upekkhako”ti iminā paṭiniddiṭṭhoti tesaṃ vasena niddesapaṭiniddesā yojetabbā. Pakārenāti upekkhāya “upekkhanā”tiādidhammappakārena “upeto samupeto”tiādipuggalappakārena ca upekkhakasaddassa atthaṃ ṭhapento paṭṭhapenti. “Upekkhā”ti etassa atthassa “upekkhanā”ti kāraṇaṃ. Upekkhanāvasena [V 0.0185] hi upekkhāti. Tathā “upeto samupeto”ti etesaṃ “upāgato samupāgato”ti kāraṇanti evaṃ dhammapuggalavasena tassa tassatthassa kāraṇaṃ dassentā vivaranti, “upekkhako”ti imasseva vā atthassa “imāya upekkhāya upeto hotī”tiādinā kāraṇaṃ dassentā. “Upekkhanā ajjhupekkhanā samupeto”tiādinā byañjanānaṃ vibhāgaṃ dassentā vibhajanti. Upekkhaka-saddantogadhāya vā upekkhāya tasseva ca upekkhaka-saddassa visuṃ atthavacanaṃ “yā upekkhā upekkhanā”tiādinā, “imāya upekkhāya upeto hotī”tiādinā ca [M 0.0185] byañjanavibhāgo. Sabbathā aññātatā nikujjhitabhāvo, kenaci pakārena viññātepi niravasesaparicchindanābhāvo gambhīrabhāvo.

588. 'By way of exposition' means by way of an exposition such as, 'Therein, what is equanimity? Whatever equanimity…' They say that the passage beginning 'he is endowed with this equanimity' is by way of counter-exposition. By the passage, 'Therein, what is… he is endowed with this equanimity,' the person is expounded; by the passage beginning 'fully endowed,' he is counter-expounded. Or, he is expounded up to the word 'possessed,' and counter-expounded by 'therefore he is called equanimous.' Thus, the expositions and counter-expositions should be connected according to these. 'By way of characteristic' means they establish the meaning of the word 'equanimous' by way of the characteristic of the phenomenon, such as 'looking on' for equanimity, and by way of the characteristic of the person, such as 'endowed, fully endowed.' The reason for the meaning of 'equanimity' is 'looking on,' for it is by way of looking on that there is equanimity. Similarly, 'approached, fully approached' is the reason for 'endowed, fully endowed.' Thus they explain, showing the reason for each meaning by way of phenomena and persons; or showing the reason for the meaning of 'equanimous' itself by the passage beginning 'he is endowed with this equanimity.' They analyze by showing the distinction of expressions with the passage beginning 'looking on, closely looking on, fully endowed.' Or, the distinction of expressions is the separate statement of meaning for the equanimity contained within the word 'equanimous,' and for that same word 'equanimous,' by the passages beginning 'whatever equanimity, looking on…' and 'he is endowed with this equanimity…' Profundity is utter unknowability, a state of being hidden; it is the absence of exhaustive delimitation even when known in some way.

602. Uparibhūmippattiyāti idaṃ “rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā”ti ettheva yojetabbaṃ. Viññāṇañcāyatanādīnipi vā ākāsānañcāyatanādīnaṃ uparibhūmiyoti sabbatthāpi na na yujjati.

602. 'For the attainment of a higher plane'—this should be connected right here with 'by completely transcending perceptions of form.' And since the bases of infinite consciousness and so on are higher planes than the bases of infinite space and so on, it is not unsuitable in any case.

610. Viññāṇañcāyatananiddese “anantaṃ viññāṇanti taṃyeva ākāsaṃ viññāṇena phuṭaṃ manasi karoti anantaṃ pharati, tena vuccati anantaṃ viññāṇa”nti ettha viññāṇenāti etaṃ upayogatthe karaṇavacanaṃ, taṃyeva ākāsaṃ phuṭaṃ viññāṇaṃ manasi karotīti kira aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Ayaṃ vā etassa attho – taṃyeva ākāsaṃ phuṭaṃ viññāṇaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanaviññāṇena manasi karotīti. Ayaṃ panattho yutto – taṃyeva ākāsaṃ viññāṇena phuṭaṃ tena gahitākāraṃ manasi karoti, evaṃ taṃ viññāṇaṃ anantaṃ pharatīti. Yañhi ākāsaṃ paṭhamāruppasamaṅgī viññāṇena anantaṃ pharati, taṃ pharaṇākārasahitameva viññāṇaṃ manasikaronto dutiyāruppasamaṅgī anantaṃ pharatīti vuccatīti.

610. In the exposition of the base of infinite consciousness, it is said: '“Infinite consciousness”: one attends to that very space pervaded by consciousness and pervades it as infinite; hence, it is called “infinite consciousness.”' Here, 'by consciousness' is an instrumental case in the sense of application. It is said in the commentary that one attends to the consciousness that has pervaded that very space. Alternatively, this is its meaning: one attends to the consciousness that has pervaded that very space with the consciousness of the base of infinite consciousness. But this interpretation is fitting: one attends to the form apprehended by consciousness as it pervaded that very space, and thus that consciousness pervades infinitely. For, the meditator endowed with the first formless attainment pervades space infinitely with consciousness; by attending to that consciousness together with the mode of its pervading, the meditator endowed with the second formless attainment is said to pervade infinitely.

615. Taṃyeva viññāṇaṃ abhāvetīti yaṃ pubbe “anantaṃ viññāṇa”nti manasi kataṃ, taṃyevāti attho. Tasseva hi ārammaṇabhūtaṃ paṭhamena viya rūpanimittaṃ tatiyenāruppena abhāvetīti.

615. 'One causes that very consciousness to cease' means that which was previously attended to as 'infinite consciousness.' For with the third formless attainment, one causes that very consciousness which served as the object to cease, just as with the first formless attainment one causes the form-sign to cease.

Niddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition is concluded.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Suttanta Analysis is concluded.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Abhidhamma Analysis

623. Abhidhammabhājanīye [V 0.0186] pañcakanayadassane “pañca jhānānī”ti ca, “tattha katamaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhāna”nti ca ādinā uddhaṭaṃ. Uddhaṭānaṃyeva catunnaṃ paṭhamatatiyacatutthapañcamajjhānānaṃ dassanato, dutiyasseva visesadassanato ca.

623. In the Abhidhamma Analysis, in the exposition of the fivefold method, the text is cited beginning with “five jhānas” and “therein, what is the first jhāna?” Of those cited, there is an explanation of the four—the first, third, fourth, and fifth jhānas—and a demonstration of the special nature of the second.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Abhidhamma Analysis is finished.

3. Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Section of Questions

640. Lokuttarāpanetthāti [M 0.0186] etesu tīsujhānesu “lokuttarā siyā appamāṇārammaṇā”ti evaṃ koṭṭhāsikā pana maggakāle, phalakāle vā lokuttarabhūtā evāti adhippāyo. Paricchinnākāsakasiṇālokakasiṇānāpānabrahmavihāracatutthāni sabbatthapādakacatutthe saṅgahitānīti daṭṭhabbāni.

640. Herein, regarding the phrase ‘including the supramundane’: the intention is that in these three jhānas, while it is said ‘they may be supramundane with an immeasurable object,’ at the time of the path or the time of fruition they are indeed supramundane. It should be understood that the fourth jhānas on the limited-space kasiṇa, the light kasiṇa, mindfulness of breathing, and the divine abodes are included in the fourth jhāna that is the basis for everything.

Buddhapaccekabuddhakhīṇāsavā maggaṃ bhāvayiṃsu, phalaṃ sacchikariṃsūti, bhāvessanti sacchikarissantīti ca heṭṭhimamaggaphalānaṃ vasena vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Kusalato terasasu hi catutthesu ayaṃ kathā pavattā, na ca kusalacatutthena arahattamaggaphalāni daṭṭhuṃ sakkoti.

It should be understood that the statement ‘Buddhas, Paccekabuddhas, and arahants have developed the path and realized the fruit, and will develop and will realize’ is spoken with reference to the lower paths and fruits. For this discussion proceeds in regard to the thirteen wholesome fourth jhānas, and with a wholesome fourth jhāna one cannot see the path and fruit of arahantship.

“Kiriyato terasanna”nti ettha lokuttaracatutthaṃ kiriyaṃ natthīti “dvādasanna”nti vattabbaṃ, kusalato vā terasasu sekkhaphalacatutthaṃ antogadhaṃ katvā “kiriyato terasanna”nti asekkhacatutthena saha vadatīti veditabbaṃ. Sabbatthapādakañcettha khīṇāsavānaṃ yāni abhiññādīni santi, tesaṃ sabbesaṃ pādakattā sabbatthapādakanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Na hi tesaṃ vaṭṭaṃ atthīti. Paricchannākāsakasiṇacatutthādīni viya vā navattabbatāya sabbatthapādakasamānattā sabbatthapādakatā daṭṭhabbā.

Herein, regarding ‘of the thirteen functional ones,’ since there is no supramundane functional fourth jhāna, it should be stated as ‘of the twelve.’ Or, it should be understood that having included the fourth jhāna of the trainee’s fruition among the thirteen wholesome ones, it says ‘of the thirteen functional ones’ along with the fourth jhāna of the non-trainee. And here, the basis for everything should be understood as such because it is the basis for all the direct knowledges and so on that the arahants possess. For they have no round of existence. Or, its status as the basis for everything should be understood from its similarity to the basis for everything on account of its not being stated separately, just like the fourth jhānas on the limited-space kasiṇa and so on.

Manosaṅkhārā [V 0.0187] nāma saññāvedanā, cattāropi vā khandhā. Nimittaṃ ārabbhāti ettha “nimittaṃ nibbānañcā”ti vattabbaṃ.

‘Mental formations’ are perception and feeling, or the four aggregates. Here, regarding ‘taking the sign as object,’ it should be stated as ‘the sign and Nibbāna.’

“Ajjhatto dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 2.20.28) ettha “ajjhattā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa yathākammūpagañāṇassa anāgataṃsañāṇassa āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo”ti vuttattā na cetopariyañāṇaṃ viya yathākammūpagañāṇaṃ parasantānagatameva jānāti, sasantānagatampi pana apākaṭaṃ rūpaṃ dibbacakkhu viya apākaṭaṃ kammaṃ vibhāveti. Tenāha “attano kammajānanakāle”ti.

Regarding the passage, ‘An internal state is a condition for an internal state by way of object condition’ (Paṭṭhāna 2.20.28): since it is said here, ‘The internal aggregates are a condition, by way of object condition, for the adverting for the knowledge of the kinds of psychic power, the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings, and the knowledge of the future,’ the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings does not, like the knowledge of others’ minds, know only what pertains to the continuities of others, but it also clarifies obscure kamma pertaining to one’s own continuity, just as the divine eye clarifies obscure form. Hence it is said, ‘at the time of knowing one’s own kamma.’

Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Section of Questions is finished.

Jhānavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of Jhāna is finished.

13. Appamaññāvibhaṅgo

13. Analysis of the Immeasurables

1. Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Suttanta Analysis

642. Sabbadhīti [M 0.0187][V 0.0188] disādesodhinā anodhisopharaṇaṃ vuttaṃ, sabbattatāya sabbāvantanti sattodhinā. Tenāha “anodhiso dassanattha”nti. Tathā-saddo iti-saddo vā na vuttoti “mettāsahagatena cetasā”ti etassa anuvattakaṃ taṃ dvayaṃ tassa pharaṇantarādiṭṭhānaṃ aṭṭhānanti katvā na vuttaṃ, puna “mettāsahagatena cetasā”ti vuttanti attho.

642. The phrase 'in all directions' is stated to indicate boundless pervasion by way of specifying the directions. The phrase 'with all-inclusiveness' is stated to indicate 'all-encompassing' by way of specifying the beings. Therefore it is said: '“Boundlessly” is for the purpose of seeing.' Because the word 'tathā' or 'iti' is not stated, those two words are not stated as following the phrase 'with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness,' since that is not the basis for another pervasion and so on. The meaning is that the phrase 'with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness' is stated again.

643. Hirottappānupālitā mettā na parihāyati āsannasapattassa rāgassa sinehassa ca vipattiyā anuppattitoti adhippāyo.

643. The intention is that loving-kindness, when guarded by moral shame and moral dread, does not decline, because one does not fall into the corrupting influence of its near enemy, which is lust and affection.

645. Adhimuñcitvāti suṭṭhu pasāretvāti attho. Taṃ dassento “adhikabhāvenā”tiādimāha, balavatā vā adhimokkhena adhimuccitvā.

645. ‘Having resolved’: the meaning is ‘having thoroughly extended (the mind).’ To show this, he says, ‘in a superior manner,’ etc., or ‘having resolved with strong conviction.’

648. Heṭṭhā vuttoyevāti “sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabba”nti etesaṃ “sabbena sikkhāsamādānena sabbaṃ sikkhaṃ, sabbena sikkhitabbākārena sabbaṃ sikkha”nti ca jhānavibhaṅge (vibha. aṭṭha. 516) attho vutto. Idha pana sabbena avadhinā attasamatāya sabbasattayuttatāya ca sabbaṃ lokaṃ, sabbāvadhidisādipharaṇākārehi sabbaṃ lokanti ca attho yujjati.

648. As was stated below: the meaning of the phrases 'with all, all, in every way, all' has been explained in the Analysis of Jhāna (Vibh-a 516) as: 'with the complete undertaking of the training, the entire training; with every mode of what is to be trained, the entire training.' Here, however, the suitable meaning is: 'the entire world' in the sense of being without any limit, by way of equality with oneself, and by connection with all beings; and 'the entire world' in the sense of pervading it in all ways, that is, by the modes of pervading all limits, directions, and so on.

650. Paccatthikavighātavasenāti mettādīnaṃ āsannadūrapaccatthikānaṃ rāgabyāpādādīnaṃ vighātavasena. Yaṃ appamāṇaṃ, so averoti so averabhāvoti ayaṃ vā tassa atthoti.

650. ‘By way of destroying the adversaries’ means by way of destroying the near and far adversaries of loving-kindness and so on, that is, lust, ill will, and so on. ‘What is immeasurable, that is without enmity’: this means it is the state of being without enmity, or this is its meaning.

653. Nirayādi [V 0.0189] gati, caṇḍālādi kulaṃ, annādīnaṃ alābhitā bhogo. Ādi-saddena dubbaṇṇatādi gahitaṃ.

653. Destination means the hells and so on; family means the outcastes and so on; enjoyment means not obtaining food and so on. By the word ‘and so on,’ ugliness and the like are included.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Suttanta Analysis is finished.

3. Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Section of Questions

699. Imasmiṃ [M 0.0188] pana…pe… kathitāti iminā imasmiṃ vibhaṅge kathitānaṃ lokiyabhāvameva dassento khandhavibhaṅgādīhi visesetīti na aññattha lokuttarānaṃ appamaññānaṃ kathitatā anuññātā hoti.

699. In this case, by saying ‘…it is said in this analysis,’ only the mundane states explained in this section are shown, distinguishing them from the analysis of aggregates, etc. It is not acknowledged that the supramundane immeasurables are explained elsewhere.

Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Section of Questions is finished.

Appamaññāvibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of the Immeasurables is finished.

14. Sikkhāpadavibhaṅgo

14. The Analysis of the Training Rules

1. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Abhidhamma Analysis

703. Patiṭṭhānaṭṭhenāti [M 0.0189][V 0.0190] sampayogavasena upanissayavasena ca okāsabhāvena. Piṭṭhapūvaodanakiṇṇanānāsambhāre pakkhipitvā madditvā katā surā nāma. Madhukādipupphapanasādiphalaucchumuddikādinānāsambhārānaṃ rasā ciraparivāsitā merayaṃ nāma, āsavoti attho.

703. ‘In the sense of being a foundation’ means by way of association, by way of decisive support, and by way of being an opportunity. ‘Surā’ is that which is made by putting various ingredients like flour, cakes, cooked rice, and yeast, and kneading them. ‘Meraya’ is the juice of various ingredients like Madhuka flowers, jackfruit and other fruits, sugarcane, and raisins, fermented for a long time; its meaning is ‘āsava’ (fermented liquor).

704. Taṃsampayuttattāti viratisampayuttattā, viraticetanāsampayuttattā vā.

704. ‘Because of its association with that’ means because of its association with abstinence, or because of its association with the volition of abstinence.

Kammapathā evāti asabbasādhāraṇesu jhānādikoṭṭhāsesu kammapathakoṭṭhāsikā evāti attho. Surāpānampi “surāpānaṃ, bhikkhave, āsevitaṃ…pe… nirayasaṃvattanika”nti (a. ni. 8.40) visuṃ kammapathabhāvena āgatanti vadanti. Evaṃ sati ekādasa kammapathā siyuṃ, tasmāssa yathāvuttesveva kammapathesu upakārakattasabhāgattavasena anupaveso daṭṭhabbo.

‘Indeed the paths of action’ means that they are indeed constituents of the paths of action among the non-universal constituents such as jhāna. They say that even drinking liquor is mentioned separately as a path of action, as it is said: ‘Monks, the habitual drinking of liquor… leads to hell’ (Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.40). If that is so, there would be eleven paths of action. Therefore, its inclusion should be seen as due to its supportive nature and similarity in kind within the aforementioned paths of action.

Sattaitthipurisārammaṇatā tathāgahitasaṅkhārārammaṇatāya daṭṭhabbā. “Pañca sikkhāpadā parittārammaṇā”ti hi vuttaṃ. “Sabbāpi hi etā vītikkamitabbavatthuṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā veracetanāhi eva viramantī”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 704) ca vakkhatīti.

The sevenfold object of women and men should be seen as the object of formations grasped in that way. For it is said: ‘The five training rules have limited objects.’ And it will be said: ‘Indeed, all these abstain precisely by means of the volitions of abstinence, having made the object to be transgressed their object.’

Gorūpasīlako pakatibhaddo. Kākaṇikamattassa atthāyātiādi lobhavasena musākathane vuttaṃ. Dosavasena musākathane ca niṭṭhappatto saṅghabhedo gahito. Dosavasena parassa byasanatthāya musākathane pana tassa tassa guṇavasena appasāvajjamahāsāvajjatā yojetabbā, mandādhimattabyasanicchāvasena [V 0.0191] ca. Nissaggiyathāvaravijjāmayiddhimayā sāhatthikāṇattikesveva pavisantīti dve eva gahitā.

One whose virtue is like that of a cow is naturally good. The statement 'for the sake of a mere kākaṇika,' and so on, is made regarding false speech motivated by greed. And in false speech motivated by hatred, consummated schism in the Saṅgha is included. But in false speech motivated by hatred for the purpose of another's ruin, its blameworthiness—whether minor or major—should be determined according to the qualities of that person, and according to the desire for slight or excessive ruin. The 'nissaggiya' (requiring forfeiture), 'thāvara' (fixed), 'vijjāmaya' (knowledge-based), and 'iddhimaya' (power-based) enter only into those that are 'sāhatthika' (done by oneself) and 'āṇattika' (done by command); thus only these two are taken.

Pañcapi kammapathā evāti cetanāsaṅkhātaṃ pariyāyasīlaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, viratisīlaṃ pana maggakoṭṭhāsikanti. Tesaṃ panāti sesasīlānaṃ.

The five paths of action are indeed so—this is said with reference to the virtue of undertaking, designated as volition. But the virtue of restraint is a constituent of the path. The phrase 'of those' refers to the remaining virtues.

712. “Koṭṭhāsabhāvenā”ti vuttaṃ, “patiṭṭhānabhāvenā”ti pana vattabbaṃ. Ettha pana sikkhāpadavāre pahīnapañcābhabbaṭṭhānassa arahato viramitabbaverassa [M 0.0190] sabbathā abhāvā kiriyesu viratiyo na santīti na uddhaṭā, sekkhānaṃ pana pahīnapañcaverattepi taṃsabhāgatāya verabhūtānaṃ akusalānaṃ veranidānānaṃ lobhādīnañca sabbhāvā viratīnaṃ uppatti na na bhavissati. Akusalasamuṭṭhitāni ca kāyakammādīni tesaṃ kāyaduccaritādīni verāneva, tehi ca tesaṃ viratiyo honteva, yato naphalabhūtassapi uparimaggattayassa aṭṭhaṅgikatā hoti. Sikkhāvāre ca abhāvetabbatāya phaladhammāpi na sikkhitabbā, nāpi sikkhitasikkhassa uppajjamānā kiriyadhammāti na keci abyākatā sikkhāti uddhaṭā.

712. 'By way of a constituent' is said, but 'by way of a foundation' should be said. Here, however, in the section on the training rules, for the Arahant who has abandoned the five impossible conditions, since there is absolutely no hostility from which to abstain, abstentions in actions are not mentioned. But for trainees, even though the five kinds of enmity have been abandoned, because of the similarity to those enmities, and because of the existence of unwholesome states that are enmities and the roots of enmity like greed, the arising of abstentions will certainly occur. And unwholesome bodily actions and so on, such as their bodily misconduct, are indeed enmities for them, and abstentions from these certainly occur for them, because even the three higher paths, which have not become fruition, possess the eight factors. And in the section on training, fruition states are not to be trained in because they are not to be developed, nor are the functional states that arise for one who has completed the training; thus, no indeterminate trainings are mentioned.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation of the Abhidhamma Division is concluded.

2. Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā

2. Elucidation of the Questions

714. Sampattavirativasenāti sampatte paccuppanne ārammaṇe yathāviramitabbato virativasenāti attho.

714. 'By way of restraint on encounter' means by way of restraint according to how one should abstain in regard to a present object that has been encountered.

Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation of the Questions is concluded.

Sikkhāpadavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation of the Analysis of the Training Rules is concluded.

15. Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅgo

15. The Analysis of Analytical Knowledge

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Suttanta Exposition

1. Saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā

1. Elucidation of the Summary Section

718. Eseva [M 0.0191][V 0.0192] nayoti saṅkhepena dassetvā tameva nayaṃ vitthārato dassetuṃ “dhammappabhedassa hī”tiādimāha. Niruttipaṭibhānappabhedā tabbisayānaṃ atthādīnaṃ paccayuppannādibhedehi bhinditvā veditabbā.

718. Having briefly shown, 'This is the method,' he says, 'For the analysis of the Dhamma,' etc., to show that same method in detail. The differentiations of language and ready-wittedness should be understood by analyzing their respective subjects, such as meaning, according to distinctions such as being dependently arisen.

“Yaṃ kiñci paccayasamuppanna”nti etena saccahetudhammapaccayākāravāresu āgatāni dukkhādīni gahitāni. Saccapaccayākāravāresu nibbānaṃ, pariyattivāre bhāsitattho, abhidhammabhājanīye vipāko kiriyañcāti evaṃ pāḷiyaṃ vuttānameva vasena pañca atthā veditabbā, tathā dhammā ca.

'Whatever is dependently arisen'—by this, suffering and other states that appear in the sections on truth, cause, dhamma, condition, and aspect are taken. In the sections on truth, condition, and aspect, Nibbāna is taken; in the section on learning, the meaning of what is spoken; in the Abhidhamma division, resultant and functional consciousness—thus, five meanings should be understood according to what is stated in the Pāli, and likewise the phenomena.

Vidahatīti nibbattakahetuādīnaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ nibbacanaṃ, tadatthaṃ pana vibhāvetumāha “pavatteti ceva pāpeti cā”ti. Tesu purimo attho maggavajjesu daṭṭhabbo. Bhāsitampi hi avabodhanavasena atthaṃ pavattetīti. Maggo pana nibbānaṃ pāpetīti tasmiṃ pacchimo.

'Vidahati' is a common definition for productive causes and so on; but to elucidate its meaning, he says: 'It both initiates and brings about.' Among these, the former meaning should be understood in relation to those excluding the path. For speech, too, initiates meaning by way of understanding. But the path brings about Nibbāna; thus, the latter meaning applies to it.

Dhammaniruttābhilāpeti ettha dhamma-saddo sabhāvavācakoti katvā āha “yā sabhāvaniruttī”ti, aviparītaniruttīti attho. Tassā abhilāpeti tassā niruttiyā avacanabhūtāya paññattiyā abhilāpeti keci vaṇṇayanti. Evaṃ sati paññatti abhilapitabbā[V 0.0193], na vacananti āpajjati, na ca vacanato aññaṃ abhilapitabbaṃ uccāretabbaṃ atthi, athāpi phassādivacanehi bodhetabbaṃ abhilapitabbaṃ siyā, evaṃ sati atthadhammavajjaṃ tehi bodhetabbaṃ na vijjatīti tesaṃ niruttibhāvo āpajjati. “Phassoti ca sabhāvanirutti, phassaṃ phassāti na sabhāvaniruttī”ti dassitovāyamattho, na ca avacanaṃ evaṃpakāraṃ atthi, tasmā vacanabhūtāya eva tassā sabhāvaniruttiyā abhilāpe uccāraṇeti attho daṭṭhabbo.

Regarding 'in the utterance of the natural expression of phenomena' (`dhammaniruttābhilāpe`), here, taking the word 'dhamma' as denoting intrinsic nature, he says, 'that which is the natural expression,' meaning an unperverted expression. Some explain 'in its utterance' (`tassā abhilāpe`) as 'in the utterance of the designation (`paññattiyā`), which is the non-verbal (`avacanabhūtāya`) aspect of that expression (`niruttiyā`).' If this were so, it would follow that the designation is to be uttered, not the word. And yet, there is nothing to be uttered other than the word. Or, if what is to be uttered were that which is to be made known by words like 'contact,' then, since there is nothing to be made known by them apart from meaning and phenomena, it would follow that these are the expressions. The meaning is shown thus: 'Contact' is a natural expression, but 'contact, contact' is not a natural expression. And there is no non-verbal expression of this kind. Therefore, the meaning of `abhilāpe` should be understood as 'utterance' of that very natural expression, which is itself a verbal expression.

Taṃ sabhāvaniruttiṃ saddaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā paccavekkhantassa tasmiṃ sabhāvaniruttābhilāpe pabhedagataṃ ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidāti vuttattā niruttisaddārammaṇāya sotaviññāṇavīthiyā parato manodvāre niruttipaṭisambhidā [M 0.0192] pavattatīti vadanti. “Niruttipaṭisambhidā paccuppannārammaṇā”ti ca vacanaṃ saddaṃ gahetvā pacchā jānanaṃ sandhāya vuttanti. Evaṃ pana aññasmiṃ paccuppannārammaṇe aññaṃ paccuppannārammaṇanti vuttanti āpajjati. Yathā pana dibbasotañāṇaṃ manussāmanussādisaddappabhedanicchayassa paccayabhūtaṃ taṃ taṃ saddavibhāvakaṃ, evaṃ sabhāvāsabhāvaniruttinicchayassa paccayabhūtaṃ paccuppannasabhāvaniruttisaddārammaṇaṃ taṃvibhāvakañāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidāti vuccamāne na pāḷivirodho hoti. Taṃ sabhāvaniruttiṃ saddaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā paccavekkhantassāti ca paccuppannasaddārammaṇaṃ paccavekkhaṇaṃ pavattayantassāti na na sakkā vattuṃ. Tampi hi ñāṇaṃ sabhāvaniruttiṃ vibhāventaṃyeva taṃtaṃsaddapaccavekkhaṇānantaraṃ taṃtaṃpabhedanicchayahetuttā niruttiṃ bhindantaṃ paṭivijjhantameva uppajjatīti ca pabhedagatampi hotīti. Sabhāvaniruttīti māgadhabhāsā adhippetāti tato aññaṃ sakkaṭanāmādisaddaṃ sandhāya “aññaṃ panā”ti āha. Byañjananti nipātapadamāha.

Some say that because it is stated that 'the knowledge that has entered into the distinctions in that utterance of natural expression, for one who reviews that natural expression sound as an object, is the analytical knowledge of language,' therefore the analytical knowledge of language arises at the mind-door after the ear-consciousness process, which has the sound of language as its object. And the statement 'The analytical knowledge of language has a present object' is said with reference to knowing the sound afterward, having grasped it. In this way, however, it would follow that when there is one present object, another is said to be the present object. But just as the divine ear knowledge, which clarifies various sounds, is the condition for discerning the distinctions of sounds made by humans, non-humans, etc., so too, when the knowledge that clarifies that present natural expression sound, being the condition for discerning natural and unnatural expressions, is called 'analytical knowledge of language,' there is no contradiction with the Pāli. And when it is said, 'for one who reviews that natural expression sound as an object,' it can indeed be said that it means 'for one who carries out a review of the present sound as an object.' For that knowledge, too, arises precisely by clarifying the natural expression, immediately after reviewing the respective sound, and because it is the cause for discerning the respective distinctions, it arises by analyzing and penetrating the expression, and thus it also enters into distinctions. 'Natural expression' is intended to mean the Magadha language. Therefore, with reference to other sounds like Sanskrit names, etc., he says: 'But another...' He says 'byañjana' (letter) refers to particles and words.

Kathitaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ. Bodhimaṇḍa-saddo paṭhamābhisambuddhaṭṭhāne eva daṭṭhabbo, na yattha katthaci bodhirukkhassa patiṭṭhitaṭṭhāne. Suvaṇṇasalākanti seṭṭhasalākaṃ, dhammadesanatthaṃ salākaṃ gahetvāti attho, na paṭisambhidāyaṃ ṭhitena pavāritaṃ, tasmā paṭisambhidāto aññeneva pakārena jānitabbato na sakkaṭabhāsājānanaṃ paṭisambhidākiccanti adhippāyo.

This is stated in the commentary. The term 'bodhimaṇḍa' should be understood as referring only to the place of the first complete enlightenment, not to just any place where a bodhi tree is established. 'Suvaṇṇasalāka' means the finest ticket; the meaning is taking up a ticket for the purpose of teaching the Dhamma. It was not refused by one established in analytical knowledge; therefore, since it is to be known in a different way from analytical knowledge, the intention is that knowing the Sanskrit language is not the function of analytical knowledge.

Idaṃ kathitanti māgadhabhāsāya sabhāvaniruttitāñāpanatthaṃ idaṃ idāni vattabbaṃ kathitanti attho. Chaddantavāraṇa (jā. 1.16.97 ādayo) -tittirajātakādīsu (jā. 1.4.73 ādayo) tiracchānesu ca māgadhabhāsā ussannā, na oṭṭakādibhāsā sakkaṭaṃ vā.

'This is said'—the meaning is that this, which is now to be stated, is said for the purpose of making it known that the Magadha language is the natural expression. In the Chaddanta Elephant Jātaka (Jā. 1.16.97 ff.), the Partridge Jātaka (Jā. 1.4.73 ff.), and so on, the Magadha language is prevalent among animals, not the language of camels and so on, or Sanskrit.

Tatthāti [V 0.0194] māgadhasesabhāsāsu. Sesā parivattanti ekantena kālantare aññathā honti vinassanti ca. Māgadhā pana katthaci kadāci parivattantīpi na sabbattha sabbadā sabbathā ca parivattati, kappavināsepi tiṭṭhatiyevāti “ayamevekā na parivattatī”ti āha. Papañcoti cirāyananti attho. Buddhavacanameva cetassa visayo, teneva “nelaṅgo setapacchādo”ti gāthaṃ pucchito citto gahapati “‘kiṃ nu kho etaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā bhāsita’nti? ‘Evaṃ gahapatī’ti. ‘Tena hi, bhante, muhuttaṃ āgametha, yāvassa atthaṃ pekkhāmī’”ti (saṃ. ni. 4.347) āhāti vadanti.

There means: among the Māgadhī and the remaining languages. The others change entirely over time, become different, and perish. But the Māgadhī language, though it may change in some places at some times, does not change everywhere, always, and in every way; even at the destruction of the aeon it still endures. Thus, it was said, 'This one alone does not change.' 'Papañca' means delaying. The word of the Buddha is its very object; for that reason, when the householder Citta was asked about the verse 'Nelaṅgo setapacchādo,' he said, 'Venerable sir, was this spoken by the Blessed One?' 'Yes, householder.' 'In that case, venerable sir, wait a moment while I examine its meaning.' (Saṃ. Ni. 4.347) So they say.

Sabbatthakañāṇanti [M 0.0193] atthādīsu ñāṇaṃ. Tañhi sabbesu tesu tīsu catūsupi vā pavattattā, kusalakiriyabhūtāya paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāya dhammatthabhāvato tīsu eva vā pavattattā “sabbatthakañāṇa”nti vuttaṃ. Imāni ñāṇāni idamatthajotakānīti sātthakānaṃ paccavekkhitabbattā sabbo attho etassātipi sabbatthakaṃ, sabbasmiṃ khittanti vā. Sekkhe pavattā arahattappattiyā visadā hontīti vadanti. Pubbayogo viya pana arahattappatti arahatopi paṭisambhidāvisadatāya paccayo na na hotīti pañcannampi yathāyogaṃ sekkhāsekkhapaṭisambhidāvisadattakāraṇatā yojetabbā.

'Knowledge that is everywhere' means knowledge of meaning and so on. For it is called 'knowledge that is everywhere' because it occurs in all those three or four, or because it occurs in just three, being the state of Dhamma and meaning for the analytical knowledge of ready speech, which is a wholesome action. These knowledges illuminate this meaning; and because they are meaningful and should be reviewed, 'sabbatthaka' also means 'that which has the entire meaning' or 'that which is cast everywhere.' They say that these, when they arise in a trainee, become clear upon the attainment of arahantship. However, just as prior practice is a condition, the attainment of arahantship is also indeed a condition for the clarity of the analytical knowledges of an arahant. Therefore, the causality for the clarity of the analytical knowledges in trainees and non-trainees should be applied to all five as is appropriate.

Pucchāya parato pavattā kathāti katvā aṭṭhakathā “paripucchā”ti vuttā. Paṭipattiṃ pūretabbaṃ maññissantīti paṭipattigarutāya lābhaṃ hīḷentena satasahassagghanakampi kambalaṃ vāsiyā koṭṭetvā paribhaṇḍakaraṇaṃ mayā kataṃ āvajjitvā lābhagaruno pariyattidharā dhammakathikāva bhavituṃ na maññissantīti vuttaṃ hoti. Ettha ca therassa kaṅkhuppattiyā pubbe avisadataṃ dassetvā arahattappattassa pañhavissajjanena arahattappattiyā visadatā dassitā. Tissatthero anantaraṃ vutto tissatthero evāti vadanti.

The commentary is called 'paripucchā' because it is a discussion that proceeds from a question. This is said to mean: Having reflected on how he himself, despising gain out of reverence for the practice, had rendered a blanket worth a hundred thousand into a worthless item by striking it with an adze, thinking, 'They will understand that the practice must be fulfilled,' he concluded: 'Thus, those learned in the scriptures and Dhamma speakers who are reverent of gain will not think of themselves as being merely that.' And here, the elder's previous lack of clarity due to the arising of doubt is shown, and the clarity from his attainment of arahantship is shown by his answering of the question. They say that the Elder Tissa mentioned immediately after is that very same Elder Tissa.

Pabhedo nāma maggehi adhigatānaṃ paṭisambhidānaṃ pabhedagamanaṃ. Adhigamo tehi paṭilābho, tasmā so lokuttaro, pabhedo kāmāvacaro daṭṭhabbo. Na pana tathāti yathā adhigamassa balavapaccayo hoti, na tathā pabhedassāti attho. Idāni pariyattiyādīnaṃ adhigamassa balavapaccayattābhāvaṃ, pubbayogassa ca balavapaccayattaṃ dassento “pariyattisavanaparipucchā hī”tiādimāha. Tattha paṭisambhidā nāma natthīti paṭisambhidādhigamo natthīti adhippāyo. Idāni [V 0.0195] yaṃ vuttaṃ hoti, taṃ dassento “ime panā”tiādimāha. Pubbayogādhigamā hi dvepi visadakāraṇāti “pubbayogo pabhedassa balavapaccayo hotī”ti vuttanti.

'Differentiation' is the process of differentiating the analytical knowledges attained by the paths. Attainment is the acquisition of them; therefore, that is supramundane, while differentiation should be seen as belonging to the sense-sphere. 'But it is not so' means this: just as there is a strong condition for attainment, it is not so for differentiation.
