Although at the moment of the path, serenity and insight are yoked together, just as there are designations like 'emptiness,' so too the designations of serenity and insight may apply to the path due to their mode of approach; thus, it is said, 'It is stated based on their mode of approach.' Or, for one in whom the faculty of wisdom is predominant, the path is insight; for the other, it is serenity. In this way, the meaning should be understood here.

Samādhijāti samādhānaṭṭhova. Tato evāti samādhianuguṇakiriyattāva.

'Born of concentration' means the state of concentration itself. That is so, precisely because it is an action conforming to concentration.

Ādāya ūhitvāti gahetvā viya takketvā vitakketvā. Dvinnanti sammādiṭṭhisammāsaṅkappānaṃ. Purimakālassa viya niddeso yathā “ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā”ti, “ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca tayo mahābhūtā”ti ca.

'Ādāya ūhitvā' means having taken up and considered, as if having grasped, reasoned, and thought. 'Of the two' refers to right view and right intention. The indication is like that for a preceding term, as in 'dependent on one aggregate are three aggregates,' and 'dependent on one great element are three great elements.'

Ogāhitunti ñāṇena paṭivijjhituṃ. Gahetuṃ asakkuṇeyyatāya saṇhattaṃ. Sukhumāya paññāya gahetabbatāya sukhumattaṃ. Itīti iminā kamenāti ayamatthoti adhippāyenāha “itisaddena vijānanakkamaṃ dassetī”ti. Evaṃ pakārehīti evaṃ-saddena jotiyamāno eva attho pakāra-saddena vuccatīti “evaṃ-saddena vijānanakāraṇabhūte naye dassetī”ti vuttaṃ. Itīti vā nidassanattho. Tena vuttappabhede paccāmasanavasena nidasseti. Evaṃ-saddo idamattho. Tena evaṃ pakārehīti idaṃpakārehi, īdisehīti attho.

'To plunge into' means to penetrate with knowledge. It is fineness because of the inability to be grasped. It is subtlety because it must be grasped by subtle wisdom. 'Iti' means 'in this way'; with this intention, he says, 'The word 'iti' shows the sequence of understanding.' 'By such modes' means that the very meaning illuminated by the word 'evaṃ' is expressed by the word 'pakāra' (mode); thus, it is said, 'The word 'evaṃ' shows the principles that are the cause of understanding.' Or, 'iti' has the meaning of indication. By it, he indicates by way of reviewing the distinctions already stated. The word 'evaṃ' has the meaning of 'this.' Therefore, 'evaṃ pakārehi' means 'by these modes,' that is, 'by such as these.'

Uddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the outline is concluded.

1. Dukkhasaccaniddeso

1. The Exposition of the Truth of Suffering

Jātiniddesavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Exposition of Birth

190. “Jātiādiniddese”ti iminā “tatthā”ti padassa atthaṃ vadati. Dukkhamātikāti [V 0.0067] dukkhadukkhādīnaṃ dukkhavisesānaṃ uddeso. Padadvayeti “pariyāyadukkhaṃ, nippariyāyadukkha”nti etasmiṃ padadvaye.

190. With the phrase 'In the exposition of birth, etc.,' he states the meaning of the word 'there.' The outline of suffering is the enumeration of the specific kinds of suffering, such as suffering-as-suffering, etc. 'In the pair of terms' refers to this pair of terms: 'suffering in a figurative sense' and 'suffering in a non-figurative sense.'

Dukkhattāyevāti [M 0.0069] nippariyāyadukkhataṃ vadati. Sabhāvena nāmaṃ visesetīti anvatthasaññataṃ dasseti. Purimena sabhāvadukkhavācakena dukkhasaddena. So hi visesanaṃ avacchedakabhāvato pacchimaṃ saṅkhāradukkhaṭṭhaṃ viseseti. So hi nivattetabbagahetabbasādhāraṇattā avacchinditabbo. Tenāti vipariṇāmaadhiṭṭhānādipakāravisesena.

'Because it is suffering itself' speaks of suffering in the non-figurative sense. 'It specifies the name by its intrinsic nature' shows that it is a designation conforming to the meaning. By the preceding word 'suffering,' which expresses suffering by intrinsic nature, it specifies the latter—which has the characteristic of the suffering of formations—by way of delimiting, since it is a qualifier. For that must be delimited because it is common to what is to be turned away from and what is to be grasped. 'By that' refers to the specific modes such as change, basis, and so on.

Desetabbassa atthassa saṅkhipanaṃ idha saṅkhepo, so ca tabbibhāgānaṃ sādhāraṇabhāvoti āha “saṅkhepo sāmañña”nti. Antokaritvāti antogadhe katvā, saṅgahetvā vā. Ubhayathāpīti saṅkhepatopi vitthāratopi. Sādhāraṇabhāgānaṃ vibhajanaṃ vibhāgo, vitthāroti āha “vitthāro pana viseso”ti. Visesantaranivattakoti vibhāgantarāsaṅgāhako.

Here, the summary is the condensing of the meaning to be expounded, and since that is the common feature of its divisions, he says, 'the summary is the general.' 'Having included' means having made it go within, or having collected. 'In both ways' means both in summary and in detail. The division of the common parts is the analysis, the detail; hence he says, 'but the detail is the particular.' 'That which excludes other particulars' means that which does not include other divisions.

191. Aparatthāti bhummavacanaṃ sāmiatthe yathā “sabbattha pādaka”nti āha “sāmiatthepi hi aparatthasaddo sijjhatī”ti. Siddhi pana “itarāhipi dissatī”ti iminā veditabbā. Yasmā ca evaṃ saddo sambhavati, tasmā pāḷiyaṃ sāmivasena vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ bhummavasena dassitanti dīpento “tesaṃ tesanti vā”tiādimāha. Aparassāti aparassa sattassa. Manussādibhedo upapattibhavo gati, tabbisesabhūtā khattiyādisāmaññādhiṭṭhānā khandhā jātīti dassento “pañcagativasenā”tiādimāha.

191. 'Aparatthā' is a locative expression used in the sense of possession, as in 'sabbattha pādakaṃ'; hence he says, 'for the word aparatthā is also established in the sense of possession.' Its establishment, however, is to be known from the phrase 'it is also seen in other ways.' And because the word is possible in this way, he clarifies that what is stated in the Pāli in the sense of possession is shown in the commentary in a locative sense, saying 'or for them, for them,' and so on. 'For another' means for another being. Showing that birth is the aggregates that have become the basis for the commonality of khattiyas, etc.—which are a particularization of destiny, the existence of rebirth, the distinction among humans, etc.—he says 'in terms of the five destinies,' and so on.

Tiṇākāroti tiṇavikappo, tiṇavisesoti attho. Evanti nidassane. Tena vuttappakāraṃ paṭhamaṃ viññāṇapātubhāvaṃ paccāmasati. Tadupādāyāti tato paṭṭhāya. Ariyabhāvakaraṇattāti ariyabhāvakāraṇattā. Karotīti hi karaṇaṃ. Ariyasadisattā vā ariyasīlaṃ. Puthujjanakalyāṇakānampi hi catupārisuddhisīlaṃ ariyasīlasadisaṃ. Ākāravikārāti uppajjanādiākāravikatiyo. Sahuppādakāti uppādasahitā uppādāvatthā khandhā. Āyatanavasenāti paripuṇṇāparipuṇṇāyatanavasena. Yonivasenāti aṇḍajādiyonivasena. Ekekeneva padenāti yathā dutiyanaye jātiādipadesu dvīhi dvīhi padehi paripuṇṇāparipuṇṇāyatanayonivibhāgena sabbasatte pariyādiyitvā jāti dassitā, na evamidha. Idha [V 0.0068] panetesu ekekeneva padena avibhāgato [M 0.0070] sabbasatte pariyādiyitvā. Ubhayatthāti purimapacchimanayesu bhāvaniddesova yutto. Anabhihite vibhattividhānaṃ, nābhihiteti. Pākaṭā nibbattīti abhibyattā nibbatti.

'Form of grass' means a variety of grass, that is, a specific type of grass. 'Thus' is for illustration. By that, he reviews the first manifestation of consciousness of the kind already stated. 'Taking that as basis' means 'starting from that.' 'Because it makes one noble' means because it is the cause of the noble state. For 'it does' means 'the doing.' Or, it is 'noble virtue' because it is similar to that of the noble ones. For even the fourfold purification virtue of virtuous worldlings is similar to the virtue of the noble ones. 'Changes in appearance' means alterations of appearance such as arising, etc. 'Co-arisen' means the aggregates in the state of arising, together with arising. 'By way of the sense-spheres' means by way of complete or incomplete sense-spheres. 'By way of birth' means by way of egg-born birth, etc. 'By each single term' means that it is not as in the second method, where, with respect to terms such as 'birth,' birth was shown by encompassing all beings through the division of complete and incomplete sense-spheres and wombs, using two terms for each. Here, however, all beings are encompassed without division by each single one of these terms. 'In both places' means that in both the former and latter methods, an exposition of the abstract state is fitting. 'A rule for case endings applies to what is not specified,' not to what is specified. 'Manifest production' means evident production.

Dvinnaṃ dvinnanti ekavokārabhave rūpāyatanadhammāyatanavasena dvinnaṃ, catuvokārabhave manāyatanadhammāyatanavasena dvinnaṃ. Seseti pañcavokārabhave. Pañcannanti cakkhusotamanorūpadhammāyatanavasena pañcannaṃ. Tāni hi rūpabhave pañcavokāre upapattikkhaṇe uppajjanti. Kāmadhātuyaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe uppajjamānānanti yojanā. Vikalāvikalindriyānanti aparipuṇṇaparipuṇṇāyatanānaṃ sattānaṃ. Indriyavaseneva hi āyatanānaṃ vekallaṃ icchitabbaṃ. Tattha vikalindriyassa sattannaṃ navannaṃ dasannaṃ punapi dasannaṃ, itarassa ekādasannaṃ āyatanānaṃ vasena saṅgaho veditabbo. Sattannanti kāyamanorūpagandharasaphoṭṭhabbadhammāyatanavasena sattannaṃ. Gabbhaseyyakañhi sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Navannanti cakkhusotasaddāyatanavajjānaṃ navannaṃ. Andhabadhiravasena hidaṃ vuttaṃ. Dasannanti cakkhusaddavajjānaṃ. Puna dasannanti sotasaddavajjānaṃ. Andhavasena, badhiravasena cetaṃ dvayaṃ vuttaṃ. Ekādasannanti saddavajjānaṃ.

'Of two, of two' means: in the one-constituent existence, two by way of the form base and the mental-object base; in the four-constituent existence, two by way of the mind base and the mental-object base. 'The rest' refers to the five-constituent existence. 'Of five' means five by way of the eye, ear, mind, form, and mental-object bases. For these arise at the moment of arising in the five-constituent existence of the form realm. The connection is to those arising at the moment of rebirth-linking in the desire realm. 'Of those with deficient and non-deficient faculties' refers to beings with incomplete and complete sense bases. For the deficiency of the sense bases should be understood specifically by way of the faculties. Here, for a being with deficient faculties, the grouping should be understood in terms of seven, nine, ten, and again ten bases; for the other, in terms of eleven bases. 'Seven' means seven by way of the body, mind, form, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object bases; this is said with reference to one in the womb. 'Nine' means the nine excluding the eye, ear, and sound bases; this is said with reference to the blind and deaf. 'Ten' means the ten excluding the eye and sound bases. 'Again ten' means the ten excluding the ear and sound bases; this pair is stated with reference to the blind and the deaf respectively. 'Eleven' means the eleven excluding the sound base.

Taṃdukkhabhāvoti pariyāyadukkhabhāvo. Tattha nibbattinivāraṇenāti uppalapadumādīsu uppattipaṭikkhepena abhāvakathanena. Dukkhuppattikāraṇeti dukkhuppattiyā hetubhūte dukkhuppattiṭṭhāne.

'The state of that suffering' means the state of suffering in a figurative sense. There, 'by the prevention of production' means by the statement of absence through the rejection of arising in lotuses and the like. 'The cause of the arising of suffering' means in the place of the arising of suffering which has become the cause for the arising of suffering.

Maraṇaniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of Death

193. Khandhabhedassāti khandhavināsassa. Soti khandhabhedo. Pabandhasamucchedoti pabandhassa accantasamucchedo. Tabbhāvatoti sammutimaraṇabhāvato. Tadekadesabhāvatoti tadavayavabhāvato. Tasseva nāmanti asammohatthaṃ vuttaṃ sabbassāpi ekakammanibbattajīvitindriyappabandhavicchedabhāvato. Sammutimaraṇameva hi jātikkhayamaraṇaṃ, taṃ pana jātikkhayamaraṇaṃ upakkamamaraṇaṃ, sarasamaraṇanti duvidhaṃ. Tattha sarasamaraṇampi āyukkhayamaraṇaṃ, puññakkhayamaraṇanti duvidhaṃ. Evametesaṃ tadekadesatā veditabbā. Yañcettha upakkamamaraṇaṃ, taṃ akālamaraṇaṃ. Sarasamaraṇaṃ kālamaraṇaṃ. Maraṇena sattā yathāladdhaattabhāvena viyujjantīti āha “sampattibhavakkhandhehi viyojetī”ti.

193. By 'khandhabhedassa' is meant the destruction of the aggregates. By 'so' is meant the breaking up of the aggregates. By 'pabandhasamucchedo' is meant the complete cessation of the continuum. By 'tabbhāvato' is meant because it is the state of conventional death. By 'tadekadesabhāvato' is meant because it is the state of being a part of it. By 'tasseva nāmaṃ' is meant that this is said for the sake of dispelling confusion, since it is the state of the cutting off of the entire continuum of the life-faculty produced by a single kamma. For conventional death is indeed death as the destruction of a life-span, and that death as the destruction of a life-span is twofold: death due to an undertaking and death by its own course. Therein, death by its own course is also twofold: death by the exhaustion of the life-span and death by the exhaustion of merit. Thus, their being a part of that should be understood. Herein, death due to an undertaking is untimely death, while death by its own course is timely death. By death, beings are separated from the individual existence they have obtained—thus it is said, 'it separates them from the aggregates of the existence that have been attained.'

Kāraṇatthoti [M 0.0071][V 0.0069] mūlattho. Mūlañhi “ādī”ti vuccati “ko cādi kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ? Sīlañca suvisuddhaṃ, diṭṭhi ca ujukā”tiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 5.369). Tenāha “sandhibandhanacchedamūlakanti attho”ti.

By 'kāraṇattha' is meant the meaning of 'root'. For 'root' is called 'origin,' as in, 'What is the origin of wholesome states? Virtue that is well purified, and a straight view,' and so on (Saṃ. Ni. 5.369). Therefore, he said, 'the meaning is: the root for cutting the joints and bonds.'

Phalakiriyāgabbhā īdisī hetukiriyāti katvā vuttaṃ “antogadhā”ti. Byasanassa hi āpādakehi āpādanaṃ āpādetabbaāpattiyā saheva sijjhatīti.

Because it is a causal action of such a kind that has the action of fruition as its embryo, it is said to be 'included within'. For the bringing about of misfortune by those who bring it about is accomplished simultaneously with the offense that is to be brought about.

Sokaniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of Sorrow.

194. Sukhaṃ hinoti pavattati etenāti sukhakāraṇaṃ hitaṃ. Bhogabyasanādipadatthavisesanti bhogabyasanaṃ, sīlabyasananti evaṃ bhogasīlapadānaṃ vasena atthavisesaṃ. Samāsavisesanti “rogoyeva byasanaṃ, diṭṭhi eva byasana”nti samānādhikaraṇavasena samāsavisesaṃ. Annapānavatthayānādi paribhuñjitabbato bhogoti adhippeto, so ca dhammasamūhabhāvena. Tabbināsāti ñātibhogabyasanāni vuttānīti te vikārabhāvena paññāpetabbattā paṇṇattimattā. Parinipphannaṃ nāma khandhapañcakaṃ. Ataṃsabhāvattā paṇṇatti aparinipphannā, anipphannā ca hotīti vuttaṃ “aparinipphannataṃ sandhāya anipphannānīti āhā”ti. Na hi paṇṇatti kenaci nipphādīyati. Aññatthāpi aparinipphanne anipphannavohāro āgatoti dassetuṃ “aparinipphannataṃyevā”tiādimāha. Kāmañcettha aparinipphannaṃ “anipphanna”nti vuttaṃ, “nipphanna”nti pana na parinipphannameva vuccati, nāpi sabbo sabhāvadhammoti dassento “khandhavibhaṅge cā”tiādimāha. Nipphannatā vuttāti sambandho. Anipphannatā sabhāvadhammattepi kenaci na nipphādīyatīti katvā.

194. It is called 'beneficial' (hita) because it sends forth happiness (sukhaṃ hinoti) and because one proceeds by means of it (pavattati etenā), being a cause of happiness. By 'bhogabyasanādipadatthavisesaṃ' is meant the specific meaning of terms like 'misfortune concerning wealth' (bhogabyasanaṃ) and 'misfortune concerning virtue' (sīlabyasanaṃ), based on the terms 'wealth' and 'virtue'. By 'samāsavisesaṃ' is meant a specific compound, as in 'illness itself is misfortune' (rogoyeva byasanaṃ) and 'wrong view itself is misfortune' (diṭṭhi eva byasanaṃ), a specific compound by way of apposition. By 'bhoga' is meant what is to be enjoyed, such as food, drink, clothing, and vehicles, and this is in the sense of a collection of phenomena. By 'tabbināsā' is meant that misfortunes concerning relatives and wealth are spoken of; they are mere designations because they are to be designated as a state of alteration. What is called 'fully produced' is the five aggregates. Because of its unreal nature, a designation is not fully produced and is unproduced; thus it is said, 'They are called unproduced with reference to not being fully produced.' For a designation is not produced by anyone. To show that even elsewhere the term 'unproduced' is applied to what is not fully produced, he says, 'because of not being fully produced,' and so on. And although here what is not fully produced is called 'unproduced', yet 'produced' is not said only of what is fully produced, nor is every phenomenon with an intrinsic nature produced, as he indicates by the phrase 'and in the analysis of the aggregates,' and so on. The connection is that 'being produced' is stated. 'Being unproduced' is because, even though it is a phenomenon with an intrinsic nature, it is not produced by anyone.

Saṅkucitaṃ cintananti pītisomanassapaṭipakkhato, dosasampayogato ca ārammaṇe anabhiratippavattimāha. Anto attano nissayassa niddahanavasena vā jhānaṃ cintanaṃ antonijjhānaṃ. Satipi anusocanabhāve attano katākatakusalākusalavisayo manovilekhabhūto vippaṭisāro kukkuccaṃ, yathāvuttaantonijjhānaṃ sokoti ubhinnaṃ viseso veditabbo.

By 'contracted thought' he speaks of the occurrence of non-delight in an object, due to its opposition to joy and happiness and its association with aversion. Or, internal burning (antonijjhānaṃ) is contemplation by way of burning within one's own support. Although there is a state of grieving after, remorse (kukkucca) is regret that is a scratching of the mind concerning one's own wholesome and unwholesome deeds, both done and undone; whereas the aforementioned internal burning is sorrow. Thus, the distinction between the two should be understood.

“Manodvārajavanakkhaṇe”ti paribyattamantonijjhānaṃ sandhāyāha, itaraṃ pana pañcadvārajavanesupi [V 0.0070] labbhateva. Tenāha “kāyaviññāṇādī”tiādi. Domanassassāti [M 0.0072] asocanākārassa domanassassa, socanākārassāpi vā nānāvīthikassa. Tampi hi dukkhamevāti. Aññathāti manodvārajavane eva gahite. Tatthāti kāyavatthukamanodvārikesu.

By 'at the moment of mind-door impulsion,' he speaks with reference to well-developed internal burning; but the other is indeed obtainable also in the five-door impulsions. Therefore, he says, 'and in bodily consciousness, etc.' By 'of mental pain' (domanassassa) is meant mental pain in the mode of not sorrowing, or even mental pain in the mode of sorrowing, which has various processes. For that too is suffering. By 'otherwise' is meant if only the mind-door impulsion is taken. By 'there' is meant in those mind-door processes that have the body as their basis.

Paridevaniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of Lamentation.

195. Ādevanasaddaṃ katvāti ādevitvā, vilapitvāti attho. Puggalassa sambhamabhāvoti yassa sattassa uppajjati, tassa anavaṭṭhānabhāvo. Sambhamaṃ vā abbhantaragataṃ tassa paccupaṭṭhāpeti pākaṭabhāvakaraṇenāti sambhamapaccupaṭṭhāno.

195. By 'having made a lamenting sound' is meant having lamented, having wailed. By 'the state of agitation in a person' is meant the state of instability of the being in whom it arises. Or, it makes the internal agitation present by making it manifest—thus, it is the manifestation of agitation.

Muṭṭhīhi pothanādīni muṭṭhipothanādīni.

Striking with fists and so on is 'fist-striking and so on'.

Yena domanassena. Pubbe vuttadukkhatoti “attano khandhaṃ muṭṭhīhi pothetī”tiādinā vuttadukkhato. Taṃnidānanti paridevanidānaṃ.

By that mental pain. By 'from the suffering previously stated' is meant from the suffering stated by such phrases as 'he strikes his own aggregates with his fists,' and so on. By 'having that as its cause' is meant the cause of lamentation.

Dukkhadomanassaniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of Suffering and Mental Pain.

196-7. Kāyadukkhābhibhūtassa patikārābhilāsāya tādisadukkhāvahapayogakālādīsu kāyikadukkhassa tadupanissayatā veditabbā. Etena dukkhenāti anāthatāhatthapādacchedanādidukkhena.

196–197. For one overwhelmed by bodily suffering, due to the desire for a remedy, the state of bodily suffering as a decisive support for that should be understood in relation to such things as the time of applying a treatment that brings such suffering. By 'by this suffering' is meant by suffering such as the cutting off of hands and feet while helpless, and so on.

Upāyāsaniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of Despair.

198. Dukkhaṭṭhānanisajjādīni dukkhaṭṭhānādīni. Domanassassa vatthu hoti upāyāsoti sambandho.

198. Painful positions, sitting, and so on, are 'painful positions and so on'. The connection is: despair is the basis for mental pain.

Appiyasampayoganiddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of Association with the Disagreeable.

199. Aññasāpekkhasaddo [V 0.0071] asamatthasamāsoti taṃ dasseti “yena samāso, na tassāyaṃ paṭisedhako a-kāro”ti.

199. A word that is relative to another is an incapable compound; this he shows by saying, 'The prefix 'a-' is not a negation of that with which it is compounded.'

Pacchimadvayanti “samodhānaṃ missībhāvo”ti idaṃ padadvayaṃ. Tadatthavasenāti samodhānatthassa, missībhāvatthassa ca vasena saṅkhāresu labbhati. Āgatehi ca tehi saṅkhārehi puggalassa saṃyogo hotīti yojanā.

By 'the last two' is meant these two words: 'combination' and 'mixing'. By 'according to their meaning' is meant that by way of the meaning of 'combination' and the meaning of 'mixing', it is found in formations. And the construction is that there is an association for the person with those formations that have come about.

Taṃgahaṇamattanti āpāthagatārammaṇaggahaṇamattaṃ.

By 'the mere grasping of that' is meant the mere grasping of an object that has come into range.

Icchāniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of Desire.

201. Taṃ [M 0.0073] kālanti cuticittanirodhato uddhaṃ kālaṃ. “Yampī”ti yaṃ-saddo karaṇatthe paccattanti yenapīti attho vutto. “Yaṃ iccha”nti yaṃ-saddo yadā icchāpekkho, tadā “na labhatī”ti ettha alābhapadhānābhāvato icchā visesīyatīti āha “alābhavisiṭṭhā icchā vuttā hotī”ti. “Icchaṃ na labhati ya”nti evaṃ kiriyāparāmasanabhūto yaṃ-saddo yadā “na labhatī”ti etaṃ apekkhati, tattha guṇabhūtā icchā, padhānabhūto alābhoti āha “tadā icchāvisiṭṭho alābho vutto hotī”ti.

201. By 'that time' is meant the time after the cessation of the death-consciousness. Regarding 'yampī,' the word 'yaṃ' is in the instrumental case, so the meaning 'by which also' is stated. Regarding 'yaṃ icchaṃ,' when the word 'yaṃ' is relative to 'desire,' then in the phrase 'one does not get,' because non-attainment is not the principal factor, desire is qualified; thus he says, 'desire qualified by non-attainment is spoken of.' Regarding 'icchaṃ na labhati yaṃ,' when the word 'yaṃ,' which refers to the action, is relative to 'one does not get,' then desire is the subordinate factor and non-attainment is the principal factor; thus he says, 'then non-attainment qualified by desire is spoken of.'

Hirottapparahitā chinnikā, dhuttikāti vuccantīti āha “chinnabhinnagaṇenāti nillajjena dhuttagaṇenā”ti. Kappaṭikā sibbitapilotikadhārino.

Devoid of shame and fear of wrongdoing, they are called 'chinnikā' and 'dhuttikā'; thus he says, 'By a "cut-off and broken" group is meant by a shameless, roguish group.' 'Kappaṭikā' are wearers of sewn rags.

Alabbhaneyyaicchanti alabbhaneyyavatthusmiṃ icchaṃ.

By 'desire for the unobtainable' is meant desire for an unobtainable object.

Upādānakkhandhaniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of the Aggregates of Clinging.

202. Tādisassa vatthuno sabbhāvāti sāmaññato anavasesaggahaṇaṃ sandhāyāha.

202. By 'because of the existence of such a basis,' he speaks with reference to a general, all-inclusive grasp.

Atipākaṭena [V 0.0072] ati viya pakāsena dukkhenāti attho.

By 'with very manifest suffering,' the meaning is with suffering that is extremely manifest.

Dukkhasaccaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Truth of Suffering is concluded.

2. Samudayasaccaniddesavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Exposition of the Truth of Origin.

203. Mano viyāti mano-saddassa viya. Ika-saddenāti “ponobhavikā”ti ettha ika-saddena. Gamiyatthattāti ñāpitatthattā. Karaṇasīlatā hi idha sīlattho, so ca ika-saddena vuccatīti kiriyāvācakassa karaṇasaddassa adassanaṃ appayogo. Vuttatthānañhi appayogo. Sati paccayantarasamavāye punabbhavassa dāyikā, tadabhāve adāyikāti vuttāti āha “adāyikāpi punabbhavaṃ deticcevā”ti taṃsabhāvānativattanato. Tenevāha “samānasabhāvattā, tadānubhāvattā cā”ti. Tattha sabhāvo taṇhāyanaṃ. Ānubhāvo [M 0.0074] paccayasamavāye phalanipphādanasamatthatā. Itaresūti avasiṭṭhakilesādīsu. Pavattivipākadāyino kammassa sahāyabhūtā taṇhā “upadhivepakkā”ti adhippetāti āha “upadhimhi yathānibbatte”tiādi. Yathānibbatteti attano paccayehi nibbattappakāre. Nandanaṃ saṃuppilāvanaṃ abhitassanaṃ. Rañjanaṃ vatthassa viya raṅgajātena cittassa vipariṇāmanaṃ, ramāpanaṃ vā. Rāgasambandhenāti rāgapadasambandhena “uppannassā”ti pulliṅgavasena vuttaṃ. Rūpārūpabhavarāgo visuṃ vakkhatīti ettha vakkhati-kiriyāpadaṃ kammatthe veditabbaṃ.

203. ‘Mano viya’ means 'like the word mano.' ‘Ika-saddena’ means by the word 'ika' in 'ponobhavikā.' ‘Gamiyatthattā’ means because the meaning is conveyed. For here, the meaning of ‘sīla’ is the nature of being an instrument, and that is expressed by the word 'ika.' Therefore, there is the non-appearance, the non-application, of an action-indicating word in the instrumental case, for there is non-application for what is already stated. When a combination of other conditions is present, it gives rise to rebirth; when that is absent, it does not give rise to it. Thus, it is said: 'Even though not giving, it still gives rebirth,' because it does not transcend its own nature. Therefore, it is said: 'Because of its similar nature and because of its influence.' Here, its nature is craving. Its influence is its capacity to produce results when a combination of conditions is present. ‘Among the others’ means among the remaining defilements and so on. Craving, which is a helper of kamma that gives a result in the course of existence, is meant by 'upadhivepakkā.' Thus, it is said: 'As it ripens in the substratum,' and so forth. ‘Yathānibbatteti’ means according to the way it is produced by its own conditions. ‘Nandanaṃ’ means exultation and thirsting for. ‘Rañjanaṃ’ means the transforming of the mind, like a dye on cloth, or making it delight. ‘Rāgasambandhena’ means in connection with the word 'rāga,' 'uppannassa' is said in the masculine gender. In the phrase 'Lust for existence in the form and formless realms is separately mentioned,' the verb 'vakkhati' should be understood in the sense of the object.

“Savatthukaṃ cakkhu”nti iminā sakalaṃ cakkhudasakamāha, dutiyena sasambhāracakkhuṃ. Chiddanti kaṇṇassa chiddapadesaṃ. Kaṇṇabaddhanti kaṇṇapāḷi. Vaṇṇasaṇṭhānato rattakambalapaṭalaṃ viya, kiccato mudusiniddhamadhurarasadaṃ maññanti. Sāmaññena gahitāti visayena avisesetvā gahitā. Visayavisiṭṭhāti cakkhādivisayavisiṭṭhā. Ettha uppajjatīti samudāyāvayavehi viya sāmaññavisesehi na nānattavohāro na hoti yathā “rukkho siṃsapā”ti. Na hi sabbo rukkho siṃsapā. Tasmā kiriyābhedasabbhāvato “sayānā bhuñjanti sadhanā”tiādīsu viya “uppajjamānā”ti ettha kiriyāya lakkhaṇatā, itarattha lakkhitabbatā ca vuttā. Yadi uppajjamānā [V 0.0073] hotīti anicchitattā sāsaṅkaṃ uppādakiriyāya atthibhāvamāha. Tena uppāde satīti ayametassa atthoti “uppajjamānā”ti ettha uppādo hetubhāvena vutto, itaro ca tassa phalabhāvenāti āha “so hi tena upayojito viya hotī”ti. Uppajjamānāti vā taṇhāya tattha uppajjanasīlatā uppajjanasabhāvo, uppajjanasamatthatā vā vuttā. Tattheva cassā uppajjanasīlatā sakkāyato aññasmiṃ visaye pavattiyā abhāvato, samatthatā paccayasamavāyena, aññathā asamatthatā, yato kadāci na uppajjati. Nivisamānā nivisatīti etthāpi iminā nayena attho veditabboti.

‘Savatthukaṃ cakkhu’—by this, he refers to the entire eye-decade. By the second, he means the eye with its supporting conditions. ‘Chidda’ means the perforated part of the ear. ‘Kaṇṇabaddha’ means the ear-lobe. In terms of color and shape, it resembles a red woolen cloth, but in function, it is considered soft, smooth, and sweet-tasting. ‘Sāmaññena gahitā’ means taken without distinguishing by object. ‘Visayavisiṭṭhā’ means distinguished by the objects of the eye, and so forth. ‘Ettha uppajjati’—just as with a whole and its parts, there is indeed a differentiation in usage between the general and the specific, as in ‘a tree is a rosewood.’ For not every tree is a rosewood. Therefore, due to the existence of a difference in action, as in such phrases as ‘the sleeping ones eat, the wealthy ones,’ here ‘uppajjamānā’ denotes the characteristic of the action, while the other denotes what is to be characterized. Because ‘if it is arising’ is not intended, he states the existence of the action of arising with doubt. By this, the meaning is ‘when that arising exists.’ Here, in ‘uppajjamānā,’ the arising is spoken of as the cause, and the other as its fruit; hence it is said, ‘for it is employed by that, as it were.’ Or, ‘uppajjamānā’ refers to the nature of craving to arise there, its characteristic of arising, or its capacity to arise. Its very nature of arising there is due to the absence of its occurrence in another object because of the underlying belief in self; its capacity is due to the conjunction of conditions, and otherwise there is incapacity, since it sometimes does not arise. ‘Entering, it enters’—here too, the meaning should be understood in this way.

Samudayasaccaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the exposition of the truth of origin is completed.

3. Nirodhasaccaniddesavaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the Exposition of the Truth of Cessation

204. Taṇhāya [M 0.0075] virajjanaṃ haliddirāgassa viya palujjananti katvā āha “khayagamanavasenā”ti. Vicchinnaṃ nirujjhananti vuttaṃ “appavattigamanavasenā”ti. Cajanaṃ chaḍḍanaṃ, hāpanaṃ vāti āha “anapekkhatāya cajanavasena, hānivasena cā”ti.

204. The fading away of craving is like the perishing of turmeric's color; thus it is said, "by way of going to destruction." That which is cut off is cessation; thus it is said, "by way of going to non-occurrence." Abandonment is rejection or relinquishing; thus it is said, "by way of abandoning without longing, and by way of relinquishing."

Tadappavatti viyāti tassā tittaalābuvalliyā appavatti viya. Appavattihetubhūtampi nibbānaṃ taṇhāya appavatti viya gayhatīti āha “tadappavatti viyā”ti yathā “rāgakkhayo”ti (saṃ. ni. 4.315, 330). Appavattibhūtanti taṇhāya appavattiyā pattaṃ, pattabbanti attho. Nibbānaṃ āgamma niruddhāyapi taṇhāya piyarūpasātarūpesu niruddhāti vattabbatādassanatthaṃ vuttāti yojanā. Ettha ca yasmā maggo, nibbānañca taṇhāya samucchedasādhanaṃ, tasmā “purimā vā upamā”tiādinā upamādvayaṃ ubhayattha yathākkamaṃ yojitaṃ, ubhayaṭṭhāniyaṃ pana ubhayatthāpi labbhateva.

‘Its non-occurrence is like’ means like the non-occurrence of that bitter gourd creeper. Nibbāna, which is the cause of non-occurrence, is also regarded as like the non-occurrence of craving, hence it is said, "Its non-occurrence is like," just as it is said, "the destruction of lust" (Saṃ. Ni. 4.315, 330). ‘Having become non-occurrent’ means attained by the non-occurrence of craving, that is, attainable. The statement is construed to show that even when craving has ceased due to Nibbāna, it can still be said to have ceased in regard to agreeable and pleasurable forms. And here, since the path and Nibbāna are the means for the complete cutting off of craving, therefore, with "the first simile" and so on, the two similes are applied respectively to both cases; however, that which stands for both can be obtained in either case.

Nirodhasaccaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Truth of Cessation is concluded.

4. Maggasaccaniddesavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the Exposition of the Truth of the Path

205. Titthiyehi [V 0.0074] kappitassa maggassa pakatipurisantarañāṇādikassa. Ariyaṃ labhāpetīti ariyaṃ sāmaññaphalaṃ labhāpeti.

205. Of the path fabricated by sectarians, consisting of such things as knowledge of other ordinary persons. ‘He makes them attain the noble’ means he makes them attain the noble fruit of recluseship.

Tabbipakkhaviratisabhāvāti tassā sammāvācāya vipakkhato micchāvācāya viratisabhāvā. Bhedakaramicchāvācā pisuṇavācā, sabbāpi vā micchāvācā visaṃvādanādivasena bhedakarīti āha “bhedakaramicchāvācāpahānenā”ti. Visaṃvādanādikiccatāya hi lūkhānaṃ apariggāhakānaṃ musāvādādīnaṃ paṭipakkhabhūtā siniddhabhāvena pariggāhakasabhāvā sammāvācā tappaccayasubhāsitasampaṭiggāhake jane, sampayuttadhamme ca pariggaṇhantī pavattatīti pariggahalakkhaṇā. Tenāha “jane, sampayutte ca pariggaṇhanakiccavatī”ti. Cīvarakammādiko tādiso payogo. Kātabbaṃ cīvararajanādikaṃ. Niravajjasamuṭṭhāpanakiccavāti niravajjassa kattabbassa, niravajjākārena vā samuṭṭhāpanakiccavā. Sampayuttadhamme ca samuṭṭhāpentoti ettha samuṭṭhāpanaṃ [M 0.0076] micchākammantapaṭipakkhabhūtassa attano kiccassa anuguṇabhāvena sampayuttānaṃ pavattanameva, ukkhipanaṃ vā nesaṃ kāyikakiriyāya bhārukkhipanaṃ viya. Sampayuttadhammānaṃ, ājīvasseva vā visodhanaṃ vodāpanaṃ.

‘Having the nature of abstaining from its opposite’ means that right speech has the nature of abstaining from wrong speech, which is its opposite. ‘Divisive wrong speech’ refers to slanderous speech, or all wrong speech is divisive by way of deception and the like. Hence, it is said, "by abandoning divisive wrong speech." Because it is the opposite of lying and the like, which have the function of deception, are harsh, and are unendearing, right speech—which has an endearing nature due to its gentleness—proceeds by embracing people who accept well-spoken words on account of it, and associated states. Thus, it has the characteristic of embracing. Therefore it is said, "it has the function of embracing people and associated states." Activities such as robe-making are an example of such application. Tasks like dyeing robes should be done. ‘It has the function of initiating what is blameless’ means it has the function of initiating what ought to be done that is blameless, or in a blameless way. ‘And it initiates associated states’—here, ‘initiating’ refers to the proceeding of associated states in conformity with its own function, which is the opposite of wrong action; or it may mean uplifting them, like lifting a burden with bodily action. It is the purification and cleansing of associated states, or of livelihood itself.

Diṭṭhekaṭṭhāti diṭṭhiyā sahajapahānekaṭṭhā, paṭhamamaggasammādiṭṭhivaseneva taṃ veditabbaṃ. “Diṭṭhekaṭṭhaavijjādayo”tipi pāṭho. Etasmiṃ pakkhe catumaggasammādiṭṭhiyā saṅgaho kato hoti. Uparimaggasammādiṭṭhiyā pana diṭṭhiṭṭhāne taṃtaṃmaggavajjho māno gahetabbo. So hi “aha”nti pavattiākārato diṭṭhiṭṭhāniyo. Pakāsetīti kiccapaṭivedhena paṭivijjhati. Teneva hi aṅgenāti teneva sammādiṭṭhisaṅkhātena maggaṅgena. Tathāpavattitena karaṇabhūtena, tena vā kāraṇena. Aṅga-saddo hi kāraṇatthopi hotīti. Tatthāti magge, maggacittuppāde vā.

‘Diṭṭhekaṭṭhā’ means unified with view, unified in simultaneous abandonment. It should be understood by way of the right view of the first path. There is also the reading, ‘Diṭṭhekaṭṭhaavijjādayo.’ In this reading, the right view of the four paths is included. However, regarding the right view of the higher paths, conceit, which is to be destroyed by each respective path, should be taken in the place of view. For from its manner of occurring as "I am," it stands in the place of view. ‘Pakāseti’ means it penetrates by way of penetrating its function. ‘Teneva hi aṅgenā’ means by that very path factor known as right view. By that which has become an instrument by proceeding in such a way, or by that reason. For the word ‘aṅga’ also has the meaning of cause. ‘Tatthā’ means in the path, or in the arising of path-consciousness.

Imassevāti ariyamaggapariyāpannasseva. Yadipi viramitabbato viramantassa cetanāpi labbhateva, viratiyā eva pana tadā padhānabhāvoti āha “viramaṇakāle vā viratiyo”ti. Subhāsitādīti asamphappalāpādi. Ādi-saddena apisuṇādi saṅgahitā. Bhāsanādīti ettha pana kāyasucaritādi. Amaggaṅgattāti amaggasabhāvattā. Tameva cetanāya amaggasabhāvataṃ dassetuṃ “ekassa [V 0.0075] ñāṇassā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha sammāvācādikiccattayaṃ nāma micchāvācādīnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ pāpadhammānaṃ samucchindanaṃ, maggacetanā ca taṃsabhāvā na hotīti na tassā maggakkhaṇe sammāvācādibhāvasiddhi. Taṃsiddhiyanti kiccattayasiddhiyaṃ. Yathā panassā pubbabhāge subhāsitavācādibhāvo, evaṃ maggakkhaṇepi siyā. Evaṃ sante yathā tattha ekassa sammāsaṅkappassa tikiccatā, sammādiṭṭhiādīnañca ekekānaṃ catukiccatā, evaṃ ekā maggacetanā sammāvācādikiccattayassa sādhikā bhaveyya, tathā ca sati magge sammāvācādīni tīṇi aṅgāni na bhaveyyuṃ, chaḷaṅgiko ca ariyamaggo siyāti tayidamāha “ekāya cetanāyā”tiādinā. Yasmā panetaṃ natthi, tasmā maggapaccayatāvacanato ca na cetanāya maggabhāvoti maggakkhaṇe viratiyova sammāvācādayo.

"This very one" refers only to what is included in the Noble Path. Even though the intention to abstain is indeed present when one refrains from what should be refrained from, at that time, the abstinence itself is the primary factor. Hence, it is said, "At the time of abstaining, it is the abstinences." "Good speech, etc." refers to abstaining from idle chatter and the like. The word "etc." includes abstaining from slanderous speech and the like. "Speaking, etc." here, however, refers to bodily good conduct and so on. "Not being a path factor" means not having the nature of a path factor. To show that this very intention lacks the nature of a path factor, it is said, "of one knowledge," etc. Here, the threefold function of right speech, etc., is the eradication of the three unwholesome states of wrong speech, etc. However, the path-intention does not possess that nature; therefore, at the moment of the path, it is not established as right speech, etc. "Their establishment" means the establishment of the threefold function. Just as in the preliminary stage, there is good speech and the like, so too it might be at the moment of the path. If this were the case, then just as a single right thought has a threefold function, and each of right view, etc., has a fourfold function, so too a single path-intention might accomplish the threefold function of right speech, etc. If so, then on the path, right speech, etc., would not be three distinct factors, and the Noble Path would consist of six factors. This is what is said by "By a single intention," etc. But since this is not so, and also from the statement about the path's conditionality, intention does not have the nature of a path factor. Thus, at the moment of the path, it is the abstinences themselves that constitute right speech, etc.

Brūhanaṃ sukhaṃ. Santasukhaṃ upekkhā. Sā hi “upekkhā pana santattā, sukhamicceva bhāsitā”ti (visuddhi. 2.644; vibha. aṭṭha. 232) vuttā. Vitakkādīnanti teyeva abhiniropanādayo pākaṭapariyāyena vuttā.

Growth is happiness. Equanimity is peaceful happiness. For it is said, "Equanimity, being serene, is indeed spoken of as happiness" (Vism. 2.644; Vbh-a. 232). "Of thoughts and so forth" refers to those very things, such as initial application, expressed in a more obvious way.

Vacīsaṅkhārabhāvato [M 0.0077] vacībhedassa upakārako vitakko. “Sāvajjā…pe… upakārako evā”ti iminā vacībhedataṃ samuṭṭhāpakacetanānaṃ viya viratiyāpi visesapaccayo vitakkoti dasseti. Vacībhedaniyāmikā vācāti vacīduccaritaviratimāha. Sā hi sammāvācābhūtā micchāvācāsu saṃyaminī. Tattha yathā visaṃvādanādimicchāvācato avirato micchākammantatopi na viramateva. Yathāha – “ekaṃ dhammaṃ…pe… akāriya”nti (dha. pa. 176). Tathā avisaṃvādanādinā sammāvācāya ṭhito sammākammantampi pūretiyevāti āha “vacībheda…pe… upakārikā”ti. Dhammānaṃ pavattiniṭṭhābhāvato yathā gatīti nibbatti vuccati, evaṃ pavattibhāvato rasalakkhaṇānipīti āha “kiccādisabhāve vā”ti.

Because it is a verbal formation, applied thought is an aid to the differentiation of speech. By this—"Blameworthy... is indeed helpful"—it is shown that applied thought is a specific condition for abstention, just as are the intentions that generate the differentiation of speech. 'Speech that determines the differentiation of speech' refers to abstention from verbal misconduct. For that, being right speech, is what restrains wrong speech. In this regard, just as one who does not abstain from wrong speech such as lying also does not abstain from wrong action—as it is said: "One who has transgressed this one thing... there is no evil he cannot do" (Dhp. 176)—so too, one established in right speech through truthfulness and so on also fulfills right action. Hence it is said, "the differentiation of speech... is helpful." Just as, from the arising and ceasing of phenomena, 'course' (gati) is called 'origination' (nibbatti), so too, from their arising, the characteristics of function, etc., are also so called. Thus it is said: "or in the sense of function, nature, etc."

Abhinandananti taṇhādivasena abhinandanaṃ.

Delighting is delighting by way of craving and so forth.

Vācuggatakaraṇaṃ uggaho, atthaparipucchanaṃ paripucchāti tadubhayaṃ savanādhīnanti āha “savanañāṇe eva avarodhaṃ gacchantī”ti. Ñāṇena paricchinditvā gahaṇaṃ pariggaṇhanaṃ.

The learning of the verbal expression is study; the questioning about the meaning is inquiry. Both are dependent on hearing. Thus, it is said, "They are comprised only in the knowledge of hearing." Grasping after having delineated with knowledge is comprehension.

Tassāti [V 0.0076] payogassa.

"Of that" means of that exertion.

Soti kāmavitakkappavattiyā kāraṇabhūto subhanimitte ayonisomanasikāro. Tassāti kāmavitakkassa. Gataṃ gamanaṃ pavatti, tassa upāyoti gatamaggo.

"That" is unwise attention to an attractive sign, which is the cause for the arising of sensual thoughts. "Of that" means of the sensual thought. "Gone" means going, occurrence; its means is the path of its course.

Pahātabbaekattanti pahātabbatāsāmaññaṃ.

"The oneness of what is to be abandoned" means the general characteristic of what should be abandoned.

Maggabhāvena catubbidhampi ekattenāti sotāpattimaggādivasena catubbidhampi maggabhāvena ekattena sāmaññato gahetvā “assā”ti ekavacanena vuttanti attho. Sabbassa maggassa aññamaññaṃ sadisatā, tathā asadisatā ca ekaccasadisatā ca jhānaṅgavasena sabbasadisasabbāsadisaekaccasadisatā, so eva visesoti yojetabbaṃ. Vipassanāniyāmaṃ dhuraṃ katvā āhāti sambandho. Idha panāti imissā sammohavinodaniyaṃ. Sammasi…pe… nivattanatoti paṭhamattheravādaṃ vadanto tadajjhāsayaṃ purakkhatvā vadatīti adhippāyena vuttaṃ. Itarathā itaravādāpettha dassitā evāti. Pādakajjhānaniyāmanti pādakajjhānaniyāmaṃ dhuraṃ katvā āhāti yojanā. “Vipassanā [M 0.0078]…pe… daṭṭhabbo”ti kasmā vuttaṃ. Na hi tassā idha paṭikkhepatā atthi. Tathā hi vuttaṃ “keci vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanā niyāmetīti vadantī”ti? Nayidamevaṃ. Idhāpīti idha pādakajjhānaniyāmepi vipassanāniyāmo na paṭikkhittoti ayañhettha attho. Tenevāha “sādhāraṇattā”ti. “Idha panā”ti imināpi paṭhamattheravādo saṅgahitoti veditabbo. Yadi evaṃ kasmā vipassanāniyāmo visuṃ gahitoti? Vādattayāvidhuratādassanatthaṃ. Aññe cācariyavādāti sammasitajjhānapuggalajjhāsayavādā.

"By the nature of the path, even the fourfold is one" means that, by way of the stream-entry path and so on, the fourfold path is taken generally as one, and is spoken of in the singular as "of this"; this is the meaning. Of every path there is similarity to each other, and likewise dissimilarity and partial similarity. By way of the absorption factors, there is complete similarity, complete dissimilarity, and partial similarity; that is the distinction that should be connected. The connection is made by taking insight-determination as the guiding principle, he says. "Here, however" means in this Sammohavinodanī. When stating the first Elder's view, "Comprehending... turning away," he speaks placing that inclination foremost; it is said with this intention. Otherwise, other views would have been shown here as well. "Determination through the foundation absorption" is the interpretation for when he speaks taking determination through the foundation absorption as the guiding principle. Why is it said, "Insight... should be seen"? There is no rejection of it here. For it is said: "Some say that insight leading to emergence determines." This is not so. "Here too" means that even here, in the determination by the foundation absorption, the determination by insight is not rejected; this is the meaning here. Therefore he says, "Because of being shared." By "Here, however," the first Elder's view is also included, it should be understood. If so, why is determination by insight taken separately? To show that it is not devoid of the three views. "Other teachers' views" are the views based on the inclination of individuals for whom absorption is to be comprehended.

“Āruppe tikacatukkajjhānaṃ…pe… na lokiya”nti idaṃ theravāde āgataṃ porāṇaṭṭhakathāyaṃ tantiṃ katvā ṭhapitanti aṭṭhasāliniyaṃ saṅgahetvā vuttanti āha “vuttaṃ aṭṭhasāliniyanti adhippāyo”ti. Yesūti pacchimajjhānavajjāni sandhāya vadati. Tattha hi arūpuppattiyaṃ saṃsayo, na itarasmiṃ. “Catukkapañcakajjhāna”nti vutte avisesato sāsavānāsavaṃ apekkhīyati, nivattetabbagahetabbasādhāraṇavacanenettha sāsavato avacchindanatthaṃ “tañca lokuttara”nti vatvā nivattitadhammadassanatthaṃ “na lokiya”nti vuttanti dassento āha “samudāyañca…pe… āhā”ti. Itarathā byabhicārābhāvato “lokuttara”nti visesanaṃ niratthakaṃ [V 0.0077] siyā. Tayo maggāti dutiyamaggādayo. Tajjhānikanti tikacatukkajjhānikaṃ sotāpattiphalādiṃ. Aññajhānikāpīti tikacatukkajjhānato aññajhānikāpi catukkajjhānikāpi maggā uppajjanti. Pi-saddena tajjhānikāpi tikacatukkajjhānikāti attho. Yadi evaṃ catuvokārabhavepi pañcavokārabhave viya maggassa tikacatukkajjhānikabhāve kenassa jhānaṅgādiniyāmoti āha “jhānaṅgādiniyāmikā pubbābhisaṅkhārasamāpattī”ti. Pubbābhisaṅkhārasamāpattīti ca pādakabhūtā attanā atikkantadhammavirāgabhāvena vipassanāya pubbābhisaṅkhārakārī arūpasamāpatti, phalasamāpatti vā. Tenāha “pādaka”nti. Na sammasitabbāti na sammasitabbā samāpatti jhānaṅgādiniyāmikā sammasitabbānaṃ tikacatukkajjhānānaṃ tattha anuppajjanato, itarattha ca visesābhāvato. Phalassapīti catutthapañcamajjhānikaphalassapi.

"In the formless realm, the threefold and fourfold absorption... are not mundane." This, having come down in the Theravāda in the ancient commentary, was established as a textual principle. It is said to have been included in the Aṭṭhasālinī. Thus he says, "The meaning is, 'it is stated in the Aṭṭhasālinī.'" "In which" refers to those excluding the final absorption. For there is doubt about arising in the formless realm in that case, not in the other. When "fourfold and fivefold absorption" is stated, it is regarded without distinction as both with and without taints. To distinguish it here from that with taints by means of a statement common to what should be turned away from and what should be grasped, and to show the state that has been turned away from, it is stated "and that is supramundane," and "not mundane." Showing this, he says, "the aggregate..." etc. Otherwise, because of the absence of deviation, the qualification "supramundane" would be meaningless. "Three paths" means the second path and so on. "Of that absorption" means the fruition of stream-entry, etc., which is of the threefold and fourfold absorption. "Also of other absorptions" means that paths of other absorptions than the threefold and fourfold, and also of the fourfold absorption, arise. By the word "also," the meaning is that those of that absorption, that is, of the threefold and fourfold absorption, also arise. If so, then even in the four-constituent existence, just as in the five-constituent existence, by what is the determination of the absorption factors, etc., for the path that is of the threefold and fourfold absorption? He says, "The determination of the absorption factors, etc., is the prior formative attainment." And "prior formative attainment" is the formless attainment, or fruition attainment, which has become a foundation, making a prior formation for insight by means of dispassion for phenomena transcended by oneself. Therefore, he says, "foundation." "Not to be comprehended" means that the attainment which determines the absorption factors, etc., is not to be comprehended, because the threefold and fourfold absorptions that are to be comprehended do not arise there, and because there is no difference in the other case. "Of the fruition also" means of the fruition that is of the fourth and fifth absorption.

Dukkhañāṇādīnanti dukkhasamudayañāṇānaṃ. Taṃtaṃkusalārammaṇārammaṇattāti kāmāvacarādīsu yena yena kusalena saddhiṃ nekkhammasaṅkappādayo uppajjanti, tassa tassa kusalassa ārammaṇaṃ ārammaṇaṃ etesanti taṃtaṃkusalārammaṇārammaṇā[M 0.0079], tabbhāvato. Taṃtaṃviramitabbādiārammaṇattāti visaṃvādanavatthuādiārammaṇattā. Vītikkamitabbato eva hi viratīti. “Aṅgāna”nti idaṃ “nekkhammasaṅkappādīna”nti etthāpi yojetabbaṃ avayavena vinā samudāyābhāvato. Visesapaccayoti bhinnasīlassa, aparisuddhasīlassa vā sammappadhānāsambhavato samādhānassa viya vāyāmassa sīlaṃ visesapaccayo. Ayañca attho yadipi purimasiddhasīlavasena yutto, sahajātavasenāpi pana labbhatevāti dassento “sampayuttassāpī”ti āha. Sahajameva cettha adhippetanti āha “sampayuttasseva cā”tiādi. Sammoso pamādo, tappaṭipakkho asammoso appamādo, so cittassa ārakkhāti āha “cetaso rakkhitatā”ti.

The knowledge of suffering, etc., means the knowledges of suffering and its origin. Because they have various wholesome objects as their object—meaning that in the sense-sphere realms, etc., thoughts of renunciation and so forth arise in conjunction with whatever wholesome states, and those wholesome states serve as their object—they are called 'having various wholesome objects as their object,' due to that nature. Because they have objects to be refrained from, etc., as their object—meaning they take things like matters of deception as their object. For abstinence is precisely from what is to be transgressed. The phrase 'of the factors' should also be connected here with 'thoughts of renunciation, etc.,' because without the parts, the whole cannot exist. A special condition: because right effort is impossible for one who has broken or impure virtue, virtue is a special condition for effort, just as it is for concentration. And to show that although this meaning is fitting by way of previously established virtue, it is also attainable by way of co-arisen conditions, he said, 'and also for the associated.' To show that what is intended here is precisely the co-arisen, he said, 'and indeed for the associated,' etc. Confusion (sammoso) is negligence (pamādo); its opposite is non-confusion (asammoso), non-negligence (appamādo), which is the protection of the mind; thus he said, 'the guardedness of the mind.'

Sīlakkhandho cāti ca-saddena samādhikkhandho ca. Khantippadhānattā sīlassa adosasādhanatā, nīvaraṇajeṭṭhakassa kāmacchandassa ujuvipaccanīkabhāvato samādhissa alobhasādhanatā daṭṭhabbā. Sāsananti paṭivedhasāsanaṃ, “sāsanabrahmacariya”nti ca vadanti.

By the word 'and' (ca) in 'the aggregate of virtue and,' the aggregate of concentration is also included. Due to the predominance of patience, virtue is to be seen as the means for non-ill-will. Because it is the direct opposite of sensual desire, the chief of the hindrances, concentration is to be seen as the means for non-greed. 'The Teaching' means the teaching of penetration; they also call it 'the holy life of the Teaching.'

Maggasaccaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the exposition of the truth of the path is finished.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Suttanta exposition is finished.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Abhidhamma Exposition

206-214. “Pariññeyyabhāvarahite [V 0.0078] ekantapahātabbe”ti kasmā vuttaṃ, nanu taṇhāyapi cakkhādīnaṃ viya taṇhāvatthutāvacanena pariññeyyatā vuttā. Yathāha “rūpataṇhā loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ, etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisatī”tiādi (dī. ni. 2.400; ma. ni. 1.133; vibha. 203). Tappaṭibaddhasaṃkilesappahānavasena samatikkamitabbatā hi pariññeyyatā. Ekantapahātabbatā ca na taṇhāya eva, atha kho avasesānaṃ saṃkilesadhammānampi. Tathā hi tesaṃ sabbaso accantappahāyikā dassanabhāvanāti? Saccametaṃ, tathāpi yathā “dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pariññeyya”nti (saṃ. ni. 5.1099) taṇhāvajje upādānakkhandhapañcake pariññeyyabhāvo niruḷho, na tathā taṇhāya, taṇhāya pana “yāyaṃ taṇhā ponobhavikā”tiādinā (vibha. 203; dī. ni. 2.400; ma. ni. 1.91, 460; saṃ. ni. 5.1081; mahāva. 14; paṭi. ma. 1.34) samudayabhāvo [M 0.0080] viya sātisayaṃ pahātabbabhāvo niruḷhoti dassetuṃ “pariññeyyabhāvarahite ekantappahātabbe”ti vuttaṃ. Yassa asaṅgahito padeso atthi, so sappadeso, ekadesoti attho. Tatthāti ariyasaccasadde. Samudayoti samudayattho. “Nippadesato samudayaṃ dassetu”nti samudayassevettha gahaṇe kāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ “dukkhanirodhā panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha dukkhanirodhāti dukkhaṃ, nirodho ca. Ariyasaccadesanāyanti ariyasaccadesanāyampi saccadesanāyaṃ viya. Dhammatoti desetabbadhammato nippadesā eva. “Avasesā ca kilesā”tiādinā desanābhedo eva hi tattha viseso. Tenāha “na hi tato añño”tiādi. Apubbo natthīti dhammato apubbo natthīti attho. Tassāti samudayassa. Sabbattha tīsupi vāresūti aṭṭhaṅgikapañcaṅgikasabbasaṅgāhikabhedesu mahāvāresu, tadantogadhesu ca pañcasu koṭṭhāsesu. Apubbassāti “avasesā ca kilesā”tiādinā taṇhāya apubbassa. Avasiṭṭhakilesādīnañhi samudayatāvacanaṃ idha apubbadassanaṃ. Tassa yadipi dutiyatatiyavāresu viseso natthi, pañcasu pana koṭṭhāsesu uparūpari apubbaṃ dassitanti katvā evaṃ vuttaṃ. Tañhi samudayavisesadassanaṃ, itaraṃ pana maggavisesadassanaṃ. Tassa ca dhammato apubbābhāvo dassitoyeva. Yadi evaṃ dutiyādikoṭṭhāsesu, paṭhamakoṭṭhāsepi vā kasmā taṇhā gahitāti āha “apubbasamudayadassanatthāyapi hī”tiādi. Kevalāyāti tadaññakilesādinirapekkhāya. Desanāvasena na vuttoti na dhammavasenāti adhippāyo. Tasmā dukkhādīni tattha ariyasaccadesanāyaṃ [V 0.0079] sappadesāni dassitāni honti pariyāyenāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Abhidhammadesanā pana nippariyāyakathāti katvā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “nippadesato samudayaṃ dassetuṃ”icceva vuttaṃ. Paccayasaṅkhātanti paccayābhimataṃ paccayabhūtaṃ, paccayakoṭṭhāsaṃ vā.

206-214. Why is it said, 'devoid of the nature of what should be fully understood, to be entirely abandoned'? Is it not that craving, too, is to be fully understood, just like the eye and so on, since it is spoken of as a basis for craving? As it is said: 'Craving for forms—forms that are pleasant and delightful in the world—arises here when arising, and settles here when settling' (Dī. Ni. 2.400; Ma. Ni. 1.133; Vibha. 203). For, the nature of what is to be fully understood is that it is to be transcended by way of abandoning the defilements connected with it. And what is to be entirely abandoned is not craving alone, but the remaining defiled states as well. For is not their complete and final abandonment accomplished through seeing and development? This is true. Nevertheless, just as the nature of what is to be fully understood is established for the five aggregates of clinging, excluding craving, with the words, 'the noble truth of suffering is to be fully understood' (Saṃ. Ni. 5.1099), it is not so established for craving. Rather, for craving, its nature as what is to be abandoned is established with emphasis, like its nature as origin, by such phrases as 'this craving which leads to renewed existence' (Vibha. 203; etc.). To show this, it was said, 'devoid of the nature of what should be fully understood, to be entirely abandoned.' That which has an unincluded part is 'with a part,' meaning 'partial.' 'Therein' means in the term 'noble truth.' 'Origin' means the sense of origin. To show the reason for taking up 'origin' here completely, it is said, 'But suffering and cessation...' etc. Therein, 'suffering and cessation' means suffering and cessation. In the teaching of the noble truths, just as in the teaching of the truths, from the perspective of the phenomena to be taught, they are indeed complete. By 'and the remaining defilements,' etc., the distinction here is simply a difference in the teaching. Therefore, it is said, 'For there is none other than that,' etc. 'There is nothing unprecedented' means there is nothing unprecedented from the point of view of the phenomena. 'Of that' means of the origin. 'In all three sections' means in the great sections divided into the eightfold, fivefold, and all-inclusive, and in the five categories included within them. Regarding 'of the unprecedented': this refers to what is unprecedented in relation to craving, by way of 'and the remaining defilements,' etc. For the statement that the remaining defilements, etc., are the origin is what is shown as unprecedented here. Although there is no distinction in this regard in the second and third sections, it was said thus because in the five categories, what is unprecedented is shown successively. For that is the showing of the specifics of origin, while the other is the showing of the specifics of the path. And the absence of anything unprecedented from the point of view of the phenomena has indeed been shown. If so, in the second and following categories, or even in the first category, why is craving taken up? He says: 'For the purpose of showing the unprecedented origin...' etc. 'Of the sole [craving]' means independent of other defilements, etc. 'Not stated by way of teaching' means not by way of the phenomena; this is the intention. Therefore, it should be understood that suffering, etc., are shown there in the teaching of the noble truths as being 'with a part' by way of an indirect method. But since the Abhidhamma teaching is a direct discourse, it is said in the commentary, 'to show the origin completely.' 'Termed a condition' means what is intended as a condition, what has become a condition, or the category of conditions.

Tesanti kusaladhammānaṃ. Paccayānaṃ pahānavasenāti hetunirodhena phalanirodhaṃ dasseti, tappaṭibaddhakilesappahānena vā kusalānaṃ pahānaṃ vuttaṃ. Yathā “dhammāpi vo, bhikkhave, pahātabbā”ti (ma. ni. 1.240). Iti pariyāyato kusalānaṃ pahānaṃ vuttaṃ, na nippariyāyato tadabhāvatoti āha “na hi kusalā pahātabbā”ti. Yathā ca kusaladhammesu, abyākatadhammesupi [M 0.0081] eseva nayo. Nirodhanti asaṅkhatadhātuṃ. Appavattibhāvoti yo nirodhassa nibbānassa taṇhādiappavattihetubhāvo, taṃ pahānanti vuttanti attho.

'Of those' means of wholesome states. 'By way of abandoning conditions' shows the cessation of the fruit through the cessation of the cause; or, the abandoning of wholesome states is spoken of through the abandoning of the defilements connected with them. As it is said, 'Bhikkhus, even dhammas are to be abandoned' (MN 1.240). Thus, the abandoning of wholesome states is spoken of figuratively, not literally, because that is not the case; hence it is said, 'For wholesome states are not to be abandoned.' And this same method applies to indeterminate states as it does to wholesome states. 'Cessation' means the unconditioned element. 'The state of non-occurrence' means that the fact that cessation, Nibbāna, is the cause for the non-occurrence of craving and so on is called 'abandonment'; this is the meaning.

Kāyakammādisuddhiyāti pubbabhāgakāyakammavacīkammaājīvasuddhiyā dūratarūpanissayataṃ ariyamaggassa dassetīti sambandho. Pañcaṅgikaṃ…pe… pavattataṃ dīpeti, na pana ariyamaggassa pañcaṅgikattāti adhippāyo. Ñāpakanidassananti ñāpakabhāvanidassanaṃ, etena “vacanato”ti idaṃ hetuatthe nissakkavacananti dasseti. Vacanatoti vā īdisassa vacanassa sabbhāvato. Paṭipadāya ekadesopi paṭipadā evāti attho. Niddiṭṭho dhammasaṅgāhakehi saṅgāyanavasena.

'By the purification of bodily action, etc.': this is the connection—it shows that the preliminary purification of bodily action, verbal action, and livelihood is a more remote support for the noble path. It indicates that the five-factored... occurs, but the meaning is not that the noble path is five-factored. 'An indicative illustration' means an illustration showing the indicative nature; by this it shows that the word 'by the statement' is a conclusive statement in the sense of a cause. Or, 'by the statement' means because of the existence of such a statement. The meaning is that even a part of the path is indeed the path. It was specified by the compilers of the Dhamma by way of the recitation.

Jhānehi desanāpaveso “lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāvetī”ti (dha. sa. 277) jhānasīsena desanāva. Tathā bhāvanāpaveso. Pāḷigamananti pāḷipavatti pāṭhadesanā. Yathāvijjamānadhammavasenāti tasmiṃ cittuppāde labbhamānavitakkādidhammavasena.

The entry into the exposition by way of the jhānas is the exposition headed by jhāna, as in 'one develops supramundane jhāna' (Dhs. 277). Similarly for the entry into development. 'The course of the Pāli' means the proceeding of the Pāli, the teaching of the text. 'By way of the phenomena as they exist' means by way of the phenomena such as initial application that are found in that mind-moment.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Abhidhamma exposition is finished.

3. Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Questions

215. Tassāti suttantabhājanīyassa. Evaṃ panāti “apicesā sammādiṭṭhi nāma pubbabhāge [V 0.0080] nānākkhaṇā nānārammaṇā”tiādippakārena. Evañca katvāti lokuttaramaggasseva maggasaccabhāvassa adhippetattā. Tenāti tena kāraṇena, ariyamaggasseva uddisitvā niddiṭṭhattāti attho.

215. “Of that” (tassa) means of the Sutta section. “And in this way” (evaṃ pana) means in a manner such as, “Moreover, this right view, in its preliminary stage, has diverse moments and diverse objects,” and so on. “And having done so” (evaṃ ca katvā) means because the Path Truth is intended to refer only to the supramundane path. “Therefore” (tena) means for that reason, because only the Noble Path is designated and specified—such is the meaning.

Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition on the Questioner is concluded.

Saccavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of the Truths is concluded.

5. Indriyavibhaṅgo

5. The Analysis of the Faculties

1. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Abhidhamma Section

219. Cakkhudvārabhāveti [M 0.0082][V 0.0081] cakkhudvārabhāvahetu. Taṃdvārikehīti tasmiṃ dvāre pavattanakehi cittacetasikehi. Te hi “taṃ dvāraṃ pavattiokāsabhūtaṃ etesaṃ atthī”ti taṃdvārikā. Nanu ca tabbatthukehipi taṃ indaṭṭhaṃ kāreti. Tenāha aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “tikkhe tikkhattā, mande ca mandattā”ti? Saccaṃ kāreti, tabbatthukāpi pana idha “taṃdvārikā”icceva vuttā. Apariccattadvārabhāvaṃyeva hi cakkhu nissayaṭṭhena “vatthū”ti vuccati. Atha vā taṃdvārikesu tassa indaṭṭho pākaṭoti “taṃdvārikehī”ti vuttaṃ. Indaṭṭho parehi anuvattanīyatā paramissarabhāvoti dassento “tañhi…pe… anuvattantī”ti āha. Tattha tanti cakkhuṃ. Teti taṃdvārike. Kiriyāniṭṭhānavācī āvī-saddo “vijitāvī”tiādīsu (dī. ni. 1.258; 2.33; 3.199) viyāti āha “pariniṭṭhitakiccajānana”nti.

219. “One develops the eye-door” (cakkhudvārabhāveti) means it is the cause of the state of the eye-door. “Through those pertaining to that door” (taṃdvārikehi) means through the consciousness and mental factors that arise at that door. For they are called “pertaining to that door” because that door serves as the opportunity for their arising. But do not even those based on that (the eye) make that faculty function? Therefore, the commentary says, “Sharply, due to sharpness; dull, due to dullness.” It is true that they make it function, but here, those based on that are simply called “pertaining to that door.” For the eye is called “basis” (vatthu) in the sense of being a support, while not relinquishing its state as a door. Alternatively, it is said “through those pertaining to that door” because the function of the faculty becomes evident through them. Showing that the function of a faculty (indaṭṭha) is the state of being followed by others, the state of supreme lordship, he says, “For that… they follow.” Herein, “that” (taṃ) refers to the eye. “Those” (te) refers to those pertaining to that door. The word āvī, indicating the completion of an action, is like in “vijitāvī” (one who has conquered), etc.; therefore, he says, “knowing the completed task.”

“Cha imāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni cha? Cakkhundriyaṃ…pe… manindriya”nti (saṃ. ni. 5.495-499) evaṃ katthaci chapindriyāni āgatāni, kasmā pana suttante khandhādayo viya indriyāni ekajjhaṃ na vuttāni, abhidhamme ca vuttānīti āha “tattha suttante”tiādi. Nissaraṇūpāyādibhāvatoti ettha lokuttaresu maggapariyāpannāni nissaraṇaṃ, itarāni nissaraṇaphalaṃ, vivaṭṭasannissitena nibbattitāni saddhindriyādīni nissaraṇūpāyo, itaresu kānici pavattibhūtāni, kānici pavattiupāyoti veditabbāni.

“Monks, there are these six faculties. Which six? The eye faculty…the mind faculty” (Saṃ. 5:495–99)—thus, in some places, the six faculties are mentioned. But why are the faculties not mentioned together in the Suttas like the aggregates, etc., while they are mentioned in the Abhidhamma? He says, “There, in the Suttas…” and so on. “Because of being a means of deliverance and so on” (nissaraṇūpāyādibhāvato)—here, among the supramundane, those included in the path are deliverance; the others are the fruit of deliverance. The faculties like faith, etc., brought about by reliance on the unconditioned, are the means of deliverance; among the rest, some should be understood as being the state of occurrence, and some as the means of occurrence.

Khīṇāsavassa bhāvabhūtoti chaḷaṅgupekkhā viya khīṇāsavasseva dhammabhūto.

“Consisting of the state of one whose taints are destroyed” (khīṇāsavassa bhāvabhūto) means being of the nature of a phenomenon belonging to one whose taints are destroyed, like the six-factored equanimity.

Dve [V 0.0082] atthāti indaliṅgaindasiṭṭhaṭṭhā. Attano paccayavasenāti yathāsakaṃ kammādipaccayavasena. Taṃsahitasantāneti itthindriyasahite, purisindriyasahite ca santāne. Aññākārenāti itthiādito aññena ākārena. Anuvattanīyabhāvo itthipurisindriyānaṃ ādhipaccanti yojanā. Imasmiñcattheti ādhipaccatthe.

“Two meanings” (dve atthā) means the meaning of sexual characteristic and the meaning of being designated as a faculty. “By means of their own conditions” (attano paccayavasena) means according to their respective conditions such as kamma. “In a continuum associated with that” (taṃsahitasantāne) means in a continuum associated with the female faculty or with the male faculty. “In another way” (aññākārena) means in a manner different from female, etc. The connection is that the state of being followed is the dominance of the female and male faculties. “In this meaning” (imasmiñca atthe) refers to the meaning of dominance.

Tesanti [M 0.0083] anaññātaññassāmītindriyādīnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ. Yā sukhadukkhindriyānaṃ iṭṭhāniṭṭhākārasambhogarasatā vuttā, sā ārammaṇasabhāveneva veditabbā, na ekaccasomanassindriyādīnaṃ viya parikappavasenāti dassento “ettha cā”tiādimāha.

“Of those” (tesaṃ) refers to the three faculties beginning with the “I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown” faculty. The enjoyment of agreeable and disagreeable forms by the pleasure and pain faculties, as stated, is to be understood as being due to the nature of the object itself, not as based on conception, as in the case of the joy faculty, etc. Showing this, he says, “And here…” and so on.

Yadipi purisindriyānantaraṃ jīvitindriyaṃ rūpakaṇḍepi (dha. sa. 584) desitaṃ, taṃ pana rūpajīvitindriyaṃ, na ca tattha manindriyaṃ vatvā itthipurisindriyāni vuttāni. Idha pana aṭṭhakathāyaṃ indriyānukkamo vutto sabbākārena yamakadesanāya saṃsandatīti dassento āha “so indriyayamakadesanāya sametī”ti. Purimapacchimānaṃ ajjhattikabāhirānanti cakkhādīnaṃ purimānaṃ ajjhattikānaṃ, itthindriyādīnaṃ pacchimānaṃ bāhirānaṃ. Tesaṃ majjhe vuttaṃ ubhayesaṃ upakārakatādīpanatthanti adhippāyo. Tena evampi desanantarānurodhena jīvitindriyassa anukkamaṃ vattuṃ vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Kāmañcettha evaṃ vuttaṃ, parato pana kiccavinicchaye idha pāḷiyaṃ āgataniyāmeneva manindriyānantaraṃ jīvitindriyassa, tadanantarañca itthipurisindriyānaṃ kiccavinicchayaṃ dassessati. Sabbaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ saṅkhāradukkhabhāvena, yathārahaṃ vā dukkhadukkhatādibhāvena. Duvidhattabhāvānupālakassāti rūpārūpavasena duvidhassa attabhāvassa anupālakassa. Rūpārūpavasena duvidhampi hi jīvitindriyaṃ idha gahitaṃ. “Pavattī”ti etena sahajātadhammānaṃ pavattanarasena jīvitindriyena vedayitānaṃ pavattetabbataṃ dīpeti. “Bhāvanāmaggasampayutta”nti iminā phalabhūtaṃ aññindriyaṃ nivatteti. Bhāvanāgahaṇañcettha sakkā avattuṃ. “Bhāvetabbattā”ti vuttattā bhāvanābhāvo pākaṭova. Dassanānantarāti samānajātibhūmikena abyavahitataṃ sandhāyāha, na anantarapaccayaṃ.

Even though the life faculty is taught after the male faculty in the section on material phenomena (Dhs. 584), that refers to the material life faculty, and there the faculties of femininity and masculinity are mentioned without mentioning the mind faculty. Here, however, the commentary explains the sequence of faculties in a way that aligns completely with the exposition of the pairs, showing this by saying, “This sequence fits the teaching of the pairs of faculties.” “The earlier and later faculties—internal and external”—refers to the eye, etc., as the earlier internal ones, and the femininity faculty, etc., as the later external ones. The purpose of mentioning them in the middle is to highlight their supportive role for both—such is the meaning. Thus, he shows that even in this way, it is permissible to present the life faculty in sequence, following the context of another teaching. Although it is stated thus here, later, in the analysis of functions, he will present the analysis of functions for the life faculty after the mind faculty, and after that, for the faculties of femininity and masculinity, according to the order found in the Pāḷi text here. All that suffering is to be understood either as the suffering inherent in formations (saṅkhāradukkha) or, appropriately, as the suffering of painful feeling (dukkha-dukkhatā), etc. “Of the maintainer of the twofold nature” (duvidhattabhāvānupālakassa) means of the maintainer of the twofold existence as material and immaterial. For here, the life faculty is included in both material and immaterial forms. By “continuity” (pavatti), he indicates that the life faculty, by its function of sustaining coexistent phenomena, enables the continuity of what is to be experienced by those phenomena. By “associated with the path of development” (bhāvanāmaggasampayutta), he excludes the faculty of final knowledge, which is a result. Here, the term “development” could also be omitted, since the fact of development is evident from the statement “because it is to be developed” (bhāvetabbattā). “Immediately after seeing” (dassanānantara) refers to being uninterrupted by a faculty of the same class and plane, not to the immediate condition.

Tassāti indriyapaccayabhāvassa. Anaññasādhāraṇattāti aññehi anindriyehi asādhāraṇattā. Evaṃ sāmatthiyato kiccavisesaṃ vavatthapetvā pakaraṇatopi taṃ dasseti “indriyakathāya ca pavattattā”ti. Aññesanti aññesaṃ indriyasabhāvānampi sahajātadhammānaṃ. Yehi [V 0.0083] te indaṭṭhaṃ kārenti, tesaṃ vasavattāpanaṃ natthi, yathā manindriyassa pubbaṅgamasabhāvābhāvato sayañca te aññadatthu manindriyasseva vase vattanti. Tenāha “taṃsampayuttānipi hī”tiādi. Yadi evaṃ kathaṃ tesaṃ indaṭṭhoti? “Sukhanādilakkhaṇe sampayuttānaṃ attākārānuvidhāpanamatta”nti vuttovāyamattho[M 0.0084]. “Cetasikattā”ti iminā sampayuttadhammānaṃ cittassa padhānataṃ dasseti. Tato hi “cetasikā”ti vuccanti. Sabbatthāti vasavattāpanaṃ sahajātadhammānupālananti evaṃ yāva amatābhimukhabhāvapaccayatā ca sampayuttānanti taṃkiccaniddese. “Anuppādane, anupatthambhe ca satī”ti padaṃ āharitvā sambandhitabbaṃ. Na hi padattho sabbhāvaṃ byabhicaratīti janakupatthambhakattābhāvepīti vuttaṃ hoti. Tappaccayānanti itthipurisanimittādipaccayānaṃ kammādīnaṃ. Tappavattane nimittabhāvoti itthinimittādiākārarūpanibbattane kāraṇabhāvo. Svāyaṃ itthindriyādīnaṃ tattha atthibhāvoyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yasmiñhi sati yaṃ hoti, asati ca na hoti, taṃ tassa kāraṇanti. “Nimittabhāvo anuvidhāna”nti iminā anuvidhānasaddassa kammatthataṃ dasseti. Sukhadukkhabhāvappattā viyāti sayaṃ sukhadukkhasabhāvappattā viya, sukhantā dukkhantā ca viyāti attho. Asantassa…pe… majjhattākārānupāpanaṃ aññāṇupekkhanādivasena veditabbaṃ. Samānajātiyanti akusalehi sukhadukkhehi akusalūpekkhāya, abyākatehi abyākatūpekkhāya, kusalasukhato kusalūpekkhāya. Tatthāpi bhūmivibhāgenāyamattho bhinditvā yojetabbo. Taṃ sabbaṃ khandhavibhaṅge vuttaoḷārikasukhumavibhāgena dīpetabbaṃ. Ādisaddenāti “kāmarāgabyāpādādī”ti ettha vuttaādisaddena. Saṃyojanasamucchindanatadupanissayatā eva sandhāya aññātāvindriyassa kiccantarāpasutatā vuttā, tassāpi uddhambhāgiyasaṃyojanapaṭippassaddhippahānakiccatā labbhateva. Abyāpībhāvato vā aññātāvindriyassa paṭippassaddhippahānakiccaṃ na vattabbaṃ, tato aññindriyassāpi taṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ anuddhaṭaṃ. Maggānantarañhi phalaṃ “tāya saddhāya avūpasantāyā”tiādivacanato (dha. sa. aṭṭha. 505) kilesānaṃ paṭippassambhanavasena pavattati, na itaraṃ. Aññathā ariyā sabbakālaṃ appaṭippassaddhakilesadarathā siyuṃ. Itarassa pana nicchandarāgesu sattavohāro viya ruḷhivasena paṭippassaddhikiccatā veditabbā.

'Of that' means of the state of being a condition as a faculty. 'Because it is not common to others' means because it is unshared with other non-faculties. Thus, having established the specific function based on capability, it is also shown through the context: 'because it proceeds in the discussion of faculties.' 'Of others' refers to other co-arisen phenomena that are also of the nature of faculties. Those by which they perform the function of a lord—there is no mastery over them, just as for the mind faculty, due to the absence of a preceding nature, and they themselves, on the other hand, operate under the control of the mind faculty alone. Therefore, it is said: 'For even those associated with it,' etc. If so, how is their lordly function performed? The meaning is as stated: 'Merely the causing of conformity to their own characteristic in associated states having the characteristic of pleasure, etc.' 'Because they are mental factors'—this shows the predominance of consciousness over its associated phenomena. For this reason, they are called 'cetasikas.' 'In all respects'—mastery, the sustaining of co-arisen phenomena, and so on, up to being a condition for facing the deathless for associated states—this is explained in the discussion of their functions. The phrase 'when there is non-arising and non-support' should be brought in and connected. For the meaning of a word does not deviate from its actual nature; thus, it is said, 'even in the absence of being a generator or supporter.' 'Of those conditions' refers to conditions such as the signs of men and women, kamma, etc. 'In its manifestation, the state of being a sign' means the causal role in the production of forms like the sign of a woman, etc. This should be seen as merely the existence of the female faculty, etc., in that context. For when something exists, a thing arises, and when it does not exist, that thing does not arise—that is its cause. 'The state of being a sign is conformity'—this shows the passive sense of the word 'conformity.' 'Like attaining the state of pleasure and pain' means as if they themselves attain the nature of pleasure and pain, like having pleasure as an end and pain as an end. The absence... should be understood as the application of a neutral characteristic by way of ignorance, equanimity, etc. 'Of the same kind' refers to unwholesome pleasure and pain with unwholesome equanimity, of indeterminate states with indeterminate equanimity, of wholesome pleasure with wholesome equanimity. Here, too, the meaning should be divided according to the classification of planes and then connected. All of this should be explained by means of the division into coarse and subtle stated in the Analysis of the Aggregates. 'With the word "etc."' refers to the word "etc." stated here in 'sensual desire, ill will, etc.' The preoccupation with another function of the faculty of final knowledge is stated with reference to the cutting off of fetters and its supporting condition. Even for it, the function of calming and abandoning the higher fetters is certainly obtained. Alternatively, because of its non-pervading nature, the function of calming and abandoning should not be stated for the faculty of final knowledge; therefore, in the commentary, that is not cited for the faculty of knowledge either. For the fruit immediately following the path proceeds by way of calming the defilements, as stated in the phrase 'with that faith not being calmed,' etc., not otherwise. Otherwise, noble ones would at all times have the distress of uncalmed defilements. But for the other faculty, its function of calming should be understood by way of convention, like the conventional designation of 'a being' in those in whom desire and lust have ceased.

Etthāha – kasmā pana ettakāneva indriyāni vuttāni, etāni eva ca vuttānīti? Ādhipaccatthasambhavatoti ce. Ādhipaccaṃ nāma issariyanti vuttametaṃ. Tayidaṃ ādhipaccaṃ attano kicce balavanti aññesampi sabhāvadhammānaṃ labbhateva. Paccayādhīnavuttikā [V 0.0084] hi paccayuppannā[M 0.0085]. Tasmā te tehi anuvattīyanti, te ca te anuvattantīti? Saccametaṃ, tathāpi atthi tesaṃ viseso. Svāyaṃ viseso “cakkhuviññāṇādippavattiyañhi cakkhādīnaṃ siddhamādhipacca”ntiādinā (vibha. aṭṭha. 219) aṭṭhakathāyaṃ dassitoyeva.

Here it is said: But why are only this many faculties mentioned, and why these very ones? If it is because of the possibility of the meaning of dominance. Dominance means lordship, as has been said. This dominance is indeed attainable even by other phenomena having their own nature that are powerful in their own function. For conditionally arisen phenomena have their occurrence dependent on conditions. Therefore, are they not conformed to by them, and do they not conform to them? This is true, yet there is a distinction among them. This distinction is indeed shown in the commentary, thus: 'For in the occurrence of eye-consciousness, etc., the dominance of the eye, etc., is established,' and so on (Vibh. Aṭṭha. 219).

Apica khandhapañcake yāyaṃ sattapaññatti, tassā visesanissayo cha ajjhattikāni āyatanānīti tāni tāva ādhipaccatthaṃ upādāya “cakkhundriyaṃ…pe… manindriya”ntiādito vuttāni. Tāni pana yena dhammena pavattanti, ayaṃ so dhammo tesaṃ ṭhitihetūti dassanatthaṃ jīvitaṃ. Tayime indriyapaṭibaddhā dhammā imesaṃ vasena “itthī, puriso”ti voharīyantīti dassanatthaṃ bhāvadvayaṃ. Svāyaṃ sattasaññito dhammapuñjo pabandhavasena pavattamāno imāhi vedanāhi saṃkilissatīti dassanatthaṃ vedanāpañcakaṃ. Tato visuddhatthikānaṃ vodānasambhāradassanatthaṃ saddhādipañcakaṃ. Tato vodānasambhārā imehi visujjhanti, visuddhippattā, niṭṭhitakiccā ca hontīti dassanatthaṃ ante anaññātaññassāmītindriyādīni tīṇi vuttāni. Sabbattha “ādhipaccatthaṃ upādāyā”ti padaṃ yojetabbaṃ. Ettāvatā adhippetatthasiddhīti aññesaṃ aggahaṇaṃ.

Furthermore, in the five aggregates, that which is the designation 'a being,' its specific basis is the six internal sense bases; thus, these are first mentioned with reference to the meaning of dominance, beginning with 'the eye faculty... up to the mind faculty.' But that phenomenon by which they proceed, that very phenomenon is the cause of their stability; to show this, the life faculty is mentioned. These phenomena connected with the faculties are those by means of which one designates 'woman' or 'man'; to show this, the two genders are mentioned. This heap of phenomena designated as 'a being,' proceeding by way of continuity, is defiled by these feelings; to show this, the fivefold feeling is mentioned. Then, to show the requisites for purification for those who seek purity, the fivefold group beginning with faith is mentioned.
