Then, to show that by these requisites for purification they are purified, attain purity, and have their task accomplished, at the end the three faculties beginning with the faculty of 'I shall know the unknown' are mentioned. In all cases, the phrase 'with reference to the meaning of dominance' should be applied. To this extent, the intended meaning is accomplished, which explains the non-inclusion of others.

Atha vā pavattinivattīnaṃ nissayādidassanatthampi etāni eva vuttāni. Pavattiyā hi visesato mūlanissayabhūtāni cha ajjhattikāni āyatanāni. Yathāha “chasu loko samuppanno”tiādi (su. ni. 171). Tassā uppatti itthipurisindriyehi. Visabhāgavatthusarāganimittā hi yebhuyyena sattakāyassa abhinibbatti. Vuttañhetaṃ “tiṇṇaṃ kho pana, mahārāja, sannipātā gabbhassāvakkanti hoti, idha mātāpitaro ca sannipatitā honti, mātā ca utunī hoti, gabbho ca paccupaṭṭhito hotī”ti (ma. ni. 1.408; 2.411; mi. pa. 4.1.6). Avaṭṭhānaṃ jīvitindriyena tena anupāletabbato. Tenāha “āyu ṭhiti yapanā yāpanā”tiādi. Upabhogo vedanāhi[M 0.0086]. Vedanāvasena hi iṭṭhādisabbavisayupabhogo. Yathāha – “vedayati vedayatīti kho, bhikkhave, tasmā vedanāti vuccatī”ti (saṃ. ni. 3.79). Evaṃ pavattiyā nissayasamuppādaṭṭhitisambhogadassanatthaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ yāva upekkhindriyanti cuddasindriyāni desitāni. Yathā cetāni pavattiyā, evaṃ itarāni nivattiyā. Vivaṭṭasannissitena hi nibbattitāni [V 0.0085] saddhādīni pañca indriyāni nivattiyā nissayo. Uppādo anaññātaññassāmītindriyena tassa paṭhamaṃ uppajjanato. Avaṭṭhānaṃ aññindriyena. Upabhogo aññātāvindriyena aggaphalasamupabhogato. Evampi etāni eva indriyāni desitāni. Ettāvatā yathādhippetatthasiddhito aññesaṃ aggahaṇaṃ. Etenāpi nesaṃ desanānukkamopi saṃvaṇṇito veditabbo.

Alternatively, these are also stated to show the dependence and so on of proceeding and ceasing. For proceeding, the six internal sense bases are particularly the root dependence. As it is said: 'The world arises in six,' and so on (Su. Ni. 171). Its production is through the male and female faculties. For the manifestation of beings mostly occurs through the signs of lust for objects of a different kind. As it is stated: 'Great king, conception in the womb occurs through the union of three things: here, the mother and father come together, the mother is fertile, and the being to be reborn is present' (Ma. Ni. 1.408; 2.411; Mi. Pa. 4.1.6). The establishment is through the life faculty, since it must be maintained by that. Hence it is said: 'Life, stability, maintenance, sustenance,' and so on. The enjoyment is through feelings. For through feelings, there is the enjoyment of all desirable and other objects. As it is said: 'It feels, it feels—therefore, monks, it is called feeling' (Saṃ. Ni. 3.79). Thus, to show the dependence, arising, stability, and enjoyment of the process, the fourteen faculties—from the eye faculty up to the equanimity faculty—are taught. Just as these are for proceeding, so too are the others for ceasing. For the five faculties beginning with faith, which rely on detachment, are the dependence for ceasing. The arising is through the faculty of 'I shall know the unknown,' since it arises first in that. The establishment is through the faculty of knowledge. The enjoyment is through the faculty of one who has final knowledge, as it is the enjoyment of the highest fruit. In this way too, these faculties are taught. To this extent, the intended meaning is accomplished, which explains the non-inclusion of others. By this, their order of teaching should also be understood as well explained.

220. Kusalākusalavīriyādīnīti ettha ādi-saddena kusalasamādhiādīnaṃ, abyākatavīriyādīnañca saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo. Paccayādīti ādi-saddena desārammaṇādayo gahitā, yathāvuttavīriyādīni, cakkhādīni ca saṅgaṇhāti. Iccevaṃ sabbasaṅgāhikāni vīriyindriyādipadāni, cakkhundriyādipadāni ca. Tenāti “evaṃ santepī”tiādinā bhūmivibhāgakathanena. Tannivattanenāti sabbesaṃ sabbabhūmikattanivattanena. Avijjamānasaṅgāhakattanti tassaṃ tassaṃ bhūmiyaṃ anupalabbhamānassa indriyassa saṅgāhakatā.

220. "Wholesome, unwholesome, energy, etc."—here, by the word "etc.," the inclusion of wholesome concentration, etc., and indeterminate energy, etc., should be understood. "Conditions, etc."—by the word "etc.," location, object, etc., as well as the aforementioned energy, etc., and the eye, etc., are included. Thus, the terms energy faculty, etc., and eye faculty, etc., are all-inclusive. "Therefore"—by the explanation of the division of planes beginning with "even when it is so." "By their non-occurrence"—by the non-occurrence of all (faculties) in all planes. "The inclusion of a non-existent (faculty)"—means the inclusion of a faculty that is not found in a particular plane.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Abhidhamma division is concluded.

2. Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā

2. The Elucidation of the Interrogation

Idha imasmiṃ “sattindriyā anārammaṇā”ti evaṃ ekantānārammaṇatte vuccamāne na ābhaṭṭhaṃ jīvitindriyaṃ na bhāsitaṃ. Ṭīkāyaṃ pana anābhaṭṭhanti katasamāsaṃ katvā vuttaṃ. Rūpadhammesu saṅgahitatanti “rūpa”nti gaṇitataṃ. Arūpakoṭṭhāsena arūpabhāvena siyāpakkhe saṅgahitaṃ. Kasmā? Tassa [M 0.0087] parittārammaṇāditā atthīti. Yasmā pana rūpārūpamissakasseva vasena siyāpakkhasaṅgaho yutto, na ekadesassa, tasmā ekadesassa taṃ anicchanto āha “adhippāyo”ti. Idāni tamatthaṃ pakāsetuṃ “arūpakoṭṭhāsena panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Navattabbatāti parittārammaṇādibhāvena navattabbatā. Kathaṃ pana rūpakoṭṭhāsenassānārammaṇassa navattabbatāti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “na hi anārammaṇa”ntiādi. “Avijjamānārammaṇānārammaṇesū”ti iminā “anārammaṇā”ti bāhiratthasamāso ayanti dasseti[V 0.0086]. Navattabbesūti sārammaṇabhāvena navattabbesu. Anārammaṇattāti ārammaṇarahitattā. “Navindriyā siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā, siyā na vattabbā ‘parittārammaṇā’tipi ‘mahaggatārammaṇā’tipi ‘appamāṇārammaṇā’tipī”tiādīsu (vibha. 223) viya na sārammaṇasseva navattabbataṃ dasseti. Yathā ca na sārammaṇasseva navattabbatāpariyāyo, atha kho anārammaṇassāpīti sārammaṇe niyamābhāvo. Evaṃ navattabbaṃ sārammaṇamevāti ayampi niyamo natthīti dassento “navattabbassa vā sārammaṇata”nti āha. Tassa na dassetīti sambandho. “Na hī”tiādinā tamevatthaṃ vivarati.

Here, in this context, when it is said, "the seven faculties are objectless," the life faculty is neither brought up nor spoken of. However, in the sub-commentary, it is stated as "not brought up" by forming a compound. "Included among material phenomena"—here, "material" refers to what is counted. It may be included in the category of the immaterial due to its immaterial nature as a possible alternative. Why? Because it has the characteristic of having a limited object, etc. But since inclusion in the 'may be' category is appropriate only on the basis of a mixture of material and immaterial, not for just one part, therefore, not desiring that for one part alone, he states "the intention." Now, to clarify that meaning, it is stated, "but regarding the immaterial category," etc. The unstateability (navattabbatā) is the unstateability in terms of having a limited object, etc. But how can the unstateability of the objectless aspect of the material category be? Addressing this objection, he says, "for it is not objectless," etc. By this phrase, "among those with non-existent objects and the objectless," it shows that "objectless" is an external-attribute compound. "Among what cannot be said"—because they cannot be said to have an object. Due to being objectless—because of being devoid of an object. "Nine faculties may have a limited object, may have a great object, may have an immeasurable object, or it cannot be said whether they have a limited object, a great object, or an immeasurable object," etc. (Vibh. 223)—this does not indicate that only what has an object is unstateable. Just as it is not only what has an object that is unstateable, but the objectless also is unstateable—thus, there is no fixed rule that they must have an object. To show that there is no such fixed rule, he says, "or the state of having an object for what is unstateable." The connection is that this is not indicated. "For it is not," etc.—this explains that very point.

Tattha rūpanibbānānaṃ sukhādisampayuttabhāvena navattabbatā, na parittārammaṇādibhāvenāti codanaṃ manasi katvā āha “athāpī”tiādi. Tattha athāpi vattatīti sambandho. Siyā anārammaṇantipi vattabbaṃ siyāti anārammaṇaṃ dhammāyatanaṃ sārammaṇehi visuṃ katvā evaṃ vattabbaṃ siyā. Navattabba-saddo yadi sārammaṇesveva vatteyya, na cevaṃ vuttaṃ, avacane ca aññaṃ kāraṇaṃ natthīti dassento āha “na hi pañhapucchake sāvasesā desanā atthī”ti. Tasmā navattabba-saddo anārammaṇesupi vattatevāti adhippāyo. Yāpi “aṭṭhindriyā siyā ajjhattārammaṇā”ti ajjhattārammaṇādibhāvena navattabbatā vuttā, sā jīvitindriyassa ākiñcaññāyatanakāle paṭhamāruppaviññāṇābhāvamattārammaṇataṃ sandhāya vuttā, na sārammaṇasseva navattabbatādassanatthaṃ, nāpi anārammaṇassa parittārammaṇādibhāvena navattabbatābhāvadassanatthanti dassento [M 0.0088] “aṭṭhindriyā siyā ajjhattārammaṇāti ettha cā”tiādimāha. Tattha siyā ajjhattārammaṇātīti iti-saddo ādiattho. Tena avasiṭṭhapāḷisaṅgaṇhanena “siyā na vattabbā ‘ajjhattārammaṇā’tipi ‘bahiddhārammaṇā’tipi ‘ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā’tipī”ti imāya pāḷiyā vuttamatthaṃ jīvitindriyassa dassento “jīvitindriyassa…pe… navattabbatā veditabbā”ti āha, taṃ vuttatthameva.

Here, considering the objection that the unstateability of form and Nibbāna is in terms of being associated with happiness, etc., not in terms of having limited objects, etc., he says, "athāpi" and so on. Here, the connection is "athāpi" means "it is also said." It might be said, "It could also be without an object," meaning the objectless mind-object base (dhammāyatana), having been distinguished from those with objects, could be stated thus. If the term "not to be spoken of" were applied only to those with objects, it would not be so stated, and to show that there is no other reason for not mentioning it, it is said, "For in the Interrogation section, the teaching is not left incomplete." Therefore, the term "not to be spoken of" applies even to those without objects—this is the intended meaning. The statement, "The eight faculties might have internal objects," which refers to the unstateability in terms of having internal objects, etc., refers to the life faculty (jīvitindriya) at the time of the base of nothingness (ākiñcaññāyatana), where it has only the mere absence of the first immaterial consciousness as its object. This is not meant to show that only those with objects are unstateable, nor to show the absence of unstateability in terms of having limited objects, etc., for those without objects. To clarify this, it is said, "Therein, in 'may have an internal object,' the word 'iti' has the meaning of 'and so forth'." By this, with the remaining text taken together: "It might not be said, 'having internal objects,' or 'having external objects,' or 'having internal and external objects.'" The meaning conveyed by this passage illustrates the life faculty, stating, "The life faculty... should be understood as unstateable." That is the meaning already stated.

Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation of the Interrogation is concluded.

Indriyavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation of the Analysis of the Faculties is concluded.

6. Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅgo

6. Analysis of Dependent Arising

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Section on Discourses

Uddesavāravaṇṇanā

The Elucidation of the Summary Section

225. “Vuttattā”ti [M 0.0089][V 0.0087] idaṃ nissakkaṃ kiṃ lakkhaṇaṃ? Hetulakkhaṇaṃ. Yadi evaṃ taṃhetuko vibhajjavādibhāvo āpajjati. Na hi moggaliputtatissattherena vuttattā buddhasāvakā vibhajjavādino ahesunti? Nayidamevaṃ. Tividho hi hetu ñāpako, kārako, sampāpakoti. Tesu ñāpakahetu idhādhippeto, tasmā tena mahātherena “kiṃ vādī, bhante, sammāsambuddho”ti puṭṭhena “vibhajjavādī, mahārājā”ti tadā vuttavacanena ñāyati “sammāsambuddhasāvakā vibhajjavādino”ti imamatthaṃ dasseti kiṃ…pe… vuttattā…pe… vibhajjavādino”ti. “Ahañhi, brāhmaṇa, vinayāya dhammaṃ desemi rāgassā”tiādiṃ vatvā “no ca kho yaṃ tvaṃ sandhāya vadesī”tiādinā (pārā. 5-9) verañjabrāhmaṇassa bhagavatā venayikādibhāvo vibhajja vuttoti taṃ anuvadantā sāvakāpi tathā vadantīti āha “te hi venayikādibhāvaṃ vibhajja vadantī”ti. Cīvarādīnanti ādi-saddena somanassādīnaṃ saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo. Tānipi hi sevitabbāsevitabbabhāvena vibhajja vuttāni. Vibhajjavādiparisā vibhajjavādimaṇḍalanti etasmiṃ atthe yathā taṃ otiṇṇo nāma hoti, taṃdassanatthaṃ “ācariye anabbhācikkhantenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Sakasamayāvokkamādi hi paramatthato tadotāro. “Asaṃkiliṭṭhāpi avijjā atthi amaggavajjhā, yāya nivutā khīṇāsavāpi nāmagottādīsu ekaccaṃ na jānanti, sā kusalacittuppādesupi pavattatī”ti nikāyantariyā. Taṃ sandhāyāha “avijjā puññāneñjābhisaṅkhārānaṃ hetupaccayo hotītiādiṃ vadanto”ti. Upalakkhaṇañhetaṃ sahajātakoṭiyā. Ādi-saddena [V 0.0088] akusalacittenapi ñāṇaṃ uppajjati, yā saṃkiliṭṭhā paññāti, acetasikaṃ sīlaṃ, aviññattisaṅkhātaṃ rūpabhāvaṃ dussilyanti evamādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Parasamayāyūhanaṃ parasamaye byāpārāpattiyā. Yo tattha sakasamayena viruddho attho, tassa vā dīpanena siyā, parasamaye vādāropanena vā[M 0.0090]. Tesu purimaṃ “ācariye anabbhācikkhantenā”ti iminā apanītanti itaraṃ dasseti “parasamayaṃ…pe… anāyūhantenā”ti. Asampiṇḍentenāti upacayatthaṃ sandhāya vadanti. Āyūhana-saddo pana upacayattho na hotīti kecivādo na sārato gahetabbo.

225. “Because it was said”—what is the characteristic of this independent expression? It is the characteristic of a cause. If so, then that would lead to the position of being an advocate of analysis due to that cause. But did the Buddha's disciples not become advocates of analysis because the Elder Moggaliputtatissa said so? It is not so. For a cause is threefold: informative, causative, and fulfilling. Of these, the informative cause is intended here. Therefore, by the statement of the great elder when asked, “What doctrine does the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One advocate, venerable sir?” and replying, “He advocates analysis, great king,” it indicates and demonstrates this meaning: “the disciples of the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One are advocates of analysis”...because it was said...advocates of analysis. “Indeed, brahmin, I teach the Dhamma for the elimination of lust,” etc., and after saying “But not in the sense that you imply,” etc. (Pārājika 5-9), the Blessed One spoke analytically to the brahmin of Verañja about the nature of training, etc. Therefore, his disciples, echoing that, also say, “They speak analytically about the nature of training, etc.” By “Robes and so on”—with the word “and so on,” inclusion of joy and the like should be understood. For these too are spoken of analytically as to what should be cultivated and what should not. “The assembly of advocates of analysis, the circle of advocates of analysis”—in this meaning, as one is said to have entered it, to show that, “without misrepresenting the teacher,” etc. is said. For, in the ultimate sense, entering into one's own tenet, etc., is indeed a descent into that. “Even uncorrupted ignorance exists, not abandoned by the path, by which even arahants, though their taints are destroyed, do not know certain things regarding name and clan, etc., it occurs even in the arising of wholesome consciousness”—this is what those of other schools say. Referring to that, it is said, “Ignorance is a causal condition for meritorious and imperturbable volitional formations,” etc. This is an indication by way of the co-nascent category. By the word “etc.” it includes: knowledge arising even with unwholesome consciousness, which is called defiled wisdom; non-mental virtue; the material phenomenon called non-intimation; immorality, etc. Engaging with another's tenet refers to incurring involvement in another's tenet. If there is a meaning there that contradicts one's own tenet, it could be through clarifying it, or through instigating a debate on another's tenet. Of these, the former is removed by “without misrepresenting the teacher,” and the latter is shown by “without engaging with another's tenet.” By “without collecting”—they speak with reference to the meaning of accumulation. However, the word “engaging” does not have the meaning of accumulation; the view of some should not be regarded as essential.

Tabbipariyāyenāti yathāvinayaṃ avaṭṭhānena. Sāvajjassa anavajjatādīpanādinā kammantaraṃ bhindanto vināsento, āloḷento vā dhammataṃ dhammasabhāvaṃ vilometi viparītato dahati. Mahāpadeseti mahāapadese, buddhādayo mahante mahante apadisitvā vuttāni mahākāraṇāni. Mahāpadeseti vā mahāokāse, mahantāni dhammassa patiṭṭhānaṭṭhānānīti vuttaṃ hoti. Tatrāyaṃ vacanattho – apadisīyatīti apadeso, buddho apadeso etassāti buddhāpadeso. Esa nayo sesesupi. Atthato cāyaṃ mahāpadeso “sammukhā metaṃ bhagavato suta”ntiādinā kenaci ābhatassa “dhammo”ti vā “adhammo”ti vā vinicchayane kāraṇaṃ. Kiṃ pana tanti? Tassa yathābhatassa suttotaraṇādi eva. Yadi evaṃ kathaṃ cattāroti? Dhammassa dve sampadāyo bhagavā, sāvakā ca. Tesu sāvakā saṅghagaṇapuggalavasena tividhā. Evaṃ “amumhā mayā ayaṃ dhammo paṭiggahito”ti apadisitabbānaṃ bhedena cattāro. Tenāha “sammukhā metaṃ bhagavato suta”ntiādi. Nettiyampi vuttaṃ “buddhāpadeso saṅghāpadeso sambahulattherāpadeso ekattherāpadeso”ti.

By its opposite, it means by abiding according to the Vinaya. One who, by pointing out faultlessness in what is faulty, etc., breaks or destroys a legal procedure, or disturbs the Dhamma-nature, the inherent nature of Dhamma, reverses and corrupts it. “Mahāpadesa” means in the great authorities—those great reasons stated by citing the great ones like the Buddha, etc. Or, “Mahāpadesa” means in the great bases—it means great places for the establishment of the Dhamma. Here, this is the meaning of the word: “Authority” (apadesa) is that which is cited; the Buddha is the authority for this—thus, “Buddhāpadesa.” This method applies to the rest as well. And in essence, this “mahāpadesa” is a reason for deciding whether something that has been brought forward with “This was heard by me in the presence of the Blessed One,” etc., is “Dhamma” or “not Dhamma.” But what is the thread (tanti)? It is the verification of what has been brought forward with the suttas, etc. If so, why are there four? The Dhamma has two sources: the Blessed One and the disciples. Among them, the disciples are threefold: the Sangha, a group, or an individual. Thus, by the difference in those from whom it should be cited—“This Dhamma was received by me from such-and-such”—there are four. Therefore it is said, “This was heard by me in the presence of the Blessed One,” etc. In the Netti also it is stated: “The Buddha’s authority, the Sangha’s authority, the authority of many elders, the authority of one elder.”

Suttasuttānulomaācariyavādaattanomatimahāpadeseti ettha tisso saṅgītiyo āruḷhāni tīṇi piṭakāni atthasūcanādiatthena suttaṃ. Yathāvuttassa suttassa anulomato yathāvuttā eva cattāro mahāpadesā suttānulomaṃ. Pāḷiyā atthagāhaṇena dhammatāyaṃ patiṭṭhāpanato aṭṭhakathā ācariyavādo. Nayaggāhena anubuddhiyā attano paṭibhānaṃ attanomati. Ettha ca suttaācariyavādaattanomatīnampi kenaci ābhatassa dhammādhammādibhāvavinicchayane kāraṇabhāvasabhāvato mahāpadesatā vuttāti veditabbā. Santiṭṭhati appaṭibāhanto, avilomento ca. Tabbipariyāyena atidhāvati. Ekassa padassa ekena pakārena atthaṃ vatvā tasseva puna pakārantarena atthaṃ vadanto [M 0.0091] vā aparehi pariyāyehi niddisati nāma yathā “avijjā dukkhasaccassa [V 0.0089] yāthāvasarasalakkhaṇaṃ paṭivijjhituṃ na detī”tiādiṃ vatvā puna “ayaṃ avijjā dukkhādīsu aññāṇa”nti vuttāpi “dukkhasaccassa ekadeso hotī”tiādivacanaṃ. Atha vā hetubhāvena vuttassa atthassa puna phalabhāvena vacanaṃ tamevatthaṃ punarāvattetvā niddisanaṃ yathā “viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpa”nti vatvā puna “nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatana”nti vacanaṃ. Atha vā “sabbametaṃ bhavacakkaṃ kammañceva vipāko ca. Kilesakammavipākavasena tividha”nti ca ādinā vuttassevatthassa duvidhatividhādivibhāgadassanaṃ tamevatthaṃ punarāvattetvā niddisananti evamettha attho veditabbo.

Here, in the expression 'the great references of sutta, conformity with the suttas, the teachers' doctrine, and one's own opinion,' 'sutta' refers to the three Piṭakas included in the three Councils, in the sense of indicating the meaning, etc. 'Conformity with the suttas' refers to the four great references themselves, as described, in accordance with the aforementioned sutta. The commentary (aṭṭhakathā) is the 'teachers' doctrine' (ācariyavāda) because it establishes the teaching in the true nature of things by grasping the meaning of the Pāli text. 'One's own opinion' (attanomati) is one's own insight that arises from subsequent understanding by grasping a method. Here it should be understood that the sutta, the teachers' doctrine, and one's own opinion are also called 'great references' because of their inherent nature as a reason for deciding whether something brought forward by someone is Dhamma or not-Dhamma, and so on. It conforms when it is not contradicted and not inconsistent. It deviates when it is the opposite. Explaining the meaning of a single term in one way and then explaining its meaning again in another way, or illustrating it with other synonyms, is what is meant. For example, after saying, 'Ignorance does not allow one to penetrate the individual and general characteristics of the truth of suffering as it really is,' and then, although it has been said, 'This ignorance is non-knowledge regarding suffering, etc.,' one says, 'It is a part of the truth of suffering,' and so on. Or, after stating a meaning in terms of a cause, to state the same meaning again in terms of a result is to illustrate the same point by repetition, as when, after saying, 'With consciousness as condition, name-and-form comes to be,' one says again, 'With name-and-form as condition, the sixfold sense base comes to be.' Or, after saying, 'This entire wheel of existence is both kamma and its result. It is threefold by way of defilements, kamma, and results,' and so on, to show the division of that same meaning into two or three aspects is to illustrate the same point by repetition. Thus the meaning here should be understood.

Sattavohāroti “satto”ti samaññā. Ye hi dhamme samūhabhūte santānavasena vattamāne upādāya sattapaññatti, tassā tato aññathānāññathāaccantābhāvasaṅkhāte ante anupagamma yāthāvato saṅgahaṇaṃ, bodhanañca dhammatāyaṃ akusalassa dukkaraṃ durabhisambhavanti. Avijjādikassa paccayadhammassa saṅkhārādipaccayuppannadhammaṃ pati hetuādinā paccayena paccayabhāvo paccayākāro, paṭiccasamuppādoti attho.

The term 'being' is a conventional designation. For one who is unskilled in the true nature of things, it is difficult and hard to fully attain the grasping and understanding, as they really are, of those phenomena which, having become a group and proceeding as a continuum, are the basis for the concept of a 'being,' without arriving at the end-point which is designated as the utter non-existence of a self that is other or not other than them. The state of being a condition, the mode of conditionality, of a conditioning phenomenon such as ignorance for a conditionally arisen phenomenon such as formations, by way of being a condition such as a root-cause, etc.—this is the meaning of 'dependent origination'.

Vuttanayenāti “ācariye anabbhācikkhantenā”tiādinā vuttanayena. Kāmañcettha sabbāpi atthavaṇṇanā imināva nayena kātabbā, paṭiccasamuppādavaṇṇanāya pana garutarabhāvaṃ dassento evaṃ vadati.

“In the way stated” means in the way stated beginning with “by not misrepresenting the teacher.” And although here every explanation of the meaning should be made in this very way, he speaks thus to show the greater gravity of the explanation of dependent origination.

Pāḷidhammanti tepiṭakabuddhavacanaṃ. Paṭiccasamuppādanti paṭiccasamuppādapāḷiṃ.

“The Dhamma in the Pāli text” means the word of the Buddha in the Tipiṭaka. “Dependent origination” means the Pāli text on dependent origination.

Atthaṃ katvāti hitaṃ katvā. Yathāyaṃ hitāvaho hoti, evaṃ katvā. Aṭṭhiṃ katvāti vā attānaṃ atthikaṃ katvā. Sutacintāmayādiṃ ñāṇavisesaṃ. Tadaṅgavikkhambhanādinā kilesakkhayavisesaṃ.

“Having made the goal” means having done what is beneficial; having done it in such a way that it is beneficial. Or, “having made it essential” means having made oneself one who is desirous. A special knowledge such as that consisting of learning, reflection, and so on. A special destruction of the defilements by means of suppression by substitution, suppression by suspension, and so on.

Bhavādīsu ādīnavappaṭicchādanato, balavūpanissayato, kammassa visesahetubhāvato ca vaṭṭassa mūlakāraṇaṃ avijjā. Vipākavaṭṭanimittassa kammavaṭṭassa kāraṇabhūtampi kilesavaṭṭaṃ avijjāmūlakanti dassanatthaṃ avijjā ādito vuttā. Taṇhāpi hi avijjāya paṭicchāditādīnave eva visaye assādānupassino pavattati, na aññathā. Mūlādidassanasāmaññañcāti [V 0.0090] valliyā mūlamajjhapariyosānassa dassanena paṭiccasamuppādassa taṃdassanasāmaññañca yojetabbaṃ, samantacakkhunā sabbassa diṭṭhattepi [M 0.0092] desanākāle desanāñāṇacakkhunā bodhetabbatāvasena ekadesadassanassa adhippetattā.

Ignorance is the root cause of the round because it conceals the danger in existence, etc., because it is a strong decisive support condition, and because it is a specific cause for kamma. Ignorance is stated at the beginning in order to show that even the round of defilements—which is the cause of the round of kamma, the condition for the round of results—is rooted in ignorance. For craving, too, proceeds for one who contemplates gratification only in an object whose danger has been concealed by ignorance, not otherwise. And the common feature of showing the root, etc., should be connected with the common feature of showing the same for dependent origination by showing the root, middle, and end of a creeper; for although everything is seen with the eye of omniscience, at the time of teaching a partial seeing is intended for the purpose of awakening others with the eye of teaching-knowledge.

Diṭṭhisahitāya mānasahitāya vā taṇhāya “aha”nti, itarāya “mama”nti abhivadato. “Abhinandanato”ti hi iminā sappītikāya taṇhāya pavatti dassitā. “Abhivadato”ti iminā tato balavatarāya diṭṭhisahitāya mānasahitāya vā. “Ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato”ti iminā pana tatopi balavatamāya diṭṭhisahitāya, kevalāya vā taṇhāya pavatti dassitā. Gilitvā pariniṭṭhāpetvā ṭhānañhi ajjhosānaṃ. Tappaccayanti taṇhāpaccayaṃ. Kathaṃ pana nandivacanena catubbidhampi upādānaṃ vuttanti āha “nanditā”tiādi. Tattha nanditātadavippayogatāhīti nandibhāvena sabhāvato taṇhupādānaṃ, tāya nandiyā taṇhāya avippayogena avinābhāvena diṭṭhupādānaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. “Diṭṭhābhinandanabhāvenā”ti iminā diṭṭhiyāpi nandibhāvamāha.

Of one who declares 'I' because of craving accompanied by view or conceit, and 'mine' because of the other craving. For by 'delighting,' the occurrence of craving accompanied by zest is shown. By 'declaring,' the occurrence of a stronger craving than that, accompanied by view or conceit. But by 'clinging and remaining,' the occurrence of a craving even stronger than that, accompanied by view or just by itself, is shown. For clinging is the state of having swallowed and held on to something conclusively. 'Because of that as condition' means because of craving as condition. But how is the fourfold clinging spoken of by the word 'delight'? He says, 'because of delight,' etc. Here, by the words 'because of delight and its inseparability,' it should be understood that craving-clinging is stated by its intrinsic nature as delight, and view-clinging is stated by its non-separation from, its inseparability with, that delight which is craving. By 'by the nature of delighting in views,' he states that view, too, has the nature of delight.

Paṭisandhipavattiphassādayoti paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte ca uppannaphassamanosañcetanāviññāṇāni. “Vipākavaṭṭabhūte”ti ca idaṃ pavattavisesanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vaṭṭūpatthambhakāti vaṭṭattayūpanissayā. Itareti akammajā. Tasminti yathāvutte āhāracatukke. Vattuṃ vaṭṭantīti taṇhānidānūpanissayato “taṇhānidānā”ti vattuṃ yujjanti.

'Contact, etc., at rebirth-linking and in the course of existence' means contact, mental volition, and consciousness that have arisen at rebirth-linking and in the course of existence. And 'being in the round of results' should be seen as a qualifier of 'in the course of existence.' 'Supporting the round' means being a decisive support for the three rounds. 'The others' means those not produced by kamma. 'In that' refers to the fourfold nutriment as stated. Because they have craving as their source and decisive support, it is fitting to call them 'having craving as their source'.

Yathā ariyamaggo antadvayavajjitamajjhimapaṭipadābhāvato “ñāyo”ti vuccati, evaṃ paṭiccasamuppādopīti āha “ñāyoti maggo, soyeva vā paṭiccasamuppādo”ti. Attano paṭivedhāya saṃvattati asammohapaṭivedhena paṭivijjhitabbattā. Saṃvattatīti ca nimittassa kattūpacāravasenetaṃ vuttaṃ yathā “ariyabhāvakarāni saccāni ariyasaccānī”ti. Pakatiādayo heṭṭhā saccavibhaṅge hetuvippaṭipattikathāyaṃ dassitā eva. Akāraṇaṃ “kāraṇa”nti gaṇhanti yathā kāpilādayo. Na kiñci kāraṇaṃ bujjhanti yathā taṃ aññe bālaputhujjanā. Itarāsanti majjhato paṭṭhāya yāva pariyosānā desanādīnaṃ tissannaṃ. Tadatthatāsambhavepīti yathāsakehi kāraṇehi pavattidassanatthatāsambhavepi. Atthantarasabbhāvatoti payojanantarasabbhāvato. Vuttāni hi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (vibha. aṭṭha. 225) “jarāmaraṇādikassa [M 0.0093] dukkhassa attanā adhigatakāraṇasandassanatthaṃ. Āhāranidānavavatthāpanānusārena yāva atītaṃ addhānaṃ atiharitvā puna [V 0.0091] atītaddhato pabhuti hetuphalapaṭipāṭisandassanatthaṃ. Anāgataddhahetusamuṭṭhānato pabhuti anāgataddhasandassanattha”nti tissannaṃ yathākkamaṃ tīṇi payojanāni.

Just as the noble path is called 'the method' because it is the middle way that avoids the two extremes, so too is dependent origination. Thus he says: 'The method is the path, or that itself is dependent origination.' It leads to one's own penetration because it has to be penetrated by the penetration of non-delusion. And 'it leads to' is said by way of a figurative use of the agent for the instrument, just as in 'the truths that make one noble are the noble truths.' Nature and other causes have already been shown below in the Saccavibhaṅga in the section on wrong practice regarding cause. They take a non-cause to be a 'cause,' like the followers of Kapila and others. They do not understand any cause at all, like other foolish worldlings. The others are the three purposes of the teaching, etc., from the middle to the end. Even when that purpose—that is, the purpose of showing the process through its respective causes—is possible, it is understood through the existence of another purpose. For in the commentary (Vibh-a 225) three purposes are stated in order for the three sections: 'for the purpose of showing the cause, realized by oneself, of suffering such as aging-and-death; for the purpose of showing the sequence of cause and effect from the past onward, having extended back as far as the past time in accordance with the determination of the nutriment-condition; for the purpose of showing the future time from the origination of the cause in the future.'

Taṃtaṃphalapaṭivedhoti jātiādīnaṃ jarāmaraṇāditaṃtaṃphalāvagamo. Anuvilokayatoti purime vikappe vipassanānimittaṃ anuvilokanaṃ, dutiye desanānimittaṃ. Kāmupādānabhūtā taṇhā manosañcetanāhārasaṅkhātassa bhavassa, taṃsampayuttānaṃ, tannimittānañca sesāhārānaṃ visesapaccayo hotīti āha “āhārataṇhādayo paccuppannaddhā”ti. Ādi-saddena yāva viññāṇaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Āhārataṇhādayoti ettha paccuppannakammavaṭṭapariyāpanne āhāre gahetvā addhayojanaṃ katvā anāgatavipākavaṭṭapariyāpanne gahetvā yojetuṃ vuttaṃ “āhārā vā taṇhāya pabhāvetabbā anāgato addhā”ti. Pabhāvetabbāti āyatiṃ uppādetabbā. Yujjatīti phalabhūte āhāre paccuppanne paccakkhato dassetvā “taṃnidānaṃ taṇhaṃ tassā nidāna”ntiādinā phalaparamparāya kāraṇaparamparāya ca dassanaṃ tathābujjhanakānaṃ puggalānaṃ ajjhāsayānulomato, dhammasabhāvāvilomanato ca yuttiyā saṅgayhati. Yadi taṇhādayo atīto addhā, taṇhāggahaṇeneva saṅkhārāvijjā gahitāti kimatthaṃ puna te gahitāti āha “saṅkhārāvijjā tatopi atītataro addhā vutto saṃsārassa anādibhāvadassanattha”nti. Atītanti vā atītatāsāmaññena atītatarampi saṅgahitaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Penetration of the respective fruits means the understanding of the respective fruits of birth, etc., namely, aging-and-death, etc. Observes means: in the first alternative, the observation is of the sign of insight; in the second, of the sign of the teaching. Craving, which is the basis of sensual clinging, is a specific condition for existence—designated as the nutriment of mental volition—and for the states associated with it and for the remaining nutriments produced by it. Thus it is said: 'Nutriment, craving, etc., are the present time.' By the word 'etc.' consciousness should be included. Regarding 'nutriment, craving, etc.,' here, having taken nutriment as included in the round of kamma in the present, and having made the temporal connection, it is said, in order to connect it with what is included in the round of results in the future: 'Or nutriments are to be generated by craving; that is the future time.' 'To be generated' means to be produced in the future. It is tenable: having directly shown the nutriment that is a result in the present, the demonstration of the sequence of effects and the sequence of causes by such means as 'craving is its source, and that is its source' is consistent with the disposition of persons who understand it thus and with the unperverted nature of phenomena; it is logically coherent. If craving, etc., are the past time, since formations and ignorance are included by the taking up of craving, why are they taken up again? It is said: 'Formations and ignorance are stated as a time even more past than that in order to show the beginningless nature of saṃsāra.' Or 'past' should be seen as including even the more past by way of the generality of pastness.

Punabbhavābhinibbattiāhārakāti punabbhavūpapattipaccayā. Iti vacanatoti evaṃ vuttavacanasabbhāvato. Viññāṇāhāro tāva punabbhavābhinibbattiyā hetu, itare pana kathanti āha “taṃsampayuttattā…pe… kabaḷīkārāhārassā”ti. Tassa āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbattiāhārakā cattāro āhārāti sambandho. Saddhādīnaṃ upanissayatā pariccāgādikāle, rāgādīnaṃ gadhitassa bhojanādikāle. Tena yathākkamaṃ kusalākusalakammaviññāṇāyūhanaṃ dassitaṃ. Tasmāti yasmā āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbattiāhārakā cattāro āhārā gayhanti, tasmā. Purimoyevatthoti [M 0.0094] “āhārataṇhādayo paccuppannaddhā”tiādinā vuttaattho. Atīteti atīte addhani. Tato paranti tato atītaddhato paraṃ paccuppanne anāgate ca addhani “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇa”ntiādinā. Paccakkhānanti paccuppannabhavapariyāpannatāya paccakkhabhūtānaṃ. Paccuppannaṃ hetunti etarahi vattamānaṃ taṇhādikaṃ āhārādīnaṃ hetuṃ.

Nutriments for the production of renewed existence means conditions for rebirth in a new existence. Because of this statement means because of the existence of the statement so expressed. The nutriment of consciousness is a cause for the production of renewed existence. But how are the others? It is said: 'Because of being associated with it...pe... of the nutriment of physical food.' The connection is: 'The four nutriments are nutriments for the production of renewed existence in the future.' For faith, etc., there is the state of decisive support at the time of relinquishment, etc.; for lust, etc., at the time of eating when one is attached. Thereby the accumulation of wholesome and unwholesome kamma-consciousness is shown respectively. Therefore means: because the four nutriments are taken as nutriments for the production of renewed existence in the future, therefore. The previous meaning is the meaning stated by 'nutriment, craving, etc., are the present time,' etc. 'In the past' means in the past time. 'After that' means after that past time, in the present and future times, by 'with formations as condition, consciousness,' etc. 'Of what is directly perceived' means of what has become directly perceptible by being included in the present existence. 'The present as cause' means craving, etc., now existing, is the cause of nutriment, etc.

Suttaṃ [V 0.0092] āharati “āsavasamudayā avijjāsamudayo”ti (ma. ni. 1.103). Vaṭṭahetunoti vipākavaṭṭahetuno, sakalavaṭṭahetuno vā. Akusalañhi kammaṃ kammavaṭṭassa kilesavaṭṭassa ca paccayo hotiyeva. “Bhavataṇhāyapi hetubhūtā”ti iminā kilesavaṭṭassāpi avijjāya paccayabhāvamāha. Evañcetaṃ, bhikkhave, vuccatī”tiādinā vaṭṭasīsānampi avijjātaṇhānaṃ sappaccayatādassanāpadesena sabbesampi saṅkhatadhammānaṃ hetuphalaparamparāvicchedavuttiyā purimāya koṭiyā apaññāyanaṃ vibhāveti.

He adduces a sutta: 'With the arising of the taints, there is the arising of ignorance' (MN 9/i.55). 'As a cause for the round' means as a cause for the round of results, or as a cause for the entire round. For unwholesome kamma is indeed a condition for both the round of kamma and the round of defilements. By the phrase 'being a cause also for craving for existence,' he states that ignorance is a condition even for the round of defilements. By the passage beginning, 'And so, bhikkhus, this is said,' by way of showing that even ignorance and craving, the heads of the round, are conditioned, he clarifies the non-discernment of a first point in the uninterrupted process of the sequence of cause and effect for all conditioned phenomena.

Avijjaṃ taṇhā anuvattatīti dukkhe taṇhaṃ abhibhavitvā pavattiyā tato avijjāya balavabhāvamāha. Avijjābhibhūtā hi sattā satipi taṇhāparitassite ekantānatthasaññitaṃ attakilamathānuyogadukkhamanuyuñjanti. Taṇhaṃ avijjā anuvattatīti sukhe avijjaṃ abhibhavitvā pavattiyā tato taṇhāya balavabhāvamāha. Yadipi sāvajjasukhānubhave balavatīyeva avijjā vijjamānaādīnavaṃ paṭicchādentī tiṭṭhati, taṇhā pana tatopi balavataratāya satte vipulānatthasañhite anariye sukhe niyojetīti avijjāya tadanuvattanaṃ vuttaṃ.

‘Craving follows ignorance’: this means that because it proceeds by overpowering craving in the case of suffering, he states the powerful nature of ignorance. For beings overcome by ignorance, though they are tormented by craving, practice the suffering of the devotion to self-mortification, which is considered entirely unbeneficial. ‘Ignorance follows craving’: this means that because it proceeds by overpowering ignorance in the case of pleasure, he states the powerful nature of craving. Although in the experience of blameworthy pleasure ignorance is indeed powerful, concealing the existing danger, craving, being even more powerful than that, engages beings in ignoble pleasure, which is considered vastly unbeneficial. Thus it is said that ignorance follows it.

Āyatanachakkaṃ vā kāyoti sambandho. Cakkhādinissaye sesadhammeti cakkhādinissayabhūte, tappaṭibaddhe ca sasantānapariyāpanne dhamme. Cakkhādinissite eva katvāti cakkhādiggahaṇeneva gahite katvā. Cakkhādikāyanti cakkhādidhammasamūhaṃ paresaṃ pañcakkhandhaṃ. Phassena phuṭṭhoti ārammaṇaṃ phusantena viya uppannena sukhavedaniyena, dukkhavedaniyena ca phassena phuṭṭho. Phasse hi tathā uppanne taṃsamaṅgīpuggalo phuṭṭhoti vohāro hotīti.

The connection is: 'The sixfold sense base or the body.' 'The remaining phenomena dependent on the eye, etc.': this means the phenomena that are dependent on the eye, etc., are connected with it, and are included in one's own continuity. 'Having taken them as just dependent on the eye, etc.': this means having taken them as included by the taking up of the eye, etc. 'The body of the eye, etc.': this means the collection of phenomena, the eye, etc.; for others, the five aggregates. 'Touched by contact': this means touched by contact that is to be felt as pleasant and by contact that is to be felt as painful, which has arisen as if touching an object. For when contact has arisen in such a way, there is the convention that the person endowed with it is 'touched.'

Yathā saḷāyatanāni phassassa visesapaccayo, evaṃ vedanāyapīti dassento “saḷāyatanānaṃ vedanāya visesapaccayabhāva”nti āha. Tannissitanti [M 0.0095] saḷāyatananissitaṃ. Atītaddhāvijjātaṇhāmūlakoti atītaddhabhūtaavijjātaṇhāmūlako. Kāyassa bhedā kāyūpagoti ubhayatthāpi kāyasaddena upādinnakkhandhapañcako gahito. Tadupagatā upapajjanaṃ paṭisandhiggahaṇaṃ. Ubhayamūloti avijjātaṇhāmūlo.

Showing that just as the six sense bases are a specific condition for contact, so too are they for feeling, he says: 'the state of the six sense bases as a specific condition for feeling.' 'Dependent on that' means dependent on the six sense bases. 'Rooted in past ignorance and craving' means rooted in ignorance and craving that belong to the past. 'Upon the breakup of the body, gone to a body': in both cases, by the word 'body' the five clung-to aggregates are taken. 'Gone to that' means arising, the taking up of rebirth-linking. 'Rooted in both' means rooted in ignorance and craving.

Anabhisamayabhūtattāti abhisamayassa paṭipakkhabhūtattā. Avijjāyāti avijjāya sati.

'Because of being of the nature of non-penetration' means because of being of a nature contrary to penetration. 'With ignorance' means when there is ignorance.

Gahaṇanti [V 0.0093] gahetabbataṃ. Tasmāti yasmā sati saṅkhārasaddena āgatasaṅkhārattepi avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā padhānatāya visuṃ vuttā gobalībaddañāyena, tasmā. Tattha vuttampīti saṅkhārasaddena āgatasaṅkhāresu vuttampi abhisaṅkharaṇakasaṅkhāraṃ vajjetvā aggahetvā itare saṅkhārā yojetabbā. Evañhi atthassa uddharaṇuddharitabbatādvayaṃ asaṅkarato dassitaṃ hoti. “Idha vaṇṇetabbabhāvenā”ti iminā avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārānaṃ satipi saṅkhārasaddena āgatasaṅkhārabhāve yathāvuttameva padhānabhāvaṃ ulliṅgeti. “Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā”ti tadekadeso vuttoti sambandho. Imasmiṃ atthavikappe saṅgaṇhanavasena saṅkhārasaddena āgatasaṅkhārehi saṅgahitāpi avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā idha vaṇṇetabbabhāvena padhānāti visuṃ gahitā, purimasmiṃ te vajjetvāti ayaṃ viseso. Tenāha “vaṇṇetabbasabbasaṅgahaṇavasena duvidhatā vuttā”ti. Sāmaññato saṅgayhamānampi padhānabhāvajotanatthaṃ visuṃ gayhati yathā taṃ “puññañāṇasambhārā”ti.

'Grasping' means the state of having to be grasped. 'Therefore' means: because, although they are formations that come under the word 'formations,' the formations conditioned by ignorance are stated separately on account of their prominence, by the maxim of the ox and the bull; therefore. 'Therein, though it is stated': having excluded, not taken, the formative formation among the formations stated that come under the word 'formations,' the other formations should be connected. For in this way the duality of the meaning—the extracting and what is to be extracted—is shown without confusion. By 'here, by way of being what is to be explained,' he indicates the prominence, just as stated, of the formations conditioned by ignorance, even though they are formations that come under the word 'formations.' The connection is: 'Formations conditioned by ignorance' is stated as a part of that. In this alternative meaning, although the formations conditioned by ignorance are included by way of inclusion with the formations that come under the word 'formations,' here they are taken separately as prominent by way of being what is to be explained, excluding them in the former case—this is the difference. Therefore he says: 'the twofoldness is stated by way of the inclusion of all that is to be explained.' Even what is included generally is taken separately to illuminate its prominence, as in 'the accumulations of merit and knowledge.'

Yena kusalākusaladhammā “vipākadhammā”ti vuccanti, taṃ āyūhanaṃ, kiṃ pana tanti? Anupacchinnataṇhāvijjāmāne santāne sabyāpāratā. Tenāha “paṭisandhi…pe… āyūhanarasā”ti. Cetanāpadhānattā pana tassa cetanākiccaṃ katvā vuttaṃ. Rāsikaraṇaṃ, āyūhananti ca rāsibhūtassa rūpārūpasaṅkhātassa phalassa nibbattanato vuttaṃ. “Anārammaṇatā abyākatatā”ti idaṃ abyākatasseva anārammaṇattā abyākatasambandhinī anārammaṇatāti katvā vuttaṃ. Āyatanaṃ, ghaṭananti ca taṃtaṃdvārikadhammappavattanameva daṭṭhabbaṃ.

That by which wholesome and unwholesome states are called 'states that have a result' is accumulation. But what is that? The activity in a continuity where craving and ignorance have not been cut off. Hence he says: 'rebirth-linking...pe... has the function of accumulation.' But because volition is prominent, it is stated by making it the function of volition. 'Making a heap' and 'accumulation' are said because of the production of the result, designated as material and immaterial, which has become a heap. 'Objectlessness, indeterminacy': this is said by taking the objectlessness related to the indeterminate as the objectlessness of the indeterminate itself. 'Sphere' and 'striving' should be seen as just the occurrence of phenomena through their respective doors.

Ananubodhādayo avijjāpadaniddese āgatā. Avijjāpadasambandhena diṭṭhivippayuttāti itthiliṅganiddeso. Asaṇṭhānattāti aviggahattā.

'Non-awakening, etc.,' are found in the exposition of the term 'ignorance.' Because of its connection with the term 'ignorance,' 'disassociated from views' is a designation in the feminine gender. 'Because of having no configuration' means because of having no physical form.

Sokādīnaṃ [M 0.0096] sabbhāvāti “jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇa”nti aniṭṭhāpetvā tadanantaraṃ sokādīnampi vuttānaṃ vijjamānattā tesaṃ vasena aṅgabahuttappasaṅge paṭiccasamuppādaṅgānaṃ bahubhāve āpanne. Dvādasevāti kathaṃ dvādaseva, nanu sokādayopi dhammantarabhūtā paṭiccasamuppādadesanāyaṃ vuttāti? Saccaṃ vuttā, na pana aṅgantarabhāvenāti dassento “na hī”tiādimāha. Tattha phalenāti phalabhūtena jarāmaraṇaṅgasaṅgahitena sokādinā. Mūlaṅgaṃ dassetunti imāya paṭiccasamuppādadesanāya mūlabhūtaṃ avijjaṅgaṃ socanādīhi sammohāpattikathanena dassetuṃ te sokādayo vuttā bhavacakkassa avicchedadassanatthaṃ. Jarāmaraṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ etesanti jarāmaraṇakāraṇā[V 0.0094], sokādayo, tabbhāvo jarāmaraṇakāraṇatā. Jarāmaraṇaṃ nimittaṃ etassāti jarāmaraṇanimittaṃ. Taṃ tannimittānanti ettha tanti suttaṃ. Tannimittānaṃ dukkhanimittānaṃ sokādīnaṃ. Tato parāyāti anāgate dutiyattabhāvato parāya tatiyattabhāvādīsu paṭisandhiyā. Hetuhetubhūtāti kāraṇassa kāraṇabhūtā. Paṭisandhiyā hi saṅkhārā kāraṇaṃ, tesaṃ avijjā. Suttanti “assutavā puthujjano”ti (ma. ni. 1.2, 17; saṃ. ni. 2.61; dha. sa. 1007) imaṃ suttaṃ sandhāya vadati. Avijjā sokādīnaṃ kāraṇanti dassitā assutavatāya avijjābhibhavanadīpaniyā taduppattivacanato. “Na sokādīnaṃ bālassa jarāmaraṇanimittatāmattassa sādhakaṃ sutta”nti vuttamatthaṃ pākaṭaṃ kātuṃ “na cā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tena na ca jarāmaraṇanimittameva dukkhaṃ dukkhaṃ, atha kho avijjānimittampettha vuttanayena yojetabbanti dasseti. Evaṃ jarāmaraṇena sokādīnaṃ ekasaṅkhepaṃ katvā dvādaseva paṭiccasamuppādaṅgāni veditabbāni.

Because grief and the like exist, if, after stating 'with birth as condition, aging-and-death' without concluding there, one were to take into account grief and the like which are also mentioned immediately after, the limbs of dependent origination would become numerous. How then are there only twelve? Are not grief and the like also mentioned in the teaching on dependent origination as distinct phenomena? It is true they are mentioned, but not as separate limbs. To show this, he said, 'For they are not…' and so on. Here, 'by the fruit' means by grief and the like, which are included in the limb of aging-and-death, which is the fruit. 'To show the root limb' means that grief and the like are mentioned in this teaching on dependent origination in order to show the root limb, ignorance, by describing the falling into delusion through grieving, and in order to show the uninterruptedness of the wheel of existence. 'Aging-and-death is their cause' (jarāmaraṇakāraṇā); that is, grief and the like. Their state is causality by aging-and-death. 'Aging-and-death is its sign' (jarāmaraṇanimittaṃ). In the phrase 'taṃ tannimittānaṃ,' 'tanti' means the sutta. 'Of those having that as a sign' means of grief and the like, which have suffering as their sign. 'Beyond that' means for rebirth-linking in the future, beyond the second state of existence, in the third state of existence and so on. 'Being the cause of the cause' means being the cause of the cause. For formations are the cause of rebirth-linking, and ignorance is the cause of them. 'The discourse' refers to this discourse: 'The uninstructed ordinary person…' (MN 2; SN 12.61; Dhs 1007). Ignorance is shown to be the cause of grief and the like, since their arising is stated in a way that illuminates the overwhelming by ignorance due to being uninstructed. To clarify the statement, 'The discourse does not merely establish that grief and the like are only a sign of aging-and-death for the fool,' he said, 'And not…' and so on. Thereby he shows that suffering is not only the suffering that is a sign of aging-and-death, but also the suffering that is a sign of ignorance should be connected here in the way stated. Thus, by making a single summary of grief and the like with aging-and-death, it should be understood that there are only twelve limbs of dependent origination.

Kasmā panettha jarāmaraṇantā eva desanā katā, kiṃ tato parā pavatti natthīti? No natthi, appahīnakilesassa hi kammato, viññāṇādipariyosānabhūtāya ca cutiyā paṭisandhipātubhāvoti pavattitaduparamabhūtaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ punabbhavābhinibbattinimittaṃ. Taṃ pana kammūpapattibhavato jātiyā dassitattā “bhavapaccayā jātī”ti imināva pakāsitanti na puna vuccati, na tato paraṃ pavattiyā abhāvato. Ekakammanibbattassa ca santānassa [M 0.0097] jarāmaraṇaṃ pariyosānaṃ. Sati kilesavaṭṭe kammunā tato punabbhavūpapatti, asati pana tasmiṃ “esevanto dukkhassā”ti jarāmaraṇapariyosānāva desanā katā. Yasmā pana na amaraṇā jarā atthi sabbesaṃ uppattimantānaṃ pākānantarabhedato, na cājaraṃ maraṇaṃ apākabhedābhāvā, tasmā tadubhayamekamaṅgaṃ kataṃ, na nāmarūpaṃ viya ubhayaṭṭhāne ekajjhaṃ uppattiyā, saḷāyatanaṃ viya vā āyatanabhāvena kiccasamatāya. Yā panāyaṃ osānaṃ gatā punabbhavābhinibbatti dīpitā, tāya “viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpa”ntiādi, kilesakammābhāve tadabhāvato “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā”ti evamādi eva vā atthato pakāsito hotīti vaṭṭattayassa anavaṭṭhānena paribbhamanaṃ dassitaṃ hoti. Atha vā jarāgahaṇena paripakkaparipakkatarādikkamena vattamānaṃ nāmarūpādi, sokādi ca gayhati, tathāssa paripākakālavattinī avijjā ca. Yathāha –

Why is the teaching given here as ending only with aging-and-death? Is there no process beyond that? No, it is not that there is not. For one whose defilements are not abandoned, rebirth-linking arises from kamma and from the death that is the end of consciousness and so on. Thus aging-and-death, which is the cessation of that process, is a sign for the production of a renewed existence. But since that is shown by birth from kamma-becoming, it is explained by just this phrase, 'with becoming as condition, birth,' and is not stated again; this is not because there is no process beyond that. For a single continuum produced by one kamma, aging-and-death is the end. When the round of defilements exists, there is renewed existence from that through kamma; but when it does not exist, the teaching is given as ending with aging-and-death with the words, 'this is the end of suffering.' Moreover, since for any being that has arisen there is no aging without death—because of the breaking up immediately after ripening—and there is no death without aging—because there is no breaking up without ripening—therefore those two are made one limb. This is not like name-and-form, by arising together in a twofold state, or like the six sense bases, because of their functional similarity as bases. Now, this production of a renewed existence, which has been pointed out as the final outcome, is in meaning explained by such phrases as 'with consciousness as condition, name-and-form,' and also by 'with ignorance as condition, formations,' since in the absence of defilements and kamma, that renewed existence is absent. Thus the revolving of the three rounds through their non-cessation is shown. Alternatively, by the term 'aging,' name-and-form, etc., which proceed by way of maturing, maturing further, etc., are included, as well as grief and the like, and also the ignorance that occurs at the time of its maturation. As it is said:

“Sa [V 0.0095] kho so, bhikkhave, kumāro vuddhimanvāya indriyānaṃ paripākamanvāya pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreti cakkhuviññeyyehi rūpehi…pe… kāyaviññeyyehi phoṭṭhabbehi…pe… rajanīyehi. So cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā piyarūpe rūpe sārajjati, appiyarūpe rūpe byāpajjati, anupaṭṭhitakāyasati ca viharati parittacetaso, tañca cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, yatthassa te pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhantī”tiādi (ma. ni. 1.408).

“Bhikkhus, that boy, having come to growth and to the maturity of his faculties, enjoys himself, provided and endowed with the five cords of sensual pleasure: with forms cognizable by the eye…pe… with tangibles cognizable by the body…pe… that are desirable. Having seen a form with the eye, he lusts after an agreeable form and is repelled by a disagreeable form. He dwells with mindfulness of the body unestablished and with a limited mind, and he does not understand as it actually is that liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, wherein those evil, unwholesome states cease without remainder.” (MN 1.408)

Ettha hi paripakkindriyassa chasu dvāresu sarāgādiggahaṇena tadavinābhāvitāya vimuttiyā appajānane ca sokādīnaṃ paccayabhūtā avijjā pakāsitā. Apica “piyappabhavā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti vacanato kāmāsavabhavāsavehi, “tassa ‘ahaṃ rūpaṃ, mama rūpanti pariyuṭṭhaṭṭhāyino…pe… rūpavipariṇāmaññathābhāvā uppajjanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti (saṃ. ni. 3.1) vacanato diṭṭhāsavato, “assutavā”tiādivacanato [M 0.0098] avijjāsavato sokādīnaṃ pavatti dīpitāti tesaṃ hetutāya taggahaṇena gahitā āsavā. Tesaṃ sayañca jarāsabhāvatāya jarāgahaṇena gayhanti, tato ca “āsavasamudayā avijjāsamudayo”ti vacanato āsavanimittāya ca avijjāya jarāgahaṇena gahaṇaṃ. Tato ca “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā”ti āvaṭṭati bhavacakkaṃ. Apica “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇa”nti vatvā “bhavapaccayā jātī”ti vadantenapi bhavacakkassa anavaṭṭhānato paribbhamanaṃ dassitaṃ. Ettha hi viññāṇena avijjānivutassa punabbhavo dassito, jātiyā taṇhāya sampayuttassa, ubhayattha ubhinnaṃ anuvattamānattāti avijjātaṇhānimittaṃ bhavacakkaṃ anavaṭṭhānato paribbhamatīti ayamattho dīpitoti jarāmaraṇantāpi desanā na tato paraṃ pavattiyā abhāvaṃ sūceti atadatthattā, na ca paccayantaradassanatthameva puna vacananti sakkā viññātuṃ ekatreva tadubhayadesanāya tassa siddhattā. Tathā yaṃ kammaṃ avijjāhetukaṃ, taṃ taṇhāhetukampi. Yaṃ taṇhāhetukaṃ, taṃ avijjāhetukampi veditabbaṃ. Kasmā? Dvinnaṃ bhavamūlānaṃ aññamaññāvirahato. Yathā hi taṇhāpaccayā kāmupādānahetukaṃ kammabhavasaṅkhāraṃ vadanto na vinā bhavataṇhāya avijjā saṅkhārānaṃ paccayoti dasseti. Tathā tameva avijjāpaccayaṃ desento na antarena avijjāya bhavataṇhā kammabhavassa paccayoti. Tato ca pubbe pavattā avijjādipaccayā saṅkhārādayo[V 0.0096], taṇhupādānādipaccayā bhavādayo ca, tathā taṇhāhetuupādānapaccayā bhavo, avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā, bhavapaccayā jāti, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ, viññāṇādipaccayānāmarūpādīti evametesaṃ aṅgānaṃ pubbāparasambandho dassito hotīti veditabbaṃ.

Here, for one with mature faculties, ignorance, which is the condition for grief and the like, is explained by the grasping with lust and so on at the six doors, and by the non-understanding of the liberation that is inseparable from that. Moreover, from the statement, “From the beloved arise sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair,” the process of grief and the like is explained as arising from the taints of sensual pleasure and existence. From the statement, “For one who is obsessed with the thought, ‘I am form, form is mine’… with the change and alteration of form, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise” (SN 3.1), it is explained as arising from the taint of views. From statements like “the uninstructed,” it is explained as arising from the taint of ignorance. Thus the taints are included by the inclusion of these states, on account of their being the cause. They themselves are also included by the term 'aging' because their own nature is aging. Then, from the statement, “With the arising of the taints comes the arising of ignorance,” ignorance, which is a sign of the taints, is also included by the term 'aging.' And from that, the wheel of existence revolves with “with ignorance as condition, formations.” Furthermore, by saying “with formations as condition, consciousness” and “with becoming as condition, birth,” the revolving of the wheel of existence through its non-cessation is shown. Here, by consciousness, renewed existence is shown for one who is obstructed by ignorance; by birth, for one who is conjoined with craving. Because in both cases both are present, this meaning is explained: the wheel of existence, marked by ignorance and craving, revolves without coming to a standstill. Thus the teaching ending with aging-and-death does not indicate an absence of a process beyond that, as that is not its purpose. Nor can it be understood that the repetition is merely for the purpose of showing an intermediate condition, since that is established by the teaching of both together in one place. Similarly, whatever kamma is caused by ignorance is also caused by craving. Whatever is caused by craving should be understood as also caused by ignorance. Why? Because the two roots of existence are inseparable. For just as one who speaks of the kamma-formation of kamma-becoming caused by clinging to sensual pleasures, which is conditioned by craving, shows that ignorance is not a condition for formations without craving for existence; so too, when teaching that same ignorance as condition, he shows that craving for existence is not a condition for kamma-becoming without ignorance. And from that, it should be understood that the prior-posterior connection of these limbs is shown thus: just as formations, etc., are conditioned by ignorance, etc., which occurred previously, and becoming, etc., are conditioned by craving, clinging, etc.; so too, becoming is conditioned by craving-caused clinging, formations are conditioned by ignorance, birth is conditioned by becoming, consciousness is conditioned by formations, aging-and-death is conditioned by birth, and name-and-form, etc., are conditioned by consciousness, etc.

Uddesavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Summary Section is finished.

Avijjāpadaniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of the Term Ignorance

226. Pitā [M 0.0099] kathīyatīti asuko asukassa pitāti pitubhāvena kathīyati. Kathiyamāno ca asandehatthaṃ aññehi mittadattehi visesetvā kathīyatīti taṃ dassento āha “dīgho…pe… datto”ti.

226. 'He is called “father”': So-and-so is called the father of so-and-so on account of his fatherhood. And when he is spoken of, in order to remove doubt, he is specified in relation to other Mittadattas. To show this, it is said: 'the tall...pe... Datta.'

Yāthāvoti aviparīto. Kiccajātitoti paṭicchādanakiccato, uppajjanaṭṭhānato ca.

'Yāthāvo' means undistorted. 'Kiccajāti' means from its function of concealing and from its place of origin.

Gahaṇakāraṇavasenāti gahaṇassa kāraṇabhāvavasena. Aññasetādīnaṃ nivattakānīti padaṃ ānetvā sambandho.

'Gahaṇakāraṇavasena' means by way of being the cause of grasping. The connection is made by supplying the words 'aññasetādīnaṃ nivattakāni'.

Chādentiyāti chādanākārena pavattantiyā. Tathā pavattanahetu taṃsampayuttā avijjāsampayuttā dukkhārammaṇā honti.

'Chādentiyā' means by proceeding in the manner of concealing. Because it proceeds in such a way, the states associated with it, being associated with ignorance, have suffering as their object.

Tasmāti sabhāvato agambhīrattā tesaṃ duddasabhāvakaraṇī tadārammaṇatā avijjā uppajjati. Itaresanti nirodhamaggānaṃ. Samānepi paṇītaasaṃkilesikādibhāve sappaccayato appaccayassa visesaṃ dassetuṃ “maggassā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

'Tasmā': Because they are not profound by nature, and because it makes their nature difficult to see, ignorance arises having them as its object. 'Itaresaṃ' means of cessation and the path. Although they share the same sublime and undefiled nature, etc., in order to show the distinction of the unconditioned from the conditioned, it is said, 'of the path,' etc.

Avijjāpadaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Term Ignorance is finished.

Saṅkhārapadaniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of the Term 'Volitional Formations'

“Sodheti [V 0.0097] apuññaphalato”ti iminā puññassa vipākadukkhavivittataṃ āha, “dukkhato”ti iminā cetodukkhavivittataṃ, “saṃkilesato”ti iminā kilesadukkhavivittataṃ. “Apuññaphalato”ti vā iminā puññassa āyatiṃ hitataṃ dasseti. “Dukkhasaṃkilesato”ti iminā pavattihitataṃ pavattisukhatañca dasseti. Taṃnipphādanenāti hitasukhanibbattanena. Pujjabhavanibbattako pujjanibbattako.

By 'it purifies from the fruit of demerit,' he states the seclusion of merit from the suffering that is its result. By 'from suffering,' he states its seclusion from mental suffering. By 'from defilement,' he states its seclusion from the suffering of defilements. Or, by 'from the fruit of demerit,' he shows the future benefit of merit. By 'from suffering and defilement,' he shows the benefit and happiness in continued existence. 'By producing that' means by producing benefit and happiness. 'Producer of a worthy existence' means a producer of what is worthy.

“Evamidaṃ puññaṃ pavaḍḍhatī”tiādīsu puññaphalampi puññanti vuccatīti āha “puññupaganti bhavasampattupaga”nti.

In such passages as 'Thus this merit increases,' even the fruit of merit is called 'merit'; therefore he said: 'conducing to merit, conducing to the attainment of [good] existence.'

Ādibhāvanāti “pathavī pathavī”tiādinā kasiṇesu pavattabhāvanā. Pathavī pathavīti vā ettha iti-saddo ādiattho, pakārattho vā. Tena [M 0.0100] itarakasiṇānaṃ gahaṇaṃ. Ādibhāvanātiādibhūtā bhāvanā. Sā hi “parikamma”nti vuccati. Maṇḍalakaraṇaṃ kasiṇamaṇḍalakaraṇaṃ.

'Ādibhāvanā' is the development practiced on the kasiṇas by such means as 'earth, earth.' Here, in 'earth, earth,' the word 'iti' has the meaning of 'etc.' or 'kind.' Thereby the other kasiṇas are included. 'Ādibhāvanā' means the initial development, for it is called 'preliminary work.' 'Making a circle' means making the kasiṇa disk.

Dānavasenāti deyyadhammapariccāgavasena. Cittacetasikā dhammā dānaṃ diyyati etenāti. Tatthāti tesu cittacetasikesu. Dānaṃ ārabbhāti tehi nibbattiyamānaṃ pariccāgaṃ uddissa. Yathā vā so nippajjati, tathā ṭhapetvā. Adhikiccāti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Yathā vā sampayuttehi nibbattiyamānā dānakiriyā nipphattivasena adhikataṃ pāpuṇāti, tathā katvā. Cetanāvaseneva hi dānādikammanipphatti. Itaresūti “sīlaṃ ārabbhā”tiādīsu.

'By way of giving' means by way of relinquishing a gift. Mind and mental factors are 'giving' because by means of them one gives. 'Tattha' means among those—mind and mental factors. 'Having taken up giving' means with reference to the relinquishment being produced by them. Or, having established it as it arises. 'Adhikicca' is a synonym for that. Or, having acted in such a way that the act of giving, being produced by the associated states, attains predominance by way of its accomplishment. For the accomplishment of actions such as giving comes about only by way of volition. 'In the others' refers to 'having taken up virtue,' etc.

Asarikkhakampīti attanā asadisampi kaṭattārūpanti sambandho. Vināpi catutthajjhānavipākena. Rūpataṇhāsaṅkhātassāti “rūpataṇhā”ti ettha vuttarūpataṇhamāha. Guñjanti guñjaphalaparimāṇaṃ dhāraṇīyavatthuṃ. Tathā taṇḍulaṃ.

'Asarikkhakaṃ pi': The connection is: even what is dissimilar to oneself, that is, a created form. Even without the resultant of the fourth jhāna. 'Of that designated as craving for form': this refers to the craving for form spoken of here as 'craving for form.' 'Guñjaṃ': an object to be worn the size of a guñja fruit. Similarly, a grain of rice.

“Vacanavisesamattamevā”ti atthavisesābhāvo vuttoti atthavisesābhāvamāha “kāyadvāre pavatti [V 0.0098] eva hi ādānādipāpanā”ti. Purimenāti “kāyadvāre pavattā”ti iminā. Tañhi pavattimattakathanato dvārūpalakkhaṇaṃ hoti. Pacchimenāti “ādānā”divacanena.

Because it is said, 'it is merely a difference in expression,' an absence of a difference in meaning is stated. He states this absence of a difference in meaning by saying: 'For occurrence at the body door is itself the conveying of taking, etc.' 'By the former' means by 'occurring at the body door.' For since that is a mere statement of occurrence, it serves to characterize the door. 'By the latter' means by the expression 'taking, etc.'

Kāyavacīsaṅkhāraggahaṇeti uddesaṃ sandhāyāha. Kāyavacīsañcetanāgahaṇeti niddesaṃ. Viññāṇassāti paṭisandhiviññāṇassa. Sahajātassa pana anantarassa ca paccayo hotiyeva. “Kusalā vipākadhammā cā”ti idaṃ sekkhaputhujjanasantāne abhiññācetanā idhādhippetā, na itarāti katvā vuttaṃ. Tena yathāvuttaabhiññācetanāpi paṭisandhiviññāṇassa paccayo siyā kusalasabhāvattā, vipākadhammattā vā tadaññakusalākusalacetanā viyāti dasseti. Tayidaṃ lokuttarakusalāya anekantikaṃ. Na hi sā paṭisandhiviññāṇassa paccayo. Atha vipākadāyinīti vucceyya, evampi ahosikammena anekantikaṃ. Na hi tassā vipākuppādanaṃ atthīti āha “na vipākuppādanena kusalatā vipākadhammatā cā”ti. Kevalañhi yā aññesaṃ vipākadhammānaṃ sabyāpārā saussāhā pavatti, tadākārāvassā appahīnakilese santāne pavattīti vipākadhammatā, anavajjaṭṭhena kusalatā ca vuttā. Evampi yadi vipākadhammā abhiññācetanā, kathaṃ avipākāti? Asambhavatoti taṃ [M 0.0101] asambhavaṃ dassetuṃ “sā panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Abhiññācetanā hi yadi vipākaṃ uppādeyya, sabhūmikaṃ vā uppādeyya aññabhūmikaṃ vā. Tattha aññabhūmikassa tāva uppādanaṃ ayuttaṃ paccayābhāvato, tathā adassanato ca. Tenāha “na hī”tiādi. Sabhūmikaṃ navattabbārammaṇaṃ vā uppādeyya parittādiārammaṇaṃ vā, tesu attano kammasamānārammaṇatāya rūpāvacaravipākassa dassitattā, parittādiārammaṇattā ca abhiññācetanāya navattabbārammaṇaṃ na uppādeyya. Tathā ekantanavattabbārammaṇattā rūpāvacaravipākassa parittādiārammaṇañca na uppādeyyāti ayamasambhavo. Tenāha “attanā sadisārammaṇañcā”tiādi. Tattha tiṭṭhānikanti paṭisandhibhavaṅgacutivasena ṭhānattayavantaṃ. “Pathavīkasiṇaṃ āpokasiṇa”ntiādinā kusalena abhinnaṃ katvā vipākassa ārammaṇaṃ desitanti āha “cittuppādakaṇḍe…pe… vuttattā”ti. “Rūpāvacaratikacatukkajjhānāni kusalato ca vipākato ca kiriyato ca catutthassa jhānassa vipāko ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ ime dhammā navattabbā “parittārammaṇā”tipi ‘mahaggatārammaṇā’tipi ‘appamāṇārammaṇā’tipī”ti vacanato rūpāvacaravipāko ekantanavattabbārammaṇoti āha “na ca rūpāvacaravipāko parittādiārammaṇo atthī”ti. Svāyamasambhavo parittādiārammaṇāya abhiññācetanāya vipākābhāvaṃ sādheti, na navattabbārammaṇāya[V 0.0099]. Navattabbārammaṇāpi hi sā atthīti na byāpīti vipākānuppādane tassā aññaṃ kāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ “kasiṇesu cā”tiādimāha. Samādhivijambhanabhūtā abhiññā samādhissa ānisaṃsamattanti “samādhiphalasadisā”ti vuttaṃ. Tassa tassa adhiṭṭhānavikubbanadibbasaddasavanādikassa yadicchitassa kiccassa nipphādanamattaṃ pana abhiññācetanā, na kālantaraphalā, diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ viya nāpi vipākaphalā, atha kho yathāvuttaānisaṃsaphalā daṭṭhabbā.

'Grasping of bodily and verbal formations' refers to the summary statement. 'Grasping of bodily and verbal volitions' refers to the detailed explanation. 'Of consciousness' means of rebirth-linking consciousness. It is indeed a condition for both the conascent and the immediately proximate. The statement 'wholesome and having a resultant nature' is said here with reference to the volition of direct knowledge in the continuity of a trainee or a worldling, not any other. He shows that thereby the aforesaid volition of direct knowledge could be a condition for rebirth-linking consciousness, because of its wholesome nature or its resultant nature, just like other wholesome and unwholesome volitions. This is inconclusive with regard to supramundane wholesome volition, for that is not a condition for rebirth-linking consciousness. If it be said that it gives a result, even so it is inconclusive with regard to defunct kamma, for it does not produce a result. Thus he says: 'It is not wholesome nor of a resultant nature by way of producing a result.' For only when there is an active, energetic occurrence of other states with a resultant nature, and it occurs in that manner in a continuity where defilements are not abandoned, is it called 'of a resultant nature'; and it is called 'wholesome' in the sense of being blameless. Even so, if the volition of direct knowledge has a resultant nature, how is it without result? Because of impossibility. To show that impossibility, it is said 'But that...,' etc. For if the volition of direct knowledge were to produce a result, it would produce one either on its own plane or on another plane. Therein, the production of one on another plane is, in the first place, unsuitable due to the absence of a condition and also because it is not seen. Therefore he says 'For not...,' etc. It would produce a result with either a 'not-to-be-stated' object or with a limited, etc., object. Among these, because the form-sphere resultant is shown to have an object the same as its kamma, and because the volition of direct knowledge has a limited, etc., object, it would not produce a 'not-to-be-stated' object. Likewise, because the form-sphere resultant has an object that is exclusively 'not-to-be-stated,' it would not produce a limited, etc., object. This is the impossibility. Therefore he says 'And with an object similar to its own...,' etc. Therein, 'three-phased' means having three stations, by way of rebirth-linking, life-continuum, and decease. Because the object of the resultant is taught as being inseparable from the wholesome, by way of 'earth kasiṇa, water kasiṇa,' etc., he says: 'in the chapter on the arising of consciousness...pe... because it is stated.' From the statement, 'The four form-sphere jhānas—wholesome, resultant, and functional; the resultant of the fourth jhāna, the base of infinite space, the base of nothingness—these states are not to be spoken of as “with a limited object,” or “with a sublime object,” or “with an immeasurable object,”' the form-sphere resultant has an object that is exclusively 'not-to-be-stated.' Therefore he says: 'And there is no form-sphere resultant with a limited, etc., object.' This impossibility establishes the absence of a result for the volition of direct knowledge that has a limited, etc., object, but not for one that has a 'not-to-be-stated' object. Since it can also have a 'not-to-be-stated' object, this reasoning is not comprehensive. To show another reason for its non-production of a result, he says 'And in the kasiṇas...,' etc. Direct knowledge, being an efflorescence of concentration, is merely a benefit of concentration; thus it is called 'similar to the fruit of concentration.' But the volition of direct knowledge is merely the accomplishment of whatever desired task, such as determination, transformation, hearing divine sounds, etc. It does not have a fruit at a later time, like what is to be experienced in this very life, nor is it a resultant fruit; rather, it should be seen as having the aforesaid benefits as its fruit.

Keci pana “samānabhūmikato āsevanalābhena balavantāni jhānānīti tāni vipākaṃ denti samāpattibhāvato, abhiññā pana satipi jhānabhāve tadabhāvato tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ārammaṇe āgantukāvāti dubbalā, tasmā vipākaṃ na detī”ti vadanti. Taṃ akāraṇaṃ punappunaṃ parikammavasena abhiññāyapi vasībhāvasabbhāvato. Yaṃ pana vadanti “pādakajjhāne attanā samānasabhāvehi javanehi laddhāsevane sammadeva vasībhāvappatte [M 0.0102] parisuddhatādiaṭṭhaṅgasamannāgamena sātisaye jāte abhiññā nibbattanti, tāsañca catutthajjhānikattā catutthajjhānabhūmiko eva vipāko nibbatteyya, so ca yathāvuttaguṇena balavatā pādakajjhāneneva katokāsena sijjhatīti anokāsatāya abhiññā na vipākaṃ detī”ti. Tampi akāraṇaṃ avipākabhāvato tāsaṃ. Sati hi vipākadāyibhāve vipākassa anokāsacodanā yuttā, avipākatā ca tāsaṃ vuttanayā eva.

Some, however, say: 'Because the jhānas are strong from gaining repetition on the same plane, they give a result on account of being attainments. But the direct knowledges, though they are jhānic states, are weak because they are adventitious in regard to this or that object; therefore they do not give a result.' That is not a valid reason, because mastery of the direct knowledges also exists by way of repeated preliminary work. But as to what they say: 'Direct knowledges arise when the base jhāna, in which repetition has been gained by means of impulsions of the same nature as itself, has been fully mastered and has become excellent through possessing the eight factors such as purity, etc. And since they belong to the fourth jhāna, a result on the plane of the fourth jhāna would be produced. Since that result is accomplished by the powerful base jhāna with the aforesaid qualities, which has already created the opportunity, the direct knowledges do not give a result for lack of an opportunity.' That too is not a valid reason, because they are of a nature that does not produce a result. For if they had the nature of giving a result, the charge of 'no opportunity for a result' would be proper. But their nature of not producing a result is just as was stated.

Na hotīti viññāṇassa paccayo na hotīti. Uddhaccacetanāpi abhiññācetanāto nibbisesena vuttāti maññamāno “vipāke”ti ca vacanaṃ na vipākārahatāmattavācako, atha kho vipākasabbhāvavācakoti āha “vicāretabba”nti. Tathā ca vuttaṃ “na hi ‘vipāke’ti vacanaṃ vipākadhammavacanaṃ viya vipākārahataṃ vadatī”ti. Tattha yaṃ vicāretabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. Idaṃ panettha sanniṭṭhānaṃ – yasmā uddhaccacetanā pavattivipākameva deti, na paṭisandhivipākaṃ, tasmā tassā pavattivipākassa vasena vibhaṅge vipāko uddhaṭo. Ubhayavipākadāyikāya pana cetanāya nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayo vuccatīti tadabhāvato paṭṭhāne tassā so na vutto. Yaṃ pana aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “viññāṇassa paccayabhāve apanetabbā”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 226 saṅkhārapadaniddesa) vuttaṃ, taṃ paṭisandhiviññāṇameva sandhāya vuttaṃ. “Evaṃ uddhaccacetanāpi [V 0.0100] na hotī”ti idampi viññāṇassa paccayatābhāvamattaṃ gahetvā vuttaṃ. Evañhettha aññamaññaṃ pāḷiyā aṭṭhakathāya ca avirodho daṭṭhabbo.

It is not a condition for consciousness, it is said. Thinking that the volition of restlessness is stated without distinction from the volition of direct knowledge, and that the word 'in the result' does not merely indicate suitability for a result but actually indicates the existence of a result, he says 'it should be investigated.' And so it is said: 'For the word "in the result" does not speak of what is suitable for a result in the way the term "resultant state" does.' Therein, what is to be investigated has already been stated below. This is the conclusion here: because the volition of restlessness gives only a result in the course of life, not a rebirth-linking result, its result is therefore extracted in the Vibhaṅga on the basis of that result in the course of life. But for a volition that gives both kinds of results, a different-moment kamma-condition is spoken of; therefore, because this is absent for that volition, it is not mentioned in the Paṭṭhāna. As for what is stated in the commentary, 'it should be removed from being a condition for consciousness,' this is said with reference only to rebirth-linking consciousness. This statement, 'Thus, the volition of restlessness also is not,' is also said simply by taking up the absence of its being a condition for consciousness. Thus, the absence of contradiction between the Pāli text and the commentary should be seen here.

Etthāti uddhaccacetanāya vipākadāne. Amataggapatheti evaṃnāmake pakaraṇe. “Puthujjanasantāne akusalā dassanena pahātabbā, sekkhasantāne bhāvanāya pahātabbā”ti imassa atthassa vuttattā “puthujjanānaṃ panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Na vuccantī”ti iminā puthujjane pavattabahiddhāsaṃyojanādīnaṃ bhāvanāya pahātabbapariyāyābhāvaṃ dasseti. “Yadi vucceyyu”ntiādinā tamevatthaṃ yuttito ca āgamato ca vibhāveti. Tattha kesañcīti sakabhaṇḍe chandarāgādīnaṃ. Kecīti sakkāyadiṭṭhiādayo. Kadācīti atītādike kismiñci kāle. Cattattātiādi [M 0.0103] pariyāyavacanaṃ. Upanissāyāti upanissayapaccaye katvā.

'Here' means in the giving of a result by the volition of restlessness. 'In the Amataggapatha' means in the treatise of that name. Because the meaning of the statement, 'In the mental continuum of a worldling, unwholesome states are to be abandoned by vision; in the mental continuum of a trainee, they are to be abandoned by development,' has been stated, the passage beginning 'But for worldlings...' is said. By 'they are not spoken of,' he shows the absence of a way of abandoning by development the external fetters, etc., that occur in a worldling. With the phrase beginning 'If they were spoken of...,' he clarifies that same meaning by means of reasoning and scripture. Therein, 'of some' refers to sensual desire, etc., for one's own belongings. 'Some' refers to identity view and so on. 'Sometimes' means at some time in the past, etc. The phrase beginning 'having been abandoned' is a synonym. 'Having depended on' means having made it a decisive support condition.

Itaresanti nadassanenapahātabbānaṃ. Na ca na hontīti sambandho. Evañca katvāti yathāvuttapāḷiyaṃ uddhaccaggahaṇena uddhaccasahagatacittuppādo gahito, na yattha katthaci uddhaccanti evamatthe sati. Tanti diṭṭhiṃ. “Atītādibhāvena navattabbatte”ti kasmā vuttaṃ, nanu anāgatā eva pahātabbāti? Na, uppajjanārahā nippariyāyena anāgatā nāma, pahātabbā pana na uppajjanārahāti tesaṃ atītādibhāvena navattabbatā vuttā. Dassanaṃ apekkhitvāti bhāvitaṃ dassanamaggaṃ upanidhāya. Sahāyavirahāti dassanapahātabbasaṅkhātasahakārikāraṇābhāvato. Vipākaṃ na janayantīti sakalakilesaparikkhaye viya ekaccaparikkhayepi tannimittaṃ taṃ ekaccaṃ kammaṃ na vipaccatīti adhippāyo. Vipāko vibhaṅge vuttoti paṭisandhipavattibhedaṃ duvidhampi vipākaṃ sandhāyāha.

'Of others' means of those not to be abandoned by vision. The connection is 'and they are not non-existent.' 'And having done so' means: this being the meaning, by the taking up of restlessness in the aforesaid Pāli text, a consciousness-moment accompanied by restlessness is taken, not restlessness wherever it may occur. 'That' means the view. Why is it said, 'because they are not to be spoken of in terms of past, etc.,' when surely what is to be abandoned is future? No, what is fit to arise is called 'future' in a strict sense, but what is to be abandoned is not fit to arise; hence their not being spoken of in terms of past, etc., is stated. 'Having regard to vision' means by reference to the developed path of vision. 'Due to the absence of an assistant' means because of the absence of the contributory cause designated as 'what is to be abandoned by vision.' 'They do not generate a result'—the intention is that just as in the complete destruction of all defilements, so too in the partial destruction of some, that particular kamma, having that as its cause, does not mature. 'The result is stated in the Vibhaṅga'—he says this with reference to both kinds of result, distinguished as rebirth-linking and in the course of life.

Akusalānanti yathāvuttavisesānaṃ puthujjanasantāne akusalānaṃ. Appahātabbānanti appahātabbasabhāvānaṃ kusalādīnaṃ. Appahātabbaviruddhasabhāvatā sāvajjatā. “Evampī”tiādi dosantaradassanaṃ. Tena yadipi tesaṃ akusalānaṃ imasmiṃ tike tatiyapadasaṅgaho na siyā, navattabbatā pana āpajjatīti dīpeti. Sabbena sabbaṃ dhammavasena asaṅgahitassa tikadukesu navattabbatāpattīti āha “nāpajjatī”ti. Idāni taṃ navattabbatānāpajjanaṃ “cittuppādakaṇḍe”tiādinā kāraṇato, nidassanato ca vibhāveti. Yatthāti yasmiṃ tike. Niyogatoti niyamato ekantato. Tesanti padattayasaṅgahitadhammānaṃ. Yathāvuttapadesu viyāti yathāvuttesu [V 0.0101] paṭhamādīsu tīsu padesu. Yathā bhinditabbā cittuppādā, itare ca yathārahaṃ rāsittayavasena bhinditvā bhajāpitā taṃtaṃkoṭṭhāsato katā, evaṃ.
