Tatthāpīti catutthakoṭṭhāsepi. Bhajāpetabbeti navattabbabhāvaṃ bhajāpetabbe. Tadabhāvāti tassa catutthakoṭṭhāsassa abhāvā. Tathāti navattabbabhāvena.

'Of unwholesome states' means of the unwholesome states with the aforesaid characteristics in the mental continuum of a worldling. 'Of those not to be abandoned' means of those with a nature not to be abandoned, such as wholesome states, etc. Blameworthiness is the nature of being opposed to what is not to be abandoned. The passage beginning 'Even so...' shows another fault. He thereby indicates that even if there is no inclusion of those unwholesome states in the third term of this triad, the state of being unclassifiable still results. He says 'it does not result' because what is not included in every way by way of states in the triads and dyads results in being unclassifiable. Now, with the passage beginning 'in the chapter on consciousness-moments,' he clarifies that non-resulting in being unclassifiable by way of reason and example. 'Where' means in which triad. 'By necessity' means by rule, definitely. 'Of them' means of the states included in the three terms. 'As in the aforesaid sections' means as in the aforesaid three sections, the first, etc. Just as the consciousness-moments are to be analyzed, and the others, having been analyzed as appropriate into three groups, are assigned to their respective portions, so too here. 'Even there' means in the fourth portion. 'Are to be assigned' means they are to be assigned to the state of being unclassifiable. 'Due to its absence' means due to the absence of that fourth portion. 'Thus' means by way of being unclassifiable.

Uppannattike atītā, idha yathāvuttaakusalā na vuttā, apekkhitabbabhāvenārahitāpi taṃsabhāvānativattanato tathā vuccantīti navattabbatāpattidosaṃ pariharanto tassa udāharaṇaṃ tāva dassetuṃ “atha [M 0.0104] vā yathā sappaṭighehī”tiādimāha. Taṃsabhāvo cettha sāvajjatāvisiṭṭho dassanapahātabbabhāvābhāvo. “Evañca satī”tiādinā imasmiṃ pakkhe laddhaguṇaṃ dasseti. Bhāvanāya pahātabbānanti pariyāyena nippariyāyena ca bhāvanāya pahātabbānaṃ, tattha purimānaṃ amukhyasabhāvattā, pacchimānaṃ avipākattā nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayatā na vuttāti adhippāyo. Yathā ca bhāvanāya pahātabbānaṃ nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayabhāvo natthi, evaṃ dassanena pahātabbānaṃ vasena tesaṃ paccayalābhopi natthīti dassento “na ca…pe… vuttā”ti vatvā tattha kāraṇamāha “ye hi…pe… pavattantī”ti. Tattha na te dassanato uddhaṃ pavattantīti ye dassanena pahātabbapaccayā kilesā, te dassanena pahātabbapakkhikā evāti tesaṃ bhāvanāya pahātabbapariyāyo eva natthi, kathaṃ tesaṃ vasena dassanena pahātabbā bhāvanāya pahātabbānaṃ kenaci paccayena paccayoti vucceyyāti attho. Atha vā ye puthujjanasantāne na dassanena pahātabbā, na te paramatthato bhāvanāya pahātabbā. Ye pana te sekkhasantāne, na tesaṃ paccayabhūtā dassanena pahātabbā atthīti evampi dassanena pahātabbā bhāvanāya pahātabbānaṃ kenaci paccayena paccayoti na vuttāti veditabbaṃ. Yadi dassanenapahātabbapaccayā kilesā dassanapakkhikā, tappaccayaṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ dassanena pahātabbaṃ siyāti kathaṃ tassa ekantabhāvanāya pahātabbatā vuttāti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “dassanena pahātabbapaccayassā”tiādi. Tasmāti yasmā sarāgavītarāgasantānesu sahāyavekallena kammassa vipākāvipākadhammatā viya puthujjanasekkhasantānesu uddhaccasahagatassa vuttanayena savipākāvipākatā siddhā, tasmā. Tassāti uddhaccasahagatassa. Tādisassevāti uddhaccasahagatabhāvena ekasabhāvassa.

In the triad of the arisen, the past states are included. Here, the aforesaid unwholesome states are not mentioned. To avoid the fault of resulting in being unclassifiable—because they are called thus for not transcending their own nature even though they are devoid of a nature to be regarded—he first shows an example for this, saying: 'Or just as with those states accompanied by resistance...' And here their nature is the absence of a state to be abandoned by vision, which is characterized by blameworthiness. With the passage beginning 'And this being so...,' he shows the advantage gained in this alternative. 'Of those to be abandoned by development' means of those to be abandoned by development both indirectly and directly. The intention is that the different-moment kamma-conditionality is not stated because, among them, the former have a non-primary nature and the latter are not resultants. And just as there is no different-moment kamma-conditionality for those to be abandoned by development, so too, to show that there is no acquisition of a condition for them by way of those to be abandoned by vision, he says, 'And not... are stated,' and then gives the reason: 'For those... proceed.' Here, 'they do not proceed beyond them' means: since the defilements that are conditions to be abandoned by vision belong only to the side of what is to be abandoned by vision, there is no indirect way of abandoning them by development. How, then, could it be said that those to be abandoned by vision are a condition in some way for those to be abandoned by development? This is the meaning. Alternatively, those states in the mental continuum of a worldling that are not to be abandoned by vision are not, in the ultimate sense, to be abandoned by development. As for those in the mental continuum of a trainee, there are no states to be abandoned by vision that are their conditions. Thus too it should be understood that states to be abandoned by vision are not stated to be a condition in any way for states to be abandoned by development. To address the objection: 'If the defilements conditioned by what is to be abandoned by vision belong to the side of vision, then restlessness associated with that condition would be something to be abandoned by vision. How then is it stated to be exclusively abandoned by development?' he says the passage beginning 'Of a condition to be abandoned by vision...' 'Therefore' means: because, just as kamma has the nature of giving or not giving a result depending on the absence of an assistant in the mental continuums of one with lust and one without lust, so too, in the mental continuums of a worldling and a trainee, it is established in the way stated that what is accompanied by restlessness has a result and is without a result; therefore... 'Of that' means of what is accompanied by restlessness. 'Of just such a one' means of one having a single nature by way of being accompanied by restlessness.

Ettha ca yaṃ “na bhāvanāya pahātabbampi atthi uddhaccasahagata”ntiādi amataggapathe vuttaṃ, taṃ akāraṇaṃ, kasmā? Tassa ekantena bhāvanāya pahātabbattā. Yathāha [V 0.0102] “katame dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbā? Uddhaccasahagato cittuppādo”ti (dha. sa. 1583). Yadi hi uddhaccasahagataṃ na bhāvanāya pahātabbampi abhavissa, yathā atītārammaṇattike “niyogā anāgatārammaṇā natthī”ti [M 0.0105] vatvā “kāmāvacarakusalassa vipākato dasa cittuppādā”tiādinā puna vibhajitvā vuttaṃ, evamidhāpi “katame dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbā? Niyogā bhāvanāya pahātabbā natthī”ti vatvā “uddhaccasahagato cittuppādo siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbo, siyā na vattabbo ‘dassanena pahātabbo’tipi ‘bhāvanāya pahātabbo’tipī”tiādi vattabbaṃ siyā, na ca tathā vuttaṃ. Yā ca tamatthaṃ paṭipādentena “yadi vucceyyu”ntiādinā yutti vuttā, sāpi ayutti. Kasmā? Dassanena pahātabbārammaṇānaṃ rāgadiṭṭhivicikicchuddhaccānaṃ dassanena pahātabbabhāvasseva icchitattā.

And here, the statement in the Amataggapatha beginning, 'There is that which is accompanied by restlessness that is not to be abandoned by development,' is groundless. Why? Because it is to be abandoned exclusively by development. As it is said: 'What states are to be abandoned by development? A state of consciousness accompanied by restlessness' (Dhs §1583). For if there were something accompanied by restlessness that is not to be abandoned by development, then just as in the triad on past objects, after saying, 'By necessity there are no future objects,' it is stated with further analysis, 'From the result of wholesome sense-sphere kamma, ten states of consciousness...,' so too here, after saying, 'What states are to be abandoned by development? By necessity there are none to be abandoned by development,' it would have been necessary to say: 'A state of consciousness accompanied by restlessness might be one to be abandoned by development, or it might be one not to be spoken of as "to be abandoned by vision" or "to be abandoned by development."' But it was not stated thus. And the reasoning given by the one who established that meaning, beginning 'If it were said...,' is also unsound. Why? Because it is intended that lust, view, doubt, and restlessness, which have as their objects what is to be abandoned by vision, are themselves to be abandoned by vision.

Yañca “uddhaccaṃ uppajjatī”ti uddhaccasahagatacittuppādo vuttoti dassetuṃ adhipatipaccayaniddese uddhaccassa anuddharaṇaṃ kāraṇabhāvena vuttaṃ, tampi akāraṇaṃ aññathāpi sāvasesapāṭhadassanato. Tathā hi “atīto dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa, anāgato dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 2.18.2) etesaṃ vibhaṅge cetopariyañāṇaggahaṇaṃ katvā “paccuppanno dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassā”ti imassa vibhaṅge labbhamānampi cetopariyañāṇaggahaṇaṃ na kataṃ.

And as to the point that, in order to show that the statement 'restlessness arises' refers to the arising of consciousness accompanied by restlessness, the non-mention of restlessness is stated as a reason in the exposition of the dominance condition—that too is not a valid reason, as it is seen otherwise from a text with an omission. For instance, in the analysis of 'a past phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon, and a future phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon, by way of object condition,' the inclusion of the knowledge of others' minds has been made; but in the analysis of 'a present phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon,' though the inclusion of the knowledge of others' minds is obtainable, it is not made.

Sahāyabhāvo ca dassanena pahātabbānaṃ bhāvanāya pahātabbassa vipākadānaṃ pati vicāretabbo. Kiṃ avijjādi viya dānādīnaṃ uppattiyā eva vikuppādanasamatthatāpādanena dassanena pahātabbā bhāvanāya pahātabbānaṃ sahakārikāraṇaṃ honti, udāhu kileso viya kammassa paṭisandhidāne satīti, kiñcettha – yadi purimanayo, sotāpannādisekkhasantāne bhāvanāya pahātabbassa kiriyabhāvo āpajjati, sahāyavekallena avipākasabhāvatāya āpāditattā khīṇataṇhāvijjāmāne santāne dānādi viya. Atha dutiyo, bhāvanāya pahātabbābhimatassāpi dassanena pahātabbabhāvo āpajjati, paṭisandhidāne sati apāyagamanīyasabhāvānativattanato. Yaṃ panettha vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva, tasmā pāḷiyā aṭṭhakathāya [M 0.0106] ca avirujjhanavasenettha atthavinicchayo vuttanayeneva veditabbo.

The state of association should be considered in relation to the giving of results, with regard to what is to be abandoned by vision and what is to be abandoned by development. Is it that things to be abandoned by vision become assisting causes for things to be abandoned by development—just as ignorance and so on are for acts of giving and so on—by producing the capacity to disrupt their very arising? Or is it that, like a defilement for kamma, they are present when rebirth-linking is given? And here, if the first method is accepted, then in the continuum of a stream-enterer and other learners, what is to be abandoned by development becomes merely functional, since its nature of not yielding a result is brought about by the deficiency of its associate, just like giving and so on in the continuum of one whose craving, ignorance, and conceit are destroyed. But if the second is accepted, then even what is considered to be abandoned by development becomes something to be abandoned by vision, because when rebirth-linking occurs, its nature of leading to the plane of misery is not transcended. What should be said about this has already been stated above. Therefore, the determination of the meaning here should be understood in the way explained, in a manner that does not conflict with the Pāli text and the Commentary.

Sāti [V 0.0103] uddhaccacetanā. Viññāṇapaccayabhāveti sampuṇṇavipākaviññāṇapaccayabhāve. Kāraṇaṃ dassentoti avikalaphaluppādanādhikāre tadabhāvato yadipi uddhaccacetanā viññāṇassa paccayabhāve apanetabbā, avijjāya pana paccayuppannabhāve gahetabbāti imaṃ kāraṇaṃ dassento. Sabbāpīti vīsatipi. Tenāha “ekavīsatīti vattabba”nti. Tanti yena kāraṇena saṅkhāraggahaṇena abhiññācetanāya aggahaṇaṃ, taṃ kāraṇaṃ. Itarāvacanassāpīti uddhaccacetanāvacanassāpi. Kiṃ pana taṃ? Viññāṇassa paccayabhāvābhāvo eva. Bhedābhāvāti kāyavacīsaṅkhāravasena vibhāgābhāvato. Saṃyogoti tikantarapadavasena saṃyojanaṃ, tathā saṅgahoti attho.

That is, the volition associated with restlessness. ‘In the state of being a condition for consciousness’ means: in the state of being a condition for consciousness that is a full result. ‘Showing the reason’ means: showing this reason, namely, that although the volition associated with restlessness should be excluded from being a condition for consciousness because it is absent from the section on the production of the complete fruit, it should still be included in the state of being conditioned by ignorance. ‘All’ means: the twenty. Therefore he said: ‘“Twenty-one” should be said.’ ‘The principle’ means: the reason why the volition of direct knowledge is not included by the inclusion of formations. ‘Of the statement of the other’ means: of the statement of the volition associated with restlessness. But what is that? It is precisely the absence of the state of being a condition for consciousness. ‘Because of the absence of distinction’ means: because of the absence of division into bodily and verbal formations. ‘Connection’ means: a connection by way of the terms of another triad; the meaning is that it is thus an inclusion.

Sukhasaññāya gahaṇaṃ assādananti adhippāyenāha “sukhasaññāya…pe… dassetī”ti. “Sukhasaññāyā”ti ca idaṃ karaṇatthe karaṇavacanaṃ. Vipallāso hi dukkhe sukhasaññā. Yaṃ pana aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “aññāṇenā”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ hetumhi karaṇavacanaṃ vipallāsassādanānaṃ avijjāya hetubhāvadassanato. “Ratho setaparikkhāro”tiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 5.4) parivāratthopi parikkhārasaddo hotīti vuttaṃ “taṇhāya parivāre”ti. Taṇhāparivāreti ca taṇhāya kiccasādhanena saṅkhārānaṃ sahakārikāraṇabhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Parikkhāraṭṭho saṅkhāraṭṭho viya bhūsanaṭṭho hotīti dassento “saṅkhate alaṅkate”ti āha. Parikkharoti yathā phaladānasamatthā honti, tathā saṅkharoti. Amaraṇatthāti amatatthā, nibbānatthāti attho. Dukkarakiriyāti pañcātapatappanādidukkaracariyā. Devabhāvāya tapo devabhāvatthaṃ tapo. Māretīti maro hetuatthaṃ antonītaṃ katvā. Amaṅgalampi maṅgalapariyāyena voharanti maṅgalikāti vuttaṃ “diṭṭhe adiṭṭhasaddo viyā”ti yathā “asive sivā”ti.

With the intention that 'gratification is the grasping by means of the perception of pleasure,' he says: 'by the perception of pleasure... he shows.' And the phrase 'by the perception of pleasure' is an instrumental in the sense of instrument. For perversion is the perception of pleasure in what is suffering. As for what is said in the commentary, 'by ignorance,' that is an instrumental in the sense of cause, showing that ignorance is the cause of the gratifications that are perversions. In such phrases as 'a chariot with white equipment,' the word 'equipment' (parikkhāra) also has the meaning 'retinue'; hence it is said 'in the retinue of craving.' And 'in the retinue of craving' is said with reference to the formations' state of being an assisting cause in accomplishing the function of craving. Showing that the meaning of 'equipment,' like the meaning of 'formation,' is 'ornament,' he says 'prepared, adorned.' 'He equips' means: he prepares them so that they become capable of giving fruit. 'For the purpose of non-death' means: for the purpose of the deathless, that is, for the purpose of Nibbāna. 'Action hard to perform' means: difficult practices such as the fivefold austerity of self-mortification. 'Austerity for divine existence' means: austerity for the purpose of divine existence. 'He causes to die' (māreti), thus he is Death (maro); this is by taking the meaning of cause as implicit. Because they are fond of auspicious things, they speak of what is inauspicious using an auspicious term; it is said, 'like the word “unseen” for what is seen,' just as 'auspicious' is used for what is inauspicious.

Papātaṃ patanadukkhasadisanti katvā vuttaṃ “jātiādipapātadukkha”nti. Indaduddabrahmakūṭasaññitapabbatasikharappapāto marupapāto. Taṃ puññaphalaṃ attho payojanaṃ etassāti tadattho.

Having considered a precipice to be similar to the suffering of falling, it is said, 'the suffering of the precipice of birth, etc.' A precipice from the peak of a mountain known as Inda, Duddabrahma, or Kūṭa is a desert precipice. ‘Having that as its purpose’ means: that fruit of merit is its meaning and its aim.

Paribbājikāya [M 0.0107] taruṇiyā. Asavaso aserivihārī. Kilesāsucipaggharaṇena paṇḍitehi jigucchanīyaṃ. Rāgādipariḷāhena, kaṭukavipākatāya ca dukkhaṃ. Ārabhati karoti. Sabhayassāpi pisācanagarassa kāmaguṇasamiddhiyā sukhavipallāsahetubhāvo viyāti yojanā. Bhinnajātiyena avomissatā nirantaratā. Jarāya maraṇena ca aññathattaṃ vipariṇāmo.

Of a female wanderer: of a young one. Not under one's control: not living independently. Repulsive to the wise because of the oozing of the impurity of the defilements. Suffering because of the torment of lust, etc., and because of its bitter result. He undertakes: he does. The construction is: just as the wealth of sensual pleasures in a fearsome city of goblins is a cause for the perversion of happiness. By being of a different kind, non-intermixture means continuity. Otherness by aging and death is change.

“Na [V 0.0104] tāvāhaṃ pāpima parinibbāyissāmī”ti vacanato “tāta ehi, tāva idaṃ rajjaṃ paṭipajjāhī”tiādīsu yadipi parimāṇaniyamanakamapadapūraṇamattādīsupi tāva-saddo dissati, idha pana vakkhamānattāpekkho adhippetoti vuttaṃ “tāvāti vattabbantarāpekkho nipāto”ti. Avijjāpaccayā pana…pe… dassetīti pubbenāparaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ avirujjhanamāha.

From the statement, 'Evil One, I will not attain final Nibbāna yet,' and in such phrases as, 'Come, dear one, for now undertake this kingdom,' although the word tāva is seen in the sense of mere measure, restriction, and filling a line of verse, here, however, it is intended as having regard to what will be said later. Thus it is said: '‘Tāva’ is a particle that has regard to something else that is to be said.' By the words 'But with ignorance as condition... he shows,' he states the non-conflict of the later with the earlier in the commentary.

Rāgādiassādanakālesūti rāgādīnaṃ assādanakālesu. “Rāgadiṭṭhisampayuttāyā”ti ettha rāgasampayuttāya tāva avijjāya yojanā hotu rāgassa assādanabhāvato, diṭṭhisampayuttāya pana kathanti āha “tadavippayuttā ca diṭṭhī…pe… veditabbā”ti. Taṃsampayuttasaṅkhārassāti rāgādisampayuttasaṅkhārassa. Avijjārammaṇāditanti avijjāya ārammaṇāditaṃ. Ādi-saddena ārammaṇādhipatiārammaṇūpanissayapakatūpanissaye, anantarādike ca paccaye saṅgaṇhāti. Anavijjārammaṇassāti na avijjārammaṇassa avijjaṃ anārabbha pavattassa. Ārammaṇādhipatianantarādipaccayavacanesūti ārammaṇādhipatiārammaṇūpanissayapaccayavacanesu avuttassa anavijjārammaṇassa, anantarādipaccayavacanesu avuttassa paṭhamajavanassa, dvīsupi vuttassa avijjārammaṇassa dutiyādijavanassāti yojetabbaṃ. Anantarapaccayalābhino anantarādinā, sahajātassa hetuādinā, asahajātassa upanissayādinā saṅkhārassa avijjā paccayo hotīti ayamattho “yaṃ kiñcī”tiādinā dassitoti veditabbaṃ. Samatikkamabhavapatthanāvasenāti avijjāsamatikkamatthāya arūpāvacarajjhānāni uppādentassa, avijjāsammūḷhattā arūpabhavasampattiyo patthetvā tāneva jhānāni nibbattentassāti puññābhisaṅkhāre vuttena nayena, vuttanayānusārenāti attho.

'At the times of enjoying lust, etc.' means: at the times of enjoying lust and so on. 'Of that which is associated with lust and views': here, let there first be the connection of ignorance with that which is associated with lust, because lust has the nature of gratification. But how is it with that which is associated with views? He says: 'And the view not dissociated from that... should be known.' 'Of the formation associated with that' means: of the formation associated with lust, etc. 'Having ignorance as object, etc.' means: the state of having ignorance as object, etc. By the word 'etc.,' he includes the object, object-predominance, object-decisive-support, natural decisive-support, and proximate, etc., conditions. 'Of that not having ignorance as object' means: of that which does not have ignorance as object, which occurs without taking ignorance as its object. It should be construed thus: in the statements about the object, object-predominance, and object-decisive-support conditions, what is unstated is that which does not have ignorance as object; in the statements about the proximate, etc., conditions, what is unstated is the first impulsion; in both, what is stated is that which has ignorance as object, namely, the second and subsequent impulsions. It should be understood that this meaning is shown by 'whatever,' etc.: that ignorance is a condition for a formation by way of proximity, etc., for one that obtains the proximity condition; by way of root, etc., for a coexistent one; and by way of decisive support, etc., for a non-coexistent one. 'By way of the desire to transcend existence' means: in the case of one who produces the formless-sphere jhānas for the purpose of transcending ignorance, or who, deluded by ignorance, desires the attainments of the formless existence and generates those same jhānas; the meaning is, in accordance with the method stated for meritorious formations.

Ekakāraṇavādo [M 0.0108] āpajjati yathā pakatiissarapajāpatipurisakālādivādā. Ekasmiṃyeva lokassa kāraṇabhūte sati tato sakalāya pavattiyā anavasesato, sabbadā ca pavattitabbaṃ apekkhitabbassa kāraṇantarassa abhāvato. Na cetaṃ atthi kameneva pavattiyā dassanato. Kāraṇantarāpekkhatāya pana ekakāraṇavādo apahato siyā ekassa ca anekasabhāvatābhāvā. Yattakā tato nibbattanti, sabbehi tehi samānasabhāveheva bhavitabbaṃ, na visadisehi, itarathā tassa ekabhāvo eva na siyāti imamatthamāha “sabbassa…pe… pattito cā”ti. Pārisesenāti ekato ekaṃ, ekato anekaṃ, anekato ekanti imesu tīsu pakāresu avijjamānesu anupalabbhamānesu pārisesañāyena. Anekato anekanti ekasmiṃ catutthe eva ca [V 0.0105] pakāre vijjamāne. Yadidaṃ “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā, phassapaccayā vedanā”tiādinā ekahetuphaladīpanaṃ, taṃ ettha desanāvilāsena, vineyyajjhāsayavasena vā dhammānaṃ padhānapākaṭāsādhāraṇabhāvavibhāvanatthanti ekahetuphaladīpanaṃ na nupapajjati upapajjatiyevāti dasseti “yasmā”tiādinā.

The theory of a single cause would follow, like the theories of primal nature, a supreme lord, a progenitor, a person, time, etc. If there were only a single cause of the world, then from that the entire process of existence would have to proceed without remainder, and it would have to proceed at all times, since there would be no other cause to be awaited. But this is not so, for the process is seen to occur sequentially. Moreover, the theory of a single cause is refuted by the dependence on other causes and because one thing cannot have a multiple nature. However many things are produced from it, they must all be of the same nature, not of different natures; otherwise its single nature would not exist. He states this meaning with the words 'of all... attainment.' 'By the method of residues' means: by the principle of residues, since these three alternatives—one from one, many from one, and one from many—do not exist and are not found, and since only the fourth alternative—many from many—exists. As to the illustration of a single cause and a single effect, as in 'with ignorance as condition, formations; with contact as condition, feeling,' etc., this is for the purpose of displaying the prominence, manifestness, and uniqueness of the phenomena, either for the sake of elegance in exposition or in accordance with the disposition of the person to be trained. He shows by 'because,' etc., that the illustration of a single cause and a single effect is not inappropriate but is indeed appropriate.

Yathāphassanti sukhavedanīyādicakkhusamphassāditaṃtaṃphassānurūpanti vuttaṃ hotīti dassento “sukhavedanīya”ntiādiṃ vatvā “vedanāvavatthānato”ti padassa atthaṃ dassetuṃ “samānesū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha samānesūti avisiṭṭhesu. Phassavasenāti sukhavedanīyādiphassavasena. Vipariyāyābhāvatoti byattayābhāvato. Na hi kadāci sukhavedanīyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca dukkhavedanā, dukkhādivedanīyaṃ vā phassaṃ paṭicca sukhavedanā uppajjati. Sukhādicakkhusamphassajādīnanti sukhādīnaṃ, cakkhusamphassajādīnañca vedanānaṃ. Oḷārikasukhumādīti ādi-saddena hīnapaṇītādisaṅgaho daṭṭhabbo. Tattha yaṃ upādāya yā vedanā “oḷārikā, hīnā”ti vā vuccati, na taṃyeva upādāya tassā kadācipi sukhumatā paṇītatā vā atthīti vuttaṃ “oḷārikasukhumādisaṅkarābhāvato”ti. Yathāvuttasamphassassāti sukhavedanīyādiphassassa. Sukhavedanīyaphassatoyeva sukhavedanā, na itaraphassato. Sukhavedanīyaphassato sukhavedanāva, na itaravedanā. Tathā sesesupīti ubhayapadaniyamavasena yathāphassaṃ vedanāvavatthānaṃ, yathāvedanaṃ phassavavatthānanti padadvayena kāraṇantarāsammissatā phalassa, phalantarāsammissatā [M 0.0109] ca kāraṇassa dassitā paṭhamapakkhe asaṃkiṇṇatāvavatthānanti katvā. Dutiyapakkhe pana paccayabhedabhinnena kāraṇavisesena phalaviseso, phalavisesena ca kāraṇaviseso nicchīyatīti ayamattho dassito sanniṭṭhānaṃ vavatthānanti katvā. Purimasmiñca pakkhe dhammānaṃ asaṅkarato vavatthānaṃ vuttaṃ, dutiyasmiñca yathāvavatthitabhāvajānananti ayametesaṃ viseso. Utuādayoti ādi-saddena cittavisamācārā pittavātādayopi saṅgayhanti. Ekasmiṃ dose kupite itarepi khobhaṃ gacchanti. Santesupi tesu semhapaṭikārena rogavūpasamato semho pākaṭoti attho.

To show that it is said that feeling is in conformity with the respective contact, such as pleasant-feeling-producing eye-contact, the text says 'pleasant-feeling-producing,' etc. Then, to explain the meaning of the phrase 'by the determination of feeling,' it says 'in the case of similar,' etc. Here, 'in the case of similar' means not distinct. 'By way of contact' means by way of pleasant-feeling-producing contact, etc. 'Because there is no reversal' means because there is no contrariety. For never does painful feeling arise in dependence on a pleasant-feeling-producing contact, nor does pleasant feeling arise in dependence on a painful-feeling-producing contact, etc. 'Of pleasant, etc., eye-contact-born, etc.' refers to pleasant, etc., feelings and those born of eye-contact, etc. 'Coarse and subtle, etc.': here, the word 'etc.' should be understood to include inferior and superior, etc. In this context, that in dependence on which a feeling is called 'coarse' or 'inferior' can never be that in dependence on which it has subtlety or superiority. This is stated as 'because of the absence of mixture of coarse, subtle, etc.' 'Of the aforesaid contact' refers to pleasant-feeling-producing contact, etc. From a pleasant-feeling-producing contact only pleasant feeling arises, not from another contact. From a pleasant-feeling-producing contact only pleasant feeling arises, not another feeling. Similarly in the remaining cases. Thus, by way of the rule for both terms, the determination of feeling is according to contact, and the determination of contact is according to feeling. By these two phrases, it is shown that the cause is unmixed with another effect, and the effect is unmixed with another cause. In the first alternative, this is taken as the determination of non-confusion. In the second alternative, however, a specific effect is ascertained by a specific cause differentiated by a difference of conditions, and a specific cause is ascertained by a specific effect; this meaning is shown by taking it as the determination as a conclusion. In the former alternative, the determination is stated as from the non-mixture of phenomena; in the second, as the knowledge of the state of being determined as it is—this is the difference between them. 'Season, etc.': here, the word 'etc.' includes mental misconduct, bile, wind, etc. When one humour is provoked, the others also become agitated. Even when they are present, because the disease is pacified by a remedy for phlegm, the phlegm is prominent—this is the meaning.

“Bhavo”ti vuttānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ kāraṇassa pakāraṇaṃ, kāraṇameva vā taṇhāti āha “taṇhāya saṅkhārakāraṇabhāvassa vuttattā”ti. Tassāpīti taṇhāyapi. Taṇhā hi kāmāsavo bhavāsavo ca. Kāmāsavabhavāsavā kāmupādānaṃ, diṭṭhāsavo itarupādānanti āha “caturupādānabhūtā [V 0.0106] kāmabhavadiṭṭhāsavā”ti. Te ca “upādānapaccayā bhavo”ti vacanato upādānañca, “taṇhāpaccayā upādāna”nti vacanato taṇhā ca saṅkhārassa kāraṇanti pākaṭā. Anassādanīyesu anekādīnavavokiṇṇesu saṅkhāresu assādānupassanā avijjāya vinā na hotīti dassento āha “assādānupassino…pe… dassitā hotī”ti. Khīṇāsavassa saṅkhārābhāvatoti byatirekenapi avijjāya saṅkhārakāraṇabhāvaṃ vibhāveti. Ekantena hi khīṇāsavova viddasu. Etena bālānaṃ eva sambhavato avijjāya asādhāraṇatā vuttāti dasseti. Vatthārammaṇādīni hi itaresampi sādhāraṇāni. Vatthārammaṇataṇhupādānādīni viya avijjāpi puññābhisaṅkhārādīnaṃ sādhāraṇakāraṇanti codanaṃ manasi katvā āha “puññabhavādī”tiādi. Tattha ādi-saddena apuññāneñjabhavā gahetabbā. Puññabhavoti puññābhisaṅkhārahetuko upapattibhavo. Esa nayo sesesu. Ettha ca kiccakaraṇaṭṭhānabhedena kiccavatī avijjā bhinditvā dassitā. Na hi yadavatthā avijjā puññābhisaṅkhārānaṃ upanissayo, tadavatthā eva itaresaṃ upanissayoti sakkā viññātuṃ. Ettha ca bhavādīnavappaṭicchādananti atthato puññābhisaṅkhārādīnaṃ taṃtaṃbhavasaṅkhātadukkhahetusabhāvānabhisamayanimittatā.

The principal cause of the formations called 'becoming,' or craving itself is the cause; thus it says, 'because it has been stated that craving is the cause of formations.' 'Of that too' means of craving too. For craving is the taint of sensuality and the taint of becoming. The taint of sensuality and the taint of becoming are sensual clinging, while the taint of views is the other kinds of clinging. Thus it says: 'the taints of sensuality, becoming, and views, which have become the four kinds of clinging.' And since it is said, 'With clinging as condition, becoming,' clinging, and since it is said, 'With craving as condition, clinging,' craving too are manifest as causes of formations. To show that contemplation of gratification in formations—which are ungratifying and replete with many dangers—does not occur without ignorance, it says: 'For one who contemplates gratification… it is shown.' 'Because of the absence of formations in one whose taints are destroyed': thus he explains that ignorance is the cause of formations also by way of contrast. For one whose taints are destroyed is exclusively the wise one. By this he shows that it is stated that ignorance is specific to fools since it arises only in them. For the base, object, etc., are common to others too. Having considered the objection that just as the base, object, craving, clinging, etc., are common causes of meritorious formations, etc., so too is ignorance, he says: 'meritorious becoming, etc.' Here, by the word 'etc.,' demeritorious and imperturbable becomings are to be taken. 'Meritorious becoming' is rebirth-becoming caused by meritorious formations. The same method applies to the rest. And here, ignorance, which has a function, is shown broken down by the difference in its sphere of action and its act. For it cannot be known that the state of ignorance that is a decisive support condition for meritorious formations is the very same state that is a decisive support for the others. And here, 'the concealing of the danger of becoming' means, in substance, the characteristic of not fully understanding the nature of meritorious formations, etc., as causes of the suffering called this or that becoming.

Ṭhānanti [M 0.0110] dharamānatā adhippetāti vuttaṃ “ṭhānaviruddhoti atthitāviruddho”ti. Ṭhānāviruddhā cakkhurūpādayo. “Purimacittañhī”tiādinā ṭhānaviruddho ca udāhaṭoti āha “na idaṃ ekantikaṃ siyā”ti. “Cakkhurūpādayo”tiādinā hi parato ṭhānāviruddhā udāharīyantīti. Purimasippādisikkhā hi pacchā pavattamānasippādikiriyānaṃ samodhānāsambhavā ṭhānavirodhoti yathāvuttamatthaṃ samatthetuṃ “na ca sippādīna”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tanti paṭisandhiādiṭhānaṃ. Idhāti ṭhānasabhāvakiccādiggahaṇe. Ādi-saddena ārammaṇabhūmisantānādiviruddhā gahetabbā, te ca anulomato gotrabhussa, gotrabhuto maggassa liṅgaparivattanādivasena ca pavattiyaṃ veditabbā. Namanaruppanavirodhā sabhāvaviruddho paccayoti yojanā. Tattha namanaruppananti arūparūpabhāvameva dasseti. Kammaṃ cetanāsabhāvaṃ, rūpaṃ ruppanasabhāvanti sabhāvaviruddhaṃ. Madhurambilarasādīti khīraṃ madhurarasaṃ pittupasamanaṃ madhuravipākasabhāvaṃ, dadhi ambilarasaṃ pittabrūhanaṃ kaṭukavipākasabhāvanti ato sabhāvavirodhā.

By 'place' (ṭhāna), presence is intended, so it is said: '"Opposed by place" means opposed by existence.' The eye and forms, etc., are not opposed by place. By the phrase 'for the preceding consciousness,' etc., what is opposed by place is also exemplified, so it says: 'This would not be absolute.' For by 'the eye and forms, etc.,' things not opposed by place are exemplified later. For prior training in skills, etc., is 'opposition by place' because of the impossibility of co-presence with subsequently occurring actions of skill, etc. To support the aforesaid meaning, it is said: 'and not of skills, etc.' Herein, 'that' refers to the place of rebirth-linking, etc. 'Here' refers to the grasping of the nature, function, etc., of place. By the word 'etc.', things opposed by object, basis, continuity, etc., should be taken. These are to be understood in the process of occurrence in conformity with change-of-lineage, from change-of-lineage to the path, and by way of change of gender, etc. The connection is: 'a condition opposed by nature' because of the opposition between bending (mind) and being afflicted (matter). Herein, 'bending and being afflicted' just shows the state of the formless and form. Kamma has the nature of volition, form has the nature of being afflicted; thus they are opposed by nature. 'Sweet and sour tastes, etc.': milk has a sweet taste, pacifies bile, and has a sweet resultant nature; curd has a sour taste, increases bile, and has a pungent resultant nature. Therefore, they are opposed by nature.

Dadhiādīnīti dadhipalālāni. Bhūtiṇakassāti bhūtiṇakanāmakassa osadhivisesassa. Avī [V 0.0107] nāma eḷakā, tā pana yebhuyyena rattalomakā hontīti vuttaṃ “rattā eḷakā”ti. Vipākānampi paccayabhāvato, avipākānampi paccayuppannabhāvato na vipākadhammavipākāpekkhā paccayapaccayuppannatāti vuttaṃ “vipākāyeva te ca nā”ti. Tenāha “tasmā”tiādi. Tadavipākānanti tassā avijjāya avipākabhūtānaṃ. Na na yujjati yujjati eva paccayuppannatāmattassa adhippetattā. Tadaviruddhānanti tāya avijjāya aviruddhānaṃ.

'Curd, etc.' means curd and straw. 'Of bhūtiṇaka' means of a specific medicinal herb named bhūtiṇaka. 'Avī' are sheep. Since they are for the most part red-fleeced, it is said 'red sheep.' Because even resultants have the nature of a condition, and because even non-resultants have the nature of being conditionally arisen, the state of being a condition and conditionally arisen is not dependent on a resultant dhamma and a resultant. Thus it is said: 'and they are not only resultants.' For that reason he says: 'Therefore,' etc. 'Of its non-resultants' means of those that have become non-resultants of that ignorance. 'It is not that it is not tenable; it is indeed tenable,' because only the state of being conditionally arisen is intended. 'Of those not opposed to it' means of those not opposed to that ignorance.

Pubbāpariyavavatthānanti kāyapavattigatijātiādīnaṃ yathārahaṃ pubbāparabhāvena pavatti, sā pana kenaci akaṭā akaṭavidhā paṭiniyatasabhāvāti dassetuṃ niyativādinā vuttanidassanaṃ āharanto “acchejjasuttāvutābhejjamaṇīnaṃ viyā”ti āha. Dutiyavikappe saṅgatīti adhiccasamuppādo yādicchikatā, yaṃ sandhāya “yadicchāya pavattanaṃ nivattanaṃ yadicchāyā”tiādi vuccati. Bhāvoti dhammānaṃ sabhāvasiddhitā, yaṃ sandhāya vadanti “kaṇṭakassa koṭitikhiṇabhāvaṃ, kapiṭṭhaphalassa vaṭṭabhāvaṃ, migapakkhīnaṃ vā vicittavaṇṇasaṇṭhānāditaṃ ko abhisaṅkharoti, kevalaṃ sabhāvasiddhovāyaṃ viseso”ti. Tenāha “sabbe sattā, sabbe pāṇā[M 0.0111], sabbe bhūtā, sabbe jīvā avasā abalā avīriyā niyatisaṅgatibhāvapariṇatā”ti (dī. ni. 1.168). Etehi vikappanehīti cutiādīsu sammūḷhatāya “satto maratī”tiādivikappanehi kāraṇabhūtehi. Akusalaṃ cittaṃ katvāti ayonisomanasikāraparibrūhanena cittaṃ akusalaṃ katvā.

'The determination of prior and posterior' is the occurrence of bodily process, destiny, birth, etc., in sequence as prior and posterior as is fit. To show that this is not made by anyone, not arranged by anyone, but has a fixed nature, the proponent of fatalism, adducing an example, says: 'like unbreakable gems strung on an uncuttable thread.' In the second alternative, 'combination' is fortuitous occurrence, spontaneity, with reference to which it is said: 'Occurrence by chance, cessation by chance,' etc. 'Nature' is the inherent establishment of things, with reference to which they say: 'The sharpness of a thorn's point, the roundness of a wood-apple fruit, or the variegated colours, shapes, etc., of beasts and birds—who fashions this? This distinction is simply established by its own nature.' Therefore he said: 'All beings, all living things, all creatures, all souls are without control, without strength, without energy, transformed by fate, combination, and nature' (DN 2, i 53). 'By these imaginings': by the causal imaginings such as 'a being dies,' due to delusion about death, etc. 'Having made the mind unwholesome': having made the mind unwholesome by the cultivation of unwise attention.

Suttādidhammanti suttageyyādipariyattidhammaṃ. Pariyattidhammañhi sammadeva jānanto paṭipattidhammaṃ paripūretvā paṭivedhadhamme patiṭṭhahati. Tanti taṃ jānanaṃ, nibbānābhisamayoti attho.

The Dhamma beginning with the Suttas means the Dhamma of the scriptures, such as suttas, geyyas, and so on. For one who rightly knows the Dhamma of the scriptures fulfills the Dhamma of practice and becomes established in the Dhamma of penetration. 'That' means that knowing, which is the full understanding of Nibbāna; this is the meaning.

Saṅkhārapadaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Term 'Formations' is finished.

Viññāṇapadaniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of the Term Consciousness

227. Yathāvuttasaṅkhārapaccayāti puññābhisaṅkhārādivuttappakārasaṅkhārapaccayā. Viññāṇādayo vedanāpariyosānā [V 0.0108] etarahi vipākavaṭṭabhūtā idhādhippetāti āha “taṃkammanibbattameva viññāṇaṃ bhavituṃ arahatī”ti. Ayañca atthavaṇṇanā dhātukathāpāḷiyā na sametīti dassento “dhātukathāyaṃ panā”tiādimāha. Tattha dhātukathāyaṃ vacanato sabbaviññāṇaphassavedanāpariggaho kato dhātukathāyanti yojanā. Sappadesāti sāvasesā, vipākā evāti adhippāyo. Viññāṇādīsu hi vipākesuyeva adhippetesu yathā –

227. “Conditioned by formations as stated” means conditioned by formations of the kind previously mentioned, such as meritorious formations. Consciousness and so on, ending with feeling, which are at present the round of results, are intended here. Hence it is said: “That consciousness produced by that kamma alone is fit to come into being.” And to show that this explanation of the meaning does not accord with the Pāḷi of the Dhātukathā, he says: “But in the Dhātukathā…,” and so on. There, the connection is: in the Dhātukathā, in accordance with the Pāḷi, the inclusion of all consciousness, contact, and feeling is made. `Sappadesā` means with a remainder; the meaning is, they are only resultants. For when consciousness and so on are intended as only resultants, as:

“Vipākehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā, te dhammā asaṅkhataṃ khandhato ṭhapetvā pañcahi khandhehi dvādasahāyatanehi terasahi dhātūhi saṅgahitā. Katihi asaṅgahitā? Na kehici khandhehi na kehici āyatanehi pañcahi dhātūhi asaṅgahitā”ti (dhātu. 477) –

“Those phenomena that are dissociated from resultant phenomena, setting aside the unconditioned from the aggregates, are included in the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the thirteen elements. By how many are they not included? They are not included by any aggregates, not by any bases, and by five elements.”

Vipākavippayuttānaṃ saṅgahāsaṅgahā vissajjitā, evamidhāpi vissajjitabbaṃ siyā. Tenāha “vipākā dhammāti imassa viya vissajjanaṃ siyā”ti. Tasmāti yasmā vippayuttena saṅgahitāsaṅgahitapadaniddese nippadesāva viññāṇaphassavedanā gahitā, tasmā. Tatthāti dhātukathāyaṃ. Abhidhammabhājanīyavasenāti [M 0.0112] imasmiṃ paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅge abhidhammabhājanīyavasena. Tenāha “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā cā”tiādi. Tena yathāvuttaatthavaṇṇanā suttantabhājanīyavasena vuttāti yathādassitaṃ virodhaṃ pariharati. Yadi abhidhammabhājanīyavasena dhātukathāpāḷi pavattā, atha kasmā “kāmabhavo pañcahi khandhehi ekādasahāyatanehi sattarasahi dhātūhi saṅgahito. Rūpabhavo pañcahi khandhehi pañcahāyatanehi aṭṭhahi dhātūhi saṅgahito”tiādinā (dhātu. 67-68) upādinnakkhandhavasena bhavo vissajjitoti codanaṃ manasi katvā āha “bhavo pana…pe… na abhidhammabhājanīyavasena gahito”ti. Evañca katvāti abhidhammabhājanīyavasena aggahitattā eva. Tatthāti dhātukathāyaṃ. Vipākañhetanti hi-saddo hetuattho. Yasmā yathāvuttabāttiṃsavidhaviññāṇaṃ vipākaṃ, tasmā taṃ saṅkhārapaccayanti imamatthaṃ dassento “viññāṇassa vipākattā”tiādimāha.

The inclusion and exclusion of phenomena dissociated from resultants has been answered, and so it should be answered here too. Therefore he says: “The answer might be like that for ‘resultant phenomena.’” Therefore: since in the exposition of the term ‘included and not included by the dissociated,’ consciousness, contact, and feeling are taken without remainder, therefore. There means in the Dhātukathā. By way of the Abhidhamma analysis means: in this Analysis of Dependent Origination, by way of the Abhidhamma analysis. Hence he says: “With ignorance as condition, volitional formations…,” and so on. Thereby he resolves the contradiction that was shown by stating that the aforesaid explanation of the meaning was stated by way of the Suttanta analysis. Having considered the objection—“If the Pāḷi of the Dhātukathā proceeds by way of the Abhidhamma analysis, then why, in such passages as: ‘Sense-sphere becoming is included in five aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements. Form-sphere becoming is included in five aggregates, five bases, and eight elements,’ etc., is becoming explained by way of the aggregates subject to clinging?”—he says: “But becoming… is not taken by way of the Abhidhamma analysis.” And having done so means: precisely because of not being taken by way of the Abhidhamma analysis. There means in the Dhātukathā. It is a resultant: here the particle `hi` has the sense of reason. Since the thirty-two kinds of consciousness mentioned are resultant, therefore, to show this meaning that ‘it is conditioned by formations,’ he says: “Because consciousness is a resultant…,” and so on.

“Somanassasahagatāneva sandhāya vutta”nti idaṃ vicāretabbaṃ upekkhāsahagatakusalākusalajavanānantarampi somanassasahagatatadārammaṇassa icchitattā. Tathā hi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “catunnaṃ pana duhetukakusalacittānaṃ aññatarajavanassa pariyosāne ahetukacittaṃ tadārammaṇabhāvena [V 0.0109] patiṭṭhātī”ti (dha. sa. aṭṭha. 498 vipākuddhārakathā) vatvā “iṭṭhārammaṇe pana santīraṇampi tadārammaṇampi somanassasahagatamevā”ti vuttaṃ. Kusalākusalañhi abhiiṭṭhampi ārammaṇaṃ tathābhisaṅkharaṇena kadāci na majjhattaṃ katvā na pavattati, vipākaṃ pana yathāsabhāvatova ārammaṇarasaṃ anubhavati. Tenāha “na sakkā vipākaṃ vañcetu”nti. Kiriyajavanānaṃ pana visayābhisaṅkharaṇassa balavabhāvato tadanantarānaṃ tadārammaṇānaṃ yathāvisayaṃ vedanāvasena tadanuguṇatā icchitā. Ye pana kiriyajavanānantaraṃ tadārammaṇaṃ na icchanti, tesaṃ vattabbameva natthi. Yaṃ pana “javanena tadārammaṇaṃ niyametabba”nti vuttaṃ, taṃ kusalaṃ sandhāya vuttanti ca vuttaṃ. Tasmā yathāvutto vicāretabbo. Tihetukajavanāvasāne ca duhetukajavanāvasāne cāti samuccayattho ca-saddo. Keci pana vibhāgaṃ akatvā “kusalajavanāvasānepi ahetukatadārammaṇaṃ hotīti ‘yebhuyyenā’ti vutta”nti vadanti. Lobhacittassa vā sattānaṃ bahulaṃ uppajjanato “yebhuyyenā”ti [M 0.0113] vuttaṃ. “Sakiṃ vā”ti vacanasiliṭṭhatāvasena vuttaṃ yathā “aṭṭha vā dasa vā”ti dassetuṃ “dirattatirattādīsu viya veditabba”nti āha. Vā-saddassa abhāvāti suyyamānassa vā-saddassa abhāvena vuttaṃ. Atthato pana tatthāpi vā-saddo labbhateva. Tirattaṃ pana vāsādike labbhamāne diratte vattabbameva natthīti dirattaggahaṇaṃ visuṃ na yojetīti adhippāyena “vacanasiliṭṭhatāmattenā”ti vuttaṃ. Kevalaṃ “tiratta”nti vutte aññattha vāsādinā antaritampi tirattaṃ gaṇheyya, dirattavisiṭṭhaṃ pana tirattaṃ vuccamānaṃ tena anantaritameva tirattaṃ dīpetīti āha “nirantaratirattadassanatthaṃ vā”ti. Balavarūpādike ārammaṇeti atimahati rūpādiārammaṇe. “Adhippāyo”ti etena ekacittakkhaṇāyukepi visaye kadāci tadārammaṇaṃ uppajjeyyāti “sakiṃ evā”tiādinā vuttamatthaṃ ulliṅgeti. “Sabbadvāresu tadārammaṇe dve eva cittavārā āgatā”ti vuttattā ayampi attho vicāretvā gahetabbo. Anurūpāya paṭisandhiyāti attano attano anucchavikena paṭisandhānakiccena.

The statement, “It is said with reference to those accompanied by joy,” should be investigated, because a registration consciousness accompanied by joy is desired even after a wholesome or unwholesome impulsion accompanied by equanimity. For so it is said in the commentary: “At the end of an impulsion by any of the four wholesome cittas with two roots, a rootless citta becomes established by way of registration.” And it is further said: “But in the case of a desirable object, both the investigating consciousness and the registration consciousness are accompanied by joy.” For although the object may be highly desirable, wholesome and unwholesome states, because of the way they are prepared, sometimes do not proceed with neutrality; but the resultant experiences the flavor of the object just as it is in its own nature. Hence it is said: “The resultant cannot be deceived.” But in the case of functional impulsions, because the preparation of the object is strong, it is desired that the subsequent registration consciousnesses conform to the feeling appropriate to the object. For those who do not desire registration consciousness after functional impulsions, there is nothing to be said. And as to what was said, “The registration is to be determined by the impulsion,” it is also said that this was stated with reference to the wholesome. Therefore, the aforesaid point should be investigated. The particle `ca` in “at the end of triple-rooted impulsions and at the end of double-rooted impulsions” has a collective sense. But some say without making a distinction: “Even at the end of wholesome impulsions a rootless registration consciousness arises; hence it is said ‘for the most part.’” Or “for the most part” is said because consciousness accompanied by greed arises frequently for beings. To show that “once or” is said by way of idiomatic smoothness, as in “eight or ten,” he says: “it should be understood as in ‘two or three nights,’ etc.” The absence of the particle `vā` means it is said because of the absence of an audible particle `vā`. But in terms of meaning, the particle `vā` is indeed found there too. Since ‘three nights’ is found in contexts like ‘a stay,’ there is no need to mention ‘two nights’ separately; with the intention that the mention of ‘two nights’ should not be construed as a separate case, it is said “merely by way of idiomatic smoothness.” If one just said “three nights,” one might take it as three nights even if interrupted by a stay elsewhere, etc.; but when “three nights” is specified by “two nights,” it indicates three nights uninterrupted by that. Hence he says: “or to show three uninterrupted nights.” In a very great object such as a strong form, etc. means: in a very great object such as form, etc. By “the intention” he alludes to the meaning stated in “just once,” etc., that registration may sometimes arise even in regard to an object with a duration of a single mind-moment. Since it is said, “In all doors, only two mind-processes with registration have been given,” this meaning too should be taken after investigation. By appropriate rebirth-linking means by the function of rebirth-linking suitable to each one.

“Kati paṭisandhiyo, kati paṭisandhicittānī”tiādinā paṭisandhivicāro parato vitthārato kathīyatīti āha “paṭisandhikathā mahāvisayāti katvā pavattimeva tāva dassento”ti. Ahetukadvayādīnanti ādi-saddena mahāvipākamahaggatavipāke saṅgaṇhāti. Dvāraniyamāniyamāvacananti dvārassa niyatāniyatāvacanaṃ, niyatadvāraṃ aniyatadvāranti vā avacananti attho. Anuppattitoti na uppajjanato. Yadipi “anurūpāya paṭisandhiyā”ti paṭisandhipi [V 0.0110] heṭṭhā gahitā, “pavattiyaṃ panā”ti adhikatattā pana pavattiyeva paccāmaṭṭhā. Paccayuppannabhāvena paṭhamuddiṭṭhāni sabbānipi lokiyavipākacittāni anvādesaṃ arahantīti āha “tatrassāti pavattiyaṃ bāttiṃsavidhassā”ti.

Since the investigation of rebirth-linking, beginning with “How many rebirth-linkings? How many rebirth-linking consciousnesses?,” is discussed in detail later, he says: “Having considered the discussion on rebirth-linking to be a vast subject, for now I will show only the course of life….” Beginning with the two rootless types, etc.: by the word “etc.” he includes the great resultants and the exalted resultants. The statement of the door being fixed or unfixed: this means the statement of the door being fixed or unfixed, or the non-statement that the door is fixed or unfixed; that is the meaning. From non-arising means: not from arising. Although rebirth-linking too was taken up below with “by appropriate rebirth-linking,” yet because of the additional phrase “but in the course of life,” it is the course of life that is referred back to. Because they are conditionally arisen phenomena, all the mundane resultant consciousnesses first pointed out deserve to be included. Therefore he says: “Therein, that is, in the course of life, of the thirty-two kinds….”

Yathā kāmāvacarapaṭisandhiviññāṇasaṅkhātassa bījassa abhāvepi rūpabhave cakkhusotindriyapavattiānubhāvato cakkhusotaviññāṇānaṃ sambhavo, evaṃ teneva kāraṇena sampaṭicchanādīnampi tattha sambhavoti dassento “indriyapavattiānubhāvato evā”tiādimāha. Tattha cakkhusotadvārabhedenāti cakkhusotadvāravisesena bhavitabbanti sambandho. Tassāti cakkhusotadvārassa. Dvāravantāpekkho dvārabhāvoti āha “viññāṇavīthibhedāyattattā”ti. Tasmiñca satīti tasmiṃ [M 0.0114] dvārabhede vīthibhede ca sati. Bhāvoti uppatti. Janakaṃ anubandhati nāmāti taṃsadise tabbohāraṃ katvā vuttaṃ.

To show that just as, even in the absence of the seed called sense-sphere rebirth-linking consciousness, eye- and ear-consciousness arise in the form-sphere existence due to the power of the occurrence of the eye and ear faculties, so too, for that very reason, receiving consciousness and so on also arise there, he says: “precisely due to the power of the occurrence of the faculties…,” and so on. Therein, the connection for “by the distinction of the eye and ear doors” is that it must be by the specific eye and ear doors. Of that means: of the eye and ear door. The state of being a door is dependent on the door-process consciousness; thus he says: “because it depends on the distinction of the consciousness process.” And when that exists means: when that distinction of the door and distinction of the process exists. Existence means arising. The expression “it follows the generator” is stated by making a designation for something similar to it.

Idaṃ pana vatvāti rūpārūpāvacaradhamme ārabbha tadārammaṇānuppattiṃ vatvā. Bhāvanāyāti akusalabhāvanāya saṃkilesavaḍḍhanena, saṃkiliṭṭhasamādhānenāti attho. Tathā hi lobhadosasahagatacittuppādepi samādhi “avaṭṭhiti avisāhāro avikkhepo avisāhaṭamānasatā”tiādinā (dha. sa. 11) niddiṭṭho. Avatthubhāvadassanatthanti aṭṭhānabhāvadassanatthaṃ, anārammaṇabhāvadassanatthanti attho.

But having said this means: having spoken about the non-arising of registration consciousness in relation to form-sphere and formless-sphere phenomena. By development means: by the development of the unwholesome, by the increase of defilements; the meaning is, by defiled concentration. For so, even in the arising of a citta accompanied by greed and hatred, concentration is described as “stability, non-dissipation, non-distraction, undistracted mentality,” etc. To show the state of being without a basis means: to show the state of being groundless; the meaning is, to show the state of being without an object.

“Kena katthā”ti padassa “kena cittena kasmiṃ bhave”ti saṅkhepena vuttamatthaṃ vitthārato dassetuṃ “ekūnavīsatī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tena tena cittenāti tena tena ahetukadvayādicittena saddhiṃ pavattamānā paṭisandhikkhaṇe rūpārūpadhammā ekūnavīsati paṭisandhiyoti yojanā. Tena tena cittena sahajātādipaccayatāya hetubhūtena, karaṇabhūtena vā. Tattha tattha bhave.

To show in detail the meaning of the term 'By what? Where?,' stated concisely as 'by what mind, in what existence?,' the words 'nineteen,' etc., are said. Therein, the connection for 'by this and that citta' is: the material and immaterial phenomena occurring together with this and that citta—the two rootless cittas, etc.—at the moment of rebirth-linking are the nineteen rebirth-linkings. By this and that citta, which is a cause or an instrument by way of the conascence condition, etc. In this and that existence.

Anussaraṇattho byāpāro anussaraṇabyāpāro. Kecīti dhammasirittheraṃ sandhāya vadati. Tīsu javanavāresu…pe… bhavitabbanti kammādiupaṭṭhānassa parato tīhi javanavārehi pavattitabbanti attho. Tenāha “aneka…pe… abhippalambanañca hotī”ti. Tasmāti yasmā ekajavanavārasseva kammādiupaṭṭhānena maraṇaṃ na sambhavati, tasmā. Phoṭṭhabbassāti pahāraphoṭṭhabbassa[V 0.0111]. Bhavaṅgacitte vattamāne, antarantarā pañcadvāravīthiyā vā vattamānāya phoṭṭhabbasamāyoge paṭhamaṃ kāyadvārāvajjanuppatti yuttā, tathāpi kismiñci cintiyamāne tamevārabbha ekasmiṃ javanavāre pavatte pacchā kāyadvārāvajjanuppatti siyā cittassa lahuparivattibhāvatoti kecivādassa adhippāyo. Yathā niddāyantassa phoṭṭhabbasamāyogena pabujjhanakāle manodvārāvajjanameva āvaṭṭeti, na kāyadvārāvajjanaṃ. “Pañcahi viññāṇehi na paṭibujjhatī”ti (vibha. 751) hi vuttaṃ. Evaṃsampadaṃ vā etaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Lahukapaccupaṭṭhānanti lahuupaṭṭhānaṃ. Manodvārassa visayo kammādiko. Lahukatāti lahupaṭṭhānatā. Rūpānanti cakkhādirūpadhammānaṃ. Visayabhāvepīti rūpāyatanādivisayasabbhāvepi. Yesaṃ visayo atthīti yesaṃ nippariyāyena [M 0.0115] visayo atthi. Taṃdassanatthamevāti tesaṃ sārammaṇānaṃyeva dassanatthaṃ. Tenāti tasmā.

The activity of recollection is recollection-activity. 'Some' refers to the Elder Dhammasiri. 'In the three series of impulsions… it should be' means that the presentation of kamma, etc., must occur in the three series of impulsions that follow. Therefore it is said: “many… and there is deception.” 'Therefore' means: because death does not occur with the presentation of kamma, etc., in just one series of impulsions, therefore. 'Of a tangible object' means of the tangible object of impact. While the life-continuum mind is occurring, or while a five-door cognitive process is intermittently occurring, upon contact with a tangible object, the arising of body-door adverting should occur first. Nevertheless, when something is being considered, taking that as object, after one series of impulsions has occurred, the arising of body-door adverting may occur because of the mind’s quickly changing nature—this is the intention of the view of some. Just as for one who is sleeping, upon contact with a tangible object at the moment of waking, it is only mind-door adverting that turns, not body-door adverting. For it is said: “One does not awaken with the five consciousnesses” (Vibh 751). This should be seen as a case of this kind. 'Quick presentation' means rapid presentation. The object of the mind-door is kamma, etc. 'Quickness' means the state of being rapidly presented. 'Of forms' means of material phenomena such as visible form. 'Even when it is an object' means even when there is an object such as the visible form base. 'For which there is an object' means for which there is an object in a direct sense. 'For the purpose of seeing that' means for the purpose of seeing only those things that have an object. 'By that' means therefore.

“Bhūmicittuppādādivasenā”ti idaṃ kammaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, kammanimittassapi vasena labbhateva tassa chaḷārammaṇabhāvato. Gatinimittassa pana pabhedo nīlādikoyeva.

“By way of the arising of a mind of a plane of existence, etc.”: this is said with reference to kamma. It can also be obtained by way of the kamma-sign, as this can have any of the six kinds of objects. The variety of the destination-sign, however, is just blue, etc.

Anupacchinnesu maggena appahīnesu. Tañca kammādiṃ. Bhavantaraninnāditā cittasantānassa bhavapatthanāya tathābhisaṅkhatattā. Yasmiñhi cittasantāne puññādicetanāya viya bhavapatthanāya paribhāvanā anupacchinnā, tattheva bhavantarapariyāpannacittuppatti. Taṃ pana cittaṃ tathā uppajjamānaṃ tāya vināmitaṃ viya hotīti vuttaṃ “anupacchinnakilesabalavināmita”nti. Sabbatthāti sugatiduggatīsu. Itarāyāti sugatipaṭisandhininnāya cutiyā. “Nicchinantī”ti vuttassa nicchayassa nibandhanaṃ āgamaṃ dassento “nimittassādagadhitaṃ vā”tiādimāha.

'Uninterrupted' means not abandoned by the path. And that kamma, etc. The mental continuum’s inclination towards another existence is due to its having been conditioned by the longing for existence. For in whatever mental continuum the cultivation of the longing for existence—like the volition for merit, etc.—is uninterrupted, in that very continuum a mind pertaining to another existence arises. And that mind, arising in such a way, is as if bent by that longing; thus it is said to be “influenced by the power of the uninterrupted defilements.” 'In all' means in good and bad destinations. 'For the other' means for the death that inclines towards a rebirth-linking in a good destination. Showing the scriptural authority for the determination stated as 'determining,' he says, “or being greedy for the delight in the sign,” etc.

Akusale hi duggatūpanissaye niyamite kusalaṃ sugatūpanissayoti niyamitameva hotīti.

For when the unwholesome is fixed as the decisive support for a bad destination, the wholesome is indeed fixed as the decisive support for a good destination.

Aniṭṭhaṃ ārammaṇaṃ āha yato duggatipaṭisandhi dassīyatīti adhippāyo. Yadi evaṃ “rāgādihetubhūta”nti kasmā vuttanti āha “tampi hi…pe… hotī”ti. Tampīti aniṭṭhārammaṇampi. Yasmā pana hīnaṃ ārammaṇanti ārammaṇabhūtakammanimittaṃ adhippetaṃ, tasmā “akusalavipākajanakakammasahajātānaṃ vā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kammanimittabhūtañhi ārammaṇaṃ yaṃ vipākassa janakaṃ kammaṃ, tena sahajātānaṃ, tassa kammassa sadisāsannajavanasahajātānañca rāgādīnaṃ [V 0.0112] ārammaṇapaccayasaṅkhāto hetu hoti, so eva cassa hīnabhāvoti dassetuṃ “tañhī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kammavasena aniṭṭhanti hīnassa akusalakammassa ārammaṇato ārammaṇatāvasena hīnanti katvā aniṭṭhaṃ, sabhāvena iṭṭhampīti adhippāyo. “Aññathā cā”tiādinā kammanimittārammaṇassa akusalavipākassa na sambhavoti dasseti. Āsannakatakammārammaṇasantatiyanti āsannakatassa kammassa ārammaṇasantāne. Taṃsadisanti yathāvuttakammārammaṇasadisaṃ. Paṭisandhiārammaṇūpaṭṭhāpakanti paṭisandhiyā ārammaṇassa upaṭṭhāpakaṃ. Cutiāsannajavanānaṃ paṭisandhijanakatte ayamattho labbheyyāti codanaṃ manasi [M 0.0116] katvā āha “na ca paṭisandhiyā”tiādi. Taṃsamānavīthiyanti tāya paṭisandhiyā ekavīthiyaṃ. Na assāditānīti assādanabhūtāya taṇhāya na āmaṭṭhāni.

He speaks of an undesirable object because a rebirth-linking in a bad destination is shown thereby; this is the intention. If so, why is it said to be “caused by lust, etc.”? He says: “Because even that… becomes…” 'Even that' means even the undesirable object. However, since by 'inferior object' the kamma-sign that has become an object is intended, therefore it is said: “or of those co-nascent with the unwholesome kamma that produces the result.” For the object that has become the kamma-sign is a cause, called the object-condition, for the lust, etc., that are co-nascent with that kamma which produces the result, and co-nascent with the proximate impulsions similar to that kamma. To show that this itself is its inferior nature, it is said: “for that…” etc. 'Undesirable by way of kamma' means: because it is the object of an inferior, unwholesome kamma, it is considered inferior by way of being an object, and thus undesirable, even though it may be desirable by nature; this is the intention. With the phrase “And otherwise…,” etc., he shows that it is not possible for an unwholesome result to have a kamma-sign as its object. 'In the continuity of the object of a recently performed kamma' means in the continuum of the object of a recently performed kamma. 'Similar to that' means similar to the kamma-object as described. 'Presenter of the object for rebirth-linking' means that which presents the object for the rebirth-linking. Keeping in mind the objection that this meaning would be obtained if the death-proximate impulsions were the producers of rebirth-linking, he says: “But not for the rebirth-linking…,” etc. 'In the same cognitive process' means in the one cognitive process with that rebirth-linking. 'Not savored' means not touched by craving, which is the act of savoring.

Samattāti paripuṇṇā, pariyattā vā. “Maraṇakāle…pe… samādinnā”ti vacanato yathāvuttacutiāsannajavanānaṃ paṭisandhidānaṃ siddhanti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “na ca dubbalehī”tiādi. “Vakkhati cā”tiādinā vuttamevatthaṃ upacayena pākaṭataraṃ karoti. Ñāṇavatthuvibhaṅgavaṇṇanāyañhi “pañcahi viññāṇehi na kañci dhammaṃ paṭivijānātī”ti padānaṃ atthaṃ vivaranto vakkhati “sabbampi…pe… paṭikkhittānī”ti. Tattha paṭivijānanādīti ādi-saddena iriyāpathakappanakāyavacīkammupaṭṭhāpanakusalākusaladhammasamādānasamāpajjanavuṭṭhānāni saṅgaṇhāti. Upapajjanasupinadassanādīnaṃ manodvārikacitteneva pavatti pākaṭāti tāni bahi karonto “cavanapariyosānaṃ kicca”nti āha. Sahajavanakānīti javanasahitāni, pañcadvārikajavanehi saddhinti attho.

'Accomplished' means complete, or fully learned. With reference to the objection that, according to the statement “At the time of death… undertaken,” the giving of rebirth-linking by the aforesaid death-proximate impulsions is established, he says: “And not by weak ones…,” etc. With “And he will say…,” etc., he makes the meaning already stated even clearer by amplification. For in the commentary on the Analysis of the Grounds of Knowledge, when explaining the meaning of the words “with the five consciousnesses one does not discern any dhamma,” he will say: “all… rejected.” There, by the word “etc.” after 'discerning,' he includes: adopting postures; setting up bodily and verbal kamma; undertaking wholesome and unwholesome states; and entering into and emerging from attainments. Since the occurrence of rebirth, seeing dreams, etc., through a mind-door consciousness alone is evident, excluding these, he says: “the function ending with decease.” 'Co-nascent with impulsion' means accompanied by impulsion; that is, together with the five-door impulsions.

Tatthāti “pañcahi viññāṇehi na kañci dhammaṃ paṭivijānātī”ti pāḷivaṇṇanāyaṃ. Na kañci dhammaṃ paṭivijānātīti ettha na sabbe rūpādidhammā dhammaggahaṇena gahitāti yathādhippetadhammadassanatthaṃ “manopubbaṅgamā dhammāti (dha. pa. 1-2) evaṃ vuttaṃ ekampi kusalaṃ vā akusalaṃ vā na paṭivijānātī”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanti dassetvā tassa atthaṃ vivaranto “yesa”ntiādimāha. Tassattho – yesaṃ kusalākusaladhammānaṃ paṭivibhāvanappavattiyā siddhā vipākadhammatā yonisomanasikāraayonisomanasikārasamuṭṭhānā, yāya sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā taṃsantāne anveti anugacchati, pañcaviññāṇānaṃ sā vipākadhammatā paṭikkhittā paṭisedhitāti. Tādisamevāti kusalākusaladhammapaṭivijānanasadisameva. Yadi pañcadvāre yathāvuttakiccassa [V 0.0113] karaṇe sahajavanakāni vīthicittāni paṭikkhittāni, kathaṃ tattha cavanupapajjanāni sambhavantīti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “tadārammaṇānantaraṃ panā”tiādi. Nippariyāyena manodvārikabhāvo manodvārāvajjanuppattipubbakoti tadabhāvenāha “iminā adhippāyenā”ti. Avasesekacittakkhaṇāyuke rūpādimhīti yojanā.

There means in the commentary on the Pāḷi text “with the five consciousnesses one does not discern any dhamma.” In “one does not discern any dhamma,” not all dhammas such as visible form, etc., are included by the term “dhamma.” To show the intended dhamma, having pointed out that it is said in the commentary, “As it is said, ‘Mind precedes dhammas’ (Dhp 1–2), one does not discern even a single wholesome or unwholesome dhamma,” he explains its meaning, saying “of which…,” etc. Its meaning is this: that nature as a resultant dhamma—which is established for those wholesome and unwholesome dhammas by the occurrence of their clear comprehension arising from wise or unwise attention, and by which happiness or suffering follows along in that continuum—that nature as a resultant dhamma is rejected, is denied, for the five consciousnesses. Just the same means just the same as the discerning of wholesome and unwholesome dhammas. With reference to the objection, “If, in the five doors, the cognitive-process minds co-nascent with impulsion are rejected for performing the aforesaid function, how can decease and rebirth-linking occur there?” he says: “But immediately after the registration…,” etc. Since being directly of the mind-door is preceded by the arising of mind-door adverting, in the absence of that he says: “with this intention.” The connection is: in a visible form, etc., that has a lifespan of one remaining mind-moment.

Upacāro viya daṭṭhabbā samānārammaṇattā, upapattinimittattā ca. Kecīti dhammasirittheraṃ sandhāya vadati. Mahaggatāvasānaṃ vadantīti yathāpaccayaṃ mahaggatasamāpattiṃ [M 0.0117] samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhitassa sā vīthi uppajjati, tato cuticittaṃ hotīti vadanti. Atītārammaṇā ekādasavidhāti nava kāmāvacarasugaticutiyo, dve viññāṇañcāyatananevasaññānāsaññāyatanaāruppacutiyoti evaṃ atītārammaṇā ekādasavidhā sugaticutiyo. Pañca rūpāvacarā, vuttāvasesā dve arūpāvacarāti navattabbārammaṇā sattavidhā cutiyo. Duggaticuti pana parato vuccatīti idha na gahitā. Tathā hi vakkhati “duggaticutiyā pana…pe… na dassitā”ti.

It should be seen as a figurative expression because of having the same object and because it is a sign of rebirth. Some refers to the Elder Dhammasiri. They speak of it ending with a sublime state, meaning that for one who has emerged from a sublime attainment entered into in accordance with conditions, that cognitive process arises, and then the decease-consciousness occurs—so they say. There are eleven kinds with a past object: nine kinds of decease in a good destination in the sense sphere, and two formless deceases, in the base of infinite consciousness and the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Thus there are eleven kinds of decease in a good destination with a past object. Five are form-sphere deceases, and the remaining two mentioned are formless-sphere deceases; thus there are seven kinds of decease with an ineffable object. Decease in a bad destination, however, is spoken of later, so it is not included here. For he will say: “But regarding decease in a bad destination… not shown.”

Evamādiketi ādi-saddena “suddhāya vā javanavīthiyā”tiādivacanaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Tathā hi vuttaṃ “suddhāya vāti mahaggatakammanimittārammaṇāya javanavīthiyā”ti. “Viññāyatī”ti iminā yadipi “pathavīkasiṇādī”tiādisaddena arūpāvacarajjhānārammaṇassāpi saṅgaho sambhavati, “cakkhusotānaṃ vā”ti pana dvāradvayasseva vasena vikappantarakaraṇaṃ yathādhippetassa atthassa ñāpakanti dasseti. Ñāpakañca nāma agatikā gatīti yathāvuttaṃ ñāpakaṃ asambhāvento “athāpī”tiādimāha. Yo yattha sambhavati, tassa yojanā yathāsambhavayojanā, tāya. Ayampi paṭisandhīti āruppacutiyā anantaraṃ paṭisandhiṃ vadati. Tatthevāti “pathavīkasiṇādikaṃ vā nimitta”nti vutte paṭhame vikappe eva. Heṭṭhimā heṭṭhimā paṭisandhi natthīti yojanā. Tenāti tasmā. Tatoti catutthāruppacutito. Tatthevāti catutthāruppe eva. Atītārammaṇā paṭisandhi, tato catutthāruppacutito kāmāvacare atītapaccuppannārammaṇā paṭisandhi. Itarāhīti āruppacutīhi. Dutiyā āruppapaṭisandhi atītārammaṇā, itarā navattabbārammaṇāti āha “yathāsambhava”nti. Atītapaccuppannārammaṇā ca kāmāvacarapaṭisandhīti etthāpi itarāhīti sambandho. Sabbattha ca “yojetabbā”ti sambandhitabbaṃ. Imassa visesassāti “tenā”tiādinā yathāvuttassa visesassa. Visuṃ uddharaṇaṃ kataṃ adhikavacanamaññamatthaṃ bodhetīti.

‘Thus, etc.’—by the word ‘etc.,’ it includes statements like ‘or of the pure javana course.’ For it is said: ‘Or of the pure’ means the javana course with a sublime kamma-sign as object. ‘Is discerned’—by this, even the inclusion of the object of the formless absorptions (jhānas), mentioned by the word ‘earth kasiṇa, etc.,’ is possible. However, ‘or of the eye and ear’ shows that the distinction is made only by way of the two doors, indicating the intended meaning. An indicator, indeed, is a path without a fixed course. One who does not comprehend the indicator as stated says, ‘or else,’ etc. Whatever is possible in a given case, its application is according to what is possible, by that. ‘This too is rebirth-linking’—it refers to rebirth-linking immediately after the decease from the formless realm. ‘Therein’—when ‘or the sign of the earth kasiṇa, etc.’ is stated, it refers only to the first alternative. The application is that ‘the lower rebirth-linking does not exist.’ ‘Therefore’—that is, because of that. ‘From there’—that is, from the decease from the fourth formless realm. ‘Therein’—that is, only in the fourth formless realm. Rebirth-linking has a past object. Then, from the decease from the fourth formless realm, rebirth-linking in the sense-sphere has a past or present object. ‘The others’—that is, from the deceases from the other formless realms. The second rebirth-linking in the formless realm has a past object; the others have an indeterminable object—thus he says, ‘as is possible.’ And rebirth-linking in the sense-sphere has a past or present object—here too, the connection is ‘the others.’ And in all cases, ‘should be connected’—it should be connected. ‘Of this distinction’—that is, of the distinction stated by ‘therefore,’ etc. A separate extraction has been made; the additional words indicate another meaning.

Ārammaṇavasena [V 0.0114] ekavidhāyāti atītārammaṇatāvasena ekavidhāya. Duvidhāti atītārammaṇā, paccuppannārammaṇā cāti dvippakārā. Duggaticutiyā ārammaṇavasena “ekavidhāyā”ti padaṃ ānetvā yojetabbaṃ. Atītapaccuppannārammaṇatāya dvippakārā kāmāvacarapaṭisandhi, navattabbārammaṇatāya [M 0.0118] ekappakārā rūpāvacarapaṭisandhi, navattabbātītārammaṇatāya dvippakārā āruppapaṭisandhīti āha “dviekadvippakārānaṃ kāmarūpāruppānaṃ vasenā”ti. “Tathevā”ti iminā “dviekadvippakārānaṃ kāmarūpāruppānaṃ vasenā”ti padadvayaṃ ākaḍḍhati. Duvidhāyāti navattabbātītārammaṇatāvasena duvidhāya. Paccekanti visuṃ visuṃ. Dvinnaṃ dvinnaṃ kāmāruppānanti etthāyaṃ yojanā – navattabbārammaṇāya āruppacutiyā anantarā atītārammaṇā paccuppannārammaṇā ca dve kāmapaṭisandhī, navattabbārammaṇā atītārammaṇā ca dve āruppapaṭisandhī, tathā atītārammaṇāyapīti imāsaṃ vasena aṭṭhavidhā.

‘By way of object, it is single’ means it is single by way of having a past object. ‘It is twofold’ means it is of two kinds, having a past object and a present object. For the decease in the woeful destinations, the word ‘it is single’ should be applied by way of object. Rebirth-linking in the sense-sphere is of two kinds by way of having past and present objects; rebirth-linking in the form realm is of one kind by way of having an indeterminable object; and rebirth-linking in the formless realm is of two kinds by way of having an indeterminable and a past object—thus he says, ‘by way of the sense-sphere, form, and formless realms, which are of two kinds, one kind, and two kinds respectively.’ ‘Similarly’—by this, he draws in the two phrases ‘by way of the sense-sphere, form, and formless realms, which are of two kinds, one kind, and two kinds respectively.’ ‘It is twofold’ means it is twofold by way of having an indeterminable and a past object. ‘Individually’ means separately. For the two pairs, of sense-sphere and formless realms—here, the application is as follows: Immediately after the decease from the formless realm which has an indeterminable object, there are two sense-sphere rebirth-linkings, one with a past object and one with a present object. And there are two formless-realm rebirth-linkings, one with an indeterminable object and one with a past object. Similarly, even for that with a past object—thus, by way of these, there are eight kinds.

“Dvidvī”ti gāthāya vuttamevatthaṃ sukhaggahaṇatthaṃ saṅgahetvā dasseti. Yadipi “kammassa katattā”tiādināpi kammassa vipākānaṃ upanissayapaccayabhāvo gahitoyeva hoti, “kusalākusalaṃ kamma”ntiādinā pana visuṃ upanissayapaccayabhāvo dassīyatīti “kāmāvacarassa…pe… ādinā nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayabhāvo dassitappakāro”ti āha.

He summarizes and shows the meaning expressed in the verse beginning 'Dvidvī' for ease of comprehension. Although the nature of kamma as a decisive support condition for its results is already grasped by 'because of the performance of kamma,' etc., the condition of decisive support is shown separately by 'wholesome and unwholesome kamma,' etc. Thus, he says, 'Of the sense-sphere... etc.,' to indicate the manner of showing the nature of kamma as a condition arising at different moments.

Ādinā vimissaviññāṇenāti ekassa bhavassa ādibhūtena rūpavimissena paṭisandhiviññāṇena. Aññatthāti saṃsedajaopapātikayoniyaṃ. Avacanaṃ paṭikkhepaṃ maññamāno “gandharasāhārānaṃ paṭikkhittattā”ti vatvā sabbena sabbaṃ rūpabhave te natthīti adhippāyenāha “cakkhusotavatthusattakajīvitachakkabhāvepī”ti. Pāḷiyanti dhammahadayavibhaṅgapāḷiyaṃ. Pañcāyatanānīti cakkhusotamanarūpadhammāyatanāni. Pañca dhātuyoti tā eva pañca dhātuyo. Vuttañhi – “rūpadhātuyā upapattikkhaṇe katamāni pañcāyatanāni pātubhavanti? Cakkhāyatanaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ sotāyatanaṃ manāyatanaṃ dhammāyatanaṃ. Imāni pañcāyatanāni pātubhavanti. Katamā pañca dhātuyo pātubhavanti? Cakkhudhātu…pe… dhammadhātu. Imā pañca dhātuyo pātubhavantī”ti (vibha. 1016). Cha āyatanāni saddāyatanena saddhiṃ tāniyeva. Nava dhātuyoti cakkhurūpacakkhuviññāṇasotasaddasotaviññāṇamanodhammamanoviññāṇadhātuyo. Sabbasaṅgahavasenāti anavasesapariggahavasena. Tatthāti rūpadhātuyaṃ. “Kathāvatthumhi cā”tiādinā na kevalaṃ dhammahadayavibhaṅgapāḷiyaṃyeva, atha kho pakaraṇantarepi gandhādayo paṭikkhittāti dasseti. Tattha ghānāyatanādīnaṃ [V 0.0115] viyāti sadisūdāharaṇadassanaṃ. Yathā [M 0.0119] ghānāyatanādīnaṃ tattha rūpabhave bhāvo atthi, tā paṭikkhittā, evaṃ gandhāyatanādīnañcāti. Atthi tattha ghānāyatananti pucchā sakavādissa. Yañhi tattha āyatanaṃ natthi, tassa vasenāyaṃ codanā. Tato paravādī yaṃ tattha ajjhattikānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ āyatanānaṃ ghānādikaṃ saṇṭhānanimittaṃ, tadeva āyatananti laddhiyā “āmantā”ti paṭijānāti. Bāhirānaṃ gandhāyatanādīnaṃ vasena puṭṭho yasmā ghānappasādādayo tattha na icchati, tasmā tesaṃ gocaraṃ paṭisedhento “na hevaṃ vattabbe”ti paṭikkhipati. Ādi-saddena “atthi tattha jivhāyatananti? Āmantā. Atthi tattha rasāyatananti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe”tiādinayappavattānaṃ anulomapaṭilomasaṃsandanapañhādīnaṃ saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo. Aphoṭṭhabbāyatanānanti phoṭṭhabbāyatanabhāvarahitānaṃ, aphoṭṭhabbasabhāvānanti attho.

‘With the initial mixed consciousness’ means with the rebirth-linking consciousness, which is the initial basis of one existence, mixed with form. ‘Elsewhere’ means in the moisture-born and spontaneous-birth wombs. Considering the non-mention as a rejection, he states, ‘Because odors, tastes, and nutriment are rejected,’ and with the intention that they are entirely absent in the form realm, he says, ‘even in the state of the eye-septad, ear-septad, basis-septad, and life-hexad.’ ‘In the Pāḷi’ means in the Dhammahadayavibhaṅga Pāḷi. ‘Five sense bases’ means the eye base, ear base, mind base, form base, and mental-object base. ‘Five elements’ means those same five elements. For it is said: ‘At the moment of rebirth in the form realm, which five sense bases become manifest? The eye base, form base, ear base, mind base, and mental-object base. These five sense bases become manifest. Which five elements become manifest? The eye element… up to… the mental-object element. These five elements become manifest’ (Vibh. 1016). ‘Six sense bases’ means those same ones along with the sound base. ‘Nine elements’ means the eye element, form element, eye-consciousness element, ear element, sound element, ear-consciousness element, mind element, mental-object element, and mind-consciousness element. ‘By way of complete inclusion’ means by way of inclusion without remainder. ‘There’ means in the form realm. ‘Also in the Kathāvatthu, etc.’ shows that not only in the Dhammahadayavibhaṅga Pāḷi but also in other texts, odors and so on are rejected. Here, ‘like the nose base, etc.’ is the showing of a similar example. Just as the nose base and so on are rejected—though their existence there in the form realm is asserted—so too are the odor base and so on. ‘Is there a nose base there?’ is a question for the proponent of one's own view. For this objection is made based on what sense base is absent there. Then, the opponent, holding the view that the sign of the shape of the three internal bases—nose, etc.—is itself the sense base, answers, ‘Yes.’ When asked about the external odor base, etc., since he does not accept the nose sensitivity, etc., there, he rejects their objects by saying, ‘This should not be said.’ By the word ‘etc.,’ one should understand the inclusion of questions following the method of direct and reverse connection, such as, ‘Is there a tongue base there? Yes. Is there a taste base there? This should not be said,’ and so on. ‘Non-tangible bases’ means those devoid of the nature of the tangible base, that is, those whose nature is non-tangibility.

Idāni anāyatanasabhāve gandharase paṭijānitvāpi dosaṃ vadanto “yadi cā”tiādimāha. Avacane natthi kāraṇaṃ yathādhammasāsane abhidhamme, tesaṃ vā nisattanijjīvasabhāvattāti adhippāyo. Yathā ca dhātubhāvo, evaṃ dhammabhāvo ca tesaṃ ekantiko, tathā āyatanabhāvo cāti sabbathāpi tattha vijjamānānaṃ gandharasānaṃ āyatanesu avacane kāraṇaṃ natthīti dassento “dhammabhāvo cā”tiādimāha. Aññassa paramatthassa abhāvā. Koci āyatanasabhāvoti dhammāyatanameva sandhāya vadati. Tena yadi rūpabhave gandharasā vijjanti, yathāvuttakāraṇato gandharasāyatanabhāvena avuccamānāpi dhammāyatanabhāvena vattabbā siyuṃ, na ca vuttā. Tasmā niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ “nattheva rūpabhave gandharasā”ti dasseti. Kiñca rūpadhātuyaṃ gandharasabhāvena avuttānaṃ, kāmadhātuyaṃ vuttānaṃ tesaṃ kiṃ gandharasabhāvato aññena sabhāvena rūpadhātuyaṃ atthibhāvo, udāhu gandharasabhāvena. Yadi purimo pakkho dhammāyatane tesaṃ saṅgaho siyā anāyatanasabhāvassa sabhāvadhammassa abhāvā, atha dutiyo teneva kāraṇena nesaṃ gandharasāyatanabhāvo siddhoti imamatthaṃ dassento “yadi cā”tiādimāha. Tasmāti yasmā gandharasā dhammahadayavibhaṅge na vuttā, kathāvatthumhi ca tesaṃ bhāvo paṭikkhitto, phusituṃ asakkuṇeyyā pathavīādayo viya ghāyituṃ sāyituñca asakkuṇeyyā te natthi, dhātusaddena ca te gahitā, dhammabhāvo ca tesaṃ ekantiko, tasmiñca [M 0.0120] sati siddho āyatanabhāvo, tasmā. Tathāti pāḷiyaṃ avuttadhamme hāpetvā cakkhusattakādivasena. Evanti cakkhusattakādivasena rūpagaṇanāya kariyamānāya. Dhammatāti pāḷidhammo[V 0.0116], rūpabhave vā pavattanakarūpadhammatā. “Na vilomitā”ti iminā yathāpaṭiññātaṃ dhammaṃ dīpitaṃ ulliṅgeti.

Now, even while acknowledging the absence of a sense-base nature in odors and tastes, he points out a fault, saying, ‘If indeed…’ etc. There is no reason for their non-mention in the Abhidhamma, the teaching according to reality, or because of their non-sentient, lifeless nature—this is the meaning.
