Just as there is the nature of elements, so too the nature of phenomena is entirely theirs, and similarly, the nature of sense-bases is also theirs; thus, in every way, there is no reason why the odors and tastes existing there should not be mentioned in the sense-bases. To show this, he says, ‘the nature of phenomena, etc.’ Because of the absence of another ultimate reality. When someone speaks of the nature of a sense-base, they are referring only to the mental-object base. Therefore, if odors and tastes exist in the form realm, even though they are not spoken of as having the nature of odor and taste sense-bases for the reasons stated, they should still be spoken of as having the nature of the mental-object base—yet they are not so spoken. Thus, he shows that the conclusion to be reached here is: ‘There are indeed no odors and tastes in the form realm.’ Furthermore, regarding those not spoken of as having the nature of odors and tastes in the form realm, but spoken of in the sense-sphere realm—do they exist in the form realm by some other nature apart from the nature of odors and tastes, or by the nature of odors and tastes? If the former alternative is taken, their inclusion in the mental-object base would be possible, because a real phenomenon that has a non-sense-base nature does not exist. But if the latter alternative is taken, then by that very reason, their nature as odor and taste sense-bases is established. To explain this meaning, he says, ‘If indeed…’ etc. ‘Therefore’—that is, because odors and tastes are not mentioned in the Dhammahadayavibhaṅga, and their existence is rejected in the Kathāvatthu; and because, just as earth and so on that cannot be touched do not exist, so too those things that cannot be smelled or tasted do not exist; and they are included under the term ‘element,’ and their nature as phenomena is definitive, and when this is the case, their nature as sense-bases is established, therefore. ‘In the same way’—that is, by way of the eye-septad, etc., excluding phenomena not stated in the Pāḷi. ‘Thus’—that is, when the enumeration of forms is made by way of the eye-septad, etc. ‘Dhammatā’ means the teaching of the Pāḷi, or the nature of form that causes occurrence in the form realm. ‘Not contradicted’—by this, he illuminates and upholds the Dhamma as it was acknowledged.

Ettha ca rūpāvacarasattānaṃ ghānajivhāyatanābhāvato vijjamānāpi gandharasā āyatanakiccaṃ na karontīti te anāmasitvā pāḷiyaṃ “pañcāyatanāni pātubhavanti, cha āyatanānī”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Tayo āhārā”ti ca ajjhoharitabbassa āhārassa abhāvena ojaṭṭhamakarūpasamuṭṭhāpanasaṅkhātassa āhārakiccassa akaraṇato, na sabbena sabbaṃ gandharasānaṃ ojāya ca abhāvato. Iti visayino kiccassa ca abhāvena visayo, kiccavā ca dhammo na vutto. Yasmiñhi bhave visayī natthi, tasmiṃ taṃhetuko nippariyāyena visayassa āyatanabhāvo natthīti vijjamānassāpi avacanaṃ, yathā rūpabhave pathavītejovāyodhātūnaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanabhāvena. Yassa pana yattha vacanaṃ, tassa tattha visayīsabbhāvahetuko nippariyāyena āyatanabhāvo vutto diṭṭho yathā tattheva rūpāyatanassa. Yadi visayīsabbhāvahetuko visayassa nippariyāyena āyatanabhāvo, kathaṃ asaññasattānaṃ devānaṃ dve āyatanāni pātubhavantīti. Asaññasattānañhi cakkhāyatanaṃ natthi, acakkhāyatanabhāvena ca nesaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ aññesaṃ avisayoti? Nāyaṃ virodho. Yena adhippāyena rūpadhātuyaṃ saññīnaṃ gandhāyatanādīnaṃ avacanaṃ, tena rūpāyatanassāpi avacananti asaññīnaṃ ekaṃ āyatanaṃ vattabbaṃ. Yathāsakañhi indriyagocarabhāvāpekkhāya yesaṃ nippariyāyena āyatanabhāvo atthi, tesu niddisiyamānesu tadabhāvato rūpadhātuyaṃ saññīnaṃ gandhādike visuṃ āyatanabhāvena avatvā dhammasabhāvānativattanato, manoviññāṇassa ca visayabhāvūpagamanato dhammāyatanantogadhe katvā “pañcāyatanānī”ti pāḷiyaṃ vuttaṃ. Etadatthañhi “dhammāyatana”nti sāmaññato nāmakaraṇaṃ, piṭṭhivaṭṭakāni vā tāni katvā “pañcāyatanānī”ti vuttaṃ. Yena ca pana adhippāyena asaññīnaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ vuttaṃ, tena saññīnampi gandhādīnaṃ visuṃ gahaṇaṃ kātabbanti imassa nayassa dassanatthaṃ “asaññasattānaṃ devānaṃ dve āyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti [M 0.0121] (vibha. 1017) vuttaṃ. Asatipi hi attano indriye rūpassa vaṇṇāyatanasabhāvātikkamo natthevāti taṃ rūpāyatanantveva vuccati. Iminā ca nayadassanena gandhādīni tīṇi pakkhipitvā saññīnaṃ aṭṭha āyatanāni, asaññīnaṃ pañcāti ayamattho dassito hoti. Evañcetaṃ sampaṭicchitabbaṃ. Aññathā rūpaloke phusitumasakkuṇeyyatāya pathavīādīnaṃ vacīghoso eva na siyā. Na hi paṭighaṭṭanānighaṃsamantarena saddappavatti atthi, na ca phusanasabhāvānaṃ katthaci aphusanasabhāvatā sakkā [V 0.0117] viññātuṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanasaṅkhātassa ca bhūtattayassa abhāve rūpabhave rūpāyatanādīnampi sambhavo eva na siyā, tasmā phusituṃ sakkuṇeyyatāyapi pathavīādīnaṃ tattha kāyindriyābhāvena tesaṃ phoṭṭhabbabhāvo na vutto. Evañca katvā rūpadhātuyaṃ tesaṃ sappaṭighavacanañca samatthitaṃ hoti. Vuttañhi “asaññasattānaṃ anidassanasappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca dve mahābhūtā”tiādi (paṭṭhā. 2.22.17). Paṭigho hettha bhūtattayassa kāyappasādaṃ pati taṃnissayabhūtaghaṭṭanadvārena abhimukhabhāvo, so ca phusituṃ asakkuṇeyyasabhāvassa ghaṭṭanāya abhāvato natthi. Nanu “dve āyatanānī”ti ettha pariyāyāyatanaṃ adhippetaṃ, atha kasmā gandhāyatanādīnipi gahetvā “pañcāyatanānī”ti na vuttanti? “Nayadassanavasena desanā pavattā”ti vuttovāyamattho. Atha vā tattha rūpāyatanasseva vacanaṃ kadāci aññabhūmikānaṃ pasādassa visayabhāvaṃ sandhāya, na pana itaresaṃ abhāvato. Nāpi pariyāyena gandhāyatanādīnaṃ āyatanasabhāvābhāvato. Asaññīnañhi rūpāyatanaṃ samānabhūmikānaṃ vehapphalānaṃ, uparibhūmikānañca suddhavāsānaṃ pasādassa visayabhāvaṃ gacchati, na pana gandharasāti tesaṃyeva tatthāvacanaṃ yuttaṃ. Kathāvatthumhi ca nippariyāyena gandhāyatanādīnaṃ atthibhāvaṃ paṭijānantaṃ sandhāya paṭisedho kato. Yadipi cetaṃ vacanaṃ tattha gandhāyatanādīnaṃ abhāvavibhāvanaṃ na hoti, atthibhāvadīpanampi pana aññavacanaṃ natthevāti? Nayidamevaṃ aṭṭhakathāsu tattha nesaṃ atthibhāvassa niddhāretvā vuttattā. Yañhi aṭṭhakathāvacanaṃ pāḷiyā na virujjhati, taṃ pāḷi viya pamāṇabhūtaṃ agarahitāya ācariyaparamparāya yāvajjatanā āgatattā. Tattha siyā – yaṃ pāḷiyā na virujjhati aṭṭhakathāvacanaṃ, taṃ pamāṇaṃ. Idaṃ pana virujjhatīti? Nayidamevaṃ yathā na virujjhati[M 0.0122], tathā paṭipāditattā. Cakkhādīnaṃ āyatanānaṃ, tannissayānañca viññāṇānaṃ sattasuññatāsandassanatthaṃ bhagavato dhātudesanāti āyatanabhāvena vuttānaṃyeva dhātubhāvadīpanato dhātubhāvassāpi nesaṃ avacanaṃ yujjati eva, tasmā yathā pāḷiyā avirodho hoti, tathā cakkhudasakādivasena aṭṭhakathāyaṃ rūpagaṇanā katāti na ettha dhammatāvilomanāsaṅkāya okāsoti veditabbaṃ.

Here, for beings in the form realm, because the nose and tongue sense bases are absent, even though odors and tastes exist, they do not perform the function of a sense base. Therefore, without referring to them, it is said in the Pāli: “Five sense bases appear, six sense bases,” and so on. And regarding “three kinds of nutriment,” because edible nutriment is absent, the function of nutriment—which consists of producing materiality having nutriment as its eighth factor—is not performed. This is not because odors, tastes, and nutriment are entirely absent. Thus, when the subject and its function are absent, the object and the functional phenomenon are not mentioned. For in any existence where there is no subject, the object's nature as a sense base in an absolute sense is absent due to that cause. This is why even existing things are not mentioned, just as in the form realm, the earth, fire, and wind elements are not mentioned as the tangible sense base. But where something is mentioned, there its nature as a sense base in an absolute sense is stated, due to the presence of the subject, as seen with the form sense base in that very realm. If the sense base is established in an absolute sense due to the presence of the subject, how is it that for non-percipient devas, two sense bases appear? For non-percipient devas, the eye sense base does not exist, and because they lack the eye sense base, is their form sense base not an object for others? This is not a contradiction. By the same reasoning that the odor sense base, etc., are not mentioned for percipient beings in the form realm, the form sense base also should not be mentioned for non-percipient beings, and thus it should be said that they have one sense base. For depending on the range of their respective faculties, when sense bases are defined in an absolute sense for those who have them, the absence of such faculties in the form realm for percipient beings means that odors, etc., are not separately mentioned as sense bases. Since they do not transcend the nature of phenomena and become objects of mental consciousness, they are included within the “mental phenomena sense base,” and thus the Pāli texts say “five sense bases.” For this purpose, the term “mental phenomena sense base” is a general designation, or they are treated as secondary and called “five sense bases.” And the intention behind stating the form sense base for non-percipient beings implies that for percipient beings, odors, etc., should also be separately included. To illustrate this principle, it is said: “For non-percipient devas, two sense bases appear” (Vibh. 1017). Even though their own faculty is absent, since form does not transcend its nature as the visible sense base, it is still called the form sense base. By this method of illustrating the principle, including the three (odors, tastes, and tangibles), it is shown that percipient beings have eight sense bases, and non-percipient beings have five. And thus it should be accepted. Otherwise, in the form realm, since the earth elements, etc., cannot be touched, even verbal expression of them would not exist. For sound does not arise without impact and friction, and it is impossible to conceive of tangible things as lacking tangibility anywhere. And if the three elements designated as the tangible sense base were absent in the form realm, even the form sense base, etc., could not arise there. Therefore, even though the earth elements, etc., can be touched, since the body faculty is absent there, their tangible nature is not mentioned. Thus, in the form realm, their designation as “resistant” is also justified. For it is said: “For non-percipient beings, depending on one invisible and resistant great element, there are two great elements,” etc. (Paṭṭh. 2.22.17). Here, “resistance” refers to the three elements' facing the body sensitivity through the impact that is their basis. But since what cannot be touched lacks impact, it does not exist. Now, is it that in “two sense bases,” a figurative sense base is meant? Then why are the odor sense base, etc., not included when saying “five sense bases”? The meaning is: “The teaching proceeds according to the method of exposition,” as stated before. Or alternatively, there the form sense base alone is mentioned occasionally, referring to its being an object for the sensitivity of beings in other realms, but not because the others are absent. Nor is it that the odor sense base, etc., lack the nature of sense bases even figuratively. For the form sense base of non-percipient beings becomes an object for the sensitivity of the Vehapphala devas on the same plane and for the Suddhāvāsa devas on a higher plane, but not odors and tastes. Thus, their non-mention there is appropriate. And in the Kathāvatthu, the denial is made with reference to those who assert the absolute existence of the odor sense base, etc. Even if this statement does not explicitly clarify the absence of the odor sense base, etc., there, is there no other statement indicating their existence? This is not so, for in the commentaries, their existence is ascertained there. Whatever commentary statement does not contradict the Pāli texts is authoritative, like the Pāli itself, being unreproached due to its transmission through an unbroken lineage of teachers up to the present. Here, one might ask: “Is a commentary statement authoritative only if it does not contradict the Pāli? But this one contradicts.” This is not so, for it is presented in a way that does not contradict. The Blessed One's teaching on the elements is for the purpose of demonstrating the emptiness of a being with regard to the sense bases such as the eye and the consciousnesses dependent on them. Since this teaching reveals the element-nature of precisely those things spoken of as sense bases, their non-mention as elements is also fitting. Therefore, just as there is no contradiction in the Pāli, so too in the commentaries, the enumeration of forms is given in terms of the eye-decad, etc., and therefore there is no room for doubt arising from going against the nature of phenomena.

Eḷakassa jātakāle uṇṇā jātiuṇṇāti paṭhamo attho. Tato sukhumatarataṃ sandhāya “gabbhaṃ…pe… itipi vadantī”ti vuttaṃ. Sambhavanassa bhedo vā sambhavabhedo, pavattibhedoti attho.

The wool of a ram at the time of its birth is ‘birth-wool’; this is the first meaning. Then, with reference to its finer quality, it is said: ‘womb… and so on… thus they also say.’ Sambhavabhedo is the division of arising; the meaning is the division of occurrence.

Rūpībrahmesūti [V 0.0118] adhikaraṇe bhummaṃ, opapātikayonikesūti niddhāraṇeti dassento “opapātikayonikehi rūpībrahme niddhāretī”ti āha. Tena “opapātikayonikesū”ti sāmaññato vuttarāsito “rūpībrahmesū”ti visesaṃ niddhāreti. Na sametīti na saṃsandati, virujjhatīti attho. Yāya pāḷiyā na sameti, taṃ dassento “dhammahadayavibhaṅge hī”tiādimāha.

Regarding 'Rūpībrahmesu,' it is the locative case indicating the basis, and regarding 'opapātikayonikesu,' he states it to show the determination, saying, 'He determines the rūpībrahmas from among those born spontaneously.' Therefore, from the generally stated group 'opapātikayonikesu,' he determines the specific 'rūpībrahmesu.' 'It does not agree' means it does not coincide; the meaning is that it conflicts. To show the passage with which it does not agree, he says, 'In the Dhammahadayavibhaṅga, etc.'

Ekādasāti paripuṇṇāyatanassa saddāyatanavajjāni ekādasāyatanāni. Kassaci dasāyatanānīti andhassa cakkhāyatanavajjāni. Kassaci aparāni dasāyatanānīti badhirassa sotāyatanavajjāni. Kassaci navāyatanānīti andhabadhirassa cakkhusotāyatanavajjāni. Kassaci sattāyatanānīti gabbhaseyyakassa rūpagandharasakāyaphoṭṭhabbamanodhammāyatanavasena vuttaṃ.

Eleven (bases) means the eleven sense bases excluding the sound sense base for one with complete sense bases. For some, ten sense bases (appear) means those excluding the eye sense base for the blind. For some, another ten sense bases (appear) means those excluding the ear sense base for the deaf. For some, nine sense bases (appear) means those excluding the eye and ear sense bases for the blind and deaf. For some, seven sense bases (appear) is said with reference to one in the womb, in terms of the form, odor, taste, body, tangible, mind, and mental-object sense bases.

“Na vuttaṃ aṭṭhāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti idaṃ “na hi pāḷiyaṃ…pe… vuttā”ti etassa atthavivaraṇaṃ. Cakkhusotaghānavikalassa hi upapajjamānassa aṭṭheva āyatanāni siyunti. Sati ca aghānakupapattiyaṃ punapi “kassaci aparāni dasāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti vattabbaṃ siyā. Tathā ca sati yathā andhabadhirassa vasena “kassaci navāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti (vibha. 1007) ekavāraṃ vuttaṃ, evaṃ andhāghānakassa, badhirāghānakassa ca vasena “kassaci aparāni navāyatanāni, kassaci aparāni navāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti vattabbaṃ siyā, evaṃ na vuttanti imamatthaṃ dasseti “tathā…pe… na [M 0.0123] ca taṃ vutta”nti. Evaṃ dhātupātubhāvādipañhesūti “kassaci ekādasa dhātuyo pātubhavanti, kassaci dasa dhātuyo, kassaci aparā dasa dhātuyo, kassaci nava dhātuyo, kassaci satta dhātuyo pātubhavantī”ti (vibha. 1007) evaṃ dhātupātubhāvapañho veditabbo. Ādi-saddena “kassaci cuddasindriyāni pātubhavantī”tiādi (vibha. 1007) nayappavattā indriyapañhādayo saṅgahitā.

‘It is not said that eight sense bases appear’—this is an explanation of the meaning of ‘for it is not stated in the Pāli...’ For when one is reborn lacking eye, ear, and nose, there would indeed be eight sense bases. And if there were rebirth without a nose, then it would have to be said, ‘For some, another ten sense bases appear.’ Similarly, just as it is once stated regarding one who is blind and deaf, ‘For some, nine sense bases appear’ (Vibh. 1007), so too, regarding one who is blind and lacks a nose, or deaf and lacks a nose, it would have to be said, ‘For some, another nine sense bases, for some, another nine sense bases appear.’ Yet this is not stated—this meaning is shown by ‘thus... and that is not said.’ In the same way, regarding questions about the manifestation of elements, etc., ‘For some, eleven elements appear; for some, ten elements; for some, another ten elements; for some, nine elements; for some, seven elements appear’ (Vibh. 1007)—thus should the question about the manifestation of elements be understood. By the word ‘etc.,’ questions about faculties and so forth, proceeding in the same way, are included, such as ‘For some, fourteen faculties appear,’ etc. (Vibh. 1007).

Ettha ca yathā “sattati ukkaṃsato ca rūpānī”ti padaṃ “saṃsedajopapātīsū”ti ettha yonidvayavasena yojīyati, na evaṃ “avakaṃsato tiṃsā”ti idaṃ, idaṃ pana saṃsedajayonivaseneva yojetabbaṃ, ekayoganiddiṭṭhassāpi ekadeso sambandhaṃ labhatīti. Saṃsedajasseva ca jaccandhabadhiraaghānakanapuṃsakassa jivhākāyavatthudasakānaṃ vasena tiṃsa rūpāni uppajjantīti [V 0.0119] vuttaṃ, na opapātikassāti ayamettha aṭṭhakathāya adhippāyo. Ye pana “opapātikassa jaccandha…pe… uppajjantīti mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vutta”nti vadanti, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ. So hi pamādapāṭho. Evañca katvā āyatanayamakavaṇṇanāya “kāmadhātuyaṃ pana aghānako opapātiko natthi. Yadi bhaveyya, ‘kassaci aṭṭhāyatanāni pātubhavantī’ti vadeyyā”ti (yama. aṭṭha. āyatanayamaka 18-21) vakkhati. Apare panāhu “kassaci ekādasāyatanāni pātubhavanti, yāva ‘kassaci navāyatanānī’ti pāḷi opapātike sandhāya vuttā. Tasmā pubbenāparaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ avirodho siddho hoti, tathā ca yathāvuttapāḷiyā ayamatthavaṇṇanā aññadatthu saṃsandati sametiyevā”ti. Yaṃ paneke vadanti “opapātikaggahaṇena saṃsedajāpi saṅgayhanti. Tathā hi dhammahadayavibhaṅge ‘kāmadhātuyā upapattikkhaṇe kassaci ekādasāyatanāni pātubhavantī’tiādīnaṃ (vibha. 1007) uddese ‘opapātikānaṃ petāna’ntiādinā opapātikaggahaṇameva kataṃ, na saṃsedajaggahaṇa”nti, taṃ paripuṇṇāyatanānaṃyeva saṃsedajānaṃ opapātikesu saṅgahaṇavasena vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Tathā hi vakkhati “saṃsedajayonikā paripuṇṇāyatanāparipuṇṇāyatanabhāvena opapātikasaṅgahaṃ katvā vuttā”ti “padhānāya vā yoniyā sabbaṃ paripuṇṇāyatanayoniṃ dassetuṃ ‘opapātikāna’nti vutta”nti ca. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana [M 0.0124] yonidvayaṃ sarūpeneva pakāsetuṃ, saṃsedajayonivaseneva ca avakaṃsato pavattiṃ dassetuṃ opapātikayoniyā itaraṃ asaṅgahetvā “saṃsedajopapātīsū”ti vuttanti. Sabbaṃ taṃ vīmaṃsitvā gahetabbaṃ.

Here, just as the phrase “sattati ukkaṃsato ca rūpānī” is interpreted in terms of two types of birth in the word “saṃsedajopapātīsu,” so too is not the phrase “avakaṃsato tiṃsā.” This latter, however, should be interpreted solely in terms of the moisture-born type of birth, for even a part of what is stated under a single category obtains a connection. Moreover, it is said that thirty material phenomena arise only for the moisture-born—such as those blind from birth, deaf, anosmic, or impotent—in terms of the decades of the tongue, body, and heart-base. This is not the case for the spontaneously born, as this is the intended meaning in the commentary. However, those who claim that “for the spontaneously born, those blind from birth… etc., arise as stated in the Mahā-aṭṭhakathā” should not be accepted, for that is an erroneous reading. And so, the commentary on the Āyatanayamaka will state: “In the sensual realm, there is no spontaneously born being lacking a nose. If there were, one might say, ‘For some, eight sense bases manifest.’” Others, however, argue: “The Pāli from ‘For some, eleven sense bases manifest,’ up to ‘for some, nine sense bases,’ refers to the spontaneously born. Thus, there is no contradiction between earlier and later commentaries, and this explanation indeed aligns with the stated Pāḷi.” Yet some say: “The term ‘spontaneously born’ includes the moisture-born as well. For instance, in the Dhammahadayavibhaṅga, in the section stating ‘At the moment of rebirth in the sensual realm, for some, eleven sense bases manifest,’ the term ‘spontaneously born’ is used, not ‘moisture-born.’” This should be understood as referring only to moisture-born beings with complete faculties, who are included under the spontaneously born. As it will state: “The moisture-born, by being included under the spontaneously born in terms of having complete and incomplete faculties, are thus described,” or “To emphasize the primary type of birth, all complete-faculty births are indicated by the term ‘spontaneously born.’” However, in the commentary, the two types of birth are clearly distinguished in their own form, and the phrase “saṃsedajopapātīsu” is used to explain the process of decrease solely in terms of the moisture-born type of birth, without including the other type of birth under the spontaneously born. All this should be investigated and understood.

Cutipaṭisandhīnanti anantarātītacutiyā, tadanantarāya missāmissabhedāya paṭisandhiyā. Khandhādīhīti khandhārammaṇagatihetuvedanāpītivitakkavicārehi. Mahaggataajjhattārammaṇāya mahaggataajjhattārammaṇā, amahaggatabahiddhārammaṇāya amahaggatabahiddhārammaṇāti evamādino arūpabhūmīsuyeva cutipaṭisandhīnaṃ bhedābhedavisesassa sambhavato “nayamukhamattaṃ dassetvā”ti vuttaṃ. Ekaccasugatīti mahaggatavajjasugati adhippetāti āha “rūpārūpāvacarāna”ntiādi. Keci pana “yathā mahaggatāvajjā, evaṃ uttarakurukavajjā”tipi vadanti. Ekaccasugaticutiyāti vuttasugaticutiyā. Yadipi “ayaṃ nāma duggatipaṭisandhi na hotī”ti niyamo natthi, desanā pana sotapatitā gatāti vadanti. Niyatabodhisattāpekkhāya vā evaṃ vuttaṃ. Tesañhi ekaccaduggatipaṭisandhi natthi avīciādīsu anupapajjanato. “Ekaccaduggaticutiyā”ti etthāpi iminā nayena attho veditabbo.

By “Cutipaṭisandhīnaṃ” is meant the immediately preceding death and the immediately following rebirth-linking, which is of mixed and unmixed types. By “Khandhādīhi” is meant by way of aggregates, objects, destinations, causes, feelings, joy, initial thought, and sustained thought. For ‘for one whose object is sublime and internal,’ it is a sublime internal object; for ‘for one whose object is non-sublime and external,’ it is a non-sublime external object. Thus, since the distinctions and non-distinctions of death and rebirth-linking are possible only in the formless sphere, it is said, ‘merely showing the method.’ By “Ekaccasugati” is meant a fortunate destination excluding the sublime, as it states, ‘for those of the form and formless realms,’ etc. Some, however, say, ‘just as the sublime is excluded, so too is Uttarakuru.’ By “Ekaccasugaticutiyā” is meant the death in the stated fortunate destinations. Even though there is no fixed rule that ‘this named unfortunate rebirth-linking does not occur,’ it is said that the teaching has reached the stream-attainers. Or, it is stated with reference to definite bodhisattas. For them, certain unfortunate rebirth-linkings do not occur, as they do not arise in Avīci and so forth. By “Ekaccaduggaticutiyā”—here too, the meaning should be understood in this way.

Ekaccasugatipaṭisandhīti [V 0.0120] pana kāmāvacarasugatipaṭisandhi veditabbā. Sayamevāti attanā eva. “Bhedaviseso eva ca evaṃ vitthārena dassito”ti idaṃ “amahaggatabahiddhārammaṇāyā”tiādiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. “Catukkhandhāya…pe… paṭisandhi hotī”ti idaṃ pana abhedavisesadassanamevāti. Ekekasmiṃ bhedeti “amahaggatabahiddhārammaṇāyā”ti evamādike ekekasmiṃ bhāge. Tattha tatthevāti “amahaggatabahiddhārammaṇāya mahaggatabahiddhārammaṇā, amahaggatajjhattārammaṇāya mahaggatajjhattārammaṇā”tiādinā tasmiṃ tasmiṃ bhede, tattha tattheva vā bhavādike cavitvā upapajjantassa vasena cutipaṭisandhiyojanā veditabbā. Bhummatthe ayaṃ to-saddoti dassento “tato hetuṃ vināti tattha hetuṃ vinā”ti āha. Tassattho – tasmiṃ purimabhave nipphannaṃ avijjāsaṅkhārādikaṃ kāraṇaṃ vinā na hotīti.

By “Ekaccasugatipaṭisandhi” is to be understood a fortunate rebirth-linking in the sense sphere. By “Sayameva” is meant by oneself. The statement ‘the distinction of difference is thus explained in detail’ refers to what was stated earlier, such as ‘for one whose object is non-sublime and external,’ etc. The statement “‘Catukkhandhāya…pe… paṭisandhi hoti’” merely shows the absence of distinction. By ‘in each distinction’ is meant in each section, such as ‘for one whose object is non-sublime and external,’ etc. By “Tattha tattheva” is meant in each such distinction, such as ‘for one whose object is non-sublime and external, it is a sublime external object; for one whose object is non-sublime and internal, it is a sublime internal object,’ etc., the connection between death and rebirth-linking should be understood as occurring for one who, having passed away from a certain state of existence, is reborn there and then. To indicate that this particle ‘to’ has the meaning of ‘in that place,’ it states: “‘tato hetuṃ vinā’ means ‘tattha hetuṃ vinā.’” Its meaning is: it does not occur without the cause—such as ignorance, volitional formations, etc.—produced in that previous existence.

Atimandabhāvūpagamanaṃ sakiccāsamatthatā. Pañcadvārikaviññāṇavasena cuti paṭisiddhā, na tadanantaraviññāṇavasena. Svāyamattho “pañcannaṃ dvārāna”ntiādinā [M 0.0125] heṭṭhā aṭṭhakathāyamāgatoti āha “pañcadvārikaviññāṇānantarampi hi pubbe cuti dassitā”ti. Tattha yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. Cuticittena saddhiṃ cakkhāyatanādīnaṃ nirodho hotīti dassetuṃ “yamake cā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Pariṇatattāti paripākavasena pariyosānaṃ gatattāti adhippāyo. Phassādayo yathāvuttacetanāsahajātaphassādayo. Yathāupaṭṭhite kammādiārammaṇe anekavāraṃ uppattiyā santānassa abhisaṅkharaṇaṃ tattha paṭisandhiviññāṇapatiṭṭhānassa hetubhāvo.

The state of being excessively dull is the inability to fulfill one’s function. Death is precluded by way of the five-door consciousness, but not by way of the immediately following consciousness. This meaning, which appears in the commentary below by way of ‘of the five doors’ and so forth, is stated as, ‘For even after the five-door consciousness, death has been previously shown.’ What needs to be said here has already been stated below. To show that with the death-consciousness, the cessation of the eye-faculty and so forth occurs, the phrase ‘and in the Yamaka’ and so forth is stated. By ‘due to being mature’ is meant that it has reached its conclusion by way of ripening; this is the intention. Contact and so forth are contact and so forth co-arisen with volition as previously described. The conditioning of the continuity through repeated arising in relation to the object of kamma, and so forth, as it has presented itself, is the cause for the establishment of the rebirth-linking consciousness there.

Santānavasena nippajjamānānaṃ namanādikiriyānaṃ ekasmiṃ paṭisandhiviññāṇeyeva atthasiddhīti dassento āha “namana…pe… dassetī”ti. Pathaviyaṃ sabalapayogehīti pathaviyā ādhāraṇabhūtāya attano balena payogena ca karaṇabhūtena.

To show that the purpose of actions like bending and so forth, which are produced by way of continuity, is achieved only in a single rebirth-linking consciousness, it is stated: ‘bending...pe...shows.’ By ‘on the earth with one’s strength and effort’ is meant with the earth as the supporting basis, and with one’s own strength and effort as the instrumental cause.

Saddahetukoti saddassa padhānādibhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tādiso pabbatakucchiādipadesopi tassa hetuyeva. Padīpantarādīti ādi-saddena telavaṭṭiādike saṅgaṇhāti. Tato saddādippavattito pubbe abhāvā. Paṭighosādīnañhi saddādippavattito sati purimasiddhiyaṃ te saddādipaccayadesaṃ gaccheyyuṃ, na pana te atthīti vuttaṃ “tato pubbe abhāvā”ti. Upameyyepi evameva attho yojetabbo. Yathā ca hetudesaṃ na gacchati hetusamuppannaṃ, evaṃ tato nāgacchatīti [V 0.0121] āha “tasmā na…pe… āgata”nti. Te saddādayo paccayā etesanti tappaccayā. Vuttanayenāti upamāyaṃ vuttanayeneva. Purimabhavahetudese sannihitaṃ hutvā paṭisandhiviññāṇaṃ tato aññatra bhavantare taṃ upagantvā tappaccayaṃ na hotīti attho. Paccayato nibbattamānaṃ paccayuppannaṃ aññatra agantvā paccayadesaṃ anupagatameva hutvā nibbattatīti paṭhamo attho. Paṭhamaṃ paccayena samodhānagataṃ hutvā tato aññatra gantvā paccayuppannavatthubhāvaṃ nāpajjatīti dutiyo attho. Yathāsambhavanti yāya “na khīrato dadhi sambhūtaṃ siyā, na khīrasāmino dadhi siyā”ti ca khīradadhīsu ekantaṃ ekatāya nānatāya ca dosayojanā katā. Iminā nayena bījādīsu sabbahetūsu, aṅkurādīsu sabbahetusamuppannesu yathāsambhavaṃ hetuanurūpaṃ, hetusamupannānurūpañca dosayojanā kātabbā. Santānabaddhesu dhammesu ekantaekatāpaṭisedhena sassatagāhassa paṭisedhitattā vuttaṃ “sayaṃkataṃ [M 0.0126] sukhaṃ dukkhanti imaṃ diṭṭhiṃ nivāretī”ti. Tathā ekantanānatāpaṭisedhena ucchedagāho paṭisedhito hotīti āha “paraṃkataṃ sukhaṃ dukkhaṃ añño karoti, añño paṭisaṃvedetīti imaṃ diṭṭhiṃ nivāretī”ti. Tena katanāso, akatāgamo ca nivattito hotīti adhiccasamuppannadiṭṭhinivāraṇeneva niyatisabhāvavādapaṭisedhopi katoti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

By ‘caused by sound’ is stated with reference to sound being the primary factor and so forth. Such a place as a mountain cave and so forth is also its cause. By ‘another lamp, etc.’, by the word ‘ādi’ are included things like oil, wicks, and so forth. Because of its non-existence prior to the arising of sound and so forth from that. For if echoes and so forth had a prior establishment from the arising of sound and so forth, they would go to the place of the condition for sound and so forth; but they do not exist, hence it is said, ‘because of non-existence prior to that.’ The same meaning should be applied to the object of comparison as well. And just as what is produced from a cause does not go to the place of the cause, so too it does not come from that—thus it is stated: ‘therefore not...pe... come.’ Those sounds and so forth are conditions for these; hence, they are ‘conditioned by that.’ By ‘by the method stated’ is meant by the method stated in the simile. The meaning is that the rebirth-linking consciousness, having been present in the causal place of the previous existence, does not become conditioned by that by going elsewhere to another existence. The first meaning is that what arises from a condition, being conditionally arisen, arises without having gone elsewhere and without having reached the place of the condition. The second meaning is that, having first come into conjunction with the condition, it does not attain the state of being a conditionally arisen entity by going elsewhere from that. By ‘as is possible’ is meant just as in the case of milk and curd, the imputation of fault based on absolute identity and absolute difference is made by saying, ‘Curd would not arise from milk, nor would curd belong to the owner of the milk.’ In this way, regarding all causes like seeds and so forth, and all effects like sprouts and so forth, the imputation of fault should be made appropriately, in accordance with the cause and in accordance with what is produced from the cause. Since the grasping of eternalism is refuted by denying absolute identity in phenomena bound in a continuity, it is said, ‘It prevents the view that happiness and suffering are self-made.’ Similarly, by denying absolute difference, the grasping of annihilationism is refuted—hence it is said, ‘It prevents the view that happiness and suffering are made by another, that one acts and another experiences.’ Thus, the destruction of what has been done and the arrival of what has not been done are averted. It should be seen that by the very refutation of the view of accidental origination, the refutation of the doctrines of fatalism and inherent nature is also accomplished.

Tatthāti aṅkurādippabandhasaṅkhāte bhūtupādārūpasantāne. Tanti vijjāpāṭavādi. Aññassāti bālakāle katavijjāpariyāpuṇanādito aññassa. Saṅkhārato añño taṇhādiko aññapaccayo.

By ‘therein’ is meant in the continuity of primary and derived matter, which is described as the series beginning with the sprout. By ‘continuity’ is meant skill in knowledge and so forth. By ‘of another’ is meant other than the learning and thorough acquisition of knowledge done in childhood and so forth. Another condition, such as craving and so forth, is other than formations.

Niyyātanādi eva phalaṃ niyyātanādiphalaṃ, aphalitaṃ niyyātanādiphalaṃ etassāti aphali…pe… phalaṃ, yathāvuttakiriyākaraṇaṃ.

The result of leading out, etc., is itself the ‘result-of-leading-out-etc.’ For this, the result of leading out, etc., is unfruitful, hence ‘unfruitful... result,’ which is the performance of an action as has been stated.

Piṇḍavasenāti akatāvayavavibhāgassa samudāyassa vasena. Sabbatthāti puññābhisaṅkhārādike sabbasmiṃ paccayadhamme, paṭisandhibhede vā paccayuppannadhamme. Balavakammassa vasena yojetabbo. Bhuso nissayo hi upanissayo. “Avisesenā”ti vuttepi kāmāvacarapuññābhisaṅkhāro cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃ pañcannaṃ pavatte, itaro paṭhamajjhānavipākādīnaṃ pavatte ca paṭisandhiyañca paccayo hotīti pākaṭoyamatthoti taṃ avibhajitvā “sabbapuññābhisaṅkhāraṃ saha saṅgaṇhāti”cceva vuttaṃ. Dvādasākusalacetanābhedoti nayidaṃ samāsapadaṃ, sandhivasena panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Dvādasāti ca bhummatthe paccattavacanaṃ, dvādasasu akusalacetanāsu. Akusalacetanābhedoti [V 0.0122] ekādasākusalacetanāpabhedo, dvādasākusalacetanāpabhedo cāti attho veditabbo. Evañhi sati na ettha kiñci vicāretabbaṃ heṭṭhā vitthāritattā. Keci pana “dvādasākusalacetanābhedoti idaṃ ‘channaṃ pavatte’tiādinā yojetabba”nti vadanti, tesaṃ matena uddhaccacetanāya gahaṇe payojanaṃ vicāretabbameva paṭisandhiyāpi paccayabhāvassa vuttattā. Ekassāti ettha eva-saddo luttaniddiṭṭhoti āha “ekasseva paccayabhāvaniyamo”ti. Milātamālādīnanti milātamālakiliṭṭhavatthādīnaṃ. Manopadosikānaṃ tadaññavatthūnampi aniṭṭhatā kathaṃ na siyā, siyā evāti adhippāyo. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (vibha. aṭṭha. 227) pana pacuratābhāvato taṃ anāmasitvā “tathā kāmāvacaradevalokepī”ti vuttaṃ[M 0.0127]. Keci pana “devaloke aniṭṭhaṃ nāma parikappanavasena, sabhāvato pana tatthuppannaṃ iṭṭhamevā”ti vadanti.

By ‘by way of a mass’ is meant by way of an aggregate whose parts have not been divided. By ‘in all’ is meant in all conditional phenomena, such as meritorious formations, or in dependently arisen phenomena as distinguished by rebirth. It should be connected by way of strong kamma. For a strong support is a decisive support condition. Even when it is said ‘without distinction,’ the meritorious formation of the sense sphere is a condition for the five types of consciousness, such as eye-consciousness, in the course of existence, while the other is a condition for the resultants of the first jhāna, etc., in the course of existence and at rebirth-linking. This meaning is clear, so without analyzing it, it is simply stated that ‘it includes all meritorious formations together.’ ‘The twelvefold division of unwholesome volitions’ is not a compound word, but is stated by way of conjunction. ‘Twelve’ is a locative singular, meaning ‘among the twelve unwholesome volitions.’ ‘Division of unwholesome volitions’ should be understood as the division of eleven unwholesome volitions and the division of twelve unwholesome volitions. This being so, nothing needs to be investigated here, since it has been explained in detail below. Some, however, say that this ‘twelvefold division of unwholesome volitions’ should be connected with ‘in the course of existence of the six,’ etc. According to their view, the purpose of including the volition associated with restlessness must be investigated, since it has been stated that it is also a condition for rebirth-linking. By ‘of one’: here the word ‘eva’ is indicated elliptically, so it is said ‘the rule of being a condition for only one.’ By ‘of withered garlands, etc.’ is meant of withered garlands, soiled cloth, etc. How could there not be undesirability for the Manopadosika devas and for other things? There certainly would be—this is the intention. But in the Commentary (Vibhaṅga Aṭṭhakathā 227), since this is not prevalent, it is not mentioned, and it is simply stated, ‘similarly in the sense-sphere deva world.’ Some, however, say: ‘In the deva world, what is undesirable is so by way of conceptualization, but by its intrinsic nature, what arises there is only desirable.’

“Ekūnatiṃsacetanābhedampī”ti iminā uddhaccacetanāyapi pavattivipākadāyitaṃ anujānāti, aṭṭhakathāadhippāyavasena vā evamāha. Pañcadasannaṃ ahetukavipākaviññāṇānaṃ pañcaṭṭhānāni dve apanetvā avasesānaṃ terasannaṃ. Dve dve cakkhusotasampaṭicchanaviññāṇāni, tīṇi santīraṇānīti navannaṃ. Ekadesapaccayabhāvenāti ekadesassa vīsaticetanābhedassa kāmāvacaracittasaṅkhārassa paccayabhāvena ekūnatiṃsacetanābhedo samudāyo vutto. Svevāti avayavagatenāpi visesena samudāyo voharīyati yathā “alaṅkato rājakumāro”ti.

By ‘even the division of twenty-nine volitions,’ he allows that even the volition associated with restlessness gives a resultant in the course of existence, or he speaks thus according to the intention of the Commentary. For the fifteen rootless resultant consciousnesses, having removed two from the five occasions, it is a condition for the remaining thirteen. For the nine: two each of eye- and ear-receiving-consciousnesses, and three investigating consciousnesses. By ‘by way of being a condition in part’ is meant that the aggregate, the division of twenty-nine volitions, is spoken of because of the conditionality of one part, that is, the sense-sphere mental formation which is the division of twenty volitions. In the same way, an aggregate is designated by a particular that pertains to a part, just as it is said, ‘the prince is adorned.’

Yatthāti pañcavokārabhavaṃ sandhāyāha. Tattha hi “kāmāvacarasugatiyaṃ tāva ṭhitassā”tiādinā (vibha. aṭṭha. 227) paṭisandhiyaṃ pavattiyañca vipākassa vitthārappakāsanaṃ kataṃ. Catutthajjhānabhūmīti vehapphalabhūmiṃ vadati. Tenāha “asaññāruppavajjā”ti. Catutthajjhānameva hi bhāvanāvisesappavattaṃ asaññabhūmiṃ āruppabhūmiñca nipphādeti, catukkanayavasena vā saṃvaṇṇanā vuttāti veditabbā. Aṭṭha mahāvipākā, parittavipākesu pacchimo, pañca rūpāvacaravipākāti evaṃ cuddasannaṃ. Sattannanti sesānaṃ parittavipākānaṃyeva sattannaṃ.

“Where” refers to the five-constituent existence. For there, the detailed explanation of the resultant in rebirth-linking and in the course of existence has been made in the passage beginning, “First, for one established in a happy sense-sphere destination...” (Vibhaṅga Aṭṭhakathā 227). “The fourth jhāna plane” means the Vehapphala plane. Hence he says, “excluding the non-percipient and formless planes.” For it is the fourth jhāna itself, proceeding as a special development of meditation, that produces the non-percipient plane and the formless planes; or it should be understood that the explanation is given by way of the fourfold method. For the fourteen: eight great resultants, the last among the minor resultants, and five form-sphere resultants. “For seven” means for the remaining seven minor resultants.

Bhavādayoti bhavayonigatisattāvāse. Tiṇṇaṃ viññāṇānanti purimānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ āruppavipākaviññāṇānaṃ. Tīsūti pañcamādīsu tīsu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu. Vuttanayenāti “kāmabhave [V 0.0123] pana duggatiyaṃ aṭṭhannampi parittavipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte, no paṭisandhiya”ntiādinā (vibha. aṭṭha. 227) vuttanayeneva.

“Existence, etc.” means in existence, birth, destination, and abodes of beings. “Of the three consciousnesses” means of the first three formless resultant consciousnesses. “In the three” means in the three stations of consciousness beginning with the fifth. “In the way stated” means in the way stated beginning: “But in the sense-sphere existence, in a woeful destination, it is similarly a condition in the course of existence for all eight minor resultant consciousnesses, but not at rebirth-linking,” and so on (Vibhaṅga Aṭṭhakathā 227).

Viññāṇapadaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the exposition of the term 'consciousness' is concluded.

Nāmarūpapadaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Term 'Name-and-Form'

228. Yadipi suttante abhidhamme ca paṭiccasamuppādaniddese rūpapadassa desanābhedo natthi, abhidhamme pana “sabbaṃ rūpaṃ na hetū”tiādinā (dha. sa. 584) suttantato [M 0.0128] tassa desanābhedo atthevāti āha “suttantā…pe… bhedo”ti. Saṅkhyeyyesu paricchedato gahitesu atthasiddho tattha saṅkhyāparicchedoti vuttaṃ “atthato pana vuttameva hotī”ti.

228. Although in the Suttas and the Abhidhamma, in the exposition of dependent origination, there is no difference in the teaching of the term 'form,' yet in the Abhidhamma, because of such statements as “all form is not a root-cause” (Dhs 584), there is indeed a difference in its teaching from the Suttas. Hence he says “from the Suttas... difference.” When countable things are grasped by way of delimitation, the delimitation by number therein is established in meaning. Thus it is said: “But in terms of meaning, it is just as stated.”

Opapātikasattesūti vā sāmaññato sabbe opapātikā vuttā. Tesu brahmakāyikādiggahaṇena rūpāvacarāva vuttāti tadaññe sandhāya sesaopapātikānanti sesaggahaṇaṃ sātthakameva. Vuttanayenāti “dve vā tayo vā dasakā, omato ādinā sahā”tiādinā (vibha. aṭṭha. 227) rūpamissakaviññāṇe vuttanayena.

“In the case of spontaneously arisen beings”: or, in general, all spontaneously arisen beings are meant. Among them, by the inclusion of the Brahmakāyika devas, etc., only form-sphere beings are mentioned. Therefore, referring to the others, the inclusion of 'remaining' in “the remaining spontaneously arisen beings” is indeed meaningful. “In the way stated” means in the way stated in regard to consciousness mixed with form, beginning: “Two or three or ten decades...” (Vibhaṅga Aṭṭhakathā 227).

“Dve santatisīsānī”ti ārabbha yāva “satta santatisīsānī”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 228) ettakaṃ aṭṭhakathāpāṭhaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “sattakapariyosāna”nti. Ekekacittakkhaṇe tikkhattuṃ rūpuppattiṃ ananujānanto āha “iminādhippāyenā”ti. Cittassa uppādakkhaṇeyeva sabbaṃ rūpaṃ uppajjatīti hi attano adhippāyo.

Referring to the Commentary passage beginning “two heads of continuity” and extending up to “seven heads of continuity” (Vibhaṅga Aṭṭhakathā 228), it is said “ending with the set of seven.” Not allowing the arising of form three times in a single consciousness-moment, he says “with this intention.” For his own intention is that all form arises at the very arising-moment of consciousness.

“Rūpājanakakammaja”nti idaṃ bhūtakathanamattaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ pañcaviññāṇānaṃ ataṃsabhāvatābhāvā. Rūpājanakakammajanti vā cuticittaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Paṭisandhicittaṃ pana “pavattiya”nti imināva nivattitaṃ. “Sabbesampi cuticittaṃ rūpaṃ na samuṭṭhāpetī”ti (dha. sa. mūlaṭī. 636) aṭṭhasālinīṭīkāyaṃ vuttovāyamattho. Pañcaviññāṇakkhaṇe tappaccayā rūpuppattiyā abhāvena vuttaṃ “pañcaviññāṇappavattikālaṃ [V 0.0124] sandhāyā”ti. Tatthāpi asahajātaviññāṇapaccayā attheva rūpuppattīti āha “sahajātaviññāṇapaccayañcā”ti. Bhavaṅgādīti bhavaṅgasampaṭicchanasantīraṇatadārammaṇāni. Aññenāti yathāvuttakammaviññāṇato aññena abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇena. Rūpameva hi kusalākusalakiriyacittappavattikkhaṇe abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇapaccayā uppajjati, na nāmaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ. Taṃjanakenāti bhavaṅgādijanakena. Kammaviññāṇappaccayā vipākacittappavattikāle vipākanāmassa kammasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca vasena. Sahajātaviññāṇapaccayā pana itaracittappavattikālepi vipāko vipākanāmavasena, cittasamuṭṭhānarūpavasena ca nāmarūpassa sambhavo dassetabboti āha “sahajāta…pe… yojetabba”nti. Rūpasaddena ca attano ekadesenāti sambandho. “Sarūpānaṃ ekadeso ekavibhattiya”nti (pāṇinī 1.2.64) saddalakkhaṇaṃ sandhāyāha [M 0.0129] “sarūpānaṃ ekadeso”ti. Icchito hi ekadesarūpānampi ekadeso yathā “nidassitavipakkhehī”ti. Nidassito ca nidassitavipakkho ca nidassitavipakkhoti ayañhettha attho. “Ṭhāna”nti iminā sesasaddassa atthaṃ vadati. Sarūpena ṭhapanañhi idha sesanaṃ.

“Born of kamma that generates form”: this should be seen as a mere statement of fact, because the five sense-consciousnesses do not have that nature. Or, “born of kamma that generates form” is said referring to the death consciousness. But the rebirth-linking consciousness is excluded by this word “in the course of existence.” This meaning is as stated in the Aṭṭhasālinī-mūlaṭīkā (Dhs-mṭ 636): “The death consciousness of all does not generate form.” It is said “referring to the time of the process of the five consciousnesses” because at the moment of the five consciousnesses there is no arising of form conditioned by them. Even there, there is indeed an arising of form conditioned by non-conascent consciousness, so he says “and conditioned by conascent consciousness.” “Bhavaṅga, etc.” means bhavaṅga, receiving, investigating, and registration. “By another” means by another formational consciousness, other than the aforesaid kamma-consciousness. For at the moment of the process of wholesome, unwholesome, and functional consciousnesses, only form arises conditioned by formational consciousness, not the mental phenomenon, bhavaṅga. “By that which generates it” means by that which generates bhavaṅga, etc. Conditioned by kamma-consciousness, at the time of the process of resultant consciousness, the arising of name-and-form is by way of resultant mentality and kamma-born form. But conditioned by conascent consciousness, even at the time of the process of other consciousnesses, the occurrence of name-and-form should be shown by way of resultant as resultant mentality and by way of consciousness-born form. Thus he says “conascent... should be connected.” And the connection is: by a part of itself with the word 'form.' Referring to the grammatical rule “a single remainder of similar forms” (Pāṇini 1.2.64), he says “a single remainder of similar forms.” For a single remainder of even a part of the forms is intended, as in `nidassitavipakkhehi`. For here the meaning is: `nidassitavipakkha` is that which is shown and that which has a shown opponent. By `ṭhāna` he states the meaning of the word `sesa`. For here, remaining is establishing by its own form.

Yaṃ-taṃ-saddānaṃ abyabhicāritasambandhattā avuttampi tato-saddaṃ ānetvā āha “tato yuttameva idanti yojetabba”nti. Vipākassa ajanakaṃ vipākājanakaṃ, nissandaphalamattadāyakakammaṃ, taṃ samuṭṭhānaṃ etassāti vipākājanakakammasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Vuttanayenāti “vatthukāyavasena rūpato dve santatisīsāni, tayo ca arūpino khandhā”tiādinā (vibha. aṭṭha. 228) vuttena nayena. Ubhayanti nāmaṃ rūpañca.

Because of the invariable connection of the words `yaṃ` and `taṃ`, having supplied the unstated word `tato`, he says 'it should be connected thus: “Therefore this is appropriate.”' That which does not generate a resultant is non-resultant-generating; it is kamma that gives only a flow-on fruit; that is the origin of this, thus it is 'originated from kamma that does not generate a resultant.' “In the way stated” means in the way stated beginning: “By way of the physical basis, from form two heads of continuity, and the three formless aggregates,” etc. (Vibhaṅga Aṭṭhakathā 228). “Both” means name and form.

Kammārammaṇapaṭisandhiādikāleti ettha ādi-saddena sammasanādikālasaṅgaho daṭṭhabbo. Tanti abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇaṃ.

At the time of rebirth-linking with kamma as object, etc.: here, by the word 'etc.' the inclusion of the time of comprehension, etc., should be understood. “That” refers to the formational consciousness.

Yadipi “atthi rūpaṃ cittasamuṭṭhāna”ntiādivacanato (dha. sa. 584) rūpassapi viññāṇapaccayatā suttato jānitabbā, viññāṇasannissitā iṭṭhānubhavanādayo tasmiṃ sati sabbhāvato, asati ca abhāvato yathā saddheyyādivatthumhi saddhādayoti nāmassapi yuttito viññāṇapaccayatā siddhā, aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana vuttamatthaṃ dassento “suttato nāmaṃ…pe… jānitabba”nti āha. Yāvadeva paccayapaccayuppannadhammamattatāvibhāvanamukhena aviparītato pavattinivattisandassanaṃ paṭiccasamuppādadesanā, tāvadeva ca dhammacakkappavattananti dassento “yasmā”tiādimāha[V 0.0125]. Yasmā pana pavattinivattivibhāvanato saccadesanāva paccayākāradesanā, saccadesanā ca dhammacakkappavattanaṃ. Yathāha “idaṃ dukkhanti me bhikkhave…pe… bārāṇasiyaṃ isipatane migadāye anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattita”ntiādi, tasmā “viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpa”nti padassa saccadesanābhāvadīpanena dhammacakkappavattanabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ “nāmarūpamattatāvacaneneva vā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Even though from the statement “there is form originating from mind” (Dhs. 584) and so on, the conditionality of form on consciousness is to be known from the suttas; and since pleasant experiences and so on, being dependent on consciousness, exist when it is present and are absent when it is not—just as faith and other mental states exist in relation to objects like faith-objects—thus, even name (nāma) is rightly understood to depend on consciousness as a condition. However, explaining the meaning stated in the commentary, he says, “From the suttas, name... should be understood.” The teaching of dependent origination, being solely the demonstration of the undeviating arising and ceasing of phenomena through the mere manifestation of conditioned phenomena and their conditions, is precisely the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma. Showing this, he says “because” and so on. Since the teaching of the conditional structure, by way of explaining arising and ceasing, is itself the teaching of the truths, and the teaching of the truths is the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma—as stated: “This is suffering, monks... at Isipatana in the Deer Park near Varanasi, the unsurpassed Wheel of Dhamma was set in motion” and so on—therefore, to indicate that the phrase “with consciousness as condition, name-and-form” reveals its nature as a teaching of the truths and its nature as the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma, it is said, “or simply by the statement of the mere name-and-form.”

Nāmarūpapadaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the exposition of the term 'name-and-form' is concluded.

Saḷāyatanapadaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Term 'the Six Sense Bases'

229. Yathāsambhavanti [M 0.0130] sambhavānurūpaṃ. Tena catunnaṃ tāva bhūtānaṃ sahajātanissayaatthiavigatavasena cakkhāyatanādīnaṃ pañcannaṃ paccayabhāvo, vatthūsu pana hadayavatthuno chaṭṭhāyatanassa paṭisandhiyaṃ sahajātanissayaaññamaññavippayuttaatthiavigatavasena, pavattiyaṃ yasmā anantaracittena saddhiṃ uppannameva vatthu ṭhitippattiyā balavabhāvena tassa nissayo bhavituṃ sakkoti, na sahajātaṃ, tasmā purejātanissayavippayuttaatthiavigatavasena. Itaravatthūnaṃ pañcaviññāṇasaṅkhātassa chaṭṭhāyatanassa indriyapaccayavasena ca, jīvitassa indriyaatthiavigatavasena paccayabhāvo vuttoti daṭṭhabbo. Ekappakārenevāti yathā cakkhādīnaṃ manāyatanassa paṭiniyatadassanādikiccānuvidhānato niyato ekappakāreneva paccayabhāvo, na evaṃ rūpāyatanādīnaṃ, tesaṃ pana rūpārammaṇādinā pakārantarena tassa paccayabhāvoti “aniyamato”ti vuttaṃ. Keci pana “niyamato”ti padaṃ “sasantatipariyāpanna”nti iminā sambandhitvā atthaṃ vadanti “ekantena sasantatipariyāpanna”nti.

229. In accordance with how they arise. Thus, the four great elements are a condition for the five sense bases by way of co-nascence, support, presence, and non-disappearance. But among the bases, for the sixth base, the heart-base, at rebirth-linking it is a condition by way of co-nascence, mutuality, support, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. In the course of existence, because the base that has arisen together with the immediately preceding consciousness can, on account of its strength upon reaching the static phase, be a support for it, but not a co-nascent one, it is therefore a condition by way of pre-nascence, support, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. It should be understood that the other bases are a condition for the sixth base, known as the fivefold consciousness, by way of the faculty condition, and that life is a condition by way of the faculty, presence, and non-disappearance conditions. 'In a single mode' means that just as the eye-base and so on are a condition for the mind-base in a fixed, single mode by conforming to the specific functions of seeing and so on, it is not so for the form-base and so on. For them, the state of being a condition for it is in another mode, such as being a form-object; therefore, 'not fixed' is stated. Some, however, connect the word 'fixedly' with 'included in one's own continuity' and state the meaning as 'exclusively included in one's own continuity'.

“Chaṭṭhāyatanañca manāyatanañca chaṭṭhāyatana”nti iminā viggahena atthato, itarehi dvīhi saddatopi atthatopi sarūpataṃ dasseti. “Cakkhādīhi saha ‘saḷāyatana’nti vutta”nti vuttanayena ekasesaṃ katvā manāyatanaṃ cakkhādīhi saddhiṃ “saḷāyatana”nti pāḷiyaṃ vuttaṃ “nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatana”nti. Yathāvuttoti “chaṭṭhāyatanañca manāyatanañcā”tiādinā attanā [V 0.0126] vuttappakāro. Sabbatthāti nāmarūpasaddena saḷāyatanasaddena ca saddasarūpatāsu, atthasarūpatāsu vā. Yadi suttantabhājanīye vipākachaṭṭhāyatanameva adhippetaṃ, atha kasmā “itaraṃ panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Avipākañhi tattha itaranti adhippetanti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “paccayanaye panā”tiādi.

By this analysis, 'The sixth base and the mind-base are the sixth base,' he shows the identity in meaning; by the other two, he shows the identity in both word and meaning. 'With the eye, etc., it is called the sixfold sense base'—thus, by the stated method, having made a grammatical ellipsis (ekasesa), the mind-base together with the eye-base, etc., is called the 'sixfold sense base' in the Pāli, as in 'with name-and-form as condition, the sixfold sense base.' 'As stated' means in the manner stated by himself, beginning with 'the sixth base and the mind-base.' 'In all cases' means in the verbal forms of the words 'name-and-form' and 'sixfold sense base,' or in their semantic forms. If in the Suttanta analysis only the resultant sixth base is intended, then why is it said, 'but the other,' etc.? In reference to the objection that the non-resultant is intended there as 'the other,' he says, 'but in the conditional method,' etc.

Sahajātādīsu hetuāhārindriyapaccaye pakkhipitvā dasadhā, tato ekaṃ apanetvā navadhā, tato ekaṃ apanetvā aṭṭhadhā paccayabhāvo veditabbo. Evamettha sādhāraṇavasena avakaṃso, hetuādiasādhāraṇavasena ukkaṃsoti jhānādīnampi vasena veditabbo.

The state of being a condition should be understood as tenfold by including the root, nutriment, and faculty conditions among the co-nascence and other conditions. Then, by removing one, it is ninefold; then, by removing another, it is eightfold. Thus, here the minimum is by way of what is common, and the maximum is by way of what is uncommon, such as root and so on; this should also be understood by way of jhāna and so on.

Paṭisandhiyaṃ [M 0.0131] arūpadhammā kammajarūpassa uppādakkhaṇe paccayā hontīti “pavatte”ti viseseti. “Pacchājātavippayuttādayo evā”ti niyamena sahajātapurejātavippayuttādayo nivatteti.

He specifies 'in the course of existence' because at rebirth-linking, immaterial phenomena are conditions for kamma-born materiality at the moment of its arising. By the rule 'only post-nascence, dissociation, and so on,' he excludes co-nascence, pre-nascence, dissociation, and other conditions.

“Avasesamanāyatanassā”ti avasesaggahaṇampi pakaraṇato visiṭṭhavisayamevāti dassetuṃ “pañcakkhandhabhave”tiādimāha, yato aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “vatthurūpa”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Yathāsambhavaṃ yojetabboti nāmarūpassa paṭisandhiyaṃ sahajātaaññamaññanissayaatthiavigatādipaccayabhāvo sahajātādisādhāraṇapaccayabhāvo, sampayuttavipākahetuāhārindriyādipaccayabhāvo sampayuttādiasādhāraṇapaccayabhāvo nāmassa, rūpassa pana vippayuttapaccayabhāvo yojetabbo.

'Of the remaining mind-base'—to show that the inclusion of 'remaining' refers only to a specific scope according to the context, he says, 'in the five-aggregate existence,' etc., because in the commentary, 'the material base,' etc., is stated. It should be connected as is possible: for name-and-form at rebirth-linking, the state of being a condition by way of co-nascence, mutuality, support, presence, non-disappearance, and so on, is the common conditionality of co-nascence and so on. The state of being a condition by way of association, result, root, nutriment, faculty, and so on, is the uncommon conditionality of association and so on for name. For form, however, the dissociation condition should be connected.

Saḷāyatanapadaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the exposition of the term 'sixfold sense base' is concluded.

Phassapadaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Term 'Contact'

230. Tadabhedavasenāti tassa phassassa abhedavasena, phassabhāvasāmaññenāti attho. Na yuttaṃ ekasseva vacanaṃ. Aññassāpīti yathāvuttato aññassāpi. Sabbāyatanato hi ekassa phassassa asambhavacodanāyaṃ tappasaṅgena ekāyatanato anekassāpi sambhavo natthīti codanā “īdisī dhammatā natthī”ti ñāpanatthāti dasseti “aññassāpī”tiādinā. Nidassanavasenāti udāharaṇadassanavasena[V 0.0127]. Ekaphassassa sambhavatoti kāraṇāpadeso. Ekaphassasambhavassa labbhamānattā “saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso”ti bhagavatā vuttanti parihāraṃ dassentoti yojanā. Sesesūti ekantiādīsu. Navadhā paccayatte ekaṃ vipākamanāyatanaṃ vibhāvaye. Tathā cāti ārammaṇapurejātaatthiavigatavasena. Yvāyaṃ paccayabhāvo yādisānaṃ hoti, taṃ dassetuṃ “paccuppannāni…pe… sandhāya vutta”nti āha. Atītānāgatakālavimuttānampi ārammaṇamattatāya sambhavato āha “ārammaṇa…pe… sandhāya vutta”nti. Tattha tanti rūpāyatanādiṃ.

230. ‘By way of non-distinction’ means by way of non-distinction of that contact; the meaning is by way of the general nature of contact. It is not proper to speak of only one. ‘Of another as well’ means of another as has been stated. The purpose of the objection—that by implication from the challenge against the impossibility of one contact arising from all sense-bases, the arising of many contacts from one sense-base is also impossible—is to make known that ‘such a nature of things does not exist’; this is shown by ‘of another as well,’ etc. ‘By way of an illustration’ means by way of showing an example. ‘Because of the possibility of a single contact’ is a statement of the reason. The connection is that the Blessed One’s statement, “With the sixfold sense base as condition, contact,” is given as a rejoinder because the arising of a single contact is obtainable. ‘In the remaining cases’ means in such cases as ‘one.’ One should analyze one resultant mind-base in its ninefold conditionality. ‘And thus’ means by way of object, pre-nascence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions. To show for what kind of things this state of being a condition holds, he said, “It is said with reference to present… etc.” Since they are possible merely as objects even when they are past, future, or timeless, he said, “It is said with reference to the object… etc.” Therein, ‘that’ refers to the form base, etc.

Phassapadaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the exposition of the term 'contact' is concluded.

Vedanāpadaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Term 'Feeling'

231. Anantarādīhīti [M 0.0132] anantarasamanantarūpanissayanatthivigatapaccayehi. Upanissayeti anantarūpanissaye. Anantarasamanantarapaccayā hi anantaratāvaseneva anantarūpanissaye antogadhā. Natthivigatapaccayā pana anantarasamanantarapaccayadhammānaṃyeva tathābhāvato tadantogadhā. Tassāti upanissayassa.

231. ‘By immediacy, etc.’ means by the immediacy, contiguity, decisive support, absence, and disappearance conditions. ‘In decisive support’ means in immediacy decisive support. For the immediacy and contiguity conditions are included in immediacy decisive support simply by way of their immediacy. But the absence and disappearance conditions are included therein because the phenomena that are the immediacy and contiguity conditions are of such a nature. ‘Of that’ means of the decisive support.

Sabbassāti vipākassa, avipākassa ca. Paṭisandhibhavaṅgacuticittasampayuttāya hi vedanāya sahajātamanosamphasso vuttanayena aṭṭhadhā paccayo hoti. Anantaro anantarādinā, anānantaro upanissayavaseneva paccayo hoti. Sambhavadassanañcetaṃ, na tāsaṃ manodvārikabhāvadassananti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

‘Of all’ means of both resultant and non-resultant. For the mind-contact co-nascent with the feeling associated with the rebirth-linking, life-continuum, and death consciousnesses is a condition in eight ways according to the method stated. What is immediate is a condition by way of immediacy, etc.; what is not immediate is a condition only by way of decisive support. And this should be seen as showing their possibility, not as showing their state of being mind-door processes.

Vedanāpadaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the exposition of the term 'feeling' is concluded.

Taṇhāpadaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Term 'Craving'

232. Yathā [V 0.0128] ca rasāyanajāni ojājīvitāni, evaṃ taṃnimittaṃ sukhaṃ, tadapaneyyaṃ jarādidukkhañca dhammārammaṇabhāvena yojetabbaṃ.

232. Just as nutritional essence and vitality are born from elixirs, so happiness has that as its cause; and the suffering of old age, etc., which is to be removed by that happiness, should be construed as a mental object.

Kammaphalābhipatthanāvasena sattā kammānipi āyūhantīti sātisayaṃ taṇhāya vipākavedanā upanissayo, na tathā itarāti āha “vipākā visesena…pe… avisesena itarā cā”ti. Itarāti avipākāti attho. “Sukhamicceva bhāsitā”ti idaṃ iṭṭhasabhāvaṃyeva upekkhaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, na aniṭṭhasabhāvaṃ. Tenāha “upekkhā panā”tiādi. Sabbassāti avītarāgassa vītarāgassa ca vedanāvato puggalassa.

Because beings undertake actions by way of desiring the fruit of kamma, resultant feeling is a preeminent decisive support for craving, but not so the other. Thus he said: “Resultant feelings in particular… and the other not in particular.” ‘The other’ means non-resultant. The statement “spoken of as only pleasant” was said with reference only to equanimity that has a desirable nature, not to that with an undesirable nature. Therefore he said, “But equanimity…” etc. ‘Of all’ means of a person possessing feeling, whether not free from lust or free from lust.

Vedanāpaccayā evāti ayaṃ niyamo niyamantaranivattanaparoti nāssa paccayantaranivattanatthatā daṭṭhabbā. Etena paccayuppannantarapaṭikkhepopi nivattito hoti.

‘Only with feeling as condition’—this determination is for the purpose of precluding another determination; it should not be seen as being for the purpose of precluding another condition. By this, the rejection of another conditioned phenomenon is also precluded.

Taṇhāpadaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the exposition of the term 'craving' is concluded.

Upādānapadaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Term 'Clinging'

233. Purimadiṭṭhinti [M 0.0133] “sassato attā”ti (dī. ni. 1.31) pageva abhiniviṭṭhaṃ sassatagāhaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tenāha “attaggahaṇaṃ…pe… daṭṭhabba”nti. Upādiyamānanti gaṇhantaṃ. Lokoti vā gahaṇanti yaṃ “loko sassato”ti gahaṇaṃ, sā diṭṭhīti attho. Tenāha “diṭṭhupādānabhūta”nti. “Dhammasaṅkhepa…pe… diṭṭhimattamevā”ti idaṃ byavahitānaṃ padānaṃ sambandhadassanaṃ. Tattha saṅkhepato taṇhādaḷhattaṃ, saṅkhepato diṭṭhimattameva cattāri upādānānīti adhippāyo. Dhammasaṅkhepavitthāratoti samudāyabhūtato dhammasaṅkhepavitthārato tadavayavabhūtaṃ saṅkhepaṃ vitthārañca niddhāreti.

233. ‘A former view’ was said with reference to the grasping of eternalism that has been adhered to from the very start, as in “the self is eternal.” Therefore he said: “The grasping of self… should be seen.” ‘Being clung to’ means grasping. ‘World’ or ‘grasping’ means that the grasping “the world is eternal” is the view. Therefore he said: “which has become the clinging to views.” The phrase “A summary of things… is merely a view” shows the connection of the separated words. Therein, the intention is that in brief it is the tenacity of craving, and in brief the four clingings are merely a view. From the summary and detail of things, which constitute the whole, he determines the summary and detail which constitute its parts.

Sassatagāhapubbaṅgamo, ucchedagāhapubbaṅgamo ca attagāhoti yojanā. Tesanti yathāvuttasassatucchedagāhānaṃ [V 0.0129] mūlabhāvena vidhāyakattā sāmibhūto. Ādinā vāti “paṭhamaṃ attavādupādāna”ntiādinā vā vākyena.

The connection is that the grasping of self is preceded by the grasping of eternalism and preceded by the grasping of annihilationism. ‘Of them’ means being the master of the aforesaid graspings of eternalism and annihilationism because of being their root and their originator. Or by the phrase beginning ‘etc.,’ that is, by the sentence beginning, “Firstly, the clinging to the doctrine of self….”

Yena bhavassādena gadhitacitto bhavanibbattakaṃ kammaṃ katvā upapanno, sā bhavanikanti santāne cirānubandhā abhiṇhuppattikā upapannamattassa uppajjatīti āha “yadipi…pe… pavattitabbattā”ti. Arahattamaggavajjhattā bhavarāgassapi kāmupādānabhāvo atthevāti āha “taṇhādaḷhattaṃ na hotīti maññamāno”ti. Bhavarāgopi hi savisaye daḷhaṃ pavattatīti. Sabbāpi taṇhā kāmupādānanti etthāpi tassa arahattamaggavajjhatā vuttāti ānetvā yojetabbaṃ.

He said, ‘Although… because it is bound to occur,’ to show that for one who has been reborn after performing kamma that generates becoming, his mind being ensnared by the gratification in becoming, that craving for existence—long-pursuing in his continuity and arising frequently—arises for him as soon as he is reborn. To counter one who might think, ‘It is not the tenacity of craving,’ he said that because it is abandoned by the path of arahantship, even lust for existence has the nature of sensual clinging. For lust for existence, too, proceeds tenaciously in its own domain. Here too, in the statement ‘All craving is sensual clinging,’ it should be brought in and connected that this is said because it is abandoned by the path of arahantship.

Uppattiṭṭhānabhūtā na ārammaṇabhūtāti adhippāyo. Tenāti khandhānaṃ ālayabhāvena. Ārammaṇānantarapakatūpanissayāti ārammaṇūpanissayaanantarūpanissayapakatūpanissayā. Anantarapaccayādīnanti anantarasamanantaraārammaṇapaccayādīnaṃ.

The intention is that they have become a basis for arising, not that they have become a basis as object. ‘By that’ means because the aggregates are a home. ‘Object, immediacy, and natural decisive support’ means object decisive support, immediacy decisive support, and natural decisive support. ‘Of the immediacy condition, etc.’ means of the immediacy, contiguity, object conditions, etc.

Upādānapadaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Term 'Clinging' is finished.

Bhavapadaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Term 'Becoming'

234. “Bhavatī”ti [M 0.0134] idaṃ upapattibhavanibbacanaṃ. Dvayassāti kammupapattibhavadvayassa. Nipphādanaphalaṃ phalassa uppādanasamatthatā. Nibbattanaṃ nipphādanaṃ.

234. This 'it becomes' is the etymological explanation of rebirth-becoming. 'Of the twofold' refers to the pair of kamma-becoming and rebirth-becoming. 'Productive result' means the capacity to produce the fruit. 'Generation' means production.

“Bhagavaṃmūlakā”ti (a. ni. 8.83; 9.1; 10.58; 11.19) viya “saññāvaṃbhavo”ti vattabbe atthi-atthe vā vaṃ-saddo luttaniddiṭṭhoti āha “saññābhavo”ti. Tassa vā attheti tassa vantusaddassa atthe, atthi-attheti attho. Akāraṃ katvāti yathā “pītisukhaṃ assa atthī”ti atthe akāraṃ katvā uppādetvā jhānaṃ pītisukhanti vuccati, evaṃ saññā assa atthīti sañño, bhavo, sova saññabhavo. Ekasminti rūpakkhandhe eva. Pavattattāti pavattakapavattanaṭṭhānānaṃ abhedepi upacāravasena bhinnaṃ viya katvā dasseti.

Just as in 'rooted in the Blessed One' (AN 8.83; 9.1; 10.58; 11.19), when `saññāvaṃbhavo` (becoming possessing perception) should be said, the particle `vaṃ` in the sense of 'there is' is elided, so he says `saññābhavo` (perception-becoming). Or, it is in the sense of its possessive suffix `vantu`, that is, in the sense of 'there is.' By making an 'a': just as in the sense 'there is bliss and happiness for him,' by making an 'a' and forming the word, `jhāna` is called `pītisukha` (with bliss and happiness), so too, in the sense 'there is perception for him,' it becomes `sañño bhavo`, and that is `saññābhavo`. 'In one' means in just the aggregate of form. 'Because of its occurrence': although there is no difference between the prompter, the prompting, and the place, he shows them as if they were distinct by way of figurative speech.

Kammasaṅkhātatanti [V 0.0130] “kamma”nti vattabbataṃ, kammakoṭṭhāsataṃ vā. “Cetanāhaṃ, bhikkhave, kammaṃ vadāmī”tiādinā (a. ni. 6.63) suttepi cetanāya kammabhāvo āgatova. Nippariyāyena pana cetanāva kammabhavoti vuttamatthaṃ abhidhammapāḷiyāva sādhento “vuttañhī”tiādimāha. Imāya hi vedanāsaññāviññāṇakkhandhehi, manāyatanamanoviññāṇadhātūhi, saṅkhārakkhandhadhammāyatanadhammadhātuekadesena ca kammabhavassa sampayuttataṃ vadantiyā dhātukathāpāḷiyā tassa cetanābhāvo dīpitoti.

'Designated as kamma' means that which is to be called 'kamma,' or a portion of kamma. Even in the sutta beginning 'Volition, bhikkhus, I say is kamma' (AN 6.63), the nature of volition as kamma has already been established. However, to establish with the Abhidhamma Canon the meaning stated, that volition itself is kamma-becoming without qualification, he says, 'For it was stated,' etc. For by the Dhātukathā-pāḷi—which speaks of the association of kamma-becoming with the aggregates of feeling, perception, and consciousness; with the mind base and the mind-consciousness element; and with a portion of the aggregate of formations, the phenomena base, and the phenomena element—its nature as volition is illuminated.

Dhammabhedatoti cetanācetanāsampayuttabhāvena, kusalākusalābyākatabhāvena ca dhammavibhāgato. “Punavacana”nti imināva punaruttidosāpatti paṭiññātāti parassa āsaṅkaṃ dassento “sātthakamevidaṃ punavacananti etaṃ na yuttanti ce”ti āha. Bhavekadesabhāvenāti kammabhavassa ekadesattā saṅkhārānaṃ. Tena yesaṃ dhammānaṃ samudāyo bhavo vutto, tadekadesā saṅkhārā, samudāyekadesā ca atthato bhinnā evāti vuttamevetanti dasseti. Puna yathāvuttameva bhedaṃ manasi katvā atthato punavacanābhāvaṃ dassento “parena vā”tiādimāha.

'By the distinction of phenomena' means by the division of phenomena in terms of being associated with volition or not, and in terms of being wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate. To show another's doubt that by this very word 'repetition' the fault of redundancy is admitted, he says: 'If one should think: "This repetition is meaningful, so this is not proper..."' 'As being a part of becoming' means because formations are a part of kamma-becoming. Thereby he shows that it has already been said that formations are a part of those phenomena whose collection is called 'becoming,' and a part of a collection is indeed different in meaning. Again, keeping in mind the distinction just stated, to show the absence of repetition in meaning, he says, 'Or by another way,' etc.

Antogadheti kāmabhavādiantogadhe saññābhavādike. Kāmabhavādiketi kāmarūpārūpabhave.

'Included within' means it includes perception-becoming and so on, which are included within sense-sphere becoming and so on. 'Sense-sphere becoming and so on' means becoming in the sense sphere, the fine-material sphere, and the immaterial sphere.

Upādānabhedanti kāmupādānādiupādānavisesaṃ.

'The distinction of clinging' means the specific kinds of clinging, such as clinging to sensual pleasures and so on.

Tenāti [M 0.0135] sīlabbatupādānena. Vakkhamānenāti “idaṃ sīlabbataṃ nāmā”tiādinā (vibha. aṭṭha. 234) aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vakkhamānena pakārena. Purāṇaṃ brahmaṇḍaliṅgakhandapurāṇādi. “Setavadhayajjaṃ ārabhate bhūtikāmo”tiādinā (visuddhi. mahāṭī. 2.650) pasumāraṇavidhānayutto yaññavidhi pasubandhavidhi.

'By that' means by clinging to rules and observances. 'By what will be said' means by the method that will be stated in the commentary, beginning 'This is called a rule and observance' (Vibh-a 234). 'Ancient' refers to ancient Brahmanical signs, sections of ancient texts, and so on. The sacrificial method connected with the procedure of killing animals, the method of binding the animal for sacrifice, beginning with 'Desiring prosperity, he undertakes the sacrifice of a white victim' (Vism-mht 2.650).

Attano suddhimaggaparāmāsamattattā sīlabbatupādānassa attavādupādānanimittaṃ vuttaṃ.

Because clinging to rules and observances is merely the misapprehension of a path of purification as one's own, it is said to be a sign for clinging to the doctrine of self.

Maggapaccayā honti micchāniyyānasabhāvattā. Anantarassa pana kāmakammabhavassa anantarasamanantaraanantarūpanissayanatthivigatāsevanapaccayehi upādānassa paccayabhāvo pākaṭoyevāti na vutto.

They are conditions for the path because they have the nature of a wrong release. However, for the immediately following sense-sphere kamma-becoming, the fact that clinging is a condition by way of contiguity, immediate contiguity, contiguity decisive support, absence, disappearance, and repetition conditions is quite evident, so it is not stated.

Bhavapadaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Term 'Becoming' is concluded.

Jātijarāmaraṇādipadaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Terms beginning with Birth, Aging, and Death

235. Upapattibhavuppattīti [V 0.0131] upapattibhave, upapattibhavabhāvena vā upādinnakkhandhānaṃ uppatti. Jāyamānassa khandhassa. Jāti nibbattivikāro. Upapattibhavopi jātiyā paccayo. Kasmā? Upapattibhave asati jātiyā abhāvāti yojanā. “Jāyamānarūpapadaṭṭhānatā”tiādināpi tassa jātiyā paccayabhāvaṃyeva vibhāveti.

235. 'The arising in rebirth-becoming' means the arising of the appropriated aggregates in rebirth-becoming, or by way of rebirth-becoming. Of the aggregate that is being born, birth is the change that is generation. Rebirth-becoming is also a condition for birth. Why? The connection is: when there is no rebirth-becoming, there is no birth. Also with such phrases as 'being the basis for the term "arising form,"' he indeed clarifies its nature as a condition for birth.

Satipi sukkasoṇitādike pitugatavisesādikāraṇe bāhire paccaye tassa pana aniyatattā, hīnapaṇītādivisesassa ca adhippetattā vuttaṃ “ajjhatta…pe… abhāvā”ti.

Even though there is the external condition, the cause which is the specific contribution from the parents, such as semen and blood, because of its uncertainty, and because a distinction such as inferior and superior is intended, it is said: 'internal... because of the absence...'

Jātijarāmaraṇādipadaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Terms beginning with Birth, Aging, and Death is concluded.

Bhavacakkakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Wheel of Becoming

242. Sambandhaṃ itaṃ gatanti samitaṃ. Tenāha “saṅgata”nti.

242. `Samitaṃ` is `sambandhaṃ itaṃ gataṃ` (gone to a connection thus). Therefore he says 'united'.

Bhavacchando bhavarāgo. Tassāruppakathāsavananti tassa bālabhāvassa ayuttakāritāya anucchavikakathāsavanaṃ. Etena parūpavādahetukādidukkhaṃ dasseti, “kammakāraṇādassana”nti iminā daṇḍahetukaṃ, itarena duggatinibbattihetukaṃ[M 0.0136]. Gamentīti ñāpenti. Phalenāpi hi abyabhicārinā hetu ñāyati, vuṭṭhinimittena viya mahoghena uparidese vuṭṭhinipāto. Tena vuttaṃ “bodhentī”ti.

'Desire for becoming' is lust for becoming. 'Listening to talk unsuitable for him' means listening to talk that is unsuitable on account of his foolishness and improper action. By this he shows the suffering caused by others' blame and so on. By 'not seeing kamma as the cause,' he indicates suffering caused by punishment; by the other, suffering caused by rebirth in a woeful state. 'They lead' means they make known. For a cause is known by its unerring result, just as a downpour in an upper region is known by a great flood, which is its sign. Therefore it is said, 'they awaken'.

Visesanivattiattho mattasaddo “avitakkavicāramattā”tiādīsu (dha. sa. tikamātikā 6) viya. Appahīnāvijjā kāraṇalābhe uppattiarahatāya samīpeyevāti āha “sannihitabhāvakaraṇenā”ti. Vedetīti vedayati. Tassa atthavacanaṃ anubhavatīti. Vedaṃ vā ñāṇaṃ karoti uppādetīti vedeti. Tassa atthavacanaṃ jānātīti. Vediyatīti pana kammakattukammānaṃ vasena niddesoti tassapi atthaṃ dassento “jānāti, ñāyati cā”ti āha. Ca-saddatthoti [V 0.0132] samuccayattho, brahmādinā ca kārakena, attanā ca vedakena rahitanti attho. Ca-saddatthasamāsanti dvandasamāsamāha.

The word `matta` has the meaning of excluding a particular, as in 'merely without thought and examination' (Dhs. Tikamātikā 6). Because unabandoned ignorance is fit to arise when it obtains a cause, it is indeed near; therefore he says 'by making it present.' `Vedeti` means `vedayati`; the explanation of its meaning is 'he experiences.' Or, `vedeti` means 'he makes or produces `veda` or knowledge'; the explanation of its meaning is 'he knows.' `Vediyati`, however, is an exposition in terms of passive, agentive, and objective constructions; showing its meaning too, he says 'he knows, and it is known.' The meaning of the word `ca` is conjunction, meaning 'devoid of an agent such as Brahmā and of oneself as the feeler.' He calls a compound that has the meaning of the word `ca` a dvandva compound.

Catubbidhampi vā suññatanti dhuvabhāvādisuññataṃ, attādisuññatañca sandhāya vadati.

Or, 'the fourfold emptiness': he says this referring to the emptiness of a permanent nature, etc., and the emptiness of a self, etc.

Pubbantatoti atītakoṭṭhāsato. Vedanāvasānampi bhavacakkaṃ paripuṇṇamevāti dassetuṃ “vedanā vā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Avijjāgahaṇena vā taṇhupādānāni, saṅkhāraggahaṇena bhavo, viññāṇādiggahaṇena jātijarāmaraṇāni sokādayo ca gahitāti evampi vedanāvasānaṃ bhavacakkanti yuttamevetaṃ. Taṇhāmūlake cāti taṇhupādānaggahaṇena avijjā gahitātiādinā yojetabbaṃ. Tenāha “dvinnaṃ…pe… hotī”ti. Tattha dvinnanti purimapacchimānaṃ ubhinnaṃ hetuphalavajjānaṃ. Viparītābhinivesaṃ karontīti nimittaṃ kattuupacārena vadati. Anupacchedameva pakāsetīti yojanā.

'From the past end' means from the past portion. To show that the wheel of becoming is complete even when ending with feeling, 'or feeling,' etc., is said. Alternatively, by taking up ignorance, craving and clinging are taken up; by taking up formations, becoming is taken up; and by taking up consciousness and so on, birth, aging, death, sorrow, etc., are taken up. Thus, it is indeed proper that the wheel of becoming ends with feeling. And in the case of the one rooted in craving, it should be connected by stating that by the taking up of craving and clinging, ignorance is taken up, and so on. Therefore he says, 'Of the two... it is...' Therein, 'of the two' means of both the earlier and later, which are the sections of cause and effect. He speaks of the sign by figurative use of the agent, as 'they produce wrong adherence.' The connection is: 'it illuminates only non-interruption'.

Hetuphalasandhi, phalahetusandhi, punapi hetuphalasandhīti evaṃ hetuādipubbakā hetuphalahetupubbakā. Hetuphalahetuphalavasenāti avijjādihetu, viññāṇādiphala, taṇhādihetu, jātiphalavasena. Upasaggavisesena atthaviseso hotīti “ākirīyantī”ti padassa pakāsīyantīti attho vutto. Kilesakammavipākāti avijjādike vedanāpariyosāne vadati. Vipākakilesakammehīti viññāṇādīhi bhavapariyosānehi. Puna kammassa vipākasambandho vuttanayattā na gahito. “Vaṭṭānī”ti [M 0.0137] ca idaṃ “tīṇi vaṭṭānī”ti viggahavasena labbhamānaṃ gahetvā vuttaṃ.

The connection of cause and effect, the connection of effect and cause, and again the connection of cause and effect—thus there are those preceded by cause, etc., and those preceded by cause-effect-cause. 'By way of cause-effect-cause-effect' means: by way of ignorance etc. as cause, consciousness etc. as effect, craving etc. as cause, and birth as effect. Because a special meaning arises from a special prefix, the meaning of the word `ākirīyanti` (are scattered) is stated as `pakāsīyanti` (are illuminated).
