'Defilements, kamma, and results': he speaks of ignorance, etc., ending with feeling. 'By results, defilements, and kamma' means by consciousness, etc., ending with becoming. Again, the connection of kamma with its result is not taken up because its manner of exposition has been stated. And this 'rounds' is said having taken what is obtained by way of the analysis 'three rounds'.

“Purimakammabhavasmiṃ moho”tiādinā (vibha. aṭṭha. 242) aṭṭhakathāya āgatattā āsannapaccakkhataṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “imissā”ti. Vibhaṅgapāḷiyā vasena dassitaṃ, tasmā na aṭṭhakathāya pubbāparavirodho yathāpāṭhaṃ atthassa pakāsitattāti adhippāyo. Tattha cetanāsampayuttānañca cetanāya ca saṅkhārabhāvena kammabhavabhāvena ca vattabbamevāti pāḷidvayādhippāyavivaraṇavasena dassetuṃ “tatthā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Bhavassāti upapattibhavassa. “Bhavo”ti vuttā cetanāsampayuttāti sambandho. Gahaṇanti nikāmanavasena ārammaṇassa gahaṇaṃ. Tenāha “kāmupādānaṃ kiccenāhā”ti. Itarāni kiccenāhāti yojanā. Tīsu atthavikappesūti “taṃ [V 0.0133] kammaṃ karoto purimā cetanāyo”tiādinā vuttesu tīsu āyūhanacetanānaṃ atthavikappesu. Nanu ca tatiye atthavikappe āyūhanassa avasāne cetanā na vuttāti? Yadipi sarūpato na vuttā, “taṃsampayuttā”ti pana saddato padhānabhāvena vuttassa āyūhanassa appadhānabhāvena vuttā avasāne pacchato vuttā viya hotīti imaṃ pariyāyaṃ sandhāya “tīsupi…pe… avasāne”ti vuttaṃ.

Because it comes from the commentary in the passage beginning 'Delusion in the previous kamma-existence,' etc. (Vibh-a 242), the word 'of this' is said with reference to what is near and manifest. It is shown by way of the Vibhaṅga Pāḷi; therefore, there is no earlier-later contradiction in the commentary, as the meaning is explained according to the text—this is the intention. To show, by way of explaining the intention of the two Pāḷi texts, that here both things associated with volition and volition itself should be spoken of as formations and as kamma-existence, the words 'in that case,' etc., are stated. 'Of existence' means of rebirth-existence. The connection is that what is associated with volition is called 'existence.' 'Grasping' is the taking of an object by way of desire. Hence he says, 'sensual clinging is meant in the sense of its function.' The connection is that the others are also meant in the sense of their function. 'In the three interpretations of the meaning' refers to the three interpretations of the meaning of the accumulating volitions stated in the passage beginning, 'the prior volitions of one performing that kamma.' But is it not the case that in the third interpretation of the meaning, volition is not mentioned at the end of the accumulation? Although it is not stated in its own form, through the word 'associated with that,' it is stated as subordinate to the accumulation, which is mentioned as primary, and thus it is as if it were stated afterwards at the end. With reference to this method, it is said 'in all three… at the end.'

Nippariyāyena pana yesu āyūhanassa avasāne cetanā vuttā, te dassetuṃ “dvīsu…pe… āhā”ti vuttaṃ. Tatiye atthavikappe vutte āyūhanasaṅkhāre taṃsampayuttāti āhāti yojanā. Kammassa paccayabhūtanti saṅkhārapaccayaṃ. Tena “kammakaraṇakāle”ti ettha kamma-saddena sabbassapi saṅkhārassa gahitataṃ dasseti. Tenāha “na kammasampayuttamevā”ti.

However, to show directly in which cases volition is mentioned at the end of the accumulation, the words 'in two... he said...' are stated. The connection is: in the third interpretation of the meaning, regarding the stated formations of accumulation, he says 'associated with that.' 'Being a condition for kamma' means 'with formations as condition.' Thereby he shows that in the phrase 'at the time of performing kamma,' the word 'kamma' includes all formations. Hence he says, 'not only what is associated with kamma.'

Kammānevāti kammāniyeva. Vipākadhammatāya kammasarikkhakā. Sahajātakoṭiyā, upanissayakoṭiyā ca tassa kammassa upakārakāti tadupakārakā. Saṃkhippantīti saṃkhipīyanti saṃyūhīyanti. “Saṃkhippanti etthā”ti adhikaraṇasādhanavasena saṅkhepasaddassa atthaṃ vatvā puna kammasādhanavasena vattuṃ “saṃkhipīyatī”tiādi vuttaṃ.

'Kammāneva' means 'kammāni yeva' (kamma indeed). Because they have the nature of resulting, they are similar to kamma. Because they are helpful to that kamma by way of the conascent aspect and the decisive support aspect, they are 'its helpers' (tadupakārakā). 'They condense' (saṃkhippanti) means they are condensed (saṃkhipīyanti), they are amassed (saṃyūhīyanti). Having stated the meaning of the word 'saṅkhepa' by way of the locative derivation 'wherein they condense,' he again speaks by way of the objective derivation to say 'it is condensed' (saṃkhipīyati), etc.

Tatthāpīti [M 0.0138] “kamma”nti vuttakammasambhārepi. Gamanadhammanti bhaṅgupagamanadhammaṃ. Tena ittaranti bhaṅgaparanti vuttaṃ hoti. Tenāti vinassanadhammatādīpakena ittarasaddena. Nissārataṃ attasārābhāvaṃ dīpeti. Evaṃ “ittara”ntiādinā aniccaṃ calaṃ ittaraṃ addhuvanti catunnaṃ padānaṃ atthavisesavācitaṃ dasseti. Ṭhānasoti ettha vuttaṭṭhānaṃ nāma paccayo. Aññampīti aññattha vuttaṃ. Tassa tassa phalassa. Dhammamattasambhave sati vaṭṭupacchede satīti yojanā. Evanti vuttappakārena samuccayatthe ca-sadde sati.

'Therein too' means in the collection of kamma thus stated. 'Having the nature of going' means having the nature of going to dissolution. Therefore 'fleeting' (ittaraṃ) means having dissolution as its final end. 'By that' means by the word 'fleeting' (ittara), which indicates the nature of perishing. It reveals 'saplessness' (nissārataṃ), the absence of a self as core. Thus, by 'fleeting,' etc., he shows that the four terms—impermanent, trembling, fleeting, and non-lasting—denote specific meanings. In 'as a basis' (ṭhānaso), the basis mentioned here is a condition. 'Also another' means stated elsewhere. Of this or that fruit. The connection is: 'when there is the arising of mere phenomena, there is the cutting off of the round.' 'Thus' means in the stated manner, when there is the particle 'ca' in the sense of conjunction.

Saccāniyeva pabhavoti samānādhikaraṇapakkhaṃ sandhāyāha “saccappabhavatoti saccato”ti. “Yassa pahānatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti evaṃbhūtaṃ ariyasaccaṃ visesaṃ akatvā.

'The truths themselves are the origin': referring to the alternative of grammatical agreement, he says, ''having the truths as its origin' (saccappabhavato), thus 'from the truths' (saccato).' Without making a distinction regarding the noble truth which is of such a nature as 'that for the abandoning of which the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.'

Tehi sokādīhi. “Sokadomanassupāyāsā avijjāya aviyogino”tiādinā pubbe vuttanayena [V 0.0134] siddhāya avijjāya. Attanoyevāti paccayuppannaṃ anapekkhitvā attanoyeva pavattasaṅkhātakiccato.

By that sorrow, etc. By the ignorance that is established by the method previously stated in the passage beginning, 'Sorrow, displeasure, and despair are not dissociated from ignorance.' 'Of itself' means because of its function, which is described as proceeding on its own, without regard for what is dependently arisen.

Sokādayopi hīti ettha hi-saddo hetuattho. Yasmā “sokādayo paccayāyattā avasavattino”ti idaṃ “jātipaccayā…pe… sambhavantī”ti etena vacanena siddhaṃ, tasmā taṃ “attā socatī”tiādidassananivāraṇanti attho.

In 'sorrow, etc., indeed,' here the word 'hi' (indeed) has the sense of a reason. Because this—that 'sorrow and the like are dependent on conditions and not under their own control'—is established by the statement 'conditioned by birth... they arise,' therefore the meaning is that this prevents the view 'the self sorrows,' etc.

Sati ca pariggahe rajjaṃ viya gatiyo anekānatthānubandhanā, tāhi ca viññāṇassa upaddutatāti dassetuṃ “saṅkhārapariggahitaṃ…pe… rajje”ti vuttanti evaṃ vā ettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Yathāupaṭṭhitāni kammādīni cutiāsannajavanehi parikappetvā viya gahitāni paṭisandhiviññāṇenapi parikappitāni viya honti, taṃ panassa parikappanaṃ atthato ārammaṇakaraṇamevāti vuttaṃ “pari…pe… to”ti. Saṅkappanaṃ vā parikappananti vuttaṃ “vitakkena vitakkanato”ti. Sasambhāracakkhuādayo saḷāyatanassa patiṭṭhāviseso.

Or the meaning here should be seen in this way: when there is grasping, the destinies, like a kingdom, are attended by many troubles, and to show that consciousness is afflicted by them, it is said, 'grasped by formations... in a kingdom.' Just as kamma, etc., which have presented themselves, are grasped as if fashioned by the impulsion moments near death, so too they are as if fashioned by the rebirth-linking consciousness. But its fashioning is in reality just the making of an object; hence it is said 'fashioned... thus.' Or, fashioning is conceiving; hence it is said, 'by thought, as thinking.' The eye, etc., with their components, are a special basis for the sixfold sense base.

Yadākārāya jātiyā yadākāraṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ sambhavati, sambhavantañca yathānupubbaṃ pavattaṃ, so attho jātipaccayasambhūtasamudāgataṭṭho, sahitassa [M 0.0139] samuditassa puggalassa jīraṇabhijjanāvatthā dhammā jarāmaraṇāpadesena vuttā, sā ca nesaṃ avatthā jātipubbikā, te ca samuditā eva pavattantīti evaṃ jātito jarāmaraṇassa sambhūtasamudāgataṭṭho veditabbo. Jātito jarāmaraṇaṃ na na hoti hotiyeva ekantena jātassa jarāmaraṇasambhavato, na ca jātiṃ vinā hoti ajātassa tadabhāvatoti jarāmaraṇassa jātipaccayataṃ anvayabyatirekehi vibhāveti “na jātito”tiādinā. Itthanti jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇassa nibbattākāraṃ vadati.

In whatever mode birth occurs, in that same mode aging-and-death occurs. And occurring, it proceeds in due order. This is the meaning of 'originated and arisen from birth as condition.' The states of decay and breaking up of a person who is combined and collected are spoken of under the designation of aging-and-death. And that state of theirs is preceded by birth, and they proceed only when collected. In this way, the meaning of aging-and-death as 'originated and arisen' from birth should be understood. Aging-and-death does not not come from birth; it certainly does come, because for one who has been born the occurrence of aging-and-death is inevitable. And it does not occur without birth, because it is absent for one who is unborn. Thus he clarifies the conditionality of aging-and-death by birth through positive and negative concomitance with the words 'not from birth,' etc. 'Thus' means he speaks of the mode of production of aging-and-death from birth as condition.

Nirodhā nirodhasaṅkhātanti paccayanirodhā paccayuppannanirodhasaṅkhātaṃ. Anulomadesanāya ca vemajjhato paṭṭhāyāti yojanā.

‘From cessation’ means that which is designated ‘cessation’; from the cessation of the condition is designated the cessation of the conditionally arisen. And the connection is: 'of the forward exposition, starting from the middle.'

Apuññābhisaṅkhārekadeso sarāgo rāgena sahajekaṭṭhoti katvā. Sabbopi apuññābhisaṅkhāro sarāgo pahānekaṭṭhabhāvato. Yasmā pana akusaladhammo akusaladhammassa sabhāgo, anakusaladhammo visabhāgo, yathārahaṃ paccayo ca hoti, tasmā “apaṭipakkhabhāvato, rāgappavaḍḍhako”ti ca vuttaṃ[V 0.0135]. “Tadeva viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsaratī”ti micchābhinivesasabbhāvato saṃsaraṇakiriyāyapi sabyāpāratā viññāṇassa vuttā. Sabyāpāratābhinivesabalavatāya, saṅkantiabhinivesabalavatāyāti paccekaṃ yojetabbaṃ. “Asahavattanato, sahavattanato”ti etena asahavutti vinibbhogo, sahavutti avinibbhogoti dasseti.

A portion of the demeritorious formations is accompanied by lust, because it is conascent and has a single object with lust. All demeritorious formations are accompanied by lust because they have a single object in being abandoned. But since an unwholesome state is homogeneous with another unwholesome state, and a non-unwholesome state is heterogeneous, and it is a condition as appropriate, therefore it is said: 'because it is not opposed' and 'it increases lust.' Because of the existence of wrong adherence to the view 'that same consciousness runs on and transmigrates,' the active involvement of consciousness in the action of transmigrating is also stated. It should be connected with each separately: 'because of the strength of the adherence to its active involvement' and 'because of the strength of the adherence to its transition.' By 'because of non-co-occurrence' and 'because of co-occurrence,' he shows that non-co-occurrence is separateness and co-occurrence is inseparability.

Sabhāvādhigamanimittatā obhāsanaṃ. Cakkhādisannissayena hi pañcaviññāṇāni rūpādisabhāvaṃ upalabhanti. Itare phusanasaṅgatisannipātaṭṭhā. Channanti channampi samphassānaṃ.

Illumination is the sign of attaining the intrinsic nature. For it is by dependence on the eye, etc., that the five consciousnesses apprehend the intrinsic nature of forms, etc. The others have the meaning of touching, meeting, and confluence. 'Of the six' means of all six contacts.

Ādānanti upasaddena vināpi daḷhagāho adhippetoti āha “ādānaṭṭho catunnampi upādānānaṃ samāno”ti. Gahaṇanti nikāmanavasena visayassa paṭicchannanti vuttaṃ “gahaṇaṭṭho kāmupādānassā”ti. Itaresanti diṭṭhupādānādīnaṃ. Tasmāti vibhattiyā aluttabhāvato. Tenāti khipanasaddena. Hāni vā khīṇabhāvo khayoti “khayaṭṭho vā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Dvinnanti jarāmaraṇānaṃ. Maraṇūpanayanarasattā vā jarāyapi maraṇaṭṭho eva dassito.

'Taking' (ādāna): even without the prefix 'upa-,' a firm grasp is intended. Thus he says, 'The meaning of taking is common to all four kinds of clinging.' 'Grasping' (gahaṇa) is said to be the covering of an object by way of desire. Thus it is said, 'The meaning of grasping pertains to sensual clinging.' 'Of the others' means of clinging to views, etc. 'Therefore' is because the case ending is not elided. 'By that' means by the word 'throwing' (khipana). Loss or the state of being wasted away is destruction (khaya). Thus it is said, 'Or the meaning is destruction,' etc. 'Of the two' means of aging and death. Or, because it has the function of leading to death, the meaning of death is shown for aging as well.

Nīyanti [M 0.0140] gamentīti nayā, ekattādayo. Kehi nīyanti? Avijjādiatthehīti imamatthamāha “avijjādī”tiādinā. Sena bhāvenāti sakena avijjādibhāvena, taṃ amuñcitvā eva. Na hi avijjādivinimuttaṃ ekattaṃ nāma kiñci paramatthato atthi. Sena bhāvenāti vā sakena ekattādibhāvena. Avijjādīsu viññāyamāno hetuphaladhammānaṃ ekasantatipatitādisaṅkhāto ekattādibhāvo teneva sabhāvena ñāyati, na avijjādibhāvenāti. Te hi netabbāti tesaṃ nayā. Atthā eva vā avijjādayo. Anekepi samānā dhammā yena santānānupacchedena “eka”nti ñāyanti voharīyanti, so tattha karaṇabhāvena vattabbataṃ arahati, tathā itarepīti āha “ekattādīhi ca atthā ‘eka’ntiādinā nīyantī”ti. Tattha nīyantīti ñāyanti, paññāpīyanti ca. Purimapacchimānaṃ dhammānaṃ nirodhuppādanirantaratāya nāmakāyassa, sambandhavuttitāya rūpakāyassa, ubhayassa ca aññamaññasannissitatāya duviññeyyanānato ekībhūtassa viya ghanabhāvappabandho hetuphalabhāvena sambandho sammā tānoti santāno, tassa anupacchedo tathāpavatti ekattanti āha “santānānupacchedo ekatta”nti.

They are led, they are made to go, thus they are 'methods' (nayā), such as unity and so on. By what are they led? By things such as ignorance; this meaning is stated with 'by ignorance, etc.' 'By their own nature' means by their own nature of ignorance and so on, without abandoning it. For indeed, in an ultimate sense there is nothing called 'unity' that is liberated from ignorance and so on. Or, 'by their own nature' means by their own nature of unity and so on. When understood in regard to ignorance and so on, the state of unity and so forth, characterized as the falling into a single continuity of cause and effect, is known by that very nature, not by the nature of ignorance and so on. For they are to be led, thus they are their methods. Or, the meanings themselves are ignorance and so on. Even when phenomena are many, by means of the uninterrupted continuity of the stream they are known and designated as 'one.' That deserves to be spoken of in the instrumental sense there, and so too the others. Thus it is said: 'And by unity and so on, the meanings are led as "one," etc.' Therein, 'are led' means they are known and designated. Because of the uninterruptedness of the cessation and arising of preceding and subsequent phenomena of the mental body, and the connected occurrence of the physical body, and the mutual dependence of both, though they are distinct and twofold as to cognizance, the compact continuity as if unified—the connection by way of cause and effect—is properly extended; this is the stream. Its non-interruption, its proceeding thus, is unity. Thus it is said: 'The non-interruption of the stream is unity.'

Sambandharahitassāti [V 0.0136] hetuphalabhāvena aññamaññasambandhabhāvarahitassa. Sattantaroti añño satto. Ucchedadiṭṭhimupādiyatīti yathānurūpakāraṇato phalappavattiṃ asamanupassanto nānāsantāne viya asambandhanānattadassanato hetubhāvarahitānaṃ nippayojanānaṃ purimuppannānaṃ dhammānaṃ nirodhe hetuniyamābhāvato ekantena uppatti na yuttā, tathā santānena uppatti, sadisabhāvena uppatti, samānajātidesapariṇāmavayarūpabalasaṇṭhānānaṃ uppatti na yuttātiādīni vikappento ucchedadiṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti.

'Devoid of connection' means devoid of a state of mutual connection by way of cause and effect. 'Another being' means a different being. 'He adopts the annihilationist view' means that, not properly seeing the occurrence of a result from a corresponding cause, and seeing a disconnected diversity as if in different continuities, he speculates in various ways, such as: 'Since previously arisen phenomena, which are devoid of a causal nature and are useless, cease, and since there is no fixed rule of cause, arising is absolutely not proper. Similarly, arising by continuity, arising by similarity, and the arising of those with a common birth, place, transformation, age, form, strength, and shape are not proper.' Speculating on these and other such things, he adopts the annihilationist view.

Kasmā uppatti na siyāti vālikāhi viya tilehipi telassa, ucchuto viya gāvitopi khīrassa aññābhāvato kena kāraṇena tehi tesaṃ uppatti na siyā, itarehi eva ca nesaṃ uppatti hotīti. Tasmāti aññassa aññato uppattiyaṃ sabbassa sabbaso uppattiyā bhavitabbaṃ, na cetaṃ atthi, tasmā. Yasmā niyativādī anurūpā hetuto phaluppattiṃ na icchati, sabhāvasiddhameva ca dhammappavattiṃ icchati, tasmā “avijjamānepi hetumhī”ti vuttaṃ. Sabhāvasiddhā eva hi acchejjasuttāvutābhejjamaṇi viya [M 0.0141] kamalaṅghanarahitā tathā tathā sarīrindriyasukhādibhāvapariṇāmāya niyatiyāva kāyā samāgacchanti, yato gatijātibandhā, apavaggo ca hotīti niyativādo. Tenāha “niyatatāya…pe… pavattantī”ti. Niyatiattho vuttoyeva.

Why should there not be arising of oil from sand just as from sesame seeds, or of milk from sugarcane just as from a cow? Since they are other, for what reason should there not be arising from them, while arising occurs only from the others? 'Therefore': if one thing arose from another, everything would have to arise from everything. But this is not so. Therefore... Because the fatalist does not accept the arising of a result from a corresponding cause, but accepts only the occurrence of phenomena as established by their intrinsic nature, it is therefore said, 'even when a cause is non-existent.' For it is by fate alone that bodies, established by their own intrinsic nature—like an unbreakable gem strung on an uncuttable thread, and like a lotus unsullied by mud—come together in such and such a way for the transformation into the states of body, faculties, pleasure, and so forth. From this come destination, birth, and bondage, and also liberation. This is fatalism. Therefore he said: 'by the fixed nature...pe... they occur.' The meaning of 'fate' has already been stated.

Etassa atthassa sādhakaṃ suttaṃ. Ākulameva, ākulabhāvo vā ākulakaṃ. Jaṭitāti heṭṭhupariyavasena pavattamānehi kilesakammavipākehi jātajaṭā. Nīḍanti kulāvakaṃ. Saṃsāranti idha sampattibhavappabandhamāha apāyādipadehi duggatippabandhassa vuttattā.

A sutta that establishes this meaning. 'Tangled' indeed, or the state of being tangled is 'a tangle.' 'Enmeshed' means a tangle born from the defilements, kamma, and results that proceed in a lower and higher manner. 'A nest' means a bird's nest (kulāvaka). 'Wandering on' here refers to the continuity of attained existence, since the continuity of a miserable destination has been stated by terms such as 'planes of woe.'

Bhavacakkakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Wheel of Existence is concluded.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Sutta-Style Analysis is finished.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Abhidhamma-Style Analysis

243. Taṃ [V 0.0137] paṭiccasamuppādaṃ. Ekekacittāvaruddhanti abhidhammabhājanīye viya ekekasmiṃ citte avaruddhaṃ antogadhaṃ akatvā. Asahajātānañca “asahajātānaṃ, sahajātānañcā”ti evaṃ paṭhamapade ekasesaniddeso daṭṭhabbo. “Saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇa”nti asahajātāyeva paccayapaccayuppannā dassitā vipākaviññāṇasseva adhippetattā. “Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpa”nti (vibha. 225) ca evamādīsu asahajātā, sahajātā ca. “Ekekena nayenā”ti purātano pāṭho, etarahi pana “ekekena catukkena” icceva bahūsu potthakesu pāṭho. Nayacatukkavārāti nayesu catukkānaṃ vārā, avijjāmūlakādīsu navasu nayesu paccekaṃ paccayacatukkādīnaṃ catunnaṃ catukkānaṃ “nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatana”ntiādivisesabhinnā cattāro vārāti attho. Vavatthitāti yathāvuttavisesena asaṃkiṇṇā. Catukkānanti vāracatukkānaṃ vārasoḷasakassa nayabhāvatoti adhippāyo.

243. That dependent origination. Not confined to single mind-moments means not having made it confined and included within each single mind-moment, as in the Abhidhamma Analysis. And regarding non-conascence: the phrase 'of the non-conascent and of the conascent' should be seen as a specification by single-remainder in the first term. In 'with formations as condition, consciousness arises,' only non-conascent conditions and conditioned phenomena are shown, since only resultant consciousness is intended. And in such phrases as 'with ignorance as condition, formations arise' and 'with consciousness as condition, mentality-materiality arises,' there are both non-conascent and conascent phenomena. 'By each single method' is the ancient reading, but now in many books the reading is 'by each single tetrad.' 'The sections of the tetrads of methods' means the sections of the tetrads within the methods; that is, in the nine methods beginning with the one rooted in ignorance, for each of the four tetrads—the tetrad of conditions, etc.—there are four sections distinguished by such specifics as 'with mentality as condition, the sixth sense base arises.' 'Determined' means unmixed by the specific characteristics as stated. 'Of the tetrads': the intention is that this refers to the method having the nature of sixteen sections, which are the four sections for each of the four tetrads.

1. Paccayacatukkavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Tetrad of Conditions

Paccayasahitapaccayuppannāni aṅgabhāvena vuttāni, na kevalaṃ paccayā. Tasmā “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”ti ettha na chaṭṭhāyatanassa aṅgatā. Tena [M 0.0142] vuttaṃ “na, tassa anaṅgattā”ti. Evañca katvāti paccayasahitassa paccayuppannassa aṅgabhāvato. Tīsu pakāresūti “paṭhamo sabbasaṅgāhikaṭṭhenā”tiādinā (vibha. aṭṭha. 243) aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttesu tīsupi pakāresu. Paccayavisesādīti ettha nāmaṃ, chaṭṭhāyatanañca paccayaviseso. Ādi-saddena yoniviseso, āyatanānaṃ apāripūripāripūribhavaviseso ca gahito. Te hi dutiyavārādīnaṃ nānattakarā. Atthavisesenāti yadipi aññattha “saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso”ti saḷāyatanapaccayo vutto, tathāpi sahajātādināmasannissayena pavattanato nāmamattapaccayāpi so hotīti paṭiccasamuppādassa nānānayavicittatānumitassa gambhīrabhāvassa vibhāvanasaṅkhātena, anavasesanāmapaccayadassanasaṅkhātena ca atthavisesena. Tathā hi “yehi, ānanda, ākārehi yehi liṅgehi yehi nimittehi yehi uddesehi nāmakāyassa paññatti hoti, tesu ākāresu…pe… uddesesu asati api nu kho rūpakāye adhivacanasamphasso paññāyethā”ti (dī. ni. 2.114) phassassa nāmapaccayatāvibhāvanavasena mahānidānadesanā pavattā. Tathā “nāmarūpapaccayā [V 0.0138] phassoti iccassa vacanīya”nti (dī. ni. 2.97) “nāmarūpapaccayā”ti vadantena “nāmapaccayā”tipi vuttameva hotīti.

Conditions together with what is conditionally arisen are spoken of as factors, not merely as conditions. Therefore, in the phrase 'contact is conditioned by the sixth sense base,' the sixth sense base is not a factor. Hence it is said: 'No, because it is not a factor.' And this is so because what is conditionally arisen together with its condition has the status of a factor. 'In the three modes' means: in the three modes stated in the commentary (Vibh-a 243) beginning, 'the first is in the sense of being all-inclusive,' etc. Herein, mentality and the sixth sense base are specific conditions. By the word 'etc.' are included the specific mode of origin and the distinction of the sense bases as being incomplete or complete. These indeed create the diversity of the second section, etc. 'By a distinction of meaning' means: although elsewhere it is said, 'contact is conditioned by the sixfold sense base,' since it proceeds depending on conascent mentality, etc., it is also conditioned merely by mentality. Thus, by a distinction of meaning, which is designated as the clarification of the profound nature of dependent origination—inferred from its various methods—and as the demonstration of the non-residual mentality-condition. For thus the Great Discourse on Causation proceeds by way of clarifying the conditionality of contact by mentality: 'Ānanda, by whatever modes, signs, marks, or descriptions the designation of the mentality-body occurs, in the absence of those modes... would designation-contact be discerned in the materiality-body?' (DN 15). Similarly, when it is said, 'It should be said: "Contact is conditioned by mentality-materiality,"' by saying 'conditioned by mentality-materiality,' it is also said 'conditioned by mentality' (DN 15).

Vāracatukke “saṅkhāro”ti vuttaṃ, sokādayo na vuttā, purimasmiṃ vāradvaye rūpaṃ na vuttaṃ, vārattaye saḷāyatanaṃ na vuttanti yojetabbaṃ.

In the tetrad of sections, 'formations' are mentioned, but sorrow and the like are not mentioned; in the first two sections, materiality is not mentioned; in the three sections, the sixfold sense base is not mentioned—this is how it should be construed.

Sabba…pe… raṇatoti sabbassa viññāṇassa pavattiṭṭhānabhūtasabbabhavasādhāraṇato, viññāṇassa vā pavattiṭṭhānabhūtasabbabhavasādhāraṇato. Samānaṃ phalaṃ samāno paccayo sahajātādipaccayehi upakattabbato, upakārakato ca. Tassa viññāṇassa. Viññāṇāharaṇanti vipākaviññāṇanibbattanaṃ. Assa viññāṇassa.

All... etc... raṇato means: because it is common to all existence, which is the basis for the occurrence of all consciousness, or because it is common to all existence, which is the basis for the occurrence of consciousness. The result is the same, the condition is the same, because it is to be assisted by co-nascent conditions, etc., and because it is an assister. Of that consciousness. 'The bringing of consciousness' means the production of resultant consciousness. Of this consciousness.

Gatisūcakoti hi-saddaṃ loke gatiatthaṃ vadantīti katvā vuttaṃ. “Vigata”nti ettha vi-saddo paṭisedhadīpakoti dve paṭisedhā pakatiṃ ñāpentīti āha “vigatatānivāraṇavasena gati eva hotī”ti.

'Indicative of destination (gati)' is said because in the world the particle 'hi' is said to have the meaning of 'gati' (going). Herein, in 'vigata,' the prefix 'vi-' indicates negation; thus two negations make known the natural state. Hence he says: 'By way of removing that which has been removed, it is just destination (gati).'

Tidhā catudhā pañcadhā vāti ettha saññāmanasikārādayo sahajātanissayaatthipaccayavasena tidhā, phassacetanādayo tesañceva āhārādīnañca [M 0.0143] vasena catudhā, vedanāvitakkādayo tesañceva jhānindriyādīnañca vasena pañcadhā. Yathā samādhi, evaṃ vīriyampi daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tampi hi adhipatindriyamaggapaccayehi chadhā paccayo hoti.

'Threefold, fourfold, or fivefold': here, perception, attention, and the like are threefold by way of conascence, dependence, and presence conditions. Contact, volition, and the like are fourfold by way of those and also by way of nutriment, etc. Feeling, thought, and the like are fivefold by way of those and also by way of jhāna factors, faculties, etc. As with concentration, so too energy should be seen. For that too becomes a condition in six ways by way of dominance, faculty, and path conditions.

“Vacanavasenā”ti iminā imasmiṃ catukke sahajātapaccayaṃ dhuraṃ katvā desanā pavattāti tesaṃ adhippāyoti dasseti. Atthoti paccayadhammo. Katthacīti kismiñci vāre attano paccayuppannassa yathāsakehi paccayo na na hoti. “Atthato”ti ca pāṭho. “Bhavapaccayā jātī”tiādi na vattabbaṃ siyā, vuttañca taṃ. Tasmā sahajātapaccayavaseneva paṭhamacatukko vuttoti na gahetabbanti dasseti. Tenāha “na ca taṃ na vutta”ntiādi. Imassa ca “bhavapaccayā jātītiādi na vattabbaṃ siyā”ti iminā sambandho veditabbo. Paccayavacanamevāti “avijjāpaccayā”tiādīsu vuttapaccayavacanameva ca. Tesanti tesaṃ ācariyānaṃ. Ayojetvā vuttanti sambandho. Kathaṃ pana vuttanti āha “sāmaññena…pe… sandhāya [V 0.0139] vutta”nti. Ettha ca “sahajātasūcaka”ntiādinā yathādhippetassa atthassa vacanato asiddhimāha, “sahajātato”tiādinā pana atthāpattito. Asambhave hi aññassa atthato sijjheyya vacanato vā atthato vā adhippetatthasādhanāti.

'By way of expression': by this he shows that their intention is that in this tetrad the teaching proceeds by making the conascent condition primary. 'Meaning' is the conditioning phenomenon. 'In some instance' means: in any given section, a condition does not fail to be a condition for its own conditionally arisen phenomenon in its own ways. There is also the reading 'by way of meaning.' 'Birth is conditioned by becoming,' etc., should not have been said, yet it was said. Therefore, he shows that it should not be held that the first tetrad is stated solely by way of the conascent condition. Hence he says, 'And that was not unsaid,' etc. The connection of this should be understood with the phrase, 'Birth is conditioned by becoming, etc., should not have been said.' 'The mere expression of conditions' is just the expression of conditions stated in 'conditioned by ignorance,' etc. 'Theirs' means: of those teachers. The connection is: 'it is said without connecting.' But how is it said? He says: 'It is said in general... with reference to...' And here, by 'indicative of conascence,' etc., he states the non-establishment of the intended meaning on the basis of the wording; but by 'from conascence,' etc., on the basis of implication. For if something else were impossible, the intended meaning would be established either by wording or by meaning.

Aññatthāti aññasmiṃ sutte. Atītaddhaṃ niddhāretvā paccuppannānāgatehi saddhiṃ addhattayadassanatthaṃ. Taṃdesanāpariggahatthanti mahānidānadesanāpariggahatthaṃ. So ca ubhinnaṃ desanānaṃ aññamaññaṃ saṃsandanabhāvadassanatthaṃ. Evaṃ sabbaññubuddhabhāsitā desanā aññadatthu saṃsandatīti.

'Elsewhere' means: in another sutta. For the purpose of showing the three periods of time together with the present and future, after having determined the past period. 'For the purpose of grasping that teaching' means: for the purpose of grasping the Great Discourse on Causation. And that is for the purpose of showing the state of mutual correspondence between the two discourses. Thus the teaching spoken by the Omniscient Buddha indeed corresponds.

Imassāti imassa tatiyavārassa.

'Of this' means: of this third section.

Aparāpekkhatāya, aparikiliṭṭhupapattitāya, asuciamakkhitatāya kāmāvacaradevānaṃ, sabbesañca brahmānaṃ tathā upapajjanato ca opapātikayoniyā padhānatā veditabbā. Saṅgahanidassanavasenāti opapātikayoniyā eva saṃsedajayoniyā saṅgahassa nidassanavasena udāharaṇavasena. Ārammaṇapaccayassāpi phassassa satipi pavattihetubhāve so pana sahajātādipaccayabhūtassa ajjhattikassa chaṭṭhāyatanassa viya na sātisayoti vuttaṃ “ārammaṇapaccayo cettha pavattako na hotī”ti.

The predominance of the mode of spontaneous generation should be understood from its being without dependence on others, from its being an undefiled mode of generation, from its not being smeared with impurity, and because the sense-sphere devas and all brahmās are reborn in that way. 'By way of illustrating inclusion' means: by way of illustrating, by way of giving an example of, the inclusion of the moisture-born mode of generation within the spontaneous mode of generation itself. Although contact conditioned by an object does have a cause for its occurrence, since it is not superior like the internal sixth sense base, which is a conascent condition, etc., it is said: 'Herein, the object condition is not what makes it occur.'

Kesañcīti [M 0.0144] paripuṇṇāyatanānaṃ gabbhaseyyakānaṃ. “Pacchima…pe… sadā sambhavatī”ti idaṃ gabbhaseyyakānaṃ viya itarayonikānaṃ kamena āyatanuppatti natthīti vuttaṃ. Tathā cāha aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “sahuppattidīpanato”ti.

'For some' means: for womb-born beings with complete sense bases. 'The last... always arises': this is said because for those of other modes of generation, unlike for the womb-born, there is no gradual arising of the sense bases. And thus it is said in the commentary: 'because it explains simultaneous arising.'

Paccayacatukkavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Tetrad of Conditions is concluded.

2. Hetucatukkavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Tetrad of Causes

244. Abhāvatoti bhāvābhāvato. Yañhi jātikkhaṇamatteyeva bhavati, na tato paraṃ, taṃ [V 0.0140] jātiyā avigatapaccayo siyā avigatapaccayaniyamasabbhāvato. Bhavo pana yasmā jātikkhaṇato parampi bhavati, tasmā na so tassā avigatapaccayo hoti. Tena vuttaṃ “tato uddhaṃ bhāvatoti attho”ti. Bhaveti bhavapade, bhave vā nipphādetabbe. Esa nayo jātiādīsūti etthāpi. “Yathā panā”tiādinā “avigatapaccayassa abhāvato, niyamābhāvato cā”ti vuttānaṃ hetūnaṃ vuttanayena abyāpibhāvavibhāvanena akāraṇataṃ dasseti ayāvabhāvino paccayuppannassa, paccayadhammassa ca avigatapaccayabhāvadassanato. Saṅkhārakkhandhetiādi maggasodhanavasena vuttaṃ. Tassa parihāraṃ sayameva vadati. So khaṇo etassa atthīti taṅkhaṇiko, na taṅkhaṇiko ataṅkhaṇiko, tassa sabbhāvā, ayāvabhāvikasabbhāvāti attho. Yathā pana hetū honti, taṃ dassetuṃ “saṅkhatalakkhaṇānaṃ panā”tiādimāha.

244. By 'non-presence' is meant from the perspective of presence and non-presence. For what exists only for the moment of arising and not beyond, that would be a presence condition for arising, due to the existence of the rule of the presence condition. But since existence persists also beyond the moment of arising, it is therefore not a presence condition for it. Thus it is said: 'The meaning is "from then on, it is existence."' 'In existence' means in the term 'existence,' or in the existence that is to be produced. This same method applies here also to birth and so on. By the passage beginning 'But as for...,' by demonstrating in the stated manner the non-pervasiveness of the reasons given as 'due to the absence of a presence condition and due to the absence of a rule,' it shows their non-causality for a non-coextensive conditioned phenomenon and for a conditioning thing, by showing that they do not have the state of a presence condition. 'The aggregate of formations,' etc., is said by way of clearing the way for the argument. He himself states its refutation. 'That moment exists for this,' thus it is momentary; what is not momentary is non-momentary. 'Because of its existence'—the meaning is 'the existence of what is not coextensive.' To show how they are causes, he says, 'But of the characteristics of the conditioned...'

Evanti evaṃ yathāvuttanaye sati, evaṃ santeti attho. “Na hi…pe… atthī”ti iminā jātiādīnaṃ avigatapaccayavasena paccayuppannabhāvo viya paccayabhāvopi natthīti dasseti. Tattha kāraṇamāha “asabhāvadhammattā”ti.

'Thus' means: when it is thus in the stated manner, the meaning is 'it being so.' By this 'For not... etc. ...exists,' it shows that just as birth and so on do not have the state of a conditioned phenomenon by way of a presence condition, so too they do not have the state of a condition. Therein he states the reason: 'because they are things without an intrinsic nature.'

Kathaṃ pana asabhāvadhammānaṃ jātiādīnaṃ paccayuppannatā, paccayatā cāti āha “jāyamānānaṃ panā”tiādi. Tassāti jātijarāmaraṇassa. Vattabbapadesoti “ṭhapetvā”ti vattabbapadeso. Ko pana soti? Yathāvuttaṃ nāmaṃ, nāmarūpañca saṅkhārakkhandhena rūpakkhandhena ca jarāmaraṇānaṃ saṅgahitattā[M 0.0145]. “Yo bhavo jātiyā paccayo”ti etena bhavasaṅgahitānipi jātiādīni jātiyā appaccayattā eva “ṭhapetvā”ti na vuttānīti dasseti, paccayabhāvāsaṅkā eva nesaṃ tassā natthīti adhippāyo. Teneva ṭhapetabbagahetabbavisese satīti sāsaṅkaṃ vadati.

But how can birth, etc., which are things without an intrinsic nature, be conditioned and be conditions? He says: 'But of things that are arising...' etc. 'Of that' means: of birth, aging, and death. 'The passage to be stated' means: the passage to be stated is 'except for.' But what is that? The aforesaid name, and name-and-form, because aging and death are included by the aggregate of formations and the aggregate of form. By this 'That existence is a condition for birth,' it shows that although birth, etc., are included in existence, because they are not conditions for birth, they are not mentioned with 'except for.' The intention is that there is not even a suspicion that they are conditions for it. Therefore, when there is a distinction between what should be excluded and what should be included, he speaks with reservation.

Hetucatukkavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Here ends the Explanation of the Tetrad of Causes.

4. Aññamaññacatukkavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Tetrad of Mutuality

246. Paccayuppannassāti [V 0.0141] paccayuppannabhāvino. Visuṃ ṭhitassāti bhavena asaṅgahitassa. Sappadesameva gahitaṃ idha vedanādikkhandhattayasseva adhippetattā niruḷhattā ca. Paccayuppannaṃ ṭhapetvā paccayabhūtaṃyeva nāmaṃ gahitaṃ, avigatapaccayaniyamābhāvo viya bhave upādānassa aññamaññapaccayaniyamābhāvoti yojanā. Vuttanayenāti “saṅkhatalakkhaṇānaṃ panā”tiādinā vuttanayena.

246. 'Of the conditioned' means of that which has the state of being conditioned. 'Of that which stands apart' means of that which is not included in existence. Here it is taken only partially, because only the three aggregates beginning with feeling are intended and because this is the established usage. Excluding the conditioned, only name that has become a condition is taken. The construction is: just as there is an absence of the rule of the presence condition, so for clinging in relation to existence there is an absence of the rule of the mutuality condition. 'By the stated method' means by the method stated in the passage beginning, 'But of the characteristics of the conditioned...'

Aññamaññapaccayo viya aññamaññapaccayoti ayamattho idhādhippetoti dassento “aññamañña…pe… adhippeto siyā”ti āha. Tathā ca vadanti “aññamaññañcettha na paṭṭhāne āgataaññamaññavasena gahetabba”nti. Cakkhāyatanupacayādīnanti uparūpari citāni viya uppannacakkhāyatanādīni, cakkhāyatanādīnaṃ vā upatthambhakāni cakkhāyatanupacayādīni.

Showing that the meaning intended here is 'a condition of mutuality like a mutual condition,' he says, 'mutual... etc. ...would be intended.' And so they say: 'And here mutuality should not be taken in the sense of the mutuality condition as it appears in the Paṭṭhāna.' 'The accumulation of the eye base, etc.' means the eye base, etc., that have arisen as if piled up one on top of another; or the accumulation of the eye base, etc., are the supports for the eye base, etc.

Aññamaññacatukkavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Here ends the Explanation of the Tetrad of Mutuality.

Saṅkhārādimūlakanayamātikāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Matrix of Methods Rooted in Formations, etc.

247. Yadipi sāmaññato gataviseso, tathāpi sāmaññaggahaṇena nayagato viseso sarūpato dassito hotīti “nāmapaccayā avijjā”ti vatvāpi nāmavisesānaṃ tassā paccayabhāvo dassetabboti āha “nāmavisesānaṃ…pe… vuttā”ti. “Yadeva pana nāma”ntiādi kasmā vuttaṃ, nanu nāmaggahaṇena aggahitopi jātiādi bhavaggahaṇena gahitoti dassitovāyamatthoti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “bhavaggahaṇena cā”tiādi. Idhāpīti “bhavapaccayā avijjā”ti idhāpi. Na [M 0.0146] siyāti “avijjāpaccayā avijjā”ti vuttaṃ na siyā. Tasmāti yasmā sāmaññacoditaṃ visesacoditameva na hoti, tasmā. Soti bhavo. Tenāti sabhāvāsabhāvadhammasaṅgahaṇena.

247. Although a specific point is understood in general, still, by the general term a specific point pertaining to the method is shown in its own nature. Therefore, even after saying 'ignorance is conditioned by name,' in order to show that specific kinds of name are a condition for it, he says, 'of specific names... etc. ...is stated.' Why was the passage beginning 'But whatever name...' stated? In reference to the objection that this meaning is already shown since birth, etc., though not included by the term 'name,' are included by the term 'existence,' he says, 'And by the term "existence"...' etc. 'Here too' means: here too in 'ignorance is conditioned by existence.' 'It would not be' means: what is stated would not be 'ignorance is conditioned by ignorance.' 'Therefore' means: because what is generally stated is not what is specifically stated, therefore... 'It' means existence. 'By that' means: by the inclusion of things with and without an intrinsic nature.

Upādānassapi bhavekadesattā vuttaṃ “upādānapaccayā…pe… aggahite”ti. “Bhavapaccayā [V 0.0142] jātī”ti idaṃ vacanaṃ sandhāyāha “bhavasaddo…pe… vuccamāno”ti. “Nāmapaccayā avijjā”ti ettha paccayuppannaṃ ṭhapetvā paccayassa gahaṇato avijjāvinimuttā eva cattāro khandhā nāmasaddena vuccantīti āha “na nāmasaddo niravasesabodhako”ti. Na cettha ekaṃsato kāraṇaṃ maggitabbaṃ. Yena bhava-saddo niravasesabodhako, na nāma-saddoti āha “evaṃsabhāvā hi etā niruttiyo”ti. Iminā adhippāyenāti bhavasaddo niravasesabodhako upādinnacatukkhandhavisayattāti iminā adhippāyena. Jāyamānādidhammavikārabhāvato jāyamānādikkhandhapaṭibaddhā jātiādayo vucceyyuṃ, na pana jātiādipaṭibaddhā jāyamānādikkhandhāti na ekacittakkhaṇe jātiādīnaṃ avijjāya paccayabhāvo sambhavatīti imamatthamāha “jāyamānānaṃ panā”tiādinā. Nānācittakkhaṇe pana jātiādayo avijjāya upanissayapaccayo hontīti “ekacittakkhaṇe”ti visesitaṃ. Tenevāti asambhaveneva.

Because clinging too is a part of existence, it is said, 'With clinging as condition... etc. ...when not grasped.' Referring to the statement 'Birth is conditioned by existence,' he says, 'The term "existence"... etc. ...being spoken of.' Here, in 'Ignorance is conditioned by name,' since the condition is taken by excluding the conditioned phenomenon, only the four aggregates free from ignorance are referred to by the term 'name.' Thus he says, 'The term "name" is not an exhaustive indicator.' And here a conclusive reason should not be sought as to why the term 'existence' is an exhaustive indicator but the term 'name' is not. Thus he says, 'For such is the nature of these expressions.' 'By this intention' means: by the intention that the term 'existence' is an exhaustive indicator because its domain is the four clung-to aggregates. Because they are alterations of phenomena such as those that are arising, birth, etc., would be said to be connected to the aggregates that are arising, etc., but the aggregates that are arising are not connected to birth, etc. Thus it is not possible for birth, etc., to be a condition for ignorance in a single mind-moment. He states this meaning with the passage beginning, 'But of those that are arising...' But in different mind-moments, birth, etc., are a decisive support condition for ignorance; hence it is specified 'in a single mind-moment.' 'By that very reason' means: precisely because of the impossibility.

Mātikāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Here ends the Explanation of the Matrix.

Akusalaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Unwholesome

248-9. Tanti diṭṭhupādānaṃ. Itarassāti kāmupādānassa. Taṇhāgahaṇenāti “taṇhāpaccayā”ti ettha taṇhāgahaṇena gahitattā. Yadi evaṃ nāmaggahaṇena gahitā taṇhā kasmā puna vuttāti āha “nāme viya visesapaccayattābhāvā”ti. “Nāmapaccayā chaṭṭhāyatana”nti ettha hi kāmataṇhāpi nāme saṅgahitāti nāmassa yathārahaṃ chaṭṭhāyatanassa paccayabhāvo vuttoti atthi tattha visesapaccayattaṃ, upādānassa pana bhavasaṅgahopi atthīti “taṇhāpaccayā upādāna”nti etena “kāmupādānapaccayā bhavo”ti etassa nattheva visesoti vuttaṃ “nāme viya visesapaccayattābhāvā”ti. Taṇhā etissā paccayoti taṇhāpaccayā, diṭṭhi[M 0.0147]. Bhavassa paccayabhūtāti duvidhassapi bhavassa kāraṇabhūtā. Ubhayenapi upādānassa bhavaniddese ṭhapetabbataṃyeva vibhāveti. Paccayuppannaṃ paccayo ca ekamevāti “taṇhāpaccayā upādāna”nti ettha vuttapaccayuppannaṃ, “upādānapaccayā bhavo”ti ettha vuttapaccayo ca eko evattho, tasmā paccayo visuṃ paccayuppannato bhinnaṃ katvā na vibhatto.

248-9. This is clinging to views. The other refers to clinging to sensual pleasures. By the inclusion of craving: because it is included by the inclusion of craving in the phrase 'dependent on craving.' If craving is thus included by the inclusion of name, why is it mentioned again? He says: 'Because, unlike in the case of name, it lacks specific conditionality.' For in the phrase 'dependent on name, the sixth sense base,' craving for sensual pleasures is also included under name. Thus, the conditionality of name for the sixth sense base is stated appropriately, and there is a specific conditionality there. But since clinging is also included in becoming, by the statement 'dependent on craving, clinging,' it is said that there is no specific distinction for 'dependent on clinging to sensual pleasures, becoming,' unlike in the case of name. Craving is the condition for this; thus, 'dependent on craving' refers to view. It is the cause of both kinds of becoming. He clarifies that clinging is to be placed in the description of becoming in both instances. The conditioned and the condition are one and the same: in the phrase 'dependent on craving, clinging,' the conditioned is stated, and in 'dependent on clinging, becoming,' the condition is stated, but the meaning is one and the same. Therefore, the condition is not separated and analyzed as distinct from the conditioned.

252. Upatthambhakasamuṭṭhāpanapacchājātapaccayavasenāti [V 0.0143] upatthambhakassa cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa samuṭṭhāpanavasena, pacchājātapaccayavasena ca.

252. By way of the supportive-arising and post-nascence conditions: This means by way of the arising of supportive, mind-originated matter, and by way of the post-nascence condition.

254. Pañcannanti cakkhāyatanādīnaṃ pañcannaṃ. Sahajātādipaccayoti sahajātanissayaatthiavigatādipaccayo. Vatthusaṅkhātaṃ rūpaṃ. Purejātādipaccayoti purejātanissayavippayuttaatthiavigatapaccayo. Pacchājātādipaccayoti pacchājātavippayuttaatthiavigatapaccayo. Chaṭṭhassa sahajātādīti ādi-saddena aññamaññanissayasampayuttaatthiavigatādayo gahitā.

254. Of the five: this refers to the five sense bases beginning with the eye-base. The condition of co-nascence, etc.: this means the condition of co-nascence, dependence, presence, non-disappearance, etc. The matter designated as the base. The condition of pre-nascence, etc.: this means the condition of pre-nascence, dependence, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. The condition of post-nascence, etc.: this means the condition of post-nascence, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. For the sixth, co-nascence, etc.: by the word 'etc.' are included reciprocity, dependence, association, presence, non-disappearance, and so on.

264. Yassāti “yassa ca hotī”ti ettha vuttaṃ “yassā”ti padaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tenāha “hotīti yojetabba”nti.

264. 'Of which': this refers to the word 'of which' (yassā) mentioned in the phrase 'of which there is' (yassa ca hoti). Therefore, he says: 'It should be connected with "there is."

280. Tassāti “balavakilesabhūtāya vicikicchāyā”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 280) padassa. Tenāti “taṇhāṭṭhāne”ti padena. Cittuppādakaṇḍādīsūti ādi-saddena imasmiṃ paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅge suttantabhājanīyādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti.

280. 'Of that': this refers to the phrase 'of doubt which has become a strong defilement' (Vibh-a 280). 'By that': this refers to the phrase 'in the place of craving.' 'In the section on the arising of consciousness, etc.': here, by the word 'etc.' are included the Suttanta Analysis and so on in this Analysis of Dependent Origination.

Akusalaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Unwholesome is concluded.

Kusalābyākataniddesavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Wholesome and the Indeterminate

306. Sabyāpārānīti saussāhāni, vipākadhammānīti attho. Parihīnaṃ avijjāṭṭhānaṃ etesanti parihīnāvijjāṭṭhānā.

306. ‘With activity’ means with effort; the meaning, however, is ‘resultant phenomena.’ ‘The basis of ignorance is abandoned for them,’ thus they are ‘those for whom the basis of ignorance has been abandoned.’

Sandhāyāti adhippāyaṃ vibhāvento viya vadati, sarūpeneva pana “na ca cakkhuviññāṇādīni rūpaṃ samuṭṭhāpentī”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 306) aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Nāmarūpaṃ na na labbhatīti yojanā.

'Having intended': this is spoken as if explaining the intention, but in essence it is said in the commentary: 'nor do eye-consciousness, etc., produce matter' (Vibh-a 306). The construction is: 'Name-and-form is not unobtainable.'

Kusalābyākataniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Wholesome and the Indeterminate is concluded.

Avijjāmūlakakusalaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Wholesome Rooted in Ignorance

334. Kusalaphaleti [M 0.0148][V 0.0144] kusalavipākapaṭisandhiviññāṇassa gahitattā tassa sādurasavisarukkhabījasadisatā vuttā.

334. ‘In wholesome result’: because the rebirth-linking consciousness, which is a wholesome result, is included, its similarity to the seed of a poison-tree with a sweet taste is stated.

Yadipi “saṅkhārahetuka”ntiādinā yojanā labbhati, avigatacatukkādīni pana na labbhanti yathālābhayojanāya dassitattā.

Although a construction beginning with ‘conditioned by formations’ is obtained, the tetrads beginning with the non-disappearance condition are not obtained, since they are shown by way of application according to what is available.

Avijjāmūlakakusalaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of Wholesome States Rooted in Ignorance is concluded.

Kusalamūlakavipākaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Exposition of Results Rooted in Wholesome Qualities

343. Kammaṃ viya paccayo hoti vipākabhāvatoti adhippāyo. Vipākassa kammaṃ paccayo hontaṃ sātisayaṃ hotīti tassa nippariyāyatā, taṃsampayuttānaṃ pariyāyatā siyāti adhippāyena “pariyāyena upanissayapaccayoti vuttānī”ti āha. “Kusalo dhammo abyākatassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo (paṭṭhā. 1.1.423), akusalo dhammo abyākatassa dhammassa (paṭṭhā. 1.1.423), vipākadhammadhammo nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.3.103) pana vacanato nippariyāyena sabbepi kusalākusalā dhammā vipākassa upanissayapaccayo hotīti ayamattho dissati. “Kusalamūlaṃ akusalamūla”nti imesaṃ anvādesopi paccayasaddāpekkhāya “esā”ti pulliṅgavasena vuttoti dassento āha “esāti…pe… yojetabba”nti.

343. The intention is that, due to being a result, it is a condition in the same way as kamma. When kamma is a condition for its result, it is pre-eminent—this is its non-figurative nature. With the intention that for states associated with it, there could be a figurative nature, he says: 'They are stated as decisive-support conditions by way of figurative expression.' However, from the statements 'A wholesome state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of the decisive-support condition (Paṭṭh. 1.1.423), an unwholesome state is a condition for an indeterminate state (Paṭṭh. 1.1.423), a resultant-state-dhamma is a condition for a neither-resultant-nor-resultant-state-dhamma by way of the decisive-support condition (Paṭṭh. 1.3.103),' this meaning appears: that all wholesome and unwholesome dhammas are, in a non-figurative sense, a decisive-support condition for a result. Regarding the subsequent reference to ‘wholesome root, unwholesome root,’ to show that ‘this’ is stated in the masculine gender with reference to the word ‘condition,’ he says: ‘“This”... should be connected.’

“Manasikāropī”tiādinā appahīnāvijjānampi kiriyāya kusalākusalamūlāni, avijjā ca upanissayā na hontīti dasseti. Kammavaṭṭavipākavaṭṭabhūtāniyeva saṅkhāraviññāṇāni pacchimanaye adhippetānīti vuttaṃ “kiriyāni pana…pe… gacchantī”ti. Tesaṃ paccayānaṃ vasena anekappakāratoti adhippāyoti yojanā.

By the phrase beginning with ‘even attention,’ he shows that for those who have not abandoned ignorance, the wholesome and unwholesome roots, and ignorance itself, do not become decisive-support conditions for functional consciousness. It is said that the formations and consciousness that constitute the round of kamma and the round of result are indeed what are intended in the latter method, as was stated: 'But functional states... proceed.' The construction is that the meaning is 'being of various kinds due to those conditions.'

Navādibhedānanti [V 0.0145] navaaṭṭhasattachāti evaṃpabhedānaṃ. Catunnaṃ catukkānanti purimanaye pacchimanaye ca āgatānaṃ yathālābhaṃ catunnaṃ catunnaṃ catukkānaṃ. “Kusalākusalānaṃ [M 0.0149] pana vipāke cā”ti ca-saddena kusalākusale cāti samuccetabboti āha “kusala…pe… vattabba”nti. Mūlapadekapaccayatāvasenāti mūlapadassa ekapaccayabhāvavasena upanissayapaccayatāvasena. Ekasseva nayassāti kusalākusalesu avijjāmūlakassa, vipākesu kusalākusalamūlakassāti evaṃ ekasseva nayassa vasena. Dhammapaccayabhedeti dhammassa paccayabhūtassa, paccayuppannassa vā paccayabhāvena bhedeti imamatthaṃ dassento “avijjādīna”ntiādiṃ vatvā puna tameva “taṃtaṃcittuppādā”tiādinā pakārantarena vibhāveti.

Of the divisions beginning with nine: this refers to divisions such as nine, eight, and seven. Of the four tetrads: this refers to the four tetrads that have appeared in the preceding method and the subsequent method, according to what is obtained. 'And as for the results of wholesome and unwholesome states': by the word 'ca' (and), wholesome and unwholesome states should also be included, hence he says: 'wholesome... should be stated.' By way of the root-term being a single condition: this means by way of the root-term being a single condition, that is, by way of the decisive-support conditionality. According to a single method: this means according to a single method, such as in the case of wholesome and unwholesome states rooted in ignorance, and in the case of results rooted in wholesome and unwholesome qualities. The distinction in the condition of phenomena: to show this meaning—that there is a distinction in the condition of a phenomenon as a condition, or of a conditioned phenomenon by way of its conditionality—having stated 'beginning with ignorance,' etc., he then explains the same in another way with 'that particular arising of mind,' etc.

Kusalamūlakavipākaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Results Rooted in Wholesome Qualities is concluded.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Abhidhamma Analysis is concluded.

Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of Dependent Origination is concluded.

7. Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅgo

7. The Analysis of the Foundations of Mindfulness

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Suttanta Analysis

Uddesavāravaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Summary Section

355. Samānasaddavacanīyānaṃ [M 0.0150] atthānaṃ uddharaṇaṃ atthuddhāro. So yasmā saddatthavicāro na hoti, tasmā vuttaṃ “na idha…pe… atthadassana”nti. Pa-saddo padhānatthadīpako “paṇītā dhammā”tiādīsu (dha. sa. tikamātikā 14) viya.

355. The extraction of meanings of things to be expressed with similar words is meaning-extraction. Since this is not an investigation of words and meanings, therefore it is said, 'Not here... but seeing the meaning.' The prefix 'pa-' indicates the primary meaning, as in 'excellent qualities' and so on (Dhs. Tikamātikā 14).

Anavassutatā anupakiliṭṭhatā. Tenāha “tadubhayavītivattatā”ti.

Non-infusion is being undefiled. Hence it is said, 'transcending both.'

Bhusatthaṃ pakkhandananti bhusatthavisiṭṭhaṃ pakkhandanaṃ anupavisanaṃ.

'Plunging into what is significant' means plunging into and entering what is distinguished by its great significance.

Assādassāti taṇhāya. “Niccaṃ attā”ti abhinivesavatthutāya diṭṭhiyā visesakāraṇānaṃ cittadhammānaṃ taṇhāyapi vatthubhāvato visesaggahaṇaṃ, tathā kāyavedanānaṃ diṭṭhiyāpi vatthubhāvasambhavato “visesenā”ti vuttaṃ. Sarāgavītarāgādivibhāgadvayavaseneva cittānupassanāya vuttattā taṃ “nātipabhedagata”nti vuttaṃ. Dhammāti idha saññāsaṅkhārakkhandhā adhippetā, saṅkhārakkhandho ca phassādivasena anekabhedoti dhammānupassanā “atipabhedagatā”ti vuttā. Sarāgādivibhāgavasena soḷasabhedattā vā cittānupassanā nātipabhedagatā vuttā, sutte āgatanayena nīvaraṇādivasena anekabhedattā dhammānupassanā atipabhedagatā vuttā. “Visuddhimaggoti [V 0.0147] vuttānī”ti ānetvā yojetabbaṃ. Tā anupassanā etesanti tadanupassanā, cittadhammānupassino puggalā, tesaṃ.

‘Of delight’ refers to craving. There is a specific inclusion of certain mental states, which are special causes, because they are a basis for craving and also for views that adhere to ‘permanent self.’ Similarly, since it is possible for the body and feelings to be a basis for views, it is said ‘especially.’ Since the contemplation of mind is described only by way of the twofold division—with lust and without lust, etc.—it is said to be ‘not overly differentiated.’ Here, ‘dhammas’ are understood to refer to the aggregates of perception and formations, and since the aggregate of formations has many aspects such as contact, etc., the contemplation of dhammas is said to be ‘highly differentiated.’ Alternatively, because the contemplation of mind has sixteen divisions based on whether it is with or without lust, etc., it is said to be ‘not overly differentiated,’ whereas the contemplation of dhammas, following the method found in the suttas, is said to be ‘highly differentiated’ due to its many divisions such as the hindrances, etc. The phrase ‘they are called the Path of Purification’ should be brought in and connected. ‘Those contemplations are theirs’ is the meaning of tadanupassanā; this refers to those individuals who contemplate mind and dhammas, and the word is in the genitive case, ‘of them.’

Tattha “asubhabhāvadassanenā”ti yathāṭhitavasenāpi yojanā labbhateva. Bhavoghassa vedanā vatthu bhavassādabhāvato. Niccaggahaṇavasenāti attābhinivesavisiṭṭhassa niccaggahaṇassa vasena. Tathā hi vuttaṃ “sassatassa attano”ti. Oghesu vuttanayā eva yogāsavesupi yojanā atthato abhinnattāti te na gahitā. Niccaggahaṇavasenāti [M 0.0151] attābhinivesavisiṭṭhassa niccaggahaṇassa vasena. Paṭhamoghatatiyacatutthaganthayojanāyaṃ vuttanayeneva kāyacittadhammānaṃ itarupādānavatthutā gahetabbāti vedanāya diṭṭhupādānavatthutā dassitā. Tathā kāyavedanānaṃ chandadosāgativatthutā kāmoghabyāpādakāyaganthavatthutāvacanena vuttāti. Tenāha “avuttānaṃ vuttanayena vatthubhāvo yojetabbo”ti.

Here, 'by seeing the foul nature'—the connection can be obtained even by interpreting it in accordance with its literal meaning. Feeling is the basis for the flood of becoming, because of delight in becoming. 'By way of grasping at permanence' means by way of the grasping at permanence that is specified by the adherence to self. Thus it was said, 'of an eternal self.' The application to the yokes and taints is the same as the method stated for the floods, since their meanings are not different in substance; therefore, they are not taken up. 'By way of grasping at permanence' means by way of the grasping at permanence that is specified by the adherence to self. In connecting the first flood and the third and fourth ties, that the body, mind, and dhammas are the basis for the other kinds of clinging should be understood in the same way as stated; thus, it is shown that feeling is the basis for the clinging to views. Similarly, that the body and feelings are the basis for going astray through desire and aversion is stated by the statement that they are the basis for the flood of sensual desire and the bodily tie of ill will. Therefore, it is said, 'the status as a basis for what is unstated should be connected by the method for what has been stated.'

Dhāraṇatā asammussanatā, anussaraṇameva vā. Ekatteti ekasabhāve nissaraṇādivasena. Samāgamo sacchikiriyā. Satipaṭṭhānasabhāvo sammāsatitā niyyānasatitā samānabhāgatā ekajātitā sabhāgatā. Purimasminti “ekatte nibbāne samāgamo ekattasamosaraṇa”nti etasmiṃ atthe. Visunti nānāatthadvayabhāvena. Tadeva gamanaṃ samosaraṇanti satisaddatthantarābhāvā…pe… ekabhāvassāti yojetabbaṃ. Satisaddatthavasena avuccamāneti “eko satipaṭṭhānasabhāvo ekatta”ntiādinā avuccamāne, “ekatte nibbāne samāgamo ekattasamosaraṇa”nti evaṃ vuccamāneti attho. Dhāraṇatāva satīti “saraṇatā”ti (dha. sa. 14) vuttadhāraṇatā eva satīti katvā. Satisaddatthantarābhāvāti satisaṅkhātassa saraṇekattasamosaraṇasaddatthato aññassa atthassa abhāvā. Purimanti saraṇapadaṃ. Nibbānasamosaraṇepīti yathāvutte dutiye atthe saraṇekattasamosaraṇapadāni sahitāneva satipaṭṭhānekabhāvassa ñāpakāni, evaṃ nibbānasamosaraṇepi “ekatte nibbāne samāgamo ekattasamosaraṇa”nti etasmimpi atthe sati…pe… kāraṇāni.

The state of retaining, non-forgetting, or simply remembering. 'Oneness' means in a single nature, by way of liberation, and so on. 'Coming together' is realization. The nature of the foundations of mindfulness is right mindfulness, mindfulness leading to release, having a common part, being of a single birth, and having a similar nature. 'In the former' means in this sense: 'coming together in the oneness of Nibbāna, convergence in oneness.' 'Separately' means in the state of having two different meanings. That very going is convergence—due to the absence of another meaning for the word 'mindfulness'…it should be connected as 'of the single state.' When it is not stated by way of the meaning of the word 'mindfulness'—such as 'the single nature of the foundations of mindfulness is oneness,' and so on—but rather, it is stated as 'coming together in the oneness of Nibbāna, convergence in oneness,' this is the meaning. The state of retaining itself is mindfulness—taking it that the state of retaining mentioned as 'remembering' (Dhs. 14) is indeed mindfulness. 'Due to the absence of another meaning for the word mindfulness' means that apart from the meanings of the words 'remembering,' 'oneness,' and 'convergence,' there is no other meaning for what is designated as 'mindfulness.' 'The former' refers to the word 'remembering.' Even in the convergence upon Nibbāna—just as in the second meaning mentioned, the words 'remembering,' 'oneness,' and 'convergence' together indicate the single nature of the foundations of mindfulness, so too in the convergence upon Nibbāna—'coming together in the oneness of Nibbāna, convergence in oneness'—in this sense as well, mindfulness…are the causes.

Ānāpānapabbādīnanti ānāpānapabbairiyāpathacatusampajañña koṭṭhāsa dhātumanasikāranavasivathikapabbānīti etesaṃ. Imesu pana yasmā kesuci devānaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ na ijjhati, tasmā tāni anāmasitvā yadipi koṭṭhāsadhātumanasikāravasenevettha desanā pavattā, desanantare [V 0.0148] pana āgataṃ anavasesaṃ kāyānupassanāvibhāgaṃ dassetuṃ “cuddasavidhena kāyānupassanaṃ bhāvetvā”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 355) vuttaṃ. Tenāha “mahāsatipaṭṭhānasutte vuttāna”nti. “Tathā”ti iminā “mahāsatipaṭṭhānasutte (dī. ni. 2.382) vuttāna”nti imameva upasaṃharati. Pañcavidhenāti nīvaraṇaupādānakkhandhāyatanabojjhaṅgaariyasaccānaṃ vasena pañcadhā. Bhāvanānubhāvo ariyamaggaggahaṇasamatthatā.

‘Of the sections on mindfulness of breathing, and so on’ refers to these: the sections on mindfulness of breathing, the postures, the fourfold clear comprehension, the parts of the body, the contemplation of the elements, and the nine cemetery contemplations. Among these, however, since for some deities the meditation subject does not succeed, those are not touched upon. And although the teaching here proceeds only by way of the contemplation of the parts of the body and the elements, in another discourse, to show the complete division of the contemplation of the body that is found there, it is said: 'Having developed the contemplation of the body in fourteen ways' (Vibh-a 355). Therefore, he said: 'As taught in the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta.' By this word 'Thus,' he concludes with this very same phrase: 'As taught in the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta' (DN 2.382). 'Fivefold' means fivefold by way of the hindrances, the aggregates of clinging, the sense bases, the factors of enlightenment, and the noble truths. The power of development is the capability of grasping the noble path.

Taṃniyamatoti [M 0.0152] tassā kāyānupassanādipaṭipattiyā niyamato. Tassā bhikkhubhāve niyate sāpi bhikkhubhāve niyatāyeva nāma hoti.

'Because of the certainty of that' means due to the certainty of that practice, beginning with the contemplation of the body. Since her state as a monastic is certain, she too is indeed certain of the state of a monastic.

Kāyānupassanāuddesavaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Summary Section on the Contemplation of the Body

Etthāti kāye. Avayavā assa atthīti avayavī, samudāyo, samūhoti attho, so pana avayavavinimuttaṃ drabyantaranti gāho laddhi avayavīgāho. Hatthapādādiaṅgulinakhādiaṅgapaccaṅge sannivesavisiṭṭhe upādāya yāyaṃ aṅgapaccaṅgasamaññā ceva kāyasamaññā ca, taṃ atikkamitvā itthipurisarathaghaṭādidrabyantiparikappanaṃ samaññātidhāvanaṃ. Atha vā yathāvuttasamaññaṃ atikkamitvā pakatiādidrabyādijīvādikāyādipadatthantaraparikappanaṃ samaññātidhāvanaṃ. Niccasārādigāhabhūto abhiniveso sārādānābhiniveso.

'Herein' means in the body. 'Having parts' (avayavī) is so called because it has parts; the meaning is an aggregate, a collection. But the grasping, the view, that it is another substance separate from the parts is 'grasping at a whole.' Based on the limbs and minor limbs such as hands, feet, fingers, and nails, which are specified by their arrangement, the conceptual fabrication of other substances like 'woman,' 'man,' 'chariot,' 'pot,' and so on, which goes beyond the designation of limbs and minor limbs and the designation of 'body,' is 'the overrunning of designation.' Or alternatively, 'the overrunning of designation' is the conceptual fabrication of other meanings for words, such as 'nature,' 'substance,' 'soul,' 'body,' and so on, going beyond the designations as stated. The adherence, which is the grasping of permanence, essence, and so on, is 'the adherence of grasping at an essence.'

Na taṃ diṭṭhanti taṃ itthipurisādi diṭṭhaṃ na hoti. Diṭṭhaṃ vā itthipurisādi na hotīti yojanā. Yathāvuttanti kesādibhūtupādāyasamūhasaṅkhātaṃ.

'That is not seen' means that a woman, man, and so on, is not seen. Or, the application is that what is seen is not a woman, man, and so on. 'As stated' refers to what is reckoned as the collection of primary and derived matter beginning with the hair of the head.

Kesādipathavinti kesādisaññitaṃ sasambhārapathaviṃ. Pubbāpariyabhāvenāti santānavasena. Aññatthāti “āpokāya”nti evamādīsu.

'The earth element beginning with hair' means the earth element designated as beginning with hair, together with its associated components. 'By way of before and after' means in terms of the continuity. 'Elsewhere' refers to expressions such as 'the water element' and so on.

Ajjhattabahiddhāti saparasantāne kāyo vuttoti. “Kāyo”ti cettha sammasanupagā rūpadhammā adhippetāti āha “ajjhattabahiddhādhammāna”nti. Ghaṭitaṃ ekābaddhaṃ ārammaṇaṃ ghaṭitārammaṇaṃ, ekārammaṇabhūtanti attho. Tenāha “ekato ārammaṇabhāvo natthī”ti.

'Internally and externally' means that the body is spoken of in one's own and others' continuities. Here, by 'body,' the material phenomena that are subject to comprehension are intended; hence it is said, 'of internal and external phenomena.' A 'connected object' (ghaṭitārammaṇaṃ) is a connected (ghaṭitaṃ), single, bound object; the meaning is 'having become a single object.' Therefore, he said, 'there is no state of being a single object.'

Antoolīyanā [V 0.0149] antosaṅkoco antarāvosānaṃ.

Shrinking within (antoolīyanā) means internal contraction, cessation within.

Dvīhīti abhijjhāvinayadomanassavinayehi.

'By two things' means by the removal of covetousness and the removal of displeasure.

Sati ca sampajaññañca satisampajaññaṃ, tena. Etena karaṇabhūtena. Vipakkhadhammehi anantaritattā avicchinnassa. Tassa sabbatthikakammaṭṭhānassa.

Mindfulness and clear comprehension is 'mindfulness-and-clear-comprehension'; by that. By this, which has become the instrument. Of that which is uninterrupted, because it is not interrupted by opposing states. Of that meditation subject which is applicable in all situations.

Kāyānupassanāuddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Summary Section on the Contemplation of the Body is concluded.

Vedanānupassanādiuddesavaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Summary Section on the Contemplation of Feeling, and so on

Sukhādīnanti [M 0.0153] sukhadukkhādukkhamasukhānaṃ.

'Of pleasure, and so on' means of pleasure, pain, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant.

Rūpādiārammaṇanānattabhedānaṃ vasena yojetabbanti sambandho. Tathā ca sesesupi. Savatthukāvatthukādīti ādi-saddena hīnādiyoniādibhedaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Visuṃ visuṃ na vattabbanti codanaṃ dassetīti yojanā. Ekatthāti kāyādīsu ekasmiṃ. Purimacodanāyāti “pubbe pahīnattā puna pahānaṃ na vattabba”nti codanāya. Pahīnanti vikkhambhitaṃ. Paṭipakkhabhāvanāyāti maggabhāvanāya. Ubhayatthāti ubhayacodanāya. Ubhayanti parihāradvayaṃ. Yasmā purimacodanāya nānāpuggalaparihāro, nānācittakkhaṇikaparihāro ca sambhavati, dutiyacodanāya pana nānācittakkhaṇikaparihāroyeva, tasmā vuttaṃ “sambhavato yojetabba”nti. Maggasatipaṭṭhānabhāvanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sabbatthāti sabbesu kāyādīsu.

The connection is that it should be connected by way of the various distinctions of objects such as form, and so on. And similarly in the remaining cases. 'With basis, without basis, and so on'—here, the word 'and so on' includes distinctions such as inferior, and so on, and origin, and so on. The application is that this shows the objection: 'They should not be spoken of separately.' 'In one' refers to one among the body, and so on. 'Regarding the former objection' refers to the objection that 'since it was abandoned before, its abandonment should not be spoken of again.' 'Abandoned' means suppressed. 'By the development of the counterpart' refers to the development of the path. 'In both cases' refers to both objections. 'Both' means the two kinds of refutations. Because for the first objection, a refutation by way of different individuals and a refutation by way of different moments of consciousness are both possible, whereas for the second objection, only the refutation by way of different moments of consciousness is possible, therefore it is said, 'it should be connected according to possibility.' This is stated with reference to the development of the path and the foundations of mindfulness. 'In all' refers to all instances, such as the body, and so on.

Vedanānupassanādiuddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Summary Section on the Contemplation of Feeling, and so on, is concluded.

Uddesavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Chapter of Summaries is concluded.

Kāyānupassanāniddesavaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Detailed Exposition on the Contemplation of the Body

356. Ajjhattādīti [V 0.0150] ādi-saddena idha vuttā bahiddhāajjhattabahiddhāanupassanappakārā viya mahāsatipaṭṭhānasutte vuttā samudayadhammānupassiādianupassanappakārāpi kāyānupassanābhāvato gahitā icceva veditabbaṃ. Tatthāti ajjhattādianupassanāyaṃ. Cuddasa pakārā mahāsatipaṭṭhānasutte āgatacuddasappakārādike apekkhitvā idha vuttā. Ajjhattādippakāro eko pakāroti āha “ekappakāraniddesenā”ti. Bāhiresūti ekaccesu aññatitthiyesu. Tesampi hi ānāpānādivasena samathapakkhikā kāyānupassanā sambhavati. Tenāha “ekadesasambhavato”ti.

356. Ajjhattādi (internal, etc.): by the word 'etc.' it should be understood that just as the modes of contemplation mentioned here—such as external and internal-external—so too the modes of contemplation mentioned in the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta—such as contemplating the nature of arising, etc.—are also included, because they are forms of contemplation of the body. Tattha (therein) refers to this contemplation of the internal, etc. The fourteen modes are mentioned here with reference to the fourteen modes, etc., that appear in the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta. That the mode of 'internal, etc.' is one mode, he says, 'by way of a single mode of exposition'. Bāhiresu (in externals) refers to some adherents of other sects. For even among them, contemplation of the body, which belongs to the side of serenity, is possible by way of mindfulness of breathing, etc. Therefore, he said, 'because of its possibility in part'.

Tacassa ca atacaparicchinnatā tacena aparicchinnatā atthīti yojanā. “Dīghabāhu naccatū”tiādīsu viya aññapadatthepi samāse avayavapadatthasaṅgaho labbhatevāti vuttaṃ “kāyekadesabhūto taco gahito evā”ti. Tacapaṭibaddhānaṃ nakhadantanhārumaṃsānaṃ, tacapaṭibaddhānaṃ tadanuppaviṭṭhamūlānaṃ kesalomānaṃ, tappaṭibaddhapaṭibaddhānaṃ itaresaṃ samūhabhūto sabbo kāyo [M 0.0154] “tacapariyanto”tveva vuttoti dassento “tappaṭibaddhā”tiādimāha. Atthi kesā, atthi lomāti sambandho. Tattha atthīti puthuttavācī ekaṃ nipātapadaṃ, na kiriyāpadaṃ. Kiriyāpadatte hi santīti vattabbaṃ siyā, vacanavipallāsena vā vuttanti.

The construction is that for the skin, there is non-delimitation by what is not skin, and it is not delimited by the skin. Just as in phrases like 'Dīghabāhu dances,' etc., even in a compound with a different meaning, the inclusion of the meaning of the constituent terms is obtained; thus it was said, 'The skin is indeed taken as a part of the body'. To show that the nails, teeth, sinews, and flesh connected to the skin; the roots of the hair and body hair, which have entered into it and are connected to the skin; and the remainder, which are connected to what is connected to it—the whole body being a mass—is called 'having skin as its boundary' (tacapariyanto), he said, 'connected to it,' and so on. 'There are head hairs, there are body hairs'—this is the connection. Therein, 'atthi' (there is/are) is a particle denoting plurality, not a verb. For if it were a verb, it would be appropriate to say 'santi' (they exist), or it is said due to a change of number.

Kammaṭṭhānassa vācuggatakaraṇādinā uggaṇhanaṃ uggaho. Koṭṭhāsapāḷiyā hi vācuggatakaraṇaṃ, manasikiriyāya kesādīnaṃ vaṇṇādito upadhāraṇassa ca paguṇabhāvāpādanaṃ idha uggaho. Yena pana nayena yogāvacaro tattha kusalo hoti, so vidhīti vutto.

Uggaha (grasping) is the grasping of the meditation subject by learning it by heart and other methods. Here, uggaha refers to learning the Pāli text of the parts by heart, and also making proficient, through attention, the determining of the characteristics of the hair and other parts, starting with their color. The method by which the meditator becomes skilled in that is called vidhi (procedure).

Purimehīti purimapurimehi pañcakachakkehi sambandho vutto. “Maṃsaṃ…pe… vakka”nti hi anulomato vakkapañcakassa puna “vakkaṃ…pe… kesā”ti vakkapañcakassa, tacapañcakassa ca paṭilomato sajjhāyakkamo sambandho dassito. Svāyaṃ sajjhāyoti sambandho. Visuṃ tipañcāhanti anulomato pañcāhaṃ, paṭilomato pañcāhaṃ, anulomapaṭilomato pañcāhanti evaṃ pañcakachakkesu paccekaṃ tipañcāhaṃ. Purimehi ekato tipañcāhanti tacapañcakādīhi saddhiṃ anulomato vakkapañcakādīni ekajjhaṃ katvā vuttanayeneva tipañcāhaṃ[V 0.0151]. Ādiantadassanavasenātiādibhūtassa anulomato sajjhāyassa, anulomapaṭilomato sajjhāye antabhūtassa paṭilomato sajjhāyassa dassanavasena. Tenāha “anuloma…pe… antimo”ti. Etampīti yadidaṃ purimehi saddhiṃ pacchimassa pañcakādino ekato sajjhāyakaraṇaṃ, pañcakādīnaṃ paccekaṃ anulomādinā sajjhāyappakārato añño sajjhāyappakāro esoti attho. Dvinnaṃ hatthānaṃ ekamukhā aññamaññasambandhā ṭhapitā aṅguliyo idha hatthasaṅkhalikāti adhippetāti āha “aṅgulipantī”ti. Asubhalakkhaṇaṃ kesādīnaṃ paṭikkūlabhāvo. Thaddhādibhāvo dhātulakkhaṇaṃ.

Purimehi (with the preceding) means that the connection with the very preceding fivefold and sixfold groups has been stated. Indeed, 'flesh... up to kidneys' shows the sequence of recitation in forward order for the kidney pentad, and again, 'kidneys... up to hair' shows the sequence of recitation in reverse order for the kidney pentad and the skin pentad. This recitation is the connection. Visuṃ tipañcāhaṃ (separately, three five-day periods) means five days in forward order, five days in reverse order, and five days in forward-reverse order; thus, for each of the fivefold and sixfold groups, there are three five-day periods. Purimehi ekato tipañcāhaṃ (with the preceding groups, three five-day periods together) means three five-day periods in the manner stated, by combining the kidney pentad, etc., in forward order, together with the skin pentad, etc. Ādiantadassanavasena (by way of seeing the beginning and the end) means by way of seeing the forward recitation as the beginning, and the reverse recitation as the end of the forward-reverse recitation. Therefore, he said, 'forward... up to the last'. Etampi (this too) means that this is another mode of recitation, distinct from the mode of reciting each of the fivefold groups, etc., in forward and other orders, namely, reciting the later fivefold group, etc., together with the preceding ones. Dvinnaṃ hatthānaṃ ekamukhā aññamaññasambandhā ṭhapitā aṅguliyo (the fingers of two hands placed interconnectedly facing one another) are intended here as the hatthasaṅkhalikā (hand-chain); hence, he said, 'aṅgulipantī' (row of fingers). Asubhalakkhaṇaṃ (the characteristic of the unattractive) is the repulsiveness of hair, etc. Thaddhādibhāvo (the state of rigidity, etc.) is the characteristic of the elements.

Attano koṭṭhāso, samāno vā koṭṭhāso sakoṭṭhāso, tattha bhavo sakoṭṭhāsiko, kammaṭṭhānaṃ.

Sakoṭṭhāso (one's own part) means one's own part, or an equal part; sakoṭṭhāsiko (belonging to one's own part) is that which occurs therein, namely, the meditation subject.

Kāyānupassanaṃ hitvāti asubhato vā dhātuto anupassanaṃ manasikāraṃ akatvā. Pubbe viya pariyantatālañca āditālañca agantvā.

Kāyānupassanaṃ hitvā (having abandoned contemplation of the body) means not having applied the mind to the contemplation of unattractiveness or of the elements. Not having reached the final key-point and the initial key-point as before.

Samādhānādivisesayogena adhikaṃ cittanti adhicittaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “samathavipassanācitta”nti. Manasikaraṇaṃ cittanti ekantaṃ samādhinimittasseva samannāhārakaṃ [M 0.0155] cittaṃ. Vikkhepavasena cittassa nānārammaṇe visaṭappavatti idha pabhañjanaṃ, samādhānena tadabhāvato na ca pabhañjanasabhāvaṃ.

Adhicittaṃ (higher mind) is the mind that is superior by the special application of concentration and other factors. Hence it is said, 'the mind of serenity and insight'. Manasikaraṇaṃ cittaṃ (the mind that attends) is the mind exclusively applying itself to the sign of concentration. Here, pabhañjanaṃ (scattering) is the dissipated activity of the mind on various objects due to distraction; but through concentration, there is an absence of that, and thus it is not of a scattered nature.

Sakkhibhavanatā paccakkhakāritā. Pubbahetādiketi ādi-saddena tadanurūpamanasikārānuyogādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti.

Sakkhibhavanatā (the state of being a witness) means direct experiencing. Pubbahetādike (prior cause, etc.): by the word 'etc.' it includes appropriate attention, application, and so on.

Samappavattanti līnuddhaccarahitaṃ. Tathāpavattiyāti majjhimasamathanimittaṃ paṭipattiyā, tattha ca pakkhandanena siddhāya yathāvuttasamappavattiyā.
