Paññāya tosetīti yāyaṃ tattha jātānaṃ dhammānaṃ anativattanā, indriyānaṃ ekarasatā, tadupagavīriyavāhanā, āsevanāti imāsaṃ sādhikā bhāvanāpaññā, tāya adhicittaṃ toseti pahaṭṭhaṃ karoti. Yathāvuttavisesasiddhiyāva hi taṃsādhikāya paññāya taṃ cittaṃ sampahaṃsitaṃ nāma hoti. Evaṃ sampahaṃsanto ca yasmā sabbaso paribandhavisodhanena paññāya cittaṃ vodāpetīti ca vuccati, tasmā “samuttejeti cā”ti vuttaṃ. Nirassādanti [V 0.0152] pubbenāparaṃ visesālābhena bhāvanārasavirahitaṃ. Sampahaṃsetīti bhāvanāya cittaṃ sammā pahāseti pamodeti. Samuttejetīti sammā tattha uttejeti.

Samappavattaṃ (flowing evenly) means free from sluggishness and restlessness. Tathāpavattiyā (by such even flow) means by the practice towards the middle sign of serenity, and by the even flow as described, which is accomplished by striving therein. Paññāya toseti (it satisfies with wisdom) means that the wisdom of development, which is effective in these qualities—namely, not transgressing the qualities that have arisen, the unity of the faculties, the exertion that supports them, and the cultivation—by that wisdom, it satisfies and gladdens the higher mind. For only through the attainment of the special distinction as described is that mind truly delighted by such effective wisdom. And since, in thus delighting it, one is also said to 'purify' the mind with wisdom through the complete cleansing of all obstacles, therefore it is said, 'and rouses it up'. Nirassādaṃ (devoid of savor) means devoid of the taste of development due to not gaining a further distinction than before. Sampahaṃseti (it delights) means it rightly brightens and gladdens the mind through development. Samuttejeti (it rouses up) means it rightly stimulates it therein.

Āsayo pavattiṭṭhānaṃ.

Āsayo (disposition) means the ground of occurrence.

Vavatthitatanti asaṃkiṇṇataṃ.

Vavatthitataṃ (determined state) means the state of being unmixed.

Antoti abbhantare koṭṭhāse. Sukhumanti sukhumanhāruādiṃ sandhāya vadati.

Anto (inside) means in the internal part. Sukhumaṃ (subtle) refers to the fine sinews and the like.

Tālapaṭṭikā tālapattavilivehi katakaṭasārako.

Tālapaṭṭikā (palm-leaf screen) means a screen made with strips of palm leaves.

Gaṇanāya mattā-saddo katipayehi ūnabhāvadīpanatthaṃ vuccati. Dantaṭṭhivajjitāni tīhi ūnāni tīṇi aṭṭhisatāni. Tasmā “timattānī”ti vuttaṃ. Yaṃ pana visuddhimagge “atirekatisataaṭṭhikasamussaya”nti (visuddhi. 1.122) vuttaṃ, taṃ dantaṭṭhīnipi gahetvā sabbasaṅgāhikanayena vuttaṃ. “Gopphakaṭṭhikādīni avuttānī”ti na vattabbaṃ “ekekasmiṃ pāde dve gopphakaṭṭhīnī”ti vuttattā, “ānisadaṭṭhiādīnī”ti pana vattabbaṃ.

In counting, the term 'matta' is used to indicate a state of being less by a few. Excluding the teeth-bones, there are three hundred bones less by three. Therefore, it is said, `timattāni` (a quantity of three hundred less three). However, what is stated in the Visuddhimagga as 'an aggregate of more than three hundred bones' (Vism. 1.122) is said in a comprehensive way, including the teeth-bones. It should not be said that 'the ankle bones, etc., are not mentioned,' because it is stated that 'in each foot there are two ankle bones.' But it should be said, 'the sitting-bone, etc.'

Tena aṭṭhināti ūruṭṭhinā.

Tena aṭṭhinā (by that bone) means by the thigh bone.

Marumpehīti marumpacuṇṇehi.

Marumpehīti means by powders of gravel.

Susamāhitacittena [M 0.0156] hetubhūtena. Nānārammaṇavipphandanavirahenāti nānārammaṇabhāvena vipphandanaṃ nānārammaṇavipphandanaṃ, tena virahena. Anatikkantapītisukhassa jhānacittassa. Taṃsamaṅgīpuggalassa vā.

By a well-concentrated mind, which is the cause. Nānārammaṇavipphandanavirahena (by freedom from agitation regarding various objects): that is, agitation due to the state of being various objects is 'agitation regarding various objects'; by freedom from that. Of a jhāna-mind that has not transcended rapture and pleasure. Or of a person endowed with that.

Paṭikkūladhātuvaṇṇavisesanti paṭikkūlavisesaṃ, dhātuvisesaṃ, vaṇṇakasiṇavisesaṃ. Vakkapañcakādīsu pañcasu visuṃ, heṭṭhimehi ekato ca sajjhāye channaṃ channaṃ pañcāhānaṃ vasena pañca [V 0.0153] māsā paripuṇṇā labbhanti, tacapañcake pana visuṃ tipañcāhamevāti āha “addhamāse ūnepī”ti. Māsantaragamanaṃ sajjhāyassa sattamādimāsagamanaṃ.

Paṭikkūladhātuvaṇṇavisesanti (the particular aspects of the repulsive, elements, and color) means a particular aspect of the repulsive, a particular aspect of the elements, and a particular aspect of the color kasiṇa. In the five groups beginning with the kidney pentad, five full months are obtained by way of six five-day periods for each of the five recited separately, and also together with the preceding ones. But in the case of the skin pentad, there are only three five-day periods separately; thus it is said, 'even if less by half a month.' Māsantaragamanaṃ (progressing to another month) means the recitation's progressing to the seventh month, etc.

Yamentanti bandhentaṃ.

Yamentanti means binding.

“Nīlaṃ pīta”ntiādinā saṅghāṭe nīlādivavatthānaṃ taṃnissayattā mahābhūte upādāyāti āha “mahābhūtaṃ…pe… duggandhantiādinā”ti. Upādāyarūpaṃ mahābhūtena paricchinnanti yojanā. Tassāti upādārūpassa. Tatoti mahābhūtato. Chāyāya ātapapaccayabhāvo ātapo paccayo etissāti, ātapassa chāyāya uppādakabhāvo chāyātapānaṃ ātapapaccayachāyuppādakabhāvo. Tena uppādetabbauppādakabhāvo aññamaññaparicchedakatāti dasseti. Āyatanāni ca dvārāni cāti dvādasāyatanāni, tadekadesabhūtāni dvārāni ca.

By 'blue, yellow,' etc., is meant the determination of blue and so on in the robe. That this is by taking up the great elements, due to its dependence on them, he says by 'the great elements... bad smell,' etc. The connection is that derived form is delimited by the great elements. 'Of that' means of the derived form. 'From that' means from the great elements. The state of shade having sunlight as its condition means that sunlight is the condition for it; the state of sunlight being the producer of shade is the state of sunlight being the condition for the arising of shade. By this, it shows that the state of being the produced and the state of being the producer mutually delimit each other. 'The sense bases and the doors' means the twelve sense bases, and the doors which are a part of them.

Sappaccayabhāvāti sappaccayattā.

Sappaccayabhāvāti: due to having a condition.

Yathāvuttena ākārenāti “iti idaṃ sattavidhaṃ uggahakosallaṃ suggahitaṃ katvā”tiādinā (vibha. aṭṭha. 356), “imaṃ pana kammaṭṭhānaṃ bhāvetvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇitukāmenā”tiādinā (vibha. aṭṭha. 356) vā vuttappakārena vidhinā. “Avisesato pana sādhāraṇavasena evaṃ veditabbā”ti, “ito paṭṭhāyā”ti ca vadanti. Vaṇṇādimukhenāti vaṇṇapaṭikkūlasuññatāmukhena. Upaṭṭhānanti kammaṭṭhānassa upaṭṭhānaṃ, yo uggahoti vutto. Etthāti catukkapañcakajjhānapaṭhamajjhānavipassanāsu ekasmiṃ sandhīyati. Kena? Kammaṭṭhānamanasikāreneva, tasmā uggahova sandhi uggahasandhīti veditabbaṃ.

In the manner stated: that is, by the method stated in 'having well mastered this sevenfold skill in grasping,' etc. (VibhA. 356), or 'by one desiring to attain arahantship by developing this meditation subject,' etc. (VibhA. 356). They say, 'But generally, it should be understood as common to all,' and 'From this point onward.' Through the aspect of color, etc.: that is, through the aspect of color, repulsiveness, and emptiness. Presence (upaṭṭhāna): that is, the presence of the meditation subject, which is called grasping. Here: that is, it connects to one of the fourfold jhānas, the fivefold jhānas, the first jhāna, or insight. By what? By attention to the meditation subject alone. Therefore, grasping itself is the connection; it should be understood as the connection of grasping.

Uṭṭhānakaṃ uppajjanakaṃ. Sātirekāni cha ambaṇāni kumbhaṃ. Tatoti mukhadhovanakhādanabhojanakiccato. Nivattatīti arahattādhigamena accantanivattivasena nivattati.

Uṭṭhānakaṃ: that which arises. A pot is six ambaṇas with a surplus. From that: that is, from the activities of washing the face, eating snacks, and taking meals. 'It ceases': that is, it ceases by way of complete cessation with the attainment of arahantship.

Kammamevāti [M 0.0157] manasikārakammameva. Ārammaṇanti pubbabhāgabhāvanārammaṇaṃ.

'Action itself': that is, the action of attention itself. 'The object': that is, the object of preliminary-stage development.

Tathāti vanamakkaṭo viya.

Tathā: like a forest monkey.

Ekanti [V 0.0154] ekaṃ koṭṭhāsaṃ.

Ekaṃ: one portion.

Sattagahaṇarahiteti sattapaññattimpi anāmasitvā desitattā vuttaṃ. Sasantānatāya ahaṃkāravatthumhi appahīnamānassa pahīnākāraṃ sandhāyāha “viddhastāhaṃkāre”ti. Tatthāti parassa kāye.

'Free from the grasping of a being': this is said because it was taught without even touching upon the designation of a being. Because of the continuity of one's own continuum, referring to the appearance of conceit being abandoned in the object of 'I-making' even though it is not abandoned, it is said, 'with shattered I-making.' 'Therein': that is, in the body of another.

357. Ādimhi sevanā manasikārassa uppādanā ārambho.

357. At the beginning: cultivation, the production of attention, the start.

362. Gamitāti vigamitā.

362. Gamitā: gone away.

Kāyānupassanāniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the exposition of the contemplation of the body is concluded.

Vedanānupassanāniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of the Contemplation of Feelings

363. Sampajānassāti sammā pakārehi jānantassa, vatthārammaṇehi saddhiṃ sukhasāmisādippakārehi aviparītaṃ vedanaṃ jānantassāti attho. Pubbabhāgabhāvanā vohārānusāreneva pavattatīti āha “vohāramattenā”ti. Vedayāmīti “ahaṃ vedayāmī”ti attupanāyikā vuttāti, pariññātavedanopi vā uppannāya sukhavedanāya lokavohārena “sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī”ti jānāti, voharati ca, pageva itaro. Tenāha “vohāramattena vutta”nti.

363. 'Of one who is clearly comprehending': that is, of one who knows rightly in various ways, meaning one who knows feeling without distortion, together with its basis and object, in its various kinds such as pleasant, worldly, and so on. He says 'merely by convention' because the preliminary stage of development proceeds only in accordance with conventional usage. 'I feel' (vedayāmi): this is stated with reference to oneself, as in 'I feel.' Or, even one who has fully understood feelings knows and speaks, in worldly terms, when a pleasant feeling arises, 'I feel a pleasant feeling'—how much more so the ordinary person. Therefore, it is said, 'stated merely by convention.'

Ubhayanti vīriyasamādhiṃ. Saha yojetvāti samadhurakiccato anūnādhikaṃ katvā. Atthadhammādīsu sammohaviddhaṃsanavasena pavattā maggapaññā eva lokuttarapaṭisambhidā.

'Both': that is, energy and concentration. 'Having yoked them together': that is, by making them neither deficient nor excessive, performing the task of even balance. The path wisdom that proceeds by destroying delusion in regards to meaning, the Dhamma, etc., is indeed the supramundane analytical knowledge.

Vaṇṇamukhādīsu tīsupi mukhesu. Pariggahassāti arūpapariggahassa. “Vatthu nāma karajakāyo”ti vacanena nivattitaṃ dassento “na cakkhādīni cha vatthūnī”ti āha. Aññamaññupatthambhena [V 0.0155] ṭhitesu dvīsu naḷakalāpesu ekassa itarapaṭibaddhaṭṭhititā viya nāmakāyassa rūpakāyapaṭibaddhavuttitādassanañhetaṃ nissayapaccayavisesadassananti.

In all three aspects, such as the aspect of color. 'Of the comprehension': that is, of the comprehension of the formless. Showing what is excluded by the statement 'the base is the physical body,' he says, 'not the six bases like the eye, etc.' This is the showing of the mental body's dependent activity on the physical body, like the state of one of two bundles of reeds standing by mutual support being bound to the other; this is the showing of a specific condition of dependence.

Tesanti [M 0.0158] yesaṃ phassaviññāṇāni pākaṭāni, tesaṃ. Aññesanti tato aññesaṃ, yesaṃ phassaviññāṇāni na pākaṭāni. Sukhadukkhavedanānaṃ suvibhūtavuttitāya vuttaṃ “sabbesaṃ vineyyānaṃ vedanā pākaṭā”ti. Vilāpetvā vilāpetvāti suvisuddhaṃ navanītaṃ vilāpetvā sītibhūtaṃ atisītale udake pakkhipitvā patthinnaṃ ṭhitaṃ matthetvā paripiṇḍetvā puna vilāpetvāti satavāraṃ evaṃ katvā.

'Of those': that is, of those whose contact and consciousness are evident. 'Of others': that is, of others whose contact and consciousness are not evident. Because pleasant and painful feelings are very clearly manifested, it is said, 'for all who are to be trained, feelings are evident.' 'Having melted again and again' (vilāpetvā vilāpetvā): that is, having melted very pure butter, cooled it, put it into very cold water, churned the solidified layer, formed it into a ball, and melted it again—doing this a hundred times.

Tatthāpīti yattha arūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ eva…pe… dassitaṃ, tatthāpi. Yesu suttesu tadantogadhaṃ rūpakammaṭṭhānanti yojanā.

'Even there': that is, even where the formless meditation subject is shown... The connection is that in those suttas, the form meditation subject is included therein.

Vedanānupassanāniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the exposition of the contemplation of feelings is concluded.

Cittānupassanāniddesavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Exposition of the Contemplation of Mind

365. Kilesasampayuttānaṃ na visuddhatā hotīti sambandho. Itarehipīti attanā sampayuttakilesato itarehipi asampayuttehi. Visuṃ vacananti aññākusalato visuṃ katvā vacanaṃ. Visiṭṭhaggahaṇanti visiṭṭhatāgahaṇaṃ, āveṇikasamohatādassananti attho, yato tadubhayaṃ momūhacittanti vuccati.

365. The connection is that there is no purity for those associated with defilements. ‘Also by others’ (itarehipi) means also by other, unassociated defilements, apart from the defilements associated with oneself. ‘Separate statement’ (visuṃ vacanaṃ) means a statement made by distinguishing it from other unwholesome states. ‘Grasping of the distinguished’ (visiṭṭhaggahaṇaṃ) means the grasping of distinction, the meaning being the seeing of unique delusion, since both are called ‘deluded mind’.

Cittānupassanāniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Contemplation of Mind is concluded.

Dhammānupassanāniddeso

Exposition of the Contemplation of Phenomena

Ka. nīvaraṇapabbavaṇṇanā

A. Commentary on the Section on the Hindrances

367. Ekasmiṃ [V 0.0156] yuge baddhagoṇānaṃ viya ekato pavatti yuganaddhatā.

367. Like a pair of oxen yoked together, their movement proceeds as one—this is yokedness.

Gahaṇākārenāti asubhepi ārammaṇe “subha”nti gahaṇākārena. Nimittanti cāti subhanimittanti ca vuccatīti yojanā. Ekaṃsena sattā attano attano hitasukhameva āsīsantīti katvā vuttaṃ “ākaṅkhitassa hitasukhassā”ti. Anupāyo eva ca hitavisiṭṭhassa sukhassa ayonisomanasikāro, ākaṅkhitassa vā yathādhippetassa hitasukhassa anupāyabhūto. Avijjandhā hi tādisepi pavattantīti. Nipphādetabbeti [M 0.0159] ayonisomanasikārena nibbattetabbe kāmacchandeti attho.

‘By way of grasping’ (gahaṇākārena) means by way of grasping even an unattractive object as ‘attractive’. And the connection is that ‘sign’ (nimittaṃ) is also called ‘attractive sign’ (subhanimittaṃ). Because beings, without exception, wish only for their own welfare and happiness, it is said, ‘for the desired welfare and happiness’. And indeed, improper attention is the unskillful means to happiness distinguished by welfare, or it is the unskillful means to the desired welfare and happiness as intended. For those blinded by ignorance indeed proceed even in such ways. ‘To be produced’ (nipphādetabbaṃ) means sensual desire is to be generated by improper attention—this is the meaning.

Tadanukūlattāti tesaṃ asubhe “subha”nti, “asubha”nti ca pavattānaṃ ayonisomanasikārayonisomanasikārānaṃ anukūlattā. Rūpādīsu aniccādiabhinivesassa, aniccasaññādīnañca yathāvuttamanasikārūpanissayatā tadanukūlatā.

‘Due to being favorable to that’ (tadanukūlattā) means due to being favorable to unwise attention and wise attention, which occur as ‘attractive’ and ‘unattractive’ in the unattractive. Regarding forms and so on, the state of having the aforesaid attention as a decisive support for the adherence to impermanence, etc., and for the perceptions of impermanence, etc., is its favorable nature.

Āhāre paṭikkūlasaññaṃ so uppādetīti sambandho. Tabbipariṇāmassāti bhojanapariṇāmassa nissandādikassa. Tadādhārassāti udarassa, kāyasseva vā. Soti bhojanemattaññū. Suttantapariyāyena kāmarāgo “kāmacchandanīvaraṇa”nti vuccatīti āha “abhidhammapariyāyenā”ti. Abhidhamme hi “nīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā”ti (paṭṭhā. 3.8.8) etassa vibhaṅge “arūpe kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ paṭicca thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccanīvaraṇaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ uppajjatī”tiādivacanato bhavarāgopi kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ vuttanti viññāyati. Tenāha “sabbopi lobho kāmacchandanīvaraṇa”nti.

The connection is that he develops the perception of repulsiveness toward food. ‘Of its transformation’ (tabbipariṇāmassa) means of the transformation of food, such as its results and so on. ‘Of its basis’ (tadādhārassa) means of the stomach, or even of the body itself. ‘He’ (so) means one who knows moderation in food. He says ‘in the Abhidhamma method’ because in the Sutta method, sensual desire is called ‘the hindrance of sensual desire’. For in the Abhidhamma, in the analysis of the statement ‘A hindering state arises dependent on a hindering state, not by way of the pre-nascence condition’ (Paṭṭhāna 3.8.8), from statements such as ‘In the formless realm, dependent on the hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrances of sloth and torpor, restlessness, and ignorance arise,’ it is understood that craving for existence is also called the hindrance of sensual desire. Therefore he says: ‘All greed is the hindrance of sensual desire’.

Sīmābhede kateti attādimariyādāya bhinnāya, attādīsu sabbattha ekarūpāya mettābhāvanāyāti attho. Vihārādiuddesarahitanti vihārādipadesaparicchedarahitaṃ. Uggahitāya mettāya. Aṭṭhavīsatividhāti itthiādivasena sattavidhā paccekaṃ averādīhi yojanāvasena aṭṭhavīsatividhā. Sattādiitthiādiaverādiyogenāti ettha sattādiaverādiyogena vīsati, itthiādiaverādiyogena [V 0.0157] aṭṭhavīsatīti aṭṭhacattārīsaṃ ekissā disāya. Tathā sesadisāsupīti sabbā saṅgahetvā āha “asītādhikacatusatappabhedā”ti.

‘Sīmābhede kateti’ (when the boundary is broken) means that when the limit of self and so forth is broken, the cultivation of loving-kindness is uniform everywhere in regard to self and so forth—this is the meaning. ‘Vihārādiuddesarahitaṃ’ (devoid of designation of dwellings, etc.) means without the limitation of places such as dwellings. By the loving-kindness that has been grasped. ‘Aṭṭhavīsatividhā’ (twenty-eightfold) means sevenfold by way of women, etc., and twenty-eightfold by way of combining each one with non-aversion, etc. ‘Sattādiitthiādiaverādiyogena’ (by the connection of beings, etc., and women, etc., with non-aversion, etc.)—here, by the connection of beings, etc., with non-aversion, etc., there are twenty; by the connection of women, etc., with non-aversion, etc., there are twenty-eight. Thus, there are forty-eight for one direction. Similarly in the remaining directions—thus, having summed them all up, it is said: ‘four hundred and eighty distinctions’.

Katākatānusocanañca na hotīti yojanā. “Bahukaṃ sutaṃ hoti suttaṃ geyya”ntiādivacanato (a. ni. 4.6) bahussutatā navaṅgassa sāsanassa vasena veditabbā, na vinayamattassevāti vuḍḍhataṃ pana anapekkhitvā icceva vuttaṃ, na bahussutatañcāti.

The connection is that there is no remorse over what was done and what was not done. From the statement ‘He has heard much: discourses, mixed prose and verse,’ etc. (AN 4.6), being very learned should be understood in terms of the ninefold dispensation, not merely of the Vinaya alone. However, it is said thus without regard to seniority, and not just 'and being very learned'.

Tiṭṭhati anuppannā vicikicchā ettha etesu “ahosiṃ nu kho ahamatītamaddhāna”ntiādikāya (ma. ni. 1.18; sa. ni. 2.20) pavattiyā anekabhedesu purimuppannesu vicikicchādhammesūti te ṭhānīyā vuttā.

Unarisen doubt remains here, in these previously arisen states of doubt of many kinds that occur in the manner of ‘Did I exist in the past?’, etc. (MN 1.18; SN 2.20); therefore, they are said to be its basis.

Aṭṭhavatthukāpīti [M 0.0160] na kevalaṃ soḷasavatthukā, nāpi ratanattayavatthukā ca, atha kho aṭṭhavatthukāpi. Ratanattaye saṃsayāpannassa sikkhādīsu kaṅkhāsambhavato, tattha nibbematikassa tadabhāvato ca sesavicikicchānaṃ ratanattayavicikicchāmūlikatā daṭṭhabbā. Anupavisanaṃ “evameta”nti saddahanavasena ārammaṇassa pakkhandanaṃ.

‘Aṭṭhavatthukāpi’ (also on eight grounds) means not only on sixteen grounds, nor just on the Triple Gem as its ground, but also on eight grounds. Since for one who is beset by doubt concerning the Triple Gem, uncertainty arises regarding the training, etc., and since for one free from doubt about that there is an absence of such uncertainty, the remaining kinds of doubt should be seen as rooted in doubt concerning the Triple Gem. ‘Anupavisanaṃ’ (entering into) is plunging into the object by way of conviction, thinking ‘Thus it is’.

Nīvaraṇapabbavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Section on the Hindrances is concluded.

Kha. bojjhaṅgapabbavaṇṇanā

B. Commentary on the Section on the Factors of Enlightenment

Tenāti atthasannissitaggahaṇena.

‘Tena’ (by that) means by grasping what is connected to the meaning.

Paccayavasena dubbalabhāvo mandatā.

Feebleness is a state of weakness due to conditions.

Pabbatapadesavanagahanantaritopi gāmo na dūre, pabbataṃ parikkhipitvā gantabbatāya āvāso araññalakkhaṇūpeto, tasmā maṃsasoteneva assosīti vadanti.

Although a village, screened by a mountain region and a forest thicket, is not far, because one has to go around a mountain to get there, the dwelling possesses the characteristics of a wilderness. Therefore, they say, he heard with his physical ear.

Sampattihetutāya [V 0.0158] pasādo sinehapariyāyena vutto.

Because it is a cause of success, faith is spoken of by the term 'affection'.

Indriyānaṃ tikkhabhāvāpādanaṃ tejanaṃ. Tosanaṃ pamodanaṃ.

‘Tejanaṃ’ (sharpening) is causing the faculties to become keen. ‘Tosanaṃ’ (satisfying) is gladdening.

Bojjhaṅgapabbavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Section on the Factors of Enlightenment is concluded.

Samathavipassanāvasena paṭhamassa satipaṭṭhānassa, suddhavipassanāvasena itaresaṃ. Āgamanavasena vuttaṃ aññathā maggasammāsatiyā kathaṃ kāyārammaṇatā siyāti adhippāyo. Kāyānupassiādīnaṃ catubbidhānaṃ puggalānaṃ vuttānaṃ. Tenāha “na hi sakkā ekassa…pe… vattu”nti. Anekasatisambhavāvabodhapasaṅgāti ekacittuppādena anekissā satiyā sambhavassa, sati ca tasmiṃ anekāvabodhassa ca āpajjanato. Sakiccaparicchinneti attano kiccavisesavisiṭṭhe. Dhammabhedenāti ārammaṇabhedavisiṭṭhena dhammavisesena. Na dhammassa dhammo kiccanti ekassa dhammassa aññadhammo kiccaṃ nāma na hoti tadabhāvato. Dhammabhedena dhammassa vibhāgena. Tassa bhedoti tassa kiccassa bhedo natthi. Tasmāti yasmā nayidha dhammassa vibhāgena kiccabhedo icchito, kiccabhedena [M 0.0161] pana dhammavibhāgo icchito, tasmā. Tena vuttaṃ “ekāvā”tiādi.

For the first establishment of mindfulness, it is by way of serenity and insight; for the others, by way of pure insight. It is said by way of the scriptural tradition; otherwise, the intention is, how could right mindfulness of the path have the body as its object? It is said of the four types of persons, such as those who contemplate the body. Therefore he says: ‘For it is not possible for one… to say’. ‘Anekasatisambhavāvabodhapasaṅgā’ (implication of the arising and apprehension of multiple mindfulnesses) means because, with a single mind-moment, the arising of multiple mindfulnesses and, that being the case, the occurrence of multiple apprehensions would follow. ‘Sakiccaparicchinne’ (defined by its own function) means specified by its own particular function. ‘Dhammabhedena’ (by the distinction of phenomena) means by a particular phenomenon distinguished by a difference in object. ‘Na dhammassa dhammo kiccaṃ’ (a phenomenon is not the function of a phenomenon) means for one phenomenon, another phenomenon is not its function, because of the absence of that. ‘Dhammabhedena’ means by the division of a phenomenon. ‘Tassa bhedo’ (its distinction) means there is no distinction of its function. ‘Tasmā’ (therefore) means: because here a distinction of function by way of a division of phenomena is not intended, but a division of phenomena by way of a distinction of function is intended, therefore. Hence, it is said, ‘In one way,’ etc.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Suttanta Division is concluded.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Abhidhamma Division

374. “Kāye kāyānupassī”ti idaṃ puggalādhiṭṭhānena satipaṭṭhānavisesanaṃ, tañca āgamanasiddhaṃ, aññathā tassa asambhavatoti āha “āgamanavasena…pe… desetvā”ti. Puggalaṃ anāmasitvāti “kāye kāyānupassī”ti evaṃ puggalaṃ aggahetvā. Tathā anāmasanato eva āgamanavisesanaṃ akatvā. Nayadvayeti anupassanānayo, suddhikanayoti etasmiṃ nayadvaye.

374. ‘Contemplating the body in the body’—this is a specification of the establishment of mindfulness based on a person, and that is established by the scriptural tradition; otherwise, it would be impossible. Therefore, he says, ‘by way of the scriptural tradition… having taught.’ ‘Without referring to a person’ means without grasping a person thus as ‘contemplating the body in the body.’ Similarly, precisely because of not referring in that way, the specification by way of the scriptural tradition is not made. ‘In the two methods’ means in these two methods: the method of contemplation and the method of purification.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Abhidhamma Division is concluded.

Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Establishments of Mindfulness is concluded.

8. Sammappadhānavibhaṅgo

8. The Exposition of Right Efforts

1. Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Suttanta Division

390. Kāraṇasaddo [M 0.0162][V 0.0159] yuttivācako “sabbametaṃ akāraṇaṃ vadatī”tiādīsu viya, tasmā kāraṇappadhānāti yuttippadhānā, anuppannapāpakānuppādanādikiriyāya anurūpappadhānāti evaṃ vā ettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Anuppannapāpakādīnaṃ anuppādādi anuppannapāpakānuppādādi.

390. The word `kāraṇa` is a term denoting reason, as in phrases like ‘he speaks all this without reason.’ Therefore, `kāraṇappadhāna` means predominated by reason. Or alternatively, the meaning here should be understood as predominated by suitability for the action of not producing unarisen evil states, and so forth. The non-arising, etc., of unarisen evil, etc., is the compound `anuppannapāpakānuppādādi`.

391. “Na añño dhammoti yathā taṇhāyanamicchābhinivesavāyamanasabhāvānaṃ taṇhādīnaṃ chandapariyāyo aññadhammo nāma hoti kattukamyatāsaṅkhātassa chandaniyassa tesu abhāvā, dhammacchando pana taṃsabhāvattā aññadhammo na hoti. Tenāha “dhammacchandoti sabhāvacchando”ti.

391. ‘Not another state’ (na añño dhammo)—just as the term for desire (`chanda`) that is applied to craving and so forth, which are by nature craving, wrong adherence, and exertion, is indeed called ‘another state’ because the desiderative element characterized as the wish to do is absent in them. But desire for the Dhamma, because it has that nature, is not ‘another state.’ Therefore, it is said, ‘desire for the Dhamma is desire in its own nature.’

406. Aṭṭhakathāyanti porāṇaṭṭhakathāyaṃ. Vaṭṭānatthasaṃvattanatoti saṃsāradukkhasambhavato.

406. ‘In the commentary’ means in the ancient commentary. ‘Because it is conducive to harm in the round of existence’ means because of the arising of the suffering of saṃsāra.

Na sakkontīti āha “santāya samāpattiyā parihīnā brahmacariyavāse santhambhituṃ na sakkontī”ti.

Regarding ‘They are unable,’ it is said: ‘Those who have fallen away from the peaceful attainment are unable to establish themselves in the holy life.’

Tattha duvidhāyāti yojetabbaṃ. Uppannāyevāti uppannapubbā eva uppajjanti samudācārādivasena.

There, ‘twofold’ should be connected. ‘Arisen indeed’ means: having arisen before, they arise again by way of active manifestation and so forth.

Sabbāsu avatthāsūti pakatattādiavatthāsu. Pakatattāvatthena hi sabbena sabbaṃ tāni na caritabbāni. Itarāvatthena ca tadavatthāya tāni tāniyeva caritabbāni. Vattabbantiādīnīti ādi-saddena [V 0.0160] “na ekacchanne anāvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabbaṃ, na ekāsane nisīditabbaṃ, na nīce āsane nisinne ucce āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ nisinne āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na ekacaṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na nīce caṅkame caṅkamante ucce caṅkame caṅkamitabbaṃ, na chamāyaṃ caṅkamante caṅkame caṅkamitabba”nti imāni saṅgaṇhāti. Tesanti pārivāsikavuḍḍhatarādīnaṃ vasena. Sampiṇḍetvāti saṅkaḍḍhitvā. Ekekaṃ katvāti navāpi ekamekaṃ [M 0.0163] katvā. “Abhivādanapaccuṭṭhānañjalikammasāmīcikammaṃ na sāditabbaṃ, āsanābhihāraṃ, seyyābhihāraṃ, pādodakaṃ, pādapīṭhaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, pattacīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ na sāditabba”nti idaṃ sabbampi asādiyanasāmaññena ekaṃ. Dasāti “na sīlavipattiyā, na ācāravipattiyā, na diṭṭhivipattiyā, na ājīvavipattiyā, na bhikkhū bhikkhūhi bhedetabbā, na gihiddhajo dhāretabbo, na titthiyaddhajo dhāretabbo, na titthiyā sevitabbā, bhikkhū sevitabbā, bhikkhusikkhāya sikkhitabba”nti (cūḷava. 60) evamāgatā dasa.

‘In all situations’ means in the situations of being a normal monk, etc. For in the case of a normal monk, those things should not be practiced at all. But in the case of another, in that situation, those very things should be practiced. ‘Should be done,’ and so forth—by the word ‘and so forth,’ it includes these: ‘One should not stay under a single roof in a place without a dwelling; one should not stay under a single roof, whether in a dwelling or not; one should not sit on a single seat; one should not sit on a high seat when another is sitting on a low seat; one should not sit on a seat when another is sitting on the ground; one should not walk on a single walking path; one should not walk on a high walking path when another is walking on a low one; one should not walk on a walking path when another is walking on the ground.’ ‘Of them’ means with respect to those who are senior as probationers, etc. ‘Having gathered together’ means having drawn together. ‘Making one each’ means making even the nine into one each. ‘One should not neglect bowing, rising, joining palms in greeting, proper conduct; offering a seat, offering a bed, foot water, a footstool, a foot scraper, or receiving a bowl and robe’—all this is one under the general rule of not neglecting. ‘Ten’ refers to the ten that are given thus: ‘Not on account of failure in virtue, not on account of failure in conduct, not on account of failure in view, not on account of failure in livelihood; monks should not be divided from monks; the banner of householders should not be carried; the banner of sectarians should not be carried; sectarians should not be associated with; monks should be associated with; one should train in the training for monks’ (cf. Cv.I.13.6).

“Kammañcā”ti paccattavasena vuttaṃ kammaṃ “avipakkavipākassā”ti ettha “kammassā”ti sāmivacanavasena pariṇāmetvā yojetabbaṃ. Bhūtāpagatuppannanti vuttanti sambandho. Idhāti imissā sammohavinodaniyā. “Evaṃ kate okāse vipāko…pe… uppannoti vuccatī”ti vadanto vipākameva vadati. Tatthāti aṭṭhasāliniyaṃ. Maggena samucchinnā thāmagatā kāmarāgādayo “anusayā”ti vuccantīti āha “anusayita…pe… maggena pahātabbā”ti.

“‘And action’—the action spoken of in the singular—should be construed here, in the phrase ‘of an unripened result,’ by transforming it into ‘of action’ in the genitive case. ‘Past, departed, and arisen’ is said; this is the connection. ‘Here’ means in this Sammohavinodanī. When saying, ‘Thus, when an opportunity is made, the result… is said to arise,’ he speaks only of the result. ‘There’ means in the Aṭṭhasālinī. He states that sensual desire and so forth, which are firmly established and cut off by the path, are called ‘latent tendencies,’ hence the quote: ‘underlying… to be abandoned by the path.’”

Āhatakhīrarukkho viya ārammaṇaṃ, kathaṃ? Nimittaggāhavasena. Tamevatthaṃ vivarati “adhigata”ntiādinā. Tattha nimittaggāhavasena ārammaṇassa adhiggahitattā taṃ ārammaṇaṃ anussaritānussaritakkhaṇe kilesuppattihetubhāvena uppattiṭṭhānato adhigatameva nāma hotīti āha “adhigataṃ nimittaggāhavasenā”ti, taṃ ārammaṇaṃ pātubhūtakilesanti adhippāyo. Kilesuppattinimittatāya uppattirahaṃ kilesaṃ “ārammaṇaṃ antogadhakilesa”nti vuttaṃ. Tañca kho gāhake labbhamānaṃ gahetabbe upacaritvā, yathā nissite labbhamānaṃ nissaye upacaritvā “mañcā ukkuṭṭhiṃ karontī”ti. Idāni upacāraṃ muñcitvā nippariyāyeneva atthaṃ dassento “nimittaggāha…pe… sadisā”ti āha. Vitthāretabbanti “yathā kiṃ? Sace khīrarukkha”ntiādinā vitthāretabbaṃ.

“The object is like a tapped sap-tree. How so? By way of grasping the sign. He explains this very meaning with the phrase beginning ‘acquired.’ Herein, because the object is grasped by way of grasping the sign, that object, at the moment of repeatedly recollecting it, is indeed acquired from its place of origin by being a cause for the arising of defilements; thus he says, ‘acquired by way of grasping the sign.’ The intention is that this object is a manifest defilement. Because it is a sign for the arising of defilements, the defilement fit to arise is called ‘the object with the defilement included within.’ And this is by figuratively applying what is found in the grasper to what is grasped, just as what is found in the supported is figuratively applied to the support, as in ‘the beds are shouting.’ Now, abandoning the figurative usage and showing the meaning directly, he says, ‘grasping the sign… similar.’ ‘It should be elaborated’ means it should be elaborated with the phrase beginning, ‘How so? If a sap-exuding tree…’”

Tidhāti [V 0.0161] atītādivasena tidhā. Ābhato upamāvasena. Appahīnatādassanatthampīti pi-saddena “tidhā navattabbatādassanatthampī”ti vuttameva sampiṇḍeti. Evaṃ maggena pahīnakilesā daṭṭhabbā magge anuppanne uppattirahānampi uppanne sabbena sabbaṃ abhāvato.

“‘Threefold’ means threefold by way of past, and so forth. ‘Brought’ means by way of simile. ‘Also, to show the state of not being abandoned’—with the word ‘also,’ it summarizes what was said: ‘also for the purpose of showing that it should not be said to be threefold.’ Thus, the defilements abandoned by the path should be understood: even when the path has not arisen, they are unfit to arise, and when it has arisen, they are completely non-existent.”

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Suttanta Division is concluded.

3. Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Chapter of Questions

427. Vīriyajeṭṭhikāya [M 0.0164] pana maggabhāvanāya na vattabbāni sammappadhānāni “maggādhipatīnī”ti vā “namaggādhipatīnī”ti vāti vāti ettha paṭhamassa vīriyantarābhāvo, itarassa itarādhipatino, namaggabhūtavīriyādhipatino ca abhāvo navattabbatāya kāraṇanti imamatthamāha “maggādhipatīnī”tiādinā. Tadāti vīriyajeṭṭhikamaggabhāvanākāle.

427. “However, for the path-development with energy as chief, the right strivings should not be called either ‘having the path as their dominant principle’ or ‘not having the path as their dominant principle.’ Here, for the first case, there is an absence of any other energy. For the second case, the absence of another dominant principle and the absence of a dominant principle that is energy which has not become the path is the reason for its not being said. He states this meaning with the phrase beginning ‘having the path as their dominant principle.’ ‘Then’ means at the time of developing the path with energy as chief.”

Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Chapter of Questions is finished.

Sammappadhānavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of the Right Strivings is finished.

9. Iddhipādavibhaṅgo

9. The Analysis of the Bases of Spiritual Power

1. Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Sutta-Style Exposition

431. Paṭhamo [M 0.0165][V 0.0162] kattuattho “ijjhatīti iddhī”ti. Dutiyo karaṇattho “ijjhanti etāyā”ti. Pajjitabbā iddhi vuttā “iddhiṃ pajjanti pāpuṇantī”ti kattusādhanassa iddhisaddassa karaṇasādhanena pādasaddena samānādhikaraṇatāya asambhavato, ijjhanakassa ca atthassa karaṇabhūtena pādena pajjitabbattā “iddhi eva pādo”ti saddayojanā na sambhavatīti imamatthamāha “na ca…pe… vattu”nti. Iddhikiriyākaraṇenāti ijjhanakiriyāya karaṇabhūtena atthena sādhetabbā ca iddhi pajjitabbāti yojanā. Dvinnaṃ karaṇānanti ijjhanapajjanakiriyākaraṇānaṃ iddhipādatthānaṃ. Na asamānādhikaraṇatā sambhavati paṭisedhadvayaṃ pakatiyaṃ ṭhapetīti. Tasmāti yasmā paṭhamenatthena samānādhikaraṇasamāso, dutiyena sāmivacanasamāso iddhipādasaddānaṃ na yujjati, tasmā. Yathāvuttā vā paṭhamenatthena samānādhikaraṇasamāsavaseneva yojanā yujjati pādassa pajjamānakoṭṭhāsabhāvato. Dutiyenatthena itarasamāseneva yojanā yujjati pādassa ijjhanakaraṇūpāyabhāvato.

431. “The first is the agent-meaning: ‘It prospers, thus it is spiritual power (iddhi).’ The second is the instrumental-meaning: ‘By this, one prospers.’ Spiritual power is said to be attainable: ‘They attain, they reach spiritual power.’ However, because it is impossible for the word ‘iddhi,’ derived in the agent sense, to be in apposition with the word ‘pāda,’ derived in the instrumental sense, and because the state of prospering is to be attained by means of the ‘base’ (pāda) which serves as the instrument, the verbal construction ‘spiritual power itself is the base’ is not possible. He states this meaning with the phrase ‘Nor… should it be said.’ The phrase ‘by the instrument for the action of spiritual power’ is construed thus: spiritual power is to be accomplished and attained by the means that is the instrument for the action of prospering. ‘Regarding the two instruments’ refers to the meanings of ‘iddhipāda’ as the instruments for the actions of prospering and attaining. Non-apposition is not possible, for a double negative affirms the original proposition. ‘Therefore’ means: since with the first meaning a coordinative compound (samānādhikaraṇasamāsa) is not suitable for the word ‘iddhipāda,’ and with the second a genitive compound (sāmivacanasamāsa) is not suitable, therefore… Alternatively, as stated, with the first meaning the construction is suitable precisely by way of a coordinative compound, as the ‘base’ (pāda) is the part being attained. With the second meaning, the construction is suitable precisely by way of another compound, as the ‘base’ is the means or instrument for prospering.”

Kecīti dhammasirittheraṃ sandhāya vadati. Duvidhatthāyāti nibbattiatthāya, vuddhiatthāya ca. Visunti “iddhi eva pādo iddhipādo”ti imasmā visuṃ. Samāsayojanāvasenāti “iddhiyā pādo iddhipādo”ti evaṃ samāsayojanāvasena. Yathāyuttoti kattukaraṇatthesu yo yo yutto. Paṭilābhapubbabhāgānanti visesādhigamataṃpubbabhāgānaṃ yathākkamaṃ kattiddhikaraṇiddhibhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttoti yojanā. Uttaracūḷabhājanīye “chandoyeva chandiddhipādo, cittameva, vīriyameva, vīmaṃsāva [V 0.0163] vīmaṃsiddhipādo”ti vuttattā āha “uttaracūḷabhājanīye vā vuttehi chandādīhi iddhipādehī”tiādi.

“‘Some’—he says this with reference to the Elder Dhammasiri. ‘For a twofold purpose’ means for the purpose of generation and for the purpose of growth. ‘Separately’ means separately from this: ‘spiritual power itself is the base, an iddhipāda.’ ‘By way of the compound-construction’ means by way of a compound-construction thus: ‘the base of spiritual power, an iddhipāda.’ ‘As is suitable’ means whichever is suitable among the agent- and instrumental-meanings. ‘Of the preliminary stages of attainment’: the construction is that this is said with reference to the preliminary stages for the attainment of distinction being, respectively, spiritual power in the agent sense and spiritual power in the instrumental sense. Since in the Uttaracūḷabhājanīya it is said, ‘Will itself is the base of spiritual power of will… mind itself… energy itself… investigation itself is the base of spiritual power of investigation,’ he therefore says, ‘or in the Uttaracūḷabhājanīya, by the bases of spiritual power, will, etc., that are mentioned…’”

Chandacittavīmaṃsiddhipādesu tāva yuttaṃ padhānasaṅkhāraggahaṇaṃ apubbattā, vīriyiddhipāde pana kathanti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “vīriyiddhipādaniddese”tiādi. Yadi dveyeva samannāgamaṅgāni, chandādayo kimatthiyāti āha “samādhivisesanānī”ti. Na idha…pe… vuttā hoti atabbisesanattā. Yadipi [M 0.0166] samādhivisesanasamannāgamaṅgadassanatthaṃ dvikkhattuṃ vīriyaṃ āgatanti vuttaṃ, taṃ pana “vīriyasamādhisamannāgata”nti ettāvatāpi siddhaṃ hoti. Evaṃ siddhe sati puna vacanaṃ vīriyantarasabbhāvaṃ nu kho dīpetīti kadāci āsaṅkeyyāti tadāsaṅkānivattanatthaṃ “vīriyañcā”tiādimāha. Chandādīhi visiṭṭhoti chandādīnaṃ adhipatipaccayatāvisesena visiṭṭho. Teneva hi chandādimukheneva iddhipādā desitā. Tathā ca vuttaṃ “chandaṃ ce bhikkhu adhipatiṃ karitvā labhati samādhi”ntiādi. Taṃtaṃavassayanavasenāti tassa tassa chandassa samādhino avassayatāvasena, paccayavisesatāyāti attho. Upāyatthena…pe… vuttā hoti adhigamūpāyatāpi nissayabhāvoyevāti. “Tenevā”tiādinā yathāvuttaṃ chandādīnaṃ iddhipādataṃ pāḷiyāyeva vibhāveti. Tattha tenevāti chandādīnaṃyeva upāyatthabhāveneva iddhipādabhāvassa adhippetattā. Upāyiddhipādadassanatthamevāti chandādike dhure jeṭṭhake pubbaṅgame katvā nibbattitasamādhi chandādīnaṃ iddhiyā adhigamūpāyatādassanaṃ upāyiddhipādadassanaṃ, tadatthameva “tathābhūtassa vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho”ti tattha tattha pāḷiyaṃ nissayiddhipādadassanaṃ kataṃ chandādivisiṭṭhānaṃyeva vedanākkhandhādīnaṃ adhippetattā. Evañcetaṃ sampaṭicchitabbaṃ. Aññathā kevalaṃ iddhisampayuttānaṃyeva khandhānaṃ vasena iddhipādabhāve gayhamāne catubbidhatā na hoti visesakāraṇābhāvatoti adhippāyo.

“Now, in the bases of spiritual power of will, mind, and investigation, the inclusion of ‘striving-formations’ is appropriate because it is unprecedented. But how is it in the base of spiritual power of energy? Referring to this objection, he states the phrase beginning ‘and energy…’ If there are only two constituent factors, what is the purpose of will, etc.? He says: ‘They are qualifiers of concentration.’ Here… is not said, because it is not a qualifier of that. Although it is said that ‘energy’ is mentioned twice to show it as a qualifier of concentration and a constituent factor, this is established simply by the phrase ‘endowed with concentration and energy.’ This being established, one might sometimes suspect that the repetition indicates the existence of another kind of energy. To dispel that suspicion, he states the phrase beginning ‘and energy…’ ‘Distinguished by will, etc.’ means distinguished by the specific dominant conditionality of will, etc. For it is precisely through the gateway of will, etc., that the bases of spiritual power are taught. And so it is said: ‘If, a bhikkhu, having made will the dominant factor, obtains concentration,’ and so on. ‘By way of dependence on this or that’ means by way of the dependence of concentration on this or that will; the meaning is ‘by way of a specific condition.’ ‘In the sense of a means…’ means that being a means of attainment is itself a state of dependence. By the phrase beginning ‘Therefore,’ he clarifies, just from the Pāli itself, that will, etc., are bases of spiritual power as stated. Therein, ‘therefore’ is because the status of being a base of spiritual power is intended precisely because will, etc., have the meaning of being a means. For the purpose of showing the base of spiritual power as a means: the concentration produced by making will and the others the chief, leader, and forerunner is the showing of the means for attaining the spiritual power of will, etc.—this is the showing of the base of spiritual power as a means. For that very purpose, in the Pāli here and there, the showing of the base of spiritual power as dependence is made in such passages as ‘for one who has become thus, the feeling aggregate… the consciousness aggregate,’ because it is the aggregates of feeling, etc., as distinguished by will, etc., that are intended. And this should be accepted thus. Otherwise, if the status of being a base of spiritual power were to be grasped solely by way of the aggregates that are merely associated with spiritual power, there would be no fourfold division, due to the absence of a distinguishing reason. This is the intention.”

433. Tosanaṃ satthu ārādhanaṃ, sikkhāya vā. Thāmabhāvatoti thirabhāvato. Kulāpadese jātimā purissaro hotīti “pubbaṅgamattā cittassa visiṭṭhajātisadisatā”ti vuttaṃ. Vicāraṇāpaññāhetukattā mantassa vīmaṃsāsadisatā suviññeyyāvāti na uddhaṭā.

433. 'Pleasing' is gratifying the Teacher, or it is for the training. 'Because of strength' means because of steadfastness. 'In the region of a clan, one of high birth is a leader'; thus it is said: 'The leadership of the mind is similar to a distinguished birth.' Because its cause is the wisdom of investigation, the similarity of a mantra to investigation is easily understood, so it is not cited.

Chandādiketi chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārā, vīriyacittavīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārāti ime tayo tayo dhamme. Abhedato bhedaṃ akatvā abhinditvā iddhibhāvasāmaññena, iddhipādabhāvasāmaññena ca [V 0.0164] saṅgaṇhitvā. Tenāha “sampiṇḍetvā”ti. Bhedanaṃ vā sambhedanaṃ missīkaraṇanti āha “amissetvā”ti. Tathā hi “sesā pana sampayuttakā cattāro khandhā iddhipādāyevā”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 433) iddhiiddhipāde amissetvāpi kathitaṃ. Visesenāti bhedena catūsu iddhipādesu asammissabhāvena āveṇikattā. Āveṇikā [M 0.0167] hi chandādayo tassa tassa iddhipādassa. Avisesenāti abhedena, caturiddhipādasādhāraṇabhāvenāti attho.

'By will, etc.' means these groups of three dhammas: will, concentration, and striving-formations; and energy, mind, and investigation, together with concentration and striving-formations. Without making a distinction, without separating, undifferentiatedly, having grouped them together by the commonality of the state of spiritual power and by the commonality of the state of being a base for spiritual power. Hence he says, 'having lumped them together.' Or, 'breaking apart,' 'blending' is mixing; hence he says, 'without mixing.' For so it is said: 'But the remaining four associated aggregates are themselves bases for spiritual power,' stated even without mixing spiritual power and the bases for spiritual power. 'Specifically' means distinctly, because in the four bases for spiritual power they are unmixed, being unique. For will and the rest are unique to their respective base for spiritual power. 'Non-specifically' means without distinction, that is, by way of being common to the four bases for spiritual power; this is the meaning.

Chandiddhipādasamādhiddhipādādayoti ādi-saddena padhānasaṅkhāraṃ, vīriyacittavīmaṃsā ca saṅgaṇhāti. Pādoti tehi sampayuttaṃ catukkhandhamāha. “Chandiddhipāde pavisantī”tiādinā visiṭṭhesveva pavesaṃ avatvā. Catūsūti chando, samādhi, padhānasaṅkhārā, taṃsampayuttā khandhāti evaṃ catūsu. Chandahetuko, chandādhiko vā samādhi adhippetoti āha “chandavato ko samādhi na ijjhissatī”ti. Itīti evaṃ anena pakārena, yaṃ samādhibhāvanāmukhaṃ. Samādhibhāvanānuyogena bhāvitā khandhā samādhibhāvitā.

'The base for spiritual power of will, the base for spiritual power of concentration, etc.'—by the word 'etc.' he includes striving-formations, and energy, mind, and investigation. 'Base'—he refers to the four aggregates associated with them. By the phrase 'They enter upon the base for spiritual power of will,' etc., without stating that the entry is only into the distinguished factors. 'In the four' means in these four: will, concentration, striving-formations, and the aggregates associated with them. Concentration that has will as its cause or has will as its dominant factor is intended; thus he says: 'For one who has will, what concentration will not prosper?' 'Thus' means in this way, by this method, which is the gateway to the development of concentration. The aggregates developed by devotion to the development of concentration are 'concentration-developed.'

“Ye hī”tiādinā “abhinavaṃ natthī”ti saṅkhepato vuttaṃ vivarati. Tiṇṇanti chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārānaṃ. Idanti “ime hi tayo”tiādivacanaṃ. Purimassāti “chando samādhī”tiādivacanassa. Kāraṇabhāvenāti sādhanabhāvena. Tenāti “ime hi tayo dhammā”tiādivacanena. Yasmā chandādayo tayo dhammā aññamaññaṃ, sampayuttakānañca nissayabhāvena pavattanti, tasmā tesampi iddhipādabhāvo vutto. So pana nissayabhāvo sampayogāvinābhāvīti āha “tadantogadhattā”ti, sampayuttakantogadhattāti attho. Chandādīnaṃ viya sampayuttakkhandhānaṃ sabhāvato iddhibhāvo natthīti āha “iddhibhāvapariyāyo atthī”ti. Tena vuttaṃ “sesā sampayuttakā…pe… na attano sabhāvenā”ti. Ekadesassāti chandādīnaṃ. Catunnampi khandhānaṃ, chandādīnaṃ vā catunnaṃ. Punapīti “sampayuttakā panā”tiādiṃ sandhāyāha. Iminā catukkhandhatadekadesānaṃ iddhibhāvadīpanena.

By the phrase beginning 'For those who,' he explains what was stated concisely as 'there is nothing new.' 'Of the three' means of will, concentration, and striving-formations. 'This' means the statement beginning 'for these three...' 'Of the former' means of the statement beginning 'will, concentration...' 'By way of being a cause' means by way of being a means of accomplishment. 'By that' means by the statement beginning 'for these three dhammas...' Because the three dhammas, will, etc., proceed in mutual dependence and in dependence on the associated factors, their status as bases for spiritual power is also stated. But that state of dependence is inseparable from association; thus he says, 'because of being included within that,' which means being included within the associated factors. He says, 'there is an aspect of the state of spiritual power' to show that, like will, etc., the associated aggregates do not have the status of spiritual power from their own nature. Hence it is said: 'The remaining associated factors... not by their own nature.' 'Of a part' means of will, etc.—either of the four aggregates, or of the four, i.e., will, etc. 'Again'—he says this referring to the phrase beginning 'But the associated factors...' By this explanation of the four aggregates and a part of them as having the status of spiritual power.

Pubbe vuttato vacanakkamena aññanti āha “apubbanti katvā”ti. Kenaṭṭhena iddhi paṭilābho, kenaṭṭhena pādo pubbabhāgoti yathākkamaṃ yojanā. Yadi patiṭṭhānaṭṭhena pādo, nissayiddhipādoyeva vutto siyā, na upāyiddhipādoti āha “upāyo cā”tiādi. Sabbatthāti suttantabhājanīye, abhidhammabhājanīye ca. Tenāha “suttantabhājanīye hī”tiādi. Samādhivisesanabhāvenāti [V 0.0165] “chandādhipati, chandahetuko, chandādhiko vā samādhi chandasamādhī”tiādinā samādhissa visesanabhāvena[M 0.0168]. “Samādhisevanavasenā”ti ca pāṭho. Tattha samādhisevanavasenāti chandādhike adhipatiṃ karitvā samādhissa āsevanavasena. Upāyabhūtānanti “chandavato ce samādhi ijjhati, mayheva ijjhatī”ti samādhiāsevanāya upāyabhūtānaṃ.

Because it is different from the sequence of words previously stated, he says 'having made it unprecedented.' The explanation should be applied in order: In what sense is there attainment of spiritual power? In what sense is the base the preliminary part? If the base is in the sense of a foundation, then it would be called only the base for spiritual power as a foundation, not the base for spiritual power as a means. Therefore it is said, 'and the means,' and so on. 'Everywhere' means in the Suttantabhājaniya and in the Abhidhammabhājaniya. Hence it is said, 'For in the Suttantabhājaniya,' and so on. 'As a qualifier of concentration' means by way of being a qualifier of concentration, as in 'concentration of will is concentration that has will as dominant, is caused by will, or is predominated by will.' There is also the reading 'by way of cultivating concentration.' Therein, 'by way of cultivating concentration' means by way of cultivating concentration after having made will predominant. 'To those that are the means' means to those that are the means for cultivating concentration, as in 'if concentration is accomplished for one with will, it is accomplished for me.'

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Suttantabhājaniya is concluded.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Abhidhammabhājaniya

444. Sādhipativārāni aṭṭhasatāni, tesu paccekaṃ cattāro iddhipādā na sambhavantīti āha “sādhipativārānaṃ paripuṇṇānaṃ abhāvā”ti. Tattha kāraṇamāha “na hi adhipatīnaṃ adhipatayo vijjantī”ti. Yadi hi adhipatī siyuṃ sādhipatīti iddhipādabhedena dvattiṃsa nayasatāni, suddhikāni aṭṭhāti cattāri nayasahassāni bhaveyyuṃ, taṃ pana natthīti adhippāyo. Yattakā pana nayā idha labbhanti, taṃ dassetuṃ “ekekasmiṃ panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Suddhikāni aṭṭha nayasatāni sādhipatikānipi aṭṭhevāti catunnaṃ maggānaṃ vasena soḷasa nayasatāni.

444. There are eight hundred sections with a dominant factor, but the four bases for spiritual power do not arise in each of them. Hence it is said: 'because of the absence of complete sections with a dominant factor.' Therein, the reason is stated: 'For there are no dominants of dominants.' If there were dominants of dominants, then by the division of the bases for spiritual power there would be thirty-two hundred methods with a dominant factor and eight hundred pure ones, which would make four thousand methods. But this is not the case; this is the intention. However, to show how many methods are found here, it is said, 'But in each,' and so on. There are eight hundred pure methods and eight hundred with a dominant factor, thus by way of the four paths there are sixteen hundred methods.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Abhidhammabhājaniya is concluded.

3. Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Section of Questions

Sayaṃ jeṭṭhakabhāvena pavattanato cattāro adhipatayo aññamaññaṃ garuṃ na karonti. Tasmā “cattāro iddhipādā na maggādhipatino”ti vuttā. Tenāha “aññamaññassa pana adhipatayo na bhavantī”ti. Etamatthanti “adhipatayo aññamaññassa adhipatī na bhavantī”ti etamatthaṃ. Adhipatinoti adhipati bhavituṃ samatthassa. Adhipatiṃ na karontīti adhipatiṃ katvā garuṃ katvā [V 0.0166] nappavattanti. Adhipatīnaṃ sahabhāveti adhipatikiccakaraṇena sahapavattiyaṃ. “Avīmaṃsādhipatikassa maggassa abhāvā”ti idaṃ “adhipatitāsamatthā dhammā adhipatibhāveneva pavatteyyu”nti dosāropanavasenāha, na yathādhigatavasena. Adhipatidhammānañhi pubbābhisaṅkhāre sati adhipatibhāvena pavatti, na aññathāti sahabhāvepi tadabhāvaṃ sandhāya visesanaṃ na [M 0.0169] kattabbaṃ siyāti sakkā vattuṃ. Aññamaññādhipatikaraṇabhāveti aññamaññaṃ adhipatiṃ katvā pavattiyaṃ. Vīmaṃsādhipatikattavacananti vīmaṃsādhipatikabhāvassa vacanaṃ. Na vattabbaṃ siyā sabbesampi adhipatīnaṃ sādhipatikattāti adhippāyo. Sahabhāvo paṭikkhitto eva sādhipatibhāvassa anekaṃsikatāvacanato.

Because they proceed by way of being chief, the four dominants do not regard each other as superior. Therefore it is said, 'The four bases for spiritual power are not dominants of the path.' Hence it is stated, 'Moreover, they do not become dominants for each other.' This means: 'The dominants do not become dominants for each other.' 'Of a dominant' means of one capable of being a dominant. 'They do not make a dominant' means they do not proceed by making one a dominant, by making one superior. 'In the co-arising of dominants' means in proceeding together while performing the function of a dominant. The statement 'because of the absence of a path with investigation as its dominant' is said by way of imputing a fault, not in accordance with what is actually the case. For dominant states proceed by way of being dominant when there is a prior determination, not otherwise. Therefore, it can be said that even when they co-arise, a qualification should not be made with reference to its absence. 'In the state of making each other dominant' means in proceeding by making each other dominant. 'The statement of investigation being dominant' means the statement of the state of investigation being dominant. The intention is that it should not be said that all dominants have a dominant. Co-arising is indeed rejected because of the statement that the state of having a dominant is not invariable.

Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Section of Questions is concluded.

Iddhipādavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Analysis of the Bases for Spiritual Power is concluded.

10. Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅgo

10. Analysis of the Enlightenment Factors

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Suttanta Division

Paṭhamanayavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the First Method

466. Patiṭṭhānaṃ [M 0.0170][V 0.0167] idha saṃsāre avaṭṭhānaṃ, tassa mūlaṃ kilesāti āha “kilesavasena patiṭṭhāna”nti. Patiṭṭhānāya pana byāpārāpatti kammanti vuttaṃ “abhisaṅkhāravasena āyūhanā”ti. Yasmā kilesesu taṇhādiṭṭhiyo taṇhādiṭṭhicaritānaṃ visesato saṃsāranāyikā, kilesasahitameva ca kammaṃ patiṭṭhānāya hoti, na kevalaṃ, tasmā vuttaṃ “taṇhādiṭṭhīhi…pe… āyūhanā”ti. Tathā taṇhāya bhavassādabhāvato, diṭṭhiyā vibhavābhinandanabhūtāya vibhavābhisaṅkharaṇabhāvato “taṇhāvasena patiṭṭhānaṃ, diṭṭhivasena āyūhanā”ti vuttaṃ. Diṭṭhīsupi antomukhappavattāya bhavadiṭṭhiyā visesato saṃsāre avaṭṭhānaṃ, yato olīyanāti vuccatīti āha “sassatadiṭṭhiyā patiṭṭhāna”nti. Bahimukhappavattāpi vibhavadiṭṭhi bhavābhisaṅkharaṇaṃ nātivattatīti vuttaṃ “ucchedadiṭṭhiyā āyūhanā”ti. Layāpatti yathāraddhassa ārambhassa aniṭṭhānaṃ antosaṅkocabhāvatoti āha “līnavasena patiṭṭhāna”nti. Uddhatāpatti anupāyabhūtā byāpārāpatti asaṅkocabhāvatoti vuttaṃ “uddhaccavasena āyūhanā”ti. Tathā kosajjapakkhikattā ca kāmasukhānuyogassa uddhaccapakkhikattā ca attakilamathānuyogassa tadubhayavasena patiṭṭhānāyūhanā vuttā, itaraṃ vuttanayānusārena veditabbaṃ. Idhāti imissā sammohavinodaniyā. Avuttānanti “kilesavasena patiṭṭhāna”ntiādīnaṃ vasena veditabbā patiṭṭhānāyūhanāti yojanā.

466. Here in saṃsāra, establishment (patiṭṭhāna) is remaining (avaṭṭhāna), and its root is the defilements; hence it is said, 'establishment by means of defilements.' But the engagement for establishment is kamma; hence it is said, 'accumulation by means of volitional formations.' Because among the defilements, craving and view are particularly the leaders in saṃsāra for those of a craving and view disposition, and because it is kamma accompanied by defilements, not kamma alone, that leads to establishment, it is therefore said: 'by means of craving and view ... accumulation.' Similarly, because craving consists in savoring existence and view consists in delighting in non-existence and thus forming non-existence, it is said: 'establishment by means of craving, accumulation by means of view.' Among views, too, the eternalist view, which proceeds inwardly, is particularly the remaining in saṃsāra, from which comes what is called sluggishness; hence it is said: 'establishment by means of eternalist view.' The annihilationist view, which proceeds outwardly, does not transcend the formation of existence; hence it is said: 'accumulation by means of annihilationist view.' The incurring of sloth is the non-completion of an undertaking that has been started, owing to its nature of inward contraction; hence it is said: 'establishment by means of sloth.' The incurring of restlessness is an unskillful engagement, owing to its nature of non-contraction; hence it is said: 'accumulation by means of restlessness.' Similarly, because indulgence in sensual pleasures is on the side of idleness and the practice of self-mortification is on the side of restlessness, establishment and accumulation are stated by way of this pair. The rest should be understood according to the method stated. 'Here' means in this Sammohavinodanī. The connection is: 'of what was not said' means that establishment and accumulation are to be understood by way of 'establishment by means of defilements,' and so on.

Samappavatte dhammeti līnuddhaccavirahena samappavatte sampayuttadhamme. Paṭisañcikkhatīti patirūpaṃ [V 0.0168] saṅkaleti gaṇeti tuleti. Tenāha “upapattito ikkhatī”ti. Tadākāroti paṭisaṅkhānākāro upapattito ikkhanākāro. Evañca katvāti paṭisaṅkhānasabhāvattā eva upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa. Pacchimapacchimakāraṇabhāvoti pacchimassa pacchimassa kāraṇabhāvo. Purimaṃ purimañhi pacchimassa pacchimassa visesapaccayoti.

'In the state that proceeds evenly' means in the associated states that proceed evenly, being free from sluggishness and restlessness. 'He reflects' means he suitably conceives, counts, and weighs. Hence it is said, 'he observes from the point of view of its occurrence.' 'That manner' is the manner of reflection, the manner of observing from its occurrence. 'And having done so': it is precisely because of the reflective nature of the equanimity enlightenment factor. 'The state of being a cause for each subsequent one' means the state of being a cause for each subsequent one. For each preceding one is a specific condition for each succeeding one.

467. Aviparītakāyādisabhāvaggahaṇasamatthatāya [M 0.0171] balavatī eva sati. Paññā gahitā satinepakkenāti attho. Evaṃcittoti evaṃ lābhasakkārasilokasannissitacitto. Cirakatavattādivasenāti cirakatavattādisīsena. “Vutto”ti imināpi “katvā āha kāyaviññattiṃ…pe… koṭṭhāsa”nti yojanā.

467. Mindfulness is indeed strong because of its capability to grasp the undistorted intrinsic nature of the body and so on. The meaning is that wisdom is grasped by mindfulness and prudence. 'Thus-minded' means a mind dependent on gain, honor, and fame. 'By way of long practice, etc.' means with long practice, etc., as the main points. By this word 'stated,' too, the connection should be made thus: 'having done, he speaks of bodily intimation ... to the section.'

Paresanti na anantarānaṃ. Sabbesaṃ…pe… yojetabbā “sabbe bojjhaṅgā sabbesaṃ paccayavisesā hontiyevā”ti. Kāmetīti kāmo, assādanavasena āmasatīti āmisaṃ, kāmova āmisanti kāmāmisaṃ, kilesakāmo. Vatthukāmo pana āmasīyatīti āmisaṃ. Evaṃ sesadvayampi. Tesu lokīyanti ettha sukhavisesāti loko, upapattiviseso. Vaṭṭaṃ saṃsāro. Kāmassādavasena pavatto lobho kāmāmisaṃ. Bhavavisesapatthanāvasena pavatto lokāmisaṃ. Vibhavo nāma kimatthiyo, ko vā taṃ abhipattheyyāti vaṭṭānugedhabhūto lobho vaṭṭāmisanti ca vadanti. Tadārammaṇanti tassā taṇhāya ārammaṇaṃ, rūpādi. Lokadhammā lābhādayo. Vuttāvasesā sabbāva taṇhā saṃsārajanako rāgo.

'Of others,' not of the immediately preceding ones. 'For all...' should be connected thus: 'All enlightenment factors are specific conditions for all.' One desires (kāmeti), thus it is desire (kāmo); one enjoys (assādanavasena āmasati), thus it is bait (āmisaṃ); desire itself is bait, thus 'desire-as-bait' (kāmāmisaṃ), which is sensual desire as a defilement. But an object of desire is what is enjoyed, thus it is bait. Similarly for the other two. Among them, regarding 'worldly' (lokīya): here 'world' (loka) means a particular kind of happiness, a particular kind of rebirth. The round (vaṭṭa) is saṃsāra. Greed that proceeds by way of savoring sensual pleasures is 'desire-as-bait.' Greed that proceeds by way of aspiring for a particular existence is 'world-as-bait' (lokāmisaṃ). Some say: 'What is the purpose of non-existence? Who would aspire to it?'—thus the greed that pursues the round is 'round-as-bait' (vaṭṭāmisaṃ). 'Having that as object' means having that craving's object, such as form. Worldly states are gain and so on. All the remaining craving that has been mentioned is the passion that generates saṃsāra.

Paṭhamanayavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the First Method is concluded.

Dutiyanayavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Second Method

468-9. Sabbe sattāti kāmabhavādīsu, saññībhavādīsu, ekavokārabhavādīsu ca sabbabhavesu sabbe sattā. Āhārato ṭhiti etesanti āhāraṭṭhitikā, paccayaṭṭhitikā. Yena paccayena te tiṭṭhanti, so ekova dhammo ñātapariññāsaṅkhātāya “āhāraṭṭhitikā”ti abhiññāya [V 0.0169] abhiññeyyo. Dve dhātuyoti saṅkhatāsaṅkhatadhātuyo. Tisso dhātuyoti kāmadhāturūpadhātuarūpadhātuyo. Pañca vimuttāyatanānīti “idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno satthā dhammaṃ deseti aññataro vā garuṭṭhāniyo”tiādinā (dī. ni. 3.322, 355; a. ni. 5.26) āgatāni vimuccanakāraṇāni. Anuttariyānīti dassanānuttariyādīni cha anuttariyāni. Niddasavatthūnīti yehi [M 0.0172] kāraṇehi niddaso hoti, tāni niddasavatthūni nāma. Desanāmattañcetaṃ. Khīṇāsavo hi dasavasso hutvā parinibbuto puna dasavasso na hoti. Na kevalañca dasavasso, navavassopi…pe… ekamuhuttikopi na hotiyeva puna paṭisandhiyā abhāvā, aṭṭhuppattivasena panevaṃ vuttaṃ. Tāni pana “idha, bhikkhu, sikkhāsamādāne tibbacchando hotī”tiādinā (dī. ni. 3.331) sutte āgatāniyeva. “Sammādiṭṭhissa purisapuggalassa micchādiṭṭhi nijjiṇṇā hotī”tiādīni (dī. ni. 3.360; a. ni. 10.106) dasa nijjaravatthūni. Khandhādayoti khandhāyatanadhātādayo. Vinandhananti “bhavādivinandhanaṭṭhena vānaṃ vuccati taṇhā”ti dasseti. Gamananti assādanavasena ārammaṇe pavattimāha. Tena vuttaṃ “piyarūpasātarūpesū”ti.

468-9. 'All beings' refers to all beings in all kinds of existence, such as the realms of sensual existence, the realms of perception, and the realms of single-constituent existence. 'Sustained by nutriment' means they are sustained by nutriment, that is, by conditions. The single phenomenon by which they are sustained is to be directly known by the direct knowledge called 'full understanding of the known' as 'sustained by nutriment.' 'Two elements' are the conditioned and unconditioned elements. 'Three elements' are the sensual-sphere element, the form-sphere element, and the formless-sphere element. 'Five bases for liberation' are the causes for liberation mentioned in the suttas, such as: 'Here, bhikkhus, the Teacher or a respected elder teaches the Dhamma to a bhikkhu…' 'The unsurpassables' refers to the six unsurpassables, beginning with the unsurpassable vision. 'Grounds for being declared taintless' are the reasons for which one is declared taintless; these are called the grounds for being declared taintless. This is merely a way of teaching. For one whose taints are destroyed, having attained final Nibbāna at the age of ten, does not again become ten years old. Not only ten years old, but not even nine years old… not even for a single moment, due to the absence of relinking. However, this is said based on the occasion for the teaching. These are indeed found in the sutta: 'Here, a bhikkhu has a keen desire for undertaking the training…' The ten 'grounds for wearing away' are those beginning: 'For a person with right view, wrong view is worn away…' 'Aggregates, etc.' refers to the aggregates, sense bases, elements, and so forth. 'Entanglement' is shown by the statement: 'Craving is called vāna (entanglement) because it entangles one in existence, etc.' 'Going' refers to proceeding toward an object by way of savoring. Hence it is said: 'in what is dear and agreeable.'

Vipassanāsahagatanti veditabbaṃ viññattisamuṭṭhāpakattā. “Maggaṃ appattaṃ kāyikaṃ vīriya”nti visesetvā vuttattā pana lokuttaravīriyampi pariyāyena kāyikaṃ nāma atthīti dīpitaṃ hoti.

It should be understood as 'accompanied by insight' because it gives rise to intimation. But since it is said with the specification, 'Bodily energy is the path not yet attained,' it is shown that supramundane energy, too, is figuratively called 'bodily.'

Rūpāvacare pītisambojjhaṅgoti na vuccatīti āha “rūpāvacare…pe… paṭikkhittā”ti. Yathā vipassanāsahagatā pīti pariyāyena “pītisambojjhaṅgo”ti vuccati, evaṃ rūpāvacare pīti nibbedhabhāgiyā vattabbā siyā. Evaṃ labbhamānāpi alabbhamānaṃ upādāya na vuttā. “Avitakkaavicārā”ti visesanaṃ santapaṇītāya pītiyā dassanatthaṃ. Bojjhaṅgabhūtāti pariyāyabojjhaṅgabhūtā. Avitakkaavicāro pīti…pe… na vutto savitakkasavicārattā tassa. Na hi kāmāvacarā avitakkaavicārā pīti atthi.

He says that in the form sphere it is not called the 'enlightenment factor of rapture,' with the words: 'In the form sphere… it is rejected.' Just as rapture accompanied by insight is figuratively called the 'enlightenment factor of rapture,' so too, rapture in the form sphere, being a factor leading to penetration, might be spoken of. Even though it is obtainable in this way, it is not mentioned with reference to what is unobtainable. The qualification 'without thought and examination' is for the purpose of showing that the rapture is tranquil and sublime. 'Being an enlightenment factor' means being an enlightenment factor figuratively. Rapture without thought and examination… is not mentioned because that involves thought and examination. For in the sensual sphere there is no rapture without thought and examination.

Idha vutto pariyāyenāti attho. Maggapaṭivedhānulomanato vipassanāya viya pādakajjhānesupi satiādayo “bojjhaṅgā”tveva vuccantīti āha “nibbedhabhāgiyattā na paṭikkhipitabbo”ti. Evaṃ kasiṇajjhānādīsu bojjhaṅge uddharantānaṃ adhippāyaṃ vatvā anuddharantānaṃ [V 0.0170] adhippāyaṃ vattuṃ “anuddharantā panā”tiādimāha. Te hi āsannekantakiccanibbattīhi vipassanākkhaṇe bojjhaṅge uddharanti, na jhānakkhaṇe tadabhāvato. Tenāha “vipassanākiccassa viya…pe… na uddharantī”ti. Kasiṇanissando arūpānīti āha “tadāyattānī”ti.

The meaning is that here it is stated figuratively. He says, 'because it partakes of penetration, it should not be rejected,' meaning that just as in insight meditation, so too in the basic jhānas, mindfulness and the other factors are called 'enlightenment factors' because they are in conformity with the penetration of the path. Having thus stated the intention of those who abstract the enlightenment factors in the kasiṇa-jhānas and so on, to state the intention of those who do not abstract them, he says, 'But those who do not abstract them…' For they abstract the enlightenment factors at the moment of insight because of the accomplishment of the task that is certain and imminent, but not at the moment of jhāna, because of their absence then. Hence he says, 'Unlike the function of insight… they do not abstract them.' He says 'dependent on them,' meaning that the formless attainments are the outflow of the kasiṇas.

Dutiyanayavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Second Method is finished.

Tatiyanayavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Third Method

470-1. Vossajjanaṃ [M 0.0173] pahānaṃ vossaggo, vossajjanaṃ vā vissaṭṭhabhāvo nirāsaṅkānuppavesoti āha “vossaggasaddo…pe… duvidhatā vuttā”ti. Vipassanākkhaṇe tadaṅgatanninnappakārena, maggakkhaṇe samucchedatadārammaṇakaraṇappakārena.

470-1. Relinquishment is abandonment, release. Or it is the state of being completely released, an entering without longing. Thus it is said: 'the word “relinquishment”… is spoken of in two ways.' At the moment of insight, it is in the mode of temporary abandonment and of inclining towards that; at the moment of the path, it is in the mode of eradication and of making that its object.

Tatiyanayavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Third Method is finished.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Suttanta Analysis is finished.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Abhidhamma Analysis

472. Upekkhanamupekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa sabhāvo, so ca samādhivīriyasambojjhaṅgo viya sampayuttānaṃ ūnādhikabhāvabyāvaṭo ahutvā tesaṃ anūnānadhikabhāve majjhattākārappavattīti imamatthaṃ āha “upekkhanavasenā”tiādinā. Tattha upapattito ikkhananti paṭisaṅkhānamāha.

472. Equanimity is the intrinsic nature of the enlightenment factor of equanimity. This meaning—that, unlike the enlightenment factors of concentration and energy, it is not concerned with the deficiency or excess of the associated states but proceeds in a neutral manner with respect to their being neither deficient nor excessive—is stated with the words 'by way of equanimity,' and so on. Therein, 'observing' refers to reflection.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Abhidhamma Analysis is finished.

Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Analysis of the Enlightenment Factors is finished.

11. Maggaṅgavibhaṅgo

11. Analysis of the Path Factors

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Abhidhamma Analysis

490. Abhidhammeti [M 0.0174][V 0.0171] dhammasaṅgahe. So hi nibbattitābhidhammadesanā, na vibhaṅgadesanā viya suttantanayavimissā. Ariyopapadataṃ na karoti vināpi tenassa ariyabhāvasiddhito. Tenāha aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “yathā hī”tiādi.

490. 'Abhidhamma' refers to the Dhammasaṅgaṇī. For that is a pure Abhidhamma exposition, unlike the exposition of the Vibhaṅga, which is mixed with the Suttanta method. It does not lead to arising as a noble one, since even without it one's noble state is accomplished. Therefore, it is said in the commentary: 'Just as...,' and so on.

493. “Lokiyakālenā”ti idaṃ pubbabhāgabhāvanānubhāvena kiccātirekasiddhīti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Etesanti sammādiṭṭhiādīnaṃ. Appahāne, pahāne ca ādīnavānisaṃsavibhāvanādinā visesappaccayattā sammādiṭṭhiādīni micchāvācādīni pajahāpentīti vuttāni. Micchāvācādito nivatti sammāvācādikiriyāti vuttaṃ “sammāvācādikiriyā hi viratī”ti. Sammādiṭṭhiādayo viya na kārāpakabhāvena, taṃsamaṅgīpuggalo viya na kattubhāvena. Lokuttarakkhaṇepīti na kevalaṃ lokiyakkhaṇeyeva, atha kho lokuttarakkhaṇepi.

493. 'At the worldly time'—this is said to show the accomplishment of an additional task through the power of the preliminary development. 'Of these' refers to right view and so on. Because they are a special condition—by way of contemplating the danger in not abandoning and the benefit in abandoning, and so on—it is said that right view and so on cause the abandoning of wrong speech and so on. Cessation from wrong speech and so on is the activity of right speech and so on; thus it is said: 'For the activity of right speech and so on is abstinence.' Not in the manner of an agent that causes action, like right view and so on; and not in the manner of a doer, like the person endowed with it. 'Even at the supramundane moment' means not only at the mundane moment but also at the supramundane moment.

Khandhopadhiṃ vipaccatīti paṭisandhidāyikaṃ sandhāyāha. Tattha vipaccatīti pavattivipākadāyikaṃ.

'It ripens the basis of the aggregates'—this is said referring to what gives rebirth-linking. Therein, 'it ripens' refers to what gives the resultant in the course of life.

Ekekanti “tattha katamā sammādiṭṭhī”tiādinā ekekaṃ aṅgaṃ pucchitvā. Tassa tassevāti ekekaaṅgasseva, na aṅgasamudāyassa. Saha pana pucchitvāti “tattha katamo pañcaṅgiko maggo”ti pucchitvā. Ekato vissajjanapaṭiniddesattāti yadipi “tattha katamā sammādiṭṭhi? Yā paññā”tiādinā (vibha. 495) vissajjanaṃ kataṃ, “tattha katamo pañcaṅgiko [V 0.0172] maggo”ti (vibha. 494) pana ekato katāya pucchāya vissajjanavasena paṭiniddesabhāvato na pāṭiyekkaṃ pucchāvissajjanaṃ nāma hoti. Kasmā panettha pañcaṅgikavāre eva pāṭiyekkaṃ pucchāvissajjanaṃ kataṃ, na aṭṭhaṅgikavāreti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “tatthā”tiādi. Ekekamukhāyāti sammādiṭṭhiādimukhāya. Tena vuttaṃ “ariyaṃ vo, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhiṃ desessāmi saupanisaṃ saparikkhāra”ntiādi [M 0.0175] (saṃ. ni. 5.28). Pubbasuddhiyā sijjhanti. Tathā hi vuttaṃ “pubbeva kho panassa kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ ājīvo suparisuddho hotī”ti (ma. ni. 3.431), tasmā sammāvācādimukhā bhāvanā natthīti adhippāyo. Tenāha “na maggassa upacārenā”ti.

'One by one' means having asked about each factor individually, with the words, 'Therein, what is right view?' and so on. 'Of each one' refers to each individual factor, not to the collection of factors. 'But having asked together' means having asked, 'Therein, what is the five-factored path?' Because the exposition is an answer given collectively, even though an answer is given starting 'Therein, what is right view? It is wisdom...' (Vibh. 495), since this is by way of an answer to the question asked collectively, 'Therein, what is the five-factored path?' (Vibh. 494), it is not called a separate question and answer. In reference to the objection, 'Why here is the question and answer done for each one separately only in the section on the five-factored path, not in the section on the eight-factored path?' he says, 'Therein...,' and so on. 'By way of each opening' means by way of the opening of right view and so on. Therefore it is said: 'Bhikkhus, I will teach you the noble right view with its conditions and its equipment...' (SN 45:8), and so on. They are accomplished by means of prior purity. For so it is said: 'But previously his bodily action, verbal action, and livelihood have been well purified' (MN 117). Therefore, the meaning is that there is no development by way of the opening of right speech and so on. Hence he says: 'not by way of approach to the path.'

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Abhidhamma Analysis is finished.

Maggaṅgavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Analysis of the Path Factors is finished.

12. Jhānavibhaṅgo

12. Analysis of Jhāna

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Suttanta Division

Mātikāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Mātikā

508. Pātimokkhasaṃvarādīti [M 0.0176][V 0.0173] ādi-saddena indriyesu guttadvāratā, bhojane mattaññutā, satisampajaññaṃ, jāgariyānuyogoti evamādike saṅgaṇhāti. Asubhānussatiyoti asubhajhānāni, anussatijhānāni ca. Sati samaṇabhāvakarapubbabhāgakaraṇīyasampattiyaṃ samaṇabhāvopi siddhoyeva hotīti āha “suññā…pe… dassetī”ti. Kāraṇe hi siddhe phalampi siddhameva hotīti. Sikkhāpadānaṃ sarūpaṃ, sikkhitabbākāraṃ, saṅkhepato vibhāgañca dassetuṃ “sikkhāpadesū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha nāmakāyādivasenāti nāmakāyapadakāyabyañjanakāyavasena vuttesu. Iminā sikkhāpadānaṃ sikkhāya adhigamūpāyabhūtapaññattisabhāvataṃ dasseti. Tesu sikkhitabbākāro satthuāṇānatikkamoyevāti āha “vaca…pe… tabbesū”ti. Sikkhākoṭṭhāsesūti vuttappabhedesu adhisīlasikkhābhāgesu. Tesu samādānameva sikkhitabbākāroti vuttaṃ “paripūraṇavasena sikkhitabbesū”ti. Sikkhāpadekadesabhūtāti sikkhāpadasamudāyassa avayavabhūtā. Bhikkhusikkhā hi idhādhippetā “idha bhikkhū”ti vuttattā. Tathā hi vakkhati “sesasikkhā pana atthuddhāravasena sikkhāsaddassa atthadassanatthaṃ vuttā”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 516).

508. 'Restraint of the Pātimokkha, etc.': by the word 'etc.' he includes guarding the sense doors, moderation in eating, mindfulness and clear comprehension, devotion to wakefulness, and so on. 'Recollection of the foul' means the jhānas on the foul and the jhānas that are recollections. When there is accomplishment of the preliminary duties that bring about the state of a recluse, the state of a recluse is indeed accomplished; therefore he says: 'he shows... empty...,' etc. For when the cause is accomplished, the result too is accomplished. To show the nature of the training rules, the way they are to be trained in, and their division in brief, the phrase 'in the training rules...,' and so on, is stated. Therein, 'by way of the body of names, etc.' means among those stated by way of the body of names, the body of terms, and the body of syllables. By this he shows that the training rules have the nature of a designation that is the means for attaining the training. Among them, the way they are to be trained in is simply not transgressing the Teacher's command; hence he says: '...in what is to be... by speech...,' etc. 'In the sections of the training' means in the aforementioned divisions that are parts of the training in the higher virtue. Among them, the way they are to be trained in is said to be the mere undertaking, with the words: 'in what is to be trained in by way of fulfilling.' 'Being a part of the training rules' means being a constituent of the collection of training rules. For the bhikkhu's training is intended here, because it is said, 'Here, a bhikkhu.' For so he will say: 'But the remaining trainings are stated for the purpose of showing the meaning of the word 'training' by way of extracting the meaning' (Vibh-a 348).

Mātikāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Mātikā is finished.

Niddesavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Exposition

509. Diṭṭhattāti [V 0.0174] sayambhūñāṇena sacchikatattā. Khantiādīsupi eseva nayo. Sayambhūñāṇena sacchikaraṇavaseneva hi bhagavato khamanaruccanādayo, na aññesaṃ viya anussavākāraparivitakkādimukhena. Aviparītaṭṭho ekantaniyyānaṭṭhena veditabbo.
