Sikkhiyamānoti sikkhāya paṭipajjiyamāno[M 0.0177]. Sikkhitabbāni sikkhāpadānīti sikkhāpadapāḷiṃ vadati. Khandhattayanti sīlādikkhandhattayaṃ. “Sabbapāpassa…pe… buddhāna sāsana”nti (dha. pa. 183; dī. ni. 1.90; netti. 30) vacanato āha “anusāsanadānabhūtaṃ sikkhattaya”nti.

509. 'Because of having been seen' means because of having been realized by self-originated knowledge. This same method applies also to patience, etc. For the Blessed One's patience, approval, and so on, are indeed by way of realization with self-originated knowledge, not, as with others, by way of hearsay, reflection on the aspects, and so on. The meaning 'not distorted' should be understood by the meaning 'leading out unfailingly.' 'Being trained' means being practiced in the training. 'The training rules to be trained in': he is speaking of the Pāli of the training rules. 'The three aggregates' means the three aggregates of virtue, etc. In accordance with the statement, 'The non-doing of all evil... this is the teaching of the Buddhas' (Dhp 183; DN 14), he says, 'the threefold training which is the giving of instruction.'

Sammādiṭṭhiyā paccayattāti maggasammādiṭṭhiyā ekantahetubhāvato. Ettha ca sammādiṭṭhīti kammassakatāsammādiṭṭhi, kammapathasammādiṭṭhi ca. Phalakāraṇopacārehīti phalūpacārena sammādiṭṭhipaccayattā, kāraṇūpacārena sammādiṭṭhipubbaṅgamattā. Kusaladhammehi attano ekadesabhūtehīti sammādiṭṭhidhamme sandhāyāha. Kusalapaññāviññāṇānaṃ vā pajānanavijānanavasena dassanaṃ diṭṭhīti. Tena avayavadhammena samudāyassa upacaritataṃ dasseti. Vinayanakiriyattāti desanābhūtaṃ sikkhattayamāha. Dhammenāti dhammato anapetena. Avisamasabhāvenāti avisamena sabhāvena, samenāti attho.

'Because right view is a condition' means because it is the invariable cause of path right view. And here, 'right view' means right view of ownership of kamma and right view of the path of kamma. 'By figurative usage regarding result and cause': by figurative usage regarding the result, because right view is a condition; by figurative usage regarding the cause, because it is merely preceded by right view. 'With wholesome states that are a part of oneself': this is said with reference to the states of right view. Or, 'view' is the seeing, by way of knowing and discerning, of wholesome wisdom and consciousness. Thereby he shows the figurative application of the aggregate to a constituent state. 'Because it is the act of training': he speaks of the threefold training which is the teaching. 'By the Dhamma' means not deviating from the Dhamma. 'With an even nature' means with a nature that is not uneven, that is, with an even one.

510. Anaññatthenāti garahādiaññattharahitena sakatthena. Bhinnapaṭadhareti bhikkhusāruppavasena pañcakhaṇḍādinā chedena chinnacīvaradhare.

510. 'Not for the sake of another' means for one's own purpose, a purpose devoid of what is for another, such as blame, etc. 'Wearing a patched-up robe' means wearing a robe cut with a five-section cut, etc., in a way befitting a bhikkhu.

Bhedanapariyāyavasena vuttaṃ, tasmā kilesānaṃ pahānā kilesānaṃ bhedā bhikkhūti vuttaṃ hoti.

It is said by way of the term 'breaking'; therefore, it is said that they are bhikkhus because of abandoning the defilements, because of breaking the defilements.

Guṇavasenāti sekkhadhammādiguṇānaṃ vasena. Tena bhāvatthato bhikkhusaddo dassito hoti.

'By way of virtue' means by way of the virtues such as the qualities of a learner. Thereby the word 'bhikkhu' is shown in its essential meaning.

Idaṃ dvayanti “ettha cā”tiādinā parato saṅgahadassanavasena vuttaṃ “sekkho”tiādikaṃ vacanadvayaṃ. Imināti “sekkho bhikkhu bhinnattā pāpakāna”nti padānaṃ atthadassanena. Na sameti sekkhaasekkhaputhujjanāsekkhadīpanato. Tadidanti paṭhamadvayaṃ. Nippariyāyadassanaṃ ariyānaṃ[V 0.0175], asekkhānaṃyeva ca sekkhabhinnakilesabhāvadīpanato. Vuttoti paṭiññāvacanaṃ, saccaṃ vuttoti attho. Na pana idhādhippeto atthuddhāravasena dassitattā.

'This pair' means the pair of statements beginning with 'a learner,' stated further on beginning with 'And here...' by way of showing inclusion. 'By this' means by showing the meaning of the words, 'A learner is a bhikkhu because of having broken the evil states,' etc. It does not fit, because it illuminates the learner, the non-learner, the worldling, and the non-learner. This is that first pair. The showing is direct for the noble ones, and only for non-learners, because it shows the state of having broken defilements, which is distinct from that of learners. 'Is said' is a statement of assertion; the meaning is 'is truly said.' But this is not intended here, as it is shown by way of extracting the meaning.

Bhagavato vacananti upasampadākammavācamāha. Tadanurūpanti tadanucchavikaṃ, yathāvuttanti attho. Parisāvatthusīmāsampattiyo “samaggena saṅghena akuppenā”ti (vibha. 510) iminā pakāsitāti “ṭhānāraha”nti padassa “anūna…pe… avutta”nti ettakameva atthamāha.

'The Blessed One's word': he speaks of the formal statement of the act of higher ordination. 'In accordance with that' means suitable for that; the meaning is 'as stated.' The accomplishments of the assembly, object, and boundary are indicated by this: 'by a unified Saṅgha, unshakeable...' (Vibh 510); therefore, for the phrase 'worthy of the occasion,' he states only this much meaning: 'not deficient... not unstated.'

511. Avītikkamanaviratibhāvatoti [M 0.0178] avītikkamasamādānabhūtā viratīti katvā vārittasīlaṃ patvā virati eva padhānanti cetanāsīlassapi pariyāyatā vuttā. “Nagaravaḍḍhakī vatthuvijjācariyo”ti idaṃ idhādhippetanagaravaḍḍhakīdassanaṃ. Vatthuvijjā, pāsādavijjāti duvidhā hi vaḍḍhakīvijjā. Lehitabbanti sāyitabbaṃ. Cubitabbanti pātabbaṃ.

511. 'Because it is the state of abstinence from transgression': since abstinence is what has been undertaken as non-transgression, and since, having reached the virtue of restraint, abstinence itself is primary, the synonymity of volitional virtue is also stated. 'A city carpenter, a master of architecture': this shows the city carpenter intended here. For the carpenter's craft is twofold: the science of sites and the science of mansions. 'What can be licked' means what can be tasted. 'What can be sucked' means what can be drunk.

Indriyasaṃvarāhārattāti indriyasaṃvarahetukattā. Pātimokkhasīlaṃ sikkhāpadasīlaṃ na pakatisīlādikena gayhatīti āha “pātimokkhato aññaṃ sīlaṃ kāyikaavītikkamādiggahaṇena gahita”nti. Taṃ pana pātimokkhasīlena na saṅgayhatīti na sakkā vattuṃ, kāyikavācasikasaṃvarassa tabbinimuttassa abhāvatoti dassento “iminā adhippāyena vutta”nti āha.

'Because it is nutriment for sense restraint' means because it is a cause for sense restraint. The Pātimokkha virtue, the virtue of the training rules, is not included by natural virtue, etc.; thus he says: 'Virtue other than the Pātimokkha is included by the inclusion of bodily non-transgression, etc.' But it cannot be said that this is not included by the Pātimokkha virtue, since there is no bodily and verbal restraint apart from it. Showing this, he says: 'it was said with this intention.'

Tattha pātimokkhasaddassa evaṃ attho veditabbo – kilesānaṃ balavabhāvato, pāpakiriyāya sukarabhāvato, puññakiriyāya ca dukkarabhāvato bahukkhattuṃ apāyesu patanasīloti pātī, puthujjano, aniccatāya vā bhavādīsu kammavegakkhitto ghaṭiyantaṃ viya anavaṭṭhānena paribbhamanato gamanasīloti pātī, maraṇavasena vā tamhi tamhi sattanikāye attabhāvassa pātanasīloti pātī, sattasantāno, cittameva vā. Taṃ pātinaṃ saṃsāradukkhato mokkhetīti pātimokkhaṃ. Cittassa hi vimokkhena sattopi “vimutto”ti vuccati. Vuttañhi “cittavodānā visujjhantī”ti (saṃ. ni. 3.100), “anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimutta”nti (mahāva. 28) ca. Atha vā avijjādinā hetunā saṃsāre patati gacchati pavattatīti pātī. “Avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarata”nti (saṃ. ni. 2.124; 3.99; 5.520; kathā. 75) hi [V 0.0176] vuttaṃ. Tassa pātino sattassa taṇhādisaṃkilesattayato mokkho etenāti pātimokkhaṃ. “Kaṇṭhekāḷo”tiādīnaṃ viya tassa samāsasiddhi veditabbā.

Here, the meaning of the word 'Pātimokkha' should be understood thus: Because defilements are powerful, because evil action is easy to do, and because meritorious action is difficult to do, an ordinary person is one who is inclined to fall frequently into the planes of misery; thus he is 'one who falls' (pātī). Or, because of impermanence, being hurled by the force of kamma into the various kinds of existence, he wanders about without stability like a spinning top, thus he is 'one who goes' (gamanasīlo), a pātī. Or, by way of death, he is inclined to cause his individual existence to fall into this or that class of beings; thus the continuity of a being, or the mind itself, is 'that which falls' (pātī). That which liberates this 'one who falls' from the suffering of saṃsāra is the Pātimokkha. For by the liberation of the mind, a being too is said to be 'liberated.' For it is said: 'Through the cleansing of the mind they are purified' (SN 3.100), and 'The mind is liberated from the taints through non-clinging' (Mv 28). Alternatively, due to causes such as ignorance, one falls, goes, and proceeds in saṃsāra; thus one is 'one who falls' (pātī). For it is said: 'For beings hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving, who are transmigrating and wandering on' (SN 2.124; 3.99; 5.520; Kathā 75). Liberation by means of this from the threefold defilements of craving and so on for that being who falls is the Pātimokkha. The formation of this compound should be understood to be like that of 'kaṇṭhekāḷo' (black-necked) and so on.

Atha vā pāteti vinipāteti dukkheti pāti, cittaṃ. Vuttañhi “cittena nīyati loko, cittena parikassatī”ti (saṃ. ni. 1.62). Tassa pātino [M 0.0179] mokkho etenāti pātimokkhaṃ. Patati vā etena apāyadukkhe vā saṃsāradukkhe vāti pātī, taṇhādisaṃkileso. Vuttañhi “taṇhā janeti purisaṃ (saṃ. ni. 1.55-57), taṇhādutiyo puriso”ti (itivu. 15; mahāni. 191; cūḷani. pārāyanānugītigāthā niddesa 107) ca ādi. Tato mokkhoti pātimokkhaṃ.

Alternatively, 'that which makes one fall' (pāti) is that which causes one to fall, brings one to ruin, and afflicts, namely, the mind. For it was said: 'The world is led by the mind, by the mind it is dragged around' (SN 1.62). Liberation by means of this from that which makes one fall is the Pātimokkha. Or, 'that by which one falls' (pātī) is that by which one falls into the suffering of the planes of misery or the suffering of saṃsāra, namely, defilements such as craving. For it was said: 'Craving generates a person' (SN 1.55-57), and 'A person has craving as his companion' (It 15; Mahānid. 191; Cūḷanid. Pārāyanānugītigāthā Niddesa 107), and so on. Liberation from that is the Pātimokkha.

Atha vā patati etthāti pātīni, cha ajjhattikabāhirāni āyatanāni. Vuttañhi “chasu loko samuppanno, chasu kubbati santhava”nti (saṃ. ni. 1.70; su. ni. 171). Tato chaajjhattikabāhirāyatanasaṅkhātato pātito mokkhoti pātimokkhaṃ.

Alternatively, 'places of falling' (pātīni) are so called because one falls in them; this refers to the six internal and external sense bases. For it is said: 'In the six the world has arisen; in the six it makes acquaintance' (SN 1.70; Sn 171). Therefore, liberation from these 'places of falling,' designated as the six internal and external sense bases, is the Pātimokkha.

Atha vā pāto vinipāto assa atthīti pātī, saṃsāro, tato mokkhoti pātimokkhaṃ.

Alternatively, saṃsāra is 'that which has falling' (pātī) because it has falling (pāto) and ruin (vinipāto); liberation from that is the Pātimokkha.

Atha vā sabbalokādhipatibhāvato dhammissaro bhagavā “patī”ti vuccati, muccati etenāti mokkho, patino mokkho tena paññattattāti patimokkho, patimokkho eva pātimokkhaṃ. Sabbaguṇānaṃ vā mūlabhāvato uttamaṭṭhena pati ca so yathāvuttenatthena mokkho cāti patimokkho, patimokkho eva pātimokkhaṃ. Tathā hi vuttaṃ “pātimokkhanti mukhametaṃ pamukhameta”nti (mahāva. 135) vitthāro.

Alternatively, because he is the sovereign of all worlds and the lord of the Dhamma, the Blessed One is called 'lord' (pati). One is liberated by this, thus it is 'liberation' (mokkha). It is the lord's liberation (patino mokkho) because it was laid down by him; hence Patimokkha. Patimokkha itself is Pātimokkha. Or, because it is the root of all virtues, it is a 'lord' (pati) in the sense of being supreme, and it is 'liberation' (mokkho) in the sense already stated; thus it is Patimokkha. Patimokkha itself is Pātimokkha. For so it is said: 'The Pātimokkha is the beginning, it is the principal' (Mv 135), and so on in detail.

Atha vā pa-iti pakāre, atīti accantatthe nipāto, tasmā pakārehi accantaṃ mokkhetīti pātimokkhaṃ. Idañhi sīlaṃ sayaṃ tadaṅgavasena, samādhisahitaṃ paññāsahitañca vikkhambhanavasena samucchedavasena ca accantaṃ mokkheti mocetīti pātimokkhaṃ. Pati pati [V 0.0177] mokkhoti vā patimokkho, tamhā tamhā vītikkamadosato paccekaṃ mokkhoti attho, patimokkhoyeva pātimokkhaṃ. Mokkho vā nibbānaṃ, tassa mokkhassa paṭibimbabhūtoti patimokkhaṃ. Sīlasaṃvaro hi nibbedhabhāgiyo sūriyassa aruṇuggamanaṃ viya nibbānassa udayabhūto tappaṭibhāgo viya hoti yathārahaṃ kilesanibbāpanatoti patimokkhaṃ, patimokkhaṃyeva pātimokkhaṃ.

Alternatively, 'pa' is in the sense of 'in various ways'; 'ati' is a particle in the sense of 'exceedingly'; therefore, because it liberates exceedingly in various ways, it is Pātimokkha. For this virtue itself liberates and releases exceedingly by way of substitution of opposites, and when accompanied by concentration and wisdom, by way of suppression and by way of cutting off; thus it is Pātimokkha. Or, it is 'liberation with respect to each particular case' (pati pati mokkho), thus Patimokkha; the meaning is liberation from each particular fault of transgression. Patimokkha itself is Pātimokkha. Or, 'liberation' (mokkha) is Nibbāna, and this is like a reflection of that liberation, thus Patimokkha. For restraint in virtue is conducive to penetration; like the sunrise for the sun, it is the arising of Nibbāna, like its counterpart in quenching the defilements as is fitting; thus it is Patimokkha. Patimokkha itself is Pātimokkha.

Atha [M 0.0180] vā mokkhaṃ pati vattati, mokkhābhimukhanti vā patimokkhaṃ, patimokkhaṃyeva pātimokkhanti. Idampi pātimokkhasaddassa mukhamattadassanameva. Sabbākaārena pana jinapātimokkho bhagavāva anavajjapatimokkhaṃ pātimokkhaṃ saṃvaṇṇeyya.

Alternatively, it is Patimokkha because it proceeds towards liberation, or because it is facing liberation; Patimokkha itself is Pātimokkha. This too is but a mere glimpse of the meaning of the word Pātimokkha. But in all respects, only the Blessed One, the Conqueror who is himself the Pātimokkha, could describe the faultless Pātimokkha.

513. Garubhaṇḍavissajjanakaraṇabhūtaṃ etassa atthīti garubhaṇḍavissajjanaṃ. Garubhaṇḍantarabhūtaṃ thāvarādi. Ūnakaṃ na vaṭṭatīti phātikammaṃ vuttaṃ. Atirekagghanakaṃ, tadagghanakameva vā vaṭṭatīti. Yathāvuttanti pokkharaṇito paṃsuuddharaṇādithāvarakammaṃ.

513. This has the nature of being an instrument for disposing of heavy goods, thus it is 'disposal of heavy goods.' Immovable property, etc., is included under heavy goods. Because what is of lesser value is not allowable, 'making amends' (phātikamma) is mentioned. What is of greater value, or of the exact same value, is allowable. 'As was said' refers to work on immovable property such as removing soil from a pond.

Dhāreti, poseti vā paresaṃ dārake.

He maintains or fosters the children of others.

Gihīnaṃ kariyamānaṃ vuttaṃ, na saṅghassa, gaṇassa vāti attho. Piṇḍapaṭipiṇḍanti uttarapadalopaṃ, purimapade uttarapadalopañca katvā niddesoti āha “piṇḍattha”ntiādi. Ayoniso vicāraṇaṃ ayāthāvapaṭipatti.

The meaning is that this was said concerning what is done by householders, not by the Saṅgha or a group. Regarding 'piṇḍapaṭipiṇḍa,' the explanation 'for the sake of alms,' etc., is given, this indication being made by eliding the final member of the compound and by eliding the final member in the first part of the compound. Unwise consideration is improper practice.

514. Gacchanti yathāsakaṃ visaye pavattantīti gāvo, cakkhādīni indriyāni.

514. The faculties, the eye and so on, are called 'cows' (gāvo) because they go, proceeding in their respective domains as they please.

Vidhunanaṃ papphoṭanaṃ, pavāhananti attho.

Shaking off, flapping, blowing away, is the meaning.

515. Yathā karaṇattho karaṇīyasaddo, evaṃ vikiraṇatthopi hotīti āha “vikkhipitabbānī”ti, viddhaṃsitabbānīti attho. Saṃyamanīyāni vā saṃyamakaraṇīyāni, “na puna evaṃ karomī”ti attano dahanaṃ manasā adhiṭṭhānaṃ saṃyamanaṃ, saṃyamanakaraṇīyāni saṃvarakaraṇīyānīti cittamattāyattā eva saṃyamasaṃvarā ācariyena adhippetāti āha “anāpattigamanīyānī”ti[V 0.0178]. Antevāsikatthero pana desanāpi cittuppādamanasikārehi vinā na hotīti desanāvisuddhiṃ nissaraṇaṃ vadati.

515. Just as the word 'karaṇīya' has the meaning of 'to be done,' so too it can have the meaning of 'to be scattered'; thus he says 'to be scattered,' meaning 'to be destroyed.' Alternatively, they are 'to be restrained,' that is, 'things to be made a restraint.' Restraint is the mental determination, the taming of oneself with the thought, 'I will not do so again.' Things to be made a restraint are things to be made a control. That the teacher intended restraint and control to be dependent solely on the mind is what he says by 'anāpattigamanīyāni' (to be led to a state of no offense). The resident elder, however, says that since confession (desanā) too does not occur without an arising of mind and attention, the purity of confession is the escape.

516. “Alaṅkato cepi…pe… sa bhikkhū”tiādīsu (dha. pa. 142) viya idhāpi guṇato bhikkhu adhippeto. Tathā ca vuttaṃ “idha bhikkhūti paṭipattiyā bhikkhubhāvadassanato evamāhā”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 355). Yattakaṃ ekena puggalena asesetvā samādātuṃ [M 0.0181] sakkā, taṃ sandhāyāha “yena samādānena sabbāpi sikkhā samādinnā hontī”ti yathā upasampadāpāripūriyā asesaṃ upasampannasikkhāsamādānaṃ. Tanti samādānaṃ. Anekesūti visuṃ visuṃ samādānesu. Yathā samādinnāya sikkhāya sabbena sabbaṃ avītikkamanaṃ sikkhitabbākāro, evaṃ sati vītikkame desanāgāminiyā desanā, vuṭṭhānagāminiyā vuṭṭhānaṃ tadupāyabhūtaṃ pārivāsikavattacaraṇādīti vuttaṃ “avīti…pe… ākārenā”ti. Yaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ pamādena vītikkantaṃ, taṃ sikkhiyamānaṃ na hotīti sesitaṃ nāma hotīti āha “vītikkamanavasena sesassā”ti.

516. In passages such as 'Though he be adorned… he is a bhikkhu' (Dhp 142), just as there, here too a bhikkhu is intended in terms of quality. And so it is said: 'Here, “bhikkhu” is said thus to show the state of a bhikkhu by way of practice' (Vibh-a 355). With reference to how much can be undertaken by a single person without remainder, he says, 'by which undertaking all the training rules are undertaken'—just as by the completion of the higher ordination the undertaking of the training for one who is ordained is complete. 'Tanti' means undertaking. 'Anekesu' means in various separate undertakings. Just as the mode of training is the non-transgression in any way whatsoever of a training rule that has been undertaken, so, when there is a transgression, for an offense that requires confession, there is confession; for an offense that requires rehabilitation, there is rehabilitation, the means for which are the observance of the probationer's duties, etc. This is what is said by 'non-transgression… by the mode…' When a training rule is transgressed through negligence, it is not being trained in and is thus called 'left over.' Thus he says, 'of what is left over by way of transgression.'

519. Cittaparisodhanabhāvanāti cittassa parisodhanabhūtā āvaraṇīyadhammavikkhambhikā samādhivipassanābhāvanā cittaparisodhanabhāvanā. Suppapariggāhakanti niddāpariggāhakaṃ. Idanti idaṃ abbokiṇṇabhavaṅgottaraṇasaṅkhātaṃ kiriyamayacittānaṃ appavattanaṃ suppaṃ nāma. Ito bhavaṅgottaraṇato. Pubbe ito kiriyamayacittappavattito parañca natthi. Ayaṃ kāyakilamatho, thinamiddhañca etassa suttassa paccayo.

519. 'Development of the purification of the mind' is the development of concentration and insight which purifies the mind and suppresses obstructive states. 'Embracing sleep' means taking up sleep. 'This': This non-arising of functional consciousness, which is designated as 'transcending the unbroken life-continuum,' is called 'sleep.' 'From this' means from this transcending of the life-continuum. Before this arising of functional consciousness and after it, there is nothing. This bodily fatigue, and sloth and torpor, are the conditions for this sleep.

522. Satipaṭṭhānādayoti satipaṭṭhānasammappadhānaiddhipādā, ekacce ca maggadhammā saha na pavattanti, tasmā pāḷiyaṃ na vuttāti adhippāyo. Ete tāva ekasmiṃ ārammaṇe saha na pavattantīti na gaṇheyyuṃ, indriyabalāni kasmā na gahitānīti āha “pavatta…pe… hontī”ti. Evampi saddhindriyabalāni bojjhaṅgehi na saṅgayhantīti kathaṃ tesaṃ tadantogadhatāti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “pīti…pe… vuttattā”ti.

522. 'The foundations of mindfulness and so on' refers to the foundations of mindfulness, the right strivings, and the bases of spiritual power; certain path factors do not arise together, and the intention is that this is why they are not mentioned in the Pāḷi. One should not take it that these do not arise together in a single object. Why were the faculties and powers not included? He said: 'Because they arise… they are…' Even so, in response to the objection, 'Since the faculty and power of faith are not included in the factors of enlightenment, how can they be included within them?', he says: 'Because rapture… etc., is stated…'

523. Samantatoti sabbabhāgesu sabbesu abhikkamādīsu, sabbabhāgato vā tesu eva abhikkamādīsu [V 0.0179] atthānatthādisabbabhāgato sabbākārato. Sammāti aviparītaṃ yoniso. Samanti avisamaṃ, iṭṭhādiārammaṇe rāgādivisamarahitaṃ katvāti attho.

523. 'Completely' means in all respects, in all activities such as going forward, etc.; or from every aspect, in those very activities of going forward, etc., from every aspect such as what is beneficial and what is not, in every way. 'Rightly' means non-pervertedly, wisely. 'Evenly' means without unevenness; the meaning is having made it free from the unevenness of lust, etc., in regard to desirable and other objects.

Bhikkhā carīyati etthāti bhikkhācāro, bhikkhāya caraṇaṭṭhānaṃ, so eva gocaro, bhikkhāya caraṇameva vā sampajaññassa visayabhāvato gocaro, tasmiṃ bhikkhācāragocare. So pana abhikkamādibhedabhinnanti visesanavasena vuttaṃ “abhikkamādīsu panā”ti. Kammaṭṭhānasaṅkhāteti yogakammassa bhāvanāya pavattiṭṭhānasaṅkhāte ārammaṇe, bhāvanākammeyeva [M 0.0182] vā, yogino sukhavisesahetutāya vā kammaṭṭhānasaṅkhāte sampajaññassa visayabhāvena gocare. Abhikkamādīsūti abhikkamapaṭikkamādīsu ceva cīvarapārupanādīsu ca. Asammuyhanaṃ cittakiriyāvāyodhātuvipphāravaseneva tesaṃ pavatti, na aññathāti yāthāvato jānanaṃ.

‘Alms-round’ (bhikkhācāra) is so called because one wanders (carīyati) for alms (bhikkhā) there; it is the place for wandering for alms, which is itself the resort (gocara). Alternatively, the mere wandering for alms is the resort of clear comprehension because it is its domain; in that resort of the alms-round. However, that it is divided into kinds such as going forward, etc., is stated by way of qualification as: ‘but in going forward, etc.’ In the object designated as a meditation subject, which is the place for the occurrence of the development of the yogi’s work; or in the work of development itself; or in what is designated as a meditation subject because it is a cause for the yogi’s special happiness, this being the resort as the domain of clear comprehension. ‘In going forward, etc.’ refers to going forward and returning, and also to putting on the robes, and so on. Non-bewilderment is knowing them as they really are: that their occurrence is due to the mind’s activity and the diffusion of the effort element, and not otherwise.

Kammaṭṭhānaṃ padhānaṃ katvāti cīvarapārupanādisarīrapariharaṇakiccakālepi kammaṭṭhānamanasikārameva padhānaṃ katvā.

‘Making the meditation subject the priority’ means that even during activities such as putting on robes and attending to bodily needs, one makes attention to the meditation subject the priority.

Tasmāti yasmā ussukkajāto hutvā ativiya maṃ yācasi, yasmā ca jīvitantarāyānaṃ dujjānataṃ vadasi, indriyāni ca te paripākaṃ gatāni, tasmā. Tihāti nipātamattaṃ. Te tayā. Evanti idāni vattabbākāraṃ vadati. Sikkhitabbanti adhisīlasikkhādīnaṃ tissannampi sikkhānaṃ vasena sikkhanaṃ kātabbaṃ. Yathā pana sikkhitabbaṃ, taṃ dassento “diṭṭhe diṭṭhamattaṃ bhavissatī”tiādimāha.

‘Therefore’ (tasmā): because you have become zealous and ask me excessively, because you speak of the difficulty of knowing the dangers to life, and because your faculties have matured, therefore. ‘Tiha’ is just a particle. ‘Te’ means ‘by you.’ ‘Evaṃ’ (thus) refers to the manner now to be stated. ‘Should be trained’: training should be undertaken in accordance with all three trainings, that is, the training in higher virtue, etc. Then, to show how one should train, he said: ‘In the seen, there will be only the seen,’ and so on.

Tattha diṭṭhe diṭṭhamattanti rūpāyatane cakkhuviññāṇena diṭṭhamattaṃ. Yathā hi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ rūpe rūpamattameva passati, na niccādisabhāvaṃ, evaṃ sesataṃdvārikaviññāṇehipi me ettha diṭṭhamattameva bhavissatīti sikkhitabbanti attho. Atha vā diṭṭhe diṭṭhaṃ nāma cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, rūpe rūpavijānananti attho. Mattāti pamāṇaṃ. Diṭṭhaṃ mattā etassāti diṭṭhamattaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇamattameva me cittaṃ bhavissatīti attho. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yathā āpāthagate rūpe cakkhuviññāṇaṃ na rajjati na dussati na muyhati, evaṃ rāgādivirahena cakkhuviññāṇamattameva me javanaṃ bhavissati, cakkhuviññāṇappamāṇeneva naṃ ṭhapessāmīti. Atha vā diṭṭhaṃ nāma cakkhuviññāṇena diṭṭharūpaṃ. Diṭṭhe diṭṭhaṃ nāma tattheva uppannaṃ sampaṭicchanasantīraṇavoṭṭhabbanasaṅkhātaṃ [V 0.0180] cittattayaṃ. Yathā taṃ na rajjati na dussati na muyhati, evaṃ āpāthagate rūpe teneva sampaṭicchanādippamāṇena javanaṃ uppādessāmi, nāssa taṃ pamāṇaṃ atikkamitvā rajjanādivasena uppajjituṃ dassāmīti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Esa nayo sutamutesu. Mutanti ca tadārammaṇaviññāṇehi saddhiṃ gandharasaphoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Viññāte viññātamattanti ettha pana viññātaṃ nāma manodvārāvajjanena viññātārammaṇaṃ, tasmiṃ viññāte. Viññātamattanti āvajjanappamāṇaṃ. Yathā āvajjanaṃ na rajjati na dussati na muyhati, evaṃ rajjanādivasena uppajjituṃ adatvā āvajjanappamāṇeneva cittaṃ ṭhapessāmīti ayamettha [M 0.0183] attho. Evañhi te bāhiya sikkhitabbanti evaṃ imāya paṭipadāya tayā bāhiya tissannaṃ sikkhānaṃ anupavattanavasena sikkhitabbaṃ. Iti bhagavā bāhiyassa saṃkhittarucitāya chahi viññāṇakāyehi saddhiṃ chaḷārammaṇabhedabhinnaṃ vipassanāvisayaṃ diṭṭhādīhi catūhi koṭṭhāsehi vibhajitvā tatthassa ñātatīraṇapariññaṃ dasseti.

Here, ‘in the seen, there will be only the seen’ means, in the form base, there will be only what is seen by eye-consciousness. The meaning of ‘you should train’ is this: just as eye-consciousness sees in a form only the form, not its nature as permanent and so on, so too for me, in regard to the remaining sense-door consciousnesses, there will be only the seen. Alternatively, ‘the seen’ in ‘in the seen’ is eye-consciousness, meaning the cognizing of form in a form. ‘Matta’ means measure. ‘It has the seen as its measure’ (diṭṭhamattaṃ) means ‘my mind will be just eye-consciousness.’ This is what is said: just as when a form comes into range, eye-consciousness is not impassioned, averse, or deluded, so too my impulsion will be just eye-consciousness, free from passion and so on; I will establish it at the measure of eye-consciousness. Alternatively, ‘the seen’ is the form seen by eye-consciousness. ‘The seen in the seen’ refers to the triad of cittas that arise right there, designated as receiving, investigating, and determining. The meaning to be understood here is this: just as these are not impassioned, averse, or deluded, so when a form comes into range, I will arouse impulsion only to the measure of that receiving and so on, not allowing it to exceed that measure and arise by way of passion and so on. This is the method for the heard and the sensed. ‘The sensed’ should be understood as the smell, taste, and tactile bases together with their registration consciousnesses. As to ‘in the cognized, there will be only the cognized’: here ‘the cognized’ is the object cognized by mind-door adverting. ‘Only the cognized’ means the measure of adverting. The meaning here is this: just as adverting is not impassioned, averse, or deluded, so, not allowing the mind to arise by way of passion and so on, I will establish it at the measure of adverting. ‘Thus, Bāhiya, you should train’: in this way, Bāhiya, by this practice, you should train by way of following the three trainings. Thus the Blessed One, on account of Bāhiya’s preference for brevity, having divided the domain of insight—which is differentiated by the distinction of the six sense objects together with the six bodies of consciousness—into four sections by means of ‘the seen’ and so on, showed him full understanding by knowing and investigating.

Kathaṃ? Ettha hi rūpāyatanaṃ passitabbaṭṭhena diṭṭhaṃ nāma, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ pana saddhiṃ taṃdvārikaviññāṇehi dassanaṭṭhena, tadubhayampi yathāpaccayaṃ pavattamānaṃ dhammamattameva, na ettha koci kattā vā kāretā vā. Yato taṃ hutvā abhāvaṭṭhena aniccaṃ, udayabbayapaṭipīḷanaṭṭhena dukkhaṃ, avasavattanaṭṭhena anattāti kuto tattha paṇḍitassa rajjanādīnaṃ okāsoti ayañhettha adhippāyo. Esa nayo sutādīsupi.

How so? Here, the form base is called ‘the seen’ in the sense of being what is to be seen, while eye-consciousness, together with the consciousnesses of that door, is so in the sense of seeing. Both of these, occurring in accordance with conditions, are mere phenomena; there is no doer or instigator here. Since it is impermanent in the sense of non-existence after having been, suffering in the sense of oppression by arising and vanishing, and not-self in the sense of not being subject to control, where is the opportunity there for a wise person’s passion and so on? This is the intention here. This is the method for the heard and so on as well.

Idāni ñātatīraṇapariññāsu patiṭṭhitassa upari saha phalena pahānapariññaṃ dassetuṃ “yato kho te bāhiyā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha yatoti yadā, yasmā vā. Teti tava. Tatoti tadā, tasmā vā. Tenāti tena diṭṭhādinā, diṭṭhādipaṭibaddhena vā rāgādinā. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – bāhiya, tava yasmiṃ kāle, yena vā kāraṇena diṭṭhādīsu mayā vuttavidhiṃ paṭipajjantassa aviparītasabhāvāvabodhena diṭṭhādimattaṃ bhavissati, tasmiṃ kāle, tena vā kāraṇena tvaṃ tena diṭṭhādipaṭibaddhena rāgādinā saha na bhavissasi, ratto vā duṭṭho vā mūḷho vā na bhavissasi pahīnarāgādikattā, tena vā diṭṭhādinā saha paṭibaddho na bhavissasīti. Tato tvaṃ, bāhiya, na tatthāti yadā, yasmā vā tvaṃ tena rāgena vā ratto, dosena vā duṭṭho, mohena vā mūḷho na bhavissasi, tadā, tasmā vā tvaṃ tattha diṭṭhādike na bhavissasi, tasmiṃ diṭṭhe vā sutamutaviññāte vā “etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā”ti (mahāva. 21) taṇhāmānadiṭṭhīhi allīno patiṭṭhito [V 0.0181] na bhavissasi. Ettāvatā pahānapariññaṃ matthakaṃ pāpetvā khīṇāsavabhūmi dassitā. Tato tvaṃ, bāhiya, nevidha, na huraṃ, na ubhayamantarenāti yadā tvaṃ, bāhiya, tena rāgādinā tattha diṭṭhādīsu paṭibaddho na bhavissasi, tadā tvaṃ neva idha loke, na paraloke, na ubhayattha hosi. Esevanto dukkhassāti kilesadukkhassa, vaṭṭadukkhassa ca ayameva anto ayaṃ paricchedo parivaṭumabhāvoti ayameva hi ettha attho[M 0.0184]. Ye pana “ubhayamantarenā”ti padaṃ gahetvā antarābhavaṃ nāma icchanti, tesaṃ taṃ micchā. Tattha yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ parato antarābhavakathāyaṃ (kathā. 505 ādayo ) āvi bhavissati.

Now, to show the full understanding by abandoning together with its fruit, which is above what is established in the full understanding by knowing and investigating, the passage beginning ‘When, Bāhiya…’ is stated. Herein, ‘when’ (yato) means when, or because. ‘For you’ (te) means of you. ‘Then’ (tato) means then, or therefore. ‘By that’ (tena) means by that seen, etc., or by the passion, etc., connected with the seen, etc. This is what is said: Bāhiya, at the time when, or for the reason that, for you who practice according to the method I have described regarding the seen, etc., there will be, with an understanding of their true nature without distortion, only the seen, etc.—at that time, or for that reason, you will not be with the passion, etc., connected with the seen, etc. You will not be impassioned, averse, or deluded, because passion, etc., has been abandoned; or, you will not be bound to that seen, etc. ‘Then, Bāhiya, you will not be “there”’: when, or because, you are not impassioned with passion, averse with hate, or deluded with delusion, then, or therefore, you will not be ‘in’ the seen, etc. You will not be attached to or established in the seen, heard, sensed, or cognized with craving, conceit, or views, thinking, ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self.’ Hereby, having brought the full understanding by abandoning to its culmination, the state of one whose taints are destroyed is shown. ‘Then, Bāhiya, you will be neither here, nor beyond, nor in between’: when, Bāhiya, you are not bound by passion, etc., to the seen, etc., then you will be neither in this world, nor in the next world, nor in both. ‘This is the end of suffering’: this is the end, the termination, the non-recurrence of the suffering of the defilements and the suffering of the round—this is the meaning here. But those who take the phrase ‘nor in between’ to posit an intermediate existence are mistaken. What should be said about that will become clear later in the discussion on the intermediate existence.

Etesanti atiharaṇavītiharaṇānaṃ.

‘Of these’: of carrying over and carrying away.

“Tattha hī”tiādinā pañcaviññāṇavīthiyaṃ puretaraṃ pavattaayonisomanasikāravasena āvajjanādīnaṃ ayoniso āvajjanādinā iṭṭhādiārammaṇe lobhādippavattimattaṃ hoti, na pana itthipurisādivikappagāho, manodvāreyeva pana so hotīti dasseti. Tassāti “itthī, puriso”ti rajjanādikassa. Bhavaṅgādīti bhavaṅgaāvajjanadassanāni, sampaṭicchanasantīraṇavoṭṭhabbanapañcadvārikajavanañca. Apubbatittaratāvasenāti apubbatāittarabhāvānaṃ vasena.

By the words ‘For there,’ etc., he shows that in the five-door cognitive process, through the influence of prior unwise attention, adverting and other states arise unskillfully. Towards desirable and other objects, there is merely an occurrence of greed and similar states, but not the grasping of concepts such as ‘woman’ or ‘man’; for that occurs only at the mind-door. ‘Of that’ refers to passion and other states arising from ‘woman,’ ‘man,’ and so on. ‘Bhavaṅga and so on’ includes bhavaṅga, adverting, seeing, receiving, investigating, determining, and the five-door impulsion. ‘By way of being unprecedented and successive’ means by way of the state of being unprecedented and successive.

Atiharatīti mukhadvāraṃ atikkamitvā harati. Taṃtaṃvijānananipphādakoti tassa tassa pariyesanādivisayassa, vijānanassa ca nipphādako. Yena hi payogena pariyesanādi nipphajjati, so tabbisayaṃ vijānanampi nipphādeti nāma hoti. Sammāpaṭipattinti dhammesu aviparītapaṭipattiṃ yathābhūtāvabodhaṃ.

‘He carries over’ means he carries it having passed beyond the mouth-door. ‘Producer of the knowledge of this and that’ means it is the producer of knowledge regarding that very object of search, etc. For by whatever effort the search, etc., is accomplished, that same effort is also said to produce knowledge concerning that object. ‘Right practice’ means non-perverted practice in regard to phenomena, that is, understanding things as they really are.

Gamanepīti gamanapayogepi. Atiharaṇaṃ yathāṭhitasseva kāyassa icchitadesābhimukhakaraṇaṃ. Gamanaṃ desantaruppatti. Vakkhamānoti “abhikkante paṭikkanteti…pe… addhāgamanavasena kathito. Gate ṭhite nisinneti ettha vihāre cuṇṇikapāduddhārairiyāpathavasena kathito”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 523) vakkhamāno viseso.

‘In going also’ means ‘in the effort of going also.’ ‘Carrying over’ is the turning of the body, just as it is, towards a desired place. ‘Going’ is arriving in another place. The distinction to be explained is this: ‘In “going forward, in going back”... it is spoken of by way of actual travel. Regarding “gone, stood, sat,” here in the monastery, it is spoken of by way of the postures, such as the posture of lifting a dusty foot.’

Pavatteti caṅkamādīsu pavatte rūpārūpadhamme. Pariggaṇhantassa aniccādito.

‘That occur’: the material and immaterial phenomena that occur in walking back and forth, etc. ‘Of one who comprehends’: from the standpoint of impermanence, etc.

Kāyikakiriyādinibbattakajavanaṃ [V 0.0182] phalūpacārena “kāyādikiriyāmaya”nti vuttaṃ. Kiriyāsamuṭṭhitattāti pana kāraṇūpacārena.

The impulsion that produces bodily action, etc., is called ‘consisting of bodily action, etc.’ by a figurative use based on the effect. However, the phrase ‘because it originates from action’ is by a figurative use based on the cause.

526. Kammaṭṭhānaupāsanassāti kammaṭṭhānabhāvanāya. Yogapathanti bhāvanāyoggakiriyāya pavattanamaggaṃ.

526. ‘Of the cultivation of a meditation subject’ means by the development of a meditation subject. ‘The path of practice’ means the path of proceeding in the activity suitable for development.

537. Kāyādīsūti kāyavedanācittadhammesu. Suṭṭhu pavattiyāti asubhānupassanādivasena pavattiyā. Niyyānasabhāvo sammāsatitā eva[M 0.0185]. Upaṭṭhānanti satiṃ kiccato dasseti. Ettha ca yathāvutto pariggaho jāto etissāti pariggahitā, taṃ pariggahitaṃ niyyānabhūtaṃ satiṃ katvāti attho veditabbo.

537. 'In regard to the body, etc.' means in regard to the body, feelings, mind, and mental phenomena. 'Properly proceeding' means proceeding by way of contemplation of the unattractive, etc. 'The nature of liberation' is simply right mindfulness. 'Establishment' shows mindfulness in terms of its function. Here, 'comprehended' (pariggahitā) means that the aforesaid comprehension has arisen for this mindfulness. The meaning should be understood as: 'having made that comprehended mindfulness, which is the means of liberation….'

542-3. Pakuppanaṃ idha vikārāpattibhāvo.

Here, agitation is the state of undergoing alteration.

550. Tappaṭipakkhasaññāti thinamiddhapaṭipakkhasaññā. Sā atthato tadaṅgādivasena thinamiddhavinodanākārappavattā kusalavitakkasampayuttasaññā, tathābhūto vā cittuppādo saññāsīsena vuttoti veditabbo.

550. 'The opposing perception' means the perception that is the counterpart to sloth and torpor. In meaning, this is a perception associated with wholesome thoughts, which functions to dispel sloth and torpor by way of suppression by the opposite, etc.; or it should be understood as a mental state of such a kind, spoken of with perception as its head.

553. Sārambhanti ārambhavantaṃ, sahārambhanti attho. Nirāvaraṇābhogā thinamiddhandhakāravigamena nirāvaraṇasamannāhārasaññā. Vivaṭā appaṭicchādanā.

553. 'With effort' (sārambhaṃ) means possessing effort (ārambhavantaṃ); the meaning is 'together with effort' (sahārambhaṃ). 'Unobstructed attention' (nirāvaraṇābhogā) is the perception of unobstructed advertence due to the removal of the darkness of sloth and torpor. 'Open' (vivaṭā) means unconcealed (appaṭicchādanā).

564. Tattha tatthāti “iminā pātimokkhasaṃvarena upeto hotī”tiādīsu (vibha. 511).

564. 'Here and there' means in such passages as: "He is endowed with this restraint of the Pātimokkha," etc. (Vibh 511).

588. Yathā kenaci nikkujjitaṃ “idaṃ nāmeta”nti pakatiñāṇena na ñāyati, evaṃ sabbappakārena aviditaṃ nikkujjitaṃ viya hotīti āha “sabbathā aññātatā nikkujjitabhāvo”ti. Niravasesaparicchindanābhāvoti duviññeyyatāya niravasesato paricchinditabbatābhāvo, paricchindikābhāvo vā. Ekadeseneva hi gambhīraṃ ñāyati.

588. Just as something that has been overturned is not recognized by ordinary knowledge as 'this so-and-so,' so it is as if unknown in every way, like something overturned. Thus it is said: 'The state of being overturned is being altogether unknown.' 'Absence of complete delimitation' means the impossibility of being completely delimited on account of its being difficult to understand, or the absence of one who delimits. For the profound is known only in part.

Ācikkhantītiādito [V 0.0183] paribyattaṃ kathenti. Desentīti upadisanavasena vadanti, pabodhenti vā. Paññāpentīti pajānāpenti, saṃpakāsentīti attho. Paṭṭhapentīti pakārehi asaṅkarato ṭhapenti. Vivarantīti vivaṭaṃ karonti. Vibhajantīti vibhattaṃ karonti. Uttānīkarontīti anuttānaṃ gambhīraṃ uttānaṃ pākaṭaṃ karonti. Ettha ca “paññāpentī”tiādīhi chahi padehi atthapadāni dassitāni. “Ācikkhanti desentī”ti pana dvīhi padehi byañjanapadānīti evaṃ atthabyañjanapadasampannāya uḷārāya pasaṃsāya pasaṃsanaṃ dasseti. Yaṃ panetesu atthabyañjanapadesu vattabbaṃ, taṃ nettiaṭṭhakathāyaṃ (netti. aṭṭha. 23 ādayo) vitthārato vuttameva, tasmā tattha vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

'They explain' (ācikkhanti) means they speak in a well-expressed way from the beginning. 'They teach' (desenti) means they speak by way of pointing out, or they awaken. 'They make known' (paññāpenti) means they cause to understand; the meaning is they illuminate. 'They establish' (paṭṭhapenti) means they set forth in different ways without confusion. 'They open up' (vivaranti) means they make open. 'They analyze' (vibhajanti) means they make distinct. 'They make plain' (uttānīkaronti) means they make what is not plain, what is profound, plain and manifest. Here, with the six terms beginning with 'they make known,' the terms of meaning are shown. But with the two terms 'they explain' and 'they teach,' the terms of phrasing are shown. Thus it shows praise with sublime praise endowed with terms of meaning and terms of phrasing. As to what should be said about these terms of meaning and phrasing, that has already been stated in detail in the Commentary to the Nettipakaraṇa (Netti-aṭṭh. 23ff.); therefore, it should be understood in accordance with the method stated there.

602. Ettheva [M 0.0186] yojetabbaṃ tassa heṭṭhābhūmisamatikkamanamukhena bhūmivisesādhigamupāyadīpanato. Sabbatthāpīti “rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkammā”ti sabbesupi samatikkamavacanesu.

602. It should be connected right here, because it illuminates the means of attaining a special stage by way of transcending the stage below. 'In all cases too' means in all statements of transcending, such as 'with the complete transcendence of perceptions of form…' and 'by transcending the base of the infinity of space…'

610. Taṃyeva ākāsaṃ phuṭaṃ viññāṇanti taṃyeva kasiṇugghāṭimākāsaṃ “ananta”nti manasikārena phuṭaṃ pharitvā ṭhitaṃ paṭhamāruppaviññāṇaṃ “anantaṃ viññāṇa”nti manasi karotīti attho. Dutiyavikappe pana sāmaññajotanā visese tiṭṭhatīti “phuṭa”nti iminā viññāṇameva vuttanti phuṭaṃ viññāṇanti paṭhamāruppaviññāṇamāha. Tañhi ākāsassa sapharaṇakaviññāṇaṃ. Viññāṇenāti ca karaṇatthe karaṇavacanaṃ, tañca dutiyāruppaviññāṇaṃ vadatīti āha “viññāṇañcāyatanaviññāṇena manasi karotī”ti. Tenāti paṭhamāruppaviññāṇena. Gahitākāranti anantapharaṇavasena gahitākāraṃ. Manasi karotīti dutiyāruppaparikammamanasikārena manasi karoti. Evanti yathāvuttākāraṃ kasiṇugghāṭimākāse paṭhamāruppaviññāṇena anantapharaṇavasena yo gahitākāro, taṃ manasi karontaṃyeva. Taṃ viññāṇanti taṃ dutiyāruppaviññāṇaṃ. Anantaṃ pharatīti “ananta”nti pharati, tasmā dutiyoyevattho yuttoti. “Yañhī”tiādinā yathāvuttamatthaṃ pākaṭaṃ karoti. Taṃpharaṇākārasahitanti tasmiṃ ākāse pharaṇākārasahitaṃ. Viññāṇanti paṭhamāruppaviññāṇaṃ.

610. 'That very space pervaded by consciousness': The meaning is that one attends to the first formless consciousness—which stands having pervaded that very 'removed-kasiṇa space' with the attention 'infinite'—by attending to it as 'infinite consciousness.' In the second alternative, however, since a general indication can stand for the specific, by 'pervaded' consciousness alone is meant; thus 'pervaded consciousness' refers to the first formless consciousness. For that is the consciousness that pervades space. And 'by consciousness' is the instrumental case in the sense of instrument, and it refers to the second formless consciousness; thus he says: 'one attends with the consciousness of the base of the infinity of consciousness.' 'By that' means by the first formless consciousness. 'The aspect grasped' means the aspect grasped by way of infinite pervasion. 'One attends' means one attends with the preliminary attention for the second formless attainment. 'Thus' refers to one attending to that very aspect that was grasped by the first formless consciousness by way of infinite pervasion in the 'removed-kasiṇa space.' 'That consciousness' means that second formless consciousness. 'It pervades infinitely' means it pervades as 'infinite'; therefore, the second meaning is indeed appropriate. By the passage beginning 'For what…' he clarifies the aforesaid meaning. 'Accompanied by the mode of pervading it' means accompanied by the mode of pervading in that space. 'Consciousness' means the first formless consciousness.

615. Pubbeti dutiyāruppaparikammakāle. Yaṃ “anantaṃ viññāṇa”nti manasi kataṃ, taṃyeva [V 0.0184] paṭhamāruppaviññāṇameva. Taṃyeva hi abhāveti. Ārammaṇātikkamavasena hi etā samāpattiyo laddhabbāti.

615. 'Previously' means at the time of the preliminary work for the second formless attainment. What was attended to as 'infinite consciousness' is precisely the first formless consciousness itself. For one develops that very thing. For these attainments are to be obtained by way of transcending their object.

Niddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The exposition of the Niddesa is finished.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The exposition of the Suttanta Analysis is finished.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Abhidhamma Division

623. Catukkanaye dutiyajjhānameva yesaṃ vicāro oḷārikato na upaṭṭhāti, yesañca upaṭṭhāti, tesaṃ vasena dvidhā bhinditvā desitanti [M 0.0187] catukkanayato pañcakanayo nīhatoti āha “uddhaṭānaṃyeva catunnaṃ…pe… dassanato cā”ti.

623. In the fourfold method, the second jhāna is divided into two based on whether or not investigation appears as a coarse factor. Thus the fivefold method is derived from the fourfold method. Hence it is said: 'Because of the extraction of the four... and of the views.'

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Abhidhamma Division is finished.

3. Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Interrogation

640. Tīsūti paṭhamādīsu tīsu. Catukkanayena hi taṃ vuttaṃ. Evaṃkoṭṭhāsikāti appamāṇāti vuttā. Tenāha “lokuttarabhūtā evāti adhippāyo”ti. Paricchinnākāsa…pe… catutthānaṃ vaṭṭavipassanāpādakattā “sabbatthapādakacatutthe saṅgahitānī”ti vuttaṃ.

640. 'In three' means in the first three, for this was stated according to the fourfold method. 'Thus in parts' means 'immeasurable.' Hence it is said: 'The meaning is that they are exclusively supramundane.' 'Limited space... [and so on]... of the fourth': because the fourth is the basis for insight into the round of existence, it is said: 'They are included in the fourth, which is the basis for everything.'

Ayaṃ kathāti parittārammaṇādikathā. Heṭṭhimo ariyo uparimassa ariyassa lokuttaracittāni paṭivijjhituṃ na sakkotīti vuttaṃ “na ca…pe… sakkotī”ti.

'This talk' means the talk on such topics as limited objects. It is said that a lower noble one cannot penetrate the supramundane consciousnesses of a higher noble one: 'Nor... can he penetrate.'

“Kiriyato dvādasanna”nti ca pāṭho atthi. Saha vadati lokuttaraphalacatutthatāsāmaññenāti [V 0.0185] adhippāyo. Idha sabbasaddassa padesasabbavācibhāvato ekadesassa asambhavepi sabbatthapādakatā eva veditabbāti dassetuṃ “sabbattha…pe… daṭṭhabba”nti āha. Paricchinnākāsakasiṇacatutthādīnīti ādi-saddena ānāpānacatutthādayo saṅgahitā. Navattabbatāyāti navattabbārammaṇatāya.

There is also the reading: 'Functionally, of the twelve.' The meaning is that it speaks in connection with the commonality of the fourth supramundane fruition. Here, to show that even when a part is impossible because the word 'all' refers to a limited 'all,' it should be understood simply as being the basis for everything, it is said: 'Everywhere... should be seen.' 'The fourth [jhāna] on the limited space kasiṇa, etc.': by the word 'etc.,' the fourth [jhāna] on breathing and so on are included. 'Because of unutterability' means because its object is unutterable.

Nibbānañcāti vattabbaṃ tadārammaṇassāpi bahiddhārammaṇabhāvato.

'And Nibbāna' should be stated, because even that which has it as object has an external object.

“Sasantānagatampī”ti idaṃ rūpa-saddena, kamma-saddena ca sambandhitabbaṃ “sasantānagatampi apākaṭaṃ rūpaṃ dibbacakkhu viya sasantānagatampi apākaṭaṃ kammaṃ vibhāvetī”ti. Pākaṭe pana sasantānagate rūpe, kamme ca abhiññāñāṇena payojanaṃ natthīti “apākaṭa”nti visesetvā vuttaṃ.

'Even what has occurred in one's own continuity': this should be connected with the words 'matter' and 'kamma' thus: 'It clarifies unmanifest matter that has occurred in one's own continuity, just as the divine eye does; and it clarifies unmanifest kamma that has occurred in one's own continuity.' But in regard to manifest matter and kamma that have occurred in one's own continuity, there is no need for the knowledge of direct knowing; hence it is specified by the word 'unmanifest.'

Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Interrogation is finished.

Jhānavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of Jhāna is finished.

13. Appamaññāvibhaṅgo

13. Analysis of the Immeasurables

1. Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Suttanta Division

642. Disādesodhināti [M 0.0188][V 0.0186] “ekaṃ disa”ntiādidisodhinā, vihāragāmanigamanagarajanapadarajjādidesodhinā ca. Sattodhināti “sabbā itthiyo, sabbe purisā, ariyā, anariyā”tiādivasappavattena sattodhinā. Etassāti etassa padassa, padatthassa vā. Anuvattakanti adhikāravasena pavattakaṃ. Taṃ dvayanti tathā-saddo, iti-saddoti ubhayaṃ. “Tathā dutiya”nti hi vutte “tathā-saddo yathā mettāsahagatena cetasā puratthimādīsu ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyampi disaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā pharitvā viharatī”ti imamatthaṃ dīpeti. Sesadvayepi eseva nayo. Yasmā itīti ayaṃ iti-saddo pakāratthe, evanti vuttaṃ hoti, tasmā “yathā mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ, dutiyaṃ, tatiyaṃ, catutthaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, evaṃ uddhaṃ, adho, tiriyaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā pharitvā viharatī”ti imamatthaṃ dīpeti. Tena vuttaṃ “mettā…pe… taṃ dvaya”nti. Tassāti dvayassa. Pharaṇantarādiṭṭhānanti pharaṇato aññaṃ pharaṇantaraṃ, taṃ ādi yassa, taṃ pharaṇantarādi. Pharaṇantarañhetaṃ mettābhāvanāya, yadidaṃ vipulatā. Ādi-saddena bhummantarapaguṇabhāvādi gayhati, tassa pharaṇantarādino ṭhānaṃ ṭhānabhūto “vipulenā”tiādinā vuccamāno mettābhāvanāviseso. Vuttappakāramattaparāmasanassa tassa dvayassa aṭṭhānaṃ anokāsoti. Iti katvā iminā kāraṇena na vuttaṃ taṃ dvayanti attho.

642. 'By specifying the directions' means by specifying directions such as 'one direction,' etc., and by specifying locations such as monasteries, villages, towns, cities, countries, and kingdoms. 'By specifying beings' means by specifying beings according to the classification that has begun, such as 'all women, all men, noble ones, non-noble ones,' etc. 'Of this' means of this word or of the meaning of the word. 'Consequent' means proceeding by way of the governing principle. 'That pair' means both the word 'tathā' and the word 'iti.' For when it is said, 'so a second,' this explains the meaning: 'The word "tathā" (so) means that just as one dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, so too one dwells pervading a second direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness.' The same method applies to the remaining two. Since this word 'iti' is in the sense of manner—meaning 'thus'—it explains the meaning: 'Just as one dwells pervading the first, second, third, and fourth directions with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, thus one dwells pervading above, below, and across with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness.' Hence it is said: 'loving-kindness... that pair.' 'Of that' means of the pair. 'The basis for another pervasion, etc.': another pervasion is a pervasion other than a previous one. That which has this as its beginning is 'another pervasion, etc.' For this vastness is another pervasion in the development of loving-kindness. By the word 'etc.', another plane, proficiency, and so on are included. The basis of that which has another pervasion, etc., as its beginning is the special quality of the development of loving-kindness called 'with vastness,' etc., which is its ground. It is not the place, not the occasion for that pair to refer merely to the manner stated. Therefore, for this reason, that pair is not stated; this is the meaning.

643. Rāgassāti kāmarāgassa. Sinehassāti puttasinehādisinehassa. Vipattiyāti rāgasinehasaṅkhātāya mettābhāvanāya vipattiyā vināsassa. Anuppattito hirottappabalena anuppajjanato.

643. 'Of lust' means of sensual lust. 'Of affection' means of affection such as for a son. 'Of failure' means of the destruction of the development of loving-kindness, which is the failure designated as lust and affection. 'From non-occurrence' means from not arising due to the power of moral shame and moral dread.

645. Adhimuñcitvāti [V 0.0187] bhāvanācittaṃ ārammaṇe suṭṭhu vissajjetvā, taṃ panettha adhimuccanaṃ yasmā pharaṇavaseneva hoti, tasmā vuttaṃ “suṭṭhu pasāretvā”ti. Yasmā pana ārammaṇe suṭṭhu asaṃsappanavaseneva taṃ mettābhāvanāya adhimuccanaṃ hoti, tasmā “balavatā vā adhimokkhena adhimuccitvā”ti ca vuttaṃ.

645. 'Having resolved' means having well released the mind of development upon its object. Since this resolving here occurs by way of pervading, it is therefore said: 'having well spread out.' But since that resolving in the development of loving-kindness occurs by way of not straying from the object, it is also said: 'or having resolved with strong conviction.'

648. Etesaṃ [M 0.0189] padānaṃ sabbena sakalena disādesādibhedena avadhinā. Sabbāvadhidisādipharaṇākārehīti sabbāvadhibhūtadisādesapuggalapharaṇappakārehi.

648. Of these terms: by the whole, entire specification of the division of directions, locations, etc. 'By the modes of pervading all specifications, directions, etc.' means by the modes of pervading directions, locations, and persons that constitute the entire specification.

650. Vighātavasenāti vikkhambhanavasena.

650. 'By way of removal' means by way of suppression.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Suttanta Division is finished.

3. Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Questions

699. Kathitānaṃ kusalādidhammānaṃ. Imasmiṃ pana appamaññāvibhaṅge kathitā appamaññā, tā ca sabhāvato lokiyā eva, na khandhavibhaṅgādīsu kathitā khandhādayo viya lokuttarāpīti ekaṃsato sabbāsaṃ appamaññānaṃ lokiyabhāvameva dīpetuṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “imasmiṃ panā”tiādi vuttanti imamatthaṃ dassento āha “imasmiṃ pana…pe… hotī”ti.

699. Of the wholesome and other states that have been discussed. But in this Analysis of the Immeasurables, the immeasurables that are discussed are by nature only mundane, not also supramundane like the aggregates and so on discussed in the Analysis of the Aggregates. To show decisively that all the immeasurables are exclusively mundane, it is said in the commentary: 'But in this...' etc. Showing this meaning, he says: 'But in this... (and so on)... is.'

Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Questions is finished.

Appamaññāvibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Boundless States is finished.

14. Sikkhāpadavibhaṅgo

14. The Exposition of the Training Rules

1. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Abhidhamma Section

703. Sikkhāsaṅkhātānaṃ [M 0.0190][V 0.0188] kusaladhammānaṃ pañca sīlaṅgāni nissayabhāvena vā patiṭṭhā siyuṃ, upanissayabhāvena vāti tadubhayaṃ dassento āha “sampayogavasena, upanissayavasena ca okāsabhāvenā”ti.

703. The five precepts, which are wholesome states designated as training, may serve as a foundation by way of support or by way of decisive support. To show both, it is said: 'by way of association and by way of decisive support as a basis.'

704. “Kammapathā evā”ti niyamassa katattā vuttaṃ “asabbasādhāraṇesū”ti. Na hi sakkā indriyādisādhāraṇakoṭṭhāsavasena niyamaṃ kātuṃ. Kammapathakoṭṭhāsikā eva, na jhānādikoṭṭhāsikā. Kammapathabhāvena āgatanti vadanti, duggatiyā, tattha uppajjanadukkhassa ca pavattiupāyabhāvatoti adhippāyo. Assa surāpānassa. Upakārakattaṃ sabbesaṃ. Sabhāgattaṃ micchācārassa.

704. Because the rule 'only courses of action' was made, it was said, 'in what is not common to all.' For it is not possible to make a rule based on the division common to faculties and so on. They belong only to the division of courses of action, not to the division of jhāna and so on. They say it comes in the sense of a course of action; the meaning is because it is the means for the occurrence of suffering that arises in a bad destination. Of this liquor drinking. Being an accessory to all. Shared nature with sexual misconduct.

Tathāgahitasaṅkhārārammaṇatāyāti “sattaṃ avaharāmi, satte vippaṭipajjāmī”tiādinā sattākārena gahitasaṅkhārārammaṇatāya, na pana sattapaññattiārammaṇatāyāti adhippāyo. “Pañca sikkhāpadā”tiādinā tamevatthaṃ vivarati.

'By the state of having formations grasped thus as its object' means by having as object formations grasped in the mode of a being—as in 'I take from a being,' 'I transgress against beings'—and not, it is meant, by having the concept of a being as object. He explains this same meaning with 'The five training rules,' and so on.

Tassa tassāti yassa yassa byasanatthāya. Sayaṃ vā usuādiṃ khipati, opātakhaṇanādiṃ karoti, tādisaṃ mantaṃ parijappati, kammajaiddhiṃ vaḷañjeti, aññena vā taṃ sabbaṃ kāretīti āha “nissaggiya…pe… dve eva gahitā”ti.

'For this or that' means for whomever's misfortune. Either he himself throws an arrow or the like, digs a pitfall or the like, recites such a spell, employs power born of kamma, or has another do all that—thus it is said: '...entailing forfeiture... (and so on)... only two are taken.'

Yadipi [V 0.0189] koṭṭhāsavāre virati sarūpena nāgatā “yevāpanā”tveva vuttā, bhajāpiyamānā pana maggabhāvaṃyeva bhajatīti āha “viratisīlaṃ pana maggakoṭṭhāsika”nti. Sesasīlānanti sesaavītikkantasīlānaṃ.

Although in the section on divisions, abstinence does not appear in its own form but is spoken of only by the general term `yevāpanā`, when analyzed it partakes of the very nature of the path. Therefore it is said: 'But the virtue of abstinence is a component of the path.' 'Of the remaining virtues' means of the remaining virtues of non-transgression.

712. Abhabbaṭṭhānāti pāṇātipātādayo. Yathā pāṇātipātādayo verahetutāya veraṃ, evaṃ tadaññepi akusalāti vuttaṃ “taṃsabhāgatāya verabhūtāna”nti. Viratīnaṃ uppatti na na bhavissati sekkhānanti yojanā. “Akusalasamuṭṭhitāni cā”tiādināpi sekkhānaṃ ubhayena viratisabbhāvaṃyeva vibhāveti. Tassattho – yāni akusalasamuṭṭhitāni kāyakammādīni, tāni tesaṃ sekkhānaṃ kāyaduccaritādīnīti verāniyeva[M 0.0191], tehi verehi tesaṃ sekkhānaṃ viratiyo sambhavantiyeva. Yatoti yasmā pāṇātipātādiviramitabbanippariyāyaverābhāvepi kāyaduccaritādiveramattato sekkhānaṃ viratisambhavato. Naphalabhūtassāpīti yathā phalassa maggapaṭibimbabhūtattā maggasadisaṃ sattaaṭṭhaṅgikatā siyā, evaṃ aphalabhūtassāpi sakadāgāmimaggādikassa yato viratisambhavato aṭṭhaṅgikatā hoti, aññathā pañcaṅgiko eva siyāti adhippāyo.

712. 'Impossible actions' refers to killing living beings and so on. Just as killing and other such actions are enmity because they are a cause of enmity, so too are other unwholesome states; thus it is said: 'of things that have become enmity due to having a similar nature.' The construction is: 'The arising of abstinences will not fail to occur for trainees.' By 'And those arisen from the unwholesome,' etc., he clarifies that trainees possess abstinence in both ways. The meaning is this: those bodily actions, etc., that have arisen from the unwholesome are themselves enmities for those trainees in the form of bodily misconduct, etc., and from those enmities the abstinences of those trainees certainly arise. This is because the abstinence of trainees is possible merely from the enmity of bodily misconduct, etc., even in the absence of the enmity that is a synonym for the specific things to be abstained from, such as killing. 'Of that which has not become the fruit': just as the fruit, being a reflection of the path, can have seven or eight factors like the path, so too a path that has not yet reached its fruit, such as the path of the once-returner, has eight factors because abstinence is possible for it. Otherwise, the meaning is, it would have only five factors.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Abhidhamma Section is finished.

2. Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Questions

714. Yathāviramitabbatoti yo yo pāṇātipātādi viramitabbo, tato virativasena.

714. 'As to how one should abstain' means by way of abstaining from whatever killing of living beings and so forth is to be abstained from.

Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Questions is finished.

Sikkhāpadavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of the Training Rules is finished.

15. Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅgo

15. The Analysis of the Discriminations

1. Suttantabhājanīyaṃ

1. The Sutta Section

1. Saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Summary Section

718. “Eseva [M 0.0192][V 0.0190] nayo”ti dhammādīsu kato atideso saṅkhepato tesaṃ dassanaṃ hotīti āha “saṅkhepena dassetvā”ti. Tesaṃ niruttipaṭibhānānaṃ visayā tabbisayā, tesaṃ, niruttipaṭibhānavisayabhūtānanti attho. Paccayuppannādibhedehīti paccayuppannanibbānabhāsitatthādibhedehi.

718. 'This is the method': this extension of the rule made in regard to the dhammas, etc., is a way of showing them in brief; hence he says, 'having shown in brief.' 'Their subjects' means the subjects of the discriminations of language and perspicuity; the meaning is 'of those things that have become the subjects of the discriminations of language and perspicuity.' 'By the divisions of the presently arisen, etc.' means by the divisions such as the presently arisen, Nibbāna, the spoken, the meaning, etc.

Dukkhahetuphalajātādidhammajarāmaraṇāni dukkhādīni. Saccahetudhammapaccayākāravāresu dukkhasamudayādipariyāyena āgato phalanibbattako hetu, saccapaccayākāravāresu ariyamaggo, pariyattivāre bhāsitaṃ, abhidhammabhājanīye kusalaṃ, akusalanti evaṃ pāḷiyaṃ vuttānaṃyeva vasena pañca dhammā veditabbāti imamatthamāha “tathā dhammā cā”ti iminā.

Birth, aging, death, and so on, which are dhammas born as the fruit of the cause of suffering, are instances of suffering, and so on. In the sections on the modes of conditions for the dhammas that are causes of the truths, the cause that produces the fruit is what comes under the heading 'the origin of suffering,' etc. In the sections on the modes of conditions for the truths, it is the noble path. In the section on the scriptures, it is the spoken word. In the Abhidhamma section, it is the wholesome and the unwholesome. He indicates the meaning that five dhammas are to be understood in this way, according to what is said in the Pāli text, with the words 'and the dhammas thus'.

Nibbattakahetuādīnanti nibbattakasampāpakañāpakānaṃ. Purimoti pavattanattho. Tasminti magge. Pacchimoti pāpanattho daṭṭhabbo.

‘Of the producing cause, etc.’ means of the producing, accomplishing, and indicating causes. ‘Former’ has the meaning of initiating. In that path. ‘Latter’ should be understood as having the meaning of causing attainment.

Aviparītaniruttīti buddhādīhi āciṇṇā tassa tassa atthassa vācakabhāve niruḷhā yāthāvanirutti. Yasmā viññattivikārasahito saddo paññattīti attano adhippāyo, tasmā paramatato taṃ dassento “avacanabhūtāyā”ti visesetvā “keci vaṇṇayantī”ti āha. Evaṃ satīti [V 0.0191] evaṃ niruttiyā paññattibhāve sati. Paññatti abhilapitabbāti āpajjatīti vutte, hotu, ko doso tassā vacanīyabhāvatoti kadāci vadeyyāti āsaṅkanto āha “na ca vacanato…pe… uccāretabbaṃ atthī”ti. Tesaṃ atthadhammānaṃ. Na vacananti avacanaṃ avacanasabhāvaṃ. Evaṃpakāranti evaṃvidhaṃ evaṃ niyataliṅgavisesajotanākāraṃ.

'Unperverted language' means correct language, practiced by the Buddhas and others, established in its function of denoting the meaning of this or that thing. Since his own opinion is that sound accompanied by modifications of expression is a concept, he therefore presents another's view, qualifying it with 'of that which has become speech' and saying, 'some explain it thus.' 'This being so' means: when language is a concept. When it is said, 'It follows that a concept must be expressible,' anticipating that one might say, 'Let it be so, what is the fault in its being expressible?', he says, 'And it is not from speech... (and so on)... there is a need to utter.' 'Of those meanings and things.' 'Not speech' means non-speech, the nature of non-speech. 'Of such a kind' means of this sort, of a kind that illuminates a specific, fixed characteristic.

Paratoti [M 0.0193] parabhāge anantaramanodvāre. Saddaggahaṇānusārena gahitāya nāmaniruttiyaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidā pavattatīti vadanti. Yadi evaṃ kasmā pāḷiyaṃ “niruttipaṭisambhidā paccuppannārammaṇā”ti vuttāti āha “nirutti…pe… sandhāya vutta”nti. Pacchā jānananti saddaggahaṇuttarakālaṃ nāmaniruttiyā jānanaṃ. Evanti evaṃ saddaggahaṇato pacchā nāmaniruttiṃ ārabbha pavattaṃ ñāṇaṃ niruttipaṭisambhidāti gayhamāne. Evaṃ niruttiyā nāmapaññattipakkhe pāḷiyā, aṭṭhakathāya ca virodhaṃ dassetvā saddapakkhe tadabhāvaṃ dassento “yathā panā”tiādimāha. Taṃtaṃsaddavibhāvakanti yathā tassa tassa saddappabhedanicchayassa paccayabhūtaṃ dibbasotañāṇaṃ saddārammaṇameva taṃ taṃ saddaṃ vibhūtaṃ karoti, evaṃ niruttippabhedanicchayassa paccayabhūtaṃ niruttisaddārammaṇameva niruttipaṭisambhidāñāṇaṃ taṃ vibhūtaṃ karotīti tassa paccuppannārammaṇatā vuttā. Saddaṃ pana vibhāventaṃ ekantato saddūpanibandhaṃ paññattimpi vibhāvetiyeva, yato sabhāvāsabhāvavisesavibhāvanaṃ sampajjati. Aññathā hi saddamattaggahaṇe visesāvabodho eva na siyāti porāṇā paññattivibhāvanampi tassa icchanti. Taṃvibhāvakanti niruttisaddavibhāvakaṃ. Na pāḷivirodho hotīti yadipi abhidhammabhājanīye “yāya niruttiyā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ paññatti hotī”ti (vibha. 727) vuttaṃ, tampi sabhāvaniruttisaddena dhammānaṃ pabodhanameva sandhāya vuttaṃ, na tabbinimuttaṃ paññattinti “niruttisaddārammaṇā niruttipaṭisambhidā”ti vuccamāne pāḷiyā virodho na hotīti attho. “Paccavekkhantassā”ti vuttattā saddaṃ gahetvā pacchā gahitāya paññattiyā paccavekkhaṇena bhavitabbanti āsaṅkeyyāti tadāsaṅkānivattanatthamāha “taṃ sabhāvaniruttiṃ saddaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā”tiādi. Sabhāvaniruttiṃ vibhāventaṃyevāti sabhāvaniruttivisayassa sammohassa pageva viddhaṃsitattā atthasādhanavasena abhiññāñāṇaṃ viya taṃ vibhāventameva pavattati. Tenāha “niruttiṃ bhindantaṃ paṭivijjhantameva uppajjatī”ti. Pabhedagamanañcettha anavasesato niruttivibhāgajānanaṃ. Tathā sesesu. Sakkaṭanāmādīti sakkaṭavasena vuttanāmākhyātādi. Nipātapadaṃ [V 0.0192] nāmādipadāni viya atthaṃ na vadati, atha kho byañjeti jotetīti “byañjana”nti vuttaṃ nipātapadaṃ.

'Later' means in the subsequent part, at the immediately subsequent mind-door. They say that the analytical knowledge of language operates on the language of a name that is grasped in accordance with the grasping of the sound. If so, why is it said in the Pāli, 'The analytical knowledge of language has a present object'? He says, 'It is said with reference to language... (and so on).' Knowing afterwards means knowing the language of a name after grasping the sound. 'Thus' means: when the knowledge that arises concerning the language of a name after the grasping of the sound is taken as the analytical knowledge of language. Thus, having shown the contradiction with the Pāli and the commentary in the view that language is a name-concept, he then shows the absence of contradiction in the view that it is sound, beginning with 'But as...' That which distinguishes sounds means that just as the divine ear-knowledge, which is the condition for discerning the distinctions of sound, makes that particular sound clear with sound as its object, so too the knowledge of the analytical knowledge of language, which is the condition for discerning the distinctions of language, makes that clear with language-sound as its object—thus its having a present object is stated. However, when distinguishing sound, it inevitably distinguishes the concept connected with the sound as well, since the distinction of specific intrinsic and non-intrinsic characteristics is accomplished. Otherwise, if only sound were grasped, the discernment of distinctions would not occur at all—thus the ancients hold that it also distinguishes the concept. 'That which distinguishes it' means the distinguisher of language-sound. There is no contradiction with the Pāli. Even though it is said in the Abhidhamma section, 'By whatever language the designation of those things occurs' (Vibh. 727), that too is said with reference to the natural language-sound that reveals things, not to the concept apart from it. Thus, when it is said, 'The analytical knowledge of language has language-sound as its object,' there is no contradiction with the Pāli. Because it is said, 'for one who reflects,' one might suspect that after grasping the sound, one must reflect on the concept grasped later. To dispel that suspicion, he says, 'Taking that natural language-sound as the object,' etc. It operates only while clarifying the natural language, since the delusion regarding the sphere of natural language has already been dispelled; like the knowledge of direct perception, it operates while clarifying it for the sake of accomplishing the goal. Hence it is said, 'It arises only while breaking through and comprehending the language.' Here, penetration of the divisions means knowing the divisions of language without remainder. The same applies to the rest. 'Sanskrit names,' etc., means nouns, verbs, etc., stated in Sanskrit. A particle, unlike nouns, etc., does not state a meaning but rather expresses and illuminates it; therefore a particle is called a 'letter' (byañjana).

Bodhi [M 0.0194] ñāṇaṃ maṇḍabhūtaṃ etthāti bodhimaṇḍo, mahābodhiṭṭhānaṃ. Tenāha “paṭhamābhisambuddhaṭṭhāne”ti. Aññena pakārenāti uggahādippakārena.

The knowledge of enlightenment is the essence here, hence this is the Bodhimaṇḍa, the great place of enlightenment. Therefore it is said: 'at the place of the first full enlightenment.' 'By another method' means by the method of learning, and so on.

Aññathā hontīti purisayuge purisayuge ekadesena parivattantā kālantare aññākārā bhavanti. Vinassantīti taṃtaṃbhāsānaṃ manussānaṃ vināsena na paññāyanti, manussānaṃ duruggahaṇādinā katthaci kadāci parivattantīpi brahmalokādīsu yathāsabhāveneva avaṭṭhānato na sabbattha, sabbadā, sabbathā ca parivattati. Tenāha “kappavināsepi tiṭṭhatiyevā”ti. Etassa niruttipaṭisambhidāñāṇassa.

'They become otherwise' means: changing partially in generation after generation, in the course of time they take on different forms. 'They perish' means: with the perishing of the people of those various languages, they are no longer known. Although they sometimes change somewhere on account of people’s difficulty in grasping them and so on, because language remains in its own natural state in the Brahma worlds and so on, it does not change everywhere, always, and in every way. Therefore it is said: 'Even at the destruction of the aeon, it still remains.' This refers to the knowledge of the analytical knowledge of language.

Atthādīsu ñāṇanti atthapaṭisambhidādi. Atthadhammaniruttivasena tīsu. Atthadhammaniruttipaṭibhānavasena catūsupi vā. Atthadhammādinā attanā jotetabbena saha atthenāti sātthakāni. Sabbo atthadhammādiko attho visayabhūto etassa ñāṇassa atthīti sabbatthakaṃ. Sabbasmiṃ atthādike visaye khittaṃ attano paccayehi ṭhapitaṃ pavattitaṃ. Arahattappattiyā visadā honti paṭipakkhadhammānaṃ sabbaso viddhaṃsitattā. Pañcannanti adhigamapariyattisavanaparipucchāpubbayogānaṃ. Yathāyoganti yaṃ yaṃ yassa puggalassa visadatāya yujjati, tathā yojetabbaṃ.

'Knowledge in meaning, etc.' means the analytical knowledge of meaning and the rest. It is threefold by way of meaning, Dhamma, and language; or fourfold by way of meaning, Dhamma, language, and ready-wittedness. 'With meaning' (sātthakāni) is said because they have a meaning along with that which is to be illuminated by oneself, namely meaning, Dhamma, etc. 'All-encompassing' (sabbatthakaṃ) is said because all meaning, Dhamma, etc., exists as the domain of this knowledge. In every domain of meaning and the like, it is dispatched, established, and set in motion by its own conditions. They become clear with the attainment of arahantship because the opposing states have been completely demolished. 'Of the five' means: of attainment, learning, hearing, questioning, and previous practice. 'As is suitable' means: whatever is suitable for the clarity of a particular person, that should be applied.

Paripucchāhetu pavattā kathā paripucchāti vuttāti āha “pucchāya…pe… paripucchāti vuttā”ti.

Because a talk that proceeds on account of a question is called 'questioning,' he says: 'Because of a question... (and so on)... it is called questioning.'

Tehīti maggehi. Paṭilābho nāma pubbayogasampattiyā atthādivisayassa sammohassa samucchindanaṃ, taṃ pana maggakiccamevāti āha “so lokuttaro”ti. Atthādīnaṃ pabhedato sallakkhaṇavibhāvanavavatthāpanā yathārahaṃ parittakusalamahākiriyacittavasena hotīti vuttaṃ “pabhedo kāmāvacaro”ti. Yathā pubbayogo adhigamassa balavapaccayo sabhāvahetubhāvato, na tathā pabhedassa asabhāvahetutāya, paramparapaccayatāya cāti adhippāyo. Pariyattiādīnaṃ pabhedassa balavapaccayatāya[V 0.0193], adhigamassa ca tadabhāve eseva nayo. Tatthāti nimittatthe bhummaṃ, tāsu pariyattisavanaparipucchāsu nimittabhūtāsūti attho. Yaṃ vuttaṃ hotīti “etesu panā”tiādinā aṭṭhakathāvacanena yaṃ atthajātaṃ vuttaṃ [M 0.0195] hoti. Taṃ dassentoti taṃ niddhāretvā dassento. “Pubbayogādhigamā”ti vatvā “dvepī”ti vacanaṃ adhigamasahitoyeva pubbayogo pabhedassa balavapaccayo, na kevaloti dassanatthaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “dvepi ekato hutvā”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 718). “Dvepi visadakāraṇā”ti vutte pubbayogassāpi visadakāraṇattaṃ labbhatevāti āha “dvepi visadakāraṇāti…pe… vutta”nti.

'By them' means by the paths. Acquisition is the cutting off of delusion concerning the domain of meaning, etc., through the accomplishment of previous practice. But since that is the very function of the path, he says: 'that is supramundane.' The analysis, clarification, and determination of the distinctions of meaning, etc., occurs, as is fit, by way of limited wholesome and great functional consciousness; thus it is said: 'the distinction is of the sense sphere.' The intention is that just as previous practice is a strong condition for attainment because it is a natural cause, it is not so for distinction, because it is not a natural cause and is an indirect condition. This same principle applies to the strong conditionality of distinction for learning, etc., and to the absence of attainment in that case. 'Therein' is a locative in the sense of a sign; the meaning is: 'being a sign in those cases of learning, hearing, and questioning.' 'What is said' means the collection of meanings that is stated by the commentary passage beginning 'But among these.' 'Showing that' means showing that after having determined it. Having said 'previous practice and attainment,' the word 'both' is for the purpose of showing that it is previous practice together with attainment that is a strong condition for distinction, not it alone. Therefore it is said in the commentary: 'both having come together.' When 'both are causes of clarity' is said, since the status of previous practice as a cause of clarity is also obtained, he says: 'both are causes of clarity... (pe)... is said.'

Saṅgahavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Section on Inclusion is finished.

2. Saccavārādivaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Section on the Truths, etc.

719. Kālattayepīti atītādīsu tīsupi kālesu. Hetuphaladhammā hetūnaṃ phalabhūtā dhammā, paccayanibbattāti attho. Tesañca hetudhammāti tesaṃ hetuphalānaṃ paccayanibbattānaṃ hetubhūtā dhammā “dhammā”ti vuttāti yojanā. Vineyyavasenāti tathāvinetabbapuggalajjhāsayavasena. Uppannā samuppannātiādi na vuttanti uppannā samuppannā uṭṭhitā samuṭṭhitā paccuppannātiādi na vuttaṃ ekantapaccuppannasseva saṅgāhakattā. Taṃnibbattakāti tesaṃ atthabhāvena vuttānaṃ nipphādakā. Dhammāti vuttā dhammabhāvena kathitā.

719. 'Even in the three times' means in the three times, past, etc. 'Phenomena that are the fruit of a cause' are phenomena that are the fruit of causes; the meaning is 'produced by conditions.' 'And their cause-phenomena': the construction is that the phenomena that are the causes of those condition-produced phenomena that are the fruit of a cause are called 'phenomena.' 'By way of the trainable' means by way of the disposition of persons to be trained in such a way. 'Arisen, well arisen, etc., is not said' means: the full series 'arisen, well arisen, risen, well risen, present,' etc., is not stated because this serves to include only what is exclusively present. 'Their producers' means the producers of those things stated as 'meaning.' 'Phenomena' are so called because they are spoken of as phenomena.

Saccavārādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Section on the Truths, etc., is finished.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Division in the Suttanta Way is finished.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Division in the Abhidhamma Way

725. Sāmaññena [V 0.0194] vatvā visesena avuttattāti “tesaṃ vipāke”ti yathāvuttakusalavipākatādisāmaññena vatvā sahetukāhetukādivisesena avuttattā, sarūpena niddhāretvā avuttattāti attho. Avipākattāti avipākadhammattā. Yadi evanti paccayabhāvato labbhamānopi dhammabhāvo avipākadhammatāya kiriyānaṃ yadi na vutto, evaṃ sati. Satipi paccayuppannabhāve avipākabhāvato atthabhāvopi na vattabbo. Tenāha “vipākā na hontīti atthabhāvo ca na vattabbo”ti. Evañceti yadi paccayuppannattā kiriyānaṃ atthabhāvo vutto. Nappaṭisiddho icchitovāti [M 0.0196] attho. Yadi evaṃ kasmā na vuttoti āha “vipākassa panā”tiādi. Tesanti kusalākusalānaṃ, vipākakiriyadhammānañca. Atthadhammatāti vuttanayena labbhamānopi yathākkamaṃ atthabhāvo, dhammabhāvo ca na vutto. Paccayabhāvaṃ sattivisesaṃ sanipphādetabbatanti padattayenāpi vipākadhammatamevāha. Sā hi vipākānaṃ hetubhāvato paccayabhāvo, taduppādanasamatthatāya sattiviseso, tehi sagabbhā viya hotīti “sanipphādetabbatā”ti ca vuccati. Taṃ passantī nipphādakavisesāpi nipphādetabbāpekkhā hoti dhammapaṭisambhidā. Taṃsambandhenāti nipphādetabbasambandhena. Dhammapaṭisambhidaṃ vadantena atthapaṭisambhidāpi vuttā.

725. 'Because it was stated generally and not specifically' means: because, having stated it generally as 'their result'—that is, with the generality of wholesome resultants, etc., as stated—it was not stated with the specifics of 'with cause,' 'without cause,' etc.; the meaning is that it was not stated after having determined their own nature. 'Because they are not resultants' means because they are non-resultant phenomena. 'If so' means: if, although the status as a phenomenon is obtained from their being a condition, the status as a phenomenon is not stated for functional consciousness because it is a non-resultant phenomenon, this being the case, even though the state of being conditionally arisen exists, the status as 'meaning' also should not be stated. Therefore he says: 'They are not resultants, and the status as meaning should not be stated.' 'And thus' means: if the status as meaning is stated for functional consciousness because it is conditionally arisen. The meaning is: it is not rejected, it is intended. If so, why was it not stated? He says: 'But of the resultant,' etc. 'Of them' means of wholesome and unwholesome phenomena, and of resultant and functional phenomena.
