'Status as meaning and phenomenon': although the status as meaning and the status as phenomenon are obtained in due order by the method stated, they are not stated. With the three terms 'state of being a condition,' 'specific power,' and 'producibility,' he states only the nature of being a resultant phenomenon. For that is the state of being a condition because it is the cause of resultants; it is a specific power because of its capacity to produce them; and because it is as if in the same womb with them, it is also called 'producibility.' Seeing that, even the specific producer has an expectation of what is to be produced; this is the analytical knowledge of phenomena. 'Through its connection' means through connection with what is to be produced. By one who states the analytical knowledge of phenomena, the analytical knowledge of meaning is also stated.

Sabhāvadhamme paññatti sabhāvapaññattīti āha “na sattādipaññattiyā”ti. Sabhāvena, niruttiyeva vā sabhāvapaññattīti vuttāti āha “aviparītapaññattiyā vā”ti.

A concept about a real phenomenon is a 'concept of real nature'; thus he says: 'not by a concept of a being, etc.' Or, a 'concept of real nature' is so called because it is a designation by real nature, or simply a designation; thus he says: 'or by a non-perverted concept.'

746. Vohārabhūmiṃ, adhigamabhūmiñca ekajjhaṃ katvā āha “kāmāvacarā, lokuttarā ca bhūmi bhūmī”ti. Cittuppādā vā pavattiṭṭhānabhāvato bhūmi.

746. Having combined the plane of conventional expression and the plane of attainment, he says: 'The sense-sphere plane and the supramundane plane are the planes.' Or, it is a plane because it is the ground for the occurrence of mind-arisings, by way of being their standing place.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Division in the Abhidhamma Way is finished.

3. Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the Question Section

747. Sabbañāṇārammaṇatāyāti [V 0.0195] paṭisambhidāpaṭisambhidāñāṇārammaṇatāya. “Suttantabhājanīye pana…pe… siyā”ti idaṃ abhidhammabhājanīyena virujjhati, tassa vā sāvasesadesanatā āpajjatīti codanaṃ manasi katvā āha “abhidhammabhājanīye”tiādi. Niravasesakathananti asesetvā kathanaṃ. Tena cittuppādasaṅgahite atthe asesetvā desanā idha abhidhammabhājanīyassa bhāro, na sabbañeyyadhammeti dasseti. Yathādassitavisayavacanavasenāti dassitappakāravisayassa kathanavasena, dhammatthavasena dassite taṃtaṃcittuppāde tattha dhammaniruttābhilāpena ñāṇassa kathanavasenāti attho. Aññārammaṇataṃ na paṭisedheti atapparabhāvatoti adhippāyo. Na niravasesena kathanaṃ acittuppādapariyāpannassa visayassa akathitattā. Evaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāvisayassāpi na [M 0.0197] niravasesena kathananti suttantabhājanīye avisesavacanena sabbañāṇārammaṇataṃyeva paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāya patiṭṭhāpeti. Tathā tisso paṭisambhidātiādipañhapucchakapāḷiyāpi. Tissoti atthadhammapaṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Niruttipaṭisambhidā hi “parittārammaṇā”teva vuttā.

747. “The state of having all knowledge as its object” means the state of having the knowledge of the analytical knowledges as its object. Considering the objection that “In the Suttanta classification, however... it might be...” contradicts the Abhidhamma classification, or that it implies an incomplete teaching, it is said, “In the Abhidhamma classification,” etc. “Unreserved statement” means a statement without remainder. Thereby it shows that the burden of the Abhidhamma classification here is to teach without remainder concerning the matter included in a consciousness-arising, not concerning all knowable phenomena. “By way of speaking of the subject as shown” means by way of speaking of the subject in the manner shown; the meaning is, by way of speaking of knowledge in the respective consciousness-arisings shown by way of the meaning of the Dhamma, through the expression of the Dhamma and its language. The intention is that it does not deny having other objects, because that is not its scope. There is no unreserved statement because the subject not included in a consciousness-arising is not stated. Thus, even for the subject of the analytical knowledge of ready wit, there is no unreserved statement. In the Suttanta classification, through an unqualified statement, it establishes that the analytical knowledge of ready wit has all knowledge as its object. Likewise also in the Pāḷi of the question section beginning “the three analytical knowledges.” “Three” refers to the analytical knowledge of meaning, of the Dhamma, and of ready wit. For the analytical knowledge of language is said to have only “a limited object.”

Yadipi siyā na tassā mahaggatārammaṇatāti sambandho. “Na hi maggo paccayuppanno na hotī”ti iminā “atthapaṭisambhidā na maggārammaṇā”ti vacanassa yathāvuttatthasādhakataṃ vibhāveti. Tassāti paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāya na mahaggatārammaṇatā sambhavati nanu nayaṃ anussarantassāti adhippāyo. Dvepīti “atthapaṭisambhidā na maggārammaṇā, tisso paṭisambhidā siyā parittārammaṇā, siyā mahaggatārammaṇā, siyā appamāṇārammaṇā”ti ca dvepi etā pāḷiyo. Tāsu balavatarāya ṭhānassa, itarāya adhippāyamagganassa ca upāyadassanamukhena tāsaṃ aññamaññaṃ avirodhaṃ dassetuṃ “kusalākusalānaṃ panā”tiādimāha. “Nippariyāyā tattha dhammapaṭisambhidā”ti etena tattha atthapaṭisambhidāya pariyāyabhāvamāha. Tathā vipākakiriyānantiādi yathādhippetassa atthassa visadisūdāharaṇadassanaṃ. Ubhayenapi “atthapaṭisambhidā na maggārammaṇā”ti (vibha. 749) vacanaṃ suttantanayānugataṃ nippariyāyatthassa tattha adhippetattāti dīpeti. Kiñci pana ñāṇantiādi “tisso paṭisambhidā”tiādipāḷiyā samatthakaṃ. Yathādhippetassa atthassa paṭibhānaṃ dīpanaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tenāha “ñeyyappakāsanato”ti. Iti yā “tisso paṭisambhidā”ti pāḷi, tassā balavabhāvavibhāvanena [V 0.0196] itarāya adhippāyamagganaṃ katanti veditabbaṃ. Nippariyāyāti pariyāyarahitā ujukaṃ sarūpeneva pavattā. Nippariyāya…pe… pavattiyanti ekantikaatthārammaṇaṃ ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā, ñāṇārammaṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāti gahetvā desanāyaṃ.

The connection is: even if it were so, it would not have an exalted object. By the words, “For the path is not unconditioned,” it clarifies how the statement, “The analytical knowledge of meaning does not have the path as its object,” establishes the meaning stated. The intention is: for that, for the analytical knowledge of ready wit, having an exalted object is not possible—is it not so for one who recollects the method? “Both” refers to these two Pāḷi passages: “The analytical knowledge of meaning does not have the path as its object,” and “The three analytical knowledges may have a limited object, an exalted object, or an immeasurable object.” To show their non-contradiction by way of showing the means for establishing the stronger of them and for seeking the intention of the other, he says, “But of wholesome and unwholesome states…” etc. By “The analytical knowledge of the Dhamma there is direct,” it states the indirect nature of the analytical knowledge of meaning there. Similarly, “of resultant and functional states,” etc., is the showing of a dissimilar example for the intended meaning. By both, it illuminates that the statement “The analytical knowledge of meaning does not have the path as its object” (Vibh 749) follows the Suttanta method, because the direct meaning is intended there. “But a certain knowledge,” etc., supports the Pāḷi passage “the three analytical knowledges,” etc. Ready wit is the shining forth, the illumination, of the intended meaning. Hence he says, “because it illuminates the knowable.” Thus, it should be understood that by clarifying the strength of this Pāḷi passage, 'the three analytical knowledges,' the intention of the other has been sought. “Direct” means devoid of an alternative, proceeding straight on in its own nature. “Direct… proceeding”: in this teaching, it is taken that the analytical knowledge of meaning is knowledge that has a definite meaning as its object, while the analytical knowledge of ready wit has knowledge as its object.

So evāti parassa abhilāpasaddo eva. Anuvattamānatā cassa niruttipaṭisambhidā paccuppannameva saddaṃ ārammaṇaṃ karontī, saddaṃ sutvā “ayaṃ sabhāvanirutti, ayaṃ na sabhāvaniruttī”ti jānantīti ca ādivacanavasena veditabbo.

“That itself” is just the verbal expression of another. And its nature of following along should be understood by way of the initial statement that the analytical knowledge of language, taking the present sound itself as its object, upon hearing a sound, knows: “This is conventional language, this is not conventional language.”

Pañhapucchakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Questioner is finished.

Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of the Analytical Knowledges is finished.

16. Ñāṇavibhaṅgo

16. Analysis of Knowledge

1. Ekakamātikādivaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Mātikā of Single Items, etc.

751. Sampayuttānaṃ [M 0.0198][V 0.0197] nissayapaccayatāya, ārammaṇassa pavattiṭṭhānatāya okāsaṭṭho veditabbo. Nahetādīti ādi-saddena “ahetukā”tiādikaṃ sabbaṃ ekavidhena ñāṇavatthuṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Ekaṃ nahetūti nahetutāya ekaṃ pañcaviññāṇaṃ nahetūti vuttā tesaṃ nahetutā. Ekantāhetubhāvena hi te ekappakārāvāti. Aññampīti ahetukādi. Avitathasāmaññayuttanti teneva ahetukatādinā yathābhūtena samānabhāvena yuttaṃ. Ñāṇārammaṇanti ñāṇassa ārammaṇaṃ yathāvuttapañcaviññāṇādi. Vatthuvibhāvanāti pañcaviññāṇādikassa ñāṇavatthussa yathāvuttavisesena vibhāvanā pakāsanā paññā.

751. The meaning of “occasion” should be understood as the support condition for associated states and as the place of occurrence for the object. “Not a root, etc.”: by the word “etc.” it includes everything such as “rootless,” etc., as a single kind of basis for knowledge. “One is not a root”: because of being not a root, the five sense-consciousnesses are said to be “not a root”; this is their not being a root. For they are of one kind because they are entirely rootless. “And another” means rootless, etc. “Connected with unerring commonality” means connected with the true commonality by that very rootlessness, etc. “Object of knowledge” means an object of knowledge, such as the aforesaid five sense-consciousnesses, etc. “Elucidation of the basis” is wisdom, which is the elucidation, the clarification, with the aforesaid distinction, of the basis for knowledge, such as the five sense-consciousnesses.

Osānadukassāti “atthajāpikā paññā, jāpitatthā paññā”ti imassa dukassa. Dukamātikā dhammasaṅgaṇiyaṃ vuttadukamātikāti āha “dukamātikaṃ anissāyā”ti.

“Of the final couplet” means of this couplet: “wisdom that generates meaning, wisdom whose meaning is generated.” Since the couplet mātikā is the couplet mātikā stated in the Dhammasaṅgaṇī, he says, “without relying on the couplet mātikā.”

“Cintāmayā paññā”tiādikā tikamātikaṃ anissāya vuttāti āha “evaṃ tikānurūpehīti etthāpi daṭṭhabba”nti. Yadipi jāpa-saddo byattavacane, mānase ca pavattati, jananatthepi pana daṭṭhabboti dassento āha “anekatthattā dhātusaddāna”ntiādi. Kusalapaññā vipākasaṅkhātassa, kiriyapaññā parikammādibhūtā attanā nibbattetabbaphalasaṅkhātassa atthassa nibbattanato atthajāpikāti vuttāti āha “atthajāpikā kāraṇagatā paññā”ti. Vipākapaññā, kiriyapaññā ca sahajātādipaccayavasena taṃtaṃvipākādiatthaṃ jāpeti janetīti āha “jāpito janito attho etissāti jāpitatthā”ti. Satipi sahajātānaṃ paccayabhāve vipākakiriyapaññā [V 0.0198] na kusalā viya vipākānaṃ nippariyāyena kāraṇavohāraṃ labhatīti āha “kāraṇapaññāsadisī”ti. Vibhāvanatthena paññā ārammaṇaṃ viya sampayuttepi pakāsetiyevāti vuttaṃ “phalappakāsanabhūtā”ti. Yato sā ālokobhāsapajjotapariyāyehi vibhāvitā.

He says, “Thus it should be seen here too in accordance with the triplets,” to show that “wisdom consisting of reflection,” etc., are stated without relying on the triplet mātikā. Although the word “jāpa” occurs in the sense of distinct speech and in a mental sense, to show that it should also be seen in the sense of producing, he says, “because verbal roots have many meanings,” etc. He says, “Atthajāpikā is wisdom connected to the cause,” because wholesome wisdom is called “atthajāpikā” from its producing the meaning designated as resultant, and functional wisdom, being preliminary, from its producing the meaning designated as the fruit to be produced by oneself. He says, “Jāpitatthā is that by which meaning is generated, produced,” because resultant wisdom and functional wisdom cause to be born, generate, the respective resultant meaning, etc., by way of co-nascent condition, etc. He says, “similar to causal wisdom,” because although co-nascent states have the nature of a condition, resultant and functional wisdom do not, like wholesome wisdom, obtain the designation “cause” for the resultants in a direct way. It is said, “being that which illuminates the fruit,” because by its meaning of elucidating, wisdom illuminates associated states just as it does its object. For it is elucidated by the synonyms light, radiance, and lamp.

10. Dasakamātikāvaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Decad Mātikā

760. “Jātipaccayā [M 0.0199] jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ, asati jātiyā natthi jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ. Atītampi addhānaṃ jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ, asati jātiyā natthi jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ. Anāgatampi addhānaṃ jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ, asati jātiyā natthi jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇaṃ. Yampissa taṃ dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇaṃ, tampi khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammanti ñāṇaṃ. Bhavapaccayā…pe… avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā…pe… nirodhadhamma”nti (saṃ. ni. 2.34) evamāgatāni sattasattati ñāṇāni. “Jarāmaraṇe ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ. Jātiyā ñāṇaṃ…pe… saṅkhāresu ñāṇaṃ…pe… paṭipadāya ñāṇa”nti (saṃ. ni. 2.33) evamāgatāni catucattārīsaṃ ñāṇāni. Sutamayañāṇādīni anāvaraṇañāṇapariyosānāni paṭisambhidāmagge (paṭi. ma. mātikā 1.1 ādayo) āgatāni tesattati ñāṇāni. Tenāha “tesattati pana…pe… na saṃyuttake”ti. “Saṃyuttake”ti vā idaṃ “sattasattati ñāṇānī”ti iminā sambandhitabbaṃ, na “tesattatī”ti iminā. Aññattha nikkhepakaṇḍādīsu. Yathā sammāpaṭivedhābhāvato micchāñāṇādi thusarāsimhi nikhātakhāṇuko viya ārammaṇe cañcalaṃ hoti, na evaṃ hoti yathābhūtāvabodhakaṃ ñāṇanti āha “yāthāvapaṭivedhato sayañca akampiya”nti. Adhibalakaraṇaṃ upatthambhananti taṃ puggale āropento āha “puggalañca…pe… karotī”ti. Visabhāgadhammesu vā akampiyattho, sabhāgadhammesu upatthambhanattho veditabbo.

760. “Knowledge that aging and death are conditioned by birth, knowledge that without birth there is no aging and death. Knowledge that in the past, aging and death were conditioned by birth, knowledge that without birth there was no aging and death. Knowledge that in the future, aging and death will be conditioned by birth, knowledge that without birth there will be no aging and death. Knowledge that even this knowledge of the stability of phenomena is subject to dissolution, vanishing, fading away, and cessation. Conditioned by existence… conditioned by ignorance, volitional formations… subject to cessation” (SN 12.34)—thus seventy-seven knowledges are presented. “Knowledge of aging and death, knowledge of the origin of aging and death, knowledge of the cessation of aging and death, knowledge of the path leading to the cessation of aging and death. Knowledge of birth… knowledge of volitional formations… knowledge of the path” (SN 12.33)—thus forty-four knowledges are presented. The knowledges beginning with knowledge born of hearing up to unobstructed knowledge, as found in the Paṭisambhidāmagga (PsM 1.1ff.), amount to seventy-three knowledges. Therefore, it is said, “seventy-three… not in the Saṃyutta.” The phrase “in the Saṃyutta” should be connected with “seventy-seven knowledges,” not with “seventy-three.” Elsewhere, as in the Nikkhepakaṇḍa, etc. Just as, due to the absence of right penetration, wrong knowledge, etc., like a stake planted in a heap of chaff, is unsteady in its object—not so is knowledge that comprehends things as they really are. Thus it is said, “due to right penetration, it is itself unshakable.” Strengthening is support, and applying this to a person, it is said, “a person… makes….” The meaning of unshakability should be understood in relation to dissimilar phenomena, while the meaning of support applies to similar phenomena.

Abhimukhaṃ gacchantīti “upagacchantī”ti padassa atthavacanaṃ. Upagamanañcettha sabbaññutāya paṭijānanamevāti vuttaṃ “paṭijānanavasenā”ti. Aṭṭha vā parisā upasaṅkamantīti etthāpi paṭijānanavasena sabbaññutanti yojetabbaṃ. Aṭṭhasu parisāsu dassitaakampiyañāṇayuttoti sambandho.

Facing towards, approaching—this is the meaning of the word 'upagacchantī.' And here, approaching is solely the proclaiming of omniscience, hence it is said 'by way of proclamation.' Approaching the eight assemblies—here too, omniscience should be connected by way of proclamation. The connection is: endowed with unshakable knowledge displayed in the eight assemblies.

Phalasampattipavattīti [V 0.0199] sappurisūpanissayādīnaṃ kāraṇasampattīnaṃ phalabhūtāya patirūpadesavāsaattasammāpaṇidhiādisampattiyā pavattanaṃ. Ādi-saddena suttasesā saṅgahitā. Tattha sappurisūpanissayādike. Kasmā panettha samāne atthakicce paṭivedhañāṇassa viya desanāñāṇassāpi yāva arahattamaggā uppajjamānatā na vuttāti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “paṭivedhaniṭṭhattā”tiādi[M 0.0200]. Paṭivedhaniṭṭhattāti paṭivedhassa pariyosānattā. Tenāti paṭivedhapariyosānabhūtena arahattamaggañāṇena. Tadadhigamena hi sampattasakalasabbaññuguṇo bhagavā anantapaṭibhāno anupamāya buddhalīḷāya dhammaṃ desetuṃ samattho ahosi. “Paṭiladdhassāpī”ti iminā sabbathā labhāpakassa paṭivedhānurūpatā desanāñāṇassa asakkuṇeyyāti dīpeti, tena ca paṭivedhanamattenettha atthasiddhīti dasseti. Tenāha “desanāñāṇassā”tiādi.

The occurrence of the attainment of fruition is the occurrence of the attainment of residing in a suitable place, right aspiration for oneself, and other accomplishments, which is the fruit of the attainment of causal conditions such as reliance on a true person. The term “etc.” includes the remaining factors of the discourse. Here, regarding reliance on a true person and so forth, a question arises: “Why, when the purpose is the same, is the arising of the knowledge of teaching not mentioned as occurring up to the path of arahantship, like the knowledge of penetration?” This is addressed by stating, “because of the finality of penetration.” “Because of the finality of penetration” means because of the conclusion of penetration. “By that” refers to the knowledge of the path of arahantship, which is the culmination of penetration. For it was through attaining this that the Blessed One, endowed with all the qualities of omniscience, became capable of teaching the Dhamma with boundless eloquence and incomparable Buddha-grace. The phrase “even of what is attained” indicates that the knowledge of teaching, though corresponding to penetration, cannot in every way bring about the attainment. It also shows that here, the purpose is fulfilled by penetration alone. Hence, it is stated, “of the knowledge of teaching,” etc.

Hānabhāgiyadhammanti vā hānabhāgiyabhāvassa kāraṇaṃ. Kāmasahagatasaññādidhammanti kāmaguṇārammaṇaṃ saññāmanasikārādiṃ. Pubbeva katābhisaṅkhārādinti “cande vā sūriye vā ettakaṃ gate vuṭṭhahissāmī”tiādinā samāpajjanato pubbe pavattacittābhisaṅkhāraparikammādiṃ.

A state conducive to decline, or the cause of the state conducive to decline. States such as perception associated with sensual pleasures refer to perception, attention, and so on, with sensual qualities as their object. The previously made volitional formations mean the mental volitional formations, preparatory work of the mind, and so on, that occurred before entering into attainment, such as resolving, “I will emerge when the moon or the sun has moved this much.”

Tadabhāvaggahaṇenāti kilesāvaraṇābhāvaggahaṇena. Ṭhitinti atthibhāvaṃ. Tabbiparītāyāti “natthi dinna”ntiādikāya micchādiṭṭhiyā. Ṭhānābhāvanti appavattiṃ, natthibhāvaṃ vā. Uparīti imissā balānaṃ anukkamakathāya upari anantarameva. Vipākāvaraṇābhāvadassanādikassāti ādi-saddena kammāvaraṇābhāvadassanaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Itaranti adhigamassa aṭṭhānadassanaṃ. Taṃsahitānaṃ dhātūnanti rāgādisahitānaṃ sabhāvānaṃ. Vemattatā ca tesaṃ paccayavisesasiddhena avatthādivisesena veditabbā. Cariyāhetūnanti rāgādicariyākāraṇabhūtānaṃ dhammānaṃ.

By grasping its absence: by grasping the absence of the obstruction of the defilements. Stability: the state of being. By what is contrary to that: by the wrong view such as “There is nothing given,” etc. Absence of a basis: non-occurrence, or non-existence. Above: immediately above in this sequential exposition of the powers. Of seeing the absence of the obstruction of result, etc.: by the word “etc.” one includes seeing the absence of the obstruction of kamma. The other: seeing that there is no basis for attainment. Of those elements associated with it: of the natures associated with lust, etc. Their diversity should be understood through the distinction of states, etc., established by the distinction of conditions. Of the causes of conduct: of the states that are the causes of conduct, such as lust, etc.

1. Ekakaniddesavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Singular Exposition

761. Ayaṃ visesoti samānepi nayadvayassa tesaṃ ahetubhāvādidīpane ekassa hetubhāvādipaṭisedhatā, itarassa rāsantarāsaṅgahoti idaṃ nānākaraṇaṃ. Ekāya jātiyāti ādānanikkhepaparicchinnassa ekassa bhavassa. Tadantogadhatāyāti gatiantogadhatāya. Tattha tatthāti taṃtaṃgaticutibhavesu.

761. This is the distinction: even though the two methods are similar in explaining their non-causal nature and so on, one consists in the denial of their causal nature and so on, while the other is their inclusion in a different group. This is what makes them different. 'By one birth' means of a single existence defined by the taking up and the laying down. 'By being included within that' means by being included within a destination. 'There and there' means in the passing away and existence in this or that destination.

762. Tathāti [V 0.0200] aññadvārārammaṇatāya. Khīrādīnaṃ…pe… vilakkhaṇatāti yathā khīrassa dadhibhāvena, dadhino takkabhāvena vilakkhaṇatāpatti, na evaṃ pañcaviññāṇānaṃ nahetubhāvādito aññassa sabhāvāpatti atthīti attho.

762. 'Thus' means by being an object for another door. 'The distinctness of milk, etc.' means: just as milk attains a different characteristic by becoming curds, and curds by becoming buttermilk, so it is not for the five sense-consciousnesses; because of their non-causal nature and so on, there is no attainment of another intrinsic nature. This is the meaning.

763. Mahattepīti [M 0.0201] puthuttepi. Bahubhāvavācako hi ayaṃ mahā-saddo “mahājano”tiādīsu viya rūpasaṅghāṭassa adhippetattā. Aññathā sabhāvadhammassa kā mahantatā, sukhumatā vā. Cakkhuviññāṇassa vacanaṃ katvā vuttattā āha “cakkhupasāde mama vatthumhī”ti. Issariyaṭṭhānanti issariyapavattanaṭṭhānaṃ. Tathā hi naṃ aññattha bhāvitaṃ vibhāventameva tiṭṭhati, aññaviññāṇāni ca tena dinnanayāneva tattha pavattanti, api dibbacakkhuñāṇaṃ, yato taṃ andhassa na nipphajjati.

763. 'Even in greatness' means even in abundance. For this word 'mahā,' as in 'mahājana' (a great multitude), signifies abundance, because a collection of forms is intended. Otherwise, what greatness or subtlety could a phenomenon with its own intrinsic nature possess? Because it is stated after mentioning eye-consciousness, it says: 'in the eye-sensitivity, my basis.' 'Place of sovereignty' means the place for the exercise of sovereignty. For, having been developed elsewhere, it stands there just manifesting it, and other consciousnesses proceed there only by the method it provides; this is so even for the knowledge of the divine eye, since that does not arise for a blind person.

764. Vavatthitānampīti aññamaññaṃ asaṃkiṇṇānampi. Paṭipāṭiniyamo niyatānupubbikatā. Tenāti “abbokiṇṇā”ti vacanena.

764. 'Even of those that are distinct' means even of those that are not intermingled with one another. 'Fixed order' is a definite sequence. 'By that' means by the statement 'unmixed.'

766. Āvaṭṭanabhāvo āvajjanakiccatā.

766. The state of turning towards is the function of adverting.

Tesanti rūpādīnaṃ. Etesañhi rūpādīnaṃ pañcahi viññāṇehi samāgamo. Abhinipatitabbāni ālambitabbāni, vijānitabbānīti attho. Tenāha “ārammaṇakaraṇena paṭivijānitabbānī”ti. Kusalākusalacetanāya, taṃsampayuttānañca yathāvuttānaṃ “manopubbaṅgamā…pe… akusalaṃ vā”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 766) evaṃ vuttānaṃ paṭivijānitabbānaṃ paṭivijānananti sambandho. Kammatthe hi etaṃ sāmivacanaṃ. Sahajapubbaṅgamadhammenāti dassanādīhi sahajātaphassādinā pubbaṅgamena āvajjanādinā. Kiccantaranti dassanādikiccato aññaṃ sampaṭicchanādikiccaṃ.

'Of them' means of forms and so on. For there is a meeting of these forms and so on with the five consciousnesses. They are to be impinged upon, to be taken as an object, and to be cognized—this is the meaning. Hence it is said: 'They are to be cognized by way of making them an object.' The connection is with 'the cognizing of what is to be cognized,' which refers to wholesome and unwholesome volition and their associated states, as stated thus: 'Mind is the forerunner… or unwholesome.' For this genitive is in the sense of the object. 'By the co-arisen forerunner-dhamma' means by the forerunner, such as adverting, with co-arisen states, such as contact, associated with seeing and so on. 'Another function' means a function other than the function of seeing and so on, namely, the function of receiving and so on.

Avipākabhāvena kāraṇena, tena vā saddhiṃ. Aññanti rūpabhāvādiṃ. Bhāsanakaraṇakarāti viññattisamuṭṭhāpanavasena pavattakusalākusalacittuppādadhammā. Te eva kāyaṅgavācaṅgaṃ acopetvā pavattā taṃsadisā. Pubbaṅgamapaṭivijānananti pubbaṅgamabhāvena vijānanaṃ manodvārikajavanānaṃ purecarabhāvena gahaṇaṃ. Tatthāti pañcadvāre. “Na paṭisiddha”nti vatvā svāyamappaṭisedho sāmatthiyaladdhoti [V 0.0201] dassetuṃ “na kāyakammaṃ…pe… anuññātattā”ti vuttaṃ. “Tathā”ti idaṃ yathā kāyavacīkammapaṭṭhapanaṃ, evaṃ kusalādidhammasamādānampi natthīti upasaṃharaṇatthaṃ veditabbaṃ. Yadi na bhavato cavati, kathaṃ pañcadvāre cuti vuttāti āha “na pañcadvārika…pe… ataṃdvārikattā”ti. Tassā pāḷiyā. Āpāthamattanti āpāthagamanamattaṃ [M 0.0202] ārammaṇapaccayabhāvamattaṃ. Aññanti “rūpaṃ nīla”nti evamādidhammavisesaṃ. Tenāha “dhammasabhāva”nti. Rūpanti ca na gaṇhātīti rūpārammaṇampi samānaṃ “rūpaṃ nāmeta”nti na gaṇhāti. Tathā cāhu eke “cakkhuviññāṇasamaṅgī nīlaṃ vijānāti, no tu nīla”nti. Rūpanīlādiākāro rūpārammaṇarūpādānākārapaññatti. Tajjāpaññatti hesā yathā aniccatādi. Sātisayaṃ savitakkasavicārattā. Tato aññanti saddārammaṇato aññaṃ nāmapaññattiārammaṇaṃ, aññathā sahuppattipaṭisedho na sambhaveyyāti adhippāyo.

By the reason of its not being a resultant, or together with that. 'Other' means the state of being form, etc. 'Making the cause of manifestation' means the states that are arisings of wholesome and unwholesome consciousness which proceed by way of originating intimation. Those very same ones, proceeding without agitating the bodily and verbal members, are similar to that. 'Cognizing the forerunner' means cognizing in the manner of a forerunner, the grasping by way of being a precursor to the mind-door impulsions. 'There' means at the five doors. Having said, 'it is not prohibited,' in order to show that this non-prohibition is obtained by its own capacity, it is said: 'because bodily action… is permitted.' This word 'thus' should be understood as for the purpose of concluding that just as there is no establishment of bodily and verbal action, so too there is no undertaking of wholesome and other dhammas. If it does not pass away from existence, how is passing away at the five doors stated? He says: 'not five-doored… because of its not being of that door.' Of that Pāli text. 'Merely in the range' means merely coming into the range, merely the state of being an object-condition. 'Other' means a specific dhamma such as 'form is blue.' Hence he says, 'the intrinsic nature of a dhamma.' And 'it does not grasp "form"' means that although the object is form, it does not grasp it as 'this is form.' And thus some have said: 'One endowed with eye-consciousness knows blue, but not "blue."' The appearance of form, blue, etc., is a concept of the appearance of grasping the form-object. For this is a concept produced from that, like impermanence, etc. It is pre-eminent because it is with applied and sustained thought. 'Other than that' means an object that is a name-concept, other than a sound-object; otherwise, the prohibition of co-arising would not be possible—this is the intention.

Manodvārepīti na pañcadvāreyeva dutiye moghavāre, atha kho manodvārepi. Āvajjanaṃ dvattikkhattuṃ…pe… daṭṭhabbaṃ ekacittakkhaṇikassa āvajjanassa uppattiyaṃ tathā asambhavato.

'Even at the mind-door' means not only at the five doors in the second futile instance, but also at the mind-door. 'Adverting two or three times…' etc., should be understood thus because in the arising of an adverting that lasts for a single mind-moment, such a thing is not possible.

Tassāti yāthāvakavatthuvibhāvanāya paññāya.

'Of that' means of the wisdom that clarifies a thing as it really is.

Ekakaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Singular Exposition is finished.

2. Dukaniddesavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Exposition of Dyads

767. Adhikaraṇesūti padatthesu. Aññatra sabhāvaṃ gahetvāti atthasaddassa tattha pavattanākāradassanaṃ, tena atthasaddassa sabhāvatthataṃ dasseti. Adhikaraṇavasena liṅgaparivattiṃ gacchati. “Abhidheyyānurūpaṃ liṅgavacanānī”ti hi saddavidū vadanti.

767. 'In the topics' means 'in the meanings of the words.' The phrase ‘by taking a different nature’ shows the way the word ‘meaning’ functions there, and thereby shows that the word ‘meaning’ has its own inherent meaning. It changes gender according to the topic. For experts in grammar say, ‘Gender and number agree with what is expressed.’

Dukaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of Dyads is finished.

3. Tikaniddesavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Exposition of Triads

768. Paripācitesūti [V 0.0202] sādhitesu. “Vihitesū”ti ettha duddhādīsu viya bhūtakālatā nādhippetāti āha “visayavisesanamattamevā”ti. “Kammaṃ, sippa”nti paññā kāraṇūpacārena vuttāti āha “paññā eva vā…pe… veditabbā”ti.

768. ‘Paripācitesu’ means ‘accomplished’ (sādhitesu). Regarding ‘vihitesu,’ here, unlike with milk and so on, the past tense is not intended—thus it is said, ‘it is merely a specification of the object.’ ‘Kammaṃ, sippaṃ’ (action, skill)—wisdom is spoken of metaphorically as a cause, thus it is said, ‘or wisdom alone should be understood… and so on.’

Kusalaṃ [M 0.0203] kammaṃ sakaṃ ekantaṃ hitasukhāvahattā. Tappaṭipakkhattā itaraṃ akusalaṃ kammaṃ nosakaṃ. Saccapaṭivedhānulomanaṃ saccānulomanaṃ vuttanti āha “tappaṭivedhapaccayabhāvenā”ti. Maggasaccassa anulomanato vā saccānulomikatā, tathā paramatthasaccassa anulomanato. Tenāha aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “maggasaccassā”tiādi. Paññā vuttā paññāvisaye paññākiccassa dassitattā. “Yogavihitesū”tiādinā vuttabhūminiddeso, “kammassakataṃ saccānulomika”nti vuttasarūpaniddeso, “rūpaṃ anicca”ntiādinā vuttappakāraniddeso ca yathāvuttā…pe… niddesā. “Yogavihitesu kammāyatanesu khantiṃ, kammassakataṃ khantiṃ, ‘rūpaṃ anicca’nti khanti”ntiādinā khantiādipadehi yojetabbā. Olokanaṃ paccakkhakaraṇaṃ. Dhammā olokanaṃ khamantīti paññāya tadolokanasamatthatamāha.

Wholesome kamma is one’s own because it exclusively brings benefit and happiness. Its opposite, unwholesome kamma, is not one’s own. Conformity with the realization of truth is called conformity with truth, as it is said: ‘Because it is a condition for the realization of that.’ Conformity with truth is so called either because it conforms to the truth of the path or because it conforms to the ultimate truth. Therefore, the commentary states: ‘of the truth of the path,’ and so on. Wisdom is spoken of because the function of wisdom is shown in the sphere of wisdom. The exposition of the grounds, as stated by ‘in the places for endeavor,’ etc., the exposition of the nature, as stated by ‘ownership of kamma as conforming to truth,’ and the exposition of the mode, as stated by ‘form is impermanent,’ etc., are to be understood as previously explained… up to the expositions. The terms such as ‘acquiescence in the places for endeavor,’ ‘acquiescence in ownership of kamma,’ ‘acquiescence in “form is impermanent,”’ etc., should be connected with the words like ‘acquiescence.’ Inspection is direct perception. Because phenomena endure inspection, it is said that wisdom has the capacity for such inspection.

769. Muñcatīti pajahati. Ārabbha-kiriyāya adhiṭṭhānaṃ samaṅgibhāvo, adhikaraṇaṃ paṭṭhapananti āha “muñca…pe… vattuṃ yutta”nti.

769. ‘Muñcati’ means ‘to abandon’ (pajahati). Determination by means of initiating action is the state of being endowed; the basis is establishment—thus it is said, ‘Muñca… and so on… it is fitting to speak.’

770. Pañcasīladasasīlāni kammavaṭṭekadesabhūtāni sandhāya tesaṃ dhammaṭṭhitiyaṃ samavarodho vutto. Satipi savaneti “idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako pāṇātipātā paṭivirato”tiādinā (a. ni. 8.39; katā. 480) tathāgatato savane satipi. Bhikkhuādīnampi taṃ vuttaṃ adhisīlapaññāpanaṃ viya na buddhāveṇikanti.

770. The five precepts and the ten precepts are mentioned as being part of the cycle of kamma, and their inclusion in the stability of the Dhamma is stated. Even when there is hearing, it is said: ‘Here, bhikkhus, a noble disciple abstains from killing living beings,’ and so on (A. Ni. 8.39; Kathā. 480), even when there is hearing from the Tathāgata. And this is said even of bhikkhus and others, as the exposition of higher virtue, but it is not unique to the Buddhas.

Adhipaññānibbattesūti ṭhapetvā adhipaññaṃ tadaññesu maggaphaladhammesu. Tadadhiṭṭhānesūti tassā adhipaññāya adhiṭṭhānesu vipassanādhammesu.

‘Adhipaññānibbattesū’ means, setting aside superior wisdom itself, in the other path and fruition states. ‘Tadadhiṭṭhānesū’ means in the insight phenomena that are the foundations for that superior wisdom.

771. Apāyuppādanaṃ avaḍḍhinibbattanaṃ. Tasmiṃyeva ṭhāneti tasmiṃyeva khaṇe.

771. The production of states of misery (apāyuppādanaṃ) is the generation of non-growth (avaḍḍhinibbattanaṃ). ‘In that very place’ (tasmiṃyeva ṭhāne) means ‘in that very moment’ (tasmiṃyeva khaṇe).

Tikaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Triads is concluded.

4. Catukkaniddesavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Exposition of the Fours

793. Paritassanaṃ [V 0.0203] parittāso, cittutrāso cāti “na paritassatī”ti padassa “na pattheti na uttasatī”ti atthamāha.

793. Agitation is minor fear, and trembling of the mind—thus, the meaning of the phrase ‘he does not agitate’ is explained as ‘he does not crave, he does not tremble.’

796. Ariyasaccesu [M 0.0204] dhammasaddo “diṭṭhadhammo”tiādīsu viya. Ariyamaggo, tassa ca phalaṃ dhammo yathānusiṭṭhaṃ paṭipanne apāyesu apatamāne dhāretīti. Tattha paññāti tasmiṃ ariyamaggaphale nissayabhūte paññā. Tenāha “taṃsahagatā”ti. Aviditaṃ viditaṃ viya neti ñāpetīti nayo, anumānaṃ, tassa nayanaṃ pavattanaṃ, taṃ pana visuṃyevekaṃ ñāṇuppādananti āsaṅkāya nivattanatthamāha “na añña…pe… viseso”ti. Attano hi adhigamānusārena parādhigatānaṃ kālattaye maggādīnaṃ pavattiākārānumānaṃ nayanayanaṃ. Anuminanākārameva hissa sandhāya vuttaṃ “ñāṇasseva pavattiviseso”ti. Kāraṇañca nayanayanassa saccesu paccakkhapavattanato. “Tathā”ti iminā yathā maggañāṇato aññāpi “iminā dhammenā”ti vattuṃ yuttaṃ, tathā pakārantarenapi “iminā dhammena ñāṇenā”ti ettha attho yujjatīti imamatthaṃ upasaṃharati. Tenāti tasmā ñāṇena ñātato sampayogehi nayanayanato. Ñāṇavisayabhāvenāti paṭivedhañāṇassa visayabhāvena. Ñātena paṭividdhena catusaccadhammena, ñāṇasampayogena vā ñātena jānitvā ṭhitena maggaphaladhammena.

796. The term ‘dhamma’ in the Noble Truths is used as in ‘diṭṭhadhammo’ (the seen dhamma) and similar contexts. The Noble Path and its fruit are called ‘dhamma’ because they uphold one who practices as instructed, preventing a fall into the lower realms. Here, ‘paññā’ refers to the wisdom rooted in that Noble Path and its fruit. Hence it is said, ‘associated with that.’ It makes the unknown known, thus it is called ‘nayo’ (method), inference, the act of leading or directing it. However, to dispel the doubt that this is merely the arising of a distinct knowledge, it is stated, ‘not another… but a distinction.’ For one infers the manner of occurrence in the three times of the path and other factors realized by others, based on one’s own realization. The phrase ‘a distinction in the functioning of knowledge’ is said with reference to this very manner of inferring. The reason for this inferential process is its direct occurrence in the truths. By ‘Tathā’ (thus), it summarizes this meaning: just as it is fitting to say ‘by this dhamma,’ which is other than path-knowledge, so too in another way, the meaning ‘by this dhamma, by this knowledge’ is suitable here. ‘Tena’ means therefore: because it is known by knowledge, and because of inferring by means of associated states. ‘By being the object of knowledge’ means by being the object of penetrating knowledge. By the known and penetrated dhamma of the Four Truths, or by the path and fruition dhamma which is known through association with knowledge and which is established as understood.

Sabbena sabbanti sabbappakārena sabbaṃ, anavasesanti attho. Addhattayapariyāpannañhi sabbaṃ tebhūmakasaṅkhāragataṃ sammasīyati. Nayanatoti nayaggāhato. Anurūpatthavācako vā kāraṇasaddo “kāraṇaṃ vadatī”tiādīsu viya.

‘Sabbena sabbaṃ’ means ‘everything in every way,’ that is, ‘without remainder.’ For all that is included in the three periods of time is to be contemplated as conditioned phenomena belonging to the three realms. ‘Nayanato’ means ‘by grasping the chief method.’ Or, the word ‘kāraṇa’ is a term indicating suitability, like in examples such as ‘he speaks the reason’ and so on.

Anvayañāṇassapi pariyogāhetvā pavattanato saviseso visayāvabodhoti vuttaṃ “dhamme ñāṇa…pe… abhāvā”ti. Visayobhāsanamattajānanasāmaññenāti asatipi abhisamecca gahaṇe visayavibhāvanasaṅkhātaavabodhasāmaññamattena. “Ñāṇa”nti sammatesūti “ñāṇa”nti voharitesu laddhañāṇavohāresu. Sammutivasenāti dhammañāṇādi viya samukhena visaye appavattitvā paññattimukhena pavattaṃ. Avasesanti sammutiñāṇamevāha. Itarañāṇattayavisabhāganti dhammañāṇādiñāṇattayavidhuraṃ.

The knowledge of sequence (anvayañāṇa) is also called a distinctive comprehension of the object because it operates by thoroughly investigating, hence it is said, ‘knowledge of the Dhamma… up to absence.’ ‘By the mere generality of knowing the mere appearance of the object’—even without full penetration, by grasping through comprehension, it is merely a generality of comprehension consisting of clarifying the object. ‘Knowledge’ is used in accepted terms—in expressions where the term ‘knowledge’ is conventionally acquired. ‘By way of convention’—like knowledge of the Dhamma, etc.—it operates through designation, not operating directly on the object. ‘The remainder’ refers only to conventional knowledge. It is dissimilar to the other three kinds of knowledge—namely, devoid of the three knowledges such as knowledge of the Dhamma.

797. Kāmabhavadhammeti [V 0.0204] kāmabhavasaṅkhāte dhamme.

797. ‘Kāmabhavadhamme’ means ‘in phenomena designated as sensual existence.’

798. Sāti [M 0.0205] paṭhamajjhānapaññā. Vītarāgabhāvanāvatthassāti “vītarāgo hotī”ti evaṃ vuttassa. Tanti chaṭṭhābhiññaṃ. Maggañāṇañhi kiccato maggasaccampi paṭivijjhati. Itarāti heṭṭhimamaggapaññā. Tadupanissayattāti tassā chaṭṭhābhiññāya, tassa vā paṭivijjhanassa upanissayattā paṭivijjhati nāma. Yathānurūpanti diṭṭhāsavādīnaṃ yathānurūpaṃ. Āsavakkhayeti āsavakkhayapariyāye kāraṇūpacārena. Taṃnibbattanatoti tassa āsavakkhayasaṅkhātassa phalassa nibbattanato. Idañca “āsavānaṃ khaye ñāṇaṃ chaṭṭhābhiññā”ti sutte āgatattā vuttaṃ.

798. ‘Sā’ (that) refers to the wisdom of the first jhāna. ‘Vītarāgabhāvanāvatthassa’ refers to what is stated as ‘he is detached.’ ‘Taṃ’ (that) is the sixth higher knowledge. For knowledge of the path, by its function, also penetrates the truth of the path. ‘Itara’ (the other) refers to the wisdom of the lower paths. ‘Because of being a proximate condition for that’ means because of being a proximate condition for that sixth higher knowledge, or for that penetration, it is called ‘penetration.’ ‘According to suitability’ means as is fitting for the canker of views and the others. ‘Āsavakkhaye’ (in the destruction of the cankers) is a metaphorical expression for the cause, in the context of the destruction of the cankers. ‘From the production of that’ means from the production of that result known as the destruction of the cankers. And this is stated because in the sutta it is said: ‘Knowledge in the destruction of the cankers is the sixth higher knowledge.’

801. Abhivisiṭṭhena vā ñāṇena pākaṭaṃ karontassāti adhigamavasena pakāsaṃ vibhūtaṃ karontassa.

801. ‘Or by making it manifest with superior knowledge’ means by making it clear and distinct through attainment.

802. Vasitāpañcakarahitaṃ vasibhāvaṃ apāpitaṃ paṭiladdhamattaṃ. Paṭipadārammaṇasahagatā paññā paṭipadārammaṇasambandhinīti āha “paññāya paṭipadārammaṇuddesenā”ti.

802. ‘Devoid of the fivefold mastery’ means having just attained mastery, not having had mastery fully developed. ‘Wisdom accompanied by the meditation subject’ means wisdom connected with the meditation subject. Thus it is said, ‘By the designation of the meditation subject through wisdom.’

Catukkaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Fours is concluded.

5. Pañcakaniddesavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Exposition of the Fives

804. Tameva paññaṃ “dvīsu jhānesu paññā pītipharaṇenā”tiādinā vibhajati. Abhisandanaparisandanaparipūraṇānipi parippharaṇaṃ viya pharaṇāpītiyā, taṃsahagatasukhassa ca kiccavisesabhūtāni adhippetānīti āha “abhisandetīti…pe… veditabba”nti. Ādinā nayenāti “abhisandetī”tiādinā (dī. ni. 1.226; ma. ni. 1.427) sutte āgatanayena. Pharaṇañcettha pītisukhasamuṭṭhitapaṇītarūpehi kāyassa abhibyāpanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ārammaṇeti pītipharaṇatāsukhapharaṇatāsīsena vuttānaṃ tikadukajhānānaṃ ārammaṇe. Tāti pītipharaṇatāsukhapharaṇatā.

804. He analyzes that same wisdom with the words, “wisdom in the two jhānas by the pervasion of rapture,” and so on. Drenching, steeping, and filling, like spreading, are also intended as specific functions of pervading rapture and its associated happiness. Thus he says, “It drenches… should be understood.” “By the method beginning with” means by the method that comes in the sutta beginning with “it drenches” (Dī. Ni. 1.226; Ma. Ni. 1.427). And here, pervasion should be seen as the suffusion of the body with the refined matter arising from rapture and happiness. “In the object” means in the object of the jhānas of the triad and dyad, spoken of under the headings of the state of pervasion by rapture and the state of pervasion by happiness. “That” refers to the state of pervasion by rapture and the state of pervasion by happiness.

Samādhimukhenāti [V 0.0205] samādhiṃ mukhaṃ pamukhaṃ katvā, samādhisīsenāti attho, samādhipamukhena vā uddesaniddesena. Aññe kilesā diṭṭhimānādayo[M 0.0206]. Appayogenāti jhānavimokkhādīnaṃ viya uppādanīyaparikammapayogena vinā. Āvajjanāsadiso hi phalasamāpattiattho sammasanacāro. Ṭhapitattāti pavattitattā. Satibahulatāyāti satiyā abhiṇhuppattiyā. Paricchindanasatiyā kālassa satoti dassetīti yojanā.

“By way of concentration” means having made concentration the front, the principal; the meaning is “with concentration as the head,” or by way of exposition and explanation with concentration as principal. “Other defilements” means wrong view, conceit, and so on. “Without effort” means without the application of preliminary work that must be undertaken, as in the case of the jhānas, liberations, etc. For the practice of reviewing for the sake of the attainment of fruition is similar to adverting. “Because it is established” means because it has been set in motion. “Through abundance of mindfulness” means through the frequent arising of mindfulness. The construction is that he shows that the mindfulness that delimits is “mindfulness of time.”

Pañcakaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Fives is finished.

6. Chakkaniddesavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Exposition of the Sixes

805. Visuddhibhāvanti visuddhiyā sabbhāvaṃ. “Dibbacakkhuñāṇekadesattā”ti idaṃ tassa paribhaṇḍañāṇattā vuttaṃ. Tathā hi pāḷiyaṃ “sattānaṃ cutūpapātañāṇāya cittaṃ abhinīharati abhininnāmetī”ti (dī. ni. 1.247) ārabhitvā “so dibbena cakkhunā visuddhenā”tiādi (dī. ni. 1.246) vuttaṃ. Dibbassa tirohitavippakaṭṭhādibhedassa, itarassa ca rūpāyatanassa dassanasamatthassāpi dibbacakkhuñāṇassa sikhāpatti cavamānopapajjamānasattadassananti āha “muddhappattena cā”tiādi.

805. “The state of purity” means the true nature of purity. “Because it is a part of the knowledge of the divine eye” is said because it is an ancillary knowledge to that. For in the Pāli, beginning with “He directs and inclines his mind to the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings” (D I 82), it is said, “with the divine eye, which is purified…” (D I 82). The culmination of the knowledge of the divine eye—which is capable of seeing the visible object, both divine, differentiated as hidden, remote, etc., and otherwise—is the seeing of beings passing away and reappearing. Thus he says, “with the culmination,” etc.

Chakkaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Sixes is finished.

7. Sattakaniddesavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Exposition of the Sevens

806. Chabbidhampi paccavekkhaṇañāṇanti “jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇanti ñāṇa”ntiādinā (vibha. 806) vuttaṃ paṭiccasamuppādaṅgānaṃ paccavekkhaṇavasena pavattañāṇaṃ. Saha gahetvāti ekajjhaṃ gahetvā vipassanārammaṇabhāvasāmaññena ekattena gahetvā. Saṅkhipitvā vuttenāti pubbe chadhā [V 0.0206] vuttaṃ viya dassitaṃ dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇanti evaṃ saṅkhipitvā vuttena. “Khayadhamma”ntiādinā pakārena dassananti sambandho. Pavattañāṇassāti “jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇa”ntiādinā pavattassa ñāṇassa, pavatte vā saṃsāravaṭṭe ñāṇassa. Ñāṇārammaṇā vipassanā ñāṇavipassanā. Vipassanāti ca “jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇa”ntiādinā [M 0.0207] paccayapaccayuppannadhamme vibhāgena dassanato dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇaṃ idhādhippetaṃ. Tassa khayadhammatādijānanaṃ paṭivipassanā. Tenāha “vipassanāpaṭivipassanādassanamatta”nti.

806. “The sixfold reviewing knowledge” means the knowledge that proceeds by way of reviewing the factors of dependent origination, as stated in “the knowledge that ‘with birth as condition, there is aging-and-death’” (Vibh 138), etc. “Taken together” means taken as one, gathered together, taken as a unity through the commonality of being an object for insight. “By what is stated concisely” means by what is stated concisely thus: “the knowledge of the stability of phenomena,” which was shown as if stated in six ways before. The connection is that it shows it in the manner of “subject to destruction,” etc. “Of the knowledge that proceeds” means of the knowledge that proceeds as “with birth as condition, there is aging-and-death,” etc., or knowledge in the ongoing round of saṃsāra. Insight that has knowledge as its object is knowledge-insight. And here “insight” is intended as the knowledge of the stability of phenomena, which sees by way of division the conditional and conditionally arisen phenomena, as in “with birth as condition, there is aging-and-death,” etc. The knowing of its nature of being subject to destruction, etc., is counter-insight. Therefore he says, “the mere seeing of insight and counter-insight.”

Evamettha aṭṭhakathādhippāyavasena pāḷiyā atthaṃ dassetvā idāni attano adhippāyavasena dassetuṃ “pāḷiyaṃ panā”tiādimāha. Sabbatthāti addhattaye paccayavisesena paccayuppannavisesaniddhāraṇe. Ñāṇavacanenāti “jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇa”ntiādinā ñāṇassa gahaṇena. Aṅgānanti sattasattatiyā aṅgānaṃ. Itisaddenāti “nirodhadhamma”nti ettha vuttaitisaddena. Pakāsetvāti ñāṇassa pavattiākāraṃ jotetvā. Tena dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇato aññaṃyeva pariyosāne vuttaṃ ñāṇanti dasseti. Tenāha “vipassanāñāṇaṃ sattamaṃ ñāṇa”nti. Ayameva cettha attho yuttoti dassento “na hī”tiādimāha. Tattha “tampi ñāṇanti sambandho na hotī”ti evaṃ sambandho na yutto aṅgantarabhāvassa avibhāvanatoti attho. Tena vuttaṃ “taṃñāṇa…pe… anadhippetattā”ti. Na hi visuṃ visuṃ vuttameva ekajjhaṃ vacanamattena atthantaraṃ hotīti. “Khayadhammaṃ…pe… cā”ti iminā purimasmiṃ pakkhe upacayena dosamāha.

Having thus shown the meaning of the Pāli here according to the intention of the commentary, now, to show it according to his own intention, he says, “But in the Pāli…,” etc. “Everywhere” means in the determination of the specific conditionally arisen phenomenon by the specific condition in the three periods of time. “By the word ‘knowledge’” means by the taking up of knowledge with “with birth as condition, there is aging-and-death,” etc. “Of the factors” means of the seventy-seven factors. “By the word iti” means by the word iti stated here in “subject to cessation.” “Having illuminated” means having lit up the mode of proceeding of the knowledge. By this he shows that the knowledge stated at the conclusion is indeed different from the knowledge of the stability of phenomena. Therefore he says, “Insight knowledge is the seventh knowledge.” Showing that this is the suitable meaning here, he says, “For not…,” etc. Therein, the meaning is that a connection such as “that too is knowledge” is not suitable because the state of being another factor is not clarified. Therefore it is said, “that knowledge… because it is not intended.” For it is not that what is stated separately becomes something with a different meaning merely by being spoken of together. With “subject to destruction…,” etc., he states the fault in the previous position by way of accumulation.

Sattakaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Sevens is finished.

8. Aṭṭhakaniddesavaṇṇanā

8. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Eights

808. Paccanīkadhammeti nīvaraṇādipaccanīkadhamme. Dukkhanti samāpajjane asati uppajjanakadukkhaṃ.

808. “Opposing states” means the opposing states such as the hindrances. “Suffering” means the suffering that arises when there is no attainment.

Aṭṭhakaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Eights is finished.

10. Dasakaniddeso

10. The Exposition of the Tens

Paṭhamabalaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Exposition of the First Power

809. Na [V 0.0207] ṭhānanti aṭṭhānaṃ, anupalabbhanattho ayamakāroti āha “avijjamānaṃ ṭhānaṃ aṭṭhāna”nti. Abhāvattho vā, na aññapaṭipakkhādiatthoti āha “natthi ṭhānanti vā aṭṭhāna”nti. Ko panetassa atthadvayassa [M 0.0208] visesoti? Paṭhamo hetupaccayehi anupalabbhamānataṃ vadati, dutiyo sabbena sabbaṃ abhāvanti ayametesaṃ viseso. Taṇhupādānādīnampi sukhato upagamanassa hetubhāve diṭṭhivipallāsassa so sātisayo asukhepi daḷhaṃ pavattāpanatoti āha “diṭṭhivipallāsova…pe… adhippeta”nti. “Attadiṭṭhivasenā”ti kasmā visesetvā vuttaṃ, nanu ariyasāvakassa sabbāpi diṭṭhiyo natthīti? Saccaṃ natthi, attadiṭṭhisannissayā pana sabbadiṭṭhiyoti dassetuṃ “attadiṭṭhivasenāti padhānadiṭṭhimāhā”ti vuttaṃ. Bhedānurūpassa vatthuno. Bhedānurūpena “adhamme dhammo”tiādinayappavattena.

809. “Not a basis” means an impossibility. The 'a-' prefix here has the sense of 'not being found'; thus he says: “An impossibility is a basis that does not exist.” Or it has the sense of absence, not the sense of 'other,' 'opposite,' etc.; thus he says: “Or an impossibility is ‘there is no basis.’” Now what is the difference between these two meanings? The first speaks of its not being found on account of causes and conditions; the second speaks of its complete and total absence. This is the difference between them. Since the distortion of view, being excessive, firmly establishes one even in what is suffering by treating craving, clinging, and so on as a cause for arriving at happiness, he says: “It is the distortion of view... that is intended.” Why is it specified “by way of the view of self”? Is it not the case that a noble disciple has no views at all? True, he has none. But to show that all views are dependent on the view of self, it is said: “By way of the view of self”: he states the principal view. Of the subject matter that accords with the division. By means of what accords with the division, proceeding by the method beginning “in what is not the Dhamma, the Dhamma....”

So evāti yo liṅge aparivatte tasmiṃ attabhāve bhavaṅgajīvitindriyappabandho, so eva. Tañhi upādāya ekajātisamaññā, na cettha bhāvakalāpajīvitindriyassa vasena codanā kātabbā tadaññasseva adhippetattā. Tañhi tattha avicchedavuttiyā pabandhavohāraṃ labhati, itarampi vā bhāvānupālanatāsāmaññenāti anokāsāva codanā.

“That very one”: that which, when the gender is unchanged, is the continuity of the life-continuum and the life faculty in that same individual existence—that is the very one. For based on that, there is the designation “a single birth.” And here no objection should be raised concerning the life faculty of the material group of existence, since something else is intended by that. For the former obtains the term “continuity” because of its uninterrupted occurrence, while the latter does so because of the commonality of sustaining the state of existence. Thus the objection is baseless.

Sapattavasena yojetabbanti “sapattaṃ māremīti abhisandhinā sapattena nipannaṭṭhāne nipannaṃ manussabhūto manussabhūtaṃ mātaraṃ pitaraṃ vā mārento”tiādinā yojetabbaṃ. Sabbatthāti catūsupi vikappesu. Purimaṃ abhisandhicittanti pubbabhāgiyo maraṇādhippāyo. Appamāṇaṃ tena atthasiddhiyā abhāvato. Puthujjanasseva taṃ dinnaṃ hotīti ettha yathā arahattaṃ patvā paribhuttampi puthujjanakāle dinnaṃ puthujjanadānameva hoti, evaṃ maraṇādhippāyena puthujjanakāle pahāre dinne arahattaṃ patvā teneva pahārena mate kasmā arahantaghātoyeva hoti, na puthujjanaghātoti? Visesasambhavato. Yathā hi dānaṃ deyyadhammassa pariccāgamattena hoti, na evaṃ vadho. So hi pāṇo, pāṇasaññitā, vadhakacetanā, upakkamo, tena maraṇanti imesaṃ pañcannaṃ aṅgānaṃ pāripūriyāva hoti, na apāripūriyā. Tasmā arahattaṃ pattasseva maraṇanti arahantaghātoyeva hoti[V 0.0208], na puthujjanaghāto. Yasmā pana “imaṃ māremī”ti yaṃ santānaṃ ārabbha māraṇicchā, tassa puthujjanakhīṇāsavabhāvena payogamaraṇakkhaṇānaṃ vasena satipi santānabhede abhedoyeva. Yadā ca atthasiddhi, tadā khīṇāsavabhāvo. Tasmā arahantaghātova [M 0.0209] hotīti nicchitaṃ. Kathaṃ panettha vadhakacetanā vattamānavisayā siyāti āha “vadhakacittaṃ paccuppannārammaṇampi…pe… pavattatī”ti. Tattha pabandhavicchedavasenāti yena pabandho vicchijjati, tādisaṃ payogaṃ nibbattetīti attho. Tena yadā pabandhavicchedo, tadā arahāti yathāvuttaṃ arahantaghātaṃ patiṭṭhāpeti. Na evanti yathā kālantarāpekkhakiccasiddhaṃ vadhakacittaṃ, na evaṃ cāgacetanā. “Sā hī”tiādinā cāgacetanāya kālantarānapekkhakiccasiddhitaṃyeva vibhāveti. Aññasakakaraṇanti attato vinimocetvā aññassa dakkhiṇeyyassa santakabhāvakaraṇaṃ. Tassāti cajitabbassa vatthuno. Yassāti yassa puthujjanassa. Tasseva taṃ dinnaṃ hoti, sacepi arahattaṃ patvā tena paribhuttanti attho.

It should be connected by way of an enemy, thus: 'A human being, with the intention, "I will kill my enemy," kills his mother or father, who are human beings, lying in the place where his enemy was lying,' and so on. 'In all cases': in all four alternatives. 'The prior intentional thought': the preliminary intention to kill. 'Immeasurable': because the goal is not accomplished by it. Regarding the statement, 'It is given only to a worldling': Here, just as what was given when one was a worldling remains a gift to a worldling even if it is consumed after one has attained arahantship, so too, when a blow is delivered with the intention to kill while one is a worldling, and the person dies from that very blow after attaining arahantship, why is it the killing of an arahant and not the killing of a worldling? Because of the possibility of a distinction. For giving comes about merely by relinquishing the object to be given, but killing is not like that. It comes about only through the complete fulfillment of these five factors, not through their incomplete fulfillment: a living being, the perception of it as a living being, the volition to kill, the effort, and the resulting death. Therefore, since the death occurs when he has attained arahantship, it is the killing of an arahant, not the killing of a worldling. However, since the desire to kill arises in regard to a certain continuity with the thought, 'I will kill this one,' there is no division in that continuity, even though there is a difference between the state of a worldling and that of one whose taints are destroyed at the respective moments of the effort and of death. And when the goal is accomplished, the state is that of one whose taints are destroyed. Therefore, it is settled that it is the killing of an arahant. How can the volition to kill have a present object here? He says: 'The mind set on killing also proceeds...pe... with a present object.' Therein, 'by way of severing the continuity' means: it produces such an effort by which the continuity is severed. Thus, when the continuity is severed, the person is an arahant; in this way, as stated, he establishes it as the killing of an arahant. It is not so: the volition of giving is not like the mind set on killing, which accomplishes its task with respect to a future time. By the words beginning 'For it,' he explains that the volition of giving accomplishes its task without depending on a future time. 'Making it another's property': freeing it from oneself and making it the possession of another who is worthy of offerings. 'Of that': of the object to be given up. 'Of whom': of that worldling. It is given to that very one, even if he consumes it after attaining arahantship—this is the meaning.

“Kappavināse”ti idaṃ “saṇṭhahante kappe”ti vuttattā mahākappavināsaṃ sandhāya vuttanti āha “kappaṭṭhakathāya na sametī”ti ettha āyukappassa adhippetattā. Āyukappo cettha avīciyaṃ nibbattasattānaṃ antarakappaparimāṇaṃ paramāyu veditabbaṃ. Tañhi sandhāya “ekaṃ kappaṃ asītibhāge katvā tato ekabhāgamattaṃ kāla”nti (kathā. aṭṭha. 654-657) vuttaṃ. Tayidaṃ “ekaṃ kappa”nti yadi ekaṃ mahākappanti attho, tathā sati vīsatiantarakappaparimāṇo eko asaṅkhyeyyakappoti vuttaṃ hoti. Atha ekaṃ asaṅkhyeyyakappanti attho, sabbathāpi “catusaṭṭhi antarakappā”ti vacanena virujjhatīti vīmaṃsitabbaṃ. Yathā pana kappaṭṭhakathāya ayaṃ aṭṭhakathā sameti, taṃ dassetuṃ “kappavināseyevāti panā”tiādimāha.

The statement 'at the destruction of the aeon' was said with reference to the destruction of a great aeon, because it is said 'when the aeon is ending.' He says, 'It does not agree with the commentary on the aeon,' because here a life-span aeon is intended. Here, the life-span aeon should be understood as the maximum life span for beings reborn in Avīci, which has the measure of an intermediate aeon. It is with reference to this that it is said: 'Having divided one aeon into eighty parts, the time is the measure of one part of that.' Herein, if 'one aeon' means one great aeon, in that case it would mean that one incalculable aeon has the measure of twenty intermediate aeons. If it means one incalculable aeon, then in every case it contradicts the statement 'sixty-four intermediate aeons.' This should be investigated. However, to show how this commentary agrees with the commentary on the aeon, he says what begins with: 'But it is precisely at the destruction of the aeon...'

Pakatatto vā apārājiko. Samānasaṃvāsako kammaladdhīnaṃ vasena anānāsaṃvāsakoti evamettha attho veditabbo.

Or one who is not subject to defeat by nature. One who is of equal communion becomes one of unequal communion on account of the ways of receiving the formal act. Thus the meaning should be understood here.

Niyatassa puggalassa vijjamānataṃ paṭisedhetvāti yojanā. Tattha paṭisedhetvāti “puggalo pana niyato nāma natthī”ti evaṃ paṭisedhetvā. Tattha kāraṇamāha “micchattasammattaniyatadhammānaṃ viya sabhāvato”ti. Paññattimattañhetaṃ micchattasammattaniyatadhammanissayaṃ, yadidaṃ niyato puggaloti[V 0.0209]. Yathāpucchitanti “kiṃ pubbahetu niyametī”tiādinā pucchitappakāraṃ niyāmakahetuṃ. Yenāti yena uparimaggattayavipassanāñāṇena. Niyatāniyatabhedanti [M 0.0210] sotāpannādiniyatabhedaṃ, sattakkhattuparamādianiyatabhedañca. Sotāpanno eva hi eko sattakkhattuparamo nāma hoti, eko kolaṃkolo nāma, eko ekabījī nāmāti sotāpannassa niyatabhāvo vuttoti āha “sotāpanno ca niyato”ti. Byatirekattho hi ayaṃ ca-saddo. Tato pubbeti sotāpattimaggato pubbe. “Pubbahetukiccaṃ natthī”ti idaṃ sotāpannassa niyatatāya vuttattā vakkhamānañca dosaṃ hadaye ṭhapetvā vuttaṃ. Uparimaggānaṃ saupanissayatte paṭhamamaggassāpi saupanissayatā siddhā evāti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “yadi hī”tiādi. Tañca niyatattaṃ. Assāti sotāpattimaggassa.

The construction is: 'Having denied the existence of a fixed person.' Herein, 'having denied' means: having denied thus, 'There is no such thing as a fixed person.' He states the reason for this: 'by nature, like states fixed in wrongness or rightness.' For this 'fixed person' is a mere designation dependent on states fixed in wrongness or rightness. 'As was asked': the determining cause, the manner of which was asked about with the words beginning, 'What prior cause determines it?' 'By which': by the insight knowledge of the three higher paths. 'The distinction between the fixed and the unfixed': the fixed distinction of the stream-enterer, etc., and the unfixed distinction of the seven-times-at-most, etc. For a single stream-enterer may be one called 'seven-times-at-most,' or one called 'family-to-family,' or one called 'single-seed.' Thus the fixed state of the stream-enterer is stated. Hence he says: 'And a stream-enterer is fixed.' The particle ca here has a contrastive sense. 'Before that': before the path of stream-entry. The statement 'There is no task for a prior cause' is said because of the fixed nature of the stream-enterer, and it is said keeping in mind the fault that will be mentioned. With reference to the objection that if the higher paths have a decisive support condition, the first path's having a decisive support condition is also established, he says what begins with 'For if...' And that fixed state. 'Of it': of the path of stream-entry.

Teneva khīṇāti sotāpattimaggeneva khīṇā. Kāraṇupacchedena hi phalupacchedo siyā. Tatoti sattakkhattuparamādito. Sāti sattakkhattuparamāditā. Pavattitoti vipākappabandhato. Tenāti sotāpattimaggena. Vuṭṭhāneti vuṭṭhāne sati. Kāraṇena vinā phalaṃ natthīti āha “sakkāya…pe… bhavitabba”nti. “Nāmakaraṇanimittato”ti iminā nāmakaraṇahetutāya niyāmakataṃ vibhāveti ekabījiādisamaññānaṃ anvatthasaññābhāvato. Tenāha “vipassanā…pe… sandhāya vutta”nti.

'Exhausted by that': exhausted by the path of stream-entry itself. For with the cutting off of the cause, there would be the cutting off of the fruit. 'From that': from the state of being a seven-times-at-most, etc. 'That': the state of being a seven-times-at-most, etc. 'Has occurred': because of the continuity of the resultant. 'By that': by the path of stream-entry. 'In emerging': when there is emergence. Since there is no fruit without a cause, he says: 'Identity view...pe... must be.' By this, 'from the sign for making the name,' he explains the determinative nature as being the cause for making the name, because designations such as 'single-seed' are not meaningful terms in themselves. Therefore he says: 'Insight...pe... was spoken with reference to.'

Ādi-saddena “ekomhi sammāsambuddho, sītībhūtosmi nibbuto”tiādīni (mahāva. 11; kathā. 405; ma. ni. 1.285) saṅgayhanti. Ettha ca “sadiso me na vijjati, ekomhi sammāsambuddho (mahāva. 11; kathā. 405; ma. ni. 1.285). ‘Atthetarahi aññe samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā bhagavatā samasamā sambodhiya’nti evaṃ puṭṭho ahaṃ, bhante, ‘no’ti vadeyya”ntiādi (dī. ni. 3.161) vacanehi imissā lokadhātuyā viya aññassa buddhassa aññissā lokadhātuyā uppādo nivāritoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Na hi vijjamāne “sadiso me na vijjatī”tiādi sakkā vattuṃ. Yaṃ pana vadanti “lokadhātuvisesāpekkhāya vutta”nti, tampi natthi tathā visesanassa abhāvato, buddhānubhāvassa ca asamatthabhāvavibhāvanato. Āṇākhettakittanañcettha dhammatādassanatthaṃ. Sakkoti hi bhagavā yattha yattha icchati, tattha tattha āṇaṃ [M 0.0211] vattetuṃ. “Ekissā lokadhātuyā”ti ca idaṃ buddhakhettabhūtāya lokadhātuyā dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tatthāyamattho – buddhakhettabhūtā ekāvāyaṃ lokadhātu. Tattha ekasmiṃ kāle eko eva sammāsambuddho uppajjatīti. Tenāha “buddhakhetta…pe… adhippāyo”ti.

By the word 'etcetera,' passages such as "I am the one Perfectly Self-Enlightened One; I have become cool, I am extinguished" (Mv 11; Kvu 405; MN I 285) are included. Here, it should be understood that by statements such as "My equal does not exist, I am the one Perfectly Self-Enlightened One" (Mv 11; Kvu 405; MN I 285), and "Venerable sir, if I were asked, ‘Are there now other ascetics or brahmins equal to the Blessed One in perfect enlightenment?’ I would say, ‘No’" (DN III 161), the arising of another Buddha in another world-system is precluded, just as in this world-system. For if one existed, it would not be possible to say, "My equal does not exist," and so on. As for what some say, that this was spoken with reference to a specific kind of world-system, that too is not the case, because there is no such specification and because it would imply an incapacity of the Buddha's power. And the mention here of the sphere of command is for the purpose of showing the fixed nature of things. For the Blessed One is able to extend his command wherever he wishes. The phrase "in one world-system" is stated to show the world-system that is the Buddha-field. Herein, this is the meaning: this one world-system is the Buddha-field. Therein, at one time, only one Perfectly Self-Enlightened One arises. Therefore, he said, "The Buddha-field …pe… is the intention."

Tasmāti [V 0.0210] yasmā upasampadādhīnaṃ pātimokkhaṃ, upasampadā ca pabbajjādhīnā, tasmā. Pātimokkhe siddhe, siddhāsu tāsu pabbajjūpasampadāsu. Tato paraṃ vinaṭṭhaṃ nāma hotīti pacchimapaṭivedhato paraṃ paṭivedhasāsanaṃ, pacchimasīlabhedato ca paraṃ paṭipattisāsanaṃ vinaṭṭhaṃ nāma hotīti sāsanabhāvasāmaññena pana ubhayaṃ ekajjhaṃ katvā dassento “pacchima…pe… ekato katvā”ti āha.

Therefore: since the Pātimokkha is dependent on the higher ordination, and the higher ordination is dependent on the going forth, therefore, when the Pātimokkha is established, that going forth and higher ordination are established. After that, it is called 'perished'—that is, the teaching of penetration after the final penetration and the teaching of practice after the final breach of virtue are called 'perished.' However, showing both together as one by their commonality as the Teaching, he said, "the last …pe… having made them one."

Paridevanakāruññanti paridevanena karuṇāyitabbatā karuṇāyanā.

'Lamentation-and-compassion' means being worthy of compassion on account of lamentation; it is the act of showing compassion.

Dhammānaṃ sabhāvaviseso na sakkā dhāretuṃ, yato pāramīpavicayādīsu udakapariyantaṃ katvā mahāpathavīkampo ahosi, abhisambodhidivase ca ṭhapetvā pubbuttaradisābhāge bodhirukkhamūle bhūmibhāgo mahāpurisaṃ dhāretuṃ nāsakkhi, aññadatthu ekapasse pakkhittaatibhārabharitanāvā viya cakkavāḷagabbho viparivatto. “Samuppādikā”ti vattabbe sa-kāre a-kārassa ā-kāro, ekassa ca pa-kārassa lopo katoti dassento āha “samaṃ uddhaṃ pajjatīti sāmupādikā”ti. Samaṃ upādiyatīti vā samupādā, samupādā eva sāmupādikā, samupāhinīti attho.

The distinctive nature of phenomena cannot be maintained, for when the great earth quaked after defining the limits of the water during the investigation of the perfections, and on the day of supreme enlightenment, except for the location at the foot of the Bodhi tree, the ground in the northeastern direction could not bear the great being—indeed, the entire world-sphere was overturned like an overloaded ship tossed to one side. To show that when "samuppādikā" should be said, the 'a' in the syllable "sa" becomes 'ā,' and one 'p' is elided, it is stated: "It arises evenly upwards, thus it is 'sāmupādikā.'" Or, it is called 'samupādā' because it grasps evenly, and 'samupādā' itself is 'sāmupādikā'—the meaning is 'that which takes up evenly.'

Santatikhaṇavasenāti santativasena āyūhanasamaṅgitā, sapubbapacchābhāgassa gahaṇavasena cetanākkhaṇavasena cetanāsamaṅgitāti yojetabbā. Ekasmiṃ upaṭṭhite paccayavasena tadaññassa upaṭṭhānaṃ parivattanaṃ.

By 'the moment of continuity': it should be construed that by way of continuity it is endowed with accumulation, and by way of grasping its preceding and succeeding parts and by way of the moment of volition, it is endowed with volition. When one thing is present, the presence of another due to a condition is transformation.

Paṭhamabalaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the First Power is finished.

Dutiyabalaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Second Power

810. Bhoge [M 0.0212] bhuñjituṃ na jānāti, vināsetīti yojanā.

810. The construal is: 'He does not know how to enjoy his wealth; he wastes it.'

Lahuparivattitāya jīvitassāti adhippāyo.

The meaning is: because of the swift changing of life.

Na [V 0.0211] adāsi payuttavācāya uppannanti adhippāyena.

He did not give, with the intention that this arose from a careless utterance.

Sammāpayogenāti sammāpaṭipattiyā.

'By right application' means by right practice.

Dutiyabalaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Second Power is finished.

Pañcamabalaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Fifth Power

813. Dhātusabhāvoti bhūtādisaṅkhātadhātūnaṃ sabhāvo. Sabhāgavasena phalabhūtena. Ajjhāsayadhātuparicchindanatoti ajjhāsayasabhāvassa “hīnaṃ, paṇīta”nti vā paricchijja jānanato, vuṭṭhinimittena viya mahoghena uparimeghavuṭṭhiyā.

813. 'The nature of the elements' is the nature of the elements designated as the primary elements and so on, by way of its corresponding aspect, which is the result. 'By delimiting the element of disposition' means knowing by defining the nature of the disposition as 'inferior' or 'superior,' just as one knows of rain from an upper cloud by a great flood as its sign.

Pañcamabalaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Fifth Power is finished.

Chaṭṭhabalaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Sixth Power

Saddattho sambhavati samāsanteneva tathā saddasiddhito. Tesanti paroparānaṃ visadāvisadānaṃ saddhādiindriyānaṃ. Evañca katvāti āsayādito indriyaparopariyattassa, indriyaparopariyattato ca adhimuttibhedassa visiṭṭhasabhāvattā eva.

The meaning of the word arises from the end of the compound itself, due to the word being so formed. 'Of them' refers to the faculties of faith and so on, of higher and lower beings, whether these faculties are clear or unclear. 'And thus' is said because of the specific nature of the superiority and inferiority of the faculties, which is based on disposition and so on, and of the diversity of resolutions, which is based on the superiority and inferiority of the faculties.

815. “Ke pana te ariyāvāsā”ti pucchitvā te sutteneva dassento “idha, bhikkhave”tiādipāḷiṃ āharitvā “evaṃ vuttā”ti nigametvā puna maggādhigameneva tesaṃ adhigamaṃ dassento “etesū”tiādimāha. Tattha itareti chaḷaṅgasamannāgamaekārakkhāsaṅkhāyapaṭisevanādayo.

815. Having asked, "But what are those noble abidings?" he shows them through the sutta itself by citing the passage beginning, "Here, bhikkhus," and concluding with "thus it was said." Then, to indicate their attainment through the path itself, he says what begins with "among these." Herein, 'the others' refers to such things as being endowed with six factors, having one protection, cultivating with reflection, and so on.

816. Ārammaṇasantānānusayanesūti [V 0.0212] ārammaṇānusayanaṃ, santānānusayananti dvīsu anusayanesu. Yathā hi maggena asamucchinno rāgo kāraṇalābhe [M 0.0213] uppajjanāraho thāmagataṭṭhena santāne anusetīti vuccati, evaṃ iṭṭhārammaṇepīti tassa ārammaṇānusayanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Taṃ panassa anusayanaṃ uppattiyā pākaṭaṃ hotīti dassetuṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “yathā nāmā”tiādi (vibha. aṭṭha. 816) vuttaṃ. “Āciṇṇasamāciṇṇā”ti etena iṭṭhārammaṇe rāgassa ciraparibhāvanaṃ vibhāveti. Yasmā pana evaṃ ciraparibhāvitaṃ pariveṭhetvā viya ṭhitaṃ hoti, tasmā “samantato veṭhetvā viya ṭhitabhāvena anusayitataṃ dassetī”ti vuttaṃ. Tathā hi udake nimuggasadiso udāhaṭo. “Sabbepi tebhūmakā dhammā kāmanīyaṭṭhena kāmā”tiādipāḷivasena bhavarāgassāpi vatthukāmatā veditabbā. Rāgavasenāti ārammaṇarajjanavasena.

816. 'In the latent tendencies of object and continuity' refers to the two latent tendencies: the latent tendency based on the object and the latent tendency based on the continuity. Just as lust not cut off by the path, being liable to arise when it obtains a cause, is said to 'lie latent' in the continuity because it has gained strength, so too in a desirable object; thus the latent tendency based on the object should be understood. To show that this latent tendency becomes manifest with its arising, it is said in the commentary: "Just as…" etc. (Vibh-a 816). By 'practiced and well-practiced' he explains the long-term cultivation of lust in regard to a desirable object. Because, having been cultivated for a long time in this way, it remains as if enveloping, therefore it is said, "it shows the state of latency by its state of remaining as if enveloping all around." For the simile of one submerged in water is cited. Based on the Pali passage, "All phenomena of the three planes are 'sensual pleasures' in the sense of being desirable," the lust for existence should also be understood as having sensual pleasures as its basis. 'By way of lust' means by way of lusting for the object.

818. Indriyaviseso vineyyānaṃ indriyaparopariyattaṃ.

818. The distinction of faculties is the superiority and inferiority of the faculties of those to be trained.

819. Pahātabbena upaddutanirodhanatthaṃ pahāyakaṃ pariyesatīti paṭhamaṃ pahātabbaṃ, pacchā pahāyakanti ayaṃ pahātabbapajahanakkamo pahānakkamapadena vutto. Yassāti pahātabbassa. Tanti pahātabbaṃ. Paṭhamaṃ vuccatīti pahānavicāraṇānaṃ paṭhamaṃ vuccati. Tato pacchā appahātabbaṃ yathā taṃ dassanattikādīsu.

819. Because one seeks the abandoning factor in order to cease the affliction caused by that which is to be abandoned, therefore first what is to be abandoned is considered, and afterwards the abandoning factor. This sequence of abandoning what is to be abandoned is stated by the term 'the order of abandoning.' 'Of which' means of what is to be abandoned. 'That' means what is to be abandoned. 'It is stated first' means it is stated first among the investigations of abandonment. After that, what is not to be abandoned is considered, as in the triad concerning abandonment by seeing, and so on.

826. Tanti bhavaṅgaṃ. Tassāti lokuttarassa. Pādakanti antimabhavikassa bhavaṅgaṃ sandhāyāha.

826. 'That' is the life-continuum. 'Of that' refers to the supramundane. 'As basis': he says this in reference to the life-continuum of one in their final existence.

Chaṭṭhabalaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Sixth Power is finished.

Sattamabalaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Seventh Power

828. Samāpannomhīti maññatīti attho.

828. The meaning is that one thinks, 'I have attained.'

Samādhi [V 0.0213] vā tassa ārammaṇabhūtaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ vā cittamañjūsāti yojanā. Ṭhapetunti yathāparicchinnaṃ kālaṃ samāpatticittaṃ pavattetuṃ.

The connection is: concentration, or its object which is the meditation subject, is the mind's casket. 'To place' means to make the mind of attainment proceed for a predetermined period of time.

Tehīti [M 0.0214] saññāmanasikārehi. Taṃsabhāvatāti kāmādidutiyajjhānādianupakkhandanasabhāvatā. Paguṇavodānaṃ paguṇabhāvasiddhā jhānassa paṭipakkhato visuddhi.

'By them' means by perceptions and attention. 'The nature of that' is the nature of not relapsing into the second jhāna, etc., which begins with the sensual sphere. 'Proficient purification' is the purification of the jhāna from its opponent, accomplished by its state of proficiency.

Sattamabalaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Seventh Power is finished.

Dasamabalaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Tenth Power

831. Paññāva vimuttīti rāgādīhi vimuttibhūtā paññāva vimuttīti yojanā. Kammantarassa vipākantaramevāti attho vipākantarajānanasseva dutiyabalakiccattā, kammantarajānanassa ca tatiyabalakiccattā. Balasadisatanti ekaccabalasadisataṃ. Kasmā panettha balañāṇakicce vuccamāne jhānādiabalañāṇaṃ udāhaṭanti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “yadipī”tiādi. Tadantogadhanti tasmiṃ jhānādipaccavekkhaṇāsabhāve sattamabalañāṇe antogadhaṃ. Evanti jhānādiñāṇaṃ viya. Appetuṃ, vikubbituñcāti attanā vuttākāraṃ sandhāyāha. Samudayappahānādiekaccañāṇakiccampi akarontaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ kathamappanādikaṃ jhānādikiccaṃ kareyya, balañāṇehi pana jānitabbaṃ, tato uttariñca jānantampi yasmā ekaccabalakiccaṃ na karoti, tasmā aññāneva balañāṇāni, aññaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇanti dassanatthaṃ “etesaṃ pana kiccaṃ na sabbaṃ karotī”tiādi (vibha. aṭṭha. 831) aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha yathā sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ abalakiccaṃ ekaccaṃ na karoti, evaṃ balakiccampīti udāharaṇadassanavasena “tañhi jhānaṃ hutvā appetu”ntiādi vuttanti dassetuṃ “atha vā…pe… daṭṭhabba”nti vuttaṃ.

831. 'Wisdom itself is liberation' means that wisdom, having become liberated from lust, etc., is itself liberation; this is the connection. The meaning is that one result is only for another kamma, because knowing another result is the function of the second power, and knowing another kamma is the function of the third power. 'Similarity to a power' means similarity to a certain power. In reference to the objection, 'Why, when the function of the power-knowledges is being discussed here, is the non-power knowledge of jhāna, etc., cited?' he says, 'Even if,' etc. 'Included in that' means included in the seventh power-knowledge, which has the nature of reviewing jhāna, etc. 'Thus' means like the knowledge of jhāna, etc. He says this in reference to the mode stated by himself: 'to apply and to transform.' How could the knowledge of omniscience, which does not perform even a certain function of knowledge such as the abandoning of origination, perform the jhāna-function such as application? Since, although it knows what is to be known by the power-knowledges and even beyond that, it does not perform a certain function of a power, therefore the power-knowledges are one thing and the knowledge of omniscience is another. To show this, it is said in the commentary: 'But it does not perform all the functions of these.' Therein, to show by way of example that just as the knowledge of omniscience does not perform a certain function that is not a power's, so too it does not perform a power's function, it is said, 'For that, having become jhāna, one applies it,' etc. To show this, it is said, 'Or... should be seen.'

Dasamabalaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the exposition of the tenth power is finished.

Ñāṇavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Analysis of Knowledge is finished.

17. Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅgo

17. Analysis of Minor Items

1. Ekakaniddesavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Exposition of the Single Item

843-4. Atthipaṭiccaṃ [M 0.0215][V 0.0214] nāmāti atthitā paṭiccattho nāma, asatipi sahajātapurejātādibhāve yasmiṃ sati yaṃ hoti, so tassa paccayoti katvā yathā tathā atthitāmattaṃ idha paṭiccatthoti attho. Taṃ pana paṭiccatthaṃ byatirekamukhena pākaṭataraṃ kātuṃ “yathā”tiādimāha. Tattha nissayādipaccayabhāvena paṭiccāti vuttanti nissayādipaccayabhāvato paccayabhūtaṃ cakkhādi “paṭiccā”ti vuttaṃ. Ekissā seṇiyāti aṭṭhārasasu seṇīsu mayaṃ amukāya seṇiyā jātāmha, na aññe viya appaññātāti evamettha atthaṃ vadanti.

843-4. 'Depending on existence' means the meaning is 'depending on being.'
