Even when there is no state of co-nascence, pre-nascence, etc., when something exists, whatever comes to be is its condition. Thus, the meaning here is that 'depending on' means the mere state of existence in any way whatsoever. To make this meaning of 'depending on' clearer by way of exclusion, he says, 'as,' etc. Therein, 'depending on' is said because of being a condition in the sense of support condition, etc. Thus the eye, etc., being a condition from the state of being a support condition, etc., is said to be 'depending on.' 'Of one guild': they state the meaning here thus: 'Among the eighteen guilds, we are born of such-and-such a guild, not unknown like others.'

Purato karaṇaṃ pamukhabhāvakaraṇaṃ. Nidhānarāsīti nidahitvā ṭhapitadhananicayo. Yasoti issariyaṃ. Taṃ pana yesu vattati, tesu paṭṭhāpakaāṇākaraṇehi pākaṭo hotīti “paṭṭhāpakamado, āṇākaraṇamado”ti ca vuttaṃ.

'Making foremost' means making primary. 'A heap of treasure' means an accumulation of wealth that has been buried and stored. 'Glory' means sovereignty. Since this becomes manifest in those in whom it operates through the establishing of authority and the issuing of commands, it is said: 'the intoxication of establishing and the intoxication of commanding.'

845. Vatthunāti jātiādipavattihetunā.

845. 'By the item' means by the cause for the occurrence of birth, etc.

846. Patiṭṭhābhāvoti kusalakammesu patiṭṭhānābhāvo, so pana yasmā kusalakiriyāya ṭhānaṃ na hoti, tasmā “kusalakaraṇe aṭṭhāna”nti āha. Pamādasaṅkhātassa atthassa evamādiko pariyāyoti yojanā. Ādi-saddena “vacīduccarite, manoduccarite cittassa vossaggo, makkho, paḷāso”ti ca evamādikassa saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo. “Pamādo pamajjanādī”tiādiko tadatthappakāsako, “cittassa vossaggo vossaggānuppādana”ntiādiko tappariyāyappakāsako byañjanapariyāyo [V 0.0215] ca apariyantoti sambandho. “Cattāro khandhe dassetī”ti iminā sativossaggākārappavattā cattāro akusalakkhandhā pamādoti vadati.

846. 'Absence of a basis' means the absence of a foundation in wholesome kamma. Since this is not a basis for the performance of wholesome action, he says, 'it is not a basis for doing good.' The connection is: this is a synonym, etc., for the thing designated as negligence. By the word 'ādi' (etc.), the inclusion of such things as 'misconduct in speech, misconduct in thought, letting go of the mind, hypocrisy, and disparagement' should be understood. The connection is: the expression 'negligence is heedlessness, etc.' clarifies its meaning; the expression 'letting go of the mind is the non-production of letting go,' etc., clarifies its synonyms; and the range of verbal synonyms is limitless. By this, 'he shows the four aggregates,' he says that negligence is the four unwholesome aggregates that occur in the mode of letting go of mindfulness.

847. Anivātavuttitāya hetubhūto cittasampaggaho mānaviseso.

847. A particular kind of conceit, a mental grasping that is the cause for uncompliant behavior.

848. Uttarabhāvo uttariyaṃ, karaṇena uttariyaṃ karaṇuttariyaṃ, sārambhena parassa kiriyato uttarikiriyā.

848. A superior state is superiority. Superiority by way of action is 'superior action.' Through rivalry, it is an action superior to the action of another.

849. Neruttikavidhānenāti [M 0.0216] i-kāracca-kārānañca ra-kāratāpādanena.

849. 'By the etymological method' means by transforming the letters 'i' and 'ca' into the letter 'ra'.

Attahitaṃ attāti uttarapadalopena niddesamāha yathā “rūpabhavo rūpaṃ, bhīmaseno bhīmo”ti ca. Ādinno, patto vā attho attāti niruttinayena padasiddhi veditabbā.

He states the exposition 'one's own welfare is oneself' by eliding the final word, as in 'the form-existence is form' and 'Bhīmasena is Bhīma.' Or, the derivation of the word 'atta' (self) should be understood by the etymological method as meaning 'taken up' or 'attained'.

Mudditassāti aṅkitassa.

'Of one who is sealed' means of one who is marked.

850. Jānantasseva mahājanassa. Upādānādipaccayeti indhanudakacīvarādike pāripūrihetuke.

850. For the great populace who know. 'Due to conditions such as fuel, etc.' means for the sake of fulfilling requisites such as firewood, water, and robes.

851. Gaṇṭhikā sayaṃ gaṇṭhikaraṇato. Patirūpavacanato, aññesaṃ gaṇṭhibhedato ca gaṇṭhibhūtā.

851. A 'knot' because it makes a knot of itself. It has become a knot because of its plausible speech and because it breaks the knots of others.

852. Abhejjantaratāya samāsevitatāya suṭṭhu āsevitatāya.

852. Because of being unbreakable internally, because of being frequented, because of being well frequented.

853. Cirakālaparibhāvitattena temanakaraṇaṃ allabhāvakaraṇaṃ, lobhavasena avassavananti attho.

853. Because it has been developed for a long time, it causes moistening, it makes things wet; the meaning is that it is an outflow due to greed.

Evaṃ sante kathaṃ khīyananti niddesoti āha “khīyananti cā”tiādi.

This being so, how can there be the exposition 'they are destroyed'? He says, 'And "they are destroyed,"' etc.

854. Cīvaramaṇḍanādīnanti [V 0.0216] cīvaramaṇḍanā pattamaṇḍanā senāsanamaṇḍanāti imesaṃ. Idāni taṃ visesanabhāvaṃ yojetvā dassetuṃ “cīvarena hī”tiādi vuttaṃ.

854. 'Of the adornment of robes, etc.' means: of these, namely, the adornment of robes, the adornment of the bowl, and the adornment of the lodging. Now, to show the state of distinction by connecting it, it is said, 'For by the robe,' etc.

855. Sabhāgarahito, sabhāgapaṭipakkho vā asabhāgo, ananukūlānaṃ paṭikkūlatā vā. Tenāha “mānathaddhatā, virodho vā”ti.

855. Devoid of a common lot, or the opponent of a common lot, is 'not of a common lot'; or it is repugnance towards the uncongenial. For that reason he says: 'conceit-stiffness, or opposition.'

856. Saṅkampanā ukkaṇṭhanāvasena anavaṭṭhānaṃ, anavadhānaṃ vā. Tassa tassa ārammaṇassa taṇhāyanā.

856. Shaking is instability by way of dissatisfaction, or inattention. It is craving for this or that object.

857. Kāyassāti nāmakāyassa. Tasmiñhi avipphārike rūpakāyopi avipphāriko hoti.

857. 'Of the body' means of the mental body. For when that is not diffuse, the physical body is also not diffuse.

860. Rāgādīnanti [M 0.0217] rāgamohaahirikānottappavicikicchādīnaṃ.

860. 'Of lust, etc.' means of lust, delusion, shamelessness, fearlessness of wrongdoing, doubt, etc.

861. Tividhampi kuhanavatthuṃ dassetunti sambandho. Tatthāti mahāniddese. “Tattha katamā kuhanā lābhasakkārasilokasannissitassā”tiādinā (vibha. 861) idha khuddakavibhaṅge āgataṃ desanānayaṃ nissāya mahāniddesadesanā pavattāti āha “nissayabhūtāya imāya pāḷiyā”ti.

861. The connection is: 'to show the threefold item of deceit.' 'Therein' means in the Mahāniddesa. He says, 'based on this Pāḷi text which has become the support,' because the teaching in the Mahāniddesa proceeds by relying on the method of teaching that has come in the Khuddakavibhaṅga here, beginning with: 'Therein, what is the deceit of one who is dependent on gain, honor, and fame?'

Antarahitānīti antavikalāni chindantāni.

'Vanished' means cutting off, being deficient in the end.

Lābhasakkārasilokahetu sambhāvanādhippāyena saṃyatākāradassanaṃ kohaññanti āha “pāpicchatāya niratthakakāyavacīvipphandaniggahaṇaṃ koraja”nti. Yo saṃvegabahulo kukkuccako pubbenāparaṃ attanopi kiriyaṃ parisaṅkanto paccavekkhamāno tiṭṭhati, tādisaṃ viya attānaṃ dassento “atiparisaṅkito”ti vutto.

He says that 'hypocrisy' (kohañña) is the showing of a restrained demeanor with the intention of being esteemed on account of gain, honor, and fame. He says, 'craftiness' (koraja) is the suppression of useless bodily and verbal activity out of evil desire. One who is full of spiritual urgency and scrupulous, who stands reflecting on his own action, suspicious of the latter because of the former, showing himself to be like that, is called 'overly suspicious.'

864. Pasaṃsāmukhena nindananti pasaṃsāvatthuto khipanaṃ bahi chaḍḍanaṃ yathā “adāyakaṃ aho dānapatī”ti.

864. 'Censuring by way of praise' means disparaging, casting out, on the basis of an item of praise, as when saying of a non-giver, 'Oh, what a lord of gifts!'

865. Gavesanakammanti [V 0.0217] appakena lābhena mahantassa pariyesanakabyāpāro.

865. 'The act of searching' is the business of seeking a great deal by means of a small gain.

866. Pokkharaṃ vuccati sundaraṃ, vaṇṇassa sundarabhāvo vaṇṇapāripūrī hotīti āha “vaṇṇapāripūrī vā vaṇṇapokkharatā”ti.

866. 'Pokkhara' is said to be 'beautiful.' The beautiful state of the complexion is the perfection of the complexion. Thus he says, 'the perfection of the complexion or the beauty of the complexion.'

879. Seyyamānādiniddesesūti “tattha katamo seyyassa ‘seyyohamasmī’ti māno”tiādinā (vibha. 869) niddiṭṭhesu navasu mānaniddesesu. “Seyyādipuggalo”ti idaṃ tattha pāḷiyaṃ seyyādīnaṃ navannaṃ puggalānaṃ āmaṭṭhattā vuttaṃ. Idha pana puggalāmasane sati seyyapuggalo ca āmasitabbo siyā. Tenevāha “seyyamānabhāvepī”ti. Seyyamānabhāvepīti pi-saddo ākaḍḍhako aseyyamānaniddesepi puggalāmasanassa katattā. Yassa kassacīti seyyādīsu yassa kassaci puggalassa.

879. 'In the expositions of the conceit of superiority, etc.' means in the nine expositions of conceit indicated beginning with, 'Therein, what is the conceit, "I am superior," of one who is superior?' 'The superior person, etc.' is said because the nine persons—superior, etc.—are referred to in the Pāḷi there. But here, when a person is referred to, the superior person might also be the one referred to. For that reason he says, 'even in the case of the conceit of superiority.' 'Even in the case of the conceit of superiority': the particle 'pi' (even) is inclusive because a person is referred to even in the exposition of the conceit of one who is not superior. 'Of anyone whatsoever' means of any person whatsoever among the superior, etc.

880. Purimamānassāti [M 0.0218] pubbe pavattassa sadisamānassa, hīnamānassa vā, sadisamānavaseneva pana pāḷi āgatā.

880. 'Of the former conceit' means of the previously arisen conceit of equality or conceit of inferiority. The Pāḷi, however, has come down only by way of the conceit of equality.

881. “Migānaṃ kotthuko anto, pakkhīnaṃ pana vāyaso”ti (jā. 1.3.135) vacanato āha “pakkhijātīsu vāyaso anto lāmako”ti.

881. Following the saying (Jā. 1.3.135), 'Among beasts the jackal is the lowest, and among birds the crow,' he says, 'among the species of birds, the crow is the lowest, the base one.'

882. Virāganti arahattaṃ.

882. 'Dispassion' means arahantship.

883. Mānasampayuttacchando taṇhāchando. Mānasabhāvaṃ anugato seyyādito sampaggaṇhanavasena pavatto mānasampayuttakattukamyatāchando vā mānacchando.

883. Desire connected with conceit (mānasampayuttacchando) is craving-desire (taṇhāchando). Desire that follows the nature of conceit, proceeding by way of grasping superiority and so on, or the desire-to-do associated with conceit, is conceit-desire (mānacchando).

884. Tatthāti tasmiṃ vilambane nipphādetabbe. Yuttaṃ anucchavikaṃ. Muttaṃ vissaṭṭhaṃ. Siliṭṭhaṃ sahitaṃ, atthadvayavibhāvakaṃ vā.

884. ‘Tattha’ (there) means ‘in that delay, it should be accomplished.’ ‘Yutta’ means ‘fitting, suitable’ (anucchavikaṃ). ‘Mutta’ means ‘released, detached’ (vissaṭṭhaṃ). ‘Siliṭṭha’ means ‘united, connected’ (sahitaṃ), or alternatively, ‘revealing two meanings’ (atthadvayavibhāvakaṃ).

888. Anuddayassevāti mettāyantassa viya anukampantassa viya vikappanāti āha “sahananditādikassā”ti, mettādipatirūpena pavattagehasitasinehassāti attho. Tenāha “tādiso [V 0.0218] rāgo”ti. Attho yujjatīti evampi “tatthā”ti pāḷipadassa attho yujjati. Parānuddayatāhetuko hi parānuddayatāsahito so vitakkoti.

888. ‘Anuddayassa’ (of compassion) is a way of thinking like one who is practicing loving-kindness, like one who is being compassionate—thus he said, ‘of shared joy and the like.’ The meaning is affection that arises in a household life in the guise of loving-kindness, etc. Therefore, he said, ‘such is passion.’ The meaning is fitting. Thus, the meaning of the Pali word ‘tatthā’ (there) is fitting as well. For that thought is caused by compassion for others, and accompanied by compassion for others.

890. Kāmaguṇapāripūriyā yebhuyyena loko sambhāvetīti āha “anavaññattatthameva kāmaguṇe ca patthetī”ti.

890. The world mostly esteems the complete gratification of sensual qualities, hence he said, ‘He desires sensual pleasures just for the sake of not being scorned.’

Ekakaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of Singles is concluded.

2. Dukaniddesavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Exposition of Pairs

891. Bandhatīti kujjhanākāraṃ bandhati ghaṭeti. Upanāho hi āghātavatthunā cittaṃ bandhanto viya hoti, yato aññathā pavattitvāpi avidite upanāhe āghātavatthusannissitova hoti.

891. ‘Binds’ means it binds or connects the manner of being angry. For resentment (upanāha) is like binding the mind with the object of hatred; for even though it may occur otherwise, if the resentment is unacknowledged, it still relies on the object of hatred.

892. Dantehi [M 0.0219] chinditvāti dantehi chinditvā viya ekadesaṃ apanetvā ekadesaṃ gahetvāti adhippāyo.

892. ‘Having bitten off with the teeth’ (dantehi chinditvā) means as if biting off a portion with the teeth, removing one part and taking another—this is the intended meaning.

894. Accayaṃ katvāti vītikkamaṃ katvā. Paṭicchādaneti attanā katassa accayassa paṭicchādane. Vocchindanaṃ vītikkamakiriyāya appaṭijānavasena upacchindanaṃ, vocchindanena chādanā vocchindanachādanā.

894. ‘Having committed a transgression’ (accayaṃ katvā) means having made a transgression. ‘Concealment’ (paṭicchādane) means the concealment of a transgression one has made. ‘Cutting off’ (vocchindanaṃ) means interrupting the act of transgression by way of non-acknowledgement; concealment by cutting off is ‘cutting-off and concealment’ (vocchindanachādanā).

Asammābhāsane saṭha-saddo loke niruḷhoti āha “yo na sammā bhāsati, so saṭho”ti. Saṭhassa yakkhasūkarasadisataṃ dassento “kucchi vā piṭhi vā jānituṃ na sakkā”ti āha, indajālasadiso vā eso daṭṭhabbo.

Regarding improper speech, the term ‘deceitful’ (saṭha) is established in the world, as stated: ‘one who does not speak rightly is deceitful.’ To show the nature of the deceitful as resembling a demon or a boar, it is said: ‘one cannot know whether it is the belly or the back.’ It should be seen as resembling a conjuring trick.

Yo sabbathā vipannajjhāsayopi samāno kāyavacībhedamattena attānaṃ sampannaṃ viya dassetvā [V 0.0219] lokaṃ vañcento aññathā santaṃ aññathā pavedeti. Tenāha “tenetaṃ sāṭheyyaṃ māyāto balavatarā vañcanāti daṭṭhabba”nti. Santadosapaṭicchādanameva hi māyā. Tenevāti balavataravañcanābhāveneva. Daḷhakerāṭiyañhi “parikkhatatā”ti vuttaṃ.

One whose intention is altogether corrupt, yet appearing as if accomplished merely through bodily and verbal demeanor, deceives the world, declaring what is otherwise as something else. Thus it is said: ‘this deceitfulness should be seen as a deception stronger than illusion.’ For illusion (māyā) is merely the covering up of existing faults. It is for this very reason that it is a stronger deception. Indeed, strong deceitfulness is called ‘being well-fortified.’

908. Abhāvepīti pi-saddena “ko pana vādo bhāve”ti dasseti. Yadipi hi puthujjanānaṃ, ekaccānañca sekkhānaṃ yathārahaṃ attābhinivesādīhi katūpakāraṃ rūparāgādisaṃyojanakiccaṃ sādheti, ekaccānaṃ pana vinā eva tehīti kassacipi kilesassa avikkhambhitattā kathañcipi avimutto kāmabhavo ajjhattaggahaṇassa visesapaccayoti “ajjhatta”nti vuccati, tadabhāvato “bahiddhā”ti laddhavohāre rūpārūpabhave kevalampi saṃyojanakiccaṃ sādhentaṃ pavattatīti, tato eva rūpārūpāvacarasattānaṃ bahiddhāsaṃyojanabhāvahetajātanti ca “bahiddhāsaṃyojana”nti vuccatīti imamatthamāha “sakkāyadiṭṭhādīnaṃ…pe… yojanaṃ nāmā”ti.

908. ‘Even in the absence’ (abhāvepi) — the particle ‘pi’ indicates: ‘what need is there to speak of its presence?’ For even though, in the case of ordinary people and some trainees, the function of fetters like attachment to form is accomplished through appropriate self-adherence and so forth, for some, however, it is accomplished even without these. Because no defilement has been suppressed, the realm of sensual existence is in no way freed. Thus, it is called ‘internal’ (ajjhatta) because it is a special condition for grasping within. Due to the absence of that, in the realms of form and formlessness, which are conventionally termed ‘external’ (bahiddhā), it proceeds accomplishing only the function of the fetters; and for this very reason, for beings in the form and formless realms, it is called ‘external fetters’ (bahiddhāsaṃyojana) because they are born from the cause that is the state of external fetters. This is the meaning of the statement: ‘Identity view and so forth... are called fetters.’

Dukaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of Pairs is concluded.

3. Tikaniddesavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Exposition of Triads

909. Avijjābhavataṇhāhi [M 0.0220] viya issāmacchariyadomanassādisahāyabhūtena dosenapi bhavābhisaṅkharaṇaṃ hotīti “akusalamūlāneva vaṭṭamūlānī”ti. Tenāha “tīhi…pe… kathito”ti.

909. Just as the conditioning of existence occurs through ignorance and craving for existence, so too does it occur through hate accompanied by envy, stinginess, displeasure, and the like. Thus, it is said: ‘The roots of the round are solely the unwholesome roots.’ Therefore, it is stated: ‘By three... it is explained.’

919. Rūpārūpāvacaravipākānaṃ santapaṇītabhāvena uḷāratamattā tattha sātisayo bhavarāgo vutto.

919. Due to the sublime, refined, and most excellent nature of form and formless resultant states, excessive attachment to existence is spoken of there.

920. Mānena ṭhapanāti mānena seyyādivasena attano ṭhapanā. Ṭhapanāti ca dahanā, paggaṇhanā vā.

920. ‘Establishment by conceit’ (mānena ṭhapanā) means establishing oneself through conceit as being superior and so forth. ‘Establishment’ (ṭhapanā) also means burning or upholding.

921. Taṃsampayuttāti [V 0.0220] dosasampayuttā.

921. ‘Associated with that’ (taṃsampayuttā) means associated with aversion.

922. Tesaṃ vaṇṇabhedanti tesaṃ jīvānaṃ vaṇṇavisesaṃ, tesaṃ vā tathā kathentānaṃ sutvā. Byāpīti sakalalokabyāpī, sakalasarīrabyāpī vā. Parimaṇḍaloti paramāṇuppamāṇo hutvā parimaṇḍalo. Ādi-saddena aṅguṭṭhappamāṇo vayappamāṇotiādikaṃ saṅgaṇhāti.

922. ‘The diversity of their appearance’ (tesaṃ vaṇṇabhedaṃ) refers to the distinct appearances of those beings, or having heard them described thus. ‘Pervasive’ (byāpī) means pervading the entire world or the entire body. ‘Perfectly round’ (parimaṇḍalo) means being perfectly round, having become the size of an atom. The term ‘etc.’ (ādi-saddena) includes the size of a thumb-tip, the size corresponding to age, and so forth.

923. Utuvipariṇāmajo sītādiutuviparivattajāto. Opakkamiko attano, parassa vā tādisaupakkamanibbatto. Visamaparihārajo cirāsanaciraṭṭhānādinā kāyassa visamapariharaṇato jāto. Sannipātajo sañcayato paṭṭhāya paccekaṃ visamākārato dosattayasamodhānato jāto. Kammasamuṭṭhāno utuvipariṇāmādīhi vinā kammato samuṭṭhito. Pittasemhavātasamuṭṭhānā pana pittādīnaṃ adhikabhāveneva vuttā. Sabbassāpi hi rogassa dosattayaṃ āsannakāraṇaṃ dosappakopena vinā abhāvato. Kammaṃ padhānakāraṇaṃ katokāse eva tasmiṃ uppajjanato, itaraṃ pana tassa sahakārikāraṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tayidaṃ pubbekatahetuvādino paṭikkhipanti. Upapajjavedanīyaphalampi pubbekatahetukapakkhikameva atītaddhikattā kammassāti arucisūcanatthaṃ kira-saddaggahaṇaṃ karoti “upapajjavedanīyañca kira paṭikkhipantī”ti.

923. That arising from the change of seasons (utuvipariṇāmajo) is produced by the alteration of seasons, such as cold and so forth. That which is caused by external action (opakkamiko) is produced by one’s own or another’s similar action. That arising from irregular habits (visamaparihārajo) is produced by irregular care of the body, such as prolonged sitting or prolonged standing, and so forth. That arising from a combination of humors (sannipātajo) is produced by the accumulation, individual imbalance, and combination of the three humors. That which is kamma-originated (kammasamuṭṭhāno) is that which arises from kamma, without seasonal changes and so forth. Those arising from bile, phlegm, and wind are said to be due to the predominance of bile and so forth. For in all diseases, the three humors are the proximate cause, as diseases are absent without the provocation of the humors. Kamma is the primary cause, as it manifests only when the occasion arises, while the others should be seen as auxiliary causes. Those who hold the view of past-action causality reject this. Furthermore, the result to be experienced in the subsequent existence is also on the side of past-action causality since kamma is past; the word ‘kira’ is used to indicate disapproval, as in: ‘they reject also, it seems, the result to be experienced in the subsequent existence’.

924. Dāhakāraṇatāyāti rāgādidasavidhaggidāhassa, narakaggidāhassa ca kāraṇatāya.

924. ‘Being the cause of burning’ (dāhakāraṇatāya) means being the cause of the burning by the ten kinds of fires, such as greed, and the burning by the fire of hell.

926. Puthunimittasabhāvesūti [M 0.0221] puthu nānākilesādīnaṃ kāraṇasabhāvesu.

926. ‘In diverse natures and causes’ (puthunimittasabhāvesu) means in the diverse causal natures of various defilements and so forth.

931. Addanaṃ addā maddavo, anekatthattā dhātūnaṃ tappaṭikkhepena anaddāti āha “amudutā vā anaddā”ti.

931. `Addanaṃ` or `addā` means softness. Since verbal roots have multiple meanings, by way of its negation, `anaddā`, it is said: '`anaddā` is non-softness.'

936. Ayonisomanasikārahetukattā āvajjanāya akusalānukūlakiccatā daṭṭhabbā.

936. The function of adverting should be seen as conducive to the unwholesome because it is caused by unwise attention.

Tikaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of Triads is concluded.

4. Catukkaniddesavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Exposition of Fours

939. Evaṃ-saddenāti [V 0.0221] nidassanatthena evaṃ-saddenāti adhippāyo. Bhavo eva abhivuddho abhavo yathā “asekkhā dhammā”ti (dha. sa. tikamātikā 11). Dutiyasmiṃ pakkhe bhavābhavasaddena sampattivipattiyo, vuddhihāniyo vā vuttāti veditabbā.

939. By the word 'evaṃ' (thus), the meaning is by way of illustration; this is the intention of 'by the word evaṃ'. Existence itself is developed; non-existence is like 'the phenomena of those beyond training' (Dhs. Tikamātikā 11). In the second case, by the word 'bhavābhava', accomplishment and failure, or growth and decline, are said to be understood.

Agatiyāti ayuttagatiyā, appatirūpakiriyāyāti attho.

'Agati' (wrong course) means an unfitting course, improper action; that is the meaning.

Kodhūpāyāsa…pe… mātugāmā vā ūmiādibhayanti yojanā. Pañcakāmaguṇamātugāmaggahaṇeti pañcakāmaguṇaggahaṇe, mātugāmaggahaṇe ca.

'Anger and despair'… etc.… and 'women are a fear like waves, etc.'—this is the construction. By 'the taking of the five strands of sensual pleasure and women' is meant the taking of the five strands of sensual pleasure and the taking of women.

“Sayaṃkataṃ sukhadukkha”ntiādikā diṭṭhi yadipi aññesampi diṭṭhigatikānaṃ attheva, timbaruko pana tathādiṭṭhiko bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchīti sā diṭṭhi “timbarukadiṭṭhī”ti (saṃ. ni. 2.18) vuttā. Tenāha “timbaruko…pe… āgatattā”ti.

The view "happiness and suffering are self-made," etc., although also present among other adherents of views, is called "Timbaruka's view" (SN 12.18) because Timbaruka, holding such a view, approached the Blessed One and questioned him. Therefore, it is said, "Timbaruka… etc., because it came from him."

Catukkaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Fours is completed.

5. Pañcakaniddesavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Fives

940. Āgamanassa [M 0.0222] paṭisandhiggahaṇavasenāti adhippāyo.

940. The meaning of 'coming' (`āgamanassa`) is by way of the taking of rebirth-linking.

941. Upacayanatoti vaḍḍhanato. Aññathāti lābhato takkanato ca aññappakāro gahitoti taṃ dassento “saddhāruciādīhī”ti āha. Anussavato hi saddahanaṃ, ruccanaṃ pana jātissarañāṇatopi hoti. Ādi-saddena khantiādīnaṃ saṅgaho.

941. 'From accumulation' (`upacayanato`) means from growth. 'Otherwise' (`aññathā`) refers to a different kind of grasping, different from acquisition and reasoning; showing this, it says 'by faith, preference, etc.' (`saddhāruciādīhi`). For faith comes from hearsay, while preference can also arise from the knowledge of remembering past lives. The word 'ādi' (etc.) includes patience and other such qualities.

942. Akkhanti [V 0.0222] mūlaṃ etesanti akkhantimūlakā. Dukkaṭadubbhāsitatādidosā tādisāni kāyavacīmanoduccaritāni.

942. Impatience is the root of these; thus, they are 'rooted in impatience'. Faults such as wrong-doing, wrong-speaking, and so on, are such misconduct of body, speech, and mind.

943. Udaggatāsaṅkhāto avūpasamo na uddhaccasaṅkhātoti pītiyā eva savipphārikatāsaṅkhātaṃ asantasabhāvaṃ āha. Avūpasamahetubhūtoti vikkhepahetubhūto. Pītiyā ākāroti pītiyā pavattiākāro.

943. The non-calmness (`avūpasamo`) reckoned as elation (`udaggatā`) is not reckoned as agitation (`uddhacca`); rather, it refers to the unpeaceful nature reckoned as the expansive quality of joy (`pīti`). 'Being a cause of non-calmness' means being a cause of distraction. 'The mode of joy' means the manner in which joy proceeds.

Pañcakaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Fives is completed.

6. Chakkaniddesavaṇṇanā

6. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Sixes

944. Tenāti kodhādīnaṃyeva vivādamūlattā.

944. By that (`tena`), because anger and the like are the very root of disputes.

945. Kusalānuyoge sātaccaṃ kusalānuyogasātaccaṃ.

945. `Kusalānuyogasātaccaṃ` is persistence (`sātaccaṃ`) in the pursuit of the wholesome (`kusalānuyoge`).

Gaṇena sattasamūhena saṅgaṇi sannipatanaṃ yena saddhiṃ, tena saṅgati gaṇasaṅgaṇikā. Kassaci ghāsacchādanādikassa.

Association (`saṅgati`) with a group (`gaṇena`), a multitude of beings (`sattasamūhena`), a gathering (`saṅgaṇi`), an assembly (`sannipatanaṃ`)—this is group association (`gaṇasaṅgaṇikā`). Of someone's food, clothing, and so on.

946. Upavitakketīti ārammaṇaṃ upecca takketi.

946. '`Upavitakketi`' means: having approached (`upecca`) an object (`ārammaṇaṃ`), one applies thought (`takketi`).

948. Adhiccasamuppannikoti “adhiccasamuppanno attā ca loko cā”ti evaṃvādī.

948. A proponent of accidental arising (`adhiccasamuppanniko`) is one who asserts thus: "The self and the world arise by chance."

Chakkaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Sixes is completed.

8. Aṭṭhakaniddesavaṇṇanā

8. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Eights

952. Osīdanākārenāti [M 0.0223][V 0.0223] kattabbakamme anussahanākārena.

952. 'In a manner of sinking' (`osīdanākārena`) means in a manner of not exerting oneself in the task to be done.

958. Te abhinivesā asaññīvādā vadanti etehīti.

958. They are called proponents of non-perception (`asaññīvādā`) because they speak by means of these adherences.

Aṭṭhakaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Eights is completed.

9. Navakaniddesavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Nines

960-963. Dasamassāti aṭṭhānaghātassa.

960-963. 'Of the tenth' (`dasamassa`) refers to an inopportune strike (`aṭṭhānaghātassa`).

Ajjhattanti gocarajjhattaṃ adhippetaṃ. Etassa gāthāvacanassa. Niṭṭhapetvāti abhinivissa.

'Internally' (`ajjhattaṃ`) means the internal sphere is intended. This refers to the statement of the verse. 'Having established' (`niṭṭhapetvā`) means having adhered to.

964. Aññesaṃ phassādīnaṃ saṅkhatabhāve yathāsakaṃpaccayehi. Yenākārena mānassa sātisayā pavatti, taṃ dassetuṃ “ahanti, asmīti cā”ti vuttaṃ. Attanoti diṭṭhigataparikappitassa attano. Yathā mānassa sampaggahavasena, evaṃ taṇhāya mamattavasena, diṭṭhiyā niccādivasena pavatti visesavatī samānepi anāgatakālāmasaneti āha “bhavissantī…pe… vutto”ti. “Ahamasmī”ti pana pavattamānasseva bhavatīti sabbapadasādhāraṇassa mānasseva vasena iñjitāditā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttā.

964. For other things, such as contact and so on, their conditioned nature is according to their respective conditions. To show the manner in which conceit arises excessively, it is said, 'I am' and 'I am this.' 'Of self' (`attano`) refers to the self conceived by wrong view. Just as the operation of conceit is distinct through grasping, so is that of craving through possessiveness, and that of wrong view through notions of permanence, etc. Although they are similar in not pertaining to future time, it is said, 'they will be…' etc. But 'I am' occurs only in the present; therefore, in the commentary, the stirring, etc., is said to be due to conceit alone, which is common to all these expressions.

Navakaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Nines is completed.

10. Dasakaniddesavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Tens

970. Saṅkappananti [V 0.0224] “kusalatā”ti vuttapadassa atthavacanaṃ. Tassā upāyacintāya. Micchābhāvo sāvajjabhāvo. Tadākāro mohoti yathāvuttākārena pavatte cittuppāde moho. Tassāpi yathāvuttapaccavekkhaṇāyapi yathākatapāpepi. Adhimānasampayuttaṃ sañjānanaṃ pakatipurisantaradassanādivasena pavattaṃ diṭṭhisampayuttacittaṃ phalaṃ viya vimuttanti gahitaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

970. 'Intention' (`saṅkappanaṃ`) is a word that explains the meaning of the term 'skillfulness' (`kusalatā`). It refers to the thought about expedients. Wrongness (`micchābhāvo`) is the state of being blameworthy. 'That mode is delusion' (`tadākāro moho`) means delusion in a thought-process that occurs in the aforesaid manner. This is so also in the aforesaid reflection and in the evil that was done. Perception associated with conceit, which arises by way of seeing oneself as different from an ordinary person, and a mind associated with wrong view, should be seen as being grasped as liberation, just as a fruit is grasped.

Dasakaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Tens is completed.

Taṇhāvicaritaniddesavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Wanderings of Craving.

973. Visesaṃ [M 0.0224] akatvāti anupanidhānaṃ, samato ca asamato ca upanidhānanti imaṃ vibhāgaṃ akatvā, yo “itthaṃ, evaṃ, aññathā”ti padehi pakāsito.

973. 'Visesaṃ akatvā' (without making a distinction) means without comparison (anupanidhānaṃ); without making this distinction of comparison, whether equal or unequal, which is made clear by the words 'thus, in this way, or otherwise.'

Visesassāti “itthaṃ, evaṃ, aññathā”ti yathāvuttasseva visesassa. Diṭṭhiyāti diṭṭhiyā gahitāya tadavinābhāvinī taṇhā dassitā. Sīsasīsamūlakehīti catūhi sīsehi, dvādasahi ca sīsamūlakehi. Sayameva ca taṇhā dassitāti yojanā. Yadi diṭṭhimānagāhopi idhādhippeto, yato “taṇhāmānadiṭṭhivasena samūhagāhato”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 973) aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ, kathaṃ “taṇhāvicaritānī”ti vacananti āha “diṭṭhimānesū”tiādi. Taṃmūlakattāti taṇhāmūlakattā.

'Visesassa' (of distinction) refers to the very distinction previously stated as 'thus, in this way, or otherwise.' 'Diṭṭhiyā' (by view) indicates craving (taṇhā) that is inseparable from the view that is held. 'Sīsasīsamūlakehi' (by heads and bases of heads) refers to the four heads and the twelve bases of heads. The connection (yojanā) is: 'And craving itself is shown.' If the grasping of views and conceit is also intended here, since it is said in the commentary (Vibhaṅga Aṭṭhakathā 973), 'from grasping as a group by way of craving, conceit, and view,' how then is the statement 'taṇhāvicaritānī' (wanderings of craving) to be understood? He says, 'diṭṭhimānesū' (in views and conceit), and so on. 'Taṃmūlakattā' (because it has that as its root) means because it is rooted in craving (taṇhā).

974. Na avakkarīyatīti anavakārī, taṃ anavakāriṃ katvā, taṃ padantarena vibhāvento “anavakkari, taṃ katvā”ti āha. Vikkhepanaṃ avayavato vibhāgo. Attato avinibbhujitvāti yvāyaṃ diṭṭhigatikaparikappito attā, tato avisuṃ katvā.

974. 'Na avakkarīyati' (is not discarded) means 'anavakārī' (not discarding). Having made it non-discarding, and explaining it with another term, he says, 'anavakkari, taṃ katvā' (not discarded, having made it so). Scattering (vikkhepanaṃ) is division into parts. 'Attato avinibbhujitvā' (not having separated from self) means not making it separate from that self imagined by those holding certain views.

976. Bahikatāni rūpādīni upagantvā pavattā taṇhā upādāyāti vuttāti yojanā.

976. The connection (yojanā) is: Craving, having approached external things such as form, proceeds; thus it is called 'upādāya' (clinging).

Ekaccassa [V 0.0225] puggalassa ekasmiṃ attabhāve kassaci taṇhāvicaritassa asambhavo, kassacideva sambhavoti āha “kassaci sambhavadassanatthaṃ vutta”nti.

For a certain individual in a single existence, there is the non-occurrence of one kind of wandering of craving, and the occurrence of another. Thus he said, "It is stated to show the occurrence for a certain one."

Taṇhāvicaritaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Wanderings of Craving is concluded.

Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of Minor Topics is concluded.

18. Dhammahadayavibhaṅgo

18. The Analysis of the Heart of the Dhamma.

1. Sabbasaṅgāhikavāravaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the All-Inclusive Section.

978. Dhātusambhava…pe… [M 0.0225][V 0.0226] saṅgahitattāti ettha khandhādīnaṃ kāmadhātuādidhātūsu sambhavabhedabhinnānaṃ niravasesato saṅgahitattāti vibhāgena yojanā, tathā sesesupi pariyāpannapabhedabhinnānantiādinā. Tattha “niravasesato saṅgahitattā”ti iminā “sabbasaṅgāhikavāro”ti ayamassa atthānugatā samaññāti dasseti. Yasmā cettha khandhādīnaṃ dvādasannaṃ koṭṭhāsānaṃ anavasesasaṅgaho, tasmā evaṃ dutiyavārādīnañcettha anuppaveso veditabbo. Khandhādīnameva hi tesaṃ sambhavādivicāro uppattānuppattidassanavāroti vattuṃ yuttoti yojanā. Anuppattidassanañcettha atthāpattisiddhaṃ veditabbaṃ. Na hi tattha “kati khandhā na pātubhavantī”tiādipāḷi atthi.

978. Regarding 'Dhātusambhava…pe… saṅgahitattā' (origin in the elements... because of being included): here the connection, by way of detailed explanation, is that the aggregates and so on, which are distinguished by the division of their origin in the elements such as the sense-sphere element, are included without remainder. Likewise in the remaining cases, by such phrases as 'distinguished by the division of inclusion.' Therein, by this phrase 'niravasesato saṅgahitattā' (because of being included without remainder), it shows that 'sabbasaṅgāhikavāro' (the all-inclusive section) is its designation that follows the meaning. Since there is here an inclusion without remainder of the twelve portions, such as the aggregates, therefore the inclusion herein of the second section and so on should be understood. The connection is: Indeed, it is fitting to call the investigation of the origin and so on of these very aggregates, etc., 'the section showing arising and non-arising.' And here, the showing of non-arising should be understood as established by implication, for there is no Pāli text there such as, "How many aggregates do not appear?"

979. Pucchānurūpanti yenādhippāyena pucchā katā, tadanurūpaṃ. Avitathabyākaraṇaṃ nāma buddhānaṃ eva āveṇikaṃ, aññesaṃ taṃ yādicchikaṃ sutakkharasadisanti āha “sabbaññuvacanaṃ viññāya katattā”ti.

979. 'Pucchānurūpaṃ' means: in accordance with the intention with which the question was asked. A truthful explanation (avitathabyākaraṇaṃ) is indeed a unique quality of Buddhas alone; for others, it is by chance, like a well-heard text. Thus it is said, "because it is made having understood the word of the Omniscient One."

Sabbasaṅgāhikavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the All-Inclusive Section is concluded.

2. Uppattānuppattivāravaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Section on Arising and Non-arising.

991. “Kāmabhave”ti [V 0.0227] idaṃ okāsavasena vatvā puna sattasantānavasena vattuṃ “kāmadhātusambhūtānañcā”ti vuttanti tamatthavisesaṃ dassento “iddhiyā…pe… attho”ti āha. “Na vattabbaṃ siyā”ti kasmā vuttaṃ, yadipi asaññasattānaṃ acakkhukattā rūpāyatanaṃ accantasukhumattā heṭṭhimabhūmikānañca agocaro, samānabhūmikānaṃ pana vehapphalānaṃ, uparibhūmikānañca suddhāvāsānaṃ cakkhāyatanassa gocaro hotīti āyatanādikiccaṃ karotiyevāti sakkā vattuṃ. Yaṃ panettha vitthārato vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. “Heṭṭhato avīcinirayaṃ pariyantaṃ katvā uparito paranimmitavasavattideve [M 0.0226] antokaritvā yaṃ etasmi”ntiādinā (dha. sa. 1287) vuttapadesā kāmāvacarādiokāsā. Te sattanikāyā ca dhātūti vuccanti samudāyassa avayavādhārabhāvato yathā “māsapuñjo māso”ti. Sattā uppajjanti etthāti sattuppatti, uppajjanaṭṭhena sattāva uppatti sattuppattīti evaṃ okāsasattalokadvayassa sattuppattipariyāyo veditabbo. Sattabhāvena uppatti, na anupādinnakkhandhā viya saṅkhārabhāvenevāti adhippāyo. Ke pana teti āha “sattāvāsavasena…pe… upādinnakakkhandhā”ti. Taṃtaṃpariyāpannānanti taṃtaṃsattāvāsapariyāpannānaṃ sattānaṃ, saṅkhārānameva vā. Sadisādhiṭṭhānabhāvenāti sadisākārena pavattamānānaṃ khandhānaṃ patiṭṭhānabhāvena. Yebhuyyena hi tasmiṃ sattāvāse dhammā samānākārena pavattanti.

991. Having said, "In the kamma-existence of sensual desire," in terms of location, in order to speak again in terms of the continuity of beings, it is said, "and of those originating in the sense-sphere element." Showing this distinction in meaning, he says, "by psychic power… the meaning." Why is it said, "It should not be said"? Although the form-base is not an object for non-percipient beings, due to their being without eyes, and for those in lower planes, due to its extreme subtlety, it is an object for the eye-base of the Vehapphala devas on the same plane and for the Pure Abodes on higher planes, as it performs the function of a base, etc. Thus, it can indeed be said. Whatever should be said here in detail has already been said below. The regions spoken of by the passage beginning, "Having made the Avīci hell the lower limit and including the Paranimmitavasavatti devas as the upper limit, whatever is in this…" (Dhs. 1287), are the locations of the sense-sphere, etc. And those groups of beings are called "elements" because they are the container for the parts of a collection, just as a heap of beans is called "beans." "Beings arise here," thus "arising of beings." By the meaning of arising, beings themselves are the arising, thus "arising of beings." In this way, the term "arising of beings" should be understood for the twofold world of location and of beings. The meaning is: arising with the nature of a being, not merely with the nature of formations like unappropriated aggregates. "But who are they?" He says, "by way of the abodes of beings… the appropriated aggregates." "Of those included in each" means of the beings included in each abode of beings, or of the formations themselves. "By being a similar basis" means by being the foundation for aggregates that proceed in a similar way. For in that abode of beings, phenomena generally proceed in a similar way.

Uppattānuppattivāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Section on Arising and Non-arising is concluded.

3. Pariyāpannāpariyāpannavāravaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Section on the Included and the Unincluded.

999. Tattha, aññattha cāti tasmiṃ, aññasmiñca bhave, okāse ca. Paricchedakārikāya kāmāditaṇhāya paricchijja āpannā gahitāti pariyāpannāti taṃtaṃbhavādiantogadhā taṃtaṃpariyāpannā.

999. 'Tattha, aññattha ca' (Therein and elsewhere) means in that and in another existence, and in a location. 'Pariyāpanna' (included) means that, having been delimited by the delimiting function of craving for sensual pleasures and so on, they are entered into and grasped. Being contained within those respective existences and so on, they are included in them.

Pariyāpannāpariyāpannavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Section on the Included and the Unincluded is concluded.

6. Uppādakakammaāyuppamāṇavāro

6. The Section on Productive Kamma and the Measure of the Lifespan.

1. Uppādakakammavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on Productive Kamma.

1021. Dhātuttayabhūtadevavasenāti [V 0.0228] kāmādidhātuttaye nibbattadevānaṃ vasena.

1021. 'Dhātuttayabhūtadevavasena' (by way of the devas existing in the three elements) means by way of the devas born in the three elements beginning with the sense-sphere.

Uppādakakammavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on Productive Kamma is concluded.

2. Āyuppamāṇavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Measure of the Lifespan.

1026. Suparimajjitakañcanādāsaṃ [M 0.0227] viya sobhati vijjotatīti subho, sarīrobhāso, tena subhena kiṇṇā vikiṇṇāti subhakiṇṇā.

1026. Like a well-polished golden mirror, it shines and gleams; thus 'subho' (lustrous) refers to the radiance of the body. 'Subhakiṇṇā' (Strewn with Lustre) means they are strewn and scattered with that lustre.

1027. Taṃtaṃmanasikāranti parittapathavīkasiṇādigatamanasikāraṃ. Appanākkhaṇepīti pi-saddena pubbabhāgaṃ sampiṇḍeti. Chandanaṃ ārammaṇapariyesanaṃ chando, kattukamyatāchando. Paṇidhānaṃ cittaṭṭhapanā paṇidhi, saññāvirāgādīhi ārammaṇassa visesanaṃ tathāpavattāya bhāvanāya ārammaṇakaraṇameva.

1027. 'Taṃtaṃmanasikāraṃ' (attention to this or that) means attention directed to the limited earth kasiṇa and so on. 'Appanākkhaṇepi' (even at the moment of absorption): by the particle 'pi' (even), it includes the preliminary stage. 'Chandanaṃ' (willing) is 'chando' (will), the seeking of an object; it is the will that is the desire to act. 'Paṇidhānaṃ' (aspiration) is 'paṇidhi' (aspiration), the establishing of the mind. The qualifying of the object by dispassion towards perception and so on is simply the making of it an object for the meditation that proceeds in such a way.

Vipulaṃ vuccati mahantaṃ, santabhāvopi mahanīyatāya mahantamevāti āha “vipulā phalāti vipulasantasukhāyuvaṇṇādiphalā”ti.

'Vipulaṃ' (vast) is called 'mahantaṃ' (great). The state of peace is also great on account of its venerability. Thus he says, "'Vipulā phalā' (vast fruits) means the fruits of vast peace, happiness, lifespan, beauty, and so on."

1028. Yaṃ cātumahārājikānaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ, sañjīve eso eko rattidivo, tāya rattiyā tiṃsa rattiyo māso, tena māsena dvādasamāsiko saṃvaccharo, tena saṃvaccharena pañca vassasatāni sañjīve āyuppamāṇaṃ. Yaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ, eso kāḷasutte eko rattidivo…pe… tena saṃvaccharena vassasahassaṃ kāḷasutte āyuppamāṇaṃ. Yaṃ yāmānaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ, eso saṅghāte eko rattidivo…pe… tena saṃvaccharena dve vassasahassāni saṅghāte [V 0.0229] āyuppamāṇaṃ. Yaṃ tusitānaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ, roruve eso eko rattidivo…pe… tena saṃvaccharena cattāri vassasahassāni roruve āyuppamāṇaṃ. Yaṃ nimmānaratīnaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ, mahāroruve eso eko rattidivo…pe… tena saṃvaccharena aṭṭha vassasahassāni mahāroruve āyuppamāṇaṃ. Yaṃ paranimmitavasavattīnaṃ devānaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ, tāpane eso eko rattidivo…pe… tena saṃvaccharena soḷasa vassasahassāni tāpane āyuppamāṇaṃ. Mahātāpane upaḍḍhantarakappo. Avīciyaṃ eko antarakappo ca āyuppamāṇanti vadanti. Devānaṃ adhimuttakālakiriyā viya tādisena puññabalena antarāpi maraṇaṃ hotīti “kammameva pamāṇa”nti vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Evañca katvā abbudādiāyuparicchedopi yuttataro hotīti.

1028. The lifespan of the Cātumahārājika gods is the measure of one day and night in the Sañjīva hell. Thirty such nights make a month, twelve such months make a year, and by that year, five hundred years is the lifespan in the Sañjīva hell. The lifespan of the Tāvatiṃsa gods is the measure of one day and night in the Kāḷasutta hell... and one thousand such years is the lifespan in the Kāḷasutta hell. The lifespan of the Yāma gods is the measure of one day and night in the Saṅghāta hell... and two thousand such years is the lifespan in the Saṅghāta hell. The lifespan of the Tusita gods is the measure of one day and night in the Roruva hell... and four thousand such years is the lifespan in the Roruva hell. The lifespan of the Nimmānaratī gods is the measure of one day and night in the Mahāroruva hell... and eight thousand such years is the lifespan in the Mahāroruva hell. The lifespan of the Paranimmitavasavattī gods is the measure of one day and night in the Tāpana hell... and sixteen thousand such years is the lifespan in the Tāpana hell. In the Mahātāpana hell, it is half an interim aeon. In the Avīci hell, they say one interim aeon is the lifespan. Just as the death of gods can occur in the interim by their resolve, through such power of merit, so it should be understood that it is said, 'kamma alone is the measure.' And having done so, the determination of lifespans beginning with Abbuda is more fitting.

Kiṃ [M 0.0228] jhānanti aṭṭhasu jhānesu kataraṃ jhānaṃ. Bhavasīsānīti bhavaggāni, puthujjanabhavaggaṃ ariyabhavaggaṃ sabbabhavagganti vehapphalādīnaṃ samaññā. Kassaci sattāti puthujjanassa, kassaci pañcāti sotāpannassa, sakadāgāmino ca, kassaci tayoti anāgāmino vasena vuttaṃ. Tasmā so brahmakāyikādīhi cuto arūpaṃ upapajjanto veditabbo. “Navasu brahmalokesu nibbattaariyasāvakānaṃ tatrūpapattiyeva hoti, na heṭṭhūpapattī”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 1028) ayaṃ aṭṭhakathāpāṭhoti adhippāyena “yaṃ panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Tatrūpapattipi hoti uparūpapattipi, na heṭṭhūpapattī”ti pana pāṭhoti tena “heṭṭhūpapattiyeva nivāritā”tiādivacanena payojanaṃ natthi. Arūpadhātūpapatti ca na nivāritāti sambandho. Arūpadhātūpapatti na nivāritā “matthake ṭhitova parinibbātī”ti niyamassa anicchitattā.

What is meant by jhāna? Which jhāna among the eight jhānas? 'The peaks of existence' means the highest states of existence, which are designations for the Vehapphala realm and the like, namely, the peak of an ordinary person's existence, the peak of a noble one's existence, and the peak of all existence. 'For some, seven' refers to an ordinary person. 'For some, five' refers to a stream-enterer and a once-returner. 'For some, three' is stated with reference to a non-returner. Therefore, it should be understood that this refers to one who has passed away from the Brahmā realms, such as the Brahmakāyika realm, and is reborn in the formless realm. The statement, 'For noble disciples reborn in the nine Brahmā realms, there is only rebirth there, not rebirth below' (Vibhaṅga Commentary 1028), is the reading in the commentary. With this intention, 'but what...' and so on is stated. However, if the reading is, 'Rebirth there also occurs, and rebirth above also occurs, but not rebirth below,' then there is no need for statements like 'only rebirth below is prevented.' And the connection is that rebirth in the formless realm is not prevented. Rebirth in the formless realm is not prevented because the rule that 'one must attain final nibbāna while remaining at the peak' is not accepted.

Aññatthāti kāmaloke. Tatthāti rūpaloke. Ayaṃ aṭṭhakathāti “paṭhamajjhānabhūmiyaṃ nibbatto…pe… parinibbātī”ti evaṃ pavattā aṭṭhakathā. Tenevāti yasmā rūpadhātuyaṃ upapanno adhippeto, na upapajjanāraho, teneva kāraṇena. Tassāti yathāvuttassa rūpadhātuyaṃ upapannassa ariyasāvakassa. Yena rūparāgena tattha rūpabhave upapanno, tasmiṃ arūpajjhānena vikkhambhite sammadeva diṭṭhādīnavesu yathā kāmarūpabhavesu āyatiṃ bhavābhilāso na bhavissati, evaṃ arūpabhavepīti dassento āha “puna…pe… bhavissatiyevā”ti. Tattha nibbattoti rūpadhātuyaṃ upapanno. Ariyamaggaṃ bhāvetvāti heṭṭhimaṃ ariyamaggaṃ sampādetvā. Nibbattabhavādīnavadassanavasenāti tasmiṃ rūpabhave nibbattopi tattheva ādīnavadassanavasena. Anivattitabhavābhilāsoti upari arūpabhave avissaṭṭhabhavapatthano, yato arūpadhātuyaṃ upapajjanāraho. Tassa vasenāti tādisassa ariyasāvakassa [V 0.0230] vasena. “Kassaci pañca, kassaci tayo anusayā anusentī”ti ayaṃ yamakapāḷi (yama. 2.anusayayamaka.312) pavattā.

'Elsewhere' means in the realm of sensual desire. 'There' means in the realm of form. 'This commentary' means the commentary that proceeds thus: 'Born in the first jhāna realm... attains final nibbāna.' 'Therefore' means: because one who is reborn in the form realm is intended, not one who is merely fit for rebirth, for that very reason. 'For him' means for that noble disciple who is reborn in the realm of form as described. To show that when the desire for form by which he was reborn in that form existence is suppressed by the formless jhāna, by rightly seeing the dangers, just as in the realms of sensual desire and form there will be no future craving for existence, so too in the formless existence, he says, 'Again... there will indeed be.' 'Reborn there' means reborn in the realm of form. 'Having developed the noble path' means having perfected the lower noble path. 'By way of seeing the danger in the existence where he is reborn' means even though reborn in that form existence, by way of seeing the danger there itself. 'Not relinquishing the craving for existence' means not abandoning the aspiration for existence above in the formless realm, since he is fit to be reborn in the formless realm. 'By way of him' means by way of such a noble disciple. 'For some, five underlying tendencies persist; for some, three,' this Yamaka passage (Yam. 2. Anusayayamaka.312) proceeds.

Āyuppamāṇavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the measure of lifespan is complete.

7. Abhiññeyyādivāravaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the Section on What Should Be Directly Known, etc.

1030. “Ruppanalakkhaṇaṃ [M 0.0229] rūpaṃ, anubhavanalakkhaṇā vedanā”tiādinā sāmaññalakkhaṇapariggāhikā. “Phusanalakkhaṇo phasso, sātalakkhaṇaṃ sukha”ntiādinā visesalakkhaṇapariggāhikā.

1030. 'Form has the characteristic of being impinged upon; feeling, of experiencing,' etc., is the comprehension of the general characteristic. 'Contact has the characteristic of touching; pleasure, of gratification,' etc., is the comprehension of the specific characteristic.

“Cattāro khandhā siyā kusalā”tiādīsu idha yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ khandhavibhaṅgādīsu vuttaṃ, tasmā tattha vuttanayeneva gahetabbanti adhippāyo. Sesaṃ yadettha na vuttaṃ, taṃ suviññeyyamevāti.

In regard to 'The four aggregates might be wholesome,' etc., what should be stated here has already been stated in the Analysis of the Aggregates and so on. Therefore, the meaning is that it should be grasped according to the method stated there. The remainder, whatever is not stated here, is indeed easily understood.

Abhiññeyyādivāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Section on What Should Be Directly Known, etc., is finished.

Dhammahadayavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of the Heart of the Dhamma is finished.

Iti sammohavinodaniyā ṭīkāya līnatthavaṇṇanā

Thus, the Explanation of the Hidden Meaning in the Subcommentary on the Sammohavinodanī.

Vibhaṅga-anuṭīkā samattā.

The Sub-subcommentary on the Vibhaṅga is complete.
